Once you find fish, right click on the fish object and bash it. You will shoot an arrow, and then you will get a message saying what happens . Sometimes after you shoot your arrow, your character will bend over and act like it is pulling something in. When this happens, your character is either pulling in a fish, or pulling back the arrow he/she shot. If you succesfully get a fish, you will gain XP in the fishing trade.

                                                                     Fishing With a Rod

Fishing with a rod is a bit more complicated than using a bow to fish, but still is not difficult. In order to fish with a rod, you will need...

Fishing Rod- There is only one fishing rod (Quarterstaff), and is available at the Craft Vendor.

Fishing Line- There are three lines available. 10 LBS, 30 LBS, 50 LBS. The line determines the size of fish you will be able to catch. The 10 LBS one can catch the lightest, the 50 LBS one can catch the heaviest. These are available at the Craft Vendor.

Lure/Bait- There are several objects you can use for bait. Some you can purchase, some you can dig and find. Copper Fly Lures, Copper Lures, and Grub Worms are a few examples of bait you can use to fish. If you plan on using worms, you will need a shovel in order to dig them up.

Okay, here is the list on what you have to do in order to fish with a rod...

Buy a fishing rod, a fishing line, and obtain some sort of lure/bait
Once you have the three above, find yourself a school of fish!
Equip the fishing rod in your weapon slot
Right click on your fishing line and use its unique power
Right click on your lure/bait and use its unique power
Right click on your fishing rod and use its unique power, click on the school of fish.
Using those steps, your character should sit down and begin to fish. If you catch a fish, you will gain Fishing XP in CNR.

Once you have fish, you can use them to cook, and for any other CNR recipes they are needed for.

Happy fishing.
A deed for a spell basin
A deed to a bath tub.
This is a deed for a bed. Use it to cause a bed to appear where you are standing. The bed will be facing you when it appears.
This is a deed for a bedroll. Use it to cause a bedroll to appear where you are standing. The bedroll will be facing you when it appears. You may sit on this bedroll.
Beetle Rider Armor- DO Not Loot

A mineral of great hardness, and, when transparent, of much beauty. It occurs in hexagonal prisms, commonly of a green or bluish green color, but also yellow, pink, and white. It is a silicate of aluminum and beryllium.

Corath

Aliases: The Mad God, The Black Sun  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: Humans, half-orcs, orcs, demons
Domains: Death, Evil, Chaos, Trickery
Governs: Death, blood, lust, murder, lies, hatred, deception 

Dogma:
     Corath wants his clerics to spread evil across the lands. The more insanity, the more lies, the more havoc they wreak, the better they will stand in front of his eyes. Wherever a cleric of the Mad God walks, death shall follow their trail. The Mad God also encourages his followers to let their feelings of lust and hatred fuel their existence. Corath teaches that the virulent spread of evil is the goal of his followers' existences; consequently, many worshippers of The Black Sun seek to extend their lives by making pacts to attain undeath.

Clergy Weapon and Clothing:
     Corath's clerics prefer to use a short sword, since it delivers an average amount of damage, is easy to conceal, and is quick to coat with a poison. Normally every follower of the Black Sun also carries a frost-enchanted short sword to represent the coldness of death. 

     Clerics garb themselves in chain armor to stop most piercing and slashing attacks. Their armor is usually night black and blood red and adorned with the skulls and bones of fallen enemies.

Clergy and Temples:
     Being the god of death, some of Corath's temples can be found in well-established societies. In those, Acolytes of the Bones manage graveyard duties. Those temples in the unknown areas are the center of demonic acts of corruption, and the extent of their cruelty is legendary. Acolytes and Masters of the White Skull normally handle the gathering of bodies (recruits) and the high priests (liches), leading them to spread their evil seed. As a whole, though, organization and order is sketchy at best. 

     They celebrate All-Hallow's Eve, the day when all the dead raise from their graves to haunt the living. Corath's clerics pray at midnight to regain their spells.

Prayers Before battle:
     "The blood of my enemies will only sate my thirst when I use their bodies to serve your cause."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Pyrtechon, Baraeon Ca'Duz, Grand 

Friendly: Mist, Xeen, Vierdri'ira 

Neutral: Branderback, Shindaleria, Beryl 

Unfriendly: Ilsare, Shadon, Goran, Deliar, Katia, Aragen, Sulterio, Prunilla 

Enemy: Rofirein, Vorax, Dorand, Aeridin, Toran, Lucinda, Az'atta, Kithairien, Folian S'pae, Grannoch

Cadimus stumbled apon the prime of Layonara by accident. Through his time on Layonara he fought many battles and was known as a great warrior hero, gaining much wealth and power. The only thing he kept from his homeworld was his sword, a double bladed weapon of great sentimental value, as it belonged to his father before him.

Eventually; though, he grew homesick and wished nothing more then to go back to his homeland He decided to learn more of the planes and planar travel, he took onto the arcane. It was when he became a wizard of decent power that his sickness took other forms. Madness, and eventually insanity. In his madness he abandoned the only thing left from his homeland, his sword. It is said though that a peice of him, the only part left sane, that is good remains in the sword.

In the rise of his madness he became old and desperate. He began to think that this would be the world he would die in and he would never see his home again. In his desperation he found a ritual. With the sacrifice of countless children he could prolong his life, by using all their skin as a new vessel for his soul. The vessel would prove indestructable but stationary, but his soul could travel freely taking body after body, with great ability to possess. You kill the body hes in and the soul will just take another, it seemed he was unstoppable and his madness was only getting worse, becoming obsessed with gore and death.

But rumor says that not all his soul was used for the ritual, and that part of it remains in his very sword. It is thus believed that only his old sword can be used to defeat him but its been long since the sword was found. Because of this rumor it is also beleived the sword itself is possessed and choses its possessor, the one to defeat its evil, harming those it denies and will take the form of its chosens prefered weapon.

Rumor now flies that the sword is claimed...
A deed for a set of bolts of cloth.

Although the followers of Pyrtechon generally do not favor a specific weapon, many often use ranged weapons imbued with fire when facing their enemies. These bolts are tipped with heads shaped from a strange reddish brown metal set upon a shaft of darkened bone with black fletching.

It is rumored that this metal, said to be a gift of the Dragon God Pyrtechon himself, was first discovered washed down a small stream on Firesteep after an erruption that occured while a cleric of Pyrtechon performed his prayer ritual at sunset when The Eternal Flame was prominent in the orange sky.

The tips of the bolt magically return to their molten state as they speed through the air toward the archer's target burning their victims with The Destroyer's Breath.
Bolts or quarrels are the standard ammunition for all types of crossbows, varying in function depending on the shape of the head.
A deed for the boney remains of some poor creature.

Vorax, the dwarven lord of battle, lives in a great hall beneath the mountains. He is surrounded by the souls of great warriors, a mighty host at his command. There is a great table in the mountain hall, and continous feasting. The warriors that feast with Vorax often put on martial demonstrations to amuse their lord and the others. 

Vorax himself is a well-built old dwarf, with an immaculate white beard. His scintillating silver and red plate mail is perhaps the greatest armor ever made, a gift from his cousin Dorand. Vorax's battle axe and shield are often bourne by handmaidens that dote upon him. The legends tell tales of Vorax sending his axe or his shield to the realm of mortals where the mere presence of such an item often boosts morale enough to win the day. Vorax's helm is also an artifact of great power, but it was a gift from his brother Sulterio from before their fallout, and Vorax is loathe to wear it unless the need is dire. The helm is often locked away with Vorax's horde until it is needed. 

As the All-father of dwarfs, Vorax is wise and compassionate. He is a champion of justice and good. He is a protector of the dwarven people, and a preserver of the dwarven way of life. His strategy and martial ability are second to none. Vorax preaches honor in battle, through strength of limb and courage of heart. It is dishonorable to slaughter the weak, or slay foes who have surrendered. Though Vorax's enemies are often dishonorable, Vorax's followers must stay honorable throughout, and have faith that virtue will win the day. As such, Vorax and his followers frown upon magic users. Magic is deemed an unfair advantage, a true warrior has no need to rely on external power to defeat their enemies. Magic users themselves are often frail, in a true fight they would perish quickly, but their magic changes the outcome to something unnatural.
