A deed for a pile of books.

This is a deed for bookshelves. Use it to cause bookshelves to appear where you are standing. The bookshelves will be facing you when they appear. They may be locked or unlocked with the Furniture Tool.
These boots are created by the T'oleflor for protection of those that defend the realm. They are made from the Silver Veign Plant.
A bouquet of purple, red and blue roses.
This bow has been created by the T'oleflor and the Silver Veign has added a heightened attack bonus to this weapon.

These bracers gleam red as the light reflects off them.  Born from the scales of dragon younglings fresh from their eggs, these bracers are much sought after by both dragons and common beings alike.  The reasons for each kind's search is quite different obviously.

The scales themself sparkle with a faint magic, magic that never saw the full glory of even adolescence.  The scales are bound by cobalt and adamantium, the backside of the bracers are covered with a fine padded silk as to make them quite comfortable on the wearer's wrists.
A small bush radiating an aura that seems to signify some bond.
A small sapling radiating an aura that seems to signify some bond.

These scales were rumoured to have been gifted by Fezrekthania when the order served her in her life. As tokens of servitude they were imbued by the power of the Wyrm. Now gone, they simply act as memories of a different time.
A lantern is an enclosed flame - making it more resistant to windy conditions than a torch or candle.

This is a deed for a candelabra. Use it to cause a candelabra to appear where you are standing. The candelabra will be facing you when it appears. You may click on the candelabra to turn it off or back on.

This bag contains all your loose creature cards.  When speaking to the card owner, they'll look to buy and sell cards from this bag.  Any cards you win from an ante will go to into this bag.

It's also magically bound to you, which is a hassle when trying to take a bath.
This is the carapace of the queen of the beetle nest in the foundations below Center.
This strange looking herbal brew smells quite pleasant, though it is difficult to say what is in it. It looks to have about five sips worth of liquid within the attractive glass bottle.
This is Ezekial's lantern. He must have lost it in the catacombs under Center. Perhaps you should return it to him.
The head of this strange creature is covered in scales. Those might even be gills by its severed neck, but it is hard to tell.

This charm, made by a gypsy, is made of a number of feathers bound together with silken thread. While the charm as a whole has its own magic, feathers can be pulled off and used in other ways as well ... though if one were to continue doing this, the charm would quickly fall apart.
This is a deed for a catapult. Use it to cause a catapult to appear where you are standing. The catapult will be facing you when it appears.
Another fine piece of craftmenship from the Master Smith Elmerius Dakhar.
Chain Shirt Solid Purple 3 with cloak
This is a deed for a chair. Use it to cause a chair to appear where you are standing. The chair will be facing you when it appears. You may sit in the chair.
This is a deed for a chest. Use it to cause a chest to appear where you are standing. The chest will be facing you when it appears. The chest may be locked or unlocked with the Furniture Tool.

The origin of these boots is unknown.  What tribe of men found a shaman to imbue them with their strange powers is a mystery, though it is clear by the shape of the boots that it was either half-orcs, humans, or something of that general size.

The actual leather of these boots has stone sewn and pressed in with no apparent pattern.  Extremely heavy for a pair of boots, the obvious detriment of wearing them is that they are harder to lift and move around, and generally clink together as one moves.

The enchantment appears to lie in the stone of the boots, as whatever devious shaman created these also allowed the wearer to evoke the protective magic of the stones around them for short durations.  Additionally, those wearing the boots have always felt hardier, healthier, and as strong as the stone itself.
Extremely heavy boots, they look to have chunks of strange rock sewn into them.

Generally considered to be constructed from the skin torn from a demon, the Rags of Rage are a curious design from a tailor's standpoint.  The actual construction does nothing to aid in armoring oneself, one may even contend that the devious design is instead permissive of attacks on the individual wearing it.  That said, the strange quality of this hide absorbs blows through clever overlapping of material in a rather intricate weave.

The hide strangely burns the skin of all but the most hardy individuals, and for this reason it is assumed that it is derived from some creature of a negative energy reality.  Wearers of the strange hide have also told tales of the hide becoming part of their skin, as though living through their flesh somehow.  This rather morbid thought is typically negated by the same individuals saying that they feel stronger, hardier, and more adaptable to the lands around them.

Several suits of this armor are thought to exist throughout the lands.
A barbaric looking set of armor.

This rather ingenious shortbow was clearly crafted by a follower of Shadon as the emblem of this deity is etched into the handle of the bow.

The ingenuity of this crafty little bow comes in two fashions.  First, at the top end of the bow a masterkey has been fashioned with a series of retractable lockpicks and other various size ranges of picks and gadgets for use in finding the softer spots of locks and traps.  But more impressive then this is the fact that the bow is actually trapped.  At the bottom the core of an electrical trap has been intricately designed with a bow string attached to the trap's core so that a surge of electricity will course through the string just as it's released and fly towards the target.  The trap itself is clearly enchanted in some fashion beyond mere tinkering and design, as it glows a shade of blue and purple and sparks now and then with powers surpassing a simple gnomish tinkerer.

It is clear this bow has a tendency to kill those unskilled however, as numerous bloodstains are found on the bow itself, most likely from both battle and error in the function of the trapping bow.

// GM NOTE: The arrows produced from this bow are for the sole use of the bow's owner and are not to be traded or sold under any circumstances.
A curious metal protrusion comes off the top end of this bow... it almost looks like a key.  At the bottom end of the bow the string is wound around what seems to be a trap of some sort.

This chunk of ore is imbued with the protective magics typical of olden dwarven clans.  Built by dwarves golems  made of ore such as this were enchanted prior to completion so that their protective mithril coating would be resistant to all elemental attacks, and thus resist both attacks and the depreciation to time.
A strangely bright chunk of ore.

These amulets, produced in mass quantity by a gnomish tinkerer by the name of Hriligril, were probably created in an effort for either Stone or Bloody Gate during the dark ages of Layonara.  They were reported lost during a shipment across Dregar intended to be sailed to Katherian.
A glimmering amulet with the initials HGL hanging off the neck of the chain.
Light as a feather, this finely crafted bow's strings are quite warm to the touch.

Curious boots, these were produced by elvish rangers around the time of Folian's rise as a deity of the lands.  In reverence to their god, these boots were initially worn with only a minor enchantment allowing deft movement about the woodland regions.  But in time, as the rangers proved their faith to Folian in their practice as diligant rangers of the lands, Folian allowed a blessing to be achieved within the soles of these boots.

As history tells it, the actual bootmaker of these had hardened the leather near the sole, which was initially frowned upon by the other rangers of their vale as it would be noisy on the leaves of the forest.  But the bootmaker retorted, saying that the true ranger of Folian would be able to connect with the very breaths of the land, it's movements, and the movements of all things around him.  He said that the blessing and enchantment that he'd provided these simple boots would feel the very vibration of the lands and everything in them.  He claimed that the appearance of the land would change, that the true ranger would see all around him in a new light, in full connection with the lands.  He also claimed that this ability would render them quicker on their feet, more capable of reaction and perhaps even foresight to those actions around them.

For many years, his boots did no such thing other then make increased noise in the woodlands.  But the rangers held true to their faith, and it is of course part of the legend, that it was indeed Folian who eventually saw it fit to bless these boots.
A pair of old leather boots with a symbol of a wolf etched in to the sole.

A strange helmet.  It looks to have fit a dwarf at one time.  The ores in this helm are clearly of mithril origin, though the manner in which it has been crafted lends to great curiousity regarding its origin.  Runes glimmer all about the magnificent helm, whilst dwarven scripture circle the inside of the helmet.

The Preacher's Tower dates back to the year 149 during the race wars of Elves and Humans.  Constructed by holy men of the human armies, an almost fanatical following rallied during these ages under the banner of human dieties.  The shields themselves were constructed for heavy warfare, with no consideration as to the training of the holy warriors, it instead relied on the logic of creating a barrier amongst hundreds of warriors that could advance on the elven warriors using the tactic of pikes through eyelets of the shield's side.  It proved quite effective against the far more agile elven warriors and ultimately, tactics such as these, inventions such as these, and sheer numbers in the face of older, wiser, and more adept armies prevailed.

The enchantments on this shield are minimal, save for a consecration of faith for the holy warriors who wield it.  The majority of it's qualities derive from it's sheer size, which makes it difficult to manuever in battle.

Interestingly enough, these types of shields all but vanished from the human trade, and prior to the boycott of all human products in 229, the dwarven clans acquired the majority of these shields as fine additions to their general defenses.

Hoods such as these are despised amongst the ranks of mages, notably the Black Mages.  Created for the sole purpose of pemitting the assassinations of mages across the realms with greater ease and safety, only the most reckless, or reclusive, of black markets will openly sell such an item as this.

Leaves glimmer with autumn color on this belt of a curious red leather.  Holding it in your hand, it's colors and very nature provide a warmth to the environment around you.

Who made these beautifully simple belts is unknown, though the two slender eyes carved into the belt's underside betray any condition of anonymity.

It is believed by scholars who have studied these belts that they were created by a follower of Katia to imbue the wearer with a natural sense of direction and balance in the lands around them.  It is known that the blessing of this belt renders the bearer hardier, and more resistant to all energies unnatural.  It is assumed that these were created to be worn by the clerics of Katia.

True followers of Katia often know better however...
A red wrap of a belt, it seems simple yet beautiful in it's design.

Modelled after Beryl's constellation in the sky, seven sparkling emeralds glimmer with a deep and strange purple glow that shimmers and circles around in almost an illusory glow.  Four larger emeralds shine brightly in the center of the other seven.

This type of belt is rare and even more rare to be seen on any race that is not Deep Gnome.  They are granted sometimes as gifts to those races and followers of dieties that find peace with the Deep Gnomes, though this is exceedingly uncommon given the distrustful nature of the Deep Gnomes.

The belts are more often worn by clerics of Beryl, and granted only by the Diamond of Beryl.  Most cases of these rare and beautiful creations being found in other places can most likely be explained as unfortunate deaths by the previous bearer.

The magic of the belt is well known to the Deep Gnomes.  Hunted for ages, these belts serve as magical protection against the oppression of the dark elves of the deep.  Enchanted to defend against the attacks of dark elf assassins or weavespinners, it turns both blade and imprisonment in an eternal resistance against slavers.  The belt itself is magnificent, and is usually worn on the outside of one's clothing.  The beauty of the constellation of emeralds instills a great natural power in the wearer.

The belt itself is a small mithril wrap, which does not flex.  A clasp lies in the back of the belt where it can be fastened around it's wearer.

It is likely that any dark elf, dark dwarf, or aberration of the Deep that attempted to wear this belt would be destroyed by it's magics in any ordinary instance.
A magnificent looking belt, it has 7 emeralds encircling 4 larger emeralds in the center.

Notes:  Legend of Iliarial

By Hadrian Quillsong


In my days of research, I have come across a legend most intriguing.  The validity of it I have sought to test, far and wide.  Of it's truth, I've found little backing.  It remains, however, one of the more interesting, though elusive, tales I've researched.

Tattered parchments that for all I may know may be the figment of a bard's imagination put on paper, tell of a line of kings who bore the name Iliarial.  These parchments were brought to me by a fellow scholar of ancient peoples, and though I am curious to what is written, I was not impressed by their condition.  What I did note was that the parchment used was a strange variant of paper from a yew tree, which is quite rare to begin with and generally not wasted on trifle tales.  The condition of the parchment was pitiful however, and knowing the lasting nature of paper made from yew, it would seem that these texts are quite ancient indeed.

The apparent writer was seeking out some ruins, his purpose for doing so quite obvious... to loot them.  From what I have made out from his text, written in a curious mixture of the Elvish and T'oleflor languages, these ruins were of a kingdom ruled by men, with the surname of Iliarial.  I have not been able to determine where he indicated these ruins were, though vague references seem to cancel out the possibility of Mistone or the greater Dregar continents.  The Ruins of Iliarial seem to have held some allure to this adventurer of old, passages I've translated such as the following indicate adequate optimism:

"Statues of rubies, shields of emeralds, cloths sewn from diamonds... hold for me Iliarials Tomb will."

Or:

"Found the key I have, or found the key has me.  The key the key, the key to loosening the ancient blades."

Various mentions of treasures pour out in the little readable text I have.  And for an apparent rogue such as our writer, the allure is clear.  The old names for mithril and titanium are used, and some mention of magical silver is made several times, though the translation is difficult on these topics.  Needless to say, our writer felt that this kingdom of men had quite a command over their crafts, in particular magical imbuing if I've read correctly.  The magical nature of this culture is made clear in several passages:

"Never seen metals of golems I have seen..."

Or:

"Statues live or dead neither have been, wandering the hallways where I have hidden..."

The latter passage is interesting to note, as it implies the rogue adventurer did indeed see these ruins, and perhaps walk their halls if any still stand.  In my research this has confused me the most, as the writer implied the only access to these ruins was a magical password.  In one section he suggests he has discovered the password, and much to my lamentations this section has been oddly burned from its page.  However, multiple mentions of passwords fill these pages, and they hold a notable theme.  See here phrases used repeatedly, and sometimes even with reference to a password:

"Virtue and Justice"
"Golden on thy Skin"
"Wisdom beget Knowledge"
"Hraykirlar of Lihariax"  Note: This latter word appears unfinished in the scripts.
"Reverence and Honor"
"Debasement of Evil"
"The Broken Blade"

There may in fact be several more passwords, though these phrases seem indicative.  My confusion on this subject arises on the validity of this writer even seeing the ruins.  As mentioned, he claims to have seen these treasures and magical apparatus.  He claims to have seen many things, which I will proceed onto shortly.  But the problem with these claims comes in the introductory passage:

"If to never again be seen may I be, then leave these pages for you I will.  And if to be doomed I am, then under the first treasured gem will again you see me.  I go now to the floatingman's tree, for my password I think will to he bring me...."

The remainder of this passage has withered over time, and I have been unable to finish the last sentence nor the obviously positioned password underneath this farewell.  Regardless, it becomes a contradiction with other passages describing the ruins in full, since this text begins as a departing tale.  The plausibility therefore of Iliarial's Ruins is fully in question based on this fact.

But still I seek it out.  The single most disturbing passages have been quite difficult to translate, but there seems to be a motif of what can be best described as light becoming darkness.  Whether this is literal or figurative, the wording is not descriptive enough to say for certain.  However, there is clear reference to demons several times in the text.  Once again these references appear to have been written in hindsight.  There is no rhyme or reason to this reference, though light to darkness, and either fire to ice or ice to fire, is mentioned several times in conjunction with demonic parallels.  For this reason I believe there is a figurative expression herein.  Especially when coupled with the probable passwords which indicate what can best be described as Toranite, Voraxian, or perhaps even Rofireinite sentiments.  The possible age of this parchment begs questions as to what gods were even in power at the time, however that is not our focus.  These ruins, or the tale of them, appear to contain a fallen grace theme, which becomes quite colorful at times.  I shall continue to seek the truth on this matter out, but for now I have recorded this for the benefit of other researchers that might know something of the names or implied histories within these texts.

One last note regarding the possibility of a password or other such code to enter these ruins, again if they should in fact have an entrance.  On every page of the rogue adventurer's parchments there lay a strange symbol in the center of each page.  I do not understand the nature of this symbol as it is quite foreign to anything I've seen before.  However, should it be required to fashion something with this symbol to fit a keylock perhaps, or simply to recognize it as some key to a puzzle... I am tracing it on the following page to make sure anyone who does go out in search of these ruins has this symbol in front of them to decipher.  Should this symbol be integral to entrance, or escape for that matter, of these ruins, it is my recommendation that all who seek out the Ruins of Iliarial bring a copy of this symbol as I have taken great care to trace it in its full detail in this tome.

Krisial's Armor was an honorary suit of the lightest leathers known by the tailors of Krisial's people.  Krisial himself was a proud warrior defending the people surrounding the lands of Alibor at around the time that the lands withered and the River of Death emerged in place of the once lush and beautiful lands of those islands.

History tells that Krisial shunned the usage of any heavy armor, and was revered as one of the greatest warrios ever known in the region.  This is mostly in part due to the fact that he alone had proven it possible to combat the more typical heavily armored warriors of other lands in just his basic clothing.

It would happen some time late in his life that the greatest tailors and enchanters of Alibor would work with Krisial to develop a suit of armor suitable for the warriors of his ilk.  This wonderful suit of padded silk is the result.  Lightweight and flowing gently over the skin, it allows for an incredibly natural and flowing movement for warriors that pursue the purest means of their arts in battle.  The magics of the padded silks allow for some degree of resiliance to incoming blows, though the focus is clearly on the ideal of deft movement of agile warriors.
This armor is extremely light weight, and  the dyes used on it are a brilliantly contrasting deep red and jet black.  Whoever wore this armor was clearly an epic warrior in his day.

Klinkutter Hogsbreath, the gnomish mage of the swamplands who ultimately fell to his own madness.  This strange creation is imbued with some of Klinkutter's chaos magics, though it retains a quality very different then most of the mad mage's creations.

The Song of Chaos was designed in mind for the bardic magi, who Klinkutter had become quite enraptured by in his later days.  For what reason or by what emotions this occurred, none can say.  Though it is clear by several of Klinkutter's creations late in his life that his desire for a bardic companion was immensely strong.  He imbued this shield with the powers of his chaos magic in a strange fashion.  The shield itself hums with the buzz of chaos magic, but in this buzzing there is strange harmony.  Typically only individuals in tune with the chaos of the lands around them are capable of hearing the strange beauty of it's song, and are capable of finding the tune by which to compliment it's power.
This shield randomly shocks, burns, or otherwise stings you as you hold it.  It appears... tempermental.

Jorel, a ranger from the far northern reaches of Krashin. A man of honor, he held a great hatred for all aspects of the dark arts. The reasons behind his deep hatred sprung from a fountain lost in history, but it is known that his mission throughout life would bring a reckless doom onto all magic users.

Throughout his life, Jorel made the mistake of entrusting a gnomish mage to smith and enchant weapons, armors, and other creations of antimagery. At first Jorel would be applauded for his efforts in destroying necromancers throughout the lands. But in his ignorance and arrogance, his goals shifted towards darkness themselves, as he began to slay all things magic, good and evil alike.

The gnomish mage, still in his youth, was named Klinkutter Hogsbreath. An honorable young gnome with a bright future in tinkering and magic alike, Klinkutter began aiding Jorel with the purest of intentions. As Jorel began his blind crusade however, Klinkutter reluctantly sought to somehow cease the madness by enchanting these creations. So one day he imbued them all with the ability for only a truly good being to wield them. He merely sought to teach his dear friend Jorel a lesson in what it was he was doing. Jorel, however, rushed foolishly into battle that evening, only to find the weapons burn in his hands, his cloak withering from his shoulders. He fell dead that night to the mages he had rushed upon, feebly charging with his fists alone.

Klinkutter fell to insanity after hearing the news, unable to distinguish his mistake in the hard lesson he had ultimately failed to teach. He withdrew to the swamplands of Belinara, never to be seen again.

This cloak is one of many of Klinkutter's creations for Jorel.  It's threads are powerfully imbued with a resiliance to all things magic, as well as regenerative qualities and magics of hardiness.  The nature of the strange threads of this cloak make it mostly transparent.
A heavy cloak with broad shoulders.  It is clearly made for the most stout of warriors.

The Fiendish String, a terrible device constructed with the woven hairs of shadow beasts from a negative reality unlike your own.

The bow itself is of a strange wood foreign to your lands.  It is as though it exists only as a shadow of your world, a dark shadow draining to all things around it.

The string bears the most magical presence and force of the bow.  It is draining to the touch, and incredibly difficult to pull upon.  The power of the string unleashed however, is a sight to behold.  For as it whips forward projectiles of immense force and strength scream forth towards it's target, wailing their distant death cry as they whistle through the air.

// GM NOTE: The arrows produced from this bow are for the sole use of the bow's owner and are not to be traded or sold under any circumstances.
An evil aura surrounds this dark bow.

The magics in this ring are quite astounding, and it is doubtful that anyone other then the most powerful of enchanters created this relic of power.

The ring itself appears to be a strangely enchanted ring of fortitude.  Dwarvish runes encircle the beautiful ring, they appear to hold magics warding off death or other evil blights.
A wonderfully beautiful golden ring.  Holding it in your hand you are quite taken with it's intricate detail.

The truth to the demise of this clan of dwarves is lost to time, though this wondrous shield does hold some clues.

A mithril mold, runes warding magic and death cover the entire face of the shield.  The artistry of the runes is without match, and various gems have been set in the mithril.

Best known as the Lost Clan shield, it is such due to the fact that there is no reported history of the clan that built the wondrous mazes and halls beneath the Thunder Peaks.  The runes however, do uncover some truth.  The writing on the shield is mostly of magical defense, but some is written in the plain dwarven tongue, especially that which is carefully etched around the outer ring of it.

"Our halls he shall never see, for our honor shall survive the thunder of his storm.  Our stone he shall never touch, for our defenders wield the magic of our mountain.  Lost in our maze he shall be, and steadfast behind this shield he shall fall under our mighty hammers."

The inference to the storm and thunder clearly represents the battle with the giants of Essrantor's Veil.  It is interesting, in the domain of antimagic, that the shield is so well imbued to defend against it.  The truth to the demise of this obviously proud and honorable clan may forever be lost to time.

How this shield came into your possession is a mystery indeed, though its roots lie deep within the Thunder Peaks.

But the shield of the lost clan survives.
A shield apparently of dwarvish design, it has several runes etched into the what seems to be a shield of mithril.

This wondrous creation was created by Haggris Oreheart of the Runic Anvil some time ago.  In a tribute to Vorax, each axe of this type is said to go through a trial of worth.  It begins as a simple adamantium waraxe, without a single enchantment on it's edge.

Haggris deemed it without worth if the axe was not put to test, and he found the idea of magics degrading of such a magnificent tool of war.

The trial itself involves 10 years of hunting only the enemies of Vorax.  It is said that if any creature is slain that is not the enemy of Vorax, the axe will shatter during the trial of blessing.  Haggris created many of these axes, blessed simply with the name of Vorax on their edge at their beginning, though wonderfully crafted indeed.  At the trial of blessing the axe stands before the alter of Vorax, and Haggris was said to provide the final test for each one in existance.  This final blessing would prompt Vorax's judgement, and it is said that many an axe shattered upon the stone floor of the Runic Anvil in disgrace.  Though many still exist, passing the trial and recieving the final blessing, a blessing that pays homage to the user's worth.

The edge of this axe has been enchanted with a sonic vibration that lets out a clang when striking an opponent that befuddles the ears of anyone struck by it, making speaking and casting of spells difficult to impossible for a short time.

These axes have held a long tradition of construction by several of the dwarven clans in an effort to combat evil magic users, especially necromantic using ones.

The edge of this axe has been enchanted with a sonic vibration that lets out a clang when striking an opponent that befuddles the ears of anyone struck by it, making speaking and casting of spells difficult to impossible for a short time.

These axes have held a long tradition of construction by several of the dwarven clans in an effort to combat evil magic users, especially necromantic using ones.  This axe in particular has been blessed by priests of Vorax to strike down upon evil foes.
Greater Dwarven Waraxe of the Antimagi

The defender's helm was originally created by the dwarves of the Runic Anvil Clan.  This helm uses both magic and well designed eyeslits to enhance the watchful eye of the defender.  Additionally, the ears of the helm are actually deep channelling tubes of ore that enable enhanced acuity of hearing.

The major benefit to this helm however, is the protective runes warding off the evils of negative energy.

The dwarvish helm of the berserker, it is prided for the enabling of many a battlerager to charge their foes both fearsome and unfearful.  Most of the magics of this helmet are based on runes evoking ferocity within the individual wearing it.

A prided helm amongst the warriors of the Runic Anvil Clan, it is said the first lord of the clan crafted the first helmet of this kind.  The helm itself is imbued with simple protective runes no more powerful then a novice mage's defenses, but the artwork and crafting of the intricate scriptures surrounding the eye slits is quite impressive.

The heavy plate often used by guardians of the Runic Anvil Clan.

The armor itself is not spectacular in many ways.  It is made of a variant of copper and iron, but the fashioning of the joints and the extremely thick plate used in almost every armored region is quite profound.

Weighing quite a bit more then normal full plate, this armor is welded at every joint to prevent entry of slashing weapons or piercing blows from ranged weapons.

This has the unfortunate side effect of causing all but the most stout to become effectively immobile.

The Lichbane Mace.  In it's simplicity it earns great respect amongst all living beings opposed to undeath and necromancy.  The make of these maces are said to have derived from The Shining Hand of Toran sometime around the 5th century following the cataclysm.  These weapons were distributed amongst the Order of Undead Hunters at that time, though in recent ages the making of such weapons seems a lost art.

The weapon is quite simple and quite plain despite it's powerful enchantments.  The metals and ores used are simple and unimpressive, though the rough edges glimmer with a magic and divine energy crackling within.  One lone mithril ring of ore circles the mace at it's midline, and a gold star made of a tiny topaz shines alone, centered on that ring.

A powerful tool of magic, this scale was ripped from the corpse of an ancient blue dragon.  The powers of this scale are strange, though most magic using individuals can quickly harness the powers intrinsic of them without difficulty.

This particular scale seems to hold the natural powers of the dragon to resist magical attacks.

A powerful tool of magic, this scale was ripped from the corpse of an ancient black dragon.  The powers of this scale are strange, though most magic using individuals can quickly harness the powers intrinsic of them without difficulty.

This particular scale seems to hold the natural powers of the dragon's fortitude.

A powerful tool of magic, this scale was ripped from the corpse of an ancient red dragon.  The powers of this scale are strange, though most magic using individuals can quickly harness the powers intrinsic of them without difficulty.

This particular scale seems to hold the natural fire of the dragon's soul.

A powerful tool of magic, this scale was ripped from the corpse of an ancient shadow dragon.  The powers of this scale are strange, though most magic using individuals can quickly harness the powers intrinsic of them without difficulty.

This particular scale seems to hold the natural powers of the shadows around you.
A strange purplish-black scale, it has an ethereal appearanc almost.

Styrbjorn Kitleatin fashioned these boots with the help of gnomish mages at the height of his wanderings.

The common name for these boots "Styrbjorn's Boots of Fleetness" describes the boots well, though they are often also referred to as "Styrbjorn's Curse of Fleetness", "Styrbjorn's Flighty Boon", and "Styrbjorn's Boots of the Distant Mind".

These boots are both loved and hated by those who wear them.  The tale tells that Styrbjorn was a dwarven outcast, who had deserted his clan early in his youth to wander and experience the lands that were always distant in his mind.  He was known to have always maintained his eyes on the horizon, insofar as to never maintain his attention on any conversation or matter that was directly at hand and in front of him.

During his wanderings, Styrbjorn befriended a group of Goranite gnomes.  The assumptions made in the tales surrounding these boots is that the gnomes, so creative and so wild in every project they worked on managed to maintain Styrbjorn's interest and prompt the discussion of his old boots.

Styrbjorn was fascinated by the wonders of the items and creations of the gnomes, and begged of them to work with him on creating boots for wanderers that would ever keep them able in their wanderings, never slow them, and never distract their mind from the horizons of wonder beyond.  The gnomes took this ideal, word for word, and set off to create boots that would achieve this goal.  They enchanted the boots with the ability to move freely through the lands, and provided each pair with an inset diamond enchanted with the power to provide them the fortitude and constitution to carry on in their travels.

But with his wishes clearly expressed, they also imbued their boots with a special enchantment.  This enchantment lightened the mind of the wearer, and gave them a sense of fogginess in their immediate surroundings.  The wearers of these boots found themselves less apt to concentrate on their immediate surroundings, or listen to the conversations of those surrounding them.  It made them flighty, distant, and apathetic towards anything but the unknown still beyond.

Many a creature has found their feet inside these boots.  Many have found themselves soon a vagrant traveller, wandering the lands, ever distant and yearning of exploration.  Without a single true to their name, barely surviving and never settling in one place too long, these travellers became what many regarded as 'cursed by the touch of Styrbjorn's Fleetness'.

Many though have found these boot's magics well within their capability to manage.  And while their eyes often cloud in the face of a beautiful sun rising over some distance they've never been, their inherent abilities in concentrating on the world around them finds itself in a happy medium with Styrbjorn's wanderlust.

Klinkutter Hogsbreath, the gnomish mage of the swamplands who ultimately fell to his own madness.  This strange creation is curiously made in a fashion which takes safety into consideration, a trait quite rare in the relics of this mad mage.

It is told that the gnomish magician began creating these staves early in his life, which would explain the less chaotic nature of it's make.  At it's tip lies a massive chunk of sapphire gem.  Klinkuter seems to have carefully enchanced the magical qualities of this large deposit of untouched crystal in order to imbue the holder with some of it's inherent resistances.

The actual base of the staff is split between ore and wooden handles.  Two adamantium segments have been split by a well designed yew handle.  While the weight of this staff is often awkward for most spinners of the weave, the handle seems perfectly placed for balance, insofar as to allow a small being such as even a halfling to find balance in it's movement.  Two diamonds lie inset at the top and bottom of the yew handle, and it is apparent that they have been enchanted with particular spells to supply the holder with elements of fortitude and will.
A large sapphire clings to the tip of this staff.  It's base feels warm to the touch.

This peculiar staff is made of two parts.  The base of the staff appears to be mahogany, while the tip of the staff is some sort of fashioned ivory tusk.  From what creature it came, not even the wisest of druids can discern.  The ivory is smoothed and very obviously enchanted with the weave.

These staves are said to derive from the northern isles of Krashin, though remarkably similar staves of identical construction show signs of origin in the southern hemisphere of Layonara as well.  The supposed origin of the Krashin isles indicates the enchantment by barbaric seers and wisemen that practiced both arcane and divine magics as the witchdoctors of their people.  The runes displayed on the mahogany portion of the staff are a mixture of arcane and divine expressions of magic, though the divine expressions are entirely linked to the natural world in the fashion a druid would find power in.

These staves are old, though not overly uncommon amongst the well travelled of the lands.  Their magic is rumored to bring good tidings to the natural world, and any wielder of this staff will find flow with both the weave and the land as he travels.
A rune circled wooden staff with an ivory tusk on the end.

*The text appears to be a rubbing from the original.  A glowing gem is found inset inside the bound leather cover that shines a brilliant yellow.*

On Dorand's Hammer what I declare that what I write is true.

I, Dalliac, servant of Dorand, braced myself against the Curse of Firelight Tower and sought to enter it and uncover its mystery of many years.

Fellisax, our scout, found a strange groove in the solid stone and that was all we needed to understand that we had found the path to the tower. The climb was nothing a stout dwarf couldn't handle, even with a heavy burden on his back. I was struck at the ability of the stone cutters that wrought the steps - a staircase invisible in the mountain to all except those that know what to look for, The Master of Crafts must have been proud of his son's work.

We reached the lower entrance to the tower, a stone door tightly shut that granted us entrance upon being pressed in the right spots - another sign of the fine ability on our ancients. Smooth as the finest glass was the surface despite years of water and wind daring break on its surface. The three of us entered the tower and sealed ourselves in from the bitter wind outside.

The air was calm but not still, a cool breeze, much slower than the gale that blew outside, greeted us. The floors were with a thin layer of dust, much less than we expected, as though only a few weeks of sweeping had been missed. Along the walls, several stone hooks were set for equipment and Jaellax, our strongest arm, absentmindedly placed his pack on one of them and called out for mead. I spat out my disapproval of such wanton disrespect for the mystery to which he responded, "I feel as though there are still brothers here."

That was also the feeling that I had, along with Fellisax. The place was in excellent conditions and further exploration of the barracks, mess hall and observation deck held the strong feeling that the guard had just stepped out for a smoke and would be back soon. We found salted meats, cheese, water and firewood - all frozen but still serviceable after defrosting them. Barrels of ale, wine and rolls of smoke weed neatly stashed and also usable - the ale didn't age well but the wine did, a bottle of it lies on my table.

I searched and found the tower's register and the commander's log for signs of its being abandoned but found none, it was as though Dorand and Vorax themselves whisked the guard away into thin air for some secret purpose.

It was in the lower basement, within the mountain, that the mystery that had been taunting us was solved. A stone door, crudely cut - definitely not by kinsman's hands, not by those that had built the tower, was found ajar. Jaellax's curse and wards were heard echoing in all the tower for what he saw. In that room, probably a crude cavern that had been enlarged, the frozen and decayed bodies of twenty five was found but only twenty two of them were of our kin, the others were of elves, dark ones for their hair was white and the remaining skin was coal black.

From what we guess, the elves had stolen the guards and killed them in that room for reasons unknown. After eliminating the guard, they simply withdrew through a door set in the back of the cavern without taking a thing nor any of the fine weapons and armor. On close inspection, Fellisax declared that he could not and would not even try to open the drow door for it was, according to him, rigged with the deadliest of traps so we let it be as we recovered the bodies of our fallen and gave them a proper burial and sealed the cavern for good after leaving a few traps of our own for the dark elves.

We left a few days later and until this day we cannot understand what the purpose of the massacre was.

On Dorand's Hammer what I declare that what I wrote is true.
A simple book with dwarven initials on the outer cover.

Constructed by the dwarves of the K'halziras Clan of the Great Spikes, this fine set of armor combines cobalt scales with mithril chain.  The resulting masterpeice of dwarven construction is extraordinarily resistant to peircing attacks, as well as permitting great mobility in the joints.

It is said that a K'halziras Defender would pass their rite of clanhome with the descent into the Caverns of the Menace with naught but a skinning knife, their blade, and this armor for three moonless moons before attaining their status as a defender of K'halziras's gates to the Great Spikes.

Another superb example of the craftsmanship of the K'halziras clan of dwarves.  This maul was used by a particular segment of the K'halziras clan defenders, the North Pass Wardens.  The North Pass of K'halziras leads into the Deep, and is known for it's magnificently crafted gates which require a special password to cross.  Nevertheless, the North Pass marked the greatest territory of threat, and the Wardens were highly regarded amongst the clan.

A maul such as this was granted to a Warden during the early stages of their training.  The maul itself was both for offense and defense, and of the latter were the warden's most concerned.  The defenses of the clanhome were most focused to the North Gate, and their soul enemy was always the Azure Menace of the deep pools below.  History knows little of this Azure Menace, though it is said that it would somehow curse the dwarves and the barbarian allies who lived amongst the clan to a lifeless servitude in the depths of the pools.

The length of the maul seemed historically important in this respect, though the reasoning for this is still unknown.  Suggestions have been made that the foe of the K'halziras was such that proximity was the true danger, though this is only speculation.  The maul is extremely large for a dwarf, and it is said the Warden's training circled around this weapon especially.

A beautiful blade lies before you.  From whence it came is obvious in the inscription and the gold gem that interestingly catches it's reflection only when facing north.

Inscribed in immensely intricate detail the following circles the blade itself.

* Thou shalt believe all that Rofirein teaches, and shalt observe all his directions.

Thou shalt defend the Church of Rofirein with all thy might.

Thou shalt respect all weaknesses, and shalt constitute thyself the defender of them.

Thou shalt not recoil before thine enemy.

Thou shalt make war against the Infidel followers of Pyrtechon without cessation and without mercy.

Thou shalt perform scrupulously thy duties of Justice, in line with the Teachings of the Church of Rofirein.

Thou shalt never lie, and shall remain faithful to thy pledged word.

Thou shalt be generous, and give largess to all that have need.

Thou shalt avoid avarice like the deadly pestilence and shalt embrace its opposite.

Thou shalt keep thyself chaste for the sake of her whom Rofirein has chosen for thee to love.

Thou shalt only step foot in Temples dedicated to Rofirein and his Holy allies, unless thy enemies seek sanctuary in an unholy temple, in which case it is thy duty to cleanse the place of their filth.

Thou art a Paladin of Rofirein, one of his beloved few. Remember this in all that thy do. As one of the few Paladins of the Holy Order of Rofirein, it is your task to root out evil, injustice and tyranny wherever thee may be.

A fragment melded into the evil the now controls it - this is an abomination of Iliarial's Helm, the helm held to the heir of the great line of kings bearing it's name.  The magics imbued in this helm were once filled with a pure and lawful goodness, and only those pure of heart would at one time ever wield such a helm.

Inside the helmet are ancient runes that only the most wise of lorekeepers can discern.

"For he who wields this great power shall be keeper of our people, defender of our faith, and shall he preserve our customs.  Honor find you lord, and may the great gold find justice in all betrayals on this power."

Justice however, has not been found.  This helm and others like it represent the shattered power of Iliarial and everything good the powerful kingdom stood for.  Defiled and beyond despair, the ruins and their omnipresent evil are represented well by this horrific helm.
This helmet glows a deathly cold beam in every direction.
Cut from the finger of the devious planar being Lihariatoxilal, this ring holds a fraction of his incredible mastery of magic.

A curious metal, darksteel is known only to be native in the iron of the Deep.  Much speculation has occured as to the qualities of this peculiar metal, and there is much confusion as to whether it is indeed inherent of the ore used, or if it is simply enchanted by the crafters.

These armors are exceedingly rare, and it is unknown who constructs them.  What is known, is that whether by the hands of the maker, or the magic of the ore, darksteel plate deflects magics with surprising results.
This ancient key glows with the power of the spirit portal.

It is said that the Ether Giants are the masters of storms and the lords amongst all giants.

With their superior intellect and culture, the Ethers are known to have blessed the lands with several notable creations and relics of old.  This helmet is one such relic.

What clan of Ethers was behind this particular crafted feat is unknown, though the quality is clear.  Made of cobalt melded ore, the helmet is infused with a magic that is quite apparent to the wearer.  Upon initial contact with the bearer of the helm, a tingling is felt all over the body, and a noise that can only be described as a distant and shimmering thunderclap is 'felt' within the bones of their head.

The Hood of the High Courts, also known as a hood of persuasion, is a common tool of political figures on Mistone.  The first of these hoods is said to have been sewn and enchanted by Moraken during the campaign against Sinthar Bloodstone.  It is also said that it was Ozlo, the bringer of the dragon called, who requested these fine silken enchantments be offered to the heroes who would fight against Sinthar.
The key given to you by King Iliarial XII.

This old blade shows curious craftsmanship.  A strange ore comprises the majority of the blade, it seems iron at first but is warm to the touch.

The tales surrounding this blade are many, and date as far back as the race wars following the great cataclysm.  Which race made it is uncertain, for it is the same type of tale each time, though in each it pits the other as the enemy.

What is consistent is the reasoning behind it's construction in each tale.  In each, a melancholy hero has his family slaughtered in an apparent act of random violence based on their race alone.  Throughout the stories, the violence is unwarranted, unexpected, and a matter of poor luck in the face of racial hatred.  It's theme circles around the terrible reality of random violence, and pain in the face of having that tragedy befall the hero unfairly.

For all races, they have clung onto these tales of their blades as a coming of reckoning, lashing out at the chaos of violence on tribes, families, clans, and towns undeserving.  The enchantments on the blade show no sign of truth in one tale or the next, and what tragedy truly resulted in the construction and enchantment of these beautiful masterpeices.. it is clear that the will behind it finds unity amongst all races... that undeserving violence will face it's day of reckoning.

This small shard from Hraykirlar's abyssal portal still exudes a piercing and evil cold.  The connection it holds to the planes is obvious, as any focus on this shard of magic seems to cause it to spiral into its own small portal to the planes.  Great care should be taken with this relic of ancient mistakes.

Also known as the Epic Adventurer's Robes, these robes are commonplace amongst the greater mages of the lands.  Though the history of this style of robe is unfortunate.

It was a young mage under the guidance of Moraken who discovered the ability to infuse her garment with the energy of a magic missile. With unexpectedly powerful results, her garment became a popular black market commodity amongst a less amiable breed of customer, the Black Mages. When Moraken discovered one of his pupils had been dealing with the Black Mages, he banished her from  his tower.  The student attempted to regain her honor by making more of these robes to grant to the dragoncalled adventurers of Ozlo's age, so that the good in the world might have the power of her weave as well.  Unfortunate, when the Black Mages discovered that 'their' magical robes were being sold to outsiders, they caught her and had the her roasted slowly over an open flame.

A fragment of this cursed remainder drives from a once holy blade which was granted to the Kings Iliarial, I through XII.  It is an immensely powerful relic of this ancient civilization, and the powers of it's just cause are felt by all surrounding.

The now defiled runes of the original masterpeice of righteous good and honor shine brightly with a fire of hatred, an abomination of what this blade once stood for.
A holy sword with depictions of dragons in flight towards the tip of the blade.

Hraykirlars Blessing Belt, a strangely powerful belt emitting magics of goodness and blessing, but holding a strange and dark sadness to it's leathers.

It is uncertain why this beautiful and massively powerful relic has such strange emotions tied to it's weave.  Only those understanding the ruins of Iliarial would ever understand this it seems.
A strange belt... clearly magic in nature.

This tainted blade is a smithed shard of Vreliaxia's Silver Sword, a fabled blade of it's time, this blade was once wielded by one of the greatest knights defending the honor of the Kingdom of Iliarial.

The blade itself is mithril in making, though a strange and flowing silver seems to glimmer on it's edges, holding magics that will forever be unknown to most.

It was once said that only the true of heart might wield the blade that Vreliaxia the paladin of Iliarial once held.  Now though... fragments of her old blade have been forged with the curse she and her kingdom have been forced to bear for the mistakes of the forsaken defilers.
A mithril sword lined with a strange flowing silver.

Pulled from the corpse of an ancient abyssal wyvern, this strange piercing stinger still maintains some of the magics of the planar creature that bore it.  It glows a faint and shimmering red, and is warm to the touch.  When you look at the reflection of the strangely metallic object, it seems you are looking at a mirror of yourself, though it seems to be anticipating your actions a few seconds from now somehow.

The Healer's Hands are intricate gloves designed by Aerindite missionaries.  These gloves were created in the midst of the tragic plague that gripped Hurm around the date 1400.  With the pestilence of the plague leaving so many cursed beyond the abilities of any healer, these gloves, while wonderful in design, proved to be mostly futile.

Enchanted so powerfully by King Aldtorskel, the runes used on this helmet exude an energy that harms all those magical around it.  Runes similar to those seen on Aldtorskel's towers cover this helm.  It is clear that the power of this Giant King's antimagic flows through this metal.
This helmet glows with a strange light.  It burns all wielders of magic, divine or arcane, to hold it on their bare skin.
This is a very large key.

This belt is commonly known as a Goranite creation.  The first of these were known to appear around 1376, and with that date known, they are likely the creation of Gringilian Hobnoblik the gnomish inventor of Dregar lore.  Like many of his other creations, the quality of the creation is a mixture of mechanical and magical invention.  Gringilian was known for his outspoken support for those mages and inventors of the lands to find means to combat the forces of Sinthar Bloodstone.  His particular focus seemed to be in allowing the common man to take up arms, even if untrained and unexceptional.  This shield is an excellent example of that effort.

Aside from having a beautifully carved and enchanted cobalt emblem for a buckle which is adorned spectacularly with extremely small diamonds in a jumbled mix that would seem reminiscent of the constellation of Goran's Tool, the ingenuity of the belt comes in a rolling blue ball that rests magnetically on a single iron spine that wraps around the belt.  The spine itself seems a contorted weave, and as the wearer of the belt moves, the ball seems to roll about erratically.  The ball and spine itself are clearly enchanted with some curious manner of magic, as the ball seems to roll in a direction to counterweight the body's movement in increments of impressive minutia.

The function and impressive magic behind this seems to allow the most common of men to adjust to the weight of a shield on their arm, and it is said to also aid even in the balancing of two weapons wielded.

Another superb example of the craftsmanship of the K'halziras clan of dwarves.  This cloak was worn by a particular segment of the K'halziras clan defenders, the North Pass Wardens.  The North Pass of K'halziras leads into the Deep, and is known for it's magnificently crafted gates which require a special password to cross.  Nevertheless, the North Pass marked the greatest territory of threat, and the Wardens were highly regarded amongst the clan.  Perhaps the only dwarves more highly regarded then those that defended the northern gates were the Deepsoul Hunters, which were known to actively delve into the Deep from the northern passages by themselves.  Typically rangers, well trained stalkers of what lay beneath the clanhome, the Deepsouls rose from the ranks of the Wardens to become the lone hunters of the depths, and as such, wore this cloak in their duties.

The cloak is woven from a strange silk, likely spiders from the Deep.  It is surprisingly difficult to feel on the shoulders, and allows superb mobility without any hinderance at all.  The pattern inside the cloak is said to be a K'halziras rune of movement, and while not granting powerful enchantments such as the freedom magic, it is said to make the wearer quicker on their feet.

In K'halziras tradition, the greatest warriors of the clan were the Deepsoul Hunters.  Defense from the tribes and wilds aboveland were left to the main defenders of the dwarven clan.  But to venture into the depths, to defend the clanhome from the Azure threat that lay in wait... this was a task for only the Deepsoul Hunters.

The rangers of K'halziras were not rangers in the traditional sense.  They were bred assassins, hunters of a known enemy.  With limited supplies these honored warriors would set forth, always alone, to combat the creatures of the Deep below their clanhome.  Survival and stealth was paramount to these hunters.  They sought out the greatest enemy of the K'halziras.  That which comes from the Azure Pools to steal man and dwarf from their home.

The Deepsoul armor is enchanted specifically for assault of the foes of the Deep below K'halziras.

In K'halziras tradition, the greatest warriors of the clan were the Deep Hunters.  Defense from the tribes and wilds aboveland were left to the main defenders of the dwarven clan.  But to venture into the depths, to defend the clanhome from the Azure threat that lay in wait... this was a task for only the Deep Hunters.

The rangers of K'halziras were not rangers in the traditional sense.  They were bred assassins, hunters of a known enemy.  With limited supplies these honored warriors would set forth, always alone, to combat the creatures of the Deep below their clanhome.  Survival and stealth was paramount to these hunters.  They sought out the greatest enemy of the K'halziras.  That which comes from the Azure Pools to steal man and dwarf from their home.

These axes are holy, and in the days of K'halziras, they were given to only a handful of hunters in each generation of the clan.  They are imbued with magics for seeking out this particular prey... though as tales tell, very few of the Azure Hunters would ever return from the depths they set out to assault.
K'halziras Holy Axe of the Azure Hunter
The key to the outer door of the Crescent Moon & Shield Clan home.

Encapsulated within the dark crystal atop this magical staff is the eye of a black dragon.

It is unknown what dragon this came from, the eye is quite small so the assumption is that it was retrieved from a young dragon, most likely still under the watchful eye of it's mother.

The magic inherent of a dragon has been used in conjunction with quite powerful enchantments to create this potent staff.

It is unlikely that others like this exist, though considering the maker is unknown (for good reason given the implications), it is possible that there are others like it.  The general craftsmanship and design are indicative of relics created during the time of Bloodstone's wars against dragonkind.  It is quite likely this powerful artifact was created by one of Bloodstone's minions.

This staff was passed down the line of the Krakaria family beginning with Sivious Rexigal Krakaria.  The legacy of Sivious upon the Krakarian noble family is such that his actions against mankind ultimately forced a wedge between the Boyer royalty and the Krakarian family, thus resulting in their silent exile to the mountains ouside Willow's Weep.  While not remembered fondly in this aspect, his powers in magecraft have been respected and honored by the Krakarian family despite their less then benevolent nature.

The shimmering wail of Scilia's tear drifts through your body in harmonic waves, from your neck down your spine and weaving out until it hits your fingers and toes.  It is a strange sensation mized with emotion, one of known anguish but realized wisdom.  A chill passes through you constantly as the harmony of this magical weave wraps itself around your soul.

Scilia's Tear, a relic of the Krakaria family that has been held in a mysterious but fearful regard for generations.  It sat in a beautiful casing on a headless female model behind a thick window of fine glass for centuries before now.

The cursed but wondrous magics of this fine cloth passed through you the moment you placed it around your body.  After falling unconcious to the ground, your party of friends and close allies watched in fear as a searing light emerged from your right arm in a powerful display of magic seldom seen.  You now bear the scar of Scilia's Tear upon your right arm for all eternity.

The tale of this armor was inscribed within your conscious mind from the terrifying moment that you placed it on your body.  

Cursed you are until the day you find the soul mother, with the burden of the final robe of Scilia Vrilin Krakaria, a sorceress of fantastic power in the Krakaria family lineage.

Born unto greatness in the arts of sorcery and manipulation of the weave, Scilia excelled in all facets of magic through to her adult years.  She held no great love for any one man, but in the effort to maintain the name of her family, she took upon herself a child to bear, of a man she would never again see.  Scilia was a great women in many ways, though her heart was cold and calculated for most of her life.  That is, until her son Likisir was born.

Likisir was a different breed of man from the day he was born.  Kindness showered down on all who surrounded him, and his ability to love and to heal all in need, even in his youngest years... it softened the heart of Scilia to a state of utter content and purpose.  She would support his benevolence in spirit by sending him to school with the Aerindites, and in her great love for the boy she would travel along with him in his youthful studies.  As the tale you know within your heart unravels is a sad ending of anguish and dark purpose.  Likisir was slain, robbed, and left with little more then a young shattered body outside the very small settlement of North Point at that time.  This was done by a man he had thought wounded on the roadside, the sad truth of the petty villain not made apparent until the first dagger struck Likisir's side.

Scilia's world collapsed in that instant.  She had never held the benevolent soul that her young Likisir had helped her find, and her most terrible of sorcery's powers unleashed itself upon the lands when her young boy was brought to her, long since dead, and barely an image of what she had loved.  Several gypsy's were brought in in the search for the murderer, but justice of simple systems was not hasty enough in Scilia's great fury.

She would roam the lands for weeks after, evoking the powers of the weave so dark that only those truly devoid of compassion would attempt.  All fell in her path, any traveller that looked the part of a wandering or disguised gypsy.  Her conviction was unmatched, though her goal without end or hope.

The resolute madness of Scilia Krakaria found her to her demise in a short amount of time.  When they found her broken body, she still wore the garb she had worn on the day her dead and blood crusted son was handed into her sorrowful arms.  The garb had changed however, the blood of her son, the sorcery in her veins, the conviction mixed with enraged madness... it had fallen with her.  Blackened a color of ancient blood that holds no color, chilled by the mixture of her emotions and powers.  The magical fibers of the once beautiful dress had soaked in all that occurred in that short period of time.

The enchantment of the garb is such that you remember her chilled heart, you feel the cold along the fibers of the threads.  You remember her anguish as a distant memory.  Though above all else, you hold a fragment of her absolute conviction.  The strange whispers of her resolution of revenge vibrate along you bones.

You remember the day she carved the tearing eye on her arm, with the blade of the first gypsy she had slain.  Dark promises she made with that mark, dark promises mixed with powerful enchantments... you sometimes feel the sting of the blade along your own arm where you too share the same mark.

The fibers of the garb wrap tightly on your skin.  The curse of her powers is so great that you are unable to remove it.  The fibers and precious metals that once shined with a brilliant sapphire sparkle are now the deepest emptiness of black, and can never be recolored or reshaped in their curse.

The powers of Scilia's final act of great magic, however, imbue you with her strength and conviction.  It is not just the chill you feel or the whispering of her promises.  The fibers of the garb empower you with their strange but wonderful curse.  The pain you feel the cloth feels, and in turn whispers with great power upon any who harm you.  The strange and distant knowledge of Scilia's demise flows through your body like it was once your own pain.  The killing curse of the great wailing is almost petty to the wail of Scilia that you have now heard and feel inside.

Your conviction is greater then ever in your tasks, but Scilia's cold shall forever now chill your soul.

An Aerindite priest, Dhalgrin Linbahr wandered the lands in a manner that most would deem aimless.  Yet for Dhalgrin the aim was clear and along the curious metal running around the wrist the following is inscribed:

The path of healing is not bound by direction.

The gloves are smooth and gentle to the touch despite being metal, and glimmer with a subdued greatness inherent of the selfless priests of Aeridin.

The blessings on these quite old gauntlets are reportedly made by Dhalgrin himself during his early years as a priest of Aeridin.  They were last reported bought by a member of the Krakaria family in the Boyer Kingdom.  The purpose of their acquisition is otherwise a mystery.

How Hengrid's Equalizer came into the possession of the Krakarian family is quite well known and documented by in their annals of Krakarian lineage.

Sivious Rexigal Krakaria came upon this curious weapon of war by killing it's owner.  A mage of terrible power Sivious ultimately drove a rift between the Krakarian family and the Boyer Kingdom, resulting in the Krakarian exile to the mountainous regions outside Willow's Weep.

Sivious found the weapon quite curious in his utter inability to wield it after retrieving it from the dead dwarf's body, and was further fascinating by the searing burn on his fingers upon even grasping it with his bare hand.

In his studies he found that Hengrid Thornflail was the previous keeper of this relic of flails.  This dwarf had once been a defender of a dwarven clan preceeding the Runic Anvil.  In his search to unfold the magics of this flail, Sivious found only that the nature of it's power lies in what appears to be Hengrid's life tale of distaste in the outcomes of battles involving righteousness on both sides of what most call good and evil.  It is hazy what turn of events spiralled this dwarf into his ambivalence in regarding the preachings of war, though Sivious has documented some research on his history.  It is clear that whatever these events were, they had involved the death of his family at the hand of an enemy that his clan had sought out war against for no reason save for their religious inclinations.  They caused this dwarf to adopt a great hatred of all preachings of war based on religious differentiation, and in the end he left his clan alone, without any surviving family of blood relations.

Sivious also uncovered that Hengrid's journey's following his departure led him to become a hunter of what he deemed religious fanatics, in particular the paladins of toran and the unholy champions of pyrtechnon and corath.  While the dwarf was not evil at heart, his hatred of blind faith amongst these sorts did lead to the killing of many paladins, but moreso did he hunt down the unholy champions of the lands and their ilk.

This flail was enchanted in an unknown manner, but it's magics seem consistent with the dogma of neutrality that Hengrid held dear in his later years of demise.

The magics of this flail are such that it can never be altered by conventional crafting means.

Belatrin Xavius Krakaria was an outcast of his own family.  Discontent with the stringency of the Monastery and the expectation by his kin to continue in their footsteps of teaching, he left the school around the coming of his 15th year on Layonara.

Belatrin would wander the lands for 50 years before perishing at the hands of a band of mercenaries somewhere on the isles of Vanavar.

A ranger and a wanderer, Belatrin worshipped many gods of nature, but thought mostly of the wisdoms of Folian Spae.  This aspect of his life made him quite an anomoly of the Krakarian family, most likely part of the reason for his sudden and early departure.

In his travels and through his prayers to Folian, he was blessed with the powers that now lie in the thin strand of this bowstring.  The blessings of wandering, of moving with grace through the world have found their way into the magic of this bow, and it is said that those who wield it are able to move so gracefully through the lands that world itself seems to slow around you.

This bow is the sole possession that still lies in the Krakarian family from Belatrin.  It is said that he came into and left the world with nothing more then he needed, and at his death this is all that remained.  His nephews Jilirid and Oprion would ultimately seek out their lost uncle to discover his old bow in the hands of the same mercenaries on Vanavar... it is said that all blood relatives of those who they killed have since perished.

Whether that would've been the wish of the simple wanderer Belatrin will never be known.

One of the oldest suits of armor in the Krakaria family lineage, Uril's Plate belonged to a battlepriest named Uril Krilin Krakaria.  It is written in the annals of the Krakaria family lineage that Uril was a warpriest of Vorax, and while unusually small for a human, his girth was more like a well fed dwarf.

Uril fell during the late race wars following the cataclysm, and this ancient armor is all that remains of his short lived legacy.  It is said to be inbued with the divine blessing of his lord for his fearless nature in battle.  This fearlessness ultimately led to a short life, though of his lord's pride Uril could be confident.

Northwind Howl, a relic amongst skalds.  Oprion Helius Krakaria was the bearer of this great shield.  A study of the bardic magics from the very beginnings of his teachings within the halls of the Krakarian Monastery, Oprion would ultimately find a distinct distaste in the simplicity of song and seek out the teachings of the northern peoples and the powers of the skald.

Oprion was a clever if not devious youth, his charisma and wit unmatched amongst his cousins and classmates alike.  There was a darkness to his temperment however, a darkness that ultimately found it's closure in the revenge of his lost uncle Belatrin.  The tale is well documented that he and a close and older cousin within the Krakaria family, Jilirid Yilor Krakaria, sought out the source of their uncles demise.

Belatrin had vanished mysteriously from the Monastery nearly 51 years prior, far before the birth of these two young men.  But his tale rang of dissent and misdirection, which the two boys found intruiging in their youthful and reckless manner.

In their searchings, they discovered the fate of their uncle quite near to the time it occurred.  They had tracked him down in a manner of sport almost, for they wished to surprise this strange ranger in their family with their clever seekings.  On the isles of Vanavar they heard that a man bearing only a bow and a small backpack had disappeared into the surrounding woods where bandits and mercenaries were known to reside, and had not been seen since.

The two young men, boys by all measure but their abilities and training in war began their search in the surrounding lands cautiously and in an calculated manner, and it was not long before they found a camp of bandits where a man was strung naked from a treebranch, quite clearly tortured and left to his slow death.

The two approached during the night in great stealth, towards this barely breathing man.  They immediately recognized him as one of their own ilk, and attempted to quietly revive him.  What is recorded in their tellings of the following events is that in his first and last words to these boys he gasped that he did not seek vengeance from the blades of his family.  The boys watched him die, and in a look without words the bond of vengeance was sworn.

Jilirid and Oprion did not return for the following season of their schooling.  They instead began with their dark deeds by slaughtering the camp of bandits and mercenaries around them, ensnaring them in traps before they awoke the next morning, and then promising them freedom if they would simply tell the boys their names.  The boys took their names, killed every last one, and took their oath to every blood relative of the men who had killed their uncle.  They did not rest for three years until they had slain the 94 men, women and children that comprised the bloodlines of Belatrin's murderers.

It is with a great and dark irony the truth in Belatrin's departure from the Monastery and the great distortion of his hopes in breaking his ties by unleashing the family's fury upon so many in the lands Belatrin had grown to love.

This shield was borne by Oprion from the day he left the Krakarian Monastery to the day he died.  It is said that a curse of vengeance lies within the metals of this shield.

In the great tribes of the Krashin northlands a wondrous pride was held in the creation of such blades as these.

Before glimmers a tooth of sparkling blue, cold misting the air around it.  This is a tooth of an elder winter wolf, taken in a ceremony honoring the dead beast by the elders of the barbaric tribes.  The ceremony itself involves prayer to the lord and keeper of the wolves in the gods above, and a continued life of great hunts for both the wolves and the people of the tribe.

Krashin mystics are said to enchant these tooths upon their removal from the mouth of the ancient wolves, using the holy power of the tribal union of men and wolves, both hunters of great prowess and cunning that rely on the common saying amongst tribes that worship the northern wolves in their cultures:

The strength of the wolf lies in the pack and the strength of the pack lies in the wolf.

A very small and extremely beautiful pair of gloves.  Their weave shimmers with a brilliance rarely seen.

Delicate strands of ancient woven ores of mithril, and what seems to be some type of strange silver lace the outer weaves of this smooth silken cloth.  At the wrist of these gloves exquisite rubies of the smallest size dangle in what at first appears to be a tenuos connection to the weave of the glove, though upon inspection, they are quite impossible to pull off as fine mithril strands have been somehow interlaced with the cut of the gem itself.

Upon placing these gloves on one's hands, the fingers immediately vibrate with the energy of the woven enchantments.  It is said by most who have managed, rather been allowed, to place their hands in these tiny gloves that a brief surge of confidence, conviction, and what many describe as a powerful emotion washes over them.

These wondrous guantlets came into the possession of the Krakaria Family by unknown means, but are clearly a prized peice of what this noble family has come to own in its great store of heirlooms and treasures.

The namesake of these gloves is in no way true to it's origin, which is speculated to be as old as the race wars of -1812.  The name they now carry was borne unto a young boy of the Krakaria family who died at the age of 9.  Likisir Haliar Krakaria was murdered at the hands of what he thought an injured gypsy to whom he'd blindly run to aid.  The story recorded in the Krakarian Lineage Annals tells that Likisir was a particularly benevolent young boy, who at a very young age began to study the preachings of Aeridin, and had begun his studies entirely towards ends of aiding those sick or weak.  The Krakarian family fully supported this effort, as in his youth, he was the only of their family to ever find the ability to place his hands in these wondrous gloves they had kept for ages, unused.
They knew the gloves to be enchanted with a power of healing, and encouraged his benevolence and capability in curing those ailing.  In this event however, the boy had apparently been alone on the roads outside North Point, and had run to aid a man injured and bleeding on the ground.  The man slew Likisir and robbed him, though found himself unable to pry the beautiful gloves from the young boy's hands.

What is known of these silken gloves is that they are imbued with an incredible healing power, and that the magics that vibrate within will shimmer and vibrate in the presence of any being that is tainted with a malevolent presence.

The magic of these gloves are such that they may never be altered by conventional crafting means.

This smooth and beautiful cloak was crafted for Jilirid Yilor Krakaria by a Mistite priest who instructed the more talented of the students at the Krakarian Monastery.

Jilirid was a talented student of war, and maintained a great cleverness combined with a depth of wisdom uncharacteristic of a boy so young.  He, like many of his cousins, held a strange darkness in his heart however, and it would be with his cousin Oprion that he would find the medium for unleashing the storm upon the world around him.  Oprion and Jilirid would both find the darkness in their own hearts in their search for their lost uncle Belatrin.

Belatrin had vanished mysteriously from the Monastery nearly 51 years prior, far before the birth of these two young men.  But his tale rang of dissent and misdirection, which the two boys found intruiging in their youthful and reckless manner.

In their searchings, they discovered the fate of their uncle quite near to the time it occurred. The boys watched him die, and in a look without words the bond of vengeance was sworn.
