They did not rest for three years until they had slain the 94 men, women and children that comprised the bloodlines of Belatrin's murderers.

It is with a great and dark irony the truth in Belatrin's departure from the Monastery and the great distortion of his hopes in breaking his ties by unleashing the family's fury upon so many in the lands Belatrin had grown to love.

This cloak was worn by Jilirid until the day he died, and it still maintains the magics imbued within it's finely woven cloth by his teacher, a priest of Mist.  Jildrid would continue for most his life alongside his cousin Oprion, and bring the tidings of the faith of Mist to the world around him in a powerful, if not oppressive, manner.

Xilidias Granthis Krakaria is perhaps one of the most elusive member of the long lineage of the family Krakaria.  One of the first to bear the name Krakaria, prior to the founding of the Monastery, Xilidias was a wandering mage of neither ill repute nor fame.

It is know he wandered the Dregarian lands alone and aimless, and had some affinity for the art of conjuring.  What he did with these skills, few know.  What is known is that at the end of his life he left two things to his only son, Azirine Janid Krakaria.  One was this helmet.  The second was a massive amount of gold which ultimately funded the the beginnings of what is now the Krakarian Monastery.  None in the family know from where this gold came, they simply know that their status derived from a wandering ancient relative of notable magical affinity.

Made under rare and strict conditions from the softest yet most durable silk of an ancient Silver Orb Spider these boots are a great boon to any wearer. Dark brown in colour they are perhaps the most comfortable boots ever made and never give any signs of wearing out. No dirt, grime or blood ever stains them.

This cloak seems to shimmer and ripple as one moves making it hard to focus on the exact location of the wearer. When put on it appears to wrap itself around it wearer clinging closely to their body as if a web. This unusual garment was originally worn by Orphenzala Donowameela, an extremely gifted and high ranked member of the exclusive and secretive Fmaawamla eo Irela Irilana (Breeders of His Hate). The Cloak was used by the dark elf to enable him to travel either above or below ground without being seen. 

Possessing a brilliant mind for alchemy he wove into the very fabric of the cloak wards and chemical compounds that would draw to the surface any poisons which he might have invariably ingested or received through spider bites since this was his most avid focus.

This blade was reportedly designed by a guild of pirates running smuggling operations outside of Hurm.  The dagger itself is unimpressive save for the strange enchantment cursed upon it to deal death to those of better nature then the bearer.  Additionally, devious poisons run from the tip of the blade deriving from an internal resevoir.  The poison itself blinds the prey on striking, though it requires a deep strike to be made for the poison to have effect.
This somewhat large dagger was designed to enable the bearer greater dualing capacity.  It is light on the hand and promises great agility on the user from the handle to the tip.

This dagger is well known amongst assassins.  The exceptionally sharp edge of the simple iron weapon has strange barbs at it's sides which are weakly molded to the blade.  On close examination, these barbs have numerous 'burrowing' protrustions.  The intent is that upon thrusting the blade into the victim, the barbs will break free and burrow with the victim's movement thereafter.

Very little is identifiable about this weapon save for the elven words that circle the spiralling blade to it's tip.

"The darkness shall one day know my fear as it's own, for my blade is many, and its light shall glimmer in such number that it shall suffocate the emptiness of the Deep"

This reflective blade was designed by a strange group of bandits operating outside of Audiria around the time of Bloodstone's Fall.  Apparently smuggling goods into and out of Prantz since the takeover by General Broegar, these bandits had need for a weapon that would enable them to deal with the guards with sufficient surprise.  The surprise in itself would not be enough, for the goal was not to kill all any guards, but rather conceal the identities of the bandits while letting the guards live.  The intent in this was to prevent any investigation on dead guards that would link the smuggling operations to them, or cause any hassle in their business.  The poison coating the blade here is said to blind an individual on mixing it with their blood, and the scimitar was the most effective slicing weapon they could think of.

This plan naturally failed miserably, as Lord Broegar ultimately found of the smuggling operations and destroyed the bandits in one fell swoop.  The upside to this is of course the numerous blades of this make on the black market.

An impressive little blade, the magics imbued in the hilt and the blade itself are such that they enhance the seeking instinct of the hunter.

These blades were designed by an assassin of unknown origin, though it is suspected he found great success in them as his identity has always been concealed.  It is said that a blade of this type is left in the body of each victim he has found... and such is the reason for so many being available in marketplaces of the underworld.
This short sword has the qualities of vampiric leeching in it's metal.  It is otherwise unimpressive.
This torch is carried by the Stormcrest Guides.

An ancient rune carved by a dwarven spirit of the Lost Hammer Clan, this rune can bring up a shield of antimagic around the wearer for a very short period of time.

The fine ore this rune is inscribed in glows faintly with the magic of the rune carved magically upon its face.

You came into posession of this armor after defeating the Spirit Guardian of the Valley of the Moons. It allows the wearer to become closer to the spirit world for a period of time each day.

GM note: this item is not supposed to end up in player hands.
GM note: This item is not supposed to fall into player hands

Constructed from the silk gathered from killed rock devourers, this armor is as impressive as the beast from whom the silk derives.  Rock devourers are peculiar to the many regions of the Deep.  They burrow through stone and ore, and are known to be near impossible to kill.

Xantril
    It can be said that in the history of Xantril there are two moments that both devastated all foundations and became the cornerstones for the twisted continent that emerged. The first was the Cataclysm, which tore Xantril apart from Dregar and sent it drifting east for many dark ages of relative isolation. The second was the arrival of the Prince of Demons, Xandrial, and his merciless minions. There are many tales of Xandrial's arrival upon Layonara.     Some believe that Xandrial was the first demon that forced its way through the gate made by the foolish experiments of Oriax on the continent of Mistone.  Some believe that Xandrial was called by one of the most concentrated efforts of Drow faith and magic to torment the surface dwellers.     Some believe that Xandrial was summoned forth by Bloodstone or Milara to serve their vile purposes. Whatever the truth, the continent of Xantril belongs to the Prince of Demons. All who lived on this continent prior to his arrival either quickly bent to Xandrial's will, were tortured and died in dances of demonic desire, or now live an inescapable nightmare to further pleasure the demons. This is what we know of Xantril, and we know it because Xandrial wants all of Layonara to know it. 

Well-known cities:

Arabel 
Location: 
    Southern tip of the continent of Xantril 
Population: 
    24,000 (37% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 15% dwarf, 10% orc, 5% gnome, 1% dark elf, 1% demon, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tyrany 
Defenses:   
    A heavily fortified masonry wall surrounds this city. 
Miscellaneous Information:
    When you first enter Arabel, you'll know you are in Xantril and that the terrible things you have heard are true. From all around, tortured screams will accost your ears and tear at your soul. Much of the city is in ruins. Disease, famine, and violence are all part of the everyday routine of Arabel. Somehow the city manages to operate the docks with relative efficiency. Likely this is because the demons want fresh souls to torment, even though most know by now to stay far away from Arabel.
Arabel was not always a tormented city under the sway of demons. Between the Cataclysm and the arrival of Xandrial, Arabel was one of the few towns on Xantril to establish some sort of prominence and connection with the other continents. Arabel's location on the southern tip of Xantril gave them an advantage in securing trade with both Dregar and the Kingdom of Roldem. Over the years, the merchant families of Arabel built themselves up into a commercial powerhouse, funneling most of the surplus goods from the middle and south of the island through their docks. The former stature of Arabel can still be seen in glimpses of its working ruin. Those who lived in the old Arabel are haunted by its memory. Those who contributed to its glory are now forced to work the sewers.
Major Temples to Corath and Shadon have been constructed in Arabel.

Westgate 
Location:
    Western shore of the continent of Xantril. 
    Population: 4,000 (40% human, 15% half-orc, 12% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% orc, 6% gnome, 4% dark elf, 2% demon, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tyrany 
Defenses:   
    A reinforced masonry wall surrounds this city. It is also enhanced with magic. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
    Westgate is a port city directly west of the Demon Mountains. When Xandrial sends his demonic minions to Dregar or beyond, they go through Westgate. The only creatures allowed to live in this city are those who directly serve this purpose and as such are evil to the core.
 
Reth 
Location:
    Western side of the Great Forest on the Island of Xantril. 
Population:   500 (55% human, 45% elf) 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses: 
     A wooden palisade surrounds this small town. 
Miscellaneous Information:
    Some say this small forest hamlet is the gathering point for rangers and druids who are dedicated to protecting the sanctity of the Great Forest of Xantril. Their secondary concern, rumors have it, is to keep the demons from descending upon the Ancient Oak. As the northernmost town in Xantril, and since it is shrouded by the Great Forest, it is one of the few places on Xantril where Xandrial's influence is not complete. This gives the dedicated few rangers and druids a chance to work undetected on the forest's behalf. As this is a dangerous occupation, these agents of the Great Forest are re-circulated, though none but the druids and rangers themselves are sure how.

Fort Militrix
Location:  
    Located at approximately the center of the continent, Fort Militrix overlooks the road north towards the Roughlands.
Population: 375
Defenses:  
    Fort Militrix is defended by alternating sections of stone and wood walls. Inside are platforms for ranged attacks, and historically speaking the fort has always been well garrisoned.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Militrix is of key military concern, as it is situated on the road which runs east and west between Prumar and Mithrain and divides the continent into its northern and southern sections. All traffic between the north and south falls under the watch of Fort Militrix. For this reason the Fort has always been heavily garrisoned with the most disciplined and skilled troops Pranzis could muster. The officers were also bolstered five or six times their numbers by recruits gathered on the march north from Arabel. This, of course, was all prior to Xandrial's arrival. But this fortitude made Militrix resilient to Xandrial's onslaught. Some believe that Militirx is holding fast, a bastion of hope amidst a sea of raging demons. 

Fort of Last Hope
Location:  
    At the edge of the Demon Mountains, in the wastes of the Tortured Lands, lies the Fort of Last Hope.
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    Hope Fort is well defended by stone walls and battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    The name of Hope Fort has become something of a Xantril joke. More often now it goes by Fort of Last Hope. It is said that a handful of soldiers still fight against the waves of evil minions that pour from Xandrial's keep. If they do, it is assumed that Xandrial allows them to do so for some other twisted purpose, for none could live free so close to Xandrial's seat of power.

Hilm Castle
Location:
    At the edge of the Fields of Death and the Orsraun Mountains stands Hilm Castle.
Population: 1600
Government:  Theocracy
Defenses:  
    Hilm is heavily defended with high stone walls and well designed battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Hilm is dreadfully close to the Demon Mountains. Still, Xandrial's gaze is somewhat obscured by the Orsraun Mountains which lie between the demon king and Hilm. Hilm also lies to the north of Xandrial's keep, away from the more heavily populated areas of Xantril. These two facts give Hilm some room to maneuver on this demon-dominated continent.
    For ages, Hilm ruled the north as the last major settlement on the road to the Archwood and the Great Forest. By looking at the arrangement, you would likely have thought Hilm ruled with an iron fist, putting the wild folk of the forest under the civilized boot. This is simply not the case. Hilm established its authority in the northern regions by repeatedly defending the interests of the Great Forest and its residents from the waves of settlers and treasure seekers who fled the central region of Xantril, tortured and convoluted in the seismic events of the Cataclysm. Hilm regulated all traffic north, allowed only some to continue into the forest and turned back many. This, of course, makes Hilm particularly unpopular with the residents of the lands to the south. The forest folk to the north, however, have a deep respect for Hilm that they are reminded of daily as they enjoy the wilds in which they reside.
    This conflict, like all other conflicts on Xantril, shows signs of flaring up. The southerners, possessed with demonic rage, grasp at targets to lash their hate upon. To them, Hilm is a perfect choice. Only minor forces have thrown themselves upon the Hilm walls thus far. Either they are wild groups of the demonically driven whipped into a spontaneous frenzy and thus unorganized, or they are simply testing the defenses. In either case, fear intensifies in Hilm, as all within its walls can feel the darkness sweeping across the Tortured Lands toward their gates.
Cities of the Demon East by Xantril scholar Dulugu Ganalan

Within the chruch of Az'atta, the tale goes that these cloaks were given to the first generations of her clergy by Az'atta Herself.  In the days before Her name was known, the clergy often found it best to choose when to spread her word carefully, and that avoiding certain confrontations was often wise.  While it is unlikely that all of these cloaks, or even any of them, were gifts from Az'atta herself, they serve to teach a valuable lesson, both through the telling of their tale when they are gifted and through their use, to the newest members of the clergy.  This particular example also embodies Az'atta's hatred of poisons and its divine magic serves to strengthen the wearer against its evils.

Apple juice gives this brew it's amber color and delightful flavor. The name is derived from the Axe Head flower, which grows on Alindor in the apple groves.

If most folks knew what went into this drink it might not be such a popular seller. Crushed pearls and some limestone dust oddly enough give this brew its unique full-bodied flavor. It is popular amongst the dwarven kind, some of whom claim that they don't mind the taste of rock and stone since they hammer away at it all day under a mountain.

This recipe was traced back to its maker who lived on Dregar. He would mix just the right amount of blackberries with almonds. The fellow owned a black stallion, which he rode to Prantz making ale deliveries to the Hotel Layonara. In time his horse became known around Dregar and the drink was named after it. A good thing too as the man's name was Phillibuster McGillicutty and that didn't seem to roll off the tongue as well as Black Horse Ale.

The partial recipe for this brew was found behind a stack of barrels by one of the Leringard Arms Brewers. He experimented with the partial recipe adding other ingredients to develop this dark and bitter malt that packs a punch. A hint of blackberry makes this brew one to try.

This delightful brew compliments the smooth and refreshing tastes of fresh picked, succulent blueberries with a tangy sharp bite, likened to the edge of a sword. Surprisingly misleading, just like its rumored creators, Blue Sword Swill plays tricks on those who drink it. 

The origin of this favorite is said to be the hidden Fairy Shee, lost some place on the continent of Dregar near The Forest of the Mists. The rumor goes that any fool who partakes of food or drink offered by the fairies there will quickly forget his or her purpose and stay and play for the rest of their days. 

Nobody knows for sure just how the recipe for this mystical blue drink traveled from the Shee, but it seems to have lost a bit of its potency. Instead of completely forgetting their purpose, those who drink it usually recover with in a few days.

A dwarven Cleric of Vorax who used to frequent Hlint is rumored to have come up with the idea for this odd drink. After a night of cleansing the local crypts of undead he would belly up to the bar in the Wild Surge, and order a large stein of ale. He would drop a few skeleton bones into it, typically ones from the hand. Then down the drink leaving the bones behind to rattle in the empty stein. The bones seem to take some of the bitter edge off of this brew.

Traveling the mountains of Northern Dregar a man found a cherry tree grove. This man happened to be a renowned brew master.  He kept the secret of where he found the best cherries in all of Layonara for nearly 30 years. When he passed he told his son where to find the cherries and his son sold that knowledge and made a king's profit. Cherry River Lambic is one of the finest drinks in all the lands. Its tangy flavor invites you to have another, and another, and hides how strong the drink truly is. Many have learned this lesson the hard way.

It sounds far worse than it tastes. Its name was simply taken from the brewing process. Into each brew you would "crack open" the seedpods of the skullcap plant and allow the seeds to soak in the mixture. Thus the name Cracked Skull was adopted. A smoother ale one will never find than a good cream ale.

This recipe was developed by a Dwarven follower of Rofirein long ago. The warriors of Rofirein required strong drink to quench their mighty thirst after delivering justice to the enemies of Mistone. The recipe was given to various inns and taverns across the land so that the Draught of the Dragon would lend courage to traveling adventurers.  One must be careful when consuming this drink however, it's intoxicating effects are said to vary from drink to drink.  Perhaps it is due to the raw eggs used in the brew, one can not be sure though.

Why the creator of this drink named it Dead Orc Porter remains a mystery, and a favorite discussion amongst drunken bar patrons as they tip back two or three of them. Its mixture of sweet cherries and tart raspberries is hard to miss. Perhaps the brew master thought the name sounded more exciting than Cherry and Raspberry Porter.

This strong ale was once only served to dwarven nobility, thus it's name. It was only placed at the Kings table, the Head table. This drink first found its way to the general population at the celebration honoring the dwarven champion, Gotak Gungur. Still today when you see a table of dwarves raise their steins you will hear this declaration... "Deathward is fer pansies!"

After many tries and failures he added a bit of honey and it was an overnight success. The honey took the edge off the tart cranberries and the drink went on to be a Rilaran favorite.

A deep crimson colored lager that is brewed from the finest of fresh cranberries, it hints at another taste that is difficult to place. An old favorite to gypsies everywhere, it is often said that caravans in Dregar could be found brewing this lager by the light of the moon, near blistering campfires that throw off colors that are only matched by the color of the brew itself. 

In the history of this lager, it isn't quite clear whether the gypsies perfected the drink themselves or if it was a stolen recipe from a different source. Nevertheless, the gypsies are often credited with adding the bits of campfire charcoal and fire agate dust to this drink which gives it its wonderful full flavor. 

This strong and full-bodied lager is certain to burn all the way down and leave you feeling grand.

Who wants to drink something green? That is what most say when they see a bottle of Green Forest Draft on the shelf. One taste however and you're hooked on it for life. How the creator came upon this mixture of belladonna and peppermint is anyone's guess. One sip and you can feel it go to work soothing the body and the soul with its smooth minty flavor. It is strong for the novice drinker and it can take ones breath away quite easily. Many newcomers to the drink are heard saying "Smoooooooooth" after that first gulp as they try and regain their breath.

Slightly above your average beer. The best thing about it is the price. If you're looking for quantity over quality this strong nutty brew is the one.

A drink brewed using juice derived from the Juniper Berry. This spicy brew was first introduced at the Juniper Berry Festival in Lan's Port on Alindor. The juice is extracted from the berries by jumping up and down in a tub of the fruit. The sweet yet tangy flavor will always leave you wanting more.

The Basics of Armor Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Armor types - There are 7 basic armor types that a crafter can make. These range from a chain shirt to full plate armor.
 
2. Armor Materials - Armor can be crafted from Bronze, Iron, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt and Mithril. Armor may also be adorned with gold. Adorned armor has a higher AC than regular armor. 

3. Armor Components - Armor requires ingots and a pattern.  

4. Crafting Armor - To craft a set of armor, one must equip a smiths hammer, posess the required raw materials and use an armor crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Armor may be smelted. Smelted armor generally yields two less ingots than were originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tailoring, and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Mining
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

In addition to ore, miners may also mine clay and sand. 

2. Mining Equipment - To mine ore, one must use a pickaxe. Pickaxes require the martial weapon feat, so certain non combat classes will have difficulty mining. A shovel is required to mine clay and sand.

Pickaxes and Shovels are subject to damage while mining and will eventually break. it is advised to acquire a backup pickaxe and shovel prior to attempting mining.

3. Misc. Infomation - Ocassionally, one might get lucky and chip off a second nugget of ore or find a rare gem or other  item. 

4. Related Skills - Smelting, Weapon Crafting, Armor Crafting and Tinkering all use ore, sand and clay byproducts. Please read their respective books for more information about them.
The book of patterns contains a large collection of pattern designs used by tailors and armor crafters to make various pieces of clothing and armor.

The Basics of Smelting
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. All may be smelted. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

2. Smelting Equipment - To smelt ore, one must use a smelting tongs. Ore nuggets are inserted into a smelting forge and melted into ingots. 

3. Related Skills - Weapon Crafting and Armor Crafting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Weapon Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Weapon types - There are 21 basic weapon types that a crafter can make. These range from a simple Dagger to a Greatsword.
 
2. Weapon Materials - Weapons can be crafted from Copper, Bronze and Iron. Weapons may also be coated with Silver and Titanium. Silver coated weapons are more effective against undead foes, while Titanium coated weapons do more damage.

3. Weapon Components - Weapons generally require ingots and a casting mold. Casting molds come in small, medium or large sizes. Some weapons also require wood shafts. 

4. Crafting Weapons - To craft a weapon, one must equip a smiths hammer, posses the required raw materials and use a weapon crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Weapons that require 2 or more ingots to craft may be smelted. Smelted weapons generally yield one less ingot than what was originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tinkering, Wood Crafting and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

This brew originated in Hlint. A local adventurer would help keep the road clear by hunting and killing the goblin scouts near the Red Light Caves. He would gain a reward from Quartermaster Talon and then spend the night drinking at the Wild Surge. One day the particularly thirsty adventurer with a string of ears could not find the Quartermaster. Sadly he trudged into the Inn complaining about his misfortune. His misfortune turned to fortune when a local brewer asked about the ears. He offered the adventurer ale in return for the ears. The brewer had heard tales about the odd properties in the ears of the goblin scouts. So on a whim he tossed them into his latest batch of pilsner. To the brewers surprise the drink had a smooth and robust flavor that his previous ale had not. The drink became a favorite in Hlint and the brewer grew wealthy. With much wealth the brewer moved away and took the recipe with him. A copy was found in the Great Library of all places and is now available again.

An accidental success is the best way to describe Will-O-Whiskey. An adventurer and brew master from Lorax was passing through the Black Dog Moors when he captured the essence of a Will'O wisp. In his haste to contain the essence he reached in his pouch only to find his small whisky flagon. He put the essence inside and didn't give it another thought. After a few hours of trudging through the swamp he sat on a stump, opened his flagon and took a rather large gulp of its contents.  His eyes lit up and his face flushed red. He hurried back home and perfected his new creation. Will-O-Whisky is a very powerful drink that should be sipped or mixed with juices.

This more common ale has the typical taste of a fine wheat ale but with much less potency than your average brew. Once simply called "Wheat Ale," this particular variety of wheat ale began to be known over time as, "Wizard's Wheat Ale" as it was noticed that wizards would frequently request this drink and carry it with them on long journeys. This bitter golden liquid although flavorful, has a low enough alcohol content that even wizards could handle large quantities of it without forgetting their spells. Perhaps it is the quick processing of this beverage that leads to its low alcohol, or maybe it is the cure light wounds potion thrown in the mix. Either way, this drink has little effect on most and to a dwarf, has no more effect than pure water.

A dangerously lusty red wine with intoxicating effects, this wine is an essential part of Xeenite celebrations and rituals everywhere. 

The key to making this wine is to use only grapes who's vines scale the walls of temples of Xeen. It is said that the grapes that grow on Xeen's temples already have an intoxicating affect even before being made into wine. 

The recipe for this wine is said to be guarded very closely by Xeen's priestesses themselves, and is rumored to have been stolen by one of the proprietors of the Leringard Arms Inn and Tavern after a very prominent Xeenite festival in Katherian. However, not too many people know how much truth is in this tale. If there is any truth to it, those who know, don't talk about it. Truth or not, everybody benefits from the knowledge of this recipe, as it is the finest wine ever made.

One of the world's rarest and most coveted gems, alexandrite takes on a brilliant green hue when under indirect sunlight but turns blood-red when exposed to candlelight. Loretellers claim that all alexandrite comes from the body of the oldest son of Silvanus, the Forest Father. A common nursery rhyme goes "Silvanus' wife went mad one night, murdering her child by candlelight."

As its name indicates, this gem is generally green in color. Typical samples, however, have a pattern of overlapping edges that range from yellow-green to almost black. When polished, they have a beautiful play of light within their crystalline structure.

Fire agate forms in thin brown layers that refract the incoming light, giving the gem its "fire." The refraction often forms patterns reminiscent of a dragon's scales, which makes it prized by sorcerers who claim to trace their lineage back to dragonkin. A well-cut stone has its outer layers polished and ground away until only the fire is visible.
The most valued amethyst crystals are a milky, wine-dark purple.

A singularly beautiful stone, phenalope is dusty pink in color, dramatically marked with black streaks. Even when mounted in jewelry, phenalope maintains a rough texture, pocked with tiny holes that cannot be polished out. For some, this is part of the stone's attraction, and they wear it as a symbol of their own tenacious natures.

This transparent crystal is the hardest substance found in nature. The most valued color is a clear bluish-white; most lesser stones are clear white or off-white, but other less valued color varieties are known, among them mauve, pink, peach, and chartreuse. Due to its hardness, the gem is always faceted rather than polished.

Bright and beautiful, the ruby is famous for its clear and bloody hue. To some it is the gem of love, to others the gem of revenge. To all it is unquestionably precious, and the largest, most flawless specimens are more highly prized than diamonds. The goddess Sune is said to sometimes wear rubies in her wild hair.

Favored by druids for its graceful and natural beauty, malachite is known for its strikingly ornamental bands of light and dark green that alternate throughout the entire stone. Painters have also been known to crush the gem and use it as a pigment. Adventurers have discovered that the gem bubbles and dissolves readily in acid, making it an effective - if expensive - means of identifying certain dangerous substances.

The blue sapphire is twin to the more precious ruby in all respects but color. In most stones, the sparkling blue color must be brought out by exposure to great heat. Once "cooked," the color change is permanent and does not otherwise affect the much-treasured durability of the gem.

Unlike their more common cousin, fire opals are full of vibrant hues: hot yellows, oranges, and reds so bright they almost cast their own light. Some believe that these gems derive their glow from a supernatural source, and not a few sages have claimed that each gem is a tiny portal to the Elemental Plane of Fire. However, scholars claim it is just the way the gem refracts the light around it.

Best known in its pale, orange-yellow form, topaz is an attractive gem that appears in well-formed, multifaceted crystals. These crystals can reach an incredible size, and specimens weighing several hundred pounds are not unknown. The largest stones are customarily reserved for gifts on state occasions, and only the greatest master gemcutters are allowed to work them.

Often called the "Poor Man's Ruby," the common garnet is nevertheless a distinct and attractive blood-red gem in its own right. The violet form, also called rhodolite, is the rarest, most prized, and most valuable form of the stone.

Prized for their vibrant green color, emeralds are fragile and need to be protected from the impacts and extreme temperature changes common to adventuring life. It is a highly prized gem by the wealthly and royality alike.

When cut and polished, aventurine is alluring as its name. It resembles misty quartz, but contains glistening flecks of green that give it a unique sheen. The witches of Rashemen are said to use aventurine for invocations, evocations, and spirit work.

A common but beautiful gem, feldspar comes in many colors - each of them nicely set off by the stones' glassy luster. Best known in its purple hues, which are commonly mistaken for amethyst, feldspar is the much softer of the two and will scratch, chip, and even burn easily.

Unlike most leaves, which must be dried for long periods of time before being smoked, Ausirâ€™s Pleasure is best smoked a few hours after clipping. With some effort, though, it can be well preserved and smoked at a later time. It is also best harvested late at night, when the mists from the Forest of Mists coat and soften the stalks. Then the young leaves are simply peeled off the stalk, talking long threads of stalk material with them.

The taste is a sweet and seductive on the palate as a loverâ€™s kiss but this heady mix of earthy and mineral elements hides the more dubious nature of the plant. Ausirâ€™s Pleasure stimulates the mind and body more than any other known leaf. All the euphoria and effects of freshly discovered love and the delights of lovers can be found in the smoking of this leaf but be warned, love is a fickle and the agony or despair of love lost and the pain of rejection are also the possible price of this tempting preparation. It is this convergence of pleasure and pain which has led many Layonarans to think that this plant is a gift from Xeen herself to her followers. To this end it is rumored that a process to extract a purified essence of the leaf exists and this substances is used in the creation of a ritual wine in some Xeenite ceremonies.

If you want to sit and enjoy a relaxing pipe, you'll reach first for some Flatbottom Leaf.  It is well known to be a pacifier of the senses. 

Many hard days work are left behind in a cloud of Flatbottom smoke.  Some fine medicines and sedatives are said to be made from this leaf as well.

Connoisseurs can often be heard giving praises to this smoking leaf.  Other leaves may be sharper, more pungent, with more unusual combinations of tastes, but no other leaf, it's widely held, is as balanced and well rounded as The Great Draw.

This leaf has been used in ranger and druid gatherings for ages, particularly in the Great Forest region.  The leaves are smoked as a central ritual exchange, and in great quantities used as an incense during meditation ceremonies.  Most, however, simply smoke it from a pipe.  

The taste is so smooth, and the smoke is so easy, those who smoke it often do so exclusively and form a strong attachment to it.  That's why it is called The Great Draw, some joke, not only because it is such a great draw from the pipe, but because it is the reason people are drawn to the Great Forest.

This leaf isn't much to look at.  Its aroma and raw taste are quite unremarkable as well.  But when dried, hanging upside-down by dangling stems, and then touched by fire, magic seems to happen.  The smoke actually billows green and tastes like perfect combination of green apple, chestnuts and roasted meat.  This smoking leaf has been a favorite throughout Roldem for as long as anyone can remember.  It is also a favorite among dwarves, for its cave habitat and bold flavors.

As the name suggests, this leaf erupts with a splendid sweetness in one's palate.  The honey taste can actually be overwhelming for some, and because of this is often accompanied by bitter brews.

Learning how to clip the plant properly, and which part to smoke, is challenging and open to fierce debate.  Some believe the lower leaves make the best smoking.  Others argue it is the higher leaves and their stems.  Some think the flower petals themselves should be gently plucked and combined with both types of leaves.

The Halflings who live in the Great Plains region of Dregar will argue weeks on end that this is the finest smoking leaf in all of Layonara.  It grows in the lush valleys and rolling hillsides of the Great Plains, mostly cultivated by families of Halfings who have lived in those parts and cultivated these herbs for as long as their family histories can be traced.

The leaf, when chewed or burnt, has an exceptional spicy sweetness to it.  It's this playful character which gives the leaf its playful name.  The leaf also seems to elevate ones mood, making those not acclimated to it almost seem giddy.  These qualities make the Plain's Exceptional a favorite throughout Layonara for entertaining and for company on long lonely strolls.

It took a Wolfswood Ranger to first smoke this plant, for no other would dare sink his hand deep into its thorny tentacles to clip off the soft curling leaves.  Though the leaves are soft, the stems are quite stout, and require either a firm grip or special shears to harvest just right.

Often you'll find a Wolfswood Ranger puffing on the Cuts, as they are called, during a break or relaxing after a hard day's patrol.  This sight is seen so often that some say the properties of this leaf are what give the rangers their sharpened senses and alertness.

One of the pastimes of the inhabitants of Omelas is a card game known as Creatures.  It is simple to play, yet many enjoy the combination of luck, strategy, and planning.  Though shunned by those seeking the more visceral thrills of the combat pits, most residents are happy pitting imaginary creatures against each other. 

The goal of Creatures is simple - defeat your player's avatar.  As the avatars are immobile game pieces with no combat ability, this can be a bit of a challenge.  Instead, cards are played by each side to summon creatures which do battle with your opponent's creatures and their avatar.  When one avatar falls, the game is over. 

An expert player is aware of the game's complexities.  Each creature card has a casting cost, as well as an attack and defense rating.  In order to play the card, you must have enough magic available to cover the card's casting cost. 

Magic is generated by magic generators, created by playing a magic generator card.  You can only play one generator per cycle, which limits the amount of magic you will have available to you early in the game. 

There are no clear turns in Creatures, as both players play cards continuously throughout play.  What limits the speed of the game are cycles.   At the beginning of every cycle, a new card is drawn for each player.  If a player has more than eight cards, one is randomly discarded.  Any magic generators that have had their power used up by casting spells will be replenished. It's also a time when additional magic generators may be put in play. 

At the beginning of the game, each player gets seven cards.  The first move of a game is to play a magic generator.  After the generator begins producing power, you can start summoning creatures.  You can summon as many creatures in your hand as you have magic from your generators.  Gameplay continues until one of the avatars is dead. 

There are non-creature cards you can play as well.  These spells are cast just like creature cards, but instead have a variety of effects on the game.  Read the descriptions carefully.

Certain cards can be sacrificed to produce different effects.  To sacrifice a creature, click on the gallows object to the left of the cards.

Layonara - Crime & Punishment

Law on the continent is primarily governed by a union of good between the Churches of Toran and Rofirein.

Organisation of the Law:

Official senior representatives of the church of Rofirein are responsible for overseeing the interpretation of the law and thus will act as a Judges when criminals are on trial. 
These judges in all cases are considered to have the best knowledge of Rofirein's will and are thus considered divine experts.  A priest of Rofirein is always the final deciding factor if the interpretation of the law is ever in doubt.

Powers Granted too Judges -

1.	Oversee any hearings as required. 
2.	Pass sentence upon the guilty as directed by their divine link to Rofirein. 
3.	Supersede the power of any local governing body in direct relation to interpretation of the law and punishment. 
4.	Revoke the powers of any law enforcer that has shown themselves to be unworthy of these burdens. 
5.	Consult with experts in specific fields as required for use as expert witnesses.  Specifically in the areas of Magic and Magical crime. 

Official senior representatives of the church of Toran (predominantly Paladins) are responsible for carrying out the will of the Judge and enforcing the law. Those chosen shall be known as "Justiciers".  These souls devote their lives too carrying out the duty of Toran and upholding the law.  Wherever possible a "Justicier" will be called upon to carry out all law enforcement in conjunction with local government.  Local law enforcement will relinquish in ALL cases their powers too that of the "Justicier".

Powers Granted too Justiciers - 

1.	Carry out the will of the divine court of Mistone with direct reference to punishment. 
2.	Apprehend any person believed to be guilty of a crime or as directed too by the divine court. 
3.	Where immediate action is required or a representative of Rofirein cannot be contacted carry out sentence and punishment for minor crimes. 
4.	Take control of and direct local authorities where serious crimes are involved or the stability of the continent is in jeopardy.

Local Authorities 

Local authorities are responsible for enforcing the law out with the presence of a Justicier and make up the majority of law enforcers.  These include but are not limited to Royal Guard, Local Guard etc

Individuals

Individuals have the right too -

1.	Petition the divine courts of Mistone for a hearing. 
2.	Petition a "Justicier" to apprehend a suspected criminal. 
3.	Petition the divine courts for a retrial where new evidence is discovered that is directly related to the case. 
4.	Stand as a representative during trial for an individual on trial. 
5.	Attend the court as a witness. 
6.	Receive fair and just judgement and punishment as directed by the divine Rofirein and Toran. 
7.	Appoint a representative to speak on their behalf at a trial. 
8.	Request trial by the divine courts of Mistone where fair trial and punishment is believed to have not been given by local authorities. 
9.	Be safe and secure within their home and owned lands. 
10.	Defend themselves and their property with use of appropriate force if threatened by those out with law enforcement. 
11.	Be innocent until proven guilty. 
12.	Be informed of any changes to the law made by the Churches of Rofirein and Toran.

Anything not covered by these rights will be left to the discretion of the representatives of Rofirein and Toran and assessed on an individual basis.

Crimes and their Punishment by Category

Crimes and their punishments are decided directly by the representative of the church of Rofirein who oversees the trial however the following is a guideline:

Major Crimes (Usually carry sentences of death or imprisonment decided directly by the Judge) 
Murder 

Intermediate Crimes (Do not carry sentences of death but usually prolonged periods of imprisonment or related things) 
Counterfeiting.
Impersonation of a Law enforcement official.
Rape
Theft of large items (repeat offences)
Man slaughter
Adultery

Minor Crimes (Will never carry death sentences and rarely long term prison sentences. More likely community service or rehabilitation at correctional institutes. Time in the stocks, fines, flogging etc)
Theft of minor items (first offence)
Assault
Resisting Arrest
Slander
Worship of unrecognised deities determined to be evil or directly threatening to the continent.

Deliar

Aliases: The Blessed One, The Protector and Provider  
Race: Halfling 
Worshippers: Halflings (normally male) and merchants or shopkeepers of every race.
Domains: Good, Protection, and Travel 
Governs: Trade, Money, Wealth, Luck, Fate, Harmony, Family 

Dogma: 
     Trade is the best road to enlightenment and enrichment. Use trade to bring prosperity to everyone in the world. Seek out and develop new markets and new opportunities. Hone your skills as a tradesman. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Deliar's worshippers favor a short sword, mainly because of its portability and variety of uses. They have also been known to embellish their swords with precious metals and pommel gems to show their wealth and, consequently, Deliar's favor. 

     Clerics of Deliar tend to wear chain mail, adorning it with pricey metals like gold, silver, or mithril. The higher the rank of the cleric, the rarer the metal and the more favored and wealthy they are. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Despite Deliar being a god worshiped by merchants and shopkeepers of all races, the real clergy mostly consists of halflings. Deliar's halfling followers tend to live in small clans, with the elder being the leader, though normally there is little need for any type of leadership because halflings seem to naturally work together.

     Temples are normally tents, for the lives of Deliar's servants are rarely sedentary. Protection for the temples is also easier this way, as they are not in set locations. However, most larger, more prosperous cities have huge, exquisitely decorated temples to Deliar.

     Clerics can be found praying multiple times of the day. They pray for luck before a trade, believing that it brings wealth and harmony to the family.
 
Prayers to Deliar often revolve around trade and travel:
     "Father Deliar, bless this journey with good fortune and protect us from harm."

Welcome to the Wild & Dead Magic Disturbance Tool for GMs.

This tool is used to add a temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone (which is a disturbance in the Al'Noth) to an Area. An Area can only have one Disturbance; the Disturbance affects the entire Area.

A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area which is already a permanent Wild or Dead Magic Zone. A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area marked as a no temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone Area.

Disturbances do not persist across Module resets.

Adding a Wild or Dead Magic Disturbance will create a Placeable Object for the players to interact with. This allows them to attempt to repair the disturbance in the Al'Noth. Success is dependant upon the player's highest Spellcaster level, their Spellcrafting ability, whether they are a Lucindite or Aragenite, the use of any special (World Leader Reward) Disturbance repairing items, and the difficulty of the Disturbance to be repaired. It should be noted that failure is likely to be fatal.

The Disturbance repair difficulty can be altered any time after the Disturbance has been added to the Area. There are five difficulty settings, ranging from Simple (100% multiplier to the chance of success) to Impossible (0% multiplier to the chance of success).

The Disturbance Object is created 1.5 meters in front of the tool activator, facing the activator.

The Disturbance Object can be created directly from the DM-Client "Creator" (under "Placeable Object/Custom/Visual Effects/Magic Effects"). However, it will need to be conversed with immediately afterwards by the GM to properly attach the Disturbance to the Area. Until then, it is non-functional.

A reference manual for voice commands for DMs.

There MUST be an NPC, summoned creature, familiar or "voice" within range for these functions to work.

This covers voice features other than the *emotes* that are covered in the Player Voice Command book.  The majority of these functions are simply shortcuts for what can be done with the wands, but they are quicker if you are comfortable with them.


.set / .get / .got functions
----------------------------------------

These allow you to set an NPC to a key like "!", "@", or "#".  Once set you can use them just like using ":" which is the default setting.

EX:   .set % will set the last voice target to %.

You can then use "/dm :text here" for your default NPC or "/dm %" for this character.

.get % - brings this set character to you.
.got % - takes your avatar to that character.


.broadcast commands
-----------------------------------

These commands will change how dicerolls are reported for .skill rolls and for rolls performed by the DMFI DM Dicebag

.dm           - DM send only
.private     - DM and player
.local         - roll is given via TALK
.global       - roll is given via SHOUT


.skill checks
-------------------

*TARGET NOTE*  This category will reference the last DMFI  target.  This allows you to speak for an NPC (target one with the voice widget) and roll for player (then target player with target widget prior to "scene") without manually changing the target.

All skills and abilities are available.  "all" is an optional ending  (for an NPC it rolls for all in the area and for a PC target, it is the party)

.wisdom or .wisdom all

Two animation shortcuts:

.anin  - animations NO
.aniy  - animations YES


.appearance
--------------------

*NOTE*  This function and the .skill checks use the last DMFI Target.  All other functions use the default voice target (ie one tied to ":")

Allows the change appearance to be targetable.  For a complete list of accepted entries, examine the DMFI Target / Appearance Data Widget.  Type must be ALL CAPS like shown in the widget.

.appearance COW
.appearance BALOR

-------------------------

4 general level buffs of .buff low, .buff mid, .buff high, and .buff epic.

Other options are:
 
barkskin
elements
haste
invis
unplot
plot

.lan commands
------------------------

Set an NPC to speak a particular language
EX:  .lan drow

.faction commands
------------------------------

Set target to a default faction
EX: .fac commoner

----------------------------

.dam - damage by some amount / .dam 8
.dism - dismiss the target

.fly - fly away
.fol - follow me

There MUST be an NPC, summoned creature, familiar or "voice" within range for these functions to work.  Repeated text is ALWAYS ignored (ie in testing hi, hi, hi)

BASIC VOICE FUNCTIONS:
-----------------------------------------
**structure is /dmSPACE **
The SPACE is mandatory.  The basic structure is to use the DM channel to "hide" the throwing of your voice.  There is NO way to not spam the DM channel.

will speak your "native" language.  If you have more than one, use the language widgets to determine the language you will be speaking.

/dm ; your text here

Your familiar or companion will say your text.

/dm ,your text here

Your summoned creature will say your text.


*emotes*
--------------
Bracketing text between two * will attempt to perform an emote.  This does NOT need to use the DM channel.  This applies to simple spoken text by the PC.

This will work for DM possessed creatures or for players.  The action will be taken by the speaker.

Two uses:  

1) is for skill checks or ability checks - ie *uses strength to move rock*

2) is for emotes - ie *bows to the leader of the town*

Appropriate actions include:

All abilities and all skills (spell them just like the actual skill or ability - ie use magic device)

This widget has three functions:

3) When targeting yourself, it destroys the nearest placeable.

<UNRECOGNIZED TOKEN> represents something that can be "recorded" in game.

There are two ways to set up the voice wand.  One is to write a script to load up the conversions (yuck) and the other way is to record them live using the DM client.

Recorded phrases are set as campaign variable and therefore have persistence - travel to new modules etc.  IF you record them in game,  then they are ALSO set as Tokens so you will see the text show up in the conversation to help your memory of what was recorded where.

Both tokens AND the recorded phrases are persistent - Recording them in game is recommended for easiest set-up.

The precise origins of this amulet are unknown, and as such things go, deeply shrouded in legend, rumor and hearsay.  The most plausable of these rumors is that it was created and worn by a powerful mage who many called the Stormcaller.

He was rumored both to be many things, from a devotee of Mist to a rather eccentric and insane evoker with a fascination with storms.  It was said that any time there was a storm near his home on the eastern shores of Dregar, he could be seen standing in the open at the edge of a cliff in the open, his arms stretched out above him amongst the wind, rain and lightning and seemingly without fear.  Some say he called the storms, while others claimed he simply reveled in their power. Still others say he used his own power to amplify that of the storms. For what purpose he might do any of this, no one knows.

The fate of the Stormcaller is likewise wrapped in supposition and rumor.  It was said that one morning, after a particularly violent midnight storm, his smoking remains were found near the edge of his usual cliff.  All that remained intact was his ever-present amulet, its large central gem replaying scenes of the most violent of storms ever to strike the coasts of Dregar.

The central gem of this necklace radiates magic even to the untrained.  It appears flawed at first, but looking into its depths, one can see the ever-changing chaos and energy of a fierce thunderstorm.

Constructed of a fine cloth and an unusual weave that seems to reflect very little light, making its exact color rather difficult to determine. As it moves for whatever reason, the same quality makes it seem to flow like some dark fluid.

The cut of this gem is unusual, its facets seeming to reflect inward and giving the gem an appearance of an inner glow.  The facets seem to be inside the gem itself, implying layer upon layer to a seemingly impossible degree.  Its complexity draws your eyes and thoughts inward to seek its depths.

At first glance, this stone looks to be decoratively carved with only aesthetic value.  Upon closer inspection, it is clear that the carvings are far more intricate than one might imagine.  Chains of interlocking runes form greater patterns of their own.  

For those with such sensitivities, there is an unmistakable aura of magic within this stone.

Feryl Drakeblood was a monster of a man who, with four kills to his credit, thought he had perfected the art of dragon slaying. He aided his efforts by creating magical equipment from his previous victories, including several different boots he mockingly called his Dragon Slippers. Amazingly, Feryl was not defeated by his preferred enemy, but was surprised by a small band of goblins on his way to a hunt.

These boots are all that remains of Feryl's legacy, and retain the lingering enchantments of this man's life of dragon slaying.  Who or what imbued these magics on the Dragon Slippers is unknown, be it Feryl or a hired scholar of magic and enchantment.  What does seem clear, is that the magics imbued within carry with them a distinct air of Feryl's attributes and deeds, both good and bad.  It is said that the gods amongst olden dragons had long ago laid an ancient curse upon these boots, and that all who wear them will one day meet the dragon who knows them for what they are, and exposes that weakness in the bearer's slaughter.

Layered in the finest metals from Layonara, these bracers comfortably mold to the user's arms. Cushioning the extremities in a soft velvet these bracers are nearly impossible to feel.

Red and silver plated bands border these terrifying gauntlets. Sharp skewering fingers that could tear the thickest of skins and a general size that would dwarf the hand of an Ogre, make these gloves something fierce.

Made by Dwarven Mothers to scare their kids, they have passed on from one generation to another with a far less jovial nature, and any who find themselves at the wrong end of these gauntlets, normally doesn't live to tell the story.

Granting seemingly unrestrained movement to even the most experienced Swordsman, these bracers balance hands and arms in perfect positions.

Never catching the wearer off-guard, those lucky enough to find these gloves normally end in the unlucky chase of a greedy pirate.

Such graceful shaping enhances the skills of even the most talented performing, granting insight into harmonious patterns, never seen before.

Allowing for the most advanced intricate Weave patterns, these gloves enhance the ability of the wearer to mold magic to their desires.

Precious on their own, these extremely rare gloves are a sight to behold.

Contrasting perfectly with any surface, the fine material these gloves are made of allow for inticrate examination.

Ancient documents exist still of the first known war where elves, dwarves, and humans united.  In the effort to protect their own lands as well as that of the less established free races of gnomes and halflings alike, the nations once at war united to combat the hordes of monstrous beings in the years of the -1800's.

During this age of strife coupled with unprecedented racial unity, the existance of many heroes had been documented and still exist in journals today.  One group of heroes emerged in these annals that would be known as the Order of Hryndel, a group who seems by all accounts to have held faith to an order that most closely resembles what we know today as a Sacred Fist.   As for what religion they followed is lost to time.  What is known is that these guantlets bear their namesake for the small but ever vigilant temple of this order.  It is said that during the wars of this tumultuous age, Hryndel's order patrolled the borderlands of lesser, mostly defenseless towns, villages, and clans of all races alike.  They would cover massive distances at great speeds to ensure their watch, acting purely in a defensive manner which exhibited their distaste for the allegiances and goals of the wars.  The order protected the free races they knew to exist in relative peace, but they operated under no banner save for this common effort of this particular vigil.

Shunned by the armies of humans, dwarves, and elves during their age of war for their non-participation in any semblance of the alliance's organization... time has told Hryndel's tale far more fondly as history looks back at their efforts.  By all estimation this strange order was vastly more effective then the larger armies organized by rulers of varying origin, and in their purely defensive task they likely provided a means for more constant supply of surviving youth to join ranks in the wars.

The guantlets themselves are made by a strangely flexible weave of cobalt scales laid over an extremely thick leather of unknown origin.  What power has blessed these gloves is not known by many, but their vigil remains eternal in the hands of those that live up to their namesake's intent.
These gloves sparkle at the fingers' tips.

Folian S'pae

Aliases: The Longstrider, Prince of Wolves  
Race: Wood Elf 
Alignment: NG 
Worshippers:  Wood Elves, though many rangers of various races also follow Folian. 
Domains:  Animal, Good, Plant, Sun.      Most Popular are Animal, Plant
Governs: Animals, forests 

Dogma: 
     Be one with the forests and live in harmony with nature's creatures. Take no more than you need and give as much as you can in return. 

Clergy Favored Weapons and Clothing: 
     Those who follow Folian are very skilled archers. Some even go so far as to make bows their sole weapon. Long swords, scimitars, and rapiers are the chosen blades of Folian's followers, but clubs and staves are common due to the wood from which the weapon was created. Most who use clubs, staves, or bows make their own or have it handed down to them. Folian approves of those resourceful enough to carve - often literally - their weapons out of what nature gives them.

     Leather armors are the primary garb of Folian's clerics, though lighter metal suits are used to some extent. Armors are dyed in greens and browns. Clerics of Folian will never don a full suit of armor, which, cumbersome and heavy, prevents them from feeling the connection to the lands they are sworn to protect. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Due to the highly individualistic nature of Folian himself, there is no structured Church of Folian. The majority of followers have been rangers at some point in their lives before turning to the more settled life of a cleric. Clerics usually maintain their link to the forests, not moving to cities or villages.
     Because of this, temples of Folian are always found in or near to wooded areas. Some of the oldest known places of worship are inside humongous trees, veritable living temples of nature.

     Clerics of Folian have no set time of day to pray for power and guidance, nor do they pray every single day. They pray when needed and as often as needed, no more, no less. They do, however, prefer to be close to nature when the need for prayer arises, often choosing to stop and pray in a grove of trees rather than inside the walls of town.
     Spring is significant to Folian's worshippers, for the woods and their inhabitants typically wake from their long winter's slumber to start life anew at this time of year.

Prayers: 
     "Longstrider, guide my steps. Help me to defend and serve the wood and those within."
A common goodbye: 
     "May The Prince of Wolves watch over you."

Grannoch

Aliases: 
     Mother of Giants (used by all giant-kin), Lady of Lightning (used by storm giants), Shaper of Stone (used by stone giants), Tamer of Flame (used by fire giants), Mistress of Cold (used by frost giants)
Race: Giant
Worshippers: 
     Usually giants, half-giants or humans with some giant blood in their ancestry.
Domains: 
     Protection, Fire, Air, Earth, and Water. The cleric always has the Protection domain together with one elemental domain which is always based on the type of giant they are (Fire for fire giants, for instance)
Governs: Storms, earthquakes, volcanoes, ice

Dogma: 
     The first words of Grannoch when she created the giant races of Layonara were these:
     "My Children, I, Grannoch, Mother of Giants, am the One that is Four. The Four are One inside Me. Since I am the Four, none can be supreme."

     Mother of the giant races of Layonara, Grannoch is worshipped by all of them, be they storm, fire, frost or stone giants.
     Being the ruler of all four elements, and firmly believing that none is superior to the other, Grannoch has laid down the Dogma of Elements to her clerics: "My Children, I, Grannoch, Mother of Giants, am the One that is Four. The Four are One inside Me. Since I am the Four, none can be supreme."
     Since all giant kin are her children, she does not favor one giant people above the other.  As with all children, this does not mean that the different giant kin do not strive to be better than the other: all try to curry her favor.

     Grannoch balances the elements, since she embodies all elements. All elemental powers are granted by Grannoch, and thus, all are equally powerful. None should reign supreme and those striving to make one more powerful than the other should be stopped. Never slay a fellow follower of Grannoch. Protect your homes and families.

    Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
Grannoch's followers favor mauls, often enchanted with the elemental power of the domain of the cleric. 

     Clerics are usually dressed in the colors of their domain, so red for fire, dark blue for water, brown or green for earth, and light-blue to white for air. The elemental color is possibly combined with another color of their choice, but the other color is never the color of another element. 

     Clergy and Temples: Most giant communities have a couple of clerics, both male and female; usually the most powerful is the leader, but there is no specific title given to this cleric. There is also no large, community- spanning hierarchy, although every giant race has a male and a female cleric that are considered the most wise and powerful. These are generally referred to as the Son and the Daughter of the particular element: the Son of Air and the Daughter of Air, for example. It is rare to have such powerful clerics dwelling in the same community, however.

     Grannoch is generally prayed to at dawn and at dusk, for example by praying to a fire, a bowl of water, with hands touching the ground, or with arms extended upwards to the sky. She is also invoked when strength or aid is needed: when going into battle or when child labor is difficult, for instance. When praying to Grannoch, clerics try to use words related to elements in their prayers.

     For example, a prayer of a cleric with the Earth domain, before going into battle:
     "Oh Grannoch, Shaper of Stone, make me strong as the bedrock and my foes tremble before me as if you were quaking the earth itself!"  
     Or, a cleric with the Water domain, praying to give a mother strength during a particularly difficult childbirth:
"Mother of Giants, hear my plea, please assist your daughter in bringing another one of your children into the world. Make this birth as easy as the effortless flow of a mountain stream."

     The only special day of worship is the first day of spring, also called Birth of Giants, when all giants remember the birth of their races on Mount Tulbane, as well as the birth of all the giants born since the last Birth of Giants.

Gnomes
    Gnomes are extremely intelligent and also very sought after as inventors and engineers of the highest order. They prefer to remain with their own kin, although they are also at home with dwarves (whom they are distantly related to). They are renowned for both their technical expertise and their prankish nature, though their pranks and jokes can make them hard to get along with. Gnomes are even smaller than dwarves, with the average gnome standing at about 3 feet in height. However, they have a light frame and small muscles, giving them an average weight of 45 pounds. Like many other races, gnomes have a great longevity with an average life expectancy of 340 years, though some live much longer. They share the Dwarven pride in facial hair, though gnomes prefer to have a trimmed beard compared to the long bushy ones of the dwarves. The gnomes relate well with the Dwarven and halfling races and the three get on well together. The gnomes' varied skills make them capable adventurers and their curiosity usually leads them on adventures to learn more about the world.

Deep Gnomes (Sverfneblin)
    Deep Gnomes, also called svirfneblin in their own language, are not much like their cousins on the surface. They're a gruff lot and very suspicious of other races; for good reason, as they've been betrayed or waged war upon numerous times by the other races that dwell in the Underdark, They are very good miners and gemcrafters and their jewelry are prized possessions, both in the Underdark and on the surface.

Personality: 
    Deep Gnomes are distrustful, and treat every stranger as possible enemy. However, once they've given their trust, they're loyal allies. They are not a passionate people unless it comes to gems and jewelry. They love metalwork, even more if it is made to bear gems, especially crowns, necklaces or rings. They're expert crafters and don't do half-jobs, since their culture is infused with a perfectionism and respect for the work.

Physical Description: 
    Deep Gnomes are no taller than 3 or 4 feet and have grayish skin, camouflaging them against the subterranean rocks. Their eyes are black or dark gray. Males are nearly always completely bald, but if they do have hair it's more like white patches. Females usually do have hair, which also tends to be pure white.
During the ages they've lived below ground they've grown very ugly in the eyes of other races.

Relations with other races: 
    Deep Gnomes do not trust other races, and they rarely ally themselves with anyone, preferring to remain neutral and outside of every conflict. However, the drow hunt them with a passion, so conflict cannot always be avoided. With the guidance of their goddess however, they manage to stay hidden very well. This guidance, together with the strange magics of the Underdark have given the Svirfneblin some unique powers of hiding and resiting magic.

Alignment: 
    Usually neutral good

Religion: 
    Deep Gnomes worship the goddess Beryl, who shares their passion for gems.

Language: 
    Common, Undercommon, Gnomish

Names: 
    Names often have to do with gems. Common surnames are Gemcutter or Opalcarver. First names are a lot shorter than the names of their surface cousins.

Adventurers: 
    Deep Gnome adventurers are not very common as they do not like to deal with other races. The occasional Svirfneblin that does leave his home settlement is usually a bold merchant.


Forest Gnomes
    This subrace of gnomes is not so common as the others, but its members fill an important niche in their environment. Forest gnomes are shy and reclusive, and often the mere arrival of human settlers within their wooded domain is enough to send them migrating to a new, unspoiled home. Nevertheless, they have been known to aid adventurers from other races and fight monsters invading the forests they inhabit. 

Personality: 
    Forest gnomes prefer a life in which no one knows who they are or where they live. They dwell in large swaths of woodland, and - unlike the other gnomish subraces - prefer to dwell in houses that are at least partially above ground. They are creatures of nature far more than any of their cousins, and to those rare folks who meet them they can prove to be steadfast allies and delightful companions. 

    However, forest gnomes have not totally abandoned the love of gemstones that is so inherent to all gnomes. The emerald is the favored gem of the forest gnomes, no doubt because it most accurately reflects the healthy green of their verdant homelands. While these gnomes can make excellent gemsmiths and jewelers, their work tends to be reverent images of the flora and fauna that are such a key part of their environment. 

Physical description: 
    The tiny forest gnomes are the smallest of the gnomish subraces. They share the stocky physique of the rock gnomes and the bulbous nose which is so characteristic of the race in general. They are the only gnomes inclined to wear long beards and hair. 

    The skin of a Forest Gnome tends toward a greenish cast of tan, rather like bark. Their eyes are generally brown or blue, but green eyes are not unheard of. Their hair color is usually brown, often becoming gray or white in old age. 

Relations with other races: 
    Forest gnomes prefer to live alone without contact to other races. They are friends with the elves who cohabit the forests. They hate orcs, goblins, and lizardmen and tend to attack these races which often invade the forest gnomes' homes. 

Alignment: 
    Usually true neutral 

Religion:
    Forest gnomes often worship nature gods such as Katia and Aeridin. 

Language: 
    Common, Gnome 

Names: 
    Forest gnome names are similiar to other gnomes with the exception that their surnames often including something nature-related. For example: Male: Burgell, Dorag. Female: Lyiss, Jaree. Surnames: Redtree, Greatleaf. 

Adventurers: 
    Forest Gnome adventurers are extremely rare, even more so than the race. The reason for one to adventure outside the forests they live in would have to be a very special one.

Grand

Aliases: Destroyer of Dwarves
Race: Orc
Worshippers: Orcs
Domains: War, Earth, Evil, Destruction 
Governs: Mining, smithing, craftsmanship

Dogma: 
     Other creatures are inferior to orcs, and all lands rightfully belong to the orcish hordes. Destroy the dwarves and all that they hold dear as well as all those who follow He That Is Not To Be Named.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of Grand are required to craft their own weapons as homage to their god. It does not matter what weapon it is, as long as it is made in the name of Grand. They usually enchant the weapons for added destructive power. They do not wear leather armors, only metal which they've also preferably mined and made themselves.
They usually wear a rough representation of an axe around their necks.

Clergy and Temples:
     Since Grand has not been a god for long, the faith is still young and highly disorganized. Often the clergy is in conflict with the ancestor worship that is still the main faith of the orcish hordes. If there is a small group of clergy in an orcish stronghold, they're led by the strongest orc. Temples are often just shacks or tents and are also used as smithies or crafting houses.

     Followers of Grand will never utter the name of Dorand, as this is the ultimate affront to Grand.
     Prayers to Grand are rough and to the point, often not more than short sentences like "Grand, make me strong!"

     Grand began his existence as an orc, but was destined for far greater heights. He spurned the crude work of his brethren, determined to become a true craftsman. To that end, he turned to Dorand, the god of craftsmanship. Grand forged an axe of truly wondrous quality, and laid it before the altar as an offering to Dorand. Up until this point, Dorand had seen Grand as simply another craftsman in the throng of worshippers, but when he saw the marvelous axe, he looked to its maker...and saw an orc, enemy of his dwarven people. Enraged at the audacity of the savage, beast, Dorand slammed Grand's hands down on the altar and used the axe to chop off Grand's fingers.
     Lost and forlorn, Grand wandered the wilderness. He had already turned away from his tribe, and his god had rejected him and destroyed his ability to create. Numb to all feeling and lacking a sense of purpose, he meandered into a cave, where he met a dwarven miner. The sight of the dwarf reminded Grand of Dorand's cruelty, and white-hot rage replaced the emptiness inside of him. At that moment, Grand offered his soul up to anything that could help him avenge his undoing...and something answered.
Where once were useless stubs, Grand saw his hands had been imbued with twisted, alien tools; the claw and hammer at the ends of his arms were mockeries of the blacksmithing utensils he had once used to forge his masterpiece. Driven by rage and enabled by his new appendages, Grand smote the dwarf and tore him to shreds.
