Dark Elves 

    The Dark Elves, The Drow, Those Below, Those Who Have Turned to Evil, The Accursed. These are the names given by surfacers to the obsidian-skinned elves who dwell in Underdark cities. Mysterious, elegant, dark and deadly, they are feared and hated by all the races of Layonara. They are masters of magic and treachery, trusted by none, not even each other.

    When Dark Elves come to the surface to raid, they come at night, and every child of Layonara has heard the whispered tales of the Dark Ones even before they have been officially warned of Those Below.

    Ages past, Dark Elves were already known to be a proud and warlike race, attacking their neighbors for power and wealth, or other, more insidious gains. However, after The Betrayal by the other Elven Clans around the year -2311, they were led below ground by a Dark Elven hero, Baraeon Ca'duz. With the help of Pyrtechon, Baraeon taught his people to thrive in their new subterranean home, the Underdark.
Their warlike nature had not changed after The Descent, and it did not take them long to start to establish their own territories in the vast reaches of the Underdark, often capturing settlements of other species and enslaving them in the process. However, they also fought among themselves for control of their new found realm, and as no Dark Elf trusts another, this led to the numerous independent city-states where most Dark Elves dwell today. 

Personality: 
    The Dark Elf deities, Vierdri'ira and Baraeon Ca'duz continuously strive to prove themselves better than the other. This is reflected in the personality of the Dark Elves as well. Females think they are better than males, and vice versa.
Dark Elves enjoy magic, especially releasing its power. They also love sculptures or other crafted items (especially well-made lethal weapons). They also admire physical beauty; Dark Elves are proud of their physique and do not hesitate to show it. This has also led to the custom of slaying all newborns with physical deficiencies.
Dark Elves are always in search of more personal power. Therefore, they do not trust other Dark Elves. Instead, they strive to weaken or eliminate their rivals to gain a greater advantage. This is not just the case between cities, but also in the politics of the various noble Houses inside a certain city, or even within a House itself. It is this internal strife between the Dark Elves themselves which keeps the surface races safer than they would be if the Dark Elves were united. On the occasions some Dark Elf cities did unite, they wreaked great destruction, as the capture of the human city of Westgate in the year -103 and the destruction of Port Hampshire in 834 can attest to. If all the Houses of a single city were to unite for one purpose, they could bring cities like Hlint and Haven to their knees.
Dark Elves also do not trust other races. They accept none as superior to theirs, although they may admit some races, such as Illithid or Duergar, are almost equals. Treaties with these races are usually born through hard bargaining and mutual-gain agreements. Dark Elves will negotiate with other (lesser) species, but will break such agreements at the moment they are no longer beneficial. To the Drow, bargains with lesser races are not considered to be binding. Most races have learned by now that they should be prepared for treachery when, not if, it comes.

Physical Description: 
    Dark Elves are a lot like surface elves, they tend to be lithe, slim, and graceful in their build, movements and appearance. The most striking thing that sets them apart from the surface elves is their obsidian skin. Also, females tend to be bigger and stronger than males. Because of this females tend to be the better fighter, but males tend to be the better mage. 
The second thing that sets them apart from surface elves is their eyes. Dark Elf eyes are usually red, but green, brown, or black eyes are not uncommon. When angered or upset, all Dark Elf eyes tend to turn redder. 
Thirdly, most Dark Elves have white hair, tending a bit towards yellow for females and towards gray for males as they get older. Occasionally, a Dark Elf can have silver or copper-hued hair.
Dark Elves can generally live as long as surface Elves can, and they do not show their age until about their 600th year. 

Relations with Dark Elves: 
     Dark Elf cities are ruled by a council of noble Houses, the Talthara. Every city has its First Patriarch and its First Matriarch, who preside over the Talthara (but not necessarily comply with its wishes). The Patriarch is always a cleric of Baraeon Ca'duz, and the Matriarch is always a cleric of Vierdri'ira. They need not be from the same House, although every House strives to occupy both positions for ultimate supremacy.

    Each House also has its Matriarch and Patriarch, who together rule a House. However, because of the gender struggles inherent in Drow society, it is unlikely that a House occupies both First positions on the Talthara, since a strong House Matriarch does not often condone a strong Patriarch in her own House. 
Two other powerful positions in a Dark Elf city are those of Archmage and Warmistress.

    Since males are more adept at magic, the Archmage is always a male. The Warmistress is always female, since females tend to be of bigger build. The Archmage and Warmisstress are the most important advisors to the First Matriarch and First Patriarch. In general, the House who provides a First Matriarch or First Patriarch will also try to control one of these positions. Of course, the other Houses are not likely to just allow this to happen.

    The Houses continually vie for supremacy in the Talthara, as well as for wealth and power. This struggle for power is also apparent between Dark Elf cities. Plans to increase Dark Elf power and influence are usually made by Houses who are already in excellent position, and who have nothing to lose in the plan.

    The surface world is hardly aware of the nature of Dark Elven society. 
The exact number and location of Dark Elven cities is subject to speculation. Even the Dark Elves themselves likely do not know exactly how many cities there are, due to the vastness of the Underdark and its ever changing caves and corridors.

Relations with other races: 
    Most dealings between Dark Elf cities and surfacers involve the slave trade. Dark Elves usually have goblinoid slaves, such as goblins, orcs and hobgoblins. Kobolds are considered too small, agile and independent to make good slaves. Human slaves are valued, but considered dangerous if they are trained fighters or magic-users. Slaves who are adept at crafting are valued highly, but most do not last long in the Underdark.

    With regard to other races, dwarves, humans, and of course the darthir (a word meaning both Surface Elf as well as Traitor in Dark Elf language) are traditional Dark Elf enemies on the surface. As far as other Underdark races go, Illithid and Duergar are traded with but never trusted or befriended, and there is no race a Dark Elf enjoys killing so much as a Deep Gnome.
 
Alignment: 
    The vast majority of Dark Elves are evil. However, there are a few neutral or good Drow, but these do not survive long in the twisted, cruel society of Dark Elven cities.

    Dark Elven Lands: Dark Elf cities can be found throughout the Underdark. A few locations are known, but there are probably more. Rumor has it that there is a city made of good Dark Elves, refugees from their vicious society, but that may be a myth. 

Religion: 
    Vierdri'ira and Baraeon Ca'duz (those who fail The Test are killed or turned into Driders, see also the entries for both deities). Before the treachery of Az'atta, the Dark Elven deities did not yet make a distinction on being a purely male or female faith. However, after being betrayed by Az'atta, Baraeon had his male followers expel or kill all of his female clerics as act of vengeance for Az'atta's betrayal.

    This then led to Vierdri'ira expelling all her male followers, who then turned to Baraeon Ca'duz, further polarizing Dark Elf society.

Language: 
    Dark Elves have their own language, also known as "Deep" or "Low Drow," which does not resemble the language spoken by the Surface Elves except in eloquence and musical inflection. All Dark Elves also learn "The Silent Language," a kind of "hand code" as detailed as spoken language. The Silent Language is used to communicate when silence is needed. This language, which requires a lot of tutoring, is a requirement before any Dark Elf is allowed to accompany a raiding party.

    Then there is the third, almost archaic language of "High Drow." This language is known and used only by the high clergy.

    Languages: Deep Drow, The Silent Language, Common, Elven, Undercommon. 
Other Languages: Duergar, High Drow (cleric only, for rituals)

Names: 
    Dark Elves are named at birth by their mothers. Like their Elven cousins, Dark Elves prefer names that flow off the tongue; however, their names tend to have a harsher sound to them. Names reflect and represent the race's attitudes and philosophies and usually consist of a prefix and one or more suffixes.

Female Names: 
    Zaraun (Zar meaning shadow, aun meaning dancer/player)
    Jyslin (Jys meaning hard/steel/unyielding, lin meaning arm/armor/commander).

Male names: 
    Quillyn (Quil meaning mighty, lyn meaning assassin/killer)

Adventurers: 
    Dark Elves do not often leave their cities by themselves to adventure. However, sometimes they are cast out (if they are not just killed) and make their way through the Underdark, and sometimes even to the surface.
An Adventurer's Guide to the Dark Elves

The Duergar

    Also known as the Gray Dwarves, the Duergar are one of the more commonly known races of the Underdark. They have lived since the Dwarven nations split up during the race wars, thousands of years ago. Their goal is now to dominate the riches in metals and gems found deep in Underdark. They could care less about the surface, believing that the potential rewards are outweighed by having to brave its glaring sun. Unlike the Dark Elves, the Duergar only rarely raid surface settlements, preferring to remain in the safeness of the Underdark. Dwarven settlements, being underground, enjoy no such safety: the Duergar seem to relish attacking the towns and holds of their former brethren, and will go so far as to form alliances with other races to supplement their strikes against the other dwarves.

    They live in cities hewn out of the bedrock of the Underdark. Like other dwarven nations, the Duergar ascribe to a clan system. Rulership is hereditary, and the Duergar are fiercely loyal to their clans. 

Personality: 
    Duergar hate other dwarves and are distrustful of other races (and, to a lesser extent, other Duergar clans). However, when threatened by outsiders, the clans will put aside their differences to band together against their enemies.

    They are known as a devious, greedy people that excel in mining, blacksmithing, and battle. They tend to be vicious and cruel, and their happiness often comes from the suffering or loss of others. The Duergar do trade with other races in weapons, armor, slaves, and other commodities...as long as they'll make a healthy profit.

    Duergar are distasteful of arcane magic users and therefore have none. However, there are rumors that the Duergar practice a strange runic magic. 

Physical Description: 
    Duergar look a lot like other dwarves; however, they are immensely ugly. They're also a lot less hairy. Females don't have any facial hair, and most males are bald. Their hair color varies from dark to gray. Duergar females are a proud lot, but are rarely seen by other races since they do not participate in trading or war. Together with the race's intense ugliness, the concealment of the Duergar females has given birth to the rumor that there are only male Duergar, who are hewn directly (and not very skilfully) from the rock.

    Duergar garments are bland; they often dress in clothes with a grayish hue, which allows them to blend into the stone of their native environment. They hardly ever wear jewelry, as a reflection of light on a gem might give away one's location while raiding. If they do wear jewelry, it is usually blackened out or covered.

    Their time in the Underdark has also given them some abilities that the other dwarven people do not have like being able to turn themselves invisible. 

Relations with other races: 
    Gray Dwarves are loathed by nearly every race on Layonara. However, they do often ally themselves with other races if it serves their evil purpose, using the rare minerals and gems they mine from the Underdark to coerce other races to join them. Temporary alliances with the Dark Elves are not unheard of, as long as both sides continue to benefit from the arrangement. 
 
Temperment:
   The vast majority of Duergar are evil. Those of other alignments are often cast out of the Gray Dwarf communities.

Religion: 
    Most Gray Dwarves worship Sulterio. Those involved in blacksmithing also worship Dorand.

Language: 
    Common, Duergar, Dwarven, Deep Drow 

Names: 
    Duergar names do not vary much from other dwarven names. Their surname is usually the name of their clan.

Adventurers: 
    Duergar do not go to the surface willingly. If they do, they're either forced or exiled. The glare of the sun pains their eyes and they want to avoid it. Those that do find themselves on the surface tend to adapt as much as possible after a long period of discomfort and end up in the mercenary trade.
An Adventurer's Guide to the Duergar

Blackfeather Mountains
    The Blackfeather Mountains sit just north of the forest of Mists. Years ago the Broken Glade Giants drove out the hordes of crows that settled in the eastern parts of the forest. No one is sure why the crows were there or why the Giants drove them out, but after they flapped wildly around the forest for a week or so they came to rest on the mountains just to the north. If you walk through one of the long abandoned dwarf trails through these peaks you'll find layers of crow's feathers at your feet. Despite the slippery footing, it is still worth the treacherous walk. The views of the forest, desert and ocean from even the lower ranges are breathtaking.

Black Hills
    When you are in the Black Hills you'll know it. The soil here is jet black and seems to radiate an unnatural darkness. Even on a cloudless summer's noon, the hills seem dimmed. These dark, foreboding mounds can be seen from a distance. Most people are thankful for this, as they become easier to avoid. Despite the many roads which wind their way through these hills, travelers are seldom seen.
    If you do venture to the Black Hills, and climb as high as you can go, you'll find an area known as Hangman's Bluff. Not too long ago Zoroon's Castle faced a major uprising from the peasants in the countryside. Zoroon was a reasonable and respected leader. But his son and even more so his grandson were powermongers, bent on economic exploitation for personal gain. When the peasants could no longer tolerate the squalor and servitude which had ground them to near death, they took up arms and attacked the taskmasters and tribute collectors of Zoroon III. They were quickly suppressed and many were captured. A line of their emaciated forms stretched up the slopes of the tallest Black Hill bluff. On the top, they were hung, one after the other, for three days straight. Many watched. Most cried and the word went out about the intolerable injustice being done in this central Dregar province. It didn't take long for people from the city of Dresden and the Forest of Mists to rally to their cause. Zoroon III was overthrown soon after. The castle now stands nearly abandoned, certainly not the political figure it had once been.
Some residents of the central Dregar area trace the dark dirt and dimness of the Black Hills to this event. They argue that the hundreds of souls tortured and ripped from their body spread a pungent lament across the landscape. A few priests of Pranzis were recently sent to investigate this phenomenon. They didn't get far with the research, however, as they were run off by a camp of bugbears from the Eternal Flame clan. These elite agents of Bloodstone's evil machinations find the twisted and miserable conditions of the Black Hills quite welcoming. Since few people ever visit this woeful area, the bugbears were left to assemble numbers enough to best the Pranzis guards sent to deal with the situation.

Cave of the Snake
     The Cave of the Snake lies somewhere in the southern Serpent Mountains. Those few who have spelunked in this cave report that there are indeed large snakes in the depths. However, the upper layers are filled with Blood's Eternal Flame bugbears. There are reports of snake paintings on the walls of the upper levels and that the Eternal Flames, in any region, have shed snake skins wrapped around the handles of their weapons. This leads some bugbear experts to the conclusion that the Eternal Flame bugbears are a snake worshipping cult, and that this cave has central significance for their organization.

Corax Lake
    Every year, on the spring equinox, the people of Southern Dregar and the Pranzis area gather at Corax Lake for a festival. Joyous music and wild dancing ripple the surface of this unusually calm lake. People come in large groups to avoid the danger on the roads, quickly swelling the crowds at the lake to huge proportions. 
    The main event at the festival is the Corax Dive. When the Dive is about to begin, the crowd gathers around the lake and watches a small boat paddle out to the center. From the boat several long strands of woven rope with a large bright yellow rock tied to the end are lowered into the water. Along the rope are small detachable pouches of leather which are sealed off to float and suspend the rope. These pouches are painted particular colors at different lengths of the rope. The music changes from the festival tunes and resonates with the dangerous acts about to be performed. The divers then swim to the middle of the lake and when the whistle is blown their feet fly into the air and then disappear into the depths. The winner is the diver who can bring the deepest leather pouch to the surface.
    The excitement of the contest is heightened by the sheer depth of the lake. In some places, it is said, there is no bottom. Every few years one of the ropes goes missing, supposedly pulled by the yellow rock down into an eternal depth. The lake used to be called Deep Lake until Corax came along and stunned everyone with his diving ability. The half-orc barbarian dove swiftly to the bottom of one of the ropes and after an amazingly long time holding his breath emerged near the shore with the yellow rock rather than one of the leather pouches. The crowd was whipped into jubilation. After that day, people began to call the lake Corax Lake. In recent years the surveyors in Pranzis have made this name more official, giving the lake dual nomenclature.
    Corax's dive was hundreds of years ago. Since then no-one has come closer than 10 pouches away from the yellow stone. This fact has made people grow increasingly suspicious about Corax's feat and the nature of the lake.

Dalos Lake
    Dalos Lake is named for a mid-kingdom prince who used to daydream here. He spent such an inordinate amount of time at the banks of its calm and soothing waters that his father sent spies to monitor his activities there. That same trip, a giant snatched up the prince into his huge arms and lumbered away faster than they could follow. When the king learned of this he sent a brigade of his finest after his son's kidnapper. Many giants died in the pursuit and a few horsemen fell as well. When they reached the cave where his son was, they attacked the giant before surveying the situation. Nearly all involved died:  most of the brigade, over 50 giants, the son, and the kidnapping giant. With his cracked skull held in the firm arms of a Pranzis guard, the prince whispered that the giant was a friend, not a kidnapper, and he cursed his father for his meddling. 
    In commemoration of the wicked event, the king and the giant's ruler agreed to designate Dalos Lake as neutral ground. No skirmishes should be fought there between the giants and the Pranzis guards, but often are anyway. Beyond the lake the two great powers clash with fervent hatred and a skewed battle cry, both of which are rooted in that fateful series of events.

Dark Forest
    The Dark Forest is naturally dark. Black oaks create much of the dense canopy and the soil is a rich brown color. As if drawn by the name of this forest, a few hundred years ago something turned the essence of this forest figuratively dark as well. Many adventurers have sought the cause of this darkness, but they have only ever found its effects. These effects include dark spiders and dark treants, locally twisted and powerful varieties of spiders and treants. Rumors abound of a particularly deadly spider deep in the swamps at the northern rim of the forest. The forest has also become overrun by black snakes and shadow trolls, who have established some sort of complex organization and cave system just south of the forest.
    Those who have studied the forest believe that the whole area was cursed by an evil cleric long ago. Some believe that it happened while the drow concealed themselves in these forests to launch attacks upon Pranzis. They used the dense tree cover and unnatural darkness to conceal their dark deeds and shade their red eyes. Others think the timing is off, and that the forest was tainted a few decades before the drow arrived. They suggest that there is some unholy force which continues to flow into the River of Shadows and is then absorbed into the dark soil. The likely source of this unholy contamination is the crypts which are concealed by the dense forest growth. None, however, have delved more than a few hundred yards into the overwhelmingly evil Mosscrypt, so named for its mossy opening and entryway.

Darkland Mountains
    The Darkland Mountains to the north of the Great Rift seem to siphon some of its negative energy into the area, absorbing it into the unsettled earth. Things seem to change quickly and radically in the Darkland Mountains, as if some great force rearranges the whole range every day. This, of course, makes it impossible to have predictable routes through the range and makes it easy to get lost and cornered. The changes may be due to the forces from the Great Rift themselves, or they may be wrought at the hands of the Great Rift Giants who have migrated to this area. These massive and powerful creatures have been seen carrying boulders the size of houses. They may indeed have the collective strength to move the whole mountain, as it is suggested they do. Still, what purpose they have in doing so remains another of Dregar's great mysteries.

Deadman's Pass
    Deadman's Pass is the only road through the central ranges of Dregar if you are not on foot and well prepared. The pass separates the Spine and Serpent Mountains. At one point Pranzis protected the pass with intense vigilance. Deadman's Pass is the place that the "True Line," that started with Raklin Loenar as first Emperor in Pranzis, ended. The fifth ruler in that family line was slain by a guard that protected him in this pass, and to this day you can still see his grave.
    Now, however, since the Dark Forest just west of the pass has grown even darker and fewer people use the pass for legitimate travel, Pranzis has let its vigilance slip. Every once in a while you can hear someone in the capital crying out from the steps or a crate about what should be done about this crucial road. They have a point, as scouts have reported that the powerful forces of Blood have set up camp there and perform aggressive fundraising for their evil cause. "Didn't we learn anything from the Drow attacks?  A whole army can come through that pass and down through the Dark Forest!" The paranoid crier's warning spreads throughout the city, but the King's attention seems drawn elsewhere.

Drift Lands-Anuroch Desert
    The rain shadow of the Spine Mountains creates this expansive desert. It is so expansive that those desert druids and oasis dwellers have distinguished between three desert zones. There is the high mesa region, which is home to the Oasis giants. There is the deep valley desert in the northern areas, where scorpions and vipers are said to roam. There are also the dunes and sandstorm deserts, which are whipped into their wild forms by the eastern coastal gusts. There you can find armies of ants and formians, creatures whose sturdy exoskeletons protect them from the blasting sandstorms. These creatures have dwelled in the desert as long as anyone can remember. Their presence is simply natural for those who live in the Drift Lands.
    This desert is nicknamed the Drift Lands for one reason: huge sections of the desert seem to drift around. When they drift, they pull open great chasms and cause deep sinkholes. The shifting and churning desert has swallowed whole villages. The tips of their ruined abodes reach out from the sand as if in a last gasp for recognition. There are a few stable areas, though predictably, they tend to be home for the desert dwellers mentioned above and thus are the most dangerous.

Drift Lands Caves
    Beneath the Anuroch Desert are the Drift Lands Caves. These caves stretch in all directions underneath the great desert. Some believe the caves even open up in the Spine Mountains and Forest of Mists, but those routes are unlikely to be found and impossible to remain, because the same churning which pulls the desert around in maddening directions is also what gives form to these caverns. New caverns open and old ones fold in on themselves every day. This makes the Drift Lands Caves a risky but exciting venture for many dwarves and gnomes who seek the mineral treasures uncovered by the churning caverns.
Some treasure hunters also seek the great lost city of Anuroch. This city, the jewel of Dregar in the years before the great Cataclysm, is said to have fallen deep into the earth when the Cataclysm tore the desert into the huge chunks which slide around today. Treasure hunters boast that the vaults of this ancient city would hold riches beyond belief, and whoever finds them will surely be wealthy - and famous - all the days of her or his life.
    Only the mad or ridiculously brave will even set one foot into these caves to attempt to find the treasure or chip a few minerals. Oasis Giants block almost every stable passage in these caverns. And if those who delve deep enough, like few fateful parties have done, encounter one of Layonara's most feared beasts. The locals call her the Long Storm, a dragon whose very sight sends most people into a heart wrenching panic. The Long Storm emerges from the desert cave to torment Saudiria and other hamlets near the desert from time to time. Mostly she bursts in a huge cloud of sand from the smooth desert floor right at the beginning of a great sand storm and desert quake. It is unknown whether she causes them or knows they are about to happen and leaves the earth temporarily for the safe yet exposed sky. Either demonstrates her awesome power.

Forest Giant Cave
    Within the Forest of Mists there is a cave which seems to serve as the central settlement of the Broken Glade Giants. Their chief lives with his elite guard and many other giants among the amazing natural vaults and stalagmites and stalactites that form great pillars. When Pranzis comes on their frequent giant raids, the Broken Gladers pull back into the caves and defend the entrance. With great might and amazing numbers, the Broken Gladers fight back the attack and then begin to plan, in the messy giant way, for their counter-raid on Pranzis and surrounding environs.

Forest of Mists
    One of the largest and oldest forests of Layonara, the Forest of Mists is also one of the most mysterious. It is said that more rangers and druids live in this forest than any other in Layonara. Despite this, Bloodstone's bugbears find footholds in the wooded valleys and barren bluffs, from which they strike out with their brutal raiding parties. The bugbears simply appear in the forest, despite the patrols established to track their movements and keep them out. 
    The Broken Glade giants live in these woods as well and they are no less a mystery than the suspicious movements of the bugbears. The giants lived in, and some argue tended, the forest for many years before Bloodstone's return. In recent years, however, the Broken Glade giants are being designated by officials in Pranzis as enemies and allies of Blood. These officials assert this forcefully and seem unwilling to entertain other reasoning about the giants, despite the attempts by a group of rangers to portray the situation differently. Conflict has increased and aggressive maneuvers by both the Broken Gladers and the Pranzis guard have been witnessed. The Rangers of the Glade, as they have come to be known, assert that the aggression on the part of the giants is a response to the actions of Pranzis. Pranzis, and most Dregarians, view the increased hostility as an effect of Blood's influence over these weak-minded behemoths.
    As for the forest itself, what makes it mysterious and spectacular are the unexplainable mists which sweep across the forest unpredictably and without warning. Many travelers have found themselves far off course when the thick layer of mist blanketed the forest floor. Every year some go missing, even those traveling together in the same caravan. Mothers, husbands, guards, or companions either wander wildly to their peril or are abducted somehow by the mist itself. Those who live in the forest have far less trouble as they know to wait the mist out or use the trees, which jut gracefully from the mist, as markers and guides. Occasionally, however, a ranger disappears as well.
    Many adventurers have sought the source of this mist. Some say it is a lake. Many argue it pours from the mouth of a cave. Others believe the mist is the breath of the trees or Katia herself.

Great Plains of Dregar
    Dregar's Great Plains stretch from the east to the west coast beneath the northern mountain ranges. Silt carried down from the mountain run-off makes the plains extraordinarily fertile. Those who live there, particularly in the rolling hills region, boast that the Great Plains of Dregar has the best soil and produce in all of Layonara. The plains are also subject to frequent flooding. Scholars have spent countless hours trying to apply a schedule to the flooding, but to no avail. To some this is a sign of malevolent machination; to others, it is a sign of nature's mystery.

Great Rift
    It seems like the land in this area was grabbed in both hands by a god and ripped apart, leaving a huge gouge and jagged landscape. Every step through the surface area of the rift is laborious and treacherous. The Great Rift Giants, which dwell on the plateaus on the surface and in surrounding areas, attack on sight. These giants are tall even among giants, and have displayed exceptional visual acuity in hunting the large grey-backed armadillos that superbly blend into the craggy grey rocks. Their height and sharp vision means they can see intruders coming a long way off. These giants, it is argued by scholars in Pranzis, are stone giants who have been transformed by the energy wafting out of the cracks in the violent landscape here. The Bloody Stump giants, as they are called for their unusual constitution, are able to withstand (and sometimes even regenerate limbs lost from) dismembering blows, and are regarded as a more intense version of their surface cousins.
    Besides all the chasms and cracks, there is also a cave opening somewhere in the Great Rift. No one knows for sure what creatures dwell in the unending depths of the Rift itself, but tales concoct the vilest creatures imaginable. Wafting from this cave mouth is an intense negative energy. It sweeps across and transforms the whole area. Few have stood at its opening and lived to tell about it. Those few who have, always returned somehow transformed, turned wicked. A royal survey crew, accompanied by the King's best knights, was lost at this cave opening. One of the knights was seen a few months later wearing jet black armor and singlehandedly sacking the whole town of North Fort. Since then, the Rift has been officially designated as off limits by the crown.     Those wishing to venture there are asked to speak to the King's advisors to establish a formal team.

Iron Hills
    The high iron content in the soil here gives the hills a brilliant red color. Children's stories of the region, however, attribute the red soil to the countless who have spilled blood in ogre raids. Needless to say, ogres are feared in the area. Since the local farmers stay far from the ogre cave in the Iron Hills, the ogres have, for the most part, let the farmers be.

O'Taogor
    Some of the mightiest trolls known in Layonara live in this cave system. It seems that they were drawn here by the expansive caverns and the underground lake. These Trolls are so fierce that those who have faced them insist that their power must have been gifted from Bloodstone or one of the evil gods. Their community seems nearly entirely underground and they seldom venture from the cave mouth. Despite this, many believe that the day will come when Blood or some other wicked force will whisk their masses into action. As such, the entrance along the River of Shadows is always under hidden surveillance and a system of messengers can relay an alarm quickly to Pranzis and nearby towns if the need arises.

River of Shadows
    This river either picks up its negative energy as it passes through the Dark Forest or is itself the source of that negative energy as its water is absorbed by the dark flora. In either case, the river draws dark creatures to it, whether in the forest or as it emerges from the forest and spills into the northernmost regions of the Southern Plains. Malar panthers, vampires, and black snakes all find the banks of this river a welcoming abode. There is also a temple of Baraeon Ca'Duz somewhere near one of the stagnant back-current pools. Those who know about this temple are up in arms about it. There have been many petitions to the king to do something about it and many Dregarians have tried to take matters into their own hands, with little success. Those who live near the Dark Forest blame the temple for the proliferation of the spiders which sneak into their village and steal away loved ones at night. The priests of the temple insist that they are just there to study and pay respects to the great spiders of the Black Forest region.

Rolling Hills
    The Rolling Hills are in the central region of the Great Dregar Plains. Even though they don't reach very high, they can be seen for miles around on the flat farmlands. The sudden rise of these gentle bluffs spawned all sorts of mythologies and gives the hills a spiritual presence in the lives of the nearby farmers. 
    Many halflings have settled in these comfortable hills. Recently, the human farmers down in the nearby farm plains have begun to call the halflings' land rights into question. The hills, according to the human agriculturalists, were left undeveloped for a specific reason. They were used as funerary mounds for many generations of their ancestors. As the halflings dig their homes into the hills, they claim, they are desecrating not simply graves and memories, but the connection each human farmer has with her and his ancestors. The halfing newcomers refuse to leave, claiming traditional halfling land-use customs. Dregar has sent mediators to the area to try to work something out. The talks are heated, but no violence has erupted between the two groups yet.

Serpent Mountains
    These mountains are named more for the treacherous, serpentine paths and poisonous plants than any overwhelming presence of snakes or serpent-like creatures. Reports from mountain scouts suggest that there are also bugbears holed up in many of the remote valleys. Despite these trials and dangers, the Serpent Mountains are simply sublime and draw nature lovers and adventurers throughout Layonara to behold the expansive vistas, gently tumbling waterfalls and myriad species of trees.

Singing Forest
    The amazing thing about the Singing Forest is that it actually does sing. Those residents of northern Dregar who can afford to often make treks to this forest for purposes of spiritual rejuvenation or respite from their arduous daily existence. It has long been a debate whether the gentle song of this sublime forest is magical or if it emerges out of the unplanned and un-conducted confluence of the various forest sounds. Scholars of Katia who argue the latter also believe that the forest here, because of this emergent symphonic organization, has taken on a kind of aggregate identity. In other words, many who have studied the forest say that it is alive and self-aware in a way unlike any other forest in Layonara. If you visit, expect to be asked to leave after a very short stay if you aren't willing to merge with the forest and surrender your autonomy to its supra-individual agency.
Within this forest there are ancient ruins. Some of them seem to crumble more rapidly under the sway of the forest's singing, while others seem almost animated by it. There is one ruin that somehow seems to manage both. Every once in a while a creature enters the forest and finds the singing to be hideous and piercing. They scramble about, searching frantically for a way to make the sound stop. When this happens, northerners say, they almost always find themselves at the entrance to one of the ancient ruins. And as they step through the threshold they are transformed and lost from sight. Because of this, northerners call them the Ruins of Madness and have long spread the word to avoid it at all costs.

Southern Plains
    These plains run between the west coast of Dregar and the Forest of Mists. Depending on who you ask, the whole southern tip of Dregar may be considered a part of these broad, windswept grasslands. For many years, these plains were wild and left uncivilized by the power of Pranzis, which was distracted by other dark deeds at the time. Since the horsemen rode though and established control at Lorindar, the plains have become uniquely peaceful and settled. Blood's armies seem to gather elsewhere and direct their attention to other targets. As this information spreads more and more people seem to be traveling south. Many new settlements have sprung up across the Southern Plains and the established cities in the plains are finding themselves faced with a population issue.

Spine Mountains
    The Spine Mountains are like the backbone of Dregar, jutting out from its earthy flesh as they run long-ways down the continent. Dregar mythology portrays these mountains as the spine of one of the original dragons who lay down in the ocean near the beginning of time to create the central region of Layonara. The tremors which send avalanches of snow and rock down upon the lower regions occasionally remind people of their indebtedness to this dragon. Those who actively assert this idea, rather than just live with it as a dead tradition, explain all of Dregar's natural and magical activity in terms of this dragon. They also believe that one day the dragon will shake the soil from its scales and rise into the heavens again. Then it will shrug off the arrogant non-believers to drown in the ocean while gathering the faithful to its bosom as it flies toward the stars.

Storm Horn Mountains
    As the name suggests, the Storm Horn mountains are thrashed nearly every day of the year with violent storms. Only the most resilient barbarians lived here for centuries. These barbarians, also known as scryers, eventually acclimated and adapted to their environment. One peculiar feature of these barbarians is their massive lungs and amplifying voice box. They are said to be able to hurl a battle cry through a thundering storm with far better range and force than any other barbarian standing on a sunny field.
    The Storm Horn barbarians, however, have not been seen in the Storm Horn Mountains for ages. It seems that they were forced from their homeland by an invasion of Bleeding Rock Giants supposedly delivered to the Strong Horn's door by none other than Sinthar Bloodstone. This, according to historians, is one of the first things Blood did when he returned, indicating either some crucial significance to the area or a grudge against these barbarians. Every Storm Horn, however, vows at the age of manhood to strive every day toward reclaiming their precious homeland. 

Triera Mountains and the Thunder Peaks
    There is much exposed granite in these areas. Stone giants who moved here ages ago build simple structures out of it. For many years these giants smashed and shaped the granite by hand. Either by some process of natural changes - or as a gift from Grannoch as the giants themselves claim - they have developed extraordinarily large hands with sharp knuckles that can strike a rock like the most powerful pick ever made by man or dwarf. A passing half Deep Grove giant observed these giants smashing whole granite shelves into crude blocks and was awestruck. Triera worked his way into the giant's community and began to show them how to be more precise with their stone smashing. Triera spent many years in the late 12th century selling these blocks to castles and cities throughout Dregar. He named these giants the Granite Fists and he was said to have badly exploited them. When his life drew towards its end, Triera felt remorse for this exploitation, the people of northern Dregar assert. Because of this he bought the whole range of mountains, which was really only a few parcels he didn't already own, and gifted it to the giants. 
    A recent fire in the Pranzis hall of records, however, has conveniently destroyed any documentation that the Granite Fists are the rightful owner of their granite ranges. No one really recognizes giants as true owners of land in Dregar anyway. Adventurous stonemasons now gingerly tread into the Triera mountains in search of good granite slabs to export to growing cities. Conflicts, as you might expect, have begun to flare, making this a particularly hot and contested region of Dregar. Many of the Granite Fists have now migrated to the neighboring Thunder Peaks.

Troll Mountain
    At one point in Dregar's history there were trolls throughout the northeastern region. Giants and encroaching human development pushed them far into the mountains, toward the coast. For ages they have lived there in nearly complete isolation. Because of this, they have become their own sub-species of troll. The mountain which most of them call home grants these trolls its nomenclature: they are called the Troll Mountain Trolls.
The ocean views from Troll Mountain are breathtaking. Word of Troll Mountain's snowy beauty has tumbled down the slope to nearby human settlements and explorers have begun to carve trails through the ranges to this rare coastal peak. As more and more explorers and winter wonderland seekers make their way to Troll Mountain, organizations bent on the eradication of the Troll Mountain Trolls become more populous and outspoken.
A Sojourner's Guide to the Landscapes and Locales of Dregar

.: Player Guild System :.

Creating Guilds -
Guilds are used to organize, and manage other player characters.  They require leaders with high levels of commitment, and dedication.  Players may only be associated with one guild at any given time.

Joining Guilds -
In order to join a guild, you need a guild invitation.  Members from a guild have the ability to send these - depending on their guild rank.  Some guilds may have a joining fee, which, if you cannot cover, will prevent you from joining.

Guild Factions -
Factions among other guilds allow for a more in-depth player-guild interaction.  Guilds can have allies, enemies, or remain neutral to guilds.  Enemy guild members are considered hostile, while allied guild can share guild messages.  Factions are persistent, meaning even after server restarts enemy guild members will still remain hostile towards your player character.
A deed for a cloak hanger.

These bandages require the use of the Heal skill.  The target will be healed 4d4 hitpoints plus 1.25 times your Heal skill.  In addition, if the healer succeeds a d20 + Heal vs DC15 the target is healed of all poison and disease. Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.

These bandages require the use of the Heal skill.  The target will be healed 8d8 hitpoints plus 1.5 times your Heal skill.  In addition, if the healer succeeds a d20 + Heal vs DC15 the target is healed of all poison and disease. Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.

These bandages require the use of the Heal skill.  The target will be healed 12d12 hitpoints plus 1.75 times your Heal skill.  In addition, if the healer succeeds a d20 + Heal vs DC15 the target is healed of all poison and disease. Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.

These bandages require the use of the Heal skill.  The target will be healed 16d16 hitpoints plus 2 times your Heal skill.  In addition, if the healer succeeds a d20 + Heal vs DC15 the target is healed of all poison and disease. Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.
One moderatly heavy stone with thirty meters of rope tied to it.  Commonly used for creating a rope swing.  By tossing the stone over a secure fixture, one could swing from this heavy rope.

Rigid metal shaped to uncomfortable shapes, these military helmets are given to Orc Commanders. Through the pain of adapting to its odd shape, their ranks fill with irrate yet disciplined soldiers. Toughened to resist harsh blows, these helmets are the definition of practical warfare.
A leather pouch for carrying pipe weed.
A deed for a child's hobby horse
A clay mold used to aid in the construction of horns.
This is a house key.  Use it to see what house it opens.
This stone is worn and polished. Perhaps it was done by hand recently or over many hands over time.  There are many tiny runes carved into its surface.

This is the golden Harp of Ilsare. Only one of these harps is known to exist and is rumored to have been crafted by Ilsare herself to be possessed solely by the Harper. 

Those who have possessed the harp have been rumored to  have been skilled diplomats, and stories of coaxing mortal enemies to put down their arms surround this item.
This harp shines brightly of polished gold. Not a single nick or scratch mars it surface, making its age difficult to determine.

When the gods clash and sometimes even when powerful mortal magic is drawn from the weave, the world seems to lose its stability. Disruptive waves wash through eveything. As sentient beings, this means we may become disoriented, dizzy, even loose consciousness and memories. It is seldom talked about, as it has become just another everyday matter of a Layonaran existence. It can become serious, however, as when an adventurer finds the world altered suddenly to their dismay and disadvantage. Money and goods somehow seem to disappear into the chaos as well. 

All experienced travellers, businessmen and adventurers have therefore devised ways to avoid the potential setbacks of these ruptures in time and space. By focusing thought upon a particular place and time and making some sort of impression on it, that fragment of reality becomes considerably more stable. This is possible to accomplish with no devices, through dreaming, praying or meditating. But to make a mark with far less time and effort, a gnomish mage invented this orb, which would magically aid in focusing your thoughts. As you wave your palms mystically over the orb, you are stabilized in that time and space. Then if reality seems to collapse, you will remember that moment and suddenly find yourself back in it.
This is a simple unadorned copper key that fits the locks of this inn's private rooms.

Even the indomitable librarian that loves to stay up to ungodly hours with Eld quickly shows signs of exhaustion and falls asleep drooling over a dusty tome on deific nature. Eld continues however and every tome and scripture seems to blur into one another. Eventually she simply falls unconscious in a heap of papers and the night passes by...

She is woken up by a small Blue Jay that sits on a lighted window of the library, the rays of the sun sneaking in this isolated place in the world, a sight unseen for many months. The many notes and books laid about remind Eld of the frustrations but for some reason the perky bird that whistles on the window fights that mood with its song. Soon the bird almost seems to smile to Eld and with a wink it flies away, the fluttering of its wings setting a small play of the breeze left behind and one of scrolls near Eld flies to her lap. It lands on an odd angle and in one moment of clarity disparaging notes come together and as a light in the darkness something instinctual clicks together...*

Vanavar Island
     In ages past, the only people to inhabit Vanavar were Gray Elves, who made the Broken Mountains their home. They dubbed the island Vanavar, or "strong-willed." However, as the humans expanded across the face of Layonara, they came to recognize Vanavar's strategic position and started settling the island. When Xandrial arrived, he too recognized the strategic value of Vanavar and was quick to send his forces in.
     Vanavar's forces were hardly prepared to face the hordes of the Demon Prince, and the Duke of North Hampton, as last resort, sent a messenger bird to Roldem, requesting aid and offering his allegiance to the King of Roldem if he came to Vanavar's aid. However, the Duke was too late, as Xandrial's forces arrived first and laid waste to all the settlements of the island. Now, only a few survivors are left and struggling to survive.
     With the Duke's patrols gone, Vanavar is now also an ideal base for pirates. Xandrial allows them to use the island's secluded coves as long as they don't interfere with his own ships.
Nobody knows what happened to the Gray Elves that inhabited the Broken Mountains, as they have not been heard from since the rise of the human settlements on Vanavar. It is unlikely that they still inhabit the mountains without lifting a finger against Xandrial, so it is likely that they were killed or left for Voltrex. However, no one truly knows the fate of the Vanavarian Grays.

Well-known Cities:

North Hampton
Location: Northern tip of Vanavar
Population: 150 
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Located at the northern tip of Vanavar, North Hampton was the major city of the island and one of Layonara's larger trading ports, acting mostly as a trade hub for ships from Westgate and Waysend as well as Rodez and Lorindar on the south. Now, after Xandrial nearly torched it to the ground, it is but a shell of its former self, its inhabitants either killed or enslaved.

Murdoch
Location: Southwestern tip of Vanavar
Population: 100
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Murdoch was just coming into its own, starting to becoming a prosperous village by taking Lorindar and Rodez trade from the larger city of North Hampton. Nothing much is left of it today except for a few families of fishermen, trying to survive and unable or unwilling to leave. Murdoch was the last town on Vanavar to be destroyed by Xandrial. Those that managed to flee the island did so from here.

Celine
Location: Southeastern tip of Vanavar
Population: 50
GP limit: 15
Alignment: Neutral Evil
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Celine, located at the edge of Vanavar's scant forest, was a farmer's village, responsible for most of the food supply to the other towns on Vanavar. The mayor of Celine had plans to partner with the town of Murdoch to develop a shipyard building ships from the prime wood of Krelin's Forest. This scheme never came to fruition, however; together with North Hampton, Celine was one of the first Vanavarian towns to be destroyed.

Locales:

Broken Mountains
     The mountain range at the center of Vanavar breaks the island basically in two, so when the first human settlers arrived, the name Broken Mountains quickly took hold.
     Though inhabited by Gray Elves before the human incursion and Xandrial's attacks, no one is certain of the proud elder race's fate.

Krelin Forest
     An old but small forest of tall trees, the village of Celine had big plans to use the Krelin Forest's excellent wood to enter the shipyard business.

Description: An iron helmet bearing an intricate carving the ankh of Toran, traced across the top side and decorated with strands of silver and gold.


Gifted to faithful of Toran or allies of the church for great services these helmets receive heavy magically investments by the ranking High Priest in order to aid the bearer in his or her service to the All Watching.

Description: A black leather belt with an unusually big belt buckle. The belt buckle is a massive bronze disk with a sun carved upon its surface and decorated with thin threads of silver. "Melvon" has been carved into the backside of the belt buckle in large letters.


No records regarding the history or origins of this magical belt exist. Its small size, however, indicates that the original wearer was an Elf, a Gnome or perhaps a plump Halfling. When worn by a practitioner of the arcane arts the belt seems to enhance the wearer's understanding of certain protective spells, and spells like Shield, Endure Elements or Protection from Alignment seem to be lasting longer and be more efficient in battle.
The most magnificent power of the belt is only revealed in combat, however, when a missile is aimed at the bearer. As soon as the missile is fired the bronze belt buckle begins to vibrate, increasing its frequency as the missile draws ever closer. When one manages to keep the missile within eyesight, one will notice its change in direction. It is with a growing dread that one realizes for the first time that the belt buckle is drawing the missile towards it. Running away or attempting to jump out of the missile's path only effects that the missile adjusts its direction accordingly. However, when one realizes this and waits for the inevitable an amazing thing happens. The arrow, bolt or sling stone hits the belt buckle in dead centre without doing any harm to the bearer. Only magically enchanted missiles are able to overcome the protective wards of the belt buckle, which makes the belt a true lifesaver.

Description: A pair of worn boots. What makes the pair truly magnificent is the material of which they were made. White scales ranging in size between that of a fingernail to the size of a child's hand cover the boots, the tough skin underneath the hard but flexible scales make the boots nearly indestructible.


Crafted from the hide of one of the last white dragons these boots are an item of legend, dating back to the Dragon Wars. 
No magic has been invested in the pair. Still they possess innate abilities that easily rival the most highly invested items of today, a reflection of the majestic creature that died to allow the creation of the boots.

Description: The gauntlet resembles a gigantic forearm, inscribed with runes and symbols that trace the entire length of the gauntlet. In truth the gauntlet was tailored from the forearm of a giant. Hollowed out and dried the gauntlet is a ghastly piece and exhausts very unpleasant odours when subjected to water or other liquids.


Worn by Kei'rull "Bonebreaker" during his reign as chief of the giant tribes in the Thunder Peaks, this mighty gauntlet became his symbol of power and dominion over the tribes. By means of cunning negotiations and martial prowess the half giant Kei'rull boldly united 3 tribes and lead them into a succession of raids against the neighbouring human settlements or whomever passed too close to their territories. It is said that whenever a barrier was erected or a gate closed to block the path of Kei'rull's force the chieftain himself stepped forward and battered the barrier away with a mighty punch by his gauntleted right fist.
No one seemed able to oppose the might and rage of the giant army and so Kei'rull lead them ever onward, as far south as Fort Thunder. There the army was ambushed and savagely cut down by a mixed militia of dwarves from Clan Stonesmasher and humans from the surrounding settlements and towns.

Kei'rull, however, escaped the annihilation of his army and was believed to have travelled south. It is believed that Kei'rull became the leader of a band of brigands and cutthroats roaming the outskirts of the Forest of Mists. No further records exist regarding Kei'rull's fate, nor are there records that mention the reappearance of the gauntlet that marked him as chief and champion of the tribes.

The records describe Sharl Etris Abryn as an elven ranger and devout follower of the Prince of Wolves.
Sharl was bound to a path of vengeance by a crime long forgotten. He was relentless in his hunt for the cruel and hated orcs that roamed the vast Forest of Mists. Sharl was always seeking confrontation and battle with his avowed enemies, where he was wont to come out as the victor, but was never content with his victory.
Sharl was gifted the necklace by a priest of Folian S'pae to aid him in what was perceived as being devotion to his Lord and protection of the Forest in his name. In many ways Sharl lived up to those virtues, but more and more often his path was left littered with corpses. As years went by, Sharl began to enjoy the killing of his prey. What before had been the hunter's clean kill turned into a game of torture and senseless slaughter.

In the end it was his own blinding lust for dealing death that saw him killed. A group of adventurers passed through his territory, among them a female half orc. As Sharl spotted her he was overcome by rage, his mind clouded by lust for her blood. Sharl was no match for the swords and unveiled magic of the group. He was slain and laid to rest in a clearing, at the roots of a young oak tree.
This necklace was given to you by Jasmin of the Swamp. The skeleton knuckles do look creepy on this necklace but it seems to offer some sort of protection against the undead.

Description: A golden ring. Upon close examination writing is discovered along the inner side of the ring. The writing, however, is too indistinct to read.


Nothing is known about the origins of this magically enchanted ring. A thorough investigation of the writing on the inside of the ring yields the following translation from the Halfling language.

"Do not fear. Nothing can hold me."

This cloak is a patchwork monstrosity of the pelts of a menagerie of animals. Though the tailor clearly had some skill, the voluminous nature of the material makes anyone who wears it seem bigger and tougher than they are.

The odour of the tannery still clings to the cloak, as well as a faint miasma of smells unique to the animals from which the pelts came.  As such, animals tend to shy away from those wearing these cloaks.

Rumour has it that only a few of Johan's cloaks remain in circulation, as it has been some time since Hlint's premiere fur trader has plied his trade.  Some argue that the quality of his work has deteriorated since his retirement; certainly, the group of adventurers who accepted these patchwork cloaks as a token of the old man's gratitude reported that the fur trader, though still dextrous with a needle, might soon be joining his recently departed wife in Hlint's graveyard.

The Birdlord's Gift...

This wondrous artifact of nature defies all explanation. Seemingly inconspicuous, this garb is wreathed in earthly colours of the Mother. Twigs and plants spring idly from its sides as leaves form a silky covering that looks much like leather.

However, when the Birdlord wields this magnificent creation its powers are revealed.

The Birdlord's gift allows its wielder to acquire the nimbleness of his winged friends. Speed and agility, second nature to the Gifted of Katia.

The subtle earthy moss that covers the bottom of the armour grants a degree of protection against blunt objects. This protection much to the natural skin of those who fly.

In its element, the Birdlord can stave off the charged ether, and this armour allows for such skill to become more factual, allowing the wielder to withstand high discharges of electricity. With the same token, this armour is highly flammable, granting a weakness to the man of the skies.

The soft cushion of leaves and feathers the armour posseses grants the wielder fond memories of its memories. Focus becomes easier, second nature.

Finally this armour is known to enhance the sight of the Birdlord as he or she grows into the duty of being the eyes of the Mother, keen insight into distant and foreign lands.

The Mother's Gift

This earthly armour fits perfectly to the Birdlord. Gilded feathers and leaves adapt with ease at the unique anatomy of Katia's Gifted, enhancing his features and giving him grace beyond comprehension.

The thin and delicate strands of the strange feathery substance that make this armour makes it weigh as much as a feather does, granting great comfort to its wearer.

Etched upon the leaves on this armour, powerful magic sits to enhance the Birdlord. Breaking on the basic principles of life, the armour grants focus into breaching the natural or unnatural defenses presented against the Birdlord.

Such strong drive within this magic, retroactively enhances the confidence and faith of the stalwart servant of the Mother, bringing resolution and steadfastness in the most dire of situations.

Such drive and trust in the gifts of the Mother assist the Birdlord in spreading Her word. Saying the right things... at the right time.

The Dreams Edge.

   A greataxe forged in the realm of true dreams by the Dwarf Hargranar, The Dreamers edge is truly an imposing weapon.  Slightly shorter than the rest of its kind the Dreamers Edge lacks none of the ferocity of its brethren,  having the same distinct brutality that marks all its kind.

    Clearly of potent magic, the axe displays a rich ruby head fashioned from a metal that is unknown. The twin blades seem to glimmer with the blood of the heart, yet not the kind that gives rise to images of brutality. Hopes and dreams of the worlds beyond seem to cling to the blades in rich ruby textures that cannot be denied.

    The haft also of metal is forged of black, runes that remain indecipherable mark its every surface, running the entire length of the weapons shaft.  Once imposing the runes seem to have now taken on a less menacing tangent, speaking in words unknown of defence and the preservation of dreams.

  Within the end of the axe sits a bright blue stone which glimmers erratically, setting off small sparks of light that run along the haft to the blades.  The lights far from harmful plead to the gentler aspects of the soul, to the brightness of a future where the rest of the axes dreadful craftsmanship is no longer required.

   The story of the Dreamers edge is long, the weapon having known many forms as it passed throughout history. What is well known is simply that the weapon is always found at a point of choice. The dream often in conflict the Edge appears to resolve such in a way that only it can.

    Yet such dreadful purpose is not truly its task, for not only can it represent and end it can only show true beginnings.  Once the gem of choice, known as the pivot is set into the hilt the path of The Edge becomes set, for hope or for ill. Once the pivot is passed the weapon is no longer capable of functioning in a manner against its nature, the blue of hope and true dreams or the red of destruction and ending radiance.

    Currently a blue stone sits within the hilt, glimmering brightly and preserving the dream.  The Dreamers Edge in this guise is a defender of hope, a preserver of dreams and a firm advocate of brighter tomorrows.  

    Abuse of this potent artifact has been known to cause many a disaster, lack of service to its cause often times bringing harm to the bearer. More frequently however the weapon will fall once more to component pieces, unable to be placed together until such a time as the dream once more requires the pivot.

  Many powers are attributed to The Edge, the first the ability to shift to the dream realm itself on occasion, slicing cleanly through amour and flesh, leaving terrible wounds while passing through the nether realms. Other times it is reported to be able to guard the mind from invasion, at times to cause wounds to heal of there own accord.  While rumors vary and fluctuate, it is certain that the weapon grows in power as the bearer grows in service to the dream.

As the tales tell, several centuries ago the town of List was beset by a horde of horrid trolls that poured forth from the nearby moors. Its decentralized settlements easily fell prey to the marauding trolls. In fact, word of the attacks did not even reach the town until almost all of its citizens that lived between central list and the moors had been overrun and summarily devoured.

List's salvation came from an unlikely location: the highwaymen that collected "road tolls" from merchant caravans on the road to haven. These outlaws, after calling several groups of their thieving brethren, became the largest group of men at arms near List. Led by an uncommonly noble (or scheming) commander, and armed with a score of these powerful blades of mysterious origin, the ruffians lost their status as outlaws by turning wave after wave of the troll invasion away from the town. They were hailed as "The Hero's of List" and few cared to remember what their occupation had been previously. They were granted an official pardon from the Lord of Haven. The commander and several of his officers were granted land and minor titles or political positions in the region.

The blades themselves were held in List, on display and ready to be the town's "Last Defense" if ever needed again. Over time life in the town and its surrounding settlements returned to normal, and the level of viligance slacked. Only three of the blades entitled the Last Defense now remain in the display case in List, and a few of the elderly of List if asked why only three remain may mention a cowardly theft in the night before getting lost in a tangle of ale and tangential stories.

All of these two-handed flamberge's appear identical with the most prominent feature being a gleaming many-faceted fire opal set in the pommel. Its waved blade glints red in the light of the sunset, the time of day when troll attacks begin, and sunrise, when the hordes finally retreat from the rising sun.
The greatsword is an impressive weapon by any measure, and is held with two hands by all but the largest of creatures.
