Belonging to a mighty general of old, strongest combatant against Sinthar Bloodstone, this pair of gloves was a gift from the dragons to the general.

Known only as The Defiant, the legendary figure was the last man standing in the last battlefield before Bloodstone was vanquished. 

Betrayed by one of his own men, the general faced a shameful backstabbing death and the gloves fell in Sinthar's hands.

Now defeated, they fall once more in glorious hands as a Dragoncalled becomes the new wielder of The Defiant.

A priest of Kithairen once decided to become as fast as his god would allow, to do so he wrapped metal bands to his arms and raced along the tallest mountains to capture lightning. For many days he did so until with time he tired and was never struck.

When he finally settled to a rest a powerful thunderbolt struck him fully and killed him, yet the metal bands that he wore were imbued by something special.

Taken then by some local barbarians as an artifact to their deity it soon fell to Sinthar's coffers in one of his many raids. With the war over however, they now fall to the arms of a Dragoncalled.

Made by dragons of old, this golden crystal was imbued with the essence of the Great Wyrms. Granting insight and lending strength of dragon grace, those lucky enough to wield such items are said to see everything through a new set of eyes.

Gone with the dragon purge, these crystals became legend and it is said that one for each metallic dragon exists. And to start the search, a Dragoncalled finds the Golden One.

Made by mages of old, this staff was imbued with the magic that opens the doors between worlds. Allowing to call powerful creatures from beyond and for the caster to step in the protective etherealness between planes, this staff is a treasure to many.

Strong enchantments placed on it to grant the user protections against the things that they may face, it renders the wielder immune to all the magics that might affect the mind, and as they say, a strong mind, a strong body.

This powerful mithril shield was one of the few items ever created in an alliance between dwarf and elf. The dwarven knowledge of ore and fire, combined with the delicate and detailed touch of elven hands make this shield a work of art in both beauty and practicality.

Little can penetrate this golden wall and its many layered structure makes it almost impossible for a blade to tear through.

Gone are the times when such things were even possible, yet it stands as testament now of what alliances make.

Layered in strange metals that seem to be bathed in magic, this helmet grants the user a unique view of life.

All surroundings taking a unique shade as creatures are highlighted by their auras, instead of the simple lights of their surroundings. This particular view alerts all senses to heightened degrees.

The most peculiar aspect of this helmet is that in this particular observation of life, it protects the user from anyone attempting to breach their own essence of life.

Dire stream of fallen's blood.
Bearers of weight unsought.
Defenders from evil's flood.
Blades of the Dragon brought.

Circle now memoirs of alliance.
Keep in heart the glory new.
Mind strong with defiance.
Dragoncalled, how you grew.

Souls Bound.
End Found.

Made by the druids in the Great Forest, this helmet made from the skin and horns of a forest spirit once it passed back unto the balance.

Granting freedom throughout all impediments it makes the wearer view things from the perspective of such blessed creatures. A blessing in body, and a burden in mind.

This sharp scimitar gleams with a holy touch that leaves even the most renowned weapon-smiths with a breathless gasp. The slender leather hilt is grafted with golden strings set in sinewy patterns resembling leaves from a pleasant meadow. 

Upon its blade, inscriptions of a long lost language are etched upon a mithril forging. Covered with geometrical patterns that resonate in swift motions, this blade will cut through the thickest materials.

Through time it fell into the hands of a devoted warrior who would only use it to slay creatures of evil, and would never raise it against anything else. The blade in turn, perhaps gifted by the gods, granted more power to this devotion. When she passed onto better realms, it was given to her apprentice who kept it for many years displayed in a museum in Dregar.

When one of Sinthar's agents raided the place, he took the blade to his master. Now defeated, it falls into the hands of a Dragoncalled, to forge a new destiny.

Granted in the defense of the Great Oak, this set of boots have been touched by the grace of nature.

Offering many of the qualities in the wisdom of the forest and the stoutness of its inhabitants.

A legendary hammer that has passed through many hands in its existence, records of its making date back to pre-cataclysmic times and yet the hammer looks as good as new.

Said to be created as a gift to a king or a god, it was so beautifully crafted that instead of taking it, whoever was receiving it placed their hands upon it and granted it a divine touch.

Since then it has shown in every major battlefield cleaving its way through hordes of unexpected victims. All saying that right before they were hammered by this creation, they saw a flicker of great golden wings expanding from the wielder's back.

Of course such things are left to delirium, the hammer now resurfaces once more in the battle against Sinthar Bloodstone.

Said to be strung from the Weave itself, these pearls have been imbued with the purest of all essences of magic. Made into a necklace, this powerful magical item grants protections against most bodily ailments and a strong resistance against offensive magic.

Said to be once worn by a powerful priestess of The Lifegiver, it has trickled its way from the blessed, to the wretched and now to the hands of the Dragoncalled.

This legendary cloak was once worn by a great councilor of old. His might and power both in the battlefield and in office made him a figure to both revere and fear.

The day Sinthar defeated the council, he took this cloak and vested it upon himself. Ever since, granting him great resilience in both mind and body.

Seviran, its name, now falls unto the hands of a Dragoncalled, rightfully earning it as Bloodstone's tyrannical regime ended.

Elven in design, these bracers are given to the archer squad leaders in the Dregarian militia.

Allowing for a steady hand and with a little magical aid, it makes them unequivocably, a sign of precision and deadliness.

Scales of Truth embedded with the sight of the Golden one. This thick armour seems to have been made out of the All Seeing's own scales itself. 

Granted to a mighty hero in the defense of Dregar, it shows to stand the strength of those who sacrifice all for others.

A wall of truth and resilience. This shield was crafted by Rofirein's finest in an effort to wield the mightiest with the strength of their lord. 

A work of martial art in many ways, this light tower shield imbues the wielder with the strength to confront all ill and a slight resistance to the harmful weave.

Given to the best standing captains in the Pranzis army, this beautiful cloak inspires steadfastness and pride to those that surround the wearer. By showing the strength of leaders to others, the Captain's Mantle is a sign of both respect and fear.

Made for best scouts in the army, these striding boots grant speed and quick feet when facing the dangers of the battlefield, and with short spurts of magic, they seem to make the carriers blur with their speed.
Given to the mages in the Pranzis militia, these fire imbued staves have a tendency to start chaos in the enemy ranks.
This dwarven battlefield belt seems to have a rather healthy supply of skirmish devices to wreak havoc in enemy ranks. Filled with smart pouches and pockets, its a scout's dream.
A set of pipes made for those battlesingers in the terrible times of war. Instilling an eerie tune in the enemies and a song of might and strength in those allied.
This smartly enchanted iron longsword, has a tendency to swirl clouds that disrupt those it strikes. Making their minds slightly hazy, it offers a decent advantage in battle.

This medic mask is given to all post-battle healers that tend to the wounded and go through the corpses of all the fallen looking for survivors. The pay isn't good, then again, when is it, when war strikes?
To the bearers of hope in the lands struck by evil. The banner holders in the face of despair. To the bringers of peace in times of trouble. This standard we present, for saving our days.

Extracted from a large quarry of emeralds, this crystal sword oozes with the magic of the gem. While not particularly penetrating, this sword carries a rather sharp blade that can leave searing lacerations where it strikes.

Nimble as the creatures of its namesake. This fey ring will make that which dons it rather dexterous with their fingers. Of course the playful spirits that gift them not always find the best uses for them, they have now enlarged this one ring to gift as a present to those defending their homes.

From an Aeridinite sect within the Great Forest, this set of bracers has kept many healers protected from the magics of those who would strike them. With time they adapted to the constant flows of healing energies used by the priests and priestesses of the order and some of it passed to bracers themselves. Allowing the gentle but powerful touch of the Lifegiver, to imbue those who touched by it.

Made by a group of good-hearted half-giants that roam the Great Forest, this massive bow seems to be able to knock javelin-sized arrows. 

Truly a thing meant only for the strongest, it was gifted to those who fought against the threats that would end the Great Oak.

Weaved with magic of sight, this sharpshooter bow grants keen vision to those who use it. 

Every day it can imbue a set of arrows with powerful weave fire and launch it unerringly at the opposition.

Enchanted by the spirits of the forests, this cloak has been imbued with the quick cunning of the fox. 

A degree of protection against earthly touches and fast feet whenever danger arises.

This interesting armor seems to have been shaped from petrified wood. Lighter than any metal and granting some of the protections and endurance of nature's everlasting guardians, it has been passed through many generations of warriors defending the Great Forest.

This fallen Treant branch seems to have kept some of the natural shaping magic that the tree-herders have. Allowing the user to increase aspects of the self and grant a strong body that is resilient and focused.

A gentle touch of a peaceful canopy. The strides of freedom to forest home. The strength and resilience of elder guardians. And the willingness to sacrifice all to save the Heart of Layonara.

In thanks for the protection given to the Great Oak, and its salvation from utter ruin, the keepers of the forest have granted you this amulet to remind you of their gratefulness eternal.
This small flower apparently made of jewels was found on your person upon waking.

This gold laden censer is riddled with many inscriptions of divine origin. Within it, lies a dark combustible powder that glimmers slightly at the slimmest touch of light.

Blessed by the devoted of your faith, this censer has been instilled with the magic of your Deity. 

Performing the taxing ritual, within holy ground to your faith. The fumes emitted by this censer will attune your body and spirit a step closer to the divine. Your spells will take upon a new essence, and forever will they be a forthcoming representation of your spiritual beliefs.

Made by the loving hands of the halflings Kobal rescued from the clutches of Yegar and the Bloody Axe, this dooner is a patchwork of love and devotion, small halfling hands spending hours in handcrafting each individual path and sewing them together into a dwarf sized whole that radiates the gentle spirit of these people.
 
    Crafted delicately, this multicoloured display depicts different symbols of home and hearth that are intricately linked to Prunilla and her ideals of family and comfort.  Small woven images of Clovers and cornucopias, framed in wreaths of leaves all play across its warm and cosy surface. Colourful and benign they play, offering a small portable smattering of the joy and healing that is held within the hearts of individuals so caring.

    Lastly the dooner is reinforced by the blessings of many Lucky Clovers and given over to Prunilla's divine touch to supply a healing of both body and spirit whenever it is used to cover or warm the body. Its heat promoting mending and restoration of many ills that may afflict the wearer with its simple embrace of textured patchwork.

It is said this shield was formed when the four spirits of the dwarven clans once more gave the essence of the people back to the Mount, the very soul of those who were lost imbueing the lifeless dwarven home once more with the spirit of grace that was taken from The Crecent Moon and Shield.

    Rumour runs that after destruction of the bloodpool at the ancestral home, the four spirits, summoned and embodied forces of dwarven power appeared to Kobal and there were to diffuse the essence of what they were back to those who had gifted them life in the beginning.  So it was that the spirits dissipated, finally unbound and choosing to give back to the dwarves lost and scattered to time and atrocity.

    It is said that when these four spirits, Magic, Metal, Heat and Heart dissolved, a great work of magic formed in the dead and decaying heart of the clan homes, one that was bright with promise of new life and a gathering of force for the lost.

    Rumour would hold that the light in the centre of the homes persisted for many months, bright with magic and heat, drawing metals from the ground itself and infusing it with the very heart of the clan home itself.  Dwarves have come to say that the spirits as a last gift to Kobal left a portion of themselves, held in what was, when the light faded, revealed to be an extraordinary sheild.

   Beyond early manafacture this shield seems to contain four distinct metals, each cross section forged together seamlessly into a whole of cunning craftsmanship.  Each portion inscribed with a rune of incredible detail, the making of each lost to time, yet the meaning standing clear.

   The first section of pure mithril, bright and unbending it stands as the ultimate gift of metal, a defence from sharp swords or the crushing blows of the mace. The metal unmarred seems to have not been ever touched by hammer or blow, given as the deepest of dwarven delving and forged in the fires of dwarven spirit. Sitting proud in the centre of the quarter stands the dwarven mark for metal, seeming bound and part of the very mithril itself.

    The second quarter seems to be forged of purest adamantium, far purer than can by acquired by usual means of mining and smelting. Red in colour it seems to radiate waves of warmth, its surface a constant shimmer of heat haze. Blazoned proudly upon it sits the dwarven rune for Heat, once more bound to the adamantium itself.

   The third quarter forged of silver is marked with spell forces outlined with the fierce glow of starfire, one of the finest fuels of magic.  Emanating menace the singular rune seems to jump and play, pushing at the phantasms that distract the mind, pure threads of the weave marking out the indomitable dwarven will for all to see.  Within the centre of the starfire marked portion sits the dwarven rune for magic.

    The last quarter of the shield proves to be the strangest, formed from simple but effective iron it stands stalwart and of the earth. Unlike the rest of the shield the last portion is not immaculate, indeed it seems to have taken many blows and even sits tarnished in places, dents and scratches covering its plates.  However far from being the plainest of the four, this portion seems to truly show character, each mark scribing experience and personality to the shield with battles faced and overcome.  Sitting in the middle of the final quarter, traced in diamond dust sits the dwarven rune for spirit.


   Named Wall of the Four Thanes in respect for the four guardians now considered to be integral to the clans survival it is considered to be a mark of the Thane of the Crescent Moon and Shield, a replacement for the ring lost to the bloodpool of the old Thanes.  This significant artifact marks the start of a new era for the clans of Mount Norand.

These arrows are truly a rare sight outside the elven continent of Voltrex and even there they are far from common. Hand crafted from rare stones most often fond amidst the Peaks of Voltrex by a group of elven rangers guarding the mountain range, these arrows are rarely gifted to anyone outside the ranks of the ranger unit.

The Naatyam Ã¡ Meneluin, known to humans as "The Sky Guard" or more literally "Keepers of the Blue Sky" take sometimes years to slowly hone the stones they call "Laecelam Nel" so that they will be sharp enough to serve as the point of an arrow. During the process they use secret oils and incantations to prevent the natural magical power of the stone from vanishing. Once finished the tip can serve the ranger trough multiple centuries, never losing its power as long as the ranger keeps regulating the magic trough a set of command words. Without such care however, the tip will soon lose any power it might have once held and for anyone not privy to the knowledge of the rangers it is often hard if not impossible to tap into its power.

The shaft and tail of the arrow may vary but the tip is always made of silver coloured, surprisingly light stone. On the stone, on both sides of the tip, two runes are carved. One of the runes is always the elven rune signifying both Light trough darkness and Ausir. The other rune is something personal to each ranger, something that allows them to separate their arrows from ones made by their brothers and sisters.

Somewhere around the year 1130 a human entrepreneur claimed that he had somehow succeeded in securing a large number of these arrows from a contact in Voltrex and managed to sell hundreds of them before the officials of the crown felt they had to step in and declared that the reason why people were not able to invoke any magical effects while using the arrows was not because they were inapt archers but rather because the arrows were fake.

These white feathered arrows have a stone tip made of some unidentifiable silver coloured rock. There are two small runes carved skilfully into each of the tips. The arrows are long enough to be comfortably used with a longbow.

Lost in the annals of time are the histories of those powerful mages and sorcerers who created the Academy of High Magery.  Their work is renowned as marvels of magic and those called by the Dragon can attest to the effects of their bindstones. 

An expedition to investigate baffling ruins uncovered by a local landslide on the eastern shores of Dregar lead to the discovery of 3 bags of small stone, among other artifacts.  Before the stones could be catalogued and sent on for further study they disappeared.  Oddly enough the Halfling in the archeological group disappeared the same night.  Within a year small stones began to appear on the black markets of most of the port towns.  Those versed in the arcane arts could recognize them as a repository of magic but one very old and complex.  There has been much scholarly debate about these stones but it is generally agreed upon they are the work of the Academy of High Magery.  Archmage Emile F'strame of the famed Ubem Academy of Pranzis and accepted authority on draconic artifacts recently posted a paper on the stones; stating them to be the work of Adepts with in the academy.  The fact that he magic contained within these stones seems to be draconic in origin is a bit unsettling. It is a good thing they have lost much of their potency over the tides of time.
A smooth round stone, slightly cold to the touch.

Enrich Emrlan's life's passion was for the healing arts.  This cleric of Aeridin spent his entire life producing these belts.  Pouches along the sides store valuable herbs for remedies while the very weave of the cloth allows the wearer to focus their inner energies and radiate a flow of positive power to heal those of like cause surrounding them

These sparkling blue robes were the concept of one of Lucinda's faithful.  A mage in her own right, she was dismayed at how members of her faith's clergy were unable to use the enchanted robes of arcane casters.  Over many years she successfully created these robes for the devoted divine weavers.

This cloak is fashioned from the hide of a white stag. The beast long known for its amazing longevity and disease resistance is the subject of many a tall tale. This short version reaches to the waist and is supple and seems to radiate an inner vitality.

The contraption, that seems to be worn on the head, was first contrived by the intrepid Halfling adventurer Thomas Thimbleton, formerly of Lorrindar.  It is said that Thomas devised the headgear for one of his "big" friends to distract the man from running in terror at the first moans of a ghastly foe, thus leaving the Halfling exposed to do the fighting.  It's success with the big folk enticed him to mass produce the item.
The device works to a degree; the noise it makes does drown out the bellow of foes, but makes it more difficult to concentrate on the task at hand.
The contraption, that seems to be worn on the head, is big, not very attractive and makes a strange noise.

This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind. Examined closely by one with some knowledge of knightly know how, it can clearly be seem that this virtuous vellum is for those called to a higher order.  It has a maker's mark on the back corner that resembles the runic letter T. Upon use the pages seem to want to stay to defend those left behind and must be destroyed for self preservation.
This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind.

This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind.  Examined closely by one of knowledge of the weave, one can clearly see that this is a book designed for those with an innate connection to the weave.  A series of exercises is contained within to help the user channel inner energies to produce protective results. It has a small maker's inscription on the back corner that resembles the runic letter S. Upon use the pages seem to incorporate themselves into the effect.

These boxes are traditional gifts given to aspiring mages at local academies of magic and temples to keep their collections of parchments in a neat and orderly fashion. The lid is decorated in symbols, arcane or divine though the designs tend to vary on the preferences of the original owner. The inside is nicely divided so that every item has its place.  A minor enhancement helps to lighten the load.

This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind. Examined closely the pages seem to radiate the aroma of oak leaves. This collection of essays is clearly devoted to those involved the arts of tracking and observation.  The runic letter W appears on the back cover as a maker's mark. Upon use, the pages scatter like leaves in the wind.
This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind.
Seeing the Forest for the Trees

In a time not too long ago, The Hall of Norand was restored after a long age of destruction and chaos brought on by the forces of Sinthar Bloodstone, who laid rein to this place of Dwarven skill and beauty.  With the aid of companions and many of the Dragon called of Layonara, a leader emerged to destroy the evil that brewed in the depths and bring back some of what once was.  It is said that after a battle that lasted for many days and a victory was reached that a Blessed Mithril Spirit spoke clearly these words "To the clans... I return metal, the land will flourish and deposits once dead awaken at dwarven touch.  May axes find only richness in the stones of the mountains."  Then her form glowed brightly a moment and like many fireflies, bursts to show the rock at her feet.  

These sets of armor were the first armors crafted in the Hall of Norand by the reforged Crescent Moon and Shield.  The armor's properties are inspired by the leadership shown as events transpired that day.  For as the Dwarven Hero and his companions ascended from the depths of the Halls, worn and beaten, dirtied and bruised with the wounds of war, despite the sadness in his features, the spark of perhaps pride in the dwarf's eye shone through.  The beauty of this armor reflects that spark for as the clan began to return slowly, the first order of business was a commemoration of the epic moment.  Picks were bought and rock was smashed from the very sides of the Halls and the armors were painstakingly worked to reflect all the emotion in the features of the Dwarven Leader.
Piecemeal or complete armors of this type grant protection on par with half-plate.  This armor appears to be very finely crafted with special care taken to enchance its beauty.

The way this blade catches and reflects the light is reminiscent of the first rays on dawn on a glen pond. The hilt is glided and tooled in an intricate elven design.  When taken to the hand of a master this weapon seems to come to life.  One can almost picture the fleet of foot duelist in flight as elven swordsmen fought to protect their arboreal homes from the encroachment of humans.  With the retreat to Voltrex some of these swords remained behind in the care of those who chose to stay and protect the forest and the elven ways.
A finely made rapier of high quality.

Silver Foil
The plainly bound book appears to be one of chicken recipes.  One versed in the short hand of street thieves might recognize it for what it is.  Attributed primarily to Branderback mages, this book surfaces from time to time, but generally they are kept well hidden.
A plain unadorned book of what look like recipes.

Fine Strands of silver and titanium have been woven into the canvas that makes up these boots. Originally developed by Toranite craftsman they have gained favor of undead hunters all over Layonara.  The major drawback is their skimpy protection leaves the wearer vulnerable to cold wet feet.
A pair of white cloth boots with black soles.

This cloak is fashioned from the hide of a white stag. The beast long known for its amazing longevity and disease resistance is the subject of many a tall tale. This floor length version wraps the owner in it's vitality an projects an almost majestic aura.
A floor length white pristine white cloak.

The exact origin of these whips has been obscured by rumor and innuendo, but it does seem that many have a slight odor of alcohol and sea salt in the braided leather that comprises their coils.  Those wielding these unassuming weapons seem to immune from its surprising effects.

This ornate ring that some might find garish or others consider it amazing were all the rage in Prantz a few decades ago.  First conceived and designed by an enterprising Deliarian tailor and enchanted by clerics of the faith, the ring was included with all clothing sales as a means of value added service and a clever way of reducing the time spent on alterations.  Of course items that included a ring were 100% more expensive than their mundane counterparts.

The elaborately bound book appears to be one of music.  Inside are several Sonnets devoted to the art on conjuring.  If sung in the right key, an ally just might appear. It has a small maker's inscription in the back corner that resembles the runic letters IC. Upon use the vellum seems to float away to the plane of desired calling on the wings of the song created.
The elaborately bound book appears to be one of music.

This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind. Examined closely by one with knowledge of arcane scribbling, one can clearly see that these are indeed the calculations of immense detail (almost nauseatingly so). Clearly this is something only the scholarly wizard type would have the patience for. It has a small makers mark on the back corner that resembles the runic letter M. Upon use the pages seem to almost run away glad to free to the complex calculations.
To Be or Not to Become

Designed by Roldemian assassins many years ago, this innocent looking parasol is actually lined with sharp metals at the edges, making it a lethal cutting weapon. Many have fell to this parasol without realizing what actually hit them.  It's shape makes it a perfect tool for assassination and getting away safely.

These gnomish belts were created by Goran followers to keep their tools and gadgets close at hand.  Others with less noble pursuits have taken to using them however. The belt contains a mind boggling array of dangling things that make it fairly easy to recognize someone wearing one as the noise is almost akin to the sound of plate armor.
A belt with many strange gadgets hanging from it.

The world of Layonara is a hostile place and many humanoids try to protect themselves from this hostility. While many tribes, clans, and races do not have much crafting knowledge they are able to fashion rough pieces of armor such as this hide armor.
This seems to be a piece of armor that was worn by an adventurer who likely met an untimely death. Though rusty it still offers a semblance of protection for one that may need it in times of danger.

Sometimes harvesters meet their demise while out in the wilderness, either from an accident or from aggressors of the animal or humanoid type. This appears to be an axe from one of those unfortunate victims.

Primitive tribes, clans, and races do not have much crafting knowledge so they get by with using stone for clubs like this one. While these clubs are not overly effective against large aggressors they do allow these groups and individuals to survive day-to-day.

Primitive tribes, clans, and races do not have much crafting knowledge so they get by with using stone for knives like this one. These knives are used to cut meat, strips of hides, or even leather so that families may survive in the harsh environments.
This seems to be an old piece of armor that was worn by an adventurer at one point. Either that person no longer needed this armor and discarded it or he or she meet an untimely death.

Gaco Mistbane was a Gnome so scared of sea voyages; he built the first magically enhanced Locker so light it would float even loaded with heavy contents. Whenever he had to travel at sea he would board the ship sitting in his travel case. Adventurers soon realized the ingenuity of this magical chest and the Gnome built and sold a small amount of these containers. It is rumored that on his last trip he locked himself quickly in his container to avoid a storm. However in his haste he had forgotten the container was hermetically sealed.
This is a small incredibly light locker.

Originally created by a gnomish worshipper of Goran to help brace the back during long periods of heavy lifting, the dwarves of Lar have adjusted these to help take the strain off the back during the crafting process. The brace itself is thick leather with veins of iron through it to provide additional support.

Handed out to those deemed worthy by the Shadow Thieves, these belts are prized by street workers who find it much easier to empty the purses in the crowded streets. It is a rather undescript belt to avoid undue attention. Always with a backup plan, the belt can be activated for a quick retreat by those unfortunate enough to be caught.

As many know, the town of Katherian is often full of crimes.  In order to be better protected from those who would wish to lighten loot chests, many go so far as to put traps on their doors when they sleep at night, instead of just your normal locks.  Rumor has it that the creation of these belts were inspired by what a cleric of Shadon saw one dismal night in the very docks of Katherian.

It was from the shadows that eve, this priest of Shadon peered, content with himself after a successful night of his own trickery and mischief.  He caught a glimpse of a young raven-haired elf whom he began to watch curiously as she stepped from hiding to pick the lock of the front door of the house.  Obviously from out of town, or perhaps just so excited that she picked the lock, the elf failed to realize the door was trapped.  Once unlocked, she tried to open the door, only to set off an intense electrical trap.  Although she tried to escape, she just wasn't quick enough to retreat from the lightning's bolts and ended up falling to a shocking death.  The Cleric laughed at her mishap, but was inspired to create an item that might help with the retreat of such situations.  In thanks of the idea, and in his amusement, the cleric raised the elf and sent her on her way simply saying, "Don't do that".  This is one of such belts, inspired from that dark Katherian night.
Made from a dark and slightly silky material, this belt seems to be infused with magics.

This is one item in a two item set that was created for what people long ago called The Watchers. They were instrumental in protecting the True Line of Kings. Through the ages many have been lost or stolen but a few remain stashed away and forgotten.

This green and black leather belt at first sight simply passes as tacky and strange. It's many pouches and odd dog faced buckle making it a rather bold fashion statement.

Yet to the curious onlooker that bothers examining under a hidden plate on the buckle would find the following text written in an elaborate Pranzis Cant:

"Congratulations on your acquisitions of one of our magnificent Black Hound Belts! 

This fine instrument will facilitate all business deals from this day henceforth. If you have found this message then you likely have also found the handy lenses of different calibres within your right side pouch. Useful for all those tricky details that the normal eye cannot see!

Also you will have likely found a conveniently placed set of locksmith tools. These handy devices, helpful for all situations. Particularly handy when allowing old ladies back into their locked out homes!

Under this you will have likely also found a small holder of notes. With the small charcoal provided, any interesting pieces of information found now can be recorded with ease. No more ink smudges!

You may have also found a few handy tools on the back pouch of the belt. These many odd contraptions allowing any and all the good spirit souls to work those tricky devices that may cause so much harm to anyone that may step on them. We are here to help!

Finally, if things get to tricky, just push the buckle within and twist it. You will find yourself conveniently invisible!

May the Good Lord Bless You!"
A green and black belt with many strange compartments and an elaborate dog head shaped buckle.

These feathers imbue the user with a bless from Katia herself. It is thought that each time the Bird Lord speaks to a bird then the feathers of that bird are blessed. From time to time those birds lose their feathers.

Produced during the war to retake the islands of Roldem from Bloodstone's army, blades like this were distributed to the Mistone soldiers who fought in Operation Bloodfall, thus the nickname for the longswords.  Even though the weapons were mass-produced, most of them are still of very high quality.  It bares the emblem of Mistone Alliance who coordinated the war effort, three eyes encircled by five stars.
A simple blade that bares an emblem of three eyes encircled by five stars.

There are many cults and sects scattered around Layonara that have a fondness for the whip and the pain it can inflict.  This whip is deadlier than most.  Fine shards of sharpened material similar to glass or crystal have been worked into the weave of the braid making it the inflictor of both pain and a nasty wound.  These whips are not to be trifled with.  Neither are their creators.
A impressive looking weapon. The braid of the whip seems to be embedded with something.

Two small stones are set into this silver ring; they are set and cut in such a way that they resemble a pair of elven eyes.

These rings are known as the Night Twins, as they are always forged in pairs, and the forging occurs at night when the moons Orn and Ausir are both in the sky. During the forging, they are said to absorb some of the light of the moons, causing them to emit a faint, yet continuous white light.

They are only made on the continent of Voltrex, and are often gifted to high ranking elven nobility, or servants of the Five Towers of Voltrex.

The rings protect the wearer from lesser forms of scrying, but also amplify the scrying skills of the wearer.

The rings are especially designed for small elven fingers, those of other, larger races find it hard to fit the rings around their plump fingers. Attempts at widening these rings have always led to a complete loss of power.

This ring seems to be made of silver with a small, perfectly round stone at it's centre. The colouring of the stone is rather peculiar, as it's surface is clearly divided in two equal parts by almost indistinguishable line. On one side of the line the stone is the colour of the purest white, on the other side the white has a strongly silvery hue. The silver band is covered with runes of some sort and you think the stone is giving off a soft, white glow.

These boots were rumored to be worn by a performer known simply as "The King". 
He would dazzle audiences with his dancing.... all the women would swoon over him.
The boots were stolen from him one night and since then copies of them have sprung up all over Layonara.
A pair of blue soft leather boots.
Forged from blessed silken strands for the Sisters of Rebirth, rare amulets such as these are still found where one of the sisterhood may have fallen where seeking out the corrupted.
This was one mans attempt at proving that things look better when you're drunk. Although many wonder what his motives truly were in making such an odd item.

One of only a few weapons created by the mad weapon smith Argaman Harnoshan, one of the few surviving dwarf-human hybrids that snuck through before such cross-breeding stopped altogether in the early 1400's. Although Argaman lived through his birth and grew to manhood, most say his brains were not strapped in right and he was known to alternate between lucid periods of productivity and rage-fueled killing sprees in the wilds.
These Arrows are said to have been blessed by the Longstrider, Folian S'Pae. They are handed out to those that excel in carrying out his will.
Created originally by the mage Daevinn to compliment his robe Avoidance, these gold and blue bracers have elaborate bead work on the edges.

Armor given to the rangers following Athlonus, who fought Milara's monstrosities from the woods and forests around Alindor. Most of Athlonus's followers were elves, and the armor was designed to survive massive blows from the often huge creatures.

Found at the bottom of a small, now-defunct enclave of Rofireinite priests, these one-handed staves seemed designed to repel undead that would find a desert environment hospitable. Since the re-discovery of the abandoned monastery, the staves have been reproduced and named for the city closest to their origin.

Many, many axes have been made by the orcish followers of Grand since his ascension. However, one orc smith named Bracht achieved a great deal of notoriety near the Grand Temple by producing axes of very high quality, and learning to smith the more difficult metals. Holding a grudge against elves and humans as well as dwarves, his axes were constructed to give advantages against all three races. Now working for Jukha exclusively, some of his earlier weapons have been looted by adventurers and come into the market.

This is one item in a two item set that was created for what people long ago called The Militia. They were instrumental in protecting the True Line of Kings. Through the ages many have been lost or stolen but a few remain stashed away and forgotten.

The runes of an intricate maze are etched into the side of this roughly crafted greataxe. The minotaurs make such weapons to assist in navigating the dungeons and mazes where they dwell. Always a fondness for traps and paths of complexity, the minotaurs betray their bestial nature with a fierce cunning. Those poor souls lost in their tunnels wander aimlessly for miles in fatigue through endless perils before the Maze Lords command their forces upon them. The bite of this axe may also send the mind into a maze, leaving an enemy lost on its feet.

A flat square ruby lies along the tarsal line of the gloves, glowing a warm gentle red with the occasional spark emitting now and then. The glove fabric itself shimmers with strange glows, usually rotating and cycling between a black and white. It can only be speculated as to whom crafted these masterpieces.
This simple looking sling was always at the side of a halfling known to hunt on Mistone. He was able to take down even the biggest of wild game with what many wrote off as a childs toy.

A copy of a treatise on those who defend the forests, written by a druid who was later left his order and then joined the Wolfswood Rangers. His transcriptions of spellsongs and spellweaving done by the creatures is woven into the  pages and translated into common. Excerpt: "She moved as a faun, her hooves as delicate, her modesty unheeded except for natural fur around her hips; and I could not look away for despite the goat-shaped pupils, she was as beautiful as anything I'd ever seen. It was then she sang and the voice - oh, the voice! - My falling into slumber was worth the glimpse, for the satyrs are most protective of their females." As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
Beauties and Beasts: Dryads, Satyrs, and Other Forest Natives

A mask of leather and wolf fur made to look like a hound's face that aids a stealthy individual with alertness and perception. Said to have been first created by Branderbackian mages, a very limited number of copies have been made.

This double scimitar was the lifes work of a man from Dregar. He was constantly seeking to balance good and evil. His attempt with this weapon was to find a balance by combining each. Positive, and Negative, Light and Darkness.

Given to the armies of Sinthar, this ammo is fine shot with razor edges embedded. It is slung in handfuls rather than singly. Once embedded the shot is very difficult to remove and the shrapnel does as much damage as the bullet. It is often found in areas that Blood's armies fought.
This club has no makers mark of any kind. However its creator clearly had one goal in mind. Making it a better choice for putting the undead to rest.

Originally designed by an unnamed, frustrated crossbow-wielding undead slayer. Designed with a rounded head and additional counterweight, these bolts work just fine against the walking dead and the living alike.

Used by the dwindling Broken Glade giant clans outside Prantz, these massive axes are not wieldable by anyone smaller than a half-orc. With thick oak branches for handles and iron axe heads that can weigh over forty pounds, this axe in the hands of one strong enough can kill with a single blow. With the giants almost always at war with rival tribes these axes can sometimes be found around the Forest of Fog

After the dust cleared from Operation Bloodfall on Roldem, The Wolfswood Rangers were shocked and saddened to hear of the fatality of their Commander in charge.  The Commander's passing was mourned greatly amongst the troop.  Yet with the tragedy came a glimpse of hope as a hero amongst many and a stalwart ranger rose to the promotion.  It was under the new guidance of this Commander, the Rangers began massive efforts to restructure, rearm, and outfit the Corps.  

These bows were fashioned during that time by only the best woodcrafters, and given an extra blessing from the Longstrider, Folian S'pae.  When armed with the bowstring tucked amongst your fingers, the feel of the bow heightens your very senses, awakening your eyes and ears to your surroundings to let your arrows strike hard and true.

The longbow is a refinement of the shortbow, designed to increase the range and power of an arrow strike. The stave portion of a longbow is nearly as tall as the archer, and can reach over six feet.  This particular bow seems to heighten your very senses at its touch alone.

This shirt looks to be made of woven hemp, but upon closer inspection, one finds it to instead be a mesh of incredibly tiny rings. With a strange ability to stretch to more than twice it's original size, this shirt seems to have found its way out of the hands of the fey creatures who made it.

Several sources have been credited for these powerful cloaks; Aeridin's Church being one, Az'attan's being another. The cloaks themselves provide a boost against most venoms and also grant the wearer the ability to see magically cloaked individuals.

This ring is the product of years of research from noted gemologist and wizard Kay Whitehall. Having found a deposit of diamonds in a long-abandoned site with what she claimed was a special affinity for enhancment, it was her idea to enchant the diamonds with the power to boost all aspects of a being's abilities. She was disappointed to find that the diamonds were not much stronger than their normal kin and shattered when too much magical energy was cast upon them, but not before she'd perfected a way to enhance two different attributes and add other boosts. Passing of old age in 1486, her secret went to her grave with her and shortly after, her entire collection magical ring experiments went missing with no explanation. 

A few of the rings have been spotted on the hands of the very rich over the last two decades and even fewer have popped up in odder places. The ring you hold bears her signature carving in the gold band - KHW.
These small daggers are made of Onyx, or volcanic glass. They are so razor sharp that they often leave a wound that continues to bleed.
A favorite sport in cities where animals are often used for entertainment, bull running has given rise to specialized equipment. This has become as sought-after item by cattle herders as well.

This crossbow appears to be constructed of two different types of material.  The stock is some type of lightweight hardwood. The bow itself is made mostly of metal. This seems to give the crossbow a bit more snap than its all wood relatives.
A longbow of mahogany that has seen long and hard use.

Created by a dwarven clan deep in the Spine Mountains of Tilmar during an extended war with dark elves from the deep, and later...other things, a few of these morningstar maces have made their way into the hands of traders and occasionally adventuring souls.

This rustly old helmet is badly dented, uncomfortable and difficult to see out of the eye slots. Several dents poking in feel as if they would poke into your head should you be hit while wearing it. Yet for all it's short commings it still seems to offer some protection.

This Scimitar was the only weapon of a man known as the Desert Fox. To the best of any ones knowledge he spent his entire life in the Anuroch Desert. He avoided people whenever possible. But on a rare occasion a traveler would stumble upon him as he fought the local Desert Giants. His scimitar gleaming in the hot desert sun would cut them down like they were nothing. His blade was found hung as a trophy within a settlement of Desert giants... so one can only assume he was killed.

Devised from plans only gnomes can concoct, the Bracer of Many Needles snaps open its hidden compartment at a press of a button and shoots out many needles at the target. Similar to the ability of a manticore, the bracer comes with five charges.
A strange gnomish bracer with a single button on it.  Better not mess with it without knowing what it does.
Gloves supposedly blessed by The Lifegiver, Aeridin. The power within them helps bring undead souls to rest.

A set of robes for the battle cleric, made by the aged tailor mage Shelia Basting of Spellgard. When pressed about her personal worship, she refuses to give up her denomination (if any) -- her work, she says, "is for everyone".

For the fearless and prepared who walk in the Deep, these boots have been made and copied to provide protection from a number of Deep dwellers. As a few have made their way up from the depths of Layonara they have become favored by spies, assassins, and politicians (for obvious reasons).

Once a featured dancer in the taverns around Port Hempstead, Edna Reelhawk slowly succumbed to age, as we all do. She fought, however, and fought hard; first by dying her hair, then using every anti-aging medicine she could find. When finally she could not gloss over the cracks, she turned to magic. She began paying to have her favorite dancing clothes enchanted to add to her physique and beauty. When her dancing clothes failed to cover her advanced years, she turned to questionable magics, that failed...fatally. Her enchanter was given the outfit he spent so much time weaving magic into and he decided to make a few copies and cash in on the desire for the illusion of eternal youth.

This special wind and fire wheel was made for a circus performer from Fort Wayfare. He would do special tumbling and twirling routines all while wielding one or two these wheels. Each blade tip of this wheel seems to have been enchanted with a different element.
One of several ranged weapons made by a woodsman from Alindor. His skills in crafting ranged weapons was highly sought after. Thus some of them can still be found today.
This mighty hammer displays several dwarven symbols. It has seen its fair share of battle against giant kin.
Created by a Dorand-worshipping craftswoman who moved to Gi from the Brech Mountains to join the community, these weapons stress fluidity and forethought as well as lethal efficiency.

This is one item in a two item set that was created for what people long ago called The Scouts. They were instrumental in protecting the True Line of Kings. Through the ages many have been lost or stolen but a few remain stashed away and forgotten.

These spears are often used by Giant kind to skewer a smaller creature. Either to be eaten off the spear right away or turned on a spit at a later time. Then the spear doubles as a toothpick digging bits of the meal from their teeth.

Created locally in Spellgard then enchanted at the Academy, these fine wrist-length silk gloves are powder blue with white piping. To someone attuned to the Al'Noth, they glow brightly. There is a tag on the inside embroidered with a spool of thread spelling out "Tweed, since 1301".
Having seen several of the normal archers belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.
Having seen several of the normal brawlers belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.
Having seen several of the normal swordsmans belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.

A brutal mercenary from Dregar wielded this scythe. Some who stood their ground were frozen in fear as they saw this weapon bear down on them. It got to the point that people simply ran when they saw this sinister weapon coming at them, for they knew if they stood their ground death would be greeting them soon.

For an enterprising sneak, these gnome-designed boots have it all. Made from metal-reinforced leather, they have a self-oiling mechanism (replenished from a small intake tube above the heel) to keep steps quiet. The dark-stained foot ware also has tools hidden in the top fold and inside slits along the heel, to aid in gaining entrance unannounced.

The powerful dwarf Jorgan Graniteside once wielded this axe around 1402, the Dark Ages of Layonara. He was a quiet fellow, but his axe spoke volumes. He was rumored to have bested an entire group of powerful ogres single-handed that attacked attempting to steal the ore he mined earlier that day. With this mighty axe in hand Jorgan had an ability to call upon an inner rage making him far stronger than normal. However this strength came at a price and that was his eventual downfall. Several years later copies of his mighty axe began to show up across the lands.

This deadly Katar was the favored weapon of a mercenary from the Katherian area. He could drive this Katar into his enemy with such force that it would even pierce plate armor. Though his favorite attack with it was to surprise his target from behind and place a well aimed punch to the base of the neck.

These pipes were originally made by an unknown and forgotten Dwarven Clan. All that is known is that the fathers made and handed down a new pipe to each of their sons. Originals bear the clan symbol on the bowl of the pipe. The ones found now are cheap copies of the originals and bear no clan symbols.

A sputtering, sparking nightmare with blades, bumps and pointed tips thrusting forth from various holes in the weapon's head seemingly at random. Wielding this club requires concentration and balance, which puts the wielder at a disadvantage in combat

Crafted by the mad Shadonite bard Rocco Sockopopper, this mandolin has been imbued with strange enchantments designed to make it pack a hefty punch. Known for his chaotic displays of violence against squashes, watermelons and various furniture on the stage, the demented gnome long lamented the rising costs and inconvenience of replacing instruments on the road. With alchemical gusto he studied long and hard formulas of hardening and strengthening. His works culminated into fine gems of mayhem such as this. These instruments are valued highly by both tricksters who enjoy fighting flashy, as well as skalds and battle bards who tend to be rough on their instruments

Created by the mage Miza four hundred years ago, these armored neckpieces provided extra protection for his personal guard. His eventual death and the bickering over his considerable estate resulted in a goodly number of his more interesting creations being crated away for centuries. Just before Sinthar's return, a few of these crates were opened by curious distant relatives, and the gorgets were quickly discovered and replicated. Now the occasional copy is popping up in markets all over Layonara.

Worn by the militias of Morholt, this heavy sapphire and diamond amulet practically screams "bribe me". Vicious turf wars between slavers and thieving guilds over territory have brought a few of these to the market.

This key was the brainchild of a halfling from the Hempsted area. He had hoped to create a key that once inserted into a lock would change its shape to move all the pins and tumblers into the proper position. Thus opening the lock. The drawback the key would destroy itself after one use. He never overcame this flaw thus the keys are highly sought after items.

A simple looking staff at first glance. However upon closer examination you notice a small opening at one end and a small button where you would typically hold the staff. I wonder what this button does?

Ancient tomes speak of this skull having once been that of a great wizard who sought to overcome the bonds of death.  While his spirit has long since been vanquished a part of him remains within this skull.  When placed upon the head of the worthy, this skull reveals its true nature.
A skull of a long dead creature, bleached and faded by the sun.

Given out to acolytes of Xeen, these "robes" are usually made of leather and are tailored to fit closely to the body. Creative adaptation is encouraged so long as it facilitates the purpose of the garment; to get one's way.
Path of the Vine Acolyte Robes

Given out to acolytes of Xeen, these "robes" are usually made of leather and are tailored to fit closely to the body. Creative adaptation is encouraged so long as it facilitates the purpose of the garment; to obtain obedience upon demand.
Path of the Whip Acolyte Robes
It's mithril, yes but the maker either didn't know how to forge it or the metal cooled wrong.  This doesn't feel right in the hand and doesn't move fluidly in combat.

After the failed defense of Prantz, bodies littered the city and surrounding areas. Despite Rael's attempts to collect all the armor and weapons from the battle areas, a few of these suits of half-plate found their way off of the men and women who in life wore them, and into the black markets.

From the copy of Rainstorff's axe that exists, reproductions have been made by several different dwarven smiths. A very few of these have been enchanted in an attempt to create a working copy of the great Vorax Champion's weapon. How close to the original these heavily enchanted and powerful copies are is unknown but at a couple seem to fit some of what is known of the great dwarven champion's weapon.
Favored by rat catchers in cities all over the world, this cloak is reasonably easy to copy yet provides that extra edge to vermin-hunters.

Dark elves are the enemy. We have known this for millennia, and as they and Milara become bolder in their assertions of the surface, we can no longer hide our eyes and pretend they will stay out of the light. Read these pages and know them; their spells, their abilities, and their treachery. Be ready - for they have the patience of a spider and they have been waiting." As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
This wavy blade is rusted and set with many spiked burs along the blade. It is poorly balanced and may break apart with a strong parry, but it sure looks like it would hurt like the blazes going in.

Worn by the mages that help defend Sadinia on Voltrex, these robes were scavenged from a battlefield in southern Dregar. Why they were there, and who they fought is unknown. The Sadinian ruling council has requested the return of all items belonging to their mages, but with information as to the purpose of the battle and the reason so many mages were found dead not forthcoming, the robes have begun to sneak out of custody and into the marketplace. 

The robes themselves are powdery blue with black trim, woven through with mithril thread much thicker than standard reinforced clothing. They also carry powerful enchantments that can be cast upon the wearer.

Worn by any officer of Molvaren's that lead troops numbering one-hundred or greater, these green broadcloth sashes have a mark similar to the tattoos that etched the skin of Molvaren's sentient tools enchanted indelibly upon the buckle. No attempt so far to remove the mark has worked, and that is why despite their power the sashes are rarely used.
Sash of a Green Dragon Officer

These are the favored instruments of the hedonist satyrs, played through merrymaking and drunken revelry. A free-spirited people, the winds of these pipe are as random as their wild whims. The sound of this instrument is enchanting, leading one into a sense of deep relaxation as their minds begin to wander to places distant. It is said that such woodwinds are only freely given to friends of the forest, though a good pint of dwarf sledge and a sizable slice of roasted mutton may also seem a fair trade to a satyr in his drunken state. The satyrs' sense of revelry courses through the veins of those who play these pipes, feeling the urge to stay awake just one moment more for another round, song or dance.
Plied from dead creatures or found scattered, these darts show the effects of weather and exposure.

Item description: Made and copied by countless students in Spellgard, this cloak has the outward appearance of a standard item of clothing. When worn, it makes a quiet crinkling noise; careful inspection reveals that the inside lining is a soft gauze that is see-through when pressed against the material next to it. The inner material of the cloak is tight-woven wool with a paper cover that can be removed from a zipper on the bottom. Pressing the gauze against the paper allows the wearer to see whatever is written there. Due to this item, cloaks must now be removed before a student takes his desk during a school day in Spellgard.
Modeled after one of the hoods worn by Sharina Shadowfang, it is woven with dye-able hair. The strands contain illusion magic that allows the wearer to more convincingly claim to be someone else.
This armor is constructed by tribes of various races that live in the swamps and bogs around the world. It seems to be resistent to the cold and diseases of these environments.
This armor is constructed by tribes of various creatures that live in the swamps and bogs around the world.

A thin book that includes magical studies of shaman and the few magically gifted orcs, goblins, ogres, and (included in the author's estimation) giants. Spell gestures are carefully described on the pages in common with trigger words that will release the magic. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
Shaman and Magic: Of Orcs, Goblins and Other Inferior Races

The Shewper Shillelagh (shuh-ley-lee). It's not just a club it's a Shewper Shillelagh! This was the sales pitch of the clubs creator, John Shewper. He peddled his Shillelaghs across Mistone. Unfortunatly John had a horrid lisp and often drew several giggles when he'd cry out... You will alwayshh be shaffe wiff a Shooper Shilaylee at your shide!

The Shin Biter is powerful tool and status symbol of giant hunters around the globe. Braided from the nose hairs of fallen giants, these giantbane slings are imbued with gnomish alchemy to seek out the hides of those who grew them. The Shin Biter also grants one the giantkin knowledge of "catching" rocks, albeit smaller ones. 

Originally created by the gnomish Giant hunter, Gromak Kneesplitter, this sling was his answer to his opponents' throwing boulders. It is said that the mad little barbarian would scale the tallest mountain and rain death down upon them from above, shouting "Who's the tallest now? Who's the tallest NOW?!" with maniacal fury. Giants who look upon these weapons are equally filled with fear and rage, and they have long been forbidden to the faithful of Grannoch. While Voraxians and giants layers both hold this item with high regard, no one enjoys them quite as much as the Shadonites. It is made out of nose hair, after all.

Tales speak of a rogue whose delicate touch was his bread and butter searching for a way to avoid damage to his fingers in combat; after experimenting with a metal gauntlet on his off hand, he struck on the idea of a bracer worn on the off hand with a fixed blade jutting from the fist. With the flare of the bracer, people often mistake it for a buckler with a fixed blade. Whatever it is, it's very useful for deflecting attacks and does not require the skills required by larger, more bulky shields.
This suit was formed from several parts off of dead, broken and dismantled constructs. Woven with Al'Noth it has become a good suit to have should one be dealing with constructs.

The title on the binding and cover says it all. A wealthy man wanted to be able to summon beasts to aid him but he had no Divine connection to any deity. Nor did he have any knowledge of the Al'Noth. What he did have was stacks and stacks of True coin. Which it took most of before this book was perfected.
Apparently some discarded necklace. It is so badly tarnished most would not want to show it around their necks. Its small gem does seem to have a faint glow to it if looked at in the darkness.
This large shield is particularly good at deflecting missile attacks off its flared edges. Rumor has it the design dates back to the human-elf wars, as used by the humans.
This sling was made for a wagon master from Hlint. He frequently found his caravan under attack from goblins. He had this sling made to help keep them at bay when he traveled.

Slightly north of the forest of the Mist on the continent of Dregar spans a mountain range known as Blackfeather Mountains.  It is said that years ago the Broken Glade Giants drove away flocks of crows that had made home in the eastern parts of the forest, forcing them towards the North.  The crows flapped wildly around for days of unrest after being forced from their home, until finally coming to rest on the nearby mountain range.  Some say if you walk through one of the abandoned dwarf trails at the foot of the mountain, you will find a layer of crow's feathers at your feet.

The origin of this necklace is thought to be that very place.  Rumor has it that along with the crows, a powerful shaman also inhabits the mountains.  Strangely however, those who go looking for him either never seem to find him, or never come back.  It's said that on some nights when Ausir and Orn sit just right in the sky, the Shaman of Blackfeather Mountains comes out.  His slender elven figure can be seen in the moonlight as he makes his way through the dwarf trails picking up and blessing the crow feathers with powerful magics.  Once strung together feathers give gifts of the night.  Though a powerful aid, it's important to be weary of artifacts such as this since nobody knows what exactly the Shaman had in mind when creating them.
Several black feathers are strung together to form a necklace.

Page upon page of creatures from the briny deep and the spells they learn to cast under water; from slimy aboleths to the Saguahin to the monstrous kraken, each creature is given a diagram and in the cases where spells are cast, the magic is woven into the pages. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.

This goad was changed from a simple tool that herds cattle into a formidable weapon against snakes and other vermin. A man who often roamed the deserts of Mistone had this made after having to many run-ins with snakes.

A halfling thief from Vehl once called this hammer his own. He would leap out at his targets and SMACK! land this hammers head right on their foot. Typically sending the target to the ground and often slowed considerably because of how badly they would hobble on one foot when trying to chase him down.
The first knuckle of a troll carved with arcane symbols. Rumored to be made by a necromancer from around the River of Darkness, but not verified

This sword was commissioned by Tsaryn, a Blackguard of Corath from smiths in Gi. Their fine work was unbeknownst to them enchanted with dark magic, and then used to kill the smith and a few other villagers when Tsaryn returned test his new toy.

Tales from battle lines in Rael speak of a warrior infamous for "turtling" behind his shield. After his shield's poor balance was used against him one too many times, he had a shield of this design made using the Al'Noth and mundane counterbalancing to foil those attacks and leave him on his feet.
A simple band of mithril, this ring radiates magic but has no maker's mark.

This walking stick burns with the flames eternal. One would think it would be smoldering hot, but no, it is quite cold to the touch. This is because it is food for the Fire Genesai. Those extra-planar beings craft these walking sticks to fuel their flames and fill their bellies on their long jaunts beyond the planes and into the mortal realm. Perpetually burning, the wood of this staff seems to soak up the heat around it, and visa versa... replenishing anew, only to be burned and burned again.
 
Mages who specialize in the ways of fire feel especially hungry while wielding this staff. They feel the need to cast even more fire than before, and occasionally lick of it its sweet barky sustenance as they make their long journeys across the mortal realm. This is hunger of the flame ever-burning. The blood of fire mages yearns for release when they wield this staff. The desire to burn, the desire to feed. And so, like the Fire Genesai who held this staff before them, they become bastions of the primal elements, yearning to engulf the world in flames. Some people live to watch the world burn. You would be one of these people, should you choose take up this staff. Your blood as flame, and the world around you, kindling.
Walking Stick of the Fire Genesai
Warthog Smithyz mak armur fur yu. Gud skin tak hard hit. Warthog hide mak strongr. Yu like!

A band of Shadow Thieves based out of Katherian produced these umbrellas and would sell them for exorbitant prices lauding their protection from electricity.  Any time they saw someone using their costly umbrellas, they knew the person had gold to throw around.

Growing on the skirts of the Ire Mountains, right at the edge where they meet the blazing sun of the Spirit Dunes, this strange small flower grows only during the first and few days of rain in the region.

Once collected it is normally regrown in milder weathers, but those few that manage to survive the unkind desert weather gain a unique quality.

When held high, The Desert Firstbloom Wildflower bathes the area in a brilliant blue light. This light seem to recall travellers of the stars gleaming in the desert skies, thus why some locals call it the Starlit Bud.

A few enterprising individuals who experimented with the flower discovered that if the petals are torn a stream of positive energy spews forth from its stem. Destroying the flower, yet healing wounds at a miraculous rate.
A small pink and white petaled flower.
Useful for day and night reconnaissance, these enchanted leathers are given to scouts of the Wolfswood Ranger Corps. Scouting being as dangerous as it is, not every owner of a suit returns.
This belt is for those who can dish it out but can't take it. A favored item of less than savory characters.

"These boots were made by the gnomish inventor Yolanda Shinstepp. She loved to go dancing and found that the larger people at the Tavern would knock her around while on the dance floor. She could not make people watch out for the little folks, so she got to working on an item that would improve her dancing and keep her from being knocked around.
 
After a few years of testing and failed prototypes she came up with her dancing boots. They were an instant hit with people who tried them on. They could dance the night away without fear of bumping into others, even when they got drunk. People actually got better the more they drank.
 
After a few years she started to get a desire to wear her Dancing boots even when not dancing. It got to the point where she never took them off, even to bathe.
A pinch of dust taken from the ruined land where the city of Zolinar once stood, before the city's reconstruction began.

A very in-depth study of the various magical attacks utilized by golems and their constructors. It seems the scribes who copied this book did so in extreme detail, so all footnotes, side notes, cross outs, and doodles are also included. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
A Study and Details of Constructs and Their Elemental Abilities
Reddish metal chainmail that looks like it was used for target practice by Rael's army.

Very few men and women believe that the world they live on is only one of many; most cling to the belief that their reality is the only one in existence. Fewer still have proof of another pit, and only a few handfuls have walked more than one.  These boots, exceedingly rare, are rumored to be a copy of a pair worn by a creature "not of Layonara"...and for the brave handfuls who travel far beyond their comfort zone, are very sought after
Worn leather armor that still offers some protection.
Plate armor built for the personal guard of a prominent Creedo family; the armor is hinged and enchanted to allow bursts of swift movement.
This pitchfork emits a sickly yellow light.  Perhaps that is why it was discarded.

Designed as both an offensive and defensive weapon, the U-43 is capable of releasing a blast of damaging elemental breath at a press of a button. The four buttons on the belt each corresponds to an element: red for fire, blue for electrical, white for cold, and green for acid. Each belt comes with three charges to unleash on unsuspecting foes.
A gnomish belt with four buttons. Better not mess with it without knowing what it is.

In the days when Elf fought man and dwarf alike, there existed a company of fine archers that were the bane of many an enemy troop.  Their bows were the things of legend and even after some semblance of peace arose between the nations, they were still coveted by many an archer.  Bows were handed down through families and cherished as heirlooms such that even the training versions of the more elite bows become treasures.  You see before you the bow of an elf that had obtained a more direct link with his weapon. The shaft of this longbow radiates power. The one who pulled its string was a fearsome opponent. A single arrow shot with exacting accuracy could be deadly.  This is indeed a very fine bow. The fine craftsmanship of this weapon attests for the link between elf and his bow, as such only ones of elven descent may use it.

In the days when Elf fought man and dwarf alike, there existed a company of fine archers that were the bane of many an enemy troop. Bows were handed down through families and cherished as heirlooms such that even the training versions of the more elite bows become treasures.
