Layonara Object Editing v0.9

--------------------------------------------------------
               PLEASE READ
--------------------------------------------------------

Use the quill upon the object you will be editting. Syntax for the commands follow.

Please do not place editted items on your ox pack as the edits will get lost.

You only need to use the quill once, it works the same as the language ears, requiring a voice.

You can use the ~ on any channel

You can not ever repeat the same command, the system will not "hear" a repeated command.

Please read the Notes for various commands.
--------------------------------------------------------
                 COMMANDS
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~title
Description: Changes the object's name.
Usage: ~~title Plenarius' Diary
Note: In order to see changes to the name of an object you must refresh your inventory.  Either close and open it or flip between tabs in your inventory.
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~
Description: Write upon the object's description.
Usage: ~So I was walking down the street the other day when a dragon fell from the sky.
Note: If you want a space before your word, then put one between the ~ and the first letter (i.e. ~ A new sentence)
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~!
Description: Begins a new paragraph with the text following.
Usage: ~!The next morning dawned and things seemed a little better.
Note: Essentially inserts two new lines and five spaces before your text.
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~nl
Description: Creates a new line.
Usage: ~~nl or ~~nll or ~~nlll or ~~nllll or ~~nlllll
Note: The amount of the letter "l" indicates how many new lines to insert, from one to five.
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~tab
Description: Inserts some spaces.
Usage: ~~tab
--------------------------------------------------------
Command:  ~~deleteNNN
Description:  Deletes the last NNN characters.
Usage: ~~delete63
Note: If the amount of characters you try to delete exceeds the size of the text, you will erase it all.
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~erase
Description: Wipes the object's description completely.
Usage: ~~erase
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~undo
Description: Restores your text to the previous state before your last command.
Usage: ~~undo
Note: This only works once!  There is no history, you can not keep undoing.
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~author
Description: Inserts the character's name.
Usage: ~~author
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~location
Description: Inserts the character's location.
Usage: ~~location
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~date
Description: Inserts the date.
Usage: ~~date
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~datetime
Description: Inserts the date and time.
Usage: ~~datetime
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~dateplace
Description: Inserts the date and location on two separate lines.
Usage: ~~dateplace
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~datesig
Description: Inserts the character's name then the date on two separate lines.
Usage: ~~datesig
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~~~
Description: Inserts a horizontal rule of tildes.
Usage: ~~~~
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~--
Description: Inserts a horizontal rule of dashes.
Usage: ~~--
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~oo
Description: Inserts a horizontal rule of the letter "o".
Usage: ~~oo
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~header
Description: Inserts your text centered amongst two dashed horizontal rules.
Usage: ~~header Day One of My Journey
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~headerfancy
Description: Inserts your text centered amongst two horizontal rules of the letter "o".
Usage: ~~headerfancy Recipe for Hampshire Haggis
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~headerdeco
Description: Inserts your text centered amongst two horizontal rules formed from tildes.
Usage: ~~headerdeco Chapter 17
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~speak
Description: Reads the description out loud.
Usage: ~~speak
--------------------------------------------------------
Command: ~~whisper
Description: Whispers the description out loud.
Usage: ~~whisper
--------------------------------------------------------

A magnificent weapon Latyemean'Ceviran boasts the finest of Elven craftmanship. It glows softly with an inner light, rune edged blade melting seamlessly into ornate crossguard and finely wrapped hilt. Perfectly balanced the blade is an extension of the hand for those chosen.

  Yet beyond the workmanship it is the intricate elven runes traced upon the surface that catch the eye. For those runes tell the tale of the blade, from forging onwards.   Over the years the tale has lengthened, the story adding itself in elven scripture to the blade itself, writing its history as it is once more wielded by a new owner. As the tale of the owner lengthens the blade becomes more potent, molding itself to the needs, and the fears of the one who uses it.

For those who can read the runes the tale reads:


    "Forged in fire to fight the dark, thus where all birthed. To four families did we go, receptacles to traits that they hold. Secret not given, need to be found, make the mark on the metal he ground.

  Two families found the grace of blades, one died and was lost, and I, the other never made. 

  Generation passed. Onto the next I moved, a son who had no desire for the blade. His talents called elsewhere, to the arcane he gave.

  A Knight he was made, to fight the dark until grave, yet none could see the impression the first had gave.

  Turn he did, fled under dark moon. Heirloom was all he took from his room. His family wept for the son they lost, the blade was forgotten as a loss of trust.

  Under the earth light grew dim, rust coated the surface, runes grew thin, the bearer, this shard of a soul committed evil after evil and we all grew old. 

  Death came at last as to all it does. Placed in a tomb, a relic of the past. There the blade sat until one picked it up.

  The shard reunited with its brothers a portion he left. Enough for the blade to pick up its true gift.

  Hands of righteous blade did find, hands that swung in place divine. Justice was met on swift knife edge, dispensation with holy Toranite pledge.

  Evil vanquished in tides and flood, dimmed runes brightend in paths of blood. Traces of heart in majesty found, yet runes and sigils to dull upon ground.

  For in a compassionate heart weakness found root, a place of love, shoulder of despair, deception was found in a heart once so fair.

  Holy Toranite vows forgotten, misplaced, the paladin fell from Torans shining grace. Standing head bowed, golden crown stricken, titles and roles now duly forbidden.

  Yet for paths feet found, lost in human embrace, the story continues to travel apace. In Torans grace will it ascend once more, or will it be caught in passionate encore?

Description: Az'atta was a devout priestess of Baraeon, a high priestess. She excelled and was favoured by him. Baraeon rewarded her with a mission to slay the avatar of the god of enlightenment - a child monk known as the Llama. Az'atta took a host of followers to the monastery where the child was staying. Though the monks fought courageously, they were caught unprepared. The monastery was razed, and the child captured. Az'atta performed a ritual, and killed the child. She took some of his blood in a goblet and drank it. The blood changed Az'atta, she briefly glimpsed the path of enlightenment. She renounced Baraeon, and fled the dark elf kingdom, taking a few of her loyal followers with her. For many years she lived in fear of Baraeon's followers finding her and killing her. During that time Az'atta dealt with many of her own followers who wished to return to Baraeon. Only two of her retainers stayed with her, and attempted to change. Layonara Server Rules - All of this information, and much more can be found at www.layonaraonline.com

The following is a list of Rules in place on the Layonara Servers.

This list is subject too change at any time and is not exhaustive. All interpretation and punishment for breaking these rules is controlled by senior GM's. We are always willing to discuss infringements and do not wish to come down hard on people unless absolutely necessary.

Player Vendor Rules

Only End Products should ever appear on Vendors. The more items the more lag it causes on the server. End Products include but are not limited too the following - Weapons, Armor, Magical equipment (Wands, Scrolls).  Do not sell junk or raw materials to the player vendors please.

It is possible to spread Player vendors out and place them in unique areas. Acceptable locations include - Temple's, Inn's, Market places.

PVP, Pk'ing and Griefing

Here on Layonara it is a well known fact that we do not tolerate PvP, PK'ing or Griefing. I personally am not against PvP but I am against the attitudes, heated tempers, etc. that come from it.

PvP is the act of a player attacking another player in any form. Do not attack familiars, companions, the character etc. Doing so will get you a warning and a three day ban on the first occurrence. The second occurrence will be an instant ban from the server.

PK'ing is the act of killing another character and the first time it happens you will have a very stern warning, and a seven day ban. If it happens again you will be instantly banned from the server.

Griefing is the act of intentionally causing another player emotional harm by a verbal assault. It is also the act of intentionally causing players to not be able to have fun in the world (following them and being a nuisance, blocking doorways, pick pocketing/stealing, kill stealing when asked not to, camping when asked to leave an area, being rude and obnoxious etc.) Doing so will get you a warning and a three day ban on the first occurrence. The second occurrence will get you a seven day ban and the third will get you banned from the server.

Another form of griefing is the act of attacking NPC's or stealing from them. This is not tolerated. It will get you a three day ban the first time, a seven day ban the second time and then a perma ban on the third. Do NOT attack or steal from NPC's.

I hate being so strict but for the good of the community that we are trying to build this is the only way it can be.

Muling on Layonara is not allowed.

What is muling you ask?

Good question.

In my opinion it is when a character gets something for nothing (or when people are trying to beat the system then it is something for very cheap). Muling is when you have items (in the bank, in your inventory, in your house, etc. that you have earned or fairly traded for) and then you give those items to a newly created character (usually your own character or a friends) for free. This gives the character a jump start on earning his way in the world.

Logging Off Versus Dying

Recently, there has been an increase in players logging off at inappropriate times. When you are running from a battle that you know you just can't win or in a dungeon that you know you can't make it out alone; it's not okay to log out. You need to remember that you put yourself in that position in the first place. Logging out in these instances is not allowed. Doing this can and will earn some type of punishment if witnessed by a GM or reported by another player.

I would like to stress that logging off in cases like this is not keeping with the RP environment!

We are all about RP on this world. I want players to know that each and every character that has something has in some way earned it. This is an important staple to the community here and I ask that it not be cheapened.

This server does not allow inappropriate language. I want to make sure that this server can be enjoyed by all that like to RP, including families. Please make sure you do not use such language when "speaking in" says; PARTY mode, or GM mode.

Characters:

All characters must be approved before playing in Layonara.  WhY you ask?  It is a large world and I want the players to feel like they live in a world, if we allow too many of one race or alignment things will begin to deteriate.  It is important that I keep a general idea of the quality of characters and players I have in the world if I am going to be able to continue to keep this a family style server/world.

These are the rules and guidelines that should be followed to get your character approved to play on our world.

Multi-classing. It is unacceptable to multi-class a character with the intent to garner a specific class benefit with the minimum amount of levels spent for example. A Sorcerer/Paladin (19/1) This character has clearly taken a single level of the Paladin class to apply the charisma benefit they will have for being a sorcerer too their character saves granted by the level of a Paladin. Taking (17/3) is still unacceptable in this instance. The general rule is if you multi-class one single class should never reach it's maxmimum potential. I.e a multi class mage should never be casting 9th level spells.

Acceptable multi-classing is 10/10 or as near as possible too this. The nearer you are too being a completely balanced character the more believable it is too us.


Characters that twist the boundaries of the norm or of the world of Layonara will be considered on an individual basis. Those likely to be successful will be those that remain within or enhance the spirit of the world. We have a extensive pantheon so priests we would prefer followed a god so that people get too know their gods. Also priests should choose domains that match those their deity has.


At this time a maximum of 4 characters per player is allowed.


Character backgrounds can comprise of whatever you wish. You can be born in Layonara or outside layonara. You can have relationships between characters and write them into your history if you wish. You can carry characters across beta's but be aware you will have to recreate them as level 1.

To date we have not rejected a character because of it's background however backgrounds that elude to characters being super powers or gods or some such are likely to be refused. We will decide these kind of storylines. Putting these into your background in the hopes of "encouraging" us too persue them with you is not going to be looked upon favorably. i.e Claiming to be the Son of Corath.


I want to state that all SoU Prestige Classes will be allowed with the exception of the Harper Scout and Shadowdancer. There are NO Harpers on Layonara.

Yes, Blackguard and Assassin are allowed... But you can not use it to muder, pvp, pk etc. and it must be a VERY good rp reason or it will NOT be approved. And here's the biggie here... You must be evil. Currently there are NO approved evil characters in the world. ONLY IF you are turned evil by a GM will this ever be allowed. Don't hold your breath!!

On a final note some of the rules are in a fluidic state and we reserve the right too change them as we feel fit such is the nature of the world and our willingness to leave things open for future change.

Reminded of some of the techniques recently and finding my old Central Casting books... here is a series of tips for creating characters

Age events:


The ages themselves are roughly 3 groups, 4 if you include education. For each of these try to detail one or more events and how the character at that age acted or decided.

By detailing a series of different events at different ages you charcter starts play with some momenteum or flow. Rather just "shows up" he/she is a person "in motion".

The age groups are:

Childhood - The time frame where the character is totally dependent on the family

Adolscent - The "teenage" years. Often times to test, push or break boundries. Begins to develop an indpedendent identity.

Young Adult - The first few years of full independence. "out of schoo", "first job" type events

Overall Education - The quality, type and source of education will impact a character's views. What skills do they know? What ethics have they been exposed to?

Sample events include:


Religous events

Criminal events

Boon/Gift/Blessing

Tragedy/Loss/Curse

Family crisis/change

World event (new King, pestilence, surge of magic)

Made a friend

Made an enemy

Injured

Achieved a success

Had a failure

Personality event (something simple which shows a personality aspect)

Moved to different culture/race/continent

Quiet/normal/boring period

War nearby

In military/milita

Joins an employer/patron/group/guild

Learns a secret of themselves or of others

Trade/craft/profession learns one or helps with one

Witnesses an event affecting someone else (what conclusions does the character draw as a result?)

Love (may vary by age to type of relationship)

Birth may also be something else to consider. Espicially if it was something unsual. Perhaps born in town during an attack. Usually though the character's personality isnt affected by their birth but rather it might influence the parents.

Akelen was a reknowned Wizard of some repute.
He was mainly known for his tough and stern teaching methods on his apprentices.... which on some occassions, resulted in said apprentice aquiring some form of unfortunate, if minor injury.

It was said he created a few of these amulets to gift to those he took on as new apprentices.
Although whether it was to protect the apprentice from himself, or protect him from his Master... is uncertain.

An unusual tome... written by a powerful mage and scriber... for his less than intelligent friend.

It came to the mage Arian, whilst traveling with his rather burly friend in the Forest of Fogs.

They were beset upon by a group of giants, and instantly the two dived into battle to defend themselves.

The mage called forth all forms of the Al'noth to dispose of his enemies, slaying a group of six in a matter of moments.

When done, he turned to observe his muscular warrior friend, desperatly fighting for his life against a single, lone giant.

The suddeness off the battle allowed no time for the mage to cast wards upon his friend.

And so it came to him.
A book of basic spells, scribed with special enchantments and magical runes.
His friend would merely have to touch the runes inscribed upon the parchment, and speak the words printed... and the spell would be cast.

Tempests' arrows... not to be confused with the Mistite High Priest or Priestess.

Sallaron Tempest, a rather dubious individual, famed in Hurm for his Ant-Slaving works, combined his master fletching skills with the rather explosive skills of the Al'noth his wife possessed.

The result was these... finely crafted, hollow tipped arrows.. each with a small enchantment placed by his sorceress wife which.. on impact, covers the target in a small flaming spell.

Rumour tells that, upon the first batch being created, his wife made him the official "guinea pig" for their testing.

In an attempt to impress upon the simple townsfolk of Vehl, the adventurer Arkolio paid out his own pocket to have a handful of these coins crafted.

With no real tender value, each coin is merely a cheap metal, painted a golden colour.

Merely toying with it, flicking it in the air,  rolling it across the knuckles... activates a small enchantment to make the bearer more.... agreeable.

Branderback
Aliases: The Wary Shadow, The Black Hound  
Race: Halfling 
Worshippers: Halflings, humans, half-elves.
Domains: Evil, Trickery, Destruction
Governs: Stealth, night, darkness, greed, self-preservation 

Dogma: 
     Branderback teaches his followers to live their lives to their fullest extent. There should be no limit to what one may desire, and if you can obtain it, then there is no reason why you should not have it. Branderback also teaches that although temporary allegiances with like-minded groups are necessary, you should always depend on yourself. Never be caught unaware, and have a backup plan to the backup plan. If all else fails, always blame someone else; why should you take the blame for something that was meant to happen?

Clergy's Weapons and Clothing. 
     Branderback's clerics prefer ranged weapons, especially those that can be enchanted to disable your opponents. Acid and poison are also acceptable, since they can be used to enhance arrows or darts and weaken foes. Clerics of The Wary Shadow garb themselves in black leathers to be concealed, and prefer to hide their skins to avoid having weak spots.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples of Branderback are rare and normally hidden from the eye. Most of them are facets of the underworld and can often be found in alliance with a local thieves guild. Rankings are very rare since most clerics of Branderback are loners, but it is rumored that every major region is under the watch of a High Silent Shadow, a very powerful and gifted cleric. Clerics of the Black Hound pray at dusk to welcome the coming of the night, and they celebrate Winter's Solstice since it is the longest night of the year.

Prayers:
While getting spells:
     "Let my acts be hidden in the shadows of the night, so that I may gain that which is rightfully mine."

When doing something fishy:
     "I pray that wealth belong to the greedy and careless, so that I may take from them what is rightfully mine."

Xantril Locales

The Great Forest
    Dominating the northern part of Xantril, the Great Forest is one of the largest forests on Layonara, thought to have been planted by Katia Herself. It is also one of the last bastions of good on Xantril. Rangers and druids, in cooperation with the forest itself, have withstood incursions of Xandrial's forces that managed to slip by Hilm Castle. The question is, how long can they prevail?

Archwood
    Part of the Great Forest, some say Archwood is actually the start of the Great Forest, as it was here that the first trees were planted. The Archwood has some of the oldest trees on the continent. Rumor has it that some of the most powerful druids walk among these trees.

The Demon Mountains
    Largest part of the Xantril mountain range, these mountains shine an eerie red glow into the night. Seat of power of Xandrial, his demon forces patrol the evil-tinged crags.

Fields of Death
    Until Xandrial arrived, a peaceful farmer's village once cultivated these fertile plains. Setting an example for the rest of the continent, Xandrial brutally slaughtered every man, woman, and child. These plains have since become known as the Fields of Death.

Mount Tulbane
    By far the largest peak on Layonara, Mount Tulbane towers above the great Xantril mountain range. For the followers of Grannoch, this is a holy mountain, as the scripture of Grannoch tells that she gave birth to the giant races on this mountain. 

Wallach's Crypt
    With the Tortured Lands turning more and more into a desert, a vast complex of crypts has recently been uncovered by the shifting sands. Legend has it that this might be the place where Wallach the Betrayer was cursed to burn forever after trying to usurp the position of his Lord, Pyrtechon.

Orsraun Mountains
    Northwestern part of the great mountain range on Xantril. A barren and unsettled land, there is not much to find in these mountains, except for Xandrial's patrols that watch the range's few passes. 

Giants Run Mountains
    Southwestern part of the great mountain range that covers the mid-eastern Xantril. Home to clans of fierce Giants, these mountains are best avoided if one does not want to end up a Giant's slave. Even dwarves do not tread these mountains lightly in search of ore.

Shattered Mountains
    The Shattered Mountains are the southeastern part of the great Xantril mountain range. They extend into the ocean, and their peaks can be seen above the waves for miles out of the coast.

The Roughlands
    A long time ago, the entire continent of Xantril was called the Roughlands; however, a climate change most likely brought on by the Cataclysm has caused Xantril to become greener. However, some areas can still be called the Roughlands, and there, ancient ruins with long-forgotten purposes are all that break up the sand and shrub landscape.

Lake of Salt
    The Lake of Salt was once a gray-green body of water that glistened in the sun, but at some point it dried into nothing more than a crater. It now marks the division between the Roughlands to the south and the Tortured Lands to the north.

The Tortured Lands
    North of the Lake of Salt, another wasteland called the Tortured Lands stretches out to the outskirts of Hilm Castle. A few villages struggle to survive in these lands, but it is just a matter of time before the entire region turns into a desert. Several ruins also dot these lands, most likely raided long ago. Nothing moves among their shattered columns and dilapidated statuary except jackals and a harsh wind.

Walikas Lake
    Source of the River Vesper, Walikas Lake is, for the time being, still a refuge from the horrors that plague the rest of Xantril. This is mostly because of the Walikas Hermit, a retired adventurer who is happy to live out the end of his days protecting this enclave of peace.

Council Hills
    If one follows the road to Westgate, one travels past the Council Hills. The councils referred to in the name of these hills may be those of the few sparsely populated hamlets around here, but no one is sure.

Lost Hills
    No one is sure why these are called the Lost Hills; anyone can plainly see that they lay along the road to Westgate on the western coast of Xantril.

The Wetwoods
    Something of a swamp and something a forest, the Wetwoods are aptly named. Large mangrove trees make up this insect-infested forest.

Troll's Marsh
    Aptly named, this foul smelling marsh is the largest swamp on Xantril and home to one of the fiercest troll clans around.

Sharawood
    The Sharawood is a small forest west of the Troll's Marsh. The wood and its surrounding areas have been claimed by a creature called Shara. No one is certain where the allegiance of Shara lies, but it appears that Xandrial's minions give the forest a wide berth.

Dun Hills
    Before a clan of kobolds, led by a kobold hero called Dun, moved into these hills, they were just called the Cloven Foothills, as they're the northern foothills of the Cloven Mountains. However, the Dun clan has truly carved out a small realm in these hills, and their name has been changed to reflect the kobold dominance of the area.

Ankh Wood
    Nested between the Dun Hills and the Wormbones is the small, placid forest of Ankh Wood. Even though Ankh is surrounded by hills filled with evil creatures, it is a tiny beacon of good in the evil that permeates Xantril. A bastion of Toran's followers bravely defends the tiny villages that dot the forest, protecting them from Xandrial's marauding forces.

The Wormbones 
    The western foothills of the Cloven Mountains are called the Wormbones. Several dragons were slain here, their corpses cut up and scattered across these hills. Fierce creatures, drawn by the power inherent in the dragons' bones, now stalk the hills.

Cloven Mountains
    Seat of power of the Skullcrusher clan, the Cloven Mountains are a small range on Xantril's eastern shore. When Xandrial arrived, the Skullcrushers were given a choice: serve or perish. King Skullcrusher refused at first, but was killed by Xandrial in a single blow. The new King Skullcrusher, intimidated by his predecessor's fate, decided to throw in his lot with Xandrial. The unholy alliance has served the Skullcrushers well, as their domain has expanded as far south as the Shinmean River.

Landaise Plains
    These fertile plains, mostly inhabited by farmers, were quick to fall under the onslaught of the Skullcrushers. The farmers were either slaughtered or enslaved, forced to work their own fields to feed the hungry giants.

Rathgaut Hills
    Several centuries ago, Karrak Diamondback, lord of the southern part of the Roughlands, as Xantril then was called, led his forces against an invading army that threatened to overrun Fort Thunder and then march on to Arabel. After a fierce battle, Karrak and his forces were victorious. For a decade after that battle, however, ghouls would rise from the hills and descend into the flatlands for a few days, after which they would simply disappear, only to reappear a few months later. The cycle repeated itself for nearly a decade before, oddly, it just stopped. The hills, however, never lost that name.

Lake Malisus
    The Shinmaen river flows down from Lake Malisus to Wyrm's Bay on the western coast of Xantril. Rumor has it that the sea serpents frequently sighted in this bay swim up the river to lay their eggs in Lake Malisus. The area around Lake Malisus has been annexed by the Hill Giants of the Skullcrusher clan.

Misty Vale
    Once a peaceful valley with its floor permanently covered by a layer of fog, the Misty Vale has now been occupied by the hill giants of the Skullcrusher clan.

Ilsare

Aliases: 
     Archer of Love, The Heart of Gold, Lady of Dreams  
Race: Elf 
Worshippers: 
   Mostly elves, humans, half-elves and halflings; fewer worshippers among other races.
Domains: 
     Air, Good, Protection
Governs: Beauty, love, passion, dance, music, art, sculpting 

Dogma: 
     Life is worth living because of the beauty found in the world and the love that draws hearts together. True beauty is more than skin deep. Believe in romance, as true love will win over all. Always follow your heart, for it leads you to your true destination. Perform loving acts, and seek to awaken love in others. Acquire beautiful items of all sorts, and encourage, sponsor, and protect those who create them. Find love wherever it takes root, and bring it to its fullest bloom so that all may share the joy and beauty it creates.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Ilsare's clerics favor bows as their weapons. After all, Ilsare is the Archer of Love, and love indeed is like an arrow fired by a bow: it strikes swiftly and with great power. Ilsare's clerics favor beautiful clothing and any kind of armor works if it is needed, as long as it is beautiful. Red is the color of love and fiery passion and thus clerics of Ilsare often prefer red clothes.

Clergy and Temples: 
     Ilsare's clerics are somewhat flighty and the hierarchy of the church is loosely organized. Ilsare's temples are always beautifully designed buildings with numerous interesting pieces of art decorating them. Clerics of Ilsare pray in the morning, after a refreshing bath and clothing themselves in whatever wonderful raiments they will wear that day. Their greatest celebrations are held every month beneath the full moons. These celebrations involve dancing, poetry and beautiful music. Romantically involved participants are said to experience the full bloom of their affections on such nights, allowing them to evaluate the strengths of their feelings. It is not uncommon for artists to unveil their latest work at such holy days as well.

     Prayers to Ilsare are usually for situations involving love or art, and are often almost works of art themselves, as some can be quite long and poetic hymns. Clerics of Ilsare pray so that love may bloom. They pray when they watch an artist work so that Ilsare may bless their creation. For example, a cleric praying before creating a beautiful piece of clothing that can possibly help someone fall in love with the person who wears it: "Oh Ilsare, Heart of Gold, bless this dress I am about to craft with great beauty, and bless the one who is to wear it with your gift of love."

Lucinda

Aliases: Mother of All Magic, Lady of Spells 
Race: Human 
Worshippers: 
     Mostly humans, half-elves, and elves; fewer worshippers among other races. 
Domains: Good, Healing, Knowledge, Magic, Trickery 
Governs: Magic, sorcery, spellcraft, health 

Dogma: 
     Magic is the Gift of the Lady of Spells, and those who wield it are greatly privileged. Magic will make the world prosper if used wisely. Use magic to shape the world when you know it will eventually serve the greater good. Do not keep your knowledge to yourself; teach magic to all those with the will to learn and follow Lucinda's teachings, and tell all about the Weave.      Encourage creativity in magic in all ways and at all times. Always help others out of the goodness of your heart. Do everything you can for the Weave, for otherwise, magic may fade away. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Lucinda favors strongly enchanted weapons over normal ones. Clerics of Lucinda often carry staves and wands containing useful magic, and heavier quarterstaves for melee combat.      Lucinda's clerics often wear useful enchanted robes like arcane spellcasters. The colors on these robes are usually light and vivid, most often white and blue. 


Clergy and Temples: 
     The hierarchy of the Lucindite church is varied, separating into eight Orders that each concentrate on one school of magic: abjuration, conjuration, divination, enchantment, evocation, illusion, necromancy, or transmutation. Each Order consists of numerous groups that include both arcane and divine spellcasters. These orders have their own places of study and their own hierarchy. Each group with more than thirty members is led by a master of the spell school who is usually the most powerful and experienced caster in the group. All of the orders are led by a grandmaster; for instance, the Order of Evocation is led by the Grandmaster of Evocation. All the Orders are good aligned and led by the Council of Magic, which consists of the eight Grandmasters of the Orders. 
     There are also some academies of magic and many smaller temples where spells of all schools of magic are taught to any willing students. This is the part of the clergy that is most visible to the public. These academies and temples have members of each Order of magic working in them, and they also provide healing, supplies, and shelter for traveling Lucindites. The church also sponsors a small society of paladins, often called the Chosen of Lucinda or the Protectors of the Weave. They defend Lucinda's temples, protect the Weave from any possible harm, and keep magical artifacts out of evil's reach. Lucinda's temples (and related buildings, such as the academies) can be of any size and any style, but they all have one thing in common: all temples to Lucinda are great works of the Art, enwrapped in countless spells, containing numerous magical items, and surrounded by an aura born of the very strong Weave about the place. 
Lucindites pray for spells any time they need to, as Lucinda recognizes the need to be able to cast at any time. Lucindites don't have too many calendar-related holy days but they celebrate many things on a more individual level. Discovering new spells and ways to use magic or creating great magical items are often times for great celebrations among Lucindites. Temples and academies have annual events at which local mages to gather and share whatever they have accomplished during the past year. These events are generally called Spellmeets, but many temples call them by different names. Lucindites and Xeenites have a special night of celebration once a year called "The Night of Flesh and Magic," which celebrates the birth of Lucinda's daughter Xeen. Usually more Xeenites than Lucindites join this event, as it mostly concentrates on worldly pleasures rather than the somewhat ascetic discipline of magic. 

     Prayers to Lucinda can be heard almost anywhere involving magic and spellcasting. For example: "Oh great Lady of Spells, empower my Art, that it may better World and Weave."

Dorand

Aliases: Master of Crafts, The Priceless Gem  
Race: Dwarf 
Worshippers: 
     Nearly all worshippers of Dorand are either dwarvish or human. Given that there are members of all races that craft, there are pockets of worshippers of nearly any race. He accepts all those that desire to Make.
Domains: Earth, Fire, Protection, and Strength
     Dorand's clerics can choose any two of the above domains; it is well known, however, that nearly all clerics of Dorand embrace the Strength domain, which represents the strength and endurance needed for long hours at the forge. While this is not universal, it comes naturally with the process of becoming a Hammer of Dorand. Mostly, those who practice the crafts not involving mining and smithing are the clerics that do not practice the Strength domain.
Governs: Mining, Smithing, Craftsmanship, Stonework 

Dogma:
     Follow the Way of the Hammer. Create the new for the greater glory of Dorand. If you do not craft, you are not serving His purpose. Serve as tool and instrument of Dorand and strive to perfect your craft. Never fall into inaction. Support those that seek new knowledge or create new inventions.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Nearly all clerics of Dorand wield some version of a hammer or axe, since these are the tools used in both their craft and their worship and thus are the most important things that a Hammer of Dorand possess. They tend towards browns and greys, the colors of earth and stone.

Clergy and Temples:
     Nearly all clerics of Dorand are known as Hammers, the reason being that his clerics consider themselves his tools, and the greatest instrument of creation for Dorand is the Hammer. Within the church hierarchy there are different ranks, from Acolyte of the Hammer (lowest) to the High Hammer, the most exalted cleric of Dorand on Layonara.

     Creation is Dorand's primary concern. It is true, however, that many people confuse clerics of Dorand with clerics of Deliar since many of his priests fund themselves though the selling of their creations. Dorand's clerics, as they rise through the ranks and study the Way of the Hammer ever more, sell their wares less often, crafting instead to perfect their art. Often these items are given to Dorand as offerings.

     Most temples of Dorand are natural things, usually dug into a mountain or hill, though there are exceptions where a master builder wanted to plan, design, and build a temple of unusual size, beauty, or dÃ©cor.

     Clerics of Dorand pray for spells when they can. They can often be found catching a quick nap in the forge while waiting for the coal to heat up, for it is during the art of creation that they are most directly worshipping Dorand. Many use time at the forge (or other craft) as a time of quiet meditation, relaxing their mind and communicating with Dorand on a spiritual level, while allowing him to guide their bodies to create.

Goran

Aliases: The Deep Brother, The Master of Metal 
Race: Gnome  
Alignment: CG 
Worshippers: Mostly gnomes and humans. 
Domains: Earth, Fire, Good, Knowledge 
Governs: Invention, inspiration, scholarship, engineering, mining 

Dogma: 
     Discuss and spread ideas of new innovations. Strive to refine known techniques, invent new processes, and tell others about them. Once you begin to work on a new invention, do not stop until it is finished and working. If you think something can be improved, try improving it till you succeed. 
Question the impossible with new devices. Sacrifices must be made for the glory of science. Try to keep and share records of your strivings, ideas, and sample devices so that others may follow your work and improve on what you leave behind. Encourage others to think of new tools, improved ways of crafting, new ways of using their existing gear, and new ways of doing things. Acquire and store the inventions of others and share their secrets with others. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Clerics of Goran prefer the light hammer as a weapon as it is also a useful tool for creating and fixing things. Technical weapons are prefered over enchanted ones, but those can be useful as well. They prefer practical, durable clothing and armor that can be worn while working. Robes with numerous pockets for tools and scrolls are popular among Goran's clerics. They prefer metal armor in combat, and they do not show any preference towards color in their choices of clothing and armor. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The clergy of Goran is very loosely organized. Various temples exist and share knowledge with each other. Clerics who have created something great are considered the closest to Goran; thus, a cleric's reputation and status is based entirely upon the prolificacy and importance of their working inventions. The same criteria are used when weighing "academies," as the clergy like to call Goran's temples: the more and better inventions, the greater the temple. 

     Academies of Goran tend to be very much like workshops full of tinkered devices and plans for more. Clerics can constantly be seen planning or experimenting. Many experiments are dangerous, and for this reason, the temples are often in isolated places and do not get many visitors other than the faithful of Goran. 
     Clerics of Goran pray for spells in the morning, before they plan their day. Goran doesn't have many set holy days, but each working invention is cause for celebration. 
     Worshippers of Goran tend to take their time on inventions, and thus, celebrations of completion are rare. Goranites celebrate the day they started working on their life-quest annually by gathering many people in one place and telling them about the progress they made during the year. 

     The most important day for a Goranite is the 13th of Oclar, which is called "The Day of Amazing Innovations" by Goran's followers. It is the day Goran supposedly invented inventing and ascended to godhood. Goranites celebrate the greatest invention by gathering together, sharing their plans and displaying their inventions. One very significant day is the 24th of Apreal, when the winter is considered to be over. This day is called the Great Fixing among Goranites and they travel the surrounding lands, fixing any broken tools and items for the local townsfolk. 

     Prayers to Goran can often be heard in situations where new inventions are tested. For example: "Great Goran, allow this device I created in your honor to work, and if it for some reason doesn't, grant me the wisdom and intellect to bring my plans to fruition."

4) Unsuccessful, attempts at alchemy will destroy recipe ingredients, but glass vial and flasks will remian.

-----------------------------------

1) Brewing beer, wine and liquor begins with the gathering of wheat grains. Corn, barley, wheat, rice, rye and oat grains. 

2) Grains must be roasted to bring out their flavor using the Brewer's Oven. 

3) The Farmerâ€™s Mill is then used to crack the roasted grains to produce malted gain.

4) Malted grain can then be combined with other natural resources and cooked to make wort using the Brewerâ€™s Kettle.

5) Finally, the wort and sugar are combined with water and bottles in the Brewerâ€™s Keg.

Basics of Enchanting
---------------------------------

1) Enchanters can make a variety of items as well as enchant weapons, armor and shields. Enchanters require items made by Tinkering, Gem Crafting, Weapon Crafting, Armor crafting, Baking, Alchemy and Smelting. 

2) Enchanters use the following crafting devices: 

Enchanting Alter: Used to create elemental bags, enchanted gems and enchanted ingots. 

Enchanting Statue: Used to enchant shields. 

Enchanting Pool: Used to enchant weapons.

Cloth: 2 cotton

Padding: 1 cloth and 2 cotton

Patterns: 1 Book of Patterns and 1 cloth

Hides: 1 animal skin, 1 curing salt,  and 1 tanning acid 

Leathers: 1 cured animal hide and 1 tanning oil

Light Bow String: 2 spider silk and 2 almond oil

Sling: 1 bat leather and 1 pattern

Belt: 1 badger leather and 1 belt pattern

Gloves: 2 rat leather and 1 glove pattern

Boots: 2 deer leather and 1 boot pattern

Cloak: 2 cloth and 1 cloak pattern
The Initiate's Guide to Tailored Base Items

The Basics of Gem Crafting
-------------------------------------------

1)  The process of working with gems is a very detailed one that involves multiple steps and multiple crafting devices. These are as follows: 

Gem Deposits:  First you must gather gem minerals from the gem deposits. 

Gem Cutting Stone: Used to cut gems. 

Gem Crafters Table: Used to detail cut gems. 

Mineral Wash: Used to identify the mystery minerals that are found while mining. 

Jewelers Bench: Used to create rings, scarabs, necklaces and amulets. 

2) To begin, the player must locate a gem deposit and successfully dig an uncut gem mineral. The player must have a Gem Chisel equipped in order to mine gem minerals.

3) Once a gem mineral is extracted, it needs to be cut. This is done at the Gem Cutting Stone. The player will need to have a Set of Gem Crafterâ€™s Tools in their inventory. This process will yield either cut gems or flawed gems and gem dust as a bi-product. 

4) To detail a cut gem, the player will again need to have a Set of Gem Crafterâ€™s Tools in their inventory. This process is done at the Gem Crafters Table and will yield either fine gems or flawed gems. 

5) To create rings, necklaces, scarabs and amulets, the player must use the Jewelers Bench. These items require a mold, enchanted gems and enchanted ingots. 

6) Occasionally, players will find mystery minerals while mining. These minerals can be identified by washing them in the Mineral Bath.

The Basics of Scribing
----------------------------------

1) Scribing begins with the collection of sawdust produced by the carpenterâ€™s bench. 

2) Saw dust must be used to make raw parchment at the farmerâ€™s press.

3) The raw parchment is then baked into scrolls by the bakerâ€™s oven.

4) Inks are made at the scribing ink desk using misc plant resources. 

5) Finally, the scrolls and Inks can be combined along with a spell to produce a scroll.

The Basics of Tailoring
------------------------------------

1) Tailoring involves both the creation of leather and cloth, and the creation of leather and cloth based items, respectively. These items include various armor types, boots, belts, gloves and cloaks. 

2) To create cloth the player must harvest cotton. To create leather, the player must obtain animal skins. These can be acquired by hunting the desired animal and skinning it. To skin an animal, the player must equip a Skinning Knife on the animal corpse. 
3) Animal skins come in small, medium and large sizes. To create leather, the skins must first be cured. This process is done at the Curing Tub and uses various ingredients. 

4) Leather is created at the Tailors Table and requires a cured hide and tanning oil. Tailors must also possess a Sewing Kit in their inventory in order to use the Tailors Table. 

5) To craft leather armor and other pieces of clothing, the player must combine leather or cloth, a pattern and any other required ingredients.

6) To create a pattern, the player must include a Book of Patterns and a piece of cloth. These are also made using the Tailors Table.

The Basics of Tinkering
--------------------------------------

1) Tinkering requiresa set of tinkers tools in. Tinkers can make a variety of different items ranging from glass ingots to crafting tools to deadly traps. These items are created at the following crafting devices: 

Tinkers Device: This strange looking device is used to create arrowheads and misc tinkering items. 

Tinkers Toolkit: This device is used to create traps and crafting tools. 

Tinkers Furnace: This device is very similar to the forge, except that it makes molds, glass ingots, and various glass products. 

2) Tinkering uses two raw materials that can be mined. These are sand and clay. To mine these, the player must have a Shovel in their inventory. 

3) Sand deposits yield bags of sand and clay deposits yield lumps of clay. 
4) Shovels, like the minerâ€™s pickaxes, will wear out from time to time when used.

The Basics of Wood Crafting
---------------------------------------------

1) Wood crafting combines carpentry, bow crafting and fletching. 

2) Wood Crafting also involves harvesting wood. This is done by equipping a Woodcutterâ€™s Axe and using it to bash a Hickory Tree, a Mahogany Tree or an Oak Tree. 

3) Trees produce branches that can be turned into wood shafts, wood planks and wood staves.

4) To create wood crafting items, the Carpenters Bench must be used while possessing a Set of Carpenterâ€™s Tools.

Description: A set of darkly coloured clothes. Reinforced by leather pads and metallic plates in several places this set could be taken for an armour instead of simple clothing. A sinister aura permeates its appearance and when worn one often feels chilled even when sitting at a warm fireplace. Others, especially priests or people of faith, often display intense or even angry reactions towards whomever wears the armour in public.


The history of the armour of the Final Rest is as blurred as it is bloody. Having been in the possession of numerous assassins, assassin mages and other sinister personae in the past the Final Rest has seen much use and changed hands many times. 
The most notable owner of the armour through history was the assassin and Shadow Thief Dubron Tevorel. Rumoured to have been one of the founders of the famous Shadow Thieves, Dubron was a man both feared and revered. It was Dubron who lead three Claws of assassins to a meeting of the leaders of every thieves guild in the city, thereby dealing the death blow to organizations such as the Scarlet Glove and the Veiled Dagger. The bloodbath in 1321, which eliminated all other competition to the Shadow Thieves in Port Hampshire, is remembered to this day.
The only lesson that may be drawn from the records of the Final Rest is that it seems to be in the nature of the armour to cause the downfall of its bearer. 

Nothing is known about the origin or the creator of the Final Rest. The massive investment of negative energy and necromantic spells in the armour, however, speaks its own language. 
The powers of the armour are undeniable, as well as the toll paid by whoever wears the Final Rest. At times the strain upon one's vitality can be physically felt, almost like a hand around one's neck. One does well in taking off the armour before going to sleep, since the Final Rest is a deliverer of nightmares that prey upon the sanity of the bearer.

The journey to the caverns is one I've heard many a tale of.  But the true impetus of my travels came from the best known of them, which I include here for all adventurers to see:


"Here lies the tale of Harolgar, Frostblade of the White Fox Clan....

The first levels were all sculpted by dwarven hands, regular and smooth walls, gentle slopes and stones alive with arcane light at regular intervals. Our dwarven companion told us that these caverns were very old and even he was surprised that not even time managed to take away its beauty. Residents of these upper caverns were all sorts of small beasts and clans of humanoid creatures, nothing that our group of well worn campaigners couldn't handle.

As we descended we came upon the last dwarven tunnel, a hallway that led to a large natural cavern. The hall was roughly as though the cutters broke through into the cavern and left their duties of perfecting the path for another time, one that never came. Thus began a descent deeper and deeper, tunnels not dug by hands but burrowed or even eaten from the solid core of the mountain high above us lead from cavern to cavern. No more level rooms were to be found as we went down, further and further into Layonara. The simple clans and beasts from above grew scarce as deeper and fouler beasts, some that have never seen the sun, turned common and our group now trekked slowly and carefully.

Agheas, our cleric, felt himself sick after coming to a lit cavern with walls covered in a stinking gray mold. He said he felt death in the air, he felt life seeping away, stolen by the mold that surrounded us, he felt as though we were crossing a gateway from life into unlife, a feeling that none of us shared with him but we all felt as we pressed on deeper.

Beyond the gray mold room, the caverns and hallways were empty of life and even our dwarf sensed that the stone, always so true to him, started to lie. An uneasy silence muffled the noise of our armor, not even our bard's song could keep it away. Cavern upon cavern of silence passed as we lost track of time and became increasingly worried of what lay beyond the next curve of the now grotesque tunnels, irregular as the slime of a slug's path.

As our will to press on wore to thin, we reached a cavern deep within the world. Its floor was flat, solid and glossy black to our arcane light and torches, the surface of a great underground lake separated us from the other exits on the other side of the odorless black water. Our expedition halted and breathed in relief for we were now forced to turn back for none of us had a way of crossing this mere. We sat on the shore sharing a quiet meal, for we were now headed back, when a subtle movement in the deep caused a single ripple spread over the water - the silent roar stole the rest of our courage and our party of weathered adventurers that have braved dragons and armies of undead ran for our lives as frightened children.

We regrouped in a cavern far above the lake and started our trek upwards, unsure of what we had seen but sure that it wasn't a good omen of what lay beyond.

Perhaps the menace is a thing lurking in the black depths or perhaps it was nothing but our heads. "

My travels did not take me as far as these proport to have seen, and no knowledge do I have of this 'lurking' menace.  Only dwarven halls have I seen, and at their end, a strange carving of letters in stone which I dared not riddle out following the burns from misjudged notions, and the slithering cobras that rose from the pits at my guesses.  I've done much research since, and have found no true keys.  The tales of the caverns tell only of azure pools, the azure eye, azure riches, and the azure soul... I can not speculate as to what truly lies beyond the dwarven gates nor what this speech of things blue truly means.  There is not even a riddle to derive a thought from, it is only the gates, and the letters.  I'd tried to use the plates to speak 'open'... but as I said... it yielded only near death.  Someday I will find the missing peices of this puzzle.

The dwarven clan home itself is a mystery to me.  Through the annals of the Runic Anvil have I searched, and the only tale I find is of a clan of dwarves which settled in the Great Spikes to create their city called K'halziras.  Their thane had apparently sought the riches of the cold mountains and led his clan there some centuries ago.  I can tell you from the little I've seen that while riches they might have found, and a glorious clanhome their efforts yielded... they found also their deaths.  Or perhaps they abandoned it... though the dwarven bones seem to defy that notion.  Or... just maybe I would venture, they did not all die, and now live beyond that passage.  Ah... one day I will find my answer.
