Divine Fury
Divine Fury does damage equal to your current hit points and then leaves you with half of your current hit points.

Against foes with HD greater than twice the level of paladin and champion levels, Divine Fury does half as much damage as you have Hit Points, but again leaves you with half of your current hit points. 

Divine Fury may be used once per day.

Rilara
    Rilara is the southernmost continent of Layonara. It has always been a battleground for conflicts over territory, political power and wealth. It is even more so now that Milara has carved his wicked throne into the Iriand Mountains. Milara's machinations have added the strongest of all ingredients into the chaotic stew that is Rilara. As such, Rilarans are pragmatically suspicious and necessarily scheming. Those who are not have simply been subsumed into Milara's plans, whether they know it or not. Any city you visit in Rilara now will have a kind of subterranean tension, which seems ready to lash out into the everyday without notice. Many communities have stockpiled supplies, weapons, and hired henchmen to protect their precious homes only to find themselves in the service of the wicked master of Rilara the next day. The continent, it is safe to say, is not far from being entirely in the sway of Milara.

Well-known cities:

Casterly Castle
Location:  
    Casterly Castle can be found on the southwesternmost corner of the continent of Rilara
Population:  1600
Government:  Military Dictatorship
Defenses:  
    The castle is heavily defended with reinforced walls and battlements. It also houses a temple of Aragen inside its walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    In the many years of conflict on the continent of Rilara, the Casterly clan has managed to establish dominance in the southwestern region. They did this not by force of arms, but as many savvy rulers throughout history have, through the morally binding obligations of gift giving. For hundreds of years the wealthy Casterly family showered the towns of the southwestern region with gifts, gifts that couldn't possibly be repaid. The towns, therefore, repaid the castle with their allegiance. 
     Now, most of the surplus agricultural and trade goods of the region are shipped to the castle for redistribution. Some of it is traded with the elite of Point Harbor. Most, however, is packed south to the Casterly's port annex of White Harbor. The White Harbor cargo ships' manifests state that the primary destination is the Kingdom of Rodlem, a fact which has not slipped the attention of their rival city Karthy. Still, as the shipping routes on the south side of the continent rarely receive surveillance, and it is therefore hard to know for sure where these goods are shipped.
    There are many rumors about the involvement of the Casterly clan in Rilaran affairs. Rumors abound that an army is being amassed behind the walls, and that weapons and supplies are being stockpiled. Some think the Casterlys are preparing to fight Milara's forces, which they believe are gathering in Fort Himlad, a key central outpost. Others believe the Casterlys have received a gift from Milara, one which they can only repay with their allegiance. Whatever the murky truth is, Casterly is a key player in the unfolding struggle over Rilara. 

Ereb 
Location:
    North of Fort Aglon and east of the Belgaer Hills on the continent of Rilara. 
Population:
    4,500 (40% human, 30% halfling, 15% dwarf, 10% elf, 3% gnome, 2% half-orc) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses: 
    A small wooden palisade surrounds this town. 
Miscellaneous Information:  
    Ereb is one of the towns that has benefited from the trade generated by Point Harbor, as it finds itself at one of the most important traderoutes of Rilara.The town's small wooden palisade does not provide much fortification, but the relative closeness of Fort Aglon gives adequate protection to this small town at the edge of the Belgaer Hills.

Bitterbridge
Location:  
    Just to the west of the Ledros Mountains lies Bitterbridge
Population:  40
Government:  Anarchy
Defenses:  None
Miscellaneous Information:
    Bitterbridge is the sister city to Bloody Gate, though far less stable. It lies on the northern portion of the Delwin River, at the point where the waterway falls from great heights from Lake Ire in the Ledros Mountains. The sight is one that many throughout Rilara once traveled to see. But it is more than a tourist attraction; the river is also the reason Bitterbrige exists. Originally many humble souls found the falls too gorgeous to part with and settled at their base. They built a bridge, where Bitterbridge now stands, for ease of passing through the rapid waters. It didn't take long for them to realize that the bridge would have to be defended from giants wandering between Wolfswood and the Mountains. The giants, not needing a structure to cross the raging Delwin, would simply smash the bridge for fun. 
    After a small fort had been established there and anti-giant measures taken, many travelers began to stay at Sweetbridge, as it was once called, to venture out at dawn for the rainbow mists of the Delwin Falls. Similar to the history of Bloody Gate, however, when Milara set his palace upon the Iriand Mountains, everything changed. Even the idea of Milara being so close sent the town into chaos. They knew Milara would march out for Karthy and would use the bridge, the product of their honest toil, to accomplish his task. Some thought to destroy it, some to defend it; others simply evacuated. Now the few who remain in the renamed Bitterbridge are said to have gone mad from the sheer stress of the situation. 

Bloody Gate 
Location: 
    South of Region Forest and on the northwestern tip of the Iriand Mountains on the continent of Rilara.
Population:
    1,600 (80% Mountain Dwarf, 10% Hill Dwarf, 5% human, 3% half-orc, 1% gnome, 1% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses: 
    Bloody Gate is a heavily fortified town whose militia is primarily made up of Dwarves. 
Miscellaneous Information:  
    There is one main route through the Iriand Mountins. This means that there is one main route between Milara's throne and the rest of Rilara. Bloody Gate is situated on that pass, between two dramatic craggy peaks. It has been the site of countless epic struggles, epic victories and epic defeats. All of these have contributed to Bloody Gate's well-deserved name.
    There is a question which haunts the thoughts of nearly every Rilaran and any Mistoner who has any sense of world events. That question revolves around the allegiance of Bloody Gate. Since Milara's army must pass through this town, how could the fierce dwarves not be under his sway?      Others retort that they are dwarves and would die before becoming servants to such a wicked ruler. Those might say that it has been these dwarves who have kept Milara from controlling Karthy. The response may come quick that Karthy and Bloody Gate fell to Milara's whims long ago. The truth is that no one knows for sure, perhaps not even Milara and the residents of Bloody Gate themselves.
 
Faroth 
Location:
    Almost in the center of Wolfswood Forest on the continent of Rilara. 
Population: 
    1,800 (90% elf, 5% human, 3% dwarf, 1% halfling, 1% gnome) 
Government:  Monarchy
Defenses: 
    A wooden palisade surrounds this city. The militia is largely made up of master Elven bowmen. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
    Faroth is the main Elven city on Rilara. They do not trust outsiders and rarely accept them unless they have proven their worth. 

Karthy 
Location: 
    Northeastern tip of the continent of Rilara.
Population:
    13,500 (60% human, 18% dwarf, 10% half-orc, 5% gnome, 5% halfling, 3% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:  
    Heavily fortified city with a reinforced masonry wall surrounding it.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Karthy is a rough and tumble city with very strict laws. The laws may be strict, but are subject to sudden change, hardly followed and yet executed with a kind of twisted pleasure by the Karthy guards. It is said that Milara has controlled this city for many years, and that its economic and political interests are his own. Supplies come to him through this port and his spies and troops depart from here. Therefore, all activity in this port is carefully monitored and recorded. A pervasive sense of paranoia grips the whole city, and travelers in particular as they are bombarded with askew glances and eyes peering through half-opened shutters. 
    The Kingdom of Roldem on the island of Calishan is trying to defeat the city but it seems that Milara is always one step ahead of them. This conflict dates back to the Cataclysm. Before Layonara was torn asunder in the great energies of the Cataclysm, Calishan and Rilara were pressed together in one huge central landmass. As they were cleaved apart, so were the people who lived in considerable turmoil on those lands. For many years two great families had battled for dominance on Calara, what people in retrospect call the unified territories. When they split, however, the two families were not split evenly. Many of the Roldem family was left on Rilara. But since they were cleaved in two by the Cataclysm and the ocean span too great to call for aid, the Roldem family was hunted down and quickly eradicated from Rilara. On Calishan, however, they established their dominance and came to rule the island. They still remember their kinsmen and have always had a mind to recapture Karthy and avenge their family's misfortune. With Milara taking control of much of Rilara, and Karthy as his primary port, this desire has intensified considerably. To say Roldem and Milara are at war would surely be an understatement.
    A major temple to Xeen can be found in Karty.

King's Landing
Location:  
    King's Landing can be found on the southern coast of Rilara.
Population:  2700
Government:  
    Monarchy, though in recent years it is suggested that King's Landing has fallen into a chaotic state.
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended castle, with bastions and reinforced walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    King's Landing, as the name suggests, is where the King first landed on Rilara after sending some of his finest men to pacify as much of Rilara as they could. Giants, bugbears, wild men, and feral elves alike fell to this solution to the Rilara settlement problem. The lands of the northeast were still too wild, and the southeast is primarily mountains, so the King's advisors directed him to this spot for his ceremonial claiming of the continent. Even now in King's Landing there stands a statue of the ancient king erecting a victorious flag on the banks where the Delwin River meets the ocean.
    Milara must have a sense of historical irony, for it is said that this is also where he first set foot on the island of Rilara. Where he came from, no one knows. But his berth at this port gives the name King's Landing a clever double meaning. As the well-buttressed city on the mouth of the southeast's most important waterway, Milara's presence here also has practical purpose.
    Whether or not it is true that Milara landed and took control of King's Landing, all reports document that this city is falling further and further into a state of lawless frenzy. The streets, it is said, are littered with corpses and looted possessions. The city elite have abandoned the town and the guards do more work keeping the wild commoners within the city than keeping any invading army without. The nearby cities of Wyk and Lann have done all that they can to keep the waves of King's Landers at bay. From the state of these towns it is easy to see that they are not very successful. 

Lannisport
Location:
    Lannisport is small village on the northern shore of Rilara.
Population: 685
Government:  Tribal council
Defenses:  
    Lannisport has a stone wall surrounding the town, though not the forces to man it in case of attack.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Traditionally, Lannisport was a fishing village. The north and central waters off the coast of Rilara boast some of the best fishing in all of Layonara. Lannisport fish can be found throughout Rilara and have been served for fine banquets in prestigious places as far as Port Hampshire, Leilon and Pranzis. The locals have always attributed their fishing prosperity to Shindaleria. Many years ago, on a cliff overlooking the natural harbor, the people of Lannisport established an impressive temple to their patron deity in a gesture of gratitude for years of prosperity but mostly to influence the future to proceed in their favor.
In the days of Milara, however, Lannisport has taken on a more nefarious pastime. Though small, or perhaps because of their diminutive stature, the docks at Lannisport have served as an ideal launching point for Milara's agents to sneak into the southern reaches of Mistone. For the most part, ships from Lannisport have been thought innocuous fishermen come to sell and spend. As such, they are mostly unquestioningly welcomed into the ports at Fort Valensk and Port Hampshire, and sometimes as far north as Forewarn Fort. Milara, it is said, uses this traditional oversight to his advantage and is said to have established himself well in certain areas of Mistone through such unsuspected vessels. 
    The situation has become more visible to Mistone authorities. The Mistone Alliance knows that at least some of the Lannisport fishing and cargo vessels are not what they appear to be. Notices have begun appearing at docks throughout Mistone, but as the gregarious fishermen swing from the rails of their vessels and dart for the bars and brothels as they always have, the notices are commonly shrugged off.

Point Harbor 
Location: 
    Northwestern tip of the continent of Rilara, at the edge of Dinen Forest.
Population:
    36,000 (45% human, 20% halfling, 12% elf, 10% dwarf, 8% half-orc, 5% gnome) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses:
    Point Harbor is a heavily fortified masonry fortress. Parts of the walls extend out into the bay. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
     Point Harbor is the most prosperous harbor of Rilara, and most of the continent's trade passes through here. Since the Forsaken Islands are so deadly that even passing by them is rumored to turn a whole crew into ghasts, goods headed east from Mistone usually come through Point Harbor. Either they re-supply and travel the dangerous north coast of Rilara or they travel overland to Karthy. Neither trek is desirable and it is not uncommon for Point Harbor to be the settled upon destination of many supposedly Dregar-bound captains.
    To protect its wealth, it is heavily fortified, both from the land as well as from the sea, making it a difficult city to capture. Its main trading partner is the city of Port Hampshire on Mistone, but passage to many of the great ports of Layonara can be booked on ships docking in Point Harbor. Boats from Point Harbor are likely the only ones you'll see on the books at any port outside of Rilara, excepting Xantril. The reason for this is simple. Being on the northwest corner of the vast continent of Rilara, Point Harbor is as far from Milara's seat as possible. This doesn't mean Milara overlooks it or cannot reach it, rather that his grasp there is less firm. Because of this, Point Harbor is one of the few ports on the island of Rilara that conducts business not entirely in the interests of Milara. 

Stone
Location:
    Stone is located in the central north of Rilara, in the foothills of Mount Taras 
Population:  
    670 (90% deep gnome, 5% human, 5% dwarf)
Government:  Miner's oligarchy
Defenses:  None that can be seen.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Stone is a town of deep gnomes. That fact alone should draw your attention to the fact that Stone is just the tip of the Mount Taras iceberg. The town itself is the relay station for mining supplies headed deep under the mountains and the point of commercial contact between the deep gnomes and the outside world. This is why the gnomes have recruited a small number of humans to manage their surface affairs, trading a very small portion of the minerals they uncover for other necessary supplies. A Temple to the deep gnomes' patron goddess, Beryl, has been established in Stone.

Fort Himlad
Location:  
    Fort Himlad lies at the southern edge of Wolfswood Forest on the banks of the Falas River. 
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Himlad lies at a strategic crossroad, with a road north leading into the Wolfswood, another heading east towards King's Landing and the Iriand Mountains, and yet another which leads west towards the numerous villages and hamlets that populate southwestern Rilara. Despite its crucial function of guarding the intersection of these key thoroughfares, it's not a big fort; its walls are wooden palisades.
    Rilarans of the southwest often send agents of seemingly meaningless commerce to Fort Himlad. Most believe they are spies. It is no secret that most of the southwest lives with a kind of rational paranoia of what Milara will do next and see Himlad as the crucial staging point or thoroughfare for any plans he might have with their homeland. Because of this, people of Himlad suspect the people of the southwest of planning an offensive against them. Minor skirmishes on the road west have already taken place. It seems only a mater of time before things escalate. Milara, it is rumored, shows up from time to time on nearby bluffs and watches the situation deteriorate with beaming expressions of gratification.

Dregar Locales

Iriand Mountains
    A vast mountain range on the southeastern edge of Rilara. In these mountains, Milara has his throne, launching attacks upon the continent from Bloody Gate. These mountains are known for the great mountain giants that inhabit them.

Region Forest
    On the northern edge of the Inand Mountains.

Ledros Mountains
    Small mountain range, east of the Wolfswood, north of the Inand mountains. 

Wolfswood Forest
    Wolfswood Forest dominates most of central Rilara. It is a huge and dense forest, where one can - from one moment to the next - encounter a peaceful glen or get ambushed by fierce creatures. Rangers and druids watch over the well-being of the forest.

Tau'ren Hills
    South Rilara, east of Greywatch Tower, 

Belgaer Hills
    These lush green hills east of Dinen Forest comprise a large part of western Rilara. It tends to rain a lot in these hills, and not many settlements have been set up here.

Dinen Forest
    Although this forest is relatively small compared to the Wolfswood, it can still hardly be avoided if traveling east from Point Harbor.

Bear Island
    South of Point Harbor, off the Rilaran coast, lays Bear Island. This small island has been home to a clan of bugbears for as long as many can remember.

Swamp of Lost Souls
    This swamp in northeast Rilara was once home to a coven of necromancers. Twelve of the dark mages convened one fateful night to form a dark pact, but an adventuring party disrupted the ritual before the spell could be completed. Due to the result of the the adventurers' interference, the swamp has since been called the Swamp of Lost Souls.

Calishan
   One of three key islands to the southeast of Dregar, Calishan is part of the kingdom of Roldem

Well-known cities:

Tibum
Location:
     Southwestern part of the Island of Calishan 
Population: 
     18,500 (85% human, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 3% elf, 2% halfling) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses: 
     A heavily fortified masonry walls surrounds this city; parts of the wall are reinforced. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
     Tiburn is the launching point of the Kingdom of Roldem's forces. Over the ages, Tiburn has fought many battles with Karthy and the people of northeast Rilara. Before the Cataclysm, these two regions were once united geographically but torn asunder by political allegiance and civil warfare. When the two factions were unevenly split by the Cataclysmic forces that tore the lands asunder, the warfare intensified on Rilara and the Roldems who were trapped there died torturous deaths. On Calishan, the Roldems prospered, and even today burn with the need to avenge their kinsmen. With the rise of Milara on that vile continent, the people of Roldem's thoughts turn more and more to these bloody desires. War between the two great regions seems on the horizon, and Milara, interestingly enough, seems to have neglected his influence in the Kingdom of Roldem. In Roldem, Milara is simply known as the tyrant of Rilara, a convenient symbol upon which to heap their festering animosity towards the continent.
     A large temple to Aragen can be found here.

Loriel
Location:
     At the eastern edge of the Blackwood on the Island of Calishan lies the city of Loriel
Population: 1685
Government: Monarchy
Defenses:
     None that are immediately noticeable.
Miscellaneous Information:
     Loriel is one of the many towns that occupy the densely packed Island of Calishan. Loriel's most notable pastime is an open invitation rogue tournament that happens once a year and is announced throughout Layonara. Throngs of people gather to try their ability to spot the spies of Roldem as they watch and infiltrate the crowd. By now, Roldem intelligence is able to identify on sight most of the skilled, yet unwise, rogues of Mistone, Rilara, and Dregar. They use this information, it is said, for purposes of recruitment and for defense.

Calishan Locales:

Tiburn Plains
     The lush plains of Tiburn are home to many prairie-like creatures. It is also the most fertile farmland of Roldem. During times of war, the plains are also used as staging areas for massive combat drills, but the plains are sacred land for the regionals, who are very careful never to spill blood there.

The Black Woods
     Rumors exist that the forests are littered with many hidden temples and monasteries. Many seek them to learn the ways of the spirits, while others seek them out to obtain the hidden knowledge they may have.
     The Roldem Forests, otherwise known as "The Black Woods," are said to come to life at night, and anyone who wanders there at night is under the danger of being stepped on by an angry oak or a powerful birch tree. The nearby monasteries use these woods as training grounds, and the monks believe that one who has been able to survive the wrath of the dark spirit of the forest is able to attain a special balance within oneself.

Lake of Dreams
     The Lake of Dreams is home to the Monastery of Dreams, where the most sublimely skilled of Layonara's monks are rumored to walk upon the walls. A great statue of a golden dragon rises over the temple walls, a guardian of the lake as well as a symbol of the rigid discipline of the monastery. Very few gain the privilege of training at these hallowed grounds, but it is said that those that can decipher the cryptic passage on the temple doors will gain the favor of the grandmaster.

Grey Watch Tower
     The Grey Watch is that time in the morning just before the dew settles and the mists of the oceans spread; it is also a time when many naval battles occur as fleet commanders jockey for surprise in the fog. In this marvelous tower, thrice have the great sailors of Roldem stopped the enemy forces from invading their precious island. All these occured during the Grey Watches, earning the tower its name. 
     During peaceful times, ferries can be taken from the Tower to Alibor, although only the stalwart or foolish try to brave the island's dangers.
Sailors' Stories of Calishan, compiled by Finneaus Finefeather

Seas and Oceans
     The seas of Layonara are both beautiful and deadly. They can bring great riches to budding adventurers and crafty merchants alike, but if underestimated, the currents can bring swift ruin and death. The seas surround all of the major continents of Layonara, and travel by ship is often the most efficient - if not the only - way to reach a destination. The oceans of Layonara beckon to adventurers, however: many islands await the daring, as does sunken treasure and even underwater dungeons that drunken sailors speak of in hushed tones. But only woe will befall those who tread lightly in domains of Mist and Shindelaria.
     In many ports, one can book passage on ships to travel to other ports on a continent, or even to other continents.

Bay of Carocsa
     The Bay of Carocsa is a mid-sized bay with gorgeous beaches that stretch all the way around its U-shaped shoreline. The sun sets gently on an often angry ocean, giving the bay a sublime attraction in the contrast of the peaceful sun with the violent water. Still, you won't find many people on the beach, and far fewer in the sun-warmed, bathlike water. The bay is notorious for a deadly undertow which has claimed many lives. Locals say the undertow is no natural phenomenon, but Mist taking fools for sacrifice.
If the undertow doesn't get you, the ever-present sharks will. There are a wide variety of sharks in the Bay of Carocsa, regardless of the season. There is a strange explanation for this unique aquamarine phenomenon: Carocsa, a sea-elf druid, lived on the beach here for many years. She established a place of worship to Shindaleria on the beach, so that at high tide the water would slap gently against the huge stone boulders of the shrine. She also created an underwater observatory for the study of marine animals, particularly the sharks that prowled the bay (not nearly as often as they do today).
     Once day the Shark-Lord and his entourage came to the bay; some say to explore the link Carocsa opened between the surface and the depths. The crowd of sharks in the bay caused chaos and one of the sharks was flung into Carocsa's observation area, throwing her bleeding body into a swarm of frenzied sharks. They circled their prey as the Shark-Lord watched. Before his astonished gaze, Carocsa polymorphed into a shark and fought off the first line of would-be feeders. At that point the Shark-Lord swept in, stopped the swarm and demanded Carocsa follow him to his territorial waters.
     What happened after that is even wilder speculation. Some believe they fell in love and Carocsa abandoned her legs and lungs to remain at the Shark-Lord's fins. Others, who claim to witness humanoid figures emerge from the bay occasionally and mysteriously reenter, guess that Carocsa taught the Shark-Lord how to obtain a humanoid form, and they spend their time plotting control both above and below. Others are certain the Shark-Lord devoured the druid. Whatever happened, it is clear that in the aftermath sharks are drawn to this spot. The influence of Shindaleria is still strong at Carocsa's shrine to her.

Windjammers' Bay
     Locations such as the Windjammers' Bay await those seeking treasure, places where many ships, their hulls laden with gleaming gold and powerful magic, have sunk. These treasure hunters succeed only if Mist permits it, because she is said to have a special interest in causing chaos in this particular bay, to the great annoyance of the inhabitants of the nearby Port Hampshire.
 
Gulf of Coreanys
     The seas of Layonara are not without their mortal dangers, either. The Gulf of Coreanys might seem a welcoming place to weather a storm, but the placid appearance of the waters deceives, as pirates and their ilk crowd the Gulf. Unwary merchant ships travelling in or near the Gulf often fall victim to pirate raids. Wary of the Gulf's reputation, most merchants either sail a long way around, or make sure to hire an able crew - sometimes including adventurers - to defend themselves. Pirate activity in this area however, also makes it an attractive site for adventuring, since pirates often have plundered treasure.

Broken Corals
     The Broken Corals are among the most perilous and feared waterways on Layonara. For those seeking to take the quickest route around the southern part of Mistone, this strait would seem the fastest, but successfully navigating the Broken Corals is a fool's hope, for even the smallest of vessels will have great difficulty in passing the perilous reefs intact, and any larger vessel entering this area is almost certainly doomed to a watery grave. Only pirates make frequent use of the corals to deter pursuing larger ships, but even for them it is perilous. Many once-mighty vessels sleep silently on the seafloor, but only the truly foolhardy will attempt to recover their lost riches.

The Great Coral Bay
     Other large masses of corals exist, such as The Great Coral Bay on the west coast of the elven island of Voltrex. Only the graceful ships of the elves are said to able to navigate these corals with success, and as such the bay deters all but the most successful of merchants from enterprising on the island. Shindelaria pays special attention to these waters, to make sure that Mist does not try to spread her chaos towards the elves. Treasure awaits those who dare explore the bay, but malevolent creatures are said to lurk in the depths.

Coral of Faces
     On the southeastern side of the continent of Rilara, one will find the Coral of Faces, which appear to be an extension of the Iriand Mountains. Though they pose navigational hazards, it is said that one's true face can be found on those beautiful corals.
Sailors' Stories of the Seas and Oceas, compiled by Finneaus Finefeather

Talimar 
     Talimar is one of three key islands to the southeast of Dregar and part of the Kingdom of Roldem. Because of its central location, the island is known for its trading ports, usually used as halfway stops or meeting grounds for trading partners. As such, the Island of Talimar has grown extraordinarily wealthy over the ages. In fact, the island, lead by the elite of Rodez, threatens to break away from the rule of the King of Roldem. Much attention, therefore, is focused on this small island, and with good reason.

Well-known cities:

Silden
Location:
     The port town of Silden is located at the southern point of the Island of Talimar.
Population: 935
Government:  Communal Collective
Defenses:  None
Miscellaneous Information:
     Silden once competed with Rodez to be the central trading port of Layonara. They grew side by side, attracting cargo vessels in a kind of maritime merchant tug-of-war. Both cities were successful and grew rapidly. Silden, however, stopped short along this trajectory, whereas Rodez became more and more committed to its dockside entrepreneurship. In a reflective moment in history, the people of Silden realized, or so the town lore goes, that in dedicating themselves to business, they were increasingly subordinating their entire lives to the pursuit of wealth. At that time a magnificently charismatic figure emerged in Silden. Stories differ whether he was born in Silden or came on one of the merchant vessels. But the all agree that he spoke with enchanting eloquence, and he used that oratory skill to speak to the unsettled sentiment of the villagers, transforming the village literally overnight. Now Silden is one of the few villages in Layonara which works as a collective. All land and resources are collectively owned by the community. They no longer trade for profit, striving instead for a semi-autonomous subsistence based economy. Any trade Sildeners do is only to attain products not available in their region. Most of the time they refuse to trade in gold, demanding direct barter instead. 
     This political and economic arrangement in Silden is reflected in the town's architecture. The symbol of the town, one which has become somewhat famous throughout Layonara, is the community longhouse. It is located in the middle of the town, and every Silden family lives in it, except for those foraging expeditions.
A temple of Shindaleria can be found in Silden as well.  

Rodez
Location:
     On the Northern coast of Talimar lays the wealthy city of Rodez. 
Population: 7985
Government: Monarchy
Defenses: 
     High white walls surround the city
Miscellaneous Information:
     The sheer opulence of this city dazzles many visitors. Nearly every building looks sparkling new and not a single cobblestone seems out of place on the streets. All visitors enter Rodez through the glorious docks, and one would have to travel far into town to observe even a cracked surface...let alone a glimpse of the meager domiciles of Rodez's servant underclass.
     The reason for the extravagance is simple: Rodez is the central trading port for all of Layonara. Rodez has adorned itself in signs of success and beacons that light up the night clouds in an attempt to lure passing cargo vessels to their markets. For ages, these tactics have worked. Ships have often stopped their journey between Dregar and Rilara short, dumping their cargo at a competitive price to be resold to a vessel traveling the opposite direction for the same goods. Captains can't resist cutting their voyage in half, even if it means paying a little extra gold for their cargo.
     Every trade good throughout Layonara makes its way at least occasionally through Rodez, a fact of which Rodez' innumerable and hard working dock-hands are proud. Ships from Voltrex have been seen at this port in recent years as well. Since the docks at Saida are closed to outsiders, Rodez has become the trading outpost for fine elven wares, boosting their economic prospects ever further.
The King of Roldem looks at Rodez with suspicion however, as the city seems to be growing too influential for his comfort. Rumors support the suspicions of the King, as it is said that Rodez thinks of itself as the ruling seat of its own kingdom on Talimar Island. Unconfirmed reports suggest that Rodez has stopped paying its tributes to Roldem as well. The ruling elite of Rodez seem to be taking advantage of the contemporary turmoil and are exacerbating it at the same time. With position, politics, and money all playing huge factors in the port's existence, Rodez is a crucial variable in the current campaign for Layonara. 

Talimar Locales:

Swamp of Reawakening
     The Swamps of Reawakening have been the stuff of many legends and rumors in the area. Strange sights are reported by those that walk near the dangerous crypts that surround these swamps. Many have entered their gloomy depths never to return, and as the legends grow, so does the number of dead or missing adventurers. One would expect trolls to live in these swamps, but the absence of the beasts makes the Swamp of Reawakening more surreal and frightening than normal. 

Swamps of Storms
     The torrential weather in this area has allowed very few adventuring groups to know much of its makeup; little is known about these swamps except rumors of moaning caves and eternal whirlwinds.
     The Beach of Thunder, Lightning Strand, The Watery Peninsula, The Swamp of Storms. Many names are given to this area of Talimar. Every attempt to clean the peninsula and make it a flourishing port city have been met with massive failure. To this day, people are trying to find out why the weather is so torrential in this area. Some even say the storms might not come from the sky at all.

The Dead Forest
     The perils of the nearby swamps spill over into this barren forest. Dead spirits are seen wandering at night, and the brash or inattentive are routinely made permanent visitors.
     The reason this once lush forest is now barren is unknown to many, but some say that a great betrayal ocurred many centuries ago and withered the forest beyond recognition. Now, during the silent hours, the spirits of those who were betrayed can be heard moaning for redemption...or revenge.. 

Backbone Mountains
     The Backbone Mountains are riddled with internal cave systems that many wondrous and dangerous creatures call home. Rumor has it that rare gems can also be found here, as well as passages that go into the unexplored depths of the earth.
The Backbone Mountains cover the central section of Talimar Island. Some say they are simply a curious geographical feature; others think that the mountain range is the body of an ancient dragon that now holds the island together. Whatever it may be, the Backbone Mountains are rumored to hide dwarven strongholds and certainly hide several tribes of giants. Very few have taken the effort to explore these mountains fully, and those who have will not speak of their experiences among the peaks and passes.
Sailors' Stories of Talimar, compiled by Finneaus Finefeather

Shindaleria

 Aliases: Mother Ocean  
Race: Sea Elf 
Description: Shindaleria is the patron goddess of sea elves. Little is known about her other than that she is the oldest of the elven gods. She is bitter enemies with Mist, as both deities struggle to exert their influence on the seas. 
Worshippers: Sea elves, sailors 
Domains: Animal, Healing, Magic, Water, Good
Governs: Sea life, oceans, healing, wisdom 

Dogma: 
     The Mother Ocean has always been and always will be; seek the embrace of her safety whenever you need it. Respect the sea and its harmony and it will not harm you in any way. Swim both the great currents and the shallow seas. Promote knowledge and use of the sea by reasonable folk, and fight those that would taint or deplete its beauty and bounty. Think long and wisely before acting; the seas do not alter quickly, but when the waters move, great change is sure to follow. Seek out fellow swimmers who honor the ways of Mother Ocean, and ally with them against those who follow Mist and who feel not the serene waters but only the chaotic waves. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Clerics of Shindaleria, most of them sea elves living underwater, prefer weapons and armor they can wear underseas. The trident is a useful weapon for underwater combat and hunting. Clerics of Shindaleria often spend most of their time in the sea, so they need to be able to swim; thus, they prefer clothing over heavy armor that makes them sink and rusts. Followers of Shindaleria prefer blue as their color, be it the light blue of the shallow seas or the deep dark blue of the deep ocean. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The clergy of Shindaleria doesn't have much of a hierarchy. The sea is quite wide and her clerics travel a lot, not meeting each other very often. The oldest and wisest of her clerics are considered closest to Mother Ocean. 

     Shindaleria has no actual temples, but numerous underwater shrines exist. They are simple grottoes, walls full of holy text, deep under the surface and rarely visited. Shindaleria's shrines are used to record events in the seas and Mother Ocean's clerics travel there once in a while to record past events in the cave walls. The locations of the most ancient shrines containing the most ancient history of Layonara are guarded secrets, known only to a few of the oldest sea elves. 

     Clerics of Shindaleria pray for spells at the high tide closest to midday. Mother Ocean doesn't really have widely recognized holy days, but individual sea elf communities celebrate certain days in her name. The only widely recognized holy day of Shindaleria is The Returning. The first week of Junar, clerics of Shindaleria walk the land, gathering beautiful objects and pieces of art and then taking them to the sea as gifts to Mother Ocean. Everything started in her waters, and eventually, everything returns to them. 

     Prayers to Shindaleria, due to most of her clerics being sea elves and spending most of their time in the water, aren't often heard. Some sailors pray to Shindaleria before crossing the sea, for example: "Mother Ocean, grant us passage through your gentle waters, as we pose no threat to you or the life of the seas."

Halflings
    Lightfoot halflings are a small race of people, but they make up for their short stature through many other useful characteristics. They are a a clever, enterprising, adaptable and extremely resourceful people, and what they lack in strength, they make up in agility. Halflings are about the same height as gnomes, standing at around 3 feet tall, but they have an even lighter frame, weighing, on average, 30 pounds. Their adaptable nature means they can assimilate themselves into any civil community on Layonara with minimal problems. Due to this carefree adaptability, you will find halflings in settlements across the world. While dwarves and gnomes value their facial hair, halflings rarely grow beards. Halflings are longer-lived than humans, but compared to other races they have a below-average life expectancy of about 270 years. Their adaptability also makes them good, solid adventurers, and their curious nature often drives them to the adventuring life.
Lightfoot halflings tend to form matriarchal nomadic clans that gravitate to places where work can be found or new unexplored lands. The mother of the clan, also known as the Story Teller, normally leads the clan in a collective direction. She also represents the clan in case of conflict and is in charge of passing the knowledge they have gained to next generations. Halfling families tend to be composed of a husband and a wife, but many clans have no qualms with a female having several husbands. 

    The varieties of halflings found in Layonara are Ghostwise Halflings and Strongheart Halfings.  I will now write a few lines about each.

Ghostwise Halflings
    Ghostwise halflings were once very much akin to their lightfoot cousins. But as they explored the lands, this small tribe of halflings came to see the atrocities commited by the bigger races. They asked all the tribes to unite to bring a balance to the chaos, but they were harshly turned down. Refusing to mimic those that they disliked the most, The Wise Tribes, as they were known at that time, decided to retire from civilized areas and isolate themselves in the forests. As time passed they chose to forget many of the lightfoot ways, opting for quiet meditation instead of non-stop adventuring. They Wise Tribes stopped worshiping Deliar and Prunilla, although they never stopped respecting the couple. They became a self-sufficient race and as such they respected their ancestors more than anything. Coming to worship their ancestors, or the "ghosts" of their past, and became to be known as the Ghostwise.

Personality: 
    Ghostwise halflings are very timid and shy. They come to trust very few, and are especially wary of tallfolk. Their lives are based around the survival of their tribe and its traditions; every ghostwise halfling is as important as the other, but the history of the tribe must survive before anything else. As such, very few of them leave their treetop villages and only do so under extreme circumstances or when facing "The Ritual of Change."

Physical Description: 
    Ghostwise halflings look very much like their lightfoot cousins in stature. Not as nimble as their cousins, some Ghostwise tend be slightly stockier in build. When leaving their treetop villages, they tend to spend most of their time outside in the sun, giving them slightly tanned skins and a light brown hair. Since they rely so much on physical communication, every Ghostwise has their name tattooed in tribal symbols on a visible place on their body, and many opt to tattoo many other tribal symbols representing people and events in their lives.

Relations with other races: 
    Ghostwise tend to trust very few outside races. They respect their cousins for carrying the same blood as their ancestors but never associate with them for extended periods of time. The only tall race they have come to freely associate with is the Wild Elves, as both races have many similar principles and traditions. It is not rare to see either Ghostwise halflings or Wild Elves visiting each other's tribes to share stories. Any other race they normally hold at an arm's distance and keep it that way.

Alignment: 
    Ghostwise seek balance, both inside themselves and around their homes, above all else. As such, most of them tend toward neutrality. A true Ghostwise is neutral to all and will not get involved in the bickering of the tall people unless their heritage is threatened.

Religion: 
    The Ghostwise stopped worshiping Deliar and Prunilla when the race split apart. They started depending on themselves and thusly hold inner strength above all. Ghostwise enjoy meditation to reach a balance within themselves, believing that inner balance is the first step to balancing one's environment. They hold Katia in great regard for giving them refuge in the forests, but never actively worship her. They respect their ancestors above all and worship the ghosts of the past. Ghostwise have many rituals of passage at different stages of their lives. The most noticeable is the Ritual of Naming and the Ritual of Change. The first one occurs when a Ghostwise reaches adulthood and is finally given her name tattoo. Before this event a child is known by many nicknames, and the one that sticks is the one tattooed onto her body. 

    The Ritual of Change occurs when a Ghostwise is not able to reach an inner balance and must seek it elsewhere. These halflings are given leave from their tribes to seek that which they need to reach a healthy state. Most Ghostwise seen roaming around the world are normally in the Ritual of Change.

Language: 
    This race of halflings, known by many as "The Silent," have developed a complex language of body expressions and hand movements. This language is so intricate that they do not need to speak in order to communicate with one another. Even when a ghostwise does speak, 90% of the time they use an old version of a halfling dialect originated during the racial split. Nevertheless, they are respectful of others, and will do their best at speaking the common language in the presence of those who will not understand them.

Names: 
    Ghostwise kept similar short first names as those of their lightfoot cousins as a sign of respect and everlasting brotherhood. However, they opted for different last names that portrayed their more naturalistic personality. Common last names are Slowillow, Stoutoak, Fallenleaf, and Wiseflower.

Adventurers: 
    Ghostwise adventurers are very rare. Normally every adventuring Ghostwise is undergoing the Ritual of Change. There are, however, Ghostwise exiles that venture the lands to either seek redemption for harm brought to the tribe or spread the seeds of the Ghosts across the world.

Strongheart Halflings
    Halflings, among the other small races, are normally known as The Children of the Earth. Many consider this a simple reference to the origin of dwarves, gnomes, and halflings, but these races know the words go far beyond that. 

    Strongheart halflings are far distant lightfoot cousins who opted to settle near mountainous regions. Brought together as a race by dwarven traders, Strongheart halflings are stout and healthy halflings that appreciate the way of the warrior and family life.

Personality: 
    Strongheart halflings are known to be the warmest of races. They treat most with a smile and a good story, and perhaps some ale or cider. They tend to their families with great responsibility and vigilantly maintain their clan and its surrounding areas. Many confuse Strongheart Halflings with young dwarves, for their love of battle is remarkable and many legends of Strongheart Giant Slayers have been assimilated into dwarven folklore. They tend not to wander the lands as much as their lightfoot cousins, thus many settled Strongheart clans are known around Layonara. The Fiercerock Clan is thought of as the strongest and most important clan, having settled a long time ago in the township of Stone.

Physical Description:
    Strongheart Halflings are not only thicker than lightfoots, but they are also taller, and consequently are often mistaken for small dwarves. Many Stronghearts are able to grow beards, and those who do are held in high regards within a clan. The women tend to be more settled than normal and grow wide hips that bear many children. "The larger the family, the stronger the clan" is a true Strongheart saying.

Relations with other races: 
    Stronghearts have a very stable trading tradition, especially with their dwarven brothers, as they like to call each other. They normally trade a lot with their lightfoot cousins, trusting them to spread Strongheart goods across the world. They get along and trade with humans, although they do not appreciate the rapid spread of their cities as much as dwarves do. They barely have contact with elves, and when they do, they have little in common to share. And as far as giants are concerned, to a Strongheart, the only good giant is a dead giant.

Alignment: 
    Strongheart Halflings respect the laws settled by the authorities of the lands they are in, and they keep utmost respect in their dealings with dwarves. As such, most of them tend to be Lawful Good.

Religion: 
    Stronghearts are very religious halflings, never missing an opportunity to celebrate and praise the couple that brought them here. They pray to Deliar every time they trade and truly worship him as The Protector. They love Prunilla for the gift of hearth and strong families and pray to her before every meal and during many family events. Many Strongheart clans have shrines to Vorax and Dorand to pay respect to their dwarven brothers.

Language: 
    Strongheart clans learn the language of those they trade with. As such they know the common language and they all strive to learn the dwarven trading language. They appreciate the halfling language and use it in their homes and among themselves.

Names: 
    Strongheart names are a strange combination of dwarven and hafling names. Common male names are Borki, Kasius, and Andrus. Female names are Jayla, Drasa, and Galgata. Their last names are always their clan name.

Adventurers: 
    Strongheart adventurers are normally those warriors sent to explore distant lands to meet other halfling and dwarven societies. Many also tend to go on adventures to train in battle before returning ready to defend their clans. But in many cases a Strongheart's life is simple and based entirely upon his homeland.

The knowledge of the origin of shields of this make is either lost to time or a guarded secret. There are two recent theories, however both seem equally fanciful. The first places their creation at somewhere between 4500 and 5000 years prior to the cataclysm. In the wake of the Second Dragon Purge there were likely hundreds of Dragon corpses littering the battlefields. Enterprising (or foolhardy) humanoids may have scavenged the corpses for their hides. The second theory is that they were made within the last millennia from the hide of a slain dragon. Due to the sheer age of the shield assuming the first theory and the rarity of dragons in the recent age, both theories are questionable. Regardless of their true origin, many such items end up hidden or locked in storage vaults as to be seen wielding such an item by a dragon is to garner its wrath.
When used properly, a small shield can grant lightweight protection with very little encumbrance to the wielder.

Dregar
    The largest continent of Layonara, Dregar is also home to the capital of Pranzis, from which the emperors ruled. The King of Dregar is still rebuilding after losing over 200,000 troops (not just in Pranzis) defending his populace from Blood and the forces that came through the rifts. The continent is in turmoil because of the rebuilding process and the lack of protection from qualified soldiers. Some upstarts are attempting to claim their own territories and bandits have their rein on the countryside. On top of all of this, Blood still has a very sizeable army and attacks outlying areas quite frequently.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This is the city to visit when you are looking for that special item or are in need of military training. It directly supplies military forces to Fort Thunder, North Fort and South Fort. 

    As largest city in the world, many religions have built temples here. Most noteworthy is the majestic cathedral of Rofirein, but temples to Toran and Branderback can also be found here.

Hurm 
Location:
    Hurm is on the west coast of the continent of Dregar, on the Bay of Carocsa, not far from the Forsaken Islands. 
Population 
    3,000 (75% human, 5% Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% halfling, 5% half-elf, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    There is a wooden palisade around this coastal town. The town is often in a state of disrepair, so its defenses are unreliable at best. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Just thirty years ago Hurm was a prosperous city with a bright future. Since Blood's return, however, it has deteriorated rapidly. The town is no longer the shipping potentate it once was, largely due to the proximity of the Forsaken Islands. 

Lorindar 
Location:  
    Lorindar is at the southernmost tip of the continent of Dregar.
Population: 
    15,000 (45% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:
    A large, well fortified masonry wall surrounds this city. The ruler is proud of the protection the wall offers the city. Some parts of the wall are also protected by spells. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    The twin horsemen of Lorindar are either the first or last landmark most people see on the continent of Dregar. In the early days of the rule of Pranzis a company of horsemen were sent into the wilds of the southern plains to make the lands livable by common folk. A massive Drow invasion in the prior century had drawn all of the capital's attention and left the south, despite being so close, to fall into shadow. The towns of the southern plains were quickly overrun and the people either fled further south or went missing. Once the capital was settled, the horsemen left the gates to reclaim the towns and clear the roads. In the end, only two made it to the southern tip of the continent. There they found an impressive and resilient throng of Dregarians living in scattered coastal communities under the constant threat of assault.

  The two horsemen, a twin brother and sister of the Galeright family, rallied these scattered tribes under the flag of the capital and brought them to the ruined outpost at Lorindar. There they rebuilt the town by hand and with primitive equipment. Still, they rebuilt it with enough motivation and skill to withstand the swarms of bugbears and giants that crashed against their walls like waves against their stone docks. Of course the Galeright twins were in front of the walls, meeting each wave with astounding skill and passion.
Rather than return to the capital, the Galeright twins settled in Lorindar and brought the king and queen themselves to witness the mighty will of the southerners. It was a glorious day in the history of Dregar, one that lives in the proud tales of Lornidarians. Shortly thereafter, the capital redirected immense funds and manpower to Lornidar, sensing its strategic, economic, and political significance as well as the sentimental unifying force it had for southern Dregarians. 

    Now Lorindar is the busiest and most strategically situated port, always bustling with commerce and strange faces. The people of Lorindar are proud of their city and their close connection with Pranzis and work hard to maintain their dominance in the shipping business of Dregar. Most of the merchants and associated industries find honor in honest and fair business dealings, and the city has become known throughout the realm as such. Nevertheless, Lorindarians are often suspicious of outsiders, particularly those from competing ports, notably their rival city, Waysend.

Redstone 
Location:
    Redstone lies west of the Serpent Mountains and north of Pranzis on the continent of Dregar. 
Population:
    950 (85% Hill Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% human, 2% halfling, 2% half elf, 1% elf) 
Government:  Clan 
Defenses:
    Redstone has masonry walls that surround the town. These walls were built by dwarves, so they are very sturdy and can withstand a large scale attack. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Redstone has one of the largest populations of Hill Dwarves on the continent of Dregar. Many dwarves end up settling in Pranzis and plying their trades and skills there. The populace of Redstone is known as hardy folks that have had a hard life. 
 
Vale 
Location: 
    Vale is in the southern part of the continent of Dregar in the Forests of Mists. 
Population: 
    600 (50% elf, 20% human, 15% half-elf, 5% halfling, 5% gnome, 5% dwarf, 5% half-orc. 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses:   
    Nestled in the great trees, this town is protected by remoteness and lore of hallowed ground. Rangers and druids have dedicated their lives to protecting Vale, and do so with passion. A short stone wall surrounds the village core. The chest-high wall is perfect for rangers to shoot over and druids to cast behind with some protection.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Vale is more of a spiritual center and forest outpost than a town. Of those who call Vale home, most live remotely among the old trees, yet they retain a practical and spiritual attachment to this place amidst nature.
On the continent of Dregar, Vale is never far from the hearts of rangers and druids. Deep in the heart of the Forest of Mists, its serene power is unsurpassed. Dregar's nature folk make regular pilgrimages to the legendary tree shrine of Vale to fulfilll their vows or renew their spirit. It is known that every decade, each druid throughout Layonara is required by oath to make a pilgrimage to this central forest and central shrine of Katia within. It is rumored that most come more frequently, as the experience is reinvigorating as well as a key to the spiritual and pragmatic unity of Layonara's druids. Through this hub of the druidic network, information is shared, new members are indoctrinated, roles are shuffled and objectives established.

Dalanthar
Location:  
    Dalanthar can be found in northern Dregar, between the Thunder Peaks and the Darkland Mountains.
Population: 1900
Government:  
    Two families struggle with each other for rule of Dalanthar
Defenses: None

Miscellaneous Information:
    Ages ago, the city of Dalanthar was the site of an awesome conflict between dragons. In the clash, the town was reduced to fire and rubble. The few survivors reconstructed the town upon the ruins. Today it is a shadow of its former glory. This is partly caused by the ever-present darkness that emanates from the Great Rift found northwest of town in the Darkland Mountains. It is also only a shell of its former self because for a powerful few, the dragon conflict still rages, animating intra-village aggression. One prominent family still sides with one dragon, blaming all the town's woes on the other. A second prominent family points its finger at the first. This conflict is manifest in the geography of town, as a huge craggy ridge separates the town into two halves. Each half is primarily under the influence of one of these two families..

Highpass
Location: In the Storm Horn Mountains
Population: 95
Government: Waysend representative

Miscellaneous Information:
    Highpass is a tiny village that sprung around Highpass Fort, and is located on one of the few usable passes through the Storm Horn Mountains. The pass is of major importance to the city of Waysend to the southeast, as this is one of the main roads for transporting goods to and from the port city. It is also home to a temple of Goran.

North Fort:
Location: 
    Bordered by Deadman's Pass and the Drift Lands on Dregar.
Population:  700
Government:  Military rule

Miscellaneous Information:
    North Fort is little more than a high desert camp. The frequency of suspicious events in the desert has kept North Fort well attached to the capital, despite the distance. The numbers of inhabitants are never high, however, as skirmishes between the king's and Bloodstone's armies are all too common. As such, the fort is continually re-supplied and at a constant state of alert.

North Point:
Location:
  North Point is the northernmost town on Dregar, west of the Singing Forest
Population:  800
Government:  
    There are several tribes which struggle for control in North Point at any given time.
Defenses:  
    North Point has no defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    For years fishermen traveled to this spot to exploit the huge schools of fish brought to the coast by the strong ocean currents off the north edge of the continent. Makeshift encampments eventually became this well-developed fishing village. Those who won this land from the hands of the previous occupants were rugged indeed, and the city still retains this surly character. This, by the way, makes North Point attractive for pirates who raid the cargo ships trying to sail swiftly by in the current and offshore winds. This doesn't seem to bother the fishermen much as pirates rarely hunt for fish and they do bring a steady supply of gold and goods into the town. A temple to Aeridin can be found here.

Orc's Watch
Location:  
    North of Vale at the north rim of the Forests of Mists
Population:  150
Government:  Tribal
Defenses:  
    A wooden wall and gates protect the meager interior of this outpost.

Miscellaneous Information:
    As its name suggests, this series of buildings on a tall hill serves as a lookout for Bloodstone's activity in the Forest of Mists. Sources say that it was overrun in a sweeping march along the north rim of the Forest of Mists by Bloodstone's army and now remains almost entirely abandoned.

Saudiria
Location:  
    On the east coast of Dregar, at the edge of the Anuroch Desert and the Drift Lands lies the city of Saudiria.
Population: 8500
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
    There is a wooden and adobe wall surrounding this city for protection. Mostly it is protected by the desert and the ocean.

Miscellaneous Information:
    How you come to Saudiria will determine your perception of it. From the desert, Saudiria will greet you with the enticing natural rhythms of an oasis. From the ocean, Saudiria wil greet you with a windblown lullaby and an inviting bed of grass made just for your weary head. Saudiria is both. It is desert oasis and costal vale. That fact, combined with the way the sun sets where desert wisps swirl in coastal gusts, make Saudiria known throughout the known islands for its magical beauty.

    The surrounding desert will testify that Saudiria hasn't always been blessed thus. Something or someone carved this coastal glade and farmland out of the sand and dust of the desert. The terrain of Saudiria is considered one of the great works of Dregar. Many come to Saudiria to enjoy its sights. Others come to answer the riddle of this amazing transformation: was it wealth, labor, magic, or some other power that created this land?  Residents never tell. Wanderers mostly choose to reside. Only fables tell the truth. Some wonder if it is the temple of Az'atta that can be found here.

Thorns Keep
Location:  
    In the Thunder Peaks in the northern part of Dregar
Population:  200
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended keep, well protected by both the walls of the keep itself and the sheer rock walls of the Thunder Peaks.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Like the name suggests, Thorn's Keep is not at all inviting. It lies in a particularly barren and inhospitable region of the Thunder Peaks. There are, however, two key reasons for the massive keep to exist there. First, there is a small but crucial body of water there which drains in the spring and summer to irrigate the fields of the Great Central Plains of Dregar below. Second, it is situated on a mountain crest which allows surveillance of that same key region. Those that reside in Thorn's Keep are therefore vigilant yet gruff, meshing perfectly with its overall persona. Contact with the keep has been cut off by Blood for sometime, however. Some believe that the Keep has fallen into the hands of the enemy.

Castle Raxswell
Location:  
    North of Lorindar, Castle Raxswell stands.
Population: 800
Government: Military rule
Defenses: 
    The castle is heavily defended by high and wide stone walls with ramparts and reinforcements.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Traveling north from Lorindar you'll come to Castle Raxwell. Both the castle itself and the temple of Prunilla located therein are notable for their spartan aesthetic. The castle is situated as a point of defense for the major port city of Lorindar. Many battles against the armies of Bloodstone have been waged on this barren and blood-soaked soil. Pranzis continually sends troops to this castle, knowing well its importance in the struggle for control of Dregar.


Willows Weep
Location:
    North of the Darkland Mountains, west of the Singing Forest and south of North Point you'll find Willows Weep.
Population:  660
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  none

Miscellaneous Information:
    This rare Elven town on Dregar exudes a mystical sullenness which seems to dance hauntingly along with the drooping willow branches. It is a small town, but built with elegant extravagance. The stylized and prominent crypts in the area have suggested to travelers that this city is somehow rooted in those crypts or servants of the dead.

Xora's Tower
Location:
    Xora's Tower can be found in the northeasternmost part of Dregar
Population:  140
Government:  Military dictatorship
Defenses:  very little

Miscellaneous Information:
    On the northeasternmost point of the continent of Dregar, perched on a rounded bluff, lies the haunting tower of Xora. For ages this tower served as a watchpoint for invaders from the sea or demons from Xantril. Rumor now spreads that this tower has been captured by demons or Bloodstone and has been turned to other purposes. Within sight of the tower lies an ancient shrine where magical force beckons. Knowledge of its origin and its use are either carefully guarded or lost over generations.

Waysend 
Location: 
    On the east cost of the continent of Dregar is the city of Waysend.
Population 
    6,000 (55% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government: Republic 
Defenses:
    There is a masonry wall that is about 80% completed that surrounds the city. The ruler is spending lots of money to ensure the city is well protected from bandits and ships alike. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Waysend has recently come into its own, since Blood's arrival. With Hurm disintegrating and with Pranzis rebuilding its troops, Waysend has been left on its own and is building a good shipping business. Waysend is one of the cities that is trying to break away from Pranzis' rule.
A Sojourner's Guide to the Cities of Dregar

Members of the Keepers elite guard were given these spears for her protection. Sadly in the raid that toppled the temple and scattered the relics, few of these weapons survived.  The tips of these coral spear heads are laced with the acid of the treacherous Moewy's Sea Viper and very sharp.
This mighty weapon once belonged to the great orc Ransh, who was chieftain of the Black Hand. It was infused by the bonecaster Omekil, so that it would take on the traits of its wielder over time.
A crude looking spear that has seen much use. Several runes are etched into its shaft.

Given only to those most favored guards and devotees to Shindaleria, this spear is as much a symbol as a formidable weapon.  It seems to be made of water given shape, with flows and waves visible within its form. The design of the spear's tip allows it to move effortlessly through water. Its ends give off a strong chill, like the cold waters of the deep sea, though its wielder is somewhat isolated from such effects.
This most unusual spear seems to glow of an inner light.

Voltrex Locales

La'Mune Forest
    La'Mune forest, also called Moon Forest, is a forest in southern Voltrex, and like most forests on Voltrex, it is a place of rest and quiet.

Lake Sahale
    Lake Sahale is the largest lake on southern Voltrex and is fed by the small streams that come down from the Peaks of Voltrex as well as by the Emerald River.

Ulambree Forest
    A large forest in the center of the continent, Ulambree Forest is home to the largest tribe of Wood Elves on Layonara. Living in complete harmony with the forest, their villages are hard to find as they are high up in the trees. Nothing that goes on in Ulambree Forest remains undetected by these Elves.

Lilanthier Forest
    A large forest in the northwestern part of Voltrex which is home to many druids and rangers. It has almost overgrown the ruins of the old elven city of Ovdear

Relishian Forest 
    A small rainforest called the Relishian Forest lies at the northeastern tip of Voltrex. It is rumored that ages past, before the cataclysm and the Elven race wars, this is the jungle the Dark Elves lived in.

Emerald River
    The Emerald river winds its way through the foothills of the peaks towards Lake Sahale. Elven children are told stories about a unicorn that calls the banks of the Emerald River its home.

Peaks of Voltrex
    These mountains basically keep the island safe from attack on the western side. They are very rugged and form a natural barrier. They lead down to sharp corals in the ocean and those help to keep ships and boats away from land.

The Five Elven Towers 
    The Five Elven Towers have stood on Voltrex for ages and probably only the elves remember who commissioned their construction. Various rumors and folklore about these Towers abound outside of Voltrex, but one can distill the following information from these rumors.

    At the edge of the Evergreens, where the western winds that come in from the ocean and the eastern winds that are re-directed south-easterly by the Peaks of Voltrex meet, lies the Windy Outcrop. On top of the outcrop the Tower of Air rises into the sky. 
The winds are ever blowing around the Tower and change direction all the time. It is said that if the Winds ever stop, the precariously balanced tower will crash to the ground.  

    In the lush greenness of La'mune forest, the Tower of Nature placidly rises among the trees. All paths eventually lead here and one can always find lots of animals living peacefully together around the Tower's outskirts.

    The firm Tower of Earth stands rooted in the earth on top of a hill. Even miles away, one knows that the Tower is near due to the minor tremors that rock the area constantly.

    At the northern edge of the Peaks of Voltrex, in an area filled with crevices where the air is almost too hot to breathe and the occasional spurt of lava shoots into the sky, the Tower of Fire stands amidst a fiery blaze.
At Voltrex's northern edge, where the sea meets the land, is a cliff upon which the Tower of Water is built. It has been raining here since anyone can remember.

    Each Tower is home to a mage of a specific element, except the Tower of Nature, which houses a druid.

    Together, these five are the judging council for Elves when it comes to magic and power from the land and elements. The Council of Five are not the rulers of Voltrex, but their advice is always listened to.
Tales of Elven Landscapes:  The current state of knowledge about the continent of Voltrex

Voltrex
    Voltrex is the continent in the southeast part of Layonara. Little is known about Voltrex, for the continent is off limits to all but noble elves, a rule which is policed vigilantly. What is known about Voltrex is that many of the elves who once resided on the other continents migrated here as a final solution to the race wars. Due to its secretive nature, many genres of Voltex folklore have emerged throughout the other continents. One thing that is often repeated about Voltrex is that it is the home of the Five of Nature.

Well-known Cities:

Saida 
Location:  
     Saida is the capital city of Voltrex and lies at the southwestern tip of the continent. 
Population: 16,570 (100% elf) 
Government: Magocracy 
Defenses: 
    A large, heavily fortified castle looks over this city. The city is surrounded by reinforced masonry walls and is heavily warded by magic.
 
Miscellaneous Information:
    Who has visited this great elf capital and returned to tell tales?  There are few, if any. It is said that the mages who guard this city know you are coming before you do, and if you are found not worthy of admittance after their rigorous investigation, you are sent either across the ocean or to its bottom, in either case without ever having set foot in or laid eyes on the precious gem of Elven civilization. 

    It is also said that the extraordinarily exclusive group of individuals who are welcomed at the Saida docks are never seen or heard from again for other reasons. The city is rumored to be so sublime as to make men and Elves alike lose themselves within its shimmering structures and resplendent residents. It is likely the only major city in all of Layonara that preserves and perhaps even amplifies the natural splendor of the forest it is constructed in. They also say that much of the city can be found suspended in the canopy, built on the massive branches of the ancient trees of the southern Evergreen Forest. Even the weather in Saida, some tell, is always perfectly cool with a gentle breeze rustling the trees and stirring the pleasant forest scents. This is remarkable as Saida is the southernmost Layonaran city and thus should be subject to intense climatic forces.

    There is perhaps no place in all of Layonara of which more has been said. And there is perhaps no place in all of Layonara of which less is known.

Seldarine
Location: 
    Seldarine lies on the southern edge of the Ulambree forest and to the east of the Voltrex Mountains.
Population: 10,800 (100% elf)
Government:  Unknown
Defenses:  Unknown

Miscellaneous Information:
    There are rumors that a second great Elven city exists to the south of the magnificent Ulambree Forest. Of those who leave Voltrex and talk about it, many speak of this place. That is because Seldarine is ideally located to serve as a hub for travel and commerce on Voltrex, and so it does. Those who venture from Voltrex are likely to be trading or traveling minded, and thus are often attached to this place. Few live here, but many call it home. As such it is a city pulsing with life, desires and magnificent things found nowhere else in Layonara. 

Amluarial
Population: 650
Government:  Magogracy
Defenses:  
    Strange tales abound of Amluarial being protected by walls of wind and great magicians who can direct its flow with simple words and gestures.

Miscellaneous Information:
    The elven scholar Ramsiad studied the lore of this place extensively. Although he was never permitted passage to Amluarial, he did compile some interesting data on the place. According to Ramsiad, this medium-sized hamlet is situated in the coastal hills on the northeastern part of Voltrex. It lies above the Great Voltrex Range of mountains, and therefore has some intense weather patterns. The winds from the east whip up against the mountains and swirl right about Amluarial before being sucked up in the western coastal gusts. There is never a day without intense and shifting winds. Great hurricanes and tornados also plague this area. Why would any elf choose to live here then?  Quite simply, the elves of Amluarial have invented devices to harness the energy of the wind and transfer it into practical and magical applications. What sort of products these machines generate was never discerned. But Ramsiad did discover that many elves across Voltrex have heard of them and heard of them being used throughout Voltrex.

Darthoriadin
Location:  
    This Ulambree Wood Elf Village lies hidden in the Ulambree forest.
Population: 265
Government:  
    There are said to be numerous tribes in this village which vie for power, and in doing so balance and share control of this Wood Elf village.
Defenses:
    The defenses of Darthoriadin, according to some loremasters, are primarily based on elevation. The entire village is in the trees. Ladders can be easily raised and Wood Elf archers find easy targets below.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Those who claim knowledge of Voltrex say that the Ulambree Wood Elf Village is the rural counterpart to Saida. Rather than resplendent stone structures erupting gracefully from the forest canopy, Darthoriadin is barely visible even when you are standing on one of its platforms. The entire city is nestled in the branches of the old Ulambree trees. Their union establishes a sort of harmony between the essence of the forest and the Wood Elves. People talk of the Darthoriadinian Elves moving through the trees with the speed of eagles and having the gift of nature's touch. Many of them never set foot on the ground, and scorn those who do.

    A Temple of Folian S'pae, the Wood Elves patron God, can be found here.
Tales of the Elven Citadels:  The current state of knowledge about the cities of Voltrex by Ramsiad
