Government:  
    Fort Hope has a two-tier system of government. There is a military commander to run the Fort's garrisons and military function as well as an appointed mayor who administers the social and economic affairs of the fort.

Defenses:  
    An old and resilient military outpost, Fort Hope is well defended.

Miscellaneous Information:
    The first thing you'll likely notice upon entering this centrally located Mistone outpost are the tents, caravans and newly built structures. These new developments arise in the wake of recent migration to the area. For years Fort Hope served as a watch station for the undead, which often overflowed from the Broken Forest. This fact made Fort Hope one of the least desirable posts on the continent. This is true particularly since clean-up crews frequently left the safety of the fort to remove the walking rot and shadows from the crucial road which runs north and south through the forest. These crews almost never returned. And for hundreds of years the road remained hopelessly overrun, controlled by some unknown sinister influence.
The optimistic name of this post has always seemed to play with this kind of historic irony. Although many believe the name of the fort derived from the hope to curtail the evil influence of the Broken Forest, more investigation will reveal that it was actually established and named during the race wars.
A small group of humans pushed past the front lines, situated on the then sublime forest, and supplanted an elven outpost in that same location. Once the fort was captured, their only hope for survival and victory was the drive of the great human general Draislar. He was to wedge through the elven armies of the Far Reach plains and the Broken Forest to regroup at the fort and use it as a base of operations. Draislar never arrived. The battle which ensued claimed the lives of Draislar and his army, but also, and quite mysteriously, the bulk of the elven armies of the region. This battle marked the beginning of the end of the elf and human wars on Mistone. And with countless souls strewn upon the desecrated forest floor, the human chapter of Far Reach began.
The most recent and most prosperous chapter of Fort Hope's history begins with the heroic deeds of the rangers Triba Guess and Enzo Reynolt, who mended the long broken nature of the forest. Once the dead no longer rose to torment the living, the road north and south became passable and the frequency of caravans looking for a respite at the Fort increased rapidly. Fort Hope is coming into its own as a key security and mercantile force, made more crucial by its central location and resilient traditions.

Forewarn Fort 
Location:  
    Fort Forewarn is on the eastern shores of the continent of Mistone. 
Population: 
4,000 (45% human, 20% halfling, 15% half-orc, 10% dwarf, 15% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    Masonry walls surround this city. The walls are reinforced for protection from attacks from the sea.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This is a primary shipping port between the continent of Mistone and Dregar. As such, Forewarn Fort is a major inlet of goods and information as well as a good place to leave Mistone in the aft horizon. With good shipping routes, however, come pirates. The Gulf of Bagira to the north of Forewarn is known to be a pirate hideout and launching point. With the Forsaken Islands off the coast, and stories of whole ships becoming marauding crews of undead, only pirates or fools would sail those waters. These facts draw the seedy elements of Mistone to Forewarn, making it a rough town as well as a sound choice for the headquarters of the Mistone Alliance.

Fort Llast
Location:  
    Fort Llast is in the northwestern part of Mistone. It can be found on the east-west road that runs through Hlint and meets up with the road that runs north and south between Blackford Castle and Krandor.
Population:  275
Government:  
    The government in Fort Llast is a strict military hierarchy under the command of Lieutenant Jursen who answers to Blackford Castle.
Defenses:  
    There is a short stone wall surrounding the city. It is also home to a Temple of Toran, so there are always a couple of paladins around.

Miscellaneous Information:
    A quick glance at a map of Mistone can tell the story of this town's significance. The fort lies at the crossroads of two of the most frequented roads on the continent. This allows the Llast guards to monitor most of the travel and trading in northern Mistone. It is also the job of the Fort to ensure the road which connects Leilon, Blackford Castle and Port Hampshire far to the south remains open and relatively safe. When Fort Llast is well staffed, and it almost always is, guards can be found patrolling the road as far south as the Broken Forest and north until it reaches the ocean at Leilon. 
Monitoring and ensuring smooth movement on Mistone, however, are secondary considerations. Fort Llast was founded in a warm summer of the early 3rd century, at the height of the Human and Elf wars. Blackford Castle was the seat of human power on the continent even then. In the 287th year after the Cataclysm, the castle nearly fell to the elves, an outcome which could have altered the fate of humans and elves on Mistone. 

    Despite being heavily garrisoned and defended, the castle was caught unprepared by the waves of elves who seemed to appear on the Grunwald Plains as swiftly as an ocean storm. Peasants, merchants and guards carrying crucial supplies scrambled to reach the castle before the portcullis fell. Many were left stranded outside and were slaughtered by a hailstorm of elven arrows and bolts. Startled and dismayed by the grisly scene just beyond the walls, the humans who did make it to the castle struggled to regain composure and perform their duties. The disciplined Blackford soldiers, however, snapped into action with drilled precision and managed to turn back wave after wave of elf invaders. 
The elves, however, came prepared to smother every human in that castle with fear and hunger. Their numbers were great, and swelled even greater with reinforcements after each skirmish. The blockade was complete. So with every human soldier pinned in the castle and the nearest garrison far to the south with no hope of contact, the castle lay under siege for months. It took that long before the humans, with the help of some dwarf miners caught in the outskirts, tunneled beneath the castle to a small valley in the Greypeak Mountains. There, two small groups of scouts emerged. One made the trek to Leilon, where they sailed south to the Rodilin Hills to alert the marauding human armies. The second traversed the treacherous peaks to call upon the aid of Haven Castle.

    The elves, pinched by a human army moving north along the Zainge River and another moving west along the northern border of Sielwood forest, were forced to retreat. Elves flowed into the Sielwood and vanished among the ancient trees. At that moment it was clear that the elves had used the cover of the forest to amass their armies and establish supply lines. Thus, Fort Llast was built, perfectly situated as a first line of defense against elven invasion from the deep shadows of the Sielwood forest.

Fort Velensk
Location: 
    Fort Velensk lies at the very southern tip of Mistone between the Battle Fens and the southern ranges of the Berhagen Mountians.
Population: 9385
Government:  
    Fort Velensk is ruled by an allegedly corrupt military dictator.
Defenses:  
    Thick stone walls and battlements surround the city to protect it from terrestrial attacks. However, the town's defenses are more oriented toward guarding the crucial docks.

Miscellaneous Information:
    At the southernmost part of the continent, Fort Velensk is the primary point of connection between Mistone and Rilara. Port Hampshire is the place for more official dockings, but anyone who knows anything about Rilara will know that is why Velensk prospers. In contrast to Port Hampshire, the relative isolation of Fort Velensk between the Berhagen Mountainsto the east and the Battle Fens to the west, as well as having no significant settlements nearby, makes it a preferred destination for more nefarious Rilaran traffic. The large and defensible docks contribute to this function as well. In Rilara, Milara's dominion is said to be total. And considering his grasping ambition, particularly his goal to bring all of Mistone under his sway, Fort Velensk is busy indeed.

    With this said, it is obvious that the fort is a wickedly volatile place. The economic and political elite barely attempt to maintain a thin veil of respectability, a veil which only ever fools the most vapid or gormless transients. Many residents live in squalor; they dwell in alleys and sewers, feeding off of the shipping rubbish and dockside rats. Pirates and outlaws and Rilaran agents of disruption flow through the city with seeming impunity. Of course, this is only true so long as such unseemly agents do not counter the direct interests of the ruling elite. With such desperate and corruptible characters in force on its streets, Fort Velensk also proves an ideal headquarters for mercenary recruiters. Equally logical is the presence of the temple of Rofirien, which beams light from its shimmering surfaces over the dark streets. It is one of the few places of mercy in Mistone's most notorious den of villainy. The men who vault their essence in the Fort Velensk temple and undertake Rofirien's mission of justice are compelled by unmatched faith, often deadly but always selfless. They are among Mistone's most valorous.

Haven
Location:  
    Haven can be found on the eastern rim of Mistone.
Population:  3,300 (50% humans, 30% dwarves, 10% halflings, 10% elves)
Government:  
    Monarchy with landed serfs in surrounding areas
Defenses:  
    The outskirts of Haven, where most reside, are not defended except for by foot patrols. If the town is raided, as many as possible are pulled into the heavily defended stone walls of the castle.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Haven is most noted for the trade route it was built upon. Forewarn Fort, which ships the majority of the continent's goods, is just to the south and Haven is directly between it and the capital of Blackford. Also, while the route is longer, it is still safer for the convoys from Port Hampshire to head through the city rather then the often treacherous forest.

    For many centuries the people of Mistone traveled this long stretch of road with nothing but their own blades to defend the goods they rode with. Eventually small towns began to sprout, offering travelers some refuge from bandits as well as the harsh seasonal weather. 

    These towns brought much relief and grew quickly as the valuable goods stopped in their markets before heading off to their ultimate destination. As the settlements grew, they became all the more ripe for any man brave enough to take advantage of their actual weaknesses. Milick was such a man. 

    Milick was an intelligent man who felt stifled and oppressed by the huge merchant conglomerates of the city. Angered by this, he decided to exact revenge. Milick organized a convoy that would follow the normal route north at the same time as many other convoys. That way, they would all stop near the same locations during the night. Of course, instead of goods, he was carrying a small army of mercenaries bought from the streets of the city. As the other convoys slept under cover of the small towns, Milick's men raided them, killing guards and merchants in their sleep and stealing the goods for themselves. 
Milick ran northwest with his men and booty, hoping to camp within the forest. There he would gather more men and fence his stolen goods to increase the numbers and quality of his army for hire. His desire for vengeance upon Haven could not be assuaged. 

    During the night a fight broke out between Milick and his own appointed mercenary captain. They quarreled over whether they should continue the plan or just settle with the money they had. Angered by the change of plans, Milick lunged at the captain and ripped him open with his blade before the mercenaries could subdue him. By the time they had finished, he had been beaten to death. The next day, they returned to the fort only to find the peasants of the Haven fields rallied and fervent about blocking the hired army's path. A fierce battle ensued, but the peasants eventually managed to overcome the mercenaries, who underestimated the determination of the farmers as well as the sharpness of their scythes. With the captured gold and goods, these unlikely heroes set about creating the fort so travelers and locals could find reliable shelter in dire times.

Krandor
Location:  
    In the central western part of Mistone.
Population: 1600 (60% human, 30% elf, 10% Halfling)
Government:  
    Krandor has a mayor, chosen by the property-owning families in the vicinity.
Defenses:  The only defense Krandor has is a few patrolling guards.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Where the western edge of the Sielwood forest dances endlessly with the expansive meadows just beyond lies the town of Krandor. The unobtrusive architecture and lack of clear border make Krandor seem in harmony with the natural landscape. Because of this, many outdoorsmen are drawn to this town. Some go to Krandor to use the town as a launching point for hunting expeditions into the Sielwood. Others fall in love with the forest and attempt to halt, or at least try to manage the impact such groups have upon the forest. 

Lar
Location: Near the Highstar lake in the Greypeak mountains.
Population: 1200
Government: Feudalism
Defenses: 
    Lar can only be reached by a narrow mountain trail, which can be easily defended by just a handful of guards. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    Lar is very small and remote. It's more of a trader's outpost than a town. Most of those who call Lar home serve the miners and trappers who live and wander in the Greypeak Mountains. Locals speak of the town being founded on the banks of a gorgeous mountain waterfall by Larnida. In recent years, a statue has been erected on that spot to commemorate the event. On founder's day, and other somewhat secretive ritual days, people bring offerings to the statue. 

    There are many dwarves in Lar. This is either a fortuitous circumstance for defense against the many giant attacks upon the city, or the dwarves have come to Lar for a piece of the action. As a trading outpost for trappers and miners, with a high dwarven population and unceasing attacks from giants, life in Lar is clearly a demanding and arduous endeavor. That's why those who call Lar home are some of the most gruff and resilient people to be found on all of Mistone. Lar is also the village where Ta'karsh Blacklung, High Hammer of Dorand, has chosen to build the Citadel of the Hammer in honor of Dorand, god of crafters.

List
Location:  
    List is southwest of the High Moor swamp on the continent of Mistone, near Haven Castle.
Population:
1,175 (45% human, 20% half-orc, 15% dwarf, 10% halfling, 5% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    List is without defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    List is affiliated, both economically and politically, with Haven Castle to the southeast. It is little more than a center for the widely dispersed farmers of the area to come for company, supplies, and transport to the Haven markets for their goods. As such, the residents of the town proper are far outnumbered by those living in the outlying agricultural areas.

Liken
Location:  
    Liken is found at the coast of the northeast corner of the continent of Mistone.
Population:  360
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
    Liken has no defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Nestled in the coastal hills of northeast Mistone and blessed with the perfect climate for growing pipeweed, Liken is a popular place for halflings. There is a single dock right in the middle of the town which launches and receives small ships for local distribution of Liken's and the northeast region's goods.

Kheldell
Location: 
    Kheldell is on the northern tip of Mistone in the High Forest.
Population:
350 (60% human, 20% elf, 5% halfling, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 5% half-orc) 
Government:  Theocracy
Defenses: 
    A wooden palisade surrounds this small hamlet. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    Kheldell is a somewhat self-sufficient town located where the High and Lost Forests together meet the ocean. The town is a part of the forest, obtaining every resource for nourishment, warmth, and shelter from the verdant woodland. As such, Kheldell's residents are raised to be resilient, surviving cycles of intense hardship. The woodsmen who take to this arduous lifestyle are proud of the town and its accomplishments. They therefore tend to discourage outsiders from doing anything more than passing through. They discourage all hopeful settlers except the occasional individual bearing the unmistakably weathered signs of a rugged past spent working the woods. The docks, used sparingly and typically to import regional goods from Liken, are closed to outsiders without prior authorization except, of course, in cases of emergency.

Krelin's Tents 
Location: 
    In the Blood Desert on the continent of Mistone 
Population:
120 (60% human, 25% half-orc, 10% halfling, 2% gnome, 2% dwarf, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tribal 
Defenses:  None 

Miscellaneous Information:
    This is a good resting spot when traveling in the Blood desert. It is virtually the only water available for nearly 100 miles. 

Port Hampshire
Location:  
    Port Hampshire is the major city and port on the southwest coast of the continent of Mistone. 
Population: 
49,000 (70% human, 15% halfling, 5% dwarf, 4% gnome, 4% elf, 2% half-orc) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses: 
    Superior masonry walls surround much of the city. In some key places the walls are also reinforced. In addition to this, some of the walls have also been magically reinforced. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This city is rich and prosperous. Large veins of gold and silver are shipped in from the Swordrust Mountains to the northeast. If an adventurer is looking for something special, she is likely to find it in this city.
Six hundred years ago, this great city was destroyed by a combined force of Drow and dragons. The city was left shattered and stripped as the forces plundered over five million gold from it. The city struggled to rebuild, as the Duke had lost his former power and its resources had been plundered. The only sources of capital in the wake of the destruction were the individual merchants. They pulled together and as quickly as they could began rebuilding the city and raising armies. Their interest in the port and their links to the invaluable resources in the surrounding areas were dear enough to risk everything to defend it. 
The Duke, still attempting to retain authority, could do little to stop the organized merchants.  On several occasions when he attempted to defy them, the merchants quickly placed him under house arrest and kept his castle guarded at all times by their own superior troops, effectively making him a puppet. For centuries this arrangement persisted, and the Dukes of each successive generation increasingly came to accept their fate as adjuncts of the city economy. Every attempt to act otherwise was swiftly curtailed. Now the Duke's tradition in Port Hampshire is to work for and within the systems of power established by the merchants. Through this arrangement, the merchant organizations and the Duke have merged interests and formed a coherent power structure.

    The bottom line in Port Hampshire is still an economic one. The peasants and landowners who live in the surrounding areas often complain about being under the boot of the Port. The laws of the land are implemented to protect the interests of the major merchant powers, who sometimes use this fact to expand their exploitative labor practices and resource capturing endeavors. Some say this is the cause of the unrest which has emerged in the southwest region. Others believe the uprising it is not a legitimate grass roots movement in the interests of those in the shadow of the port, but a machination implemented by Milara or demons or both to destabilize the region in preparation for future maneuvers. Some believe it is both.
Major Temples of Deliar and Shadon can be found in Port Hampshire.

Shoufal
Location:
    Southern part of the continent of Mistone, right in the middle of the Berhagen Mountains. 
Population: 
6,500 (85% Mountain Dwarf, 5% halfling, 5% human, 3% gnome, 1% elf, 1% half-orc) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses: 
    This Dwarven city is surrounded by superior masonry walls that are further reinforced with fiercely guarded Dwarven skills passed on through oral tradition.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Shoufal, also called Gem of Berhagen, is a very proud city steeped in tradition. They do not like outsiders and only after years of living among them will one be grudgingly accepted. This only ever happens when an individual works through the labor and crafting ranks, all the while supporting and defending the community. 
The majority of the populace are devout followers of Dorand and Vorax, and the arms and armors created by the Shoufal smithies are of great renown.
Where the Sun Sets:  A traveller's guide to the cities of Mistone by Lanzo Liftupover
A deed for a framed arched window.
A deed for a rectangular window.

This scroll can be used by players and GM's to create a chest at a specific location. This scroll should be used at that location and may only be used one time. Once used a chest will be created and the player can then open the chest and place up to three items as a reward. Once the chest is closed the chest will then disappear and a new scroll will be created on the player that closed the chest. You only have a single chance to put in the proper treasure so make it count. That new scroll can then be given to other players to seek out the treasure chest.

DO NOT nest treasure maps past the first chest.  Their information will not be preserved and the contents in the nested chest will be lost.

NOTICE:  The treasure map does not store complete items but rather blueprints. This will cause any enhancements, resistances and customizations to be stripped off of items placed into treasure chests.

** GM Note: Please ensure item rewards placed in the chest are of an appropriate level for players that will be seeking the treasure. Do not abuse this system or it will be removed from the game.
This treasure map may be used at any location in the world. If you are near the location of the buried treasure a chest will appear with the treasure inside and this map will be destroyed.

A gentle silky black and white fabric makes these powerful gloves quite the wonder to wield. Enhancing confidence and self-determination, they aid the wielder in the natural channel of their gifts. Granting not only ease in the magical aspects of the individual, these powerful gloves make that who wields them immune to all impairments caused by physical and magical sources, granting true freedom.

The Touch of Beyond has been rumored to have been worn by many famous bards and minstrels who through time and age have been in constant search of true freedom, however they eventually found their way to the hands of wizards and have been put through much different uses which has gained them quite the reputation in many circles. However, only one pair has ever been seen, and those who attempt to duplicate them have always failed, giving this pair of glove an air of mystery that persists through time and age.

This small crystal sits easily in the palm of your hand, its facets and corners perfectly formed.  As you hold it you notice that it humms and vibrates.  The soft harmonic sounds that emenate from it are soothing to the ear and at its center there is a soft glow.

This crystal is a gift given only by the now harmonic entity known as Elzabeth.  It is said to have been gifted  to a number of heroes who helped make her whole and strip an evil creature of the stolen powers of her guardians.

By placing the crystal to your ear the sounds around you are clarified and made louder, distant noises closer.  Harmonics and music gain a depth not known before.

When the crystal is struck lightly against a hard surface it can be used to direct a forcefull sonic attack at an enemy but each time this is done the light within dims slightly.

If one hums into the crystal it responds by wrapping the user in a harmonic skin that guards against some measure of elemental attacks but this causes its inner light to dim significantly.

When its inner energies are expended it is said that the crystal will grow dark and disperse into the air.

This scroll is used to create a quest. 
One option is to create a chest with onr of several items inside the chest. This in turn can be used by players to create on the fly quests for other players. The blank scroll will have the name of the player that created the chest as the title. This is a good way to verify that the proper item has been retrieved.

Another option is to create an NPC that can be used during the quest. The NPC does not interact with a player but can be used for RP purposes.

Any abuse or misuse of this item is a bannable offense so please do not misuse it.
This scroll was found in a chest placed by a quest giver. There is no function for this scroll other than to return it to the player character that is requesting the quest to be completed.

Use this item to authorize PvP between two or more characters. Target this item on each character who wishes to engage in PvP.  You cannot use this wand on yourself.  Another WL or GM must authorize you for PvP.

All uses of this item are logged. Abusing this power will quickly get you removed from World Leader status and could very well get you banned. Please do not abuse this World Leader ability.

A Rascal's Charm may get him out of and into all sorts of trouble.

Once a Rascal's Influence has been used up, a visit to one of his haunts (Katherian, Fort Vehl, or Dalanthar) is in order.

A Rascal may earn influence in many ways, giving succor to the poor, hope to the downtrodden, cleaning up the mean streets, or even by marrying into nobility.

Once a Rascal's Influence has been used up, a visit to one of his haunts (Katherian, Fort Vehl, or Dalanthar) is in order.

Bolt For Home: Using his contacts, the Rascal is whisked away to his place of refuge (Katherian).

(If the Bolt For Home ability is not able to be used, resting will resynchonise the Bolt For Home usage count with the remaining charges.)

Diversion: The Rascal has the option of attracting the attention of (summoning) a passing guard or misinformed citizen when in civilised areas, or a spider when in wilderness areas (please make the appropriate choice for the area you are in).

Influence: Exerts (buffs) the Rascal's considerable powers to Persuade or Bluff.

In the years that Holy Toran walked upon the earth as a mortal his life became a testament to the principles he evinced. In that time he drew to him people who had proven themselves not by birthright and priviledge but by deed and action. These were the people that he called to his side, to stand with him in troubled times and provide leadership that was motivated and driven by the very ideas and concepts he himself believed in. Each of these individuals bore arms and equipment forged from the best of human crafters with dragon magics to infuse the spirit of power into them. After Toran was raised by Rofirein for the very principles he built his life upon his followers spread across the world taking his message forth. With time many of the artefacts were destroyed or lost, or hidden or simply faded from the world of men until but a few remain. This particular sword is believed to have belonged to Torans second in command, Sir Manestus of the Light and has been held in secrecy by the Toranites since it was discovered over a thousand years ago in a cave to the north of Orcs Watch.

The blade itself is as strong and bright as if it was made yesterday from the finest steel available. Its edge never dulls and its light never fades. The blade itself carries etchings of runes believed to be remnants of dragon runic magic the knowledge of which has been lost forever into antiquity.

Use this item to temporarily ban other player characters. Use of this wand must be followed up by a full report to the GM Team, including relevant chat logs and/or screen shots within ONE RL HOUR of the banning.  Failure to do so may result in a loss of World Leader status and privileges.

All uses of this item are logged. Abusing this power will quickly get you removed from World Leader status and could very well get you banned. Please do not abuse this World Leader ability.
This ancient Tome holds incredible power, governing the functioning of Conjuration type magics.
Without knowing much or anything about magic, this tome simply radiates power.

Dwarven for "Axe of the Father", this axe was forged in Amais by Fenrir under the tutorship of a master mithrilsmith named Thlissn. The axe is of exceptional quality and maintains unique properties in part due to where it was forged.

A symbol of his pact with Grannoch, this belt, worn by Fenrir, is recognized by giant-kin. While there are choices on both sides, it represents a pact of non-agression.  

Beyond that, the belt has a powerful strength about it, infusing the wearer with the qualities of the stout race of giants.

In around the 10th century the Toranite High Priest of the time decided that accoutrements fit for the purpose and intended wearer in service to Toran should be produced. He proceeded to almost empty the coffers of the Toranite faith in his drive to procure the best materials, the best craftsman and the best processes for the items he wanted made. Before long, and only after a few items had been successfully made the clergy protested against his wanton waste of the Faiths resources. The High Priest resigned his position coming to realise that he had been driven by greed and jealousy in having the items made and spend the rest of his life in a monastery to atone for his sins. Some of the items that had been made were sold to try and recoup some of the losses and others, more specific to the order were kept and locked away and eventually forgotten. That is until the Auscultare ordered a complete inventory of all Toranite holdings across the world and had many long forgotten relics and items brought to the Citadel in Huanjgin. The Gauntlets of Faith were one such item.

Made from hundreds of tiny mithril discs, linked with finely wrought mithril thread the gauntlets feel smooth and soft on the wearers hand but can resist the mightiest of blows. A golden Ankh is embossed on the palm of both gauntlets and when worn by the right person grants great powers.

Given the danger to Liwich and to the nation of Dregar in its entirety by the machinations of the strange sorceress of the Deep known as Madame Tikiri, the Sabre of Liwich has granted G'ork asylum within its borders. As a sign of their thanks and protection, this amulet serves as their reward. Those attempting to act against G'ork once seeing this amulet should think twice about raising the ire of the Sabre and the nation of Liwich over the mistreatment of one of their heroes. The amulet bears the Rofireinite seal on the reverse side to indicate their own cancelling of all charges against G'ork to that date.

Woven from Ess's brain membranes, the personal attendant of the ancient beholder Malpheus Sulrouzen, this very strange hood holds within its fabric powerful enhancements to the wearer. Infused with ancient beholder magic to hold the magical bonds and odd fabric together, the wearer gets a sense of silent space around them when it's donned. Sounds and images seem to sharpen into focus or clarity and with some concentration one could sense that even thoughts could be ascertained through its weaves. Further practice allows the wearer to impose their thoughts on others.

Created by Baraeon himself for his most trusted followers so that he could send them to the surface realms and spy on his enemies. These hoods have been lost one by one throughout the Deep over time. A few rare and well protected ones remain in the highest levels of the hierarchy of the Followers of the Spider Lord.

This plain looking ring is made from a black metal entwined with a dark red, almost black substance. When placed upon the finger, sharp fangs enter the finger and form a symbiotic relationship with the host. The wearer is constantly aware of the pain of the ring's fangs in their finger, but the benefits outweigh the pain.

A simple but elegant chain of links made of silver. A small charm of Prunillan design dangles from the middle link. While there is plenty of room for other charms to be added, these two components have a faintly divine emanation.
A simple but elegant chain of links made of silver.

It was not long before he realised the power the simple shield held. It wasnt long before he realised that the shield was very light considering its size and easy to move to block enemy blows. 

It was not until later when he could have the shield properly examined he was made aware of the secret of some of its other abilities and learn't the nature of its craftmanship. Aragenite scholars sumised that the shield was very old and had been made by a powerful Beholder Al'nothist. They believed that a Beholder would have no such use for a shield but it was possible such a item was made as gifts for powerful allies or trusted personal guards; a rarity in Beholder society.

Aeridin

Aliases: The Protector and Preserver of Life, The Lifegiver  
Race: Elf 
Worshippers: Predominantly Elves 
Domains: Air, Earth, Healing, Sun, Water, Good

Clerics of Aeridin often combine the Healing domains with one of the other domains.

Governs: Weather, dawn, rebirth, vitality, youth, sun, moons 

Dogma: 
     Preserve and protect life, but bear in mind that in the Great Cycle of life, death also has its place, so life should not be artificially prolonged. Seek out the undead and put them to rest, so they can rejoin the Great Cycle. Do not harm or kill others except in the most dire of circumstances. Do not refuse to aid those who need it.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     In general, clerics of Aeridin prefer to wear white robes. They'll only don armor when absolutely necessary, and even then with great hesitation. However, if they do, they'll wear full plate, either coated with a layer of silver or - more rarely - made from mithril. Their armor is usually embossed with golden leaves.

     In general, they wield quarterstaffs and shun the use of maiming weapons like axes or greatswords. A necklace with a golden leaf is often worn around the neck as a holy symbol.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples to Aeridin can be found everywhere, from the largest city to the smallest village. Most also act as a house of healing for the wounded and the sick and as a place where the poor or unfortunate can find help to get their lives back on track. Spread far across all continents of Layonara, the Church of Aeridin stands in good regard with most peoples.

     Despite the Church's throng of followers, there is not a strong central hierarchy that dictates how the Church operates. There is a hierarchy at the local level, which is mostly based on seniority, not on the actual power a cleric is capable of wielding. All temple communities remain very much in contact.

     Clerics of Aeridin pray for their spells either at noon or during a full moon.

     Religious days are many and tied in to the positions of the sun and the moons. Nights where one of the moons is full hold special importance; however, nights where both Orn and Ausir are full are of prime importance.

Katia

Aliases: 
     Mother Nature, She Who Shapes All  
Race: Human 
Worshippers Race: Mostly humans 
Domains: 
     Air, Animal, Earth, Plant, Water. Clerics of Katia combine the Animal or Plant domains with one of the other domains.
Governs: 
     Nature, forests, agriculture, plants, gardens 


Dogma: 
     Layonara is Nature. Without Nature there is no Layonara; therefore, aid, protect and defend Nature. Oppose those who seek to unbalance Nature. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics and Druids of Katia often wear leather armor dyed in green and brown hues, as worked metal makes them feel out of touch with Nature. 

     Followers of Katia usually use large wooden staves, which are actually strong, almost straight straight branches "given" by trees. They also often use longbows. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Katia's dogma is interpretable in many ways, making her faith somewhat individualistic. So, although the clerics and druids of Katia seek to protect and defend Nature, just exactly how this is to be done varies. Despite the differences in interpretation of the dogma, however, the clergy strives to be viewed as a friendly and good faith, since that is more beneficial. There are those who help nature takes its course by nurturing the forests and the plants, planting and nourishing new growth, and helping and nursing sick animals. These are the ones who are generally seen by the populace and have given the Katian faith an aura of good.  

    However, there is more beneath the surface than meets the eye. There are also those who believe that Nature cannot survive without their help. Civilization is spreading across Layonara and is proving a threat to its wilderness. Already, the forest that once covered Mistone completely has been severed into forests of a smaller size such as the Sielwood, the High Forest, and the Dire Wood. Roads have been laid across the wild plains and agricultural fields spread every year to feed the mouths of those who live in the ever-expanding cities.

     These more extreme followers of Katia will use drastic measures to prevent the felling of the forests, the cultivation of the plains, and the expansion of the cities. They will not shy from breeding fierce animals and setting them loose in order to make areas less safe and prevent villages from expanding. They will also not shy from covertly sponsoring bands of brigands to frequent certain areas, making roads less passable and allowing them to be grown over again.

     However, regardless of how a follower of Katia interprets the dogma, they realize that everything involving Nature takes time and planning. It might take years for their plans to bear fruit, just as it takes years for a sapling to become a tree.

     Because of Katia's dogma being subject to interpretation, there is not one Church of Katia. Followers are loosely organized and tend to live in small groups, with each group being headed by its most senior member. There is no strong, central hierarchy.

     Temples to Katia cannot be found in cities, but are groves secreted away deep in the forests, or large standing stones at the edges of forests.

     Clerics of Katia pray for their spells at sunrise. Prayers to Katia usually involve terminology referencing Nature, like plants, animals, or weather.

     Special holy days are the first days of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

Xeen

Aliases: Mistress of Pleasure and Pain  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: Mostly humans
Domains: Animal, Destruction, Plant, Water 
Governs: Pleasure, wine, love, insanity 

     Xeen is the daughter of Corath and Lucinda. She is the embodiment of excess, sometimes appearing as a beautiful woman in perfect health, and sometimes appearing drained from too much debauchery. Xeen is a very fickle and emotional goddess. She is fond of perverting the inventions of Aragen and Goran, much to their ire. Xeen is credited with making wine and opiates both pleasurable and harmful at the same time.

Dogma: 
     Life is to be lived to its fullest, in decadent sensual fulfilllment of the carnal desires of yourself and others. Pleasure is to be sought at every opportunity, even if it will eventually cause harm to you or others. Reason is for those who do not know how to savor life the way it was meant to be enjoyed. Infinite experiences await those who explore the world of pleasures, so try the new as well as savoring the old. Enjoy love when you can, for it shall not last long. Make wine and other gifts of Xeen and offer them to everyone, that they may enjoy the blissful taste and free themselves of their worldly cares. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Xeenites prefer the whip, a weapon that can in skilled hands be used for both great pain and great pleasure. Clerics of Xeen prefer either loose or tight-fitting clothing, depending on the situation. They prefer leather armor and clothing over metal. They always try to be dressed as seductively as possible to invoke feelings of pleasure in others. The color of what they wear doesn't matter, as long as it makes them look desirable. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The church of Xeen is casually organized, though they often work together to organize parties and celebrations for whatever cause. The clergy of Xeen often run festhalls in bigger cities that cater to all senses and include nearly every pleasure imaginable. Xeenites are also known for their skill in making great wine, and for this reason they can be often seen working for royalty and nobility. 

     The festhalls are often considered temples of Xeen, and often serve as such since they are favorite gathering places of her worshippers. Smaller temples to Xeen exist also, but they aren't very numerous due to the clergy preferring to spend their time in the festhalls rather than some boring temple. Both the temples and the festhalls are beautifully decorated and nearly all of them contain a fountain of wine where people can gather around and enjoy the taste of the goddess' gift. 

     Clerics of Xeen pray for spells in the morning after they wake up so that they may magically remove harmful effects from the previous night's revelry and immediately begin preparing for another, more spectacular day and night of celebration. The clergy of Xeen spend most of their time celebrating and enjoying life, and they tend to make up holy days of Xeen whenever they want to have fun. This has led to no one exactly knowing what holy days exist, but they are more numerous than anyone could imagine.
     The only day of celebration that has a set date is the "Night of Flesh and Magic," which is also known as Xeen's birthday. Xeenites celebrate this day together with Lucindites, for Lucinda is Xeen's mother. Followers of Corath, Xeen's father, aren't usually invited. The Night of Flesh and Magic is celebrated annually, but never on the same day. It's always the seventh day of a month, but every year it's one month later than it was the previous year. This is because Xeen wants to appear much younger than she really is, even though she doesn't age. 1368 the night was seventh of Oclar, 1369 seventh of Novlar, etc. The celebration begins at midnight between the sixth and the seventh day, and lasts for 24 hours. 

      Prayers to Xeen can often be heard anywhere there is a celebration. An example of a prayer to bless wine: "Xeen, Mistress of Pleasure, bless this wine, that the people gathered here can enjoy the taste of your gift and find eternal joy in fleeting love and pleasure."

Baraeon Ca'duz

Aliases: Prince of Hate, Lord of Spiders, Left Hand of Black  
Race: Dark Elf 
Worshippers: Dark Elf males only
Domains: Death, Evil, Trickery
Governs: Hatred, revenge, cruelty, spiders, darkness 
 
     Baraeon was the dark elven hero that led his people into the darkness after they were betrayed by the other elven clans. 
     Baraeon taught his people how to live in the darkness, and with the help of Pyrtechon the race of dark elves thrived. Baraeon also taught his people the arts of revenge and cruelty. 
His own personal revenge against the surface elves culminated when he poisoned the first born daughter of Ilsare. Taking the form of a spider, he managed to sneak into the Ilsare's chambers, where she slept with her young child. Baraeon poisoned the child, and then woke Ilsare so she could watch the child die in her arms. Pyrtechon rewarded Baraeon by elevating him to godhood. 

Dogma: 
     Vengeance is an art. It is sweet and should be savored, a pleasure not to be rushed. Nothing is more satisfying than watching your plans for revenge come to fruition and have the object of your retribution realize you were behind it...but realize too late. The Prince of Hate will look down favorably upon you if your subterfuge remains hidden to all but your target. The weak and the faithless should be destroyed. 

     Dark elves are the supreme race, and Dark Elf males are better than females. 

     The Dark Elves shall reign supreme in Underdark. Annihilate the surface elves and take their lands from them. Do not aid the enemies of the People. Strive to better yourselves, even at the expense of others; this way you will gain and keep the power that is rightfully yours. Do not harm any spider, ever. Harming a spider is an affront to Baraeon Ca'Duz, and should only be done if the spider's poison is used for the art of vengeance.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Priests of Baraeon Ca'Duz prefer to use a shortsword slathered with poisons. Their garb is predominantly black, and stained with dark shades of green. Around their neck they wear a medallion in the shape of a spider, the symbol of their god. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Priests of Baraeon Ca'Duz are the most powerful people in Dark Elf society, next to Priestesses of Vierdri'ira. Every Dark Elf city has one temple for the Prince of Hate. Temples are led by a High Priest, who only remains in that rank as long as no craftier or more powerful Priest removes him from that position.

     Temples to the Lord of Spiders are usually shaped like a spider. One enters a Temple through one of the legs, immediately noticing the greenish light that permeates the entire temple. Depending on the size of the temple, four legs are for training the male clerics. One leg is home to the acolytes' quarters, and one is home to the high clergy. 

     The central body of the spider is the Hall of Poisons. This Hall is filled with webs and spiders, and it is here that the general worship of Baraeon Ca'Duz takes place. The head of the spider is the Inner Sanctum, where the most profane rituals are performed and the temple's treasure and relics are housed. Only the eight highest clerics are authorized to or capable of entering the Sanctum.

     Females are not allowed to enter temples of the Left Hand of Black, on pain of death. This was not the case until about 1500 years ago, when Az'atta betrayed Baraeon Ca'Duz.  Until then, both males and females worshipped the Prince of Hate. However, after being betrayed by Az'atta, Baraeon had his male followers expel or kill all of his female clerics as an act of vengeance for Az'atta's betrayal.

     Males who do not worship Baraeon Ca'Duz but enter the Inner Sanctum are to be sought out and killed unless they are converted to worship Baraeon within 7 days. Proof of conversion is given by undergoing the Test - the same set of trials all Dark Elves have to go through to prove their loyalty to their deities and their People - to demonstrate their loyalty to Vierdri'ira and Baraeon; those who fail either die or are transformed into the fearsome Driders. 

     Clerics pray for their spells before they go into reverie. Prayers are often couched with references to spiders, webs, and poison: "Lord of Spiders, grant me your favor that my enemies do not notice the web of intrigue I have spun to ensure their demise."

Crafted by Lagros Hargrinson, dwarven smith and priest of Dorand, in the time before the great Dragon War, this sword was first employed in the race wars, where elves turned upon elves. 
As a gift to his lifelong friend, Lagros put much time and effort into the creation of this magnificent blade. Elmander Luyrin'ahl, a Gray Elf of noble blood, was the recipient of this gift - a sword worthy of one of the best swordsmen the world had ever seen.
Elmander wielded "Gar Thnzoak" in the final battle against his dark skinned brethren, when he and his brothers and sisters in arms drove the last remnants of the cursed kin, who would later come to be known as the drow, into the depths of the earth.

After Elmander the sword was wielded by his son Lysindel, a restless soul and a traveller. It was Lysindel who at long last left his ancestral lands behind and turned to a life as adventurer, driven by his curiosity and hunger for adventure.

Therefore, they have no fear of death. Aeridin, the Lifegiver, Elven God of Healing.

Preserve and protect life. The gift to exist is not one to be taken lightly; thus, one must lead an exemplary life devoted to benevolence and care. Tend to those who ail, and offer your gift of healing to make their stay in the mortal realm a wholesome experience. Yet once death has taken its toll, respect the passing and enjoy the fond memories of their life. Do not dwell on or mourn too long those who pass. Death is sadness - but without understanding sorrow, one can ­not understand happiness.

Promote health and the well-being of the mind and body before anything else. Any extension, transformation, alter­ation, or corruption to the natural forms and shapes of beings is an affront against the sanctity and purity of life and should be confronted at first with gentle lessons and benevolent teaching, and if such ways do not work, with a stern and firm stance instead. Violence is the last option; use it only on those who defy these teachings.

Undeath is the most blatant aberration to the sanctity and purity of life. Put them to rest by any means necessary so that their souls may reach their homes. Use the gift of the Caring Light to bring brightness to the darkest of places. Never succumb to dark temptations for they only bring a taint upon the spirit.

Aliases: Healing Light, Caring Light, Keeper of Life, Lifegiver
Race: Elf
Worshippers: Predominantly Elves
Governs: Dawn, Health, Vitality, Youth, Sun, Moons
Mantras: Caring, Peaceful, Preserving, Stoic

Clerics act as intermediaries between the earthly and the divine (or infernal) worlds. A good cleric helps those in need, while an evil cleric seeks to spread his patron's vision of evil across the world. All clerics can heal wounds and bring people back from the brink of death, and powerful clerics can even raise the dead. Likewise, all clerics have authority over undead creatures, and they can turn away or even destroy these creatures. Clerics are trained in the use of simple weapons, and can use all forms of armor and shields without penalty, since armor does not interfere with the casting of divine spells. In addition to his normal complement of spells, every cleric chooses to focus on two of his deity's domains. These domains grants the cleric special powers, and give him access to spells that he might otherwise never learn.

WARNING: To cast a spell, a cleric must have a Wisdom score of 10 + the spell's level. For example, to cast a 2nd-level spell, a cleric must have a Wisdom of 12.

- Hit Die: d8.
- Proficiencies: All simple weapons, all armor, and shields.
- Skill Points (*4 at 1st level): 2 + Int Modifier.
- Spellcasting: Divine (Wisdom-based, spell failure from armor is ignored).

Aragen, the Wise God, Human God of Knowledge.

The collection and preservation of knowledge, of the facts, is the prime objective of any true Aragenite. The smallest detail has great value and should not be overlooked. To investigate all leads no matter how far fetched is common, as quoted by one scholar wishing to remain anonymous, "Since the Great Cataclysm, strange and wondrous things have occurred all over this world. To mistrust a source due to the strangeness of the claim does the world a great injustice. All leads should be investigated and all the details acquired in the pursuit, the goal discovered or not, should be recorded for posterity."

Aragenites are a humble group as most religions go. They seek only to further the collection of knowledge. Their prime directive is searching through objectivity. What that means is that no priest, follower, or any one who associates themselves with Aragen should prejudge the facts; remain completely objective as it is not the place of a mere individual to judge the facts. One set of eyes cannot pass a judgment because a single set could not possibly see all of the potential details to a situation or event.

In addition, Aragenites are a nonviolent group. In fact, they preach noninvolvement in all things unless one's own life is in danger. They stand strong in the face of adversity, especially where the conservation of knowledge is concerned.

In short, the dogma of Aragen reads: Knowledge should be gathered and preserved, for knowledge is the only thing that will lead you to truth.

Observe and record and do this objectively. Do not cloud the observation with speculation or supposition as that could lead to distortion. Do not judge what you see - as a single pair of eyes can only see part of the whole picture and your judgement may be faulty. Do not dismiss any information, no matter how small or irrelevant you deem it, because it may be the missing piece of the puzzle of understanding.

Do not partake in the occurrences that you are observing, as participation may influence the events. Do not use violence, unless in self-defense or in the preservation of knowledge.

Aliases: The Wise God, The Great Collector
Race: Human
Worshippers: Those who follow the Wise God come from various races; although, it is the elves who make up most of them. This is not a strange thing, even though Aragen himself was human. The long-lived elves are patient and are appreciative of the time it can take to gather knowledge properly. Close to the elves in number are the humans, driven by their short lives and desire for progress, they too strive to gather knowledge in order to have it benefit society for the future. While followers of other races exist, they are far from numerous. Most other races do not concern themselves with knowledge in its broad form. However, if one does, the Church of Aragen welcomes them with open arms.
Governs: Knowledge, Research, Stories, Poetry, Lore
Mantras: Cerebral, Passive, Scholarly, Stoic

Deliar, the Merchant of Fate, Halfing God of Merchants and Luck.

"You know the road? It isn't just the place that goes from one point to another, oh no, don't let anyone mislead you like that. The road is a wonderful new world of discoveries and adventures, it's the place where legends begin, it's the place where destiny takes you by the heels and whisks you away into the unknown. The road indeed is not just a pass; it's a journey in itself! But don't take my words to heart, the road is not for me to explain, it is for you to experience. So grab your pack, pick a good stick, and take that first step. You won't know it until you walk it. And if you find anything interesting along the way, make sure you pick it up to trade for other goodies!" ~ Words from Layson Pincher to his son


Deliar teaches that in order to lead a fulfilling life, one must constantly strive to discover new ways to trade with the world. His objectives and priorities deal with a harmonious existence in which everything is spread throughout all the communities that touch any goods or services that can be bartered with. The Lucky Wanderer promotes wealth, yes, but such wealth should not be enjoyed at the expense of others - particularly not at the expense of the community as a whole. Thus, he welcomes success in monetary gains as long as other needs have been satisfied.

Carrying their families with them if necessary, all followers of the Merchant of Fate are encouraged to explore the world; because the only way to truly appreciate existence as a whole, is by exploring all its possibilities and letting others know of the treasures from distant lands. These treasures aren't just in gold but in all the uniqueness a culture can offer. Particularly, in the things they create to identify themselves - that way, there is a bit of everyone all over Layonara.
Deliar, the Merchant of Fate, Halfing God of Merchants and Luck.

To hone your skills as a tradesman, is to worship Deliar at what he does best, which is to understand the true value of an item and make everyone gain from it even though perhaps the person they are exchanging with may not at first see the bigger picture. In the end, as long as no one is harmed by the trade, their role has been fulfilled. The best kind of exchange is the kind where each side walks away feeling like they came out on top.

Finally, all those who follow the path of the Lucky Wanderer understand that little in life is predictable, that the roads in life have only the certainty of uncertainty within them, and that every turn may throw at them a good or bad experience. The concept of luck and fate, whether good or bad, is embraced by all Deliarites fully since they know the fruits of today may not be as bountiful as those of tomorrow, and life does particularly well in bringing surprise to everyone. Because of this, many worshippers of Deliar are extremely superstitious and have many quirky rituals and talismans that must be performed or carried before embarking on a particular journey or going on about their daily routines.

Aliases: Lucky Wanderer, Merchant of Fate, Wind of Destiny
Race: Halfling
Worshippers: Halflings (usually male) and merchants or shopkeepers of every race.
Governs: Family, Fate, Harmony, Luck, Money, Trade, Wealth
Mantras: Materialistic, Nomadic, Public, Rural

Folian S'pae, the Prince of Wolves, Elven God of The Wilderness and Wolves.

Folian S'pae teaches that everyone is born into a pack. Like the wolves he protects, everyone in this pack has a role and purpose that they must accomplish for the survival of the whole. Like the wolf pack, each has his own role: protector, hunter, gatherer or scout. Pack leader, matriarch, father, mother, or pup, all working together in harmony is what makes the pack strong and allows it to endure. All members of a pack should make efforts to harmonize with their companions. The young need to be protected and nourished so that a good future of the pack is guaranteed. The safety and sanctity of hunting grounds should be protected, there should be enough food for all, but care should be taken to not hunt to excess and never only for oneself. You are part of the pack. Regardless of how you feel about another of your pack, do not let these feelings get in the way of the good of the pack.

Remember that the hunter and the prey are essential parts of nature. However, do not hunt into extinction since that upsets the balance. Use what is needed for survival of the pack, but do not use more than you need. If you have to take from the lands and forests, you are expected to give something in return sooner or later. You are the stewards of your hunting grounds, and all that live in it are under your protection. While some may be prey, they should be loved and protected nonetheless. Defend your grounds against those who would destroy them needlessly. Allow yourself to adapt to change. The passing of seasons will test you in new ways each year. And do not allow yourself to fall victim of ill preparations. Be an example to those who learn from you and mark each step safely, because those who come after you will benefit from the paths you tread.

Aliases: The Longstrider, Prince of Wolves
Race: Wood Elf
Worshippers: Wood Elves and rangers
Governs: Hunting, Predators, Shape Changers, Survival, Wilderness
Mantras: Natural, Nomadic, Private, Selfless

Grannoch, the Mother of Giants, Giant Goddess of The Elements.

The first words of Grannoch when she created the giant races of Layonara were these: "My Children, I, Grannoch, Mother of Giants, am the One that is Four. The Four are One inside Me. Since I am the Four, none can be supreme."

Grannoch balances the elements, since she embodies all elements. All elemental powers are granted by Grannoch, and thus, all are equally powerful.

Three edicts have been issued that followers are expected to follow:

Just as no element is better than any other, so no race of giants is better. Grannoch does not show favoritism. She expects her children not to fight over which giant race is better. This is both the first and most frequently ignored edict the kerekk has. There are legends passed down by the shaman of Grannoch expressing her anger at warring tribes of giants with wildly destructive storms or volcanic eruptions.
No follower of Grannoch shall slay another. The second edict and the second most ignored; usually ignored in conjunction with the first.
Protect your homes and families from those who would trespass and bring you harm. Grannoch decrees that her followers shall not kill each other or war to prove their superiority. She does not apply that to non-giants or those who do not worship her.
Aliases: All giants: Mother of Giants; Depending on race: Lady of Lightning, Shaper of Stone, Tamer of Flame, Mistress of Cold
Race: Giant
Worshippers: Usually Giants, Half Giants or Humans with some giant blood in their ancestry.
Governs: Earthquakes, Ice, Storms, Volcanoes
Mantras: Humble, Preserving, Private, Sedentary

Katia, Mother Nature, Human Goddess of Nature.

"We are one with Layonara for Layonara is Nature. Without Nature there is no Layonara. All races, all living creatures lend their time to Nature. Nurture, protect and defend Nature. Oppose those who seek to unbalance it. While we preserve and protect life, give credence that in the Great Cycle of Life, death also has its place."

Katians believe there is a place for most things within the great cycle and celebrate how each may find his or her path. Fires rejuvenate the lands. Water purifies the soil. Wind carries away excess and delivers new seeds from new places. Earth bears witness and supports all we do. People come in many varieties as well, including a mixture of these traits and more. The balanced path brings a better Layonara and an enriched life. While the great cycle's needs change and revolve, there are a few static concepts shared by most Katian followers. Katia's principles are to preserve and protect the wild places and nurture the care for Layonara within others. Katia's worshipers tend to interpret the needs of each of these principles a little differently in each place. A large factor in the definition of her dogma is in its flexibility. Doing what needs be done to protect, balance, and nurture. The paths that are taken vary in places as her followers tend to operate alone or in small isolated groups or families. Many see themselves as defenders of the wild places; others find their life's work in the grander scale of balancing the great cycle.

Katian dogma tends toward neutrality rather then good or evil, laws or chaos. The focus is centered more on a personal connection to Katia and how the self affects the world around them. Remaining true to the self and the great cycle is most paramount. Restoring balance in nature, people, and one's self are the goals of most Katians. How that is done is based on personal philosophy, the teachings of their home, and which path they follow in life. If anything would upset the balance, those actions would be considered a sin. Generally speaking, Katians find nothing more upsetting then the uncaring clearing of the forest to make way for agricultural fields. The aggressive expansion of cities into the wild lands also finds its place within the discussions of elders, attempting to find a way to slow or stop these atrocities to nature. Those who heartlessly cut down trees for use of their lumber quickly find themselves on the punishing end of a Katian's tree-given staff.

Aliases: Mother Nature, The Cruel Mother, She Who Watches
Race: Human
Worshippers: Mostly humans.
Governs: Nature, Forests, Plants, Rebirth
Mantras: Natural, Idealistic, Rural, Humble

"Learn from what I teach, teach it to others, and make sure you have no leftovers."

Prunilla teaches her followers that a true life is led when tending to the soil under your feet and caring for those who surround you through it. Planting and harvesting are part of a simple cycle, and it is in the care of our people to spice that cycle with happiness and joy. Nurture the land as if it were your body, plant crops as if you were kissing your beloved, and tend them as if you were caring for your own soul. You are a paragon of virtue and honor. Dedicate your life to justice, honor, and the pursuit of law and order. Hold the law above all else at any cost, even if this means bringing loved ones or friends to justice. Without the order of law, chaos would reign and the world would descend into dark times where Pyrtechon would thrive. Extend honor to all--even your foes. Aid others whenever and wherever possible as long as it is in accordance with the law and does not make way for acts of evil. The common people are the strongest force in bringing order and prosperity to all. We must protect them.

Clerics act as intermediaries between the earthly and the divine (or infernal) worlds. Shadon, the Trickster, Gnome God of Trickery.

Life is fleeting, and therefore must be enjoyed. Every moment spent doing something boring is a moment wasted. Relish constantly in festivals and adventuring. Go to any extent to enjoy yourself, no matter how trivial the action, no matter what the consequences may be. Rules and regulations only apply to those who need them. Boundaries, whether they are physical, moral, or emotional, are only there to be broken. Laws will only hold you back. Such things only serve those who make them. Ignore all of them, or better still, break all of them. Make a mockery of them and of all those who try to force them upon you. Practical jokes make the loudest statements and are nothing short of hilarious. Always have a prank or two up your sleeve, and Shadon will be happy with you. Put your own enjoyment before anything else. Enjoyment is the key to everything. Get back at those who would put an end to your merriment; even better if there is a crowd. Whether your actions were good or evil, helpful or harmful, it does not matter, so long as they were fun to do.

Race: Gnome

Swim both the great currents and the shallow seas. Promote knowledge and use of the sea by reasonable folk, and fight those that would taint or deplete its beauty and bounty. Think long and wisely before acting; the seas do not alter quickly, but when the waters move, great change is sure to follow. Vorax, the Father of Battle, Dwarven God of Battle.

"Hennkeson group, roit! Cap'n Fairnback, left! Cap'n Stoneangle, dig in center, an' you! Git yer group round back fer tha flank! Let's show 'em what we got boys! Red axes up!" -General Longpike, directing a skirmish with Co'rys forces near the border to the Ulgrids

Let bravery, valor, and honorable war define you. Maintain and uphold the morals of your people. Do not allow pacifism or idleness to infect you; for any ideal worth having, is worth fighting for. Idle minds are fertile grounds for schism. Idle hands become soft and unsuited for battle. You are the embodiment of what it is to be a dwarf--be eternally vigilant of this fact and do not allow the lax and decadent ways of other races to influence your heritage.

"Vorax honors all who believe in bravery, war, and valor. He despises weakness of character, believing one should have strong moral values. He hates pacifism, as any morals and ideals worth having should also be worth fighting for. He loathes an idle mind, as it becomes fertile ground for doubt to grow, and he equally hates an idle body, as it becomes soft and unsuitable for the rigors of war. Above all, he abhors dishonorable and deceitful tricksters*. War should be fought for righteous causes and won through honorable battle. War is a sacred rite for followers of Vorax; as such, war is never entered into lightly. War should always be an option of last resort and should only be engaged in for the most just of causes. Once engaged, a war should be fought strictly by the established rules and the righteous cause must be made victorious. There is no shame in losing a battle, but there is great dishonor in losing a war. To lose a war is to fail the just and the righteous, therefore, to fail the Father of Battle. Because war is so sacred, the tools of war are sacred instruments. Thus, treat weapons of war with great reverence. To encompass all of this, we who follow Vorax must have a strong and just moral character. We must be like the Eternally Vigilant himself, keeping our bodies and minds prepared at all times to defend our people." - Introduction to a War Priest College, by Captain Falkin Cartman "tricksters" here means magic users as well as all kinds of subterfuge which would be considered dishonorable.

Xeen, Mistress of Pleasure and Pain, Human Goddess of Pleasure and Wine.

The purpose of life is to enjoy and live it to its fullest. Restraining oneself to illusionary constructs established by a chained society seeking nothing but to hide their true purpose in life in order to appear civil is the biggest fallacy constructed by men. Break these bonds of restraint; for in them, you will find bliss in all its forms. Pleasure and pain exist in each nuance of life. Seek to exploit the pleasures of living for your own fulfilment but do not ignore the pain as often it can serve as a catalyst to greater pleasure. Follow your desires as you explore your world for all the delights it may bring to you. Cast off reason and temperance as they are for those who do not know how to savor life in the way it is meant to be enjoyed. Enjoy carnal passion, the only true palpable aspect of love, for any other feeling attached to the word is simply a fleeting illusion made to comfort something that is not meant to last. Make wine and other gifts of Xeen and offer them to everyone that they may enjoy the blissful taste and free themselves of their worldly cares.

Drow are known to be some of the most evil creatures outside of the lower planes, and wage an eternal war on their surface cousins.
