Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master Level 8
Specifics: By combining your ki power with alcohol, you can convert an alcoholic drink to a potion of heal up to three times per day. The alcohol activates the ki in your body, so the cure only works on you. Alcohol drunk in this way neither impairs nor improves your ability scores.
Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master Level 10
Specifics: You can use your ki to ignite the alcohol within you and spew it forth from your mouth in a breath of flame. Breath of flame deals 3d12 points of fire damage to all within the 20-foot cone (Reflex save DC 18 for half). Each time you use breath of flame, it consumes one drinks worth of alcohol. First your inventory is searched for alcohol and if none is found it uses the alcohol within you removing the effects it gives you.
Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 11
Specifics: You have become a conesour of alcoholic beverages and have developed specififc tastes. You now can combine base ingredients and brew your own ale which may grant additional bonuses along with your Drunken Rage effects.
Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 11
Specifics: Your blood has had alcohol running through it for a while now. Due to the constant content the effects of Drunken Rage last 3 hours rather than the standard one.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 13
Specifics: The alcohol you drink has made your skin strong and your pain threshold large. You gain +4 to your natural AC.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 14
Specifics: Your body has learned to use alcohol's buzz in a percise way which grants you +2 to all saving throws.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 11
Specifics: Your fighting and drinking skills have improved to the point where you can simultaneous drink alcohol from a bottle while using the bottle in a fight, thus combining Drunken Rage with Bottle Proficiency.
Useage: Use the feat and then target an alcoholic beverage. Drunken Rage and Bottle Proficiency will kick in giving you all the bonuses of the 2 feats.

Type of Feat: Class Specific
Prerequisite: Drunken Master level 15
Specifics: You've learned to use Breath of Flame and figured out how to make it more powerful. The fire damage is 5d12 now instead of 3d12.
Use: Automatic.

(PRESTIGE CLASS)
Hathran, also known as the Witches of Rashemen, comprise an elite sisterhood of spellcasters who lead the region. In Rashemi society, hathrans occupy the place reserved for powerful clerics in most Faerunian cultures. Hathran - meaning "learned sister" - heal the sick and wounded and care for the souls of their followers.

- Hit Die: d4.
- Proficiencies: Exotic weapons.
- Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier.

REQUIREMENTS:

Gender: Female.
Feats: Ethran. (This feat requires 11 Cha).
Spellcasting: Able to cast 2nd-level arcane and divine spells.
Class: Cleric
Skill: Spellcraft 9 ranks.

ABILITIES:

Level
1: Cohort - Once per day the Hathran can call for a Rashemen Barbarian to serve as her cohort. 
3: Fear  Can cast Fear as the spell once per day.
6: Fear - Can cast Fear as the spell twice per day.
8: Fear - Can cast Fear as the spell three times per day.
10: Greater Command - Can attempt hold a group of enemies once per day.

BONUS SPELLS

Every second level, the character gains new spells per day as if she had also gained a level in her highest arcane and divine classes. She does not learn any new arcane spells through this ability, however.

(PRESTIGE CLASS)
Part reconnaissance expert, part border guard, part spy and part diplomat, the vigilant is a highly trained warrior who can be confidently sent into any situation, no matter how grim the odds. Recruits who survive the harsh training and deadly initiation tests required to become a vigilant are assigned to one of the elite corps of these warriors, called a Vigil.

- Hit Die: d12.
- Proficiencies: A vigilant does not gain any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.
- Skill Points: 4 + Int Modifier.

REQUIREMENTS:

Base Attack Bonus: +5
Feats: Endurance, Track
Skills: Lore 4 ranks, Listen 5 ranks, Persuade 5 ranks.

ABILITIES:

Level
1: Sprint - Can move for a brief period of time as Hasted, three times per day.
2: Favoured Enemy - Gains a Favoured Enemy as the Ranger ability.
4: Great Fortitude - A character with this feat is tougher than normal, gaining a +2 bonus to all Fortitude saving throws.
5: Iron Will - The character's strong presence of mind gives him a +2 bonus to all Will saving throws.
6: Lightning Reflexes - The character's reflexes are faster than normal, granting him a +2 bonus to all Reflex saving throws.
7: Toughness - A character with this feat is tougher than normal, gaining one bonus hit point per level.
9: Vigilant Natural Armor - Gains plus 2 to his natural armor class.
10: Vigilant Natural Healing - Regenerates hit points at a rate of one per round.

Type of Feat: General.
Prerequisite: None.
Specifics: Gain plus 4 to saving throws against Death.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: General.
Prerequisite: None.
Specifics: Gain plus 1 to Spot, Search and Listen.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Vigilant level 9.
Specifics: Gain plus 2 bonus to Natural Armor Class.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Hathran level 1.
Specifics: Can call upon a fifth-level Rashemen barbarian to serve as a cohort once per day.
Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Hathran level 10.
Specifics: Once per day can attempt to exert control over a group of people. This will hold them in place for a number of rounds equal to your arcane caster level.
Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Vigilant level 1.
Specifics: Character can moved as hasted for a brief duration three times per day.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Vigilant level 10.
Specifics:  Gain rapid healing allowing for the regenration of 1 point per round.
Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Class.
Prerequisite: Hathran levels 3, 6 and 8.

Use: Selected.

Master Harpers are elite members of the Harpers, which is a secret society that battles evil and tyranny, preserves lore, and works to balance civilization and the wild. (PRESTIGE CLASS)
The highest art is magic, often refered to as *the* Art. Its most advanced practitionner are frequently archmages, bending spells in ways unavailable to otehr spellcasters.

- Hit Die: d4.
- Proficiencies: An Archmage does not gain any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.
- Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier. 

REQUIREMENTS:

Arcane Spellcasting: Level 7 or higher.
Feats: Skill Focus(Spellcraft), Any Spell Focus.
Skills: Spellcraft 15 or more ranks, Lore 15 or more ranks.

ABILITIES:

Level
1: High Arcana*, Mastery of Elements(Normal)
2: High Arcana*
3: High Arcana*
4: High Arcana*
5: High Arcana*

BONUS SPELLS
The Archmage sacrifices the bonus spell slots he should gain in order to take a High Arcana feat at each levels.
He does however add his level to the base caster class when determining spell powers(damage, duration ...).

HIGH ARCANA:
Each level the Archmage must choose one High Arcana feat of those:
* Arcane Fire: This feat allows the Archmage to convert any spells he knows into a powerfull bolt of raw magical energy.
* Mastery of Elements: This feat allows the Archmage to change on the fly the damage type of any elemental spells. The feat to set them back to normal is free at level 1, the fire, cold, acid, electrical and sonic damages are separated in their own feats and must be selected.
* Mastery of Shapes: This feat allows the Archmage to create "holes" in her area of effects spells to protect his companions from the effects.
* Spell Power: This feat allows the Archmage to increase his effective caster level by 1(cummulative with the normal level bonusthey get).

He does however add his level to the base caster class when determining spell powers(damage, duration ...).

HIGH ARCANA:
Each level the Archmage must choose one High Arcana feat of those:
* Arcane Fire: This feat allows the Archmage to convert any spells he knows into a powerfull bolt of raw magical energy.
* Mastery of Elements: This feat allows the Archmage to change on the fly the damage type of any elemental spells. The feat to set them back to normal is free at level 1, the fire, cold, acid, electrical and sonic damages are separated in their own feats and must be selected.
* Mastery of Shapes: This feat allows the Archmage to create "holes" in her area of effects spells to protect his companions from the effects.
* Spell Power: This feat allows the Archmage to increase his effective caster level by 1(cummulative with the normal level bonusthey get).

(PRESTIGE CLASS)
The highest art is magic, often refered to as *the* Art. Its most advanced practitionner are frequently archmages, bending spells in ways unavailable to otehr spellcasters.

- Hit Die: d4.
- Proficiencies: An Archmage does not gain any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.
- Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier. 

REQUIREMENTS:

Arcane Spellcasting: Level 7 or higher.
Feats: Skill Focus(Spellcraft), Any Spell Focus.
Skills: Spellcraft 15 or more ranks, Lore 15 or more ranks.

The healer is a peaceful servant of the gods, dedicated to the removal of pain from others, and to their well being. The healer will usually be a selfless person, who regards all life as precious, and whose life is dedicated to others rather than to himself.

- Hit Die: d4.
- Proficiencies: A Healer does not gain any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.
- Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier.

Divine Spellcasting: Level 3 or higher.

Skills: Healing 6 or more ranks, Persuade 5 or more ranks.

Level

5: Cure Serious Wounds at will
6: Heal twice per day
7: Resurrection twice per day
8: Mass Heal twice per day
9: Cure Critical Wounds at will
10: Supreme Healing once per day

A healer gains levels as normal in his main divine spellcasting class.

The healer, being peaceful by nature, abhors offensivce acts and therefore does acquire any new meele skills.

* Arcane Fire: This feat allows the Archmage to convert any spells he knows into a powerfull bolt of raw magical energy.
* Mastery of Elements: This feat allows the Archmage to change on the fly the damage type of any elemental spells. The feat to set them back to normal is free at level 1, the fire, cold, acid, electrical and sonic damages are separated in their own feats and must be selected.
* Mastery of Shapes: This feat allows the Archmage to create "holes" in her area of effects spells to protect his companions from the effects.
* Spell Power: This feat allows the Archmage to increase his effective caster level by 1(cummulative with the normal level bonusthey get).

The Legendary Dreadnought is the ultimate foot soldier, an absolute force of destruction, a total warrior who excels at sheer combat prowess. While some rely of cunning and reflexes in a fight, and others uphold a code of honor or engage in combat from horseback, the Legendary Dreadnought simply wades into battle, completely bent on relentless, steady destruction. When the tide of combat flows against him, he stands like a rock. It is the Legendary Dreadnought who has the might to breach the seemingly unbreachable gates.

- Hit Die: d12.
- Proficiencies:  All simple and martial weapons, all armor and shields.

3: Epic Toughness.* - Character gains 20 HP.
4: Epic Damage Reduction - Dreadnought gains 3/- damage reduction.
5: Bonus Feat.

*Bioware has made it impossible to add permanent HP by custom methods. Therefore, at 3rd level the Character will gain Epic Toughness 1, at 8th, Epic Fortitude, and at 13 Epic Toughness 2. Addititionally to get the Damage Reduction to stack with current damage reduction used by the Barbarian and Dwarven Defender Classes the class gains Epic Damage Reduction, plan your character builds appropriatly.

Iaijutsu is the martial art of drawing a weapon, almost always a katana and attacking with it in the same fluid motion. It is the foundation of some forms of dueling, and its masters are feared and respected throughout the world.

They started arguing about what should be the target, and one of them finally yelled out "Why, we're standing in it! Yes, indeed it did. The story of the darts got out, and the adventurer decided that the map was so full of holes after that night that he would just have to copy a new one, so he just left it pinned to the wall of the inn. I think they must have been celebrating finding some treasure, because the group of them bought round after round until they were all drunker than a Xeenite on a festival day. Then they pulled out a bunch of darts ....
Where can I get a drink?
Do you have any rooms for the night?
Thanks for the tip. Can I ask you another question?
The Bull's Eye? That's a funny name for an inn.
I'll take your word on that. Farewell.
This is a long story. Maybe I'll hear the rest another time.
Oh, do you work here? In that case, I have a question for you.
I can see where this is going!
And the name stuck, I guess?
Interesting. You seem to know a lot about this place. Can I ask you a question?
I see. Thanks for the story.
Actually, can I ask you a question?
Do you know any other stories?
Wait, I have a question for you ...
I'd like to turn in for the night. Can you find me a room?
Actually, nothing. I changed my mind.
Can I buy you a drink?
It was worth a try. Can I ask you another question?
Sorry to hear that. Farewell for now, then.

A Treatise on Warfare Volume VI
Arcana

by

Thordan Ironheart

Arcane magics are a volatile and unpredictable thing. This does not however make them unnatural.

The commander that trusts too heavily in arcane magics will be burned by them. Such a commander is doomed to suffer defeat.

The commander that refuses to acknowledge the usefulness and power of arcane magics will also be burned by them. His armies are doomed to be cut down by them and he too shall suffer defeat.

Therefore in warfare a balance must be  struck between reliance and acceptance. A good commander understands how to lay out a plan with such a balance.


The rest of this volume is dedicated to the use of arcane magics in warfare.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume VI

A Treatise on Warfare Volume II
The Ways of War

by

Thordan Ironheart


A good strategist never enters into battle until the outcome is already certain.

The ability to planning is the most important skill the leaders of a nation must possess. Planning is the basis for all successes and failures. The life and death of natins and of people is determined by this.

This volume goes on to detail the various ways planning can be broken down and applied and includes the basics of military structure.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume II

A Treatise on Warfare Volume III
The Means of War

by

Thordan Ironheart


A great deal can be discerned about the morale of a nation and its support for war by the necessity for conscription. Conscription should only be used as a final means by which to come by those who will engage in combat. It should not be entered into lightly. Nor should women, or man children beneath the age of consent be conscripted.

This volume goes on to explain various devices to be used to equip and prepare an army for war, including the conscription of soldiers and the outfitting of an army.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume III

A Treatise on Warfare Volume IV
Leadership

by

Thordan Ironheart


A commander must be smart, trustworthy, caring, brave, and strict. Ambition is good, but only if temered with loyalty. A commander must have a knowledge of military philosophy and possess the skills to implement it. Neither skill with a weapon or force of personality may make a good commander. A good commander is forged using both of these things.

This volume goes on to explain the philosophies of command and gives a more detailed explanation of how command in military endeavors works. It thoroughlly explains the right way and wrong way of exercising command authority and also how to disseminate command authority.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume IV

A Treatise on Warfare Volume V
Morale

by

Thordan Ironheart


You can fight a war for a long time or you can make your nation strong. You cannot do both.

A prolonged war drains a nation of its resources. An army consumes resources like an invader. Do not let the army consume for too long.

To fight a prolonged war is wrong. An army that fights a prolonged war gets dull and lethargic. Such an army cannot win a battle.

Therefore make your wars quick and decisive.


This volume goes on to explain how armies lose morale and th best ways to improve morale and fight off fatigue.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume V

A Treatise on Warfare Volume VIII
Espionage

by

Thordan Ironheart


Warfare is an exercise in deception. To wholly deceive one's enemy is to ensure victory. To be deceived is to ensure defeat.

A nation committted to victory knows how to properly employ the use of spies both in the gathering of intelligence and the dissemination of mis-information.


This volume goes on to describe how best to make use of spies and also covers counter-intelligence, including how best to break and turn captured spies.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume VII

A Treatise on Warfare Volume VIII
Fortification

by

Thordan Ironheart


Every nation must have a base from which to lead from. The more impenetrable the stronghold, the more secure the leadership may be defended. However a fortification is only as strong as the forces defending it. Immobile fortifications without sufficient forces to guard them are a testament to the folly of those who rely on unthinking objects such as rocks to do the job of trained personnel.


The rest of this volume deals with the various types of fortifications, their proper implementation, and how best to man them. Everything from field structures to castle strongholds is given some consideration.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume VIII

A Treatise on Warfare Volume IX
The Cost of Warfare

by

Thordan Ironheart


When the battles are over and the fields lay strewn with the bodies of fallen warriors, we should not cry for them and pray to the gods asking why loved ones died. Rather we should honor their memories and pray to the gods to give thanks that such people lived.


The rest of the volume goes on to explain the different costs associated with warfare and how best to meet each expense.
A Treatise on Warfare Volume IX

A Treatise on Warfar Volume I
The Nature of Warfare

by 

Thordan Ironheart


Warfare is a tool of last resort. To enter into a situation intent that warfare is the only solution is to already have lost. Like all tools warfare has a proper application and use. The only objective of warfare should be a tranquil, just, and lasting peace.

The book give in depth insight to the philosophy behind warfare as a tool and as a concept.

Bow-Any type

Fishing Arrows-Come in stacks of 99, sold at the Craft Vendor.

Once you have a bow and fishing arrows, all you have to do is equip the bow and arrows into their inventory slots, and then find a school of fish. Once you find fish, right click on the fish object and bash it. You will shoot an arrow, and then you will get a message saying what happens . Sometimes after you shoot your arrow, your character will bend over and act like it is pulling something in. When this happens, your character is either pulling in a fish, or pulling back the arrow he/she shot. If you succesfully get a fish, you will gain XP in the fishing trade.

                                                                     Fishing With a Rod

Fishing with a rod is a bit more complicated than using a bow to fish, but still is not difficult. In order to fish with a rod, you will need...

Fishing Rod- There is only one fishing rod (Quarterstaff), and is available at the Craft Vendor.

Fishing Line- There are three lines available. 10 LBS, 30 LBS, 50 LBS. The line determines the size of fish you will be able to catch. The 10 LBS one can catch the lightest, the 50 LBS one can catch the heaviest. These are available at the Craft Vendor.

Lure/Bait- There are several objects you can use for bait. Some you can purchase, some you can dig and find. Copper Fly Lures, Copper Lures, and Grub Worms are a few examples of bait you can use to fish. If you plan on using worms, you will need a shovel in order to dig them up.

Okay, here is the list on what you have to do in order to fish with a rod...

Buy a fishing rod, a fishing line, and obtain some sort of lure/bait
Once you have the three above, find yourself a school of fish!
Equip the fishing rod in your weapon slot
Right click on your fishing line and use its unique power
Right click on your lure/bait and use its unique power
Right click on your fishing rod and use its unique power, click on the school of fish.
Using those steps, your character should sit down and begin to fish. If you catch a fish, you will gain Fishing XP in CNR.

Once you have fish, you can use them to cook, and for any other CNR recipes they are needed for.

Happy fishing.

But rumor says that not all his soul was used for the ritual, and that part of it remains in his very sword. Vorax, the dwarven lord of battle, lives in a great hall beneath the mountains. He is surrounded by the souls of great warriors, a mighty host at his command. There is a great table in the mountain hall, and continous feasting. The warriors that feast with Vorax often put on martial demonstrations to amuse their lord and the others. 

Vorax himself is a well-built old dwarf, with an immaculate white beard. His scintillating silver and red plate mail is perhaps the greatest armor ever made, a gift from his cousin Dorand. Vorax's battle axe and shield are often bourne by handmaidens that dote upon him. The legends tell tales of Vorax sending his axe or his shield to the realm of mortals where the mere presence of such an item often boosts morale enough to win the day. Vorax's helm is also an artifact of great power, but it was a gift from his brother Sulterio from before their fallout, and Vorax is loathe to wear it unless the need is dire. The helm is often locked away with Vorax's horde until it is needed. 

As the All-father of dwarfs, Vorax is wise and compassionate. He is a champion of justice and good. He is a protector of the dwarven people, and a preserver of the dwarven way of life. His strategy and martial ability are second to none. Vorax preaches honor in battle, through strength of limb and courage of heart. It is dishonorable to slaughter the weak, or slay foes who have surrendered. Though Vorax's enemies are often dishonorable, Vorax's followers must stay honorable throughout, and have faith that virtue will win the day. As such, Vorax and his followers frown upon magic users. Magic is deemed an unfair advantage, a true warrior has no need to rely on external power to defeat their enemies. Magic users themselves are often frail, in a true fight they would perish quickly, but their magic changes the outcome to something unnatural.

One of the pastimes of the inhabitants of Omelas is a card game known as Creatures.  It is simple to play, yet many enjoy the combination of luck, strategy, and planning.  Though shunned by those seeking the more visceral thrills of the combat pits, most residents are happy pitting imaginary creatures against each other. 

The goal of Creatures is simple - defeat your player's avatar.  As the avatars are immobile game pieces with no combat ability, this can be a bit of a challenge.  Instead, cards are played by each side to summon creatures which do battle with your opponent's creatures and their avatar.  When one avatar falls, the game is over. 

An expert player is aware of the game's complexities.  Each creature card has a casting cost, as well as an attack and defense rating.  In order to play the card, you must have enough magic available to cover the card's casting cost. 

Magic is generated by magic generators, created by playing a magic generator card.  You can only play one generator per cycle, which limits the amount of magic you will have available to you early in the game. 

There are no clear turns in Creatures, as both players play cards continuously throughout play.  What limits the speed of the game are cycles.   At the beginning of every cycle, a new card is drawn for each player.  If a player has more than eight cards, one is randomly discarded.  Any magic generators that have had their power used up by casting spells will be replenished. It's also a time when additional magic generators may be put in play. 

At the beginning of the game, each player gets seven cards.  The first move of a game is to play a magic generator.  After the generator begins producing power, you can start summoning creatures.  You can summon as many creatures in your hand as you have magic from your generators.  Gameplay continues until one of the avatars is dead. 

There are non-creature cards you can play as well.  These spells are cast just like creature cards, but instead have a variety of effects on the game.  Read the descriptions carefully.

Certain cards can be sacrificed to produce different effects.  To sacrifice a creature, click on the gallows object to the left of the cards.

Prunilla teaches her followers that a true life is led when tending to the soil under your feet and caring for those who surround you through it. Planting and harvesting are part of a simple cycle, and it is in the care of our people to spice that cycle with happiness and joy. Nurture the land as if it were your body, plant crops as if you were kissing your beloved, and tend them as if you were caring for your own soul. It is those things and those who you bring close to your heart that will bring fulfillment to your life. Family is the foundation of our society, the filling in our pie. If it is not properly blessed with pure love, it will begin to crumble. Thus, endure for those you love. By showing them the purity of your heart, they will survive the hardest of times.

Generally considered to be constructed from the skin torn from a demon, the Rags of Rage are a curious design from a tailor's standpoint.  The actual construction does nothing to aid in armoring oneself, one may even contend that the devious design is instead permissive of attacks on the individual wearing it.  That said, the strange quality of this hide absorbs blows through clever overlapping of material in a rather intricate weave.

The hide strangely burns the skin of all but the most hardy individuals, and for this reason it is assumed that it is derived from some creature of a negative energy reality.  Wearers of the strange hide have also told tales of the hide becoming part of their skin, as though living through their flesh somehow.  This rather morbid thought is typically negated by the same individuals saying that they feel stronger, hardier, and more adaptable to the lands around them.

Several suits of this armor are thought to exist throughout the lands.
A barbaric looking set of armor.

Following the final Losthammer's march against Essrantor with the adventurers who waged the war to topple the pillars of Storm Tower, Essrantor's grasp on many of the trapped spirits was freed, but the damage was done. Another superb example of the craftsmanship of the K'halziras clan of dwarves.  This maul was used by a particular segment of the K'halziras clan defenders, the North Pass Wardens.  The North Pass of K'halziras leads into the Deep, and is known for it's magnificently crafted gates which require a special password to cross.  Nevertheless, the North Pass marked the greatest territory of threat, and the Wardens were highly regarded amongst the clan.

A maul such as this was granted to a Warden during the early stages of their training.  The maul itself was both for offense and defense, and of the latter were the warden's most concerned.  The defenses of the clanhome were most focused to the North Gate, and their soul enemy was always the Azure Menace of the deep pools below.  History knows little of this Azure Menace, though it is said that it would somehow curse the dwarves and the barbarian allies who lived amongst the clan to a lifeless servitude in the depths of the pools.

The length of the maul seemed historically important in this respect, though the reasoning for this is still unknown.  Suggestions have been made that the foe of the K'halziras was such that proximity was the true danger, though this is only speculation.  The maul is extremely large for a dwarf, and it is said the Warden's training circled around this weapon especially.

Leaves glimmer with autumn color on this belt of a curious red leather.  Holding it in your hand, it's colors and very nature provide a warmth to the environment around you.

Who made these beautifully simple belts is unknown, though the two slender eyes carved into the belt's underside betray any condition of anonymity.

It is believed by scholars who have studied these belts that they were created by a follower of Katia to imbue the wearer with a natural sense of direction and balance in the lands around them.  It is known that the blessing of this belt renders the bearer hardier, and more resistant to all energies unnatural.  It is assumed that these were created to be worn by the clerics of Katia.

True followers of Katia often know better however...
A red wrap of a belt, it seems simple yet beautiful in it's design.

Modelled after Beryl's constellation in the sky, seven sparkling emeralds glimmer with a deep and strange purple glow that shimmers and circles around in almost an illusory glow.  Four larger emeralds shine brightly in the center of the other seven.

This type of belt is rare and even more rare to be seen on any race that is not Deep Gnome.  They are granted sometimes as gifts to those races and followers of dieties that find peace with the Deep Gnomes, though this is exceedingly uncommon given the distrustful nature of the Deep Gnomes.

The belts are more often worn by clerics of Beryl, and granted only by the Diamond of Beryl.  Most cases of these rare and beautiful creations being found in other places can most likely be explained as unfortunate deaths by the previous bearer.

The magic of the belt is well known to the Deep Gnomes.  Hunted for ages, these belts serve as magical protection against the oppression of the dark elves of the deep.  Enchanted to defend against the attacks of dark elf assassins or weavespinners, it turns both blade and imprisonment in an eternal resistance against slavers.  The belt itself is magnificent, and is usually worn on the outside of one's clothing.  The beauty of the constellation of emeralds instills a great natural power in the wearer.

The belt itself is a small mithril wrap, which does not flex.  A clasp lies in the back of the belt where it can be fastened around it's wearer.

It is likely that any dark elf, dark dwarf, or aberration of the Deep that attempted to wear this belt would be destroyed by it's magics in any ordinary instance.
A magnificent looking belt, it has 7 emeralds encircling 4 larger emeralds in the center.

Krisial's Armor was an honorary suit of the lightest leathers known by the tailors of Krisial's people.  Krisial himself was a proud warrior defending the people surrounding the lands of Alibor at around the time that the lands withered and the River of Death emerged in place of the once lush and beautiful lands of those islands.

History tells that Krisial shunned the usage of any heavy armor, and was revered as one of the greatest warrios ever known in the region.  This is mostly in part due to the fact that he alone had proven it possible to combat the more typical heavily armored warriors of other lands in just his basic clothing.

It would happen some time late in his life that the greatest tailors and enchanters of Alibor would work with Krisial to develop a suit of armor suitable for the warriors of his ilk.  This wonderful suit of padded silk is the result.  Lightweight and flowing gently over the skin, it allows for an incredibly natural and flowing movement for warriors that pursue the purest means of their arts in battle.  The magics of the padded silks allow for some degree of resiliance to incoming blows, though the focus is clearly on the ideal of deft movement of agile warriors.
This armor is extremely light weight, and  the dyes used on it are a brilliantly contrasting deep red and jet black.  Whoever wore this armor was clearly an epic warrior in his day.

Klinkutter Hogsbreath, the gnomish mage of the swamplands who ultimately fell to his own madness.  This strange creation is imbued with some of Klinkutter's chaos magics, though it retains a quality very different then most of the mad mage's creations.

The Song of Chaos was designed in mind for the bardic magi, who Klinkutter had become quite enraptured by in his later days.  For what reason or by what emotions this occurred, none can say.  Though it is clear by several of Klinkutter's creations late in his life that his desire for a bardic companion was immensely strong.  He imbued this shield with the powers of his chaos magic in a strange fashion.  The shield itself hums with the buzz of chaos magic, but in this buzzing there is strange harmony.  Typically only individuals in tune with the chaos of the lands around them are capable of hearing the strange beauty of it's song, and are capable of finding the tune by which to compliment it's power.
This shield randomly shocks, burns, or otherwise stings you as you hold it.  It appears... tempermental.

The Fiendish String, a terrible device constructed with the woven hairs of shadow beasts from a negative reality unlike your own.

The bow itself is of a strange wood foreign to your lands.  It is as though it exists only as a shadow of your world, a dark shadow draining to all things around it.

The string bears the most magical presence and force of the bow.  It is draining to the touch, and incredibly difficult to pull upon.  The power of the string unleashed however, is a sight to behold.  For as it whips forward projectiles of immense force and strength scream forth towards it's target, wailing their distant death cry as they whistle through the air.

Haggris deemed it without worth if the axe was not put to test, and he found the idea of magics degrading of such a magnificent tool of war.

A curious metal, darksteel is known only to be native in the iron of the Deep.  Much speculation has occured as to the qualities of this peculiar metal, and there is much confusion as to whether it is indeed inherent of the ore used, or if it is simply enchanted by the crafters.

The Preacher's Tower dates back to the year 149 during the race wars of Elves and Humans.  Constructed by holy men of the human armies, an almost fanatical following rallied during these ages under the banner of human dieties.  The shields themselves were constructed for heavy warfare, with no consideration as to the training of the holy warriors, it instead relied on the logic of creating a barrier amongst hundreds of warriors that could advance on the elven warriors using the tactic of pikes through eyelets of the shield's side.  It proved quite effective against the far more agile elven warriors and ultimately, tactics such as these, inventions such as these, and sheer numbers in the face of older, wiser, and more adept armies prevailed.

The enchantments on this shield are minimal, save for a consecration of faith for the holy warriors who wield it.  The majority of it's qualities derive from it's sheer size, which makes it difficult to manuever in battle.

Interestingly enough, these types of shields all but vanished from the human trade, and prior to the boycott of all human products in 229, the dwarven clans acquired the majority of these shields as fine additions to their general defenses.

Styrbjorn Kitleatin fashioned these boots with the help of gnomish mages at the height of his wanderings.

The common name for these boots "Styrbjorn's Boots of Fleetness" describes the boots well, though they are often also referred to as "Styrbjorn's Curse of Fleetness", "Styrbjorn's Flighty Boon", and "Styrbjorn's Boots of the Distant Mind".

These boots are both loved and hated by those who wear them.  The tale tells that Styrbjorn was a dwarven outcast, who had deserted his clan early in his youth to wander and experience the lands that were always distant in his mind.  He was known to have always maintained his eyes on the horizon, insofar as to never maintain his attention on any conversation or matter that was directly at hand and in front of him.

During his wanderings, Styrbjorn befriended a group of Goranite gnomes.  The assumptions made in the tales surrounding these boots is that the gnomes, so creative and so wild in every project they worked on managed to maintain Styrbjorn's interest and prompt the discussion of his old boots.

Styrbjorn was fascinated by the wonders of the items and creations of the gnomes, and begged of them to work with him on creating boots for wanderers that would ever keep them able in their wanderings, never slow them, and never distract their mind from the horizons of wonder beyond.  The gnomes took this ideal, word for word, and set off to create boots that would achieve this goal.  They enchanted the boots with the ability to move freely through the lands, and provided each pair with an inset diamond enchanted with the power to provide them the fortitude and constitution to carry on in their travels.

But with his wishes clearly expressed, they also imbued their boots with a special enchantment.  This enchantment lightened the mind of the wearer, and gave them a sense of fogginess in their immediate surroundings.  The wearers of these boots found themselves less apt to concentrate on their immediate surroundings, or listen to the conversations of those surrounding them.  It made them flighty, distant, and apathetic towards anything but the unknown still beyond.

Many a creature has found their feet inside these boots.  Many have found themselves soon a vagrant traveller, wandering the lands, ever distant and yearning of exploration.  Without a single true to their name, barely surviving and never settling in one place too long, these travellers became what many regarded as 'cursed by the touch of Styrbjorn's Fleetness'.

Many though have found these boot's magics well within their capability to manage.  And while their eyes often cloud in the face of a beautiful sun rising over some distance they've never been, their inherent abilities in concentrating on the world around them finds itself in a happy medium with Styrbjorn's wanderlust.

On Dorand's Hammer what I declare that what I write is true.

I, Dalliac, servant of Dorand, braced myself against the Curse of Firelight Tower and sought to enter it and uncover its mystery of many years.

Fellisax, our scout, found a strange groove in the solid stone and that was all we needed to understand that we had found the path to the tower. The climb was nothing a stout dwarf couldn't handle, even with a heavy burden on his back. I was struck at the ability of the stone cutters that wrought the steps - a staircase invisible in the mountain to all except those that know what to look for, The Master of Crafts must have been proud of his son's work.

We reached the lower entrance to the tower, a stone door tightly shut that granted us entrance upon being pressed in the right spots - another sign of the fine ability on our ancients. Smooth as the finest glass was the surface despite years of water and wind daring break on its surface. The three of us entered the tower and sealed ourselves in from the bitter wind outside.

The air was calm but not still, a cool breeze, much slower than the gale that blew outside, greeted us. The floors were with a thin layer of dust, much less than we expected, as though only a few weeks of sweeping had been missed. Along the walls, several stone hooks were set for equipment and Jaellax, our strongest arm, absentmindedly placed his pack on one of them and called out for mead. I spat out my disapproval of such wanton disrespect for the mystery to which he responded, "I feel as though there are still brothers here."

That was also the feeling that I had, along with Fellisax. The place was in excellent conditions and further exploration of the barracks, mess hall and observation deck held the strong feeling that the guard had just stepped out for a smoke and would be back soon. We found salted meats, cheese, water and firewood - all frozen but still serviceable after defrosting them. Barrels of ale, wine and rolls of smoke weed neatly stashed and also usable - the ale didn't age well but the wine did, a bottle of it lies on my table.

I searched and found the tower's register and the commander's log for signs of its being abandoned but found none, it was as though Dorand and Vorax themselves whisked the guard away into thin air for some secret purpose.

It was in the lower basement, within the mountain, that the mystery that had been taunting us was solved. A stone door, crudely cut - definitely not by kinsman's hands, not by those that had built the tower, was found ajar. Jaellax's curse and wards were heard echoing in all the tower for what he saw. In that room, probably a crude cavern that had been enlarged, the frozen and decayed bodies of twenty five was found but only twenty two of them were of our kin, the others were of elves, dark ones for their hair was white and the remaining skin was coal black.

From what we guess, the elves had stolen the guards and killed them in that room for reasons unknown. After eliminating the guard, they simply withdrew through a door set in the back of the cavern without taking a thing nor any of the fine weapons and armor. On close inspection, Fellisax declared that he could not and would not even try to open the drow door for it was, according to him, rigged with the deadliest of traps so we let it be as we recovered the bodies of our fallen and gave them a proper burial and sealed the cavern for good after leaving a few traps of our own for the dark elves.

We left a few days later and until this day we cannot understand what the purpose of the massacre was.

On Dorand's Hammer what I declare that what I wrote is true.

As a gift to his lifelong friend, Lagros put much time and effort into the creation of this magnificent blade. Elmander Luyrin'ahl, a Gray Elf of noble blood, was the recipient of this gift - a sword worthy of one of the best swordsmen the world had ever seen.
Elmander wielded "Gar Thnzoak" in the final battle against his dark skinned brethren, when he and his brothers and sisters in arms drove the last remnants of the cursed kin, who would later come to be known as the drow, into the depths of the earth.

After Elmander the sword was wielded by his son Lysindel, a restless soul and a traveller. It was Lysindel who at long last left his ancestral lands behind and turned to a life as adventurer, driven by his curiosity and hunger for adventure.

Also known as the Epic Adventurer's Robes, these robes are commonplace amongst the greater mages of the lands.  Though the history of this style of robe is unfortunate.

It was a young mage under the guidance of Moraken who discovered the ability to infuse her garment with the energy of a magic missile. With unexpectedly powerful results, her garment became a popular black market commodity amongst a less amiable breed of customer, the Black Mages. When Moraken discovered one of his pupils had been dealing with the Black Mages, he banished her from  his tower.  The student attempted to regain her honor by making more of these robes to grant to the dragoncalled adventurers of Ozlo's age, so that the good in the world might have the power of her weave as well.  Unfortunate, when the Black Mages discovered that 'their' magical robes were being sold to outsiders, they caught her and had the her roasted slowly over an open flame.
