Thou shalt keep thyself chaste for the sake of her whom Rofirein has chosen for thee to love.

Thou shalt only step foot in Temples dedicated to Rofirein and his Holy allies, unless thy enemies seek sanctuary in an unholy temple, in which case it is thy duty to cleanse the place of their filth.

Thou art a Paladin of Rofirein, one of his beloved few. Remember this in all that thy do. As one of the few Paladins of the Holy Order of Rofirein, it is your task to root out evil, injustice and tyranny wherever thee may be.

A fragment melded into the evil the now controls it - this is an abomination of Iliarial's Helm, the helm held to the heir of the great line of kings bearing it's name.  The magics imbued in this helm were once filled with a pure and lawful goodness, and only those pure of heart would at one time ever wield such a helm.

Inside the helmet are ancient runes that only the most wise of lorekeepers can discern.

"For he who wields this great power shall be keeper of our people, defender of our faith, and shall he preserve our customs.  Honor find you lord, and may the great gold find justice in all betrayals on this power."

Justice however, has not been found.  This helm and others like it represent the shattered power of Iliarial and everything good the powerful kingdom stood for.  Defiled and beyond despair, the ruins and their omnipresent evil are represented well by this horrific helm.
This helmet glows a deathly cold beam in every direction.

*This ancient tome stands prominent to all who pass.  The words are familiar somehow, almost magic in nature, for you find that as you read it, no matter your race or ability.... the letters brighten in familiar script as you read, appearing then vanishing as you read over them.  The tome vibrates with a deep power, crumbling with the burden of the ages, though withstanding time far better then the ruins about you.  It reads...*

Cursed is he who does not honor our customs and justice shall be as swift as our lord's blade allows.

Honor our people as you would honor your own, know our customs and we shall learn to know yours.  Forget not the laws of our righteous lord, do not betray that which you must respect.

Cursed is he who would not walk the path of honor.  For it is under their raised honor that he shall find himself an ally.

Cursed is he who knows only greed.  For he who dares covet their glory shall know their sacrifice.

Cursed is he who does not honor knights fallen.  For he who dares step beyond the stones of honor shall see their wrath.

Fall shall he who honors not our King.  Show deference, and approach closely do not.  Show respect and honor, and walk always as allies.  For our lord above shall be always watching.

Known shall he be for he shall retreat from darkness, known from the beginning shall those weak of heart become.  And by the strength of our lord shall you fall.
The eyes of this great lord are lost behind a fire of the coldest hell imaginable.  His soul is fully broken.
Broken Soul of King Iliarial XII
The now fallen spirit of Vreliaxia.
Lord Iliarial IX.  Whatever you have done to dishonor his people's customs, it now has this spirit bent on your demise.
Oppression and cold of a truly lost kingdom.

These are what remains of a halfling or elf.  There is little left around these bones, though tattered blank peices of yew paper lie on the ground beside them which would probably crumble if touched.  The bones exude a strange cold, and you are certain you can hear an ever distant scream as you look upon them.
This door seems to require an intricate looking key to unlock it.  It's design is clearly that of men.

This pool of chilling liquid stands disturbingly still, as though not used for centuries.  The cold flowing outward from this strange device is gravely disturbing.  As you look around the room, you are able to discern the basic process.  At the corners there lie cages and racks, with strange blue stains on the floor around them.  Groved into the floor there are channels flowing down towards open drain grates surrounding the pool.  Above the pool there is a brightly burning fire, and above the fire several cages, some still holding the skeletons of what appear to be men and women.  The cages have sharp spires pointing inward towards where the skeletons lie.  This entire display appears to have harvested the blood from these victims, which would appear as standard torture save for one aspect....

Screams erupt from the pool, and ghostly faces of men and women stream forth from the brightly burning fire, their faces moving and in clear anguish.

The cold pouring from the pool is painful to all who approach.

This demon's eye's flash with delight when it see's you.  It seems to measure you, gazing at you from top to bottom before it's sickening teeth are shown bearing a sadistic smile.  It is a strange demon, for its eyes burn with a fire within, though its skin drips with an ancient cold, oddly similar to the ghosts you've seen.
This ancient key glows with the power of the spirit portal.

A powerful tool of magic, this scale was ripped from the corpse of an ancient black dragon.  The powers of this scale are strange, though most magic using individuals can quickly harness the powers intrinsic of them without difficulty.

This particular scale seems to hold the natural powers of the dragon's fortitude.

This massive portal pours evil from it's center.  Images of the abyssal planes reflect from the chilling portal, and it's destination is quite clear.  Around the rim of the massive device similar runes once again appear as you look them over:

" For our lord Iliarial XII, a gift to forever test his righteousness in the face of great evils.  May the power of Rofirein see him through the greatest test that I, Hraykirlar, Sage of Iliarial have created in Rofirein's honor.  May I always be remembered for this service to my people.  For they, the honorable and just, shall never forget the face of evil, nor the eternal battle we must maintain.  Virtue and Honor.

Hraykirlar Ulitar VII   "


The truth of these ruins becomes more apparent then ever as you gaze at the device.  Though there is something still that is confusing about this portal.  It is obvious that the cold aura dripping from the ceiling is indeed using the sourcepool in the torture chamber... a strange notion even for the most disturbed of sages.  Their is an obvious link to the souls of men feeding this device, though it it quite unbelievable that one of their own created it as such.

Cold evil pours forth from the portal, and it appears that it could be destroyed with blunt force.  No doubt the denizens of this hellish ruin can and will reconstruct the path to their dominion, though destroying it seems the clear choice of any good being, no matter how painful it might be.

This small shard from Hraykirlar's abyssal portal still exudes a piercing and evil cold.  The connection it holds to the planes is obvious, as any focus on this shard of magic seems to cause it to spiral into its own small portal to the planes.  Great care should be taken with this relic of ancient mistakes.
This altar seems a remnant of some sacrificial offerrings.

The sounds of grinding stone echo through the air as this statue of stone sword and armor wanders the ancient ruins.  This particular statue appears to be different then the others, an honorary statue of sorts.

The once embattled being has come to full power.  A union of the death and undeath and power of the strands it bridged to come here... it's quest is complete.  The power of Iliarial now fully broken, this being rises in full glory as the King of this broken land.  As you gaze for too long, it's eyes pierce into your lesser mind.  This strange planar being seems to control all evil beings surrounding with complete authority.
Lihariatoxilal, Lord and Keeper of Iliarial's Souls
Cut from the finger of the devious planar being Lihariatoxilal, this ring holds a fraction of his incredible mastery of magic.
This portal has air gusting upwards oddly, and you see a skylight shining down from above.

The inscription upon this altar is unreadable and in a terrible script that only the darkest of fiends might understand.  The skeletal remains of three humans rest at the feet of 4 statues.  One elven archer, one human bearing a rapier, a cloaked elf carved from pure obsidian, and a dwarf holding what seems to be a statue of a slain warrior, in the armor of King Iliarial.

Fresh blood covers the alter and it is clear some manner of sacrifice is made on a regular basis in reverence to this strange and very out of place monument.

*Around you lies rubble.  Rubble from a defiled statue, now emanating a deep and dark aura of cold and despair.  The runes written along the statue's base still illuminate ever so faintly in the now familiar and magical lettering of this ancient culture*

Vreliaxia, guardian of our great lord, keeper of the temple.  May she be remembered for all eternity as the defender of the lord's honor.  May she be honored in turn by all blessed by her memory.

*The shattered peices of the statue depict a heavily armored woman, regal in position and expression.  Tattoo's of a golden dragon glimmer on the remnants of her bare arm.  The fingers of her hand lie shattered on the ground, grasping at the blade that is no more.*
A deep and dark curse now lies over what was once holy.

*Inscribed in a curious script that once again glows through as you read it*

HONOR


*The script is unreadable beyond this label, but you are able to discern dates using a timeline unfamiliar to you, perhaps before the great cataclysm.  Images of a dragon seem to shine randomly over this pillar*
A sad and shattered head of a once proud statue.

*Inscribed in a curious script that once again glows through as you read it*

KNOWLEDGE


*The script is unreadable beyond this label, but you are able to discern dates using a timeline unfamiliar to you, perhaps before the great cataclysm.  Images of a dragon seem to shine randomly over this pillar*

*Runes written along the statue's now shattered base illuminate in the now familiar and magical lettering of this ancient culture*

Hraykirlar the Wise, High Priest of the Cathedral to our great lord.  May all who behold his image have the wisdom to match his pursuit of knowledge.  

*The shattered remnants of this statue lay still, a deep cold surrounding*

*Runes written along the remainger of this defiled and broken statue's base illuminate in the now familiar and magical lettering of this ancient culture.*

Lord Iliarial IX, defender of our people.  May he be remembered and honored by all in his defense against the wyrms of the skies opposite our lord.  Uphold the swift hand of justice that was stilled only by the great red.


*The peices of the shattered statue depicts a lightly armored king, both hands clutching weapons that are nowhere to be seen.  A golden circlet around his head bears the crest of a golden dragon which still glimmers in the otherwise dark and desolate chambers of the fortress.  A deep cold hovers over the remnants.*
A dark curse hovers over this defiled site.

*Inscribed in a curious script that once again glows through as you read it*

JUSTICE


*The script is unreadable beyond this label, but you are able to discern dates using a timeline unfamiliar to you, perhaps before the great cataclysm.  Images of a dragon seem to shine randomly over this pillar*
Smoke and fire flare from this beasts nostrils.
Distant, lost... these terrifying spirits exude a deep and forgotten coldness.
Impressively poisonous predators.  This one seems large.

Where these horrific beasts come from only those who lived and died in this ancient culture can say.  Cunning predators, it is uncertain if these beasts moved into the ruins before or after their great fall.  The cling to the walls moving about like spiders, then suddenly vanishing from sight to emerge on their prey.
Weathered, sparking from loose ends, and moving slowly from the sand of ages in its machinery... this golem is still quite daunting somehow.
Distant, lost... these terrifying spirits exude a deep and forgotten coldness.  This spirit bears an aura of corruption moreso then the others.
The sounds of grinding stone echo through the air as this statue of stone sword and armor wanders the ancient ruins.

The Hood of the High Courts, also known as a hood of persuasion, is a common tool of political figures on Mistone.  The first of these hoods is said to have been sewn and enchanted by Moraken during the campaign against Sinthar Bloodstone.  It is also said that it was Ozlo, the bringer of the dragon called, who requested these fine silken enchantments be offered to the heroes who would fight against Sinthar.
The key given to you by King Iliarial XII.
A distant spirit, the king looks upon you without hostility.
This being seemingly floats about this strange tower in the forest.

You are fairly sure the cracks in the wall here are climbable.  It seems quite difficult however as you'll have to bridge off the tower using just your fingertips in the thin seam of a crack.  The fall seems a less then friendly plummet into the ocean crashing below as well.
And you thought climbing up was bad...

*This statue is covered in old crusted blood.  Below the scolding figure the following is inscribed in lettering similar to the ancient tome you noticed on the coastline.*



            For he who knows no faith shall see no pity.  
                       May our honour be defended.

A fragment of this cursed remainder drives from a once holy blade which was granted to the Kings Iliarial, I through XII.  It is an immensely powerful relic of this ancient civilization, and the powers of it's just cause are felt by all surrounding.

The now defiled runes of the original masterpeice of righteous good and honor shine brightly with a fire of hatred, an abomination of what this blade once stood for.
A holy sword with depictions of dragons in flight towards the tip of the blade.

Hraykirlars Blessing Belt, a strangely powerful belt emitting magics of goodness and blessing, but holding a strange and dark sadness to it's leathers.

It is uncertain why this beautiful and massively powerful relic has such strange emotions tied to it's weave.  Only those understanding the ruins of Iliarial would ever understand this it seems.
A strange belt... clearly magic in nature.

This tainted blade is a smithed shard of Vreliaxia's Silver Sword, a fabled blade of it's time, this blade was once wielded by one of the greatest knights defending the honor of the Kingdom of Iliarial.

The blade itself is mithril in making, though a strange and flowing silver seems to glimmer on it's edges, holding magics that will forever be unknown to most.

It was once said that only the true of heart might wield the blade that Vreliaxia the paladin of Iliarial once held.  Now though... fragments of her old blade have been forged with the curse she and her kingdom have been forced to bear for the mistakes of the forsaken defilers.
A mithril sword lined with a strange flowing silver.

Pulled from the corpse of an ancient abyssal wyvern, this strange piercing stinger still maintains some of the magics of the planar creature that bore it.  It glows a faint and shimmering red, and is warm to the touch.  When you look at the reflection of the strangely metallic object, it seems you are looking at a mirror of yourself, though it seems to be anticipating your actions a few seconds from now somehow.
This massive wyvern seems to have taken domain of this watchtower.  A massive key can be seen hanging around its neck.
Goblin Hunterseeker of the Shrieking Stone Clan
This seems to be a well outfitted little goblin.
Goblin Scavenger of the Shrieking Stone Clan
Goblin Blackwing of the Shrieking Stone Clan
Troll God of the Shrieking Stone Goblin Horde
Massive with cords of muscle wrapping around it like veins of iron within stone.  This unintelligent beast knows little outside of hunger and fear.
This boat lies on what seems to be a rather large lake.  On the horizon a mist of snows can be seen, and beyond that great towers of stone and ice rising from the mists.
While quite slow in their movement, these strange serpents seem quite adept at staying alive given their unique characteristics.  Their eerie gaze chills even the most stout of beings to the bone.
An elite guardian of Hadrian Hilkraken, usually tasked only to either the defense of their lord, or to a mission of grave importance.
Hakrax, the king of the mighty Hakrax stone giant clan.
A well armored and equipped stone giant.
This stone giant looks quite hardy.
The weave flows strangely around this stone giant.
The earth trembles beneath the feet of this weave dominating stone giant.

The Healer's Hands are intricate gloves designed by Aerindite missionaries.  These gloves were created in the midst of the tragic plague that gripped Hurm around the date 1400.  With the pestilence of the plague leaving so many cursed beyond the abilities of any healer, these gloves, while wonderful in design, proved to be mostly futile.
This is a proud looking dwarf, though his eyes only hold fury.
Wha' kin ah deh feh ye strangeh?

Aye kin... yeh know wha teh deh.  Ahl bring yeh dahn aht of formalehty an' all tha.  Yeh jus' let meh know when yehd lahk teh come back seh ah kin make suh yeh make it aht alraht.  Fahn teh have ye kin.
Ter sumtin wrong 'baht yeh... canneh put meh fingeh on it.  But alraht.  Jus falleh meh dahn inteh the citeh.  Ah kin bring ye back up afteh yeh dun.  Nae funneh business!
Well ain ye teh mos wee litteh thing!  Look at yeh all wee lahk seh!  Mah mah *chuckles*.  Righ' righ'.  Jus falleh meh dahn inteh the citeh.  Ah kin bring ye back up afteh yeh dun.
*He shakes his head firmly* Nae... tat ain happenin' on meh watch wit sumthin like yeh.
Righ' ten.  Jus falla meh dahn inteh the citeh.  Ah kin bring ye back up afteh yeh dun.
*Accept the ride he offers on his shoulder and let him bring you down*

This strange spectre of a being is unnatural and distorted.  From what hell of an existance it derives from, it's presense is tainted by something resonating in chaos with our strand.  It's features are clearly human, and aged unnaturally.  But it's presence is betrayed by a new core of a strange planar spectre.
A good place to cook some fish.
This appears to be a passage to the hull of this shipwreck.  You can hear music from inside.
This tavern seems freshly built, and a nameplate near the door says "Sallaron Tempest".
These cushions seem quite comfortable looking.

A fallen human of the Ice Marches of the Spikes.  What battles amongst tribes waged in times long past is lost in history.  All that remains are the faces of the dead, floating beneath the ice, awaiting the living to awaken their tormented being.

A solemn but kind looking man.  It at first appears that his garb is simple, though the lingering eye will note the extremely fine materials used in everything on him.  His skin bears that tatoos of many military events in Layonara history, and on his forearm the symbol of the Defenders of Prantz during the final age of the Bloodstone wars is quite clear to you.
This is a very large key.

Another superb example of the craftsmanship of the K'halziras clan of dwarves.  This cloak was worn by a particular segment of the K'halziras clan defenders, the North Pass Wardens.  The North Pass of K'halziras leads into the Deep, and is known for it's magnificently crafted gates which require a special password to cross.  Nevertheless, the North Pass marked the greatest territory of threat, and the Wardens were highly regarded amongst the clan.  Perhaps the only dwarves more highly regarded then those that defended the northern gates were the Deepsoul Hunters, which were known to actively delve into the Deep from the northern passages by themselves.  Typically rangers, well trained stalkers of what lay beneath the clanhome, the Deepsouls rose from the ranks of the Wardens to become the lone hunters of the depths, and as such, wore this cloak in their duties.

The cloak is woven from a strange silk, likely spiders from the Deep.  It is surprisingly difficult to feel on the shoulders, and allows superb mobility without any hinderance at all.  The pattern inside the cloak is said to be a K'halziras rune of movement, and while not granting powerful enchantments such as the freedom magic, it is said to make the wearer quicker on their feet.
The key to the outer door of the Crescent Moon & Shield Clan home.

He looks at you with sharp, peircing eyes, discerning your every intent.  His face is frail, as is his body, though he looks poised like a whip, as though there is something within that moves the frail bones.  Shadow dances about his footsteps.
This being is unnatural.  It looks nearly dead, though it's movements flicker faster then your eye can keep focused on.
The flesh stripped away, this is what remains of Iriliax.

Encapsulated within the dark crystal atop this magical staff is the eye of a black dragon.

It is unknown what dragon this came from, the eye is quite small so the assumption is that it was retrieved from a young dragon, most likely still under the watchful eye of it's mother.

The magic inherent of a dragon has been used in conjunction with quite powerful enchantments to create this potent staff.

It is unlikely that others like this exist, though considering the maker is unknown (for good reason given the implications), it is possible that there are others like it.  The general craftsmanship and design are indicative of relics created during the time of Bloodstone's wars against dragonkind.  It is quite likely this powerful artifact was created by one of Bloodstone's minions.

This staff was passed down the line of the Krakaria family beginning with Sivious Rexigal Krakaria.  The legacy of Sivious upon the Krakarian noble family is such that his actions against mankind ultimately forced a wedge between the Boyer royalty and the Krakarian family, thus resulting in their silent exile to the mountains ouside Willow's Weep.  While not remembered fondly in this aspect, his powers in magecraft have been respected and honored by the Krakarian family despite their less then benevolent nature.

The shimmering wail of Scilia's tear drifts through your body in harmonic waves, from your neck down your spine and weaving out until it hits your fingers and toes.  It is a strange sensation mized with emotion, one of known anguish but realized wisdom.  A chill passes through you constantly as the harmony of this magical weave wraps itself around your soul.

Scilia's Tear, a relic of the Krakaria family that has been held in a mysterious but fearful regard for generations.  It sat in a beautiful casing on a headless female model behind a thick window of fine glass for centuries before now.

The cursed but wondrous magics of this fine cloth passed through you the moment you placed it around your body.  After falling unconcious to the ground, your party of friends and close allies watched in fear as a searing light emerged from your right arm in a powerful display of magic seldom seen.  You now bear the scar of Scilia's Tear upon your right arm for all eternity.

The tale of this armor was inscribed within your conscious mind from the terrifying moment that you placed it on your body.  

Cursed you are until the day you find the soul mother, with the burden of the final robe of Scilia Vrilin Krakaria, a sorceress of fantastic power in the Krakaria family lineage.

Born unto greatness in the arts of sorcery and manipulation of the weave, Scilia excelled in all facets of magic through to her adult years.  She held no great love for any one man, but in the effort to maintain the name of her family, she took upon herself a child to bear, of a man she would never again see.  Scilia was a great women in many ways, though her heart was cold and calculated for most of her life.  That is, until her son Likisir was born.

Likisir was a different breed of man from the day he was born.  Kindness showered down on all who surrounded him, and his ability to love and to heal all in need, even in his youngest years... it softened the heart of Scilia to a state of utter content and purpose.  She would support his benevolence in spirit by sending him to school with the Aerindites, and in her great love for the boy she would travel along with him in his youthful studies.  As the tale you know within your heart unravels is a sad ending of anguish and dark purpose.  Likisir was slain, robbed, and left with little more then a young shattered body outside the very small settlement of North Point at that time.  This was done by a man he had thought wounded on the roadside, the sad truth of the petty villain not made apparent until the first dagger struck Likisir's side.

Scilia's world collapsed in that instant.  She had never held the benevolent soul that her young Likisir had helped her find, and her most terrible of sorcery's powers unleashed itself upon the lands when her young boy was brought to her, long since dead, and barely an image of what she had loved.  Several gypsy's were brought in in the search for the murderer, but justice of simple systems was not hasty enough in Scilia's great fury.

She would roam the lands for weeks after, evoking the powers of the weave so dark that only those truly devoid of compassion would attempt.  All fell in her path, any traveller that looked the part of a wandering or disguised gypsy.  Her conviction was unmatched, though her goal without end or hope.

The resolute madness of Scilia Krakaria found her to her demise in a short amount of time.  When they found her broken body, she still wore the garb she had worn on the day her dead and blood crusted son was handed into her sorrowful arms.  The garb had changed however, the blood of her son, the sorcery in her veins, the conviction mixed with enraged madness... it had fallen with her.  Blackened a color of ancient blood that holds no color, chilled by the mixture of her emotions and powers.  The magical fibers of the once beautiful dress had soaked in all that occurred in that short period of time.

The enchantment of the garb is such that you remember her chilled heart, you feel the cold along the fibers of the threads.  You remember her anguish as a distant memory.  Though above all else, you hold a fragment of her absolute conviction.  The strange whispers of her resolution of revenge vibrate along you bones.

You remember the day she carved the tearing eye on her arm, with the blade of the first gypsy she had slain.  Dark promises she made with that mark, dark promises mixed with powerful enchantments... you sometimes feel the sting of the blade along your own arm where you too share the same mark.

The fibers of the garb wrap tightly on your skin.  The curse of her powers is so great that you are unable to remove it.  The fibers and precious metals that once shined with a brilliant sapphire sparkle are now the deepest emptiness of black, and can never be recolored or reshaped in their curse.

The powers of Scilia's final act of great magic, however, imbue you with her strength and conviction.  It is not just the chill you feel or the whispering of her promises.  The fibers of the garb empower you with their strange but wonderful curse.  The pain you feel the cloth feels, and in turn whispers with great power upon any who harm you.  The strange and distant knowledge of Scilia's demise flows through your body like it was once your own pain.  The killing curse of the great wailing is almost petty to the wail of Scilia that you have now heard and feel inside.

Your conviction is greater then ever in your tasks, but Scilia's cold shall forever now chill your soul.

An Aerindite priest, Dhalgrin Linbahr wandered the lands in a manner that most would deem aimless.  Yet for Dhalgrin the aim was clear and along the curious metal running around the wrist the following is inscribed:

The path of healing is not bound by direction.

The gloves are smooth and gentle to the touch despite being metal, and glimmer with a subdued greatness inherent of the selfless priests of Aeridin.

The blessings on these quite old gauntlets are reportedly made by Dhalgrin himself during his early years as a priest of Aeridin.  They were last reported bought by a member of the Krakaria family in the Boyer Kingdom.  The purpose of their acquisition is otherwise a mystery.

How Hengrid's Equalizer came into the possession of the Krakarian family is quite well known and documented by in their annals of Krakarian lineage.

Sivious Rexigal Krakaria came upon this curious weapon of war by killing it's owner.  A mage of terrible power Sivious ultimately drove a rift between the Krakarian family and the Boyer Kingdom, resulting in the Krakarian exile to the mountainous regions outside Willow's Weep.

Sivious found the weapon quite curious in his utter inability to wield it after retrieving it from the dead dwarf's body, and was further fascinating by the searing burn on his fingers upon even grasping it with his bare hand.

In his studies he found that Hengrid Thornflail was the previous keeper of this relic of flails.  This dwarf had once been a defender of a dwarven clan preceeding the Runic Anvil.  In his search to unfold the magics of this flail, Sivious found only that the nature of it's power lies in what appears to be Hengrid's life tale of distaste in the outcomes of battles involving righteousness on both sides of what most call good and evil.  It is hazy what turn of events spiralled this dwarf into his ambivalence in regarding the preachings of war, though Sivious has documented some research on his history.  It is clear that whatever these events were, they had involved the death of his family at the hand of an enemy that his clan had sought out war against for no reason save for their religious inclinations.  They caused this dwarf to adopt a great hatred of all preachings of war based on religious differentiation, and in the end he left his clan alone, without any surviving family of blood relations.

Sivious also uncovered that Hengrid's journey's following his departure led him to become a hunter of what he deemed religious fanatics, in particular the paladins of toran and the unholy champions of pyrtechnon and corath.  While the dwarf was not evil at heart, his hatred of blind faith amongst these sorts did lead to the killing of many paladins, but moreso did he hunt down the unholy champions of the lands and their ilk.

This flail was enchanted in an unknown manner, but it's magics seem consistent with the dogma of neutrality that Hengrid held dear in his later years of demise.

The magics of this flail are such that it can never be altered by conventional crafting means.

Belatrin Xavius Krakaria was an outcast of his own family.  Discontent with the stringency of the Monastery and the expectation by his kin to continue in their footsteps of teaching, he left the school around the coming of his 15th year on Layonara.

Belatrin would wander the lands for 50 years before perishing at the hands of a band of mercenaries somewhere on the isles of Vanavar.

A ranger and a wanderer, Belatrin worshipped many gods of nature, but thought mostly of the wisdoms of Folian Spae.  This aspect of his life made him quite an anomoly of the Krakarian family, most likely part of the reason for his sudden and early departure.

In his travels and through his prayers to Folian, he was blessed with the powers that now lie in the thin strand of this bowstring.  The blessings of wandering, of moving with grace through the world have found their way into the magic of this bow, and it is said that those who wield it are able to move so gracefully through the lands that world itself seems to slow around you.

This bow is the sole possession that still lies in the Krakarian family from Belatrin.  It is said that he came into and left the world with nothing more then he needed, and at his death this is all that remained.  His nephews Jilirid and Oprion would ultimately seek out their lost uncle to discover his old bow in the hands of the same mercenaries on Vanavar... it is said that all blood relatives of those who they killed have since perished.

Whether that would've been the wish of the simple wanderer Belatrin will never be known.

One of the oldest suits of armor in the Krakaria family lineage, Uril's Plate belonged to a battlepriest named Uril Krilin Krakaria.  It is written in the annals of the Krakaria family lineage that Uril was a warpriest of Vorax, and while unusually small for a human, his girth was more like a well fed dwarf.

Uril fell during the late race wars following the cataclysm, and this ancient armor is all that remains of his short lived legacy.  It is said to be inbued with the divine blessing of his lord for his fearless nature in battle.  This fearlessness ultimately led to a short life, though of his lord's pride Uril could be confident.

Northwind Howl, a relic amongst skalds.  Oprion Helius Krakaria was the bearer of this great shield.  A study of the bardic magics from the very beginnings of his teachings within the halls of the Krakarian Monastery, Oprion would ultimately find a distinct distaste in the simplicity of song and seek out the teachings of the northern peoples and the powers of the skald.

Oprion was a clever if not devious youth, his charisma and wit unmatched amongst his cousins and classmates alike.  There was a darkness to his temperment however, a darkness that ultimately found it's closure in the revenge of his lost uncle Belatrin.  The tale is well documented that he and a close and older cousin within the Krakaria family, Jilirid Yilor Krakaria, sought out the source of their uncles demise.

Belatrin had vanished mysteriously from the Monastery nearly 51 years prior, far before the birth of these two young men.  But his tale rang of dissent and misdirection, which the two boys found intruiging in their youthful and reckless manner.

In their searchings, they discovered the fate of their uncle quite near to the time it occurred.  They had tracked him down in a manner of sport almost, for they wished to surprise this strange ranger in their family with their clever seekings.  On the isles of Vanavar they heard that a man bearing only a bow and a small backpack had disappeared into the surrounding woods where bandits and mercenaries were known to reside, and had not been seen since.

The two young men, boys by all measure but their abilities and training in war began their search in the surrounding lands cautiously and in an calculated manner, and it was not long before they found a camp of bandits where a man was strung naked from a treebranch, quite clearly tortured and left to his slow death.

The two approached during the night in great stealth, towards this barely breathing man.  They immediately recognized him as one of their own ilk, and attempted to quietly revive him.  What is recorded in their tellings of the following events is that in his first and last words to these boys he gasped that he did not seek vengeance from the blades of his family.  The boys watched him die, and in a look without words the bond of vengeance was sworn.

Jilirid and Oprion did not return for the following season of their schooling.  They instead began with their dark deeds by slaughtering the camp of bandits and mercenaries around them, ensnaring them in traps before they awoke the next morning, and then promising them freedom if they would simply tell the boys their names.  The boys took their names, killed every last one, and took their oath to every blood relative of the men who had killed their uncle.  They did not rest for three years until they had slain the 94 men, women and children that comprised the bloodlines of Belatrin's murderers.

It is with a great and dark irony the truth in Belatrin's departure from the Monastery and the great distortion of his hopes in breaking his ties by unleashing the family's fury upon so many in the lands Belatrin had grown to love.

This shield was borne by Oprion from the day he left the Krakarian Monastery to the day he died.  It is said that a curse of vengeance lies within the metals of this shield.

In the great tribes of the Krashin northlands a wondrous pride was held in the creation of such blades as these.

Before glimmers a tooth of sparkling blue, cold misting the air around it.  This is a tooth of an elder winter wolf, taken in a ceremony honoring the dead beast by the elders of the barbaric tribes.  The ceremony itself involves prayer to the lord and keeper of the wolves in the gods above, and a continued life of great hunts for both the wolves and the people of the tribe.

Krashin mystics are said to enchant these tooths upon their removal from the mouth of the ancient wolves, using the holy power of the tribal union of men and wolves, both hunters of great prowess and cunning that rely on the common saying amongst tribes that worship the northern wolves in their cultures:

The strength of the wolf lies in the pack and the strength of the pack lies in the wolf.

A very small and extremely beautiful pair of gloves.  Their weave shimmers with a brilliance rarely seen.

Delicate strands of ancient woven ores of mithril, and what seems to be some type of strange silver lace the outer weaves of this smooth silken cloth.  At the wrist of these gloves exquisite rubies of the smallest size dangle in what at first appears to be a tenuos connection to the weave of the glove, though upon inspection, they are quite impossible to pull off as fine mithril strands have been somehow interlaced with the cut of the gem itself.

Upon placing these gloves on one's hands, the fingers immediately vibrate with the energy of the woven enchantments.  It is said by most who have managed, rather been allowed, to place their hands in these tiny gloves that a brief surge of confidence, conviction, and what many describe as a powerful emotion washes over them.

These wondrous guantlets came into the possession of the Krakaria Family by unknown means, but are clearly a prized peice of what this noble family has come to own in its great store of heirlooms and treasures.

The namesake of these gloves is in no way true to it's origin, which is speculated to be as old as the race wars of -1812.  The name they now carry was borne unto a young boy of the Krakaria family who died at the age of 9.  Likisir Haliar Krakaria was murdered at the hands of what he thought an injured gypsy to whom he'd blindly run to aid.  The story recorded in the Krakarian Lineage Annals tells that Likisir was a particularly benevolent young boy, who at a very young age began to study the preachings of Aeridin, and had begun his studies entirely towards ends of aiding those sick or weak.  The Krakarian family fully supported this effort, as in his youth, he was the only of their family to ever find the ability to place his hands in these wondrous gloves they had kept for ages, unused.
They knew the gloves to be enchanted with a power of healing, and encouraged his benevolence and capability in curing those ailing.  In this event however, the boy had apparently been alone on the roads outside North Point, and had run to aid a man injured and bleeding on the ground.  The man slew Likisir and robbed him, though found himself unable to pry the beautiful gloves from the young boy's hands.

What is known of these silken gloves is that they are imbued with an incredible healing power, and that the magics that vibrate within will shimmer and vibrate in the presence of any being that is tainted with a malevolent presence.

The magic of these gloves are such that they may never be altered by conventional crafting means.

This smooth and beautiful cloak was crafted for Jilirid Yilor Krakaria by a Mistite priest who instructed the more talented of the students at the Krakarian Monastery.

He, like many of his cousins, held a strange darkness in his heart however, and it would be with his cousin Oprion that he would find the medium for unleashing the storm upon the world around him.  Oprion and Jilirid would both find the darkness in their own hearts in their search for their lost uncle Belatrin.

This cloak was worn by Jilirid until the day he died, and it still maintains the magics imbued within it's finely woven cloth by his teacher, a priest of Mist.  Jildrid would continue for most his life alongside his cousin Oprion, and bring the tidings of the faith of Mist to the world around him in a powerful, if not oppressive, manner.

Xilidias Granthis Krakaria is perhaps one of the most elusive member of the long lineage of the family Krakaria.  One of the first to bear the name Krakaria, prior to the founding of the Monastery, Xilidias was a wandering mage of neither ill repute nor fame.

It is know he wandered the Dregarian lands alone and aimless, and had some affinity for the art of conjuring.  What he did with these skills, few know.  What is known is that at the end of his life he left two things to his only son, Azirine Janid Krakaria.  One was this helmet.  The second was a massive amount of gold which ultimately funded the the beginnings of what is now the Krakarian Monastery.  None in the family know from where this gold came, they simply know that their status derived from a wandering ancient relative of notable magical affinity.

"In the early days of the rule of Prantz, a company of horsemen were sent into the wilds of the southern plains to make the lands livable by common folk.  A massive drow invasion in the prior century had drawn all of the capitol's attention and left the south, despite being so close, to fall into shadow.  The towns of the southern plains were quickly overrun and the people either fled further south or went missing.  Once the capitol was settled, the horsemen left the gates to reclaim the towns and clear the roads.  In the end, only two made it to the southern tip of the continent.  There they found an impressive and resilient throng of Dregarians living in scattered coastal communities under the constant threat of assault.  

The two horsemen, a twin brother and sister of the Galeright family, rallied these scattered tribes under the flag of the capitol and brought them to the ruined outpost at Lor.  There they rebuilt the town by hand and with primitive equipment.  Still, they rebuilt it and with enough motivation and skill to withstand the swarms of bugbears and giants which crashed against their walls like waves against their stone docks.  Of course the Galeright twins were in front of the walls, meeting each wave with astounding skill and passion.

Rather than return to the capitol, the Galeright twins settled in Lor and brought the king and queen themselves to witness the mighty will of the southerners.  It was a glorious day in the history of Dregar, one that lives in the proud tales of Lorians.  Shortly thereafter, the capitol redirected immense funds and manpower to Lor, sensing it's strategic economic and political significance as well as the sentimental unifying force it had for southern Dregarians."

The truth to the demise of this clan of dwarves is lost to time, though this wondrous shield does hold some clues.

A mithril mold, runes warding magic and death cover the entire face of the shield.  The artistry of the runes is without match, and various gems have been set in the mithril.

Best known as the Lost Clan shield, it is such due to the fact that there is no reported history of the clan that built the wondrous mazes and halls beneath the Thunder Peaks.  The runes however, do uncover some truth.  The writing on the shield is mostly of magical defense, but some is written in the plain dwarven tongue, especially that which is carefully etched around the outer ring of it.

"Our halls he shall never see, for our honor shall survive the thunder of his storm.  Our stone he shall never touch, for our defenders wield the magic of our mountain.  Lost in our maze he shall be, and steadfast behind this shield he shall fall under our mighty hammers."

The inference to the storm and thunder clearly represents the battle with the giants of Essrantor's Veil.  It is interesting, in the domain of antimagic, that the shield is so well imbued to defend against it.  The truth to the demise of this obviously proud and honorable clan may forever be lost to time.

How this shield came into your possession is a mystery indeed, though its roots lie deep within the Thunder Peaks.

But the shield of the lost clan survives.

This is a statue of the elven deity Aeridin, also known as The Healing Light, The Keeper of Life, The Lifegiver, The Caring Light whose dogma is:

Preserve and protect life, the gift to exist is not one to be taken lightly and thus one must lead an exemplary life devoted to benevolence and care. Tend to those who ail, offer your gift of healing to make their stay in the mortal realm a wholesome experience, yet once death has taken its toll, respect the passing and enjoy the fond memories of their life. Do not dwell or mourn for those who pass for too long, death is sadness, but without understanding sorrow one cannot understand happiness.

Promote health and the well-being of the mind and body before anything else. Any extension, transformation, alteration or corruption to the natural forms and shapes of beings is an affront against the sanctity and purity of life and should be confronted at first with gentle lessons and benevolent teaching, and if such ways do not work, with a stern and firm stance instead. Violence is the last option; use it only on those who defy these teachings.

Undeath is the most blatant aberration to the sanctity and purity of life, put them to rest by any means necessary so that their souls may reach their homes. Use the Gift of the Caring Light to bring brightness to the darkest of places, never succumb to its temptations for they only bring a taint upon the spirit.

One. 

Use no magic, because the Al'Noth is chaos and chaos be the enemy of a prosperous people. Use of magic will be punished by imprisonment to be determined by a judge depending on circumstances. This be including pets of mages and things summoned. All who would use magic of any kind and this be including tree-lovers, mages, and the followers of other, lesser gods, must register before entering and before leaving a city under the protection of the Lord of Rael. Failure to do so or being found without proper papers will result in imprisonment of a time to be determined by the courts.

Two. 

Sulterio be the god of this realm. Be respectful of him and do not bring confusion and contradiction to the lands by worship of any other god. This includes shields, icons, flags, and banners. Tattoos must be covered. Display of items of worship not of Sulterio will be punishable by a year of prison. Open worship of a god not Sulterio will be punishable by ten years imprisonment. Leading group prayer to a god not Sulterio will be fifty years imprisonment. Attempting to open a church not dedicated to Sulterio shall result in a lifetime's imprisonment.

Three. 

The worship of Vorax in any form is punishable by death to be dealt immediately when the infraction be discovered. This be outside the courts of the Voices of Justice and on the orders of Lord Rael.

Four. 

Be remembering the Lord Rael is your leader and bow your head in fealty every morning at forge-light and dusk at tamping. Failure to show respect to the Lord of Rael is punishable by one years imprisonment.

Five. 

Weapons are not to be held at any time. This is to include all bows, all standard weapons, and any found weapons like pitchforks. This be a civilized city and brandishing of yon weaponry will be punished by imprisonment for one year. If a found weapon be used for the purposes of commerce, such as yon pitchfork, an Adamantium Guard must be present to witness.

Six. 

You may be speaking common, elven, dwarven, halfling, and gnome only. No other language will be permitted including other-worldly tongues and thieving cants. Speaking a language not supported by the Lord is punishable by a year's imprisonment.

Seven. 

Remember the Lord's Tax and be paying on every third month to the castle or forts. Punishment for refusing is forfeiture of the next quarter's goods or imprisonment to be determined by the courts.

Eight. 

Thieving of anything for any reason is punishable by imprisonment of a time to be determined by a judge and in a place pleasing to the Deep Lord.

Nine. 

Assault of any true dwarf guard or any true dwarf worker of the government for any reason is punishable by life imprisonment. Assault of any citizen of the city will be punished by imprisonment for a time to be determined by a judge and in a place pleasing to the Deep Lord.

Ten. 

All dwarves of inferior blood must register when entering and leaving a city under the protection of the Deep Lord. Papers be issued and any dwarf found on yon streets not properly registered will be arrested and imprisoned for a time to be determined by the courts and in a place pleasing to the Deep Lord.

This reflective blade was designed by a strange group of bandits operating outside of Audiria around the time of Bloodstone's Fall.  Apparently smuggling goods into and out of Prantz since the takeover by General Broegar, these bandits had need for a weapon that would enable them to deal with the guards with sufficient surprise.  The surprise in itself would not be enough, for the goal was not to kill all any guards, but rather conceal the identities of the bandits while letting the guards live.  The intent in this was to prevent any investigation on dead guards that would link the smuggling operations to them, or cause any hassle in their business.  The poison coating the blade here is said to blind an individual on mixing it with their blood, and the scimitar was the most effective slicing weapon they could think of.

This plan naturally failed miserably, as Lord Broegar ultimately found of the smuggling operations and destroyed the bandits in one fell swoop.  The upside to this is of course the numerous blades of this make on the black market.

This torch is carried by the Stormcrest Guides.
A door this large and solid must protect something very impressive or valuable.  Or perhaps the ale inside is just incredibly good.  Who can say?
It is clear many a heavy-plated dwarf has sat on this log as platemail cheek implants now have made for a few comfortable seats.
The water found in this patch is clear enough for refilling your drinking containers.
The wicker bulls-eye of this archery target bears a fresh coat of paint.

*etched roughly into the latern post is the following*

Welcome to the Stormcrest Crossroads.  The tavern is always open for all to find some shelter in, and maybe a drink or twelve.

The torch here is lit by guides when they are in the tavern or at the crossroads and are feeling up for some adventure with a stranger or friend alike.

Cheers.

K. Svadi
A retired adventurer, this dwarven wanderer has found his home tending to the Stormcrest Shack.
A door this large and solid must surely keep the cold out.

Various notes litter this board, mostly messages from coming and going adventurers.  It is interesting to read the spans of time between responses, as those visiting the Stormcrest Shack are ever travelling.

Apparently the story goes that Ketilbjorn contracted an artist to illustrate a setting where he was surrounded by all the women he adventured with.  The tale told these days is that the women were to be illustrated, feeding him grapes off the vine, in less then concealing attire.  All that remains however, is this portrait of a dwarf with tattered edges and several holes, from darts most likely, littering the portrait.
Slightly above your average beer. The best thing about it is the price. If you're looking for quantity over quality this strong nutty brew is the one.

Who wants to drink something green? That is what most say when they see a bottle of Green Forest Draft on the shelf. One taste however and you're hooked on it for life. How the creator came upon this mixture of belladonna and peppermint is anyone's guess. One sip and you can feel it go to work soothing the body and the soul with its smooth minty flavor. It is strong for the novice drinker and it can take ones breath away quite easily. Many newcomers to the drink are heard saying "Smoooooooooth" after that first gulp as they try and regain their breath.

This brew originated in Hlint. A local adventurer would help keep the road clear by hunting and killing the goblin scouts near the Red Light Caves. He would gain a reward from Quartermaster Talon and then spend the night drinking at the Wild Surge. One day the particularly thirsty adventurer with a string of ears could not find the Quartermaster. Sadly he trudged into the Inn complaining about his misfortune. His misfortune turned to fortune when a local brewer asked about the ears. He offered the adventurer ale in return for the ears. The brewer had heard tales about the odd properties in the ears of the goblin scouts. So on a whim he tossed them into his latest batch of pilsner. To the brewers surprise the drink had a smooth and robust flavor that his previous ale had not. The drink became a favorite in Hlint and the brewer grew wealthy. With much wealth the brewer moved away and took the recipe with him. A copy was found in the Great Library of all places and is now available again.

The Creme de la Creme of cream ales this deep red ale is misleading as it flows quite smoothly across one's palate. This sweet and creamy ale adds the perfect blend of fresh raspberries, sugar, and milk to the classic taste of ale. 

This ale, originally a favorite unique to the "Red Crow Tavern", which was once located on the coast of Dregar, successfully made its way across Layonara traveling with ships who set their sails to the winds from the Red Crow. 

Many years later, after the tavern had burned down and has long since escaped the memories of most, the recipe for their most famous drink has lived on. Do not be deceived however by the sweet taste and noble tale this ale offers, for this brew has extremely intoxicating effects.

Flecks of silver dust sparkle and dance in this clear drink. A strong spirit, most will mix it with water or their favorite fruit drink. Typically Dwarves drink it straight... and maybe one well-known halfling.

Why the creator of this drink named it Dead Orc Porter remains a mystery, and a favorite discussion amongst drunken bar patrons as they tip back two or three of them. Its mixture of sweet cherries and tart raspberries is hard to miss. Perhaps the brew master thought the name sounded more exciting than Cherry and Raspberry Porter.

A dangerously lusty red wine with intoxicating effects, this wine is an essential part of Xeenite celebrations and rituals everywhere. 

The key to making this wine is to use only grapes who's vines scale the walls of temples of Xeen. It is said that the grapes that grow on Xeen's temples already have an intoxicating affect even before being made into wine. 

The recipe for this wine is said to be guarded very closely by Xeen's priestesses themselves, and is rumored to have been stolen by one of the proprietors of the Leringard Arms Inn and Tavern after a very prominent Xeenite festival in Katherian. However, not too many people know how much truth is in this tale. If there is any truth to it, those who know, don't talk about it. Truth or not, everybody benefits from the knowledge of this recipe, as it is the finest wine ever made.

The key to making this wine is to use only grapes who's vines scale the walls of temples of Xeen. It is said that the grapes that grow on Xeen's temples already have an intoxicating affect even before being made into wine. 

The recipe for this wine is said to be guarded very closely by Xeen's priestesses themselves, and is rumored to have been stolen by one of the proprietors of the Leilon Arms Inn and Tavern after a very prominent Xeenite festival in Karthy. However, not too many people know how much truth is in this tale. If there is any truth to it, those who know, don't talk about it. Truth or not, everybody benefits from the knowledge of this recipe, as it is the finest wine ever made.

This more common ale has the typical taste of a fine wheat ale but with much less potency than your average brew. Once simply called "Wheat Ale," this particular variety of wheat ale began to be known over time as, "Wizard's Wheat Ale" as it was noticed that wizards would frequently request this drink and carry it with them on long journeys. This bitter golden liquid although flavorful, has a low enough alcohol content that even wizards could handle large quantities of it without forgetting their spells. Perhaps it is the quick processing of this beverage that leads to its low alcohol, or maybe it is the cure light wounds potion thrown in the mix. Either way, this drink has little effect on most and to a dwarf, has no more effect than pure water.
Milk from a cow. This resource may be used to craft other items or to drink.
Apple juice gives this brew it's amber color and delightful flavor. The name is derived from the Axe Head flower, which grows on Alindor in the apple groves.

With holy water right in the mix, it is no wonder this malted liquor is preferred by devout clerics and soldiers everywhere. Originally created in Krandor this brew was said to have gotten its name from the tower close by. Nobody really knows the history of this drink, but it seems that nobody has ever really tried to find out about it either. This is probably because although it is a fair brew, this one is definitely quantity over quality.

This recipe was traced back to its maker who lived on Dregar. He would mix just the right amount of blackberries with almonds. The fellow owned a black stallion, which he rode to Prantz making ale deliveries to the Hotel Layonara. In time his horse became known around Dregar and the drink was named after it. A good thing too as the man's name was Phillibuster McGillicutty and that didn't seem to roll off the tongue as well as Black Horse Ale.

The partial recipe for this brew was found behind a stack of barrels by one of the Leringard Arms Brewers. He experimented with the partial recipe adding other ingredients to develop this dark and bitter malt that packs a punch. A hint of blackberry makes this brew one to try.

A drink brewed using juice derived from the Juniper Berry. This spicy brew was first introduced at the Juniper Berry Festival in Lan's Port on Alindor. The juice is extracted from the berries by jumping up and down in a tub of the fruit. The sweet yet tangy flavor will always leave you wanting more.

An accidental success is the best way to describe Will-O-Whiskey. An adventurer and brew master from Lorax was passing through the Black Dog Moors when he captured the essence of a Will'O wisp. In his haste to contain the essence he reached in his pouch only to find his small whisky flagon. He put the essence inside and didn't give it another thought. After a few hours of trudging through the swamp he sat on a stump, opened his flagon and took a rather large gulp of its contents.  His eyes lit up and his face flushed red. He hurried back home and perfected his new creation. Will-O-Whisky is a very powerful drink that should be sipped or mixed with juices.

This delightful brew compliments the smooth and refreshing tastes of fresh picked, succulent blueberries with a tangy sharp bite, likened to the edge of a sword. Surprisingly misleading, just like its rumored creators, Blue Sword Swill plays tricks on those who drink it. 

The origin of this favorite is said to be the hidden Fairy Shee, lost some place on the continent of Dregar near The Forest of the Mists. The rumor goes that any fool who partakes of food or drink offered by the fairies there will quickly forget his or her purpose and stay and play for the rest of their days. 

Nobody knows for sure just how the recipe for this mystical blue drink traveled from the Shee, but it seems to have lost a bit of its potency. Instead of completely forgetting their purpose, those who drink it usually recover with in a few days.

A dwarven Cleric of Vorax who used to frequent Hlint is rumored to have come up with the idea for this odd drink. After a night of cleansing the local crypts of undead he would belly up to the bar in the Wild Surge, and order a large stein of ale. He would drop a few skeleton bones into it, typically ones from the hand. Then down the drink leaving the bones behind to rattle in the empty stein. The bones seem to take some of the bitter edge off of this brew.

Traveling the mountains of Northern Dregar a man found a cherry tree grove. This man happened to be a renowned brew master.  He kept the secret of where he found the best cherries in all of Layonara for nearly 30 years. When he passed he told his son where to find the cherries and his son sold that knowledge and made a king's profit. Cherry River Lambic is one of the finest drinks in all the lands. Its tangy flavor invites you to have another, and another, and hides how strong the drink truly is. Many have learned this lesson the hard way.

This strong ale was once only served to dwarven nobility, thus it's name. It was only placed at the Kings table, the Head table. This drink first found its way to the general population at the celebration honoring the dwarven champion, Gotak Gungur. Still today when you see a table of dwarves raise their steins you will hear this declaration... "Deathward is fer pansies!"

This strong ale was once only served to dwarven nobility, thus it's name. It was only placed at the King's table, the Head table. This drink first found its way to the general population at the celebration honoring the dwarven champion, Gotak Gungur. Still today when you see a table of dwarves raise their steins you will hear this declaration... "Deathward is fer pansies!"

This recipe was developed by a Dwarven follower of Rofirein long ago. The warriors of Rofirein required strong drink to quench their mighty thirst after delivering justice to the enemies of Mistone. The recipe was given to various inns and taverns across the land so that the Draught of the Dragon would lend courage to traveling adventurers.  One must be careful when consuming this drink however, it's intoxicating effects are said to vary from drink to drink.  Perhaps it is due to the raw eggs used in the brew, one can not be sure though.

A brew master from Rilara was constantly pushing his cranberry ale. However too few cared for the tart flavor it had. After many tries and failures he added a bit of honey and it was an overnight success. The honey took the edge off the tart cranberries and the drink went on to be a Rilaran favorite.

A deep crimson colored lager that is brewed from the finest of fresh cranberries, it hints at another taste that is difficult to place. An old favorite to gypsies everywhere, it is often said that caravans in Dregar could be found brewing this lager by the light of the moon, near blistering campfires that throw off colors that are only matched by the color of the brew itself. 

In the history of this lager, it isn't quite clear whether the gypsies perfected the drink themselves or if it was a stolen recipe from a different source. Nevertheless, the gypsies are often credited with adding the bits of campfire charcoal and fire agate dust to this drink which gives it its wonderful full flavor. 

This strong and full-bodied lager is certain to burn all the way down and leave you feeling grand.

All territories to the west fall under the rule of the Zuan Empire.  Entrance into this territory is at your own risk and is vigorously discouraged by the Raven Trade Company.

No rescue will be arranged for those not heeding this warning under the agreements of non-involvement stated in the Zuan-Raven Treaty.
A carefully constructed marker denoting a point of interest.
The steady rains of the isle have taken their toll on the once fine equipment that was kept on this rooftop.  A lean-to now sits for the errant guard to find cover from the rain under.
I sail under the agreement with the Raven Trade Company to Lor.
Let us sail to Lor then.
I sail under the agreement with the Raven Trade Company, through Vanavar to restock offshore, and then to Nith.
Let us sail to Nith then.
This lean winged fiend looks scrappy and weathered from timeless war.  It's eyes are empty and black.
The eye of this winged watcher bleeds as thought freshly constructed.
A dark and corrupted lust drives this ageless flying fiend.
This light and flexible clothing has been reinforced with mithril fibers to give it more protection than most clothing.

These bracers gleam red as the light reflects off them.  Born from the scales of dragon younglings fresh from their eggs, these bracers are much sought after by both dragons and common beings alike.  The reasons for each kind's search is quite different obviously.

The scales themself sparkle with a faint magic, magic that never saw the full glory of even adolescence.  The scales are bound by cobalt and adamantium, the backside of the bracers are covered with a fine padded silk as to make them quite comfortable on the wearer's wrists.
Cloak Made from a Panther Skin.

This enchanted ring creates a weak insubstantial barrier around the wearer that helps protect against physical attacks.  This fine example can create a more powerfull shield for a limited period of time each day.
Rings are commonly worn on the fingers as ornamentation, but some are potent magic items.

Emerald set in a Silver Amulet
An oddly cut chunk of pure gemstone.
This rope seems to be attached around the base of this small podium for descent into the chasm below.
This rope is clearly unsafe to climb back up on after the long descent to here.
Mithril and adamantium make up this magnificent display of mechanical creation.
These waters have eddies and currents that seem to force a swimmer in all directions.
This gaseous beast approaches, sucking and leeching the air you breath as it does.

Born from the waters of death and decaying, Stillwater elementals are much like their water elemental cousins, save for their origin including those things dead and decaying.  Their form is usually spurting thick oozing waters, blackened by the myriad rotting substances.  Sometimes bones or partially decayed body parts are seen swirling within their dark core.  It is said that their nature is as dark as the death filled waters they derive from, and some go so far as to attribute their existance to powerful necromantic magics.
Hunefers are ancient mummies, embalmed heroes from centuries ago. Their rotting remains regenerate at a rapid rate, carry a vile disease and they can effortlessly summon other mummies to aid them.
This hole is narrow, and slides vertically into the black depths below.  Any light dropped into it will clank in echoes as it fades into the blackness, into silence far beyond your ear's reach.
Perhaps one of the most violent and disturbed souls of all beasts of this strand and the next.
A slimey hole looks to descend under the stillwaters.

This abomination is the result of an ancient line of aberrant insects of Undersea.  It's enormous size is something of precataclysmic proportions... an ancient breed of creature not meant to ever see the light of this age of Layonara.   It is well adapted to this strange and terrible clime, for it floats an immense thorax which keeps it from being swept away by the void of whirlpools in this tumultuous region.

Luminiscent in the deep darkness of the Understraits, these spider-like abberations typically flock to larger creatures more adept in harvesting prey.  These strange creatures are known for their necrotic poison which eats away most forms of living tissue.

An ancient rune carved by a dwarven spirit of the Lost Hammer Clan, this rune can bring up a shield of antimagic around the wearer for a very short period of time.

The fine ore this rune is inscribed in glows faintly with the magic of the rune carved magically upon its face.
Unforgiving yet determined eyes stare intently at her child in this protrait.

We were betrayed. Betrayed by those who we used to call kin. Betrayed by those who were also gifted. A betrayal that will be answered in kind...

*The long text continues in similar phrasing and fashion*

Mother of Darkness I ask for your eyes upon me as I prove my worth to you. Grant me aid in the demise of mine enemies so I can become of greater use to you and your cause. Aid me in the defeat of my obstacles, so I may overcome all in your name. ~Shri'Vrae - Weapons Mistress of Vierdri'ira

Prime Matriarch, cloud the eyes of the enemy in darkness, so that they may walk into my ambush with open eyes and will not know what hits them until they hear the sound of our whips as we bring them their demise.
Many images tie into this mural as it shows scenes of dark elves rising up in all manner of facets.

You came into posession of this armor after defeating the Spirit Guardian of the Valley of the Moons. It allows the wearer to become closer to the spirit world for a period of time each day.

This being moves with a grace as though floating in the winds around it.

This golem is alive with energies unsurpassed in standard golem making.  Hints of the most precious of Layonara's minerals are seen sparkling all over this great creation.  Borni has seemingly found enough time to even draw images of war on the shoulders, perhaps proving the strange gnome's beautiful madness.

This strangely designed ship lies tethered to the rock shore.  Ahead there lies a stream tunnel that widens as it passes into the caverns beyond.  The stream seems to continue for quite some time, though you can't be certain from this vantage as it darkens to a pitch black.

The current of the stream seems such that it will carry you downstream without much effort.
It would appear that the current of the stream tunnel is not going to allow backtracking your path to the coastal caves.
A curtain of golden mesh, it flutters in the winds of the strange isle,
The cavernous lair opens for all willing to swim within.  Waves crash up against the strange fortress, drowning out the sounds of the wind around you in a great showing of the sea's power.
This boat looks as though it could be used to brave the waves back to the main shoreline of the Coastal Crags.
This wild elf looks furious and quite well trained.
This wild elf appears furious and quite capable with the natural weave.
Head of the Leader of the Broken Horn Clan
Adapted over time, this air elemental has come into being with an enhanced natural immunity to most magics.
Primal Air Elementals are the embodiment of the very purest essence of the Elemental Plane of Air. This makes them extremely powerful and extremely dangerous.
Xora's Tower Outskirts to Wildlands Forest 2
This gnome seems jittery to say the least.
This block of stone has dwarven carvings on it.
The sleeping mat is thin but does offer some measure of protection from the cold ground beneath it.
The bear's eyes stare up at you helplessly as its matted fur sprawls out across the floor.
This barrel seems to be filled with simple supplies.  One would think to themselves the awfully poor style it would take to horde everything and not leave anything for fellow adventurers.
This tool is designed to break rock.

This scraggly looking plant reaches out in all sorts of messy directions.  The shoots have long and sharp thorns on them as well as clusters of orange berries which make the ends droop low. The Basics of Armor Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Armor types - There are 7 basic armor types that a crafter can make. These range from a chain shirt to full plate armor.
 
2. Armor Materials - Armor can be crafted from Bronze, Iron, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt and Mithril. Armor may also be adorned with gold. Adorned armor has a higher AC than regular armor. 

3. Armor Components - Armor requires ingots and a pattern.  

4. Crafting Armor - To craft a set of armor, one must equip a smiths hammer, posess the required raw materials and use an armor crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Armor may be smelted. Smelted armor generally yields two less ingots than were originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tailoring, and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Mining
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

In addition to ore, miners may also mine clay and sand. 

2. Mining Equipment - To mine ore, one must use a pickaxe. Pickaxes require the martial weapon feat, so certain non combat classes will have difficulty mining. A shovel is required to mine clay and sand.

Pickaxes and Shovels are subject to damage while mining and will eventually break. it is advised to acquire a backup pickaxe and shovel prior to attempting mining.

3. Misc. Infomation - Ocassionally, one might get lucky and chip off a second nugget of ore or find a rare gem or other  item. 

4. Related Skills - Smelting, Weapon Crafting, Armor Crafting and Tinkering all use ore, sand and clay byproducts. Please read their respective books for more information about them.
The book of patterns contains a large collection of pattern designs used by tailors and armor crafters to make various pieces of clothing and armor.

The Basics of Smelting
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. All may be smelted. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

2. Smelting Equipment - To smelt ore, one must use a smelting tongs. Ore nuggets are inserted into a smelting forge and melted into ingots. 

3. Related Skills - Weapon Crafting and Armor Crafting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Weapon Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Weapon types - There are 21 basic weapon types that a crafter can make. These range from a simple Dagger to a Greatsword.
 
2. Weapon Materials - Weapons can be crafted from Copper, Bronze and Iron. Weapons may also be coated with Silver and Titanium. Silver coated weapons are more effective against undead foes, while Titanium coated weapons do more damage.

3. Weapon Components - Weapons generally require ingots and a casting mold. Casting molds come in small, medium or large sizes. Some weapons also require wood shafts. 

4. Crafting Weapons - To craft a weapon, one must equip a smiths hammer, posses the required raw materials and use a weapon crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Weapons that require 2 or more ingots to craft may be smelted. Smelted weapons generally yield one less ingot than what was originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tinkering, Wood Crafting and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

One of the world's rarest and most coveted gems, alexandrite takes on a brilliant green hue when under indirect sunlight but turns blood-red when exposed to candlelight. Loretellers claim that all alexandrite comes from the body of the oldest son of Silvanus, the Forest Father. A common nursery rhyme goes "Silvanus' wife went mad one night, murdering her child by candlelight."
A gem cutter's cutting and chiseling tool.

As its name indicates, this gem is generally green in color. Typical samples, however, have a pattern of overlapping edges that range from yellow-green to almost black. When polished, they have a beautiful play of light within their crystalline structure.

Fire agate forms in thin brown layers that refract the incoming light, giving the gem its "fire." The refraction often forms patterns reminiscent of a dragon's scales, which makes it prized by sorcerers who claim to trace their lineage back to dragonkin. A well-cut stone has its outer layers polished and ground away until only the fire is visible.
The most valued amethyst crystals are a milky, wine-dark purple.

A singularly beautiful stone, phenalope is dusty pink in color, dramatically marked with black streaks. Even when mounted in jewelry, phenalope maintains a rough texture, pocked with tiny holes that cannot be polished out. For some, this is part of the stone's attraction, and they wear it as a symbol of their own tenacious natures.

Favored by druids for its graceful and natural beauty, malachite is known for its strikingly ornamental bands of light and dark green that alternate throughout the entire stone. Painters have also been known to crush the gem and use it as a pigment. Adventurers have discovered that the gem bubbles and dissolves readily in acid, making it an effective - if expensive - means of identifying certain dangerous substances.

The blue sapphire is twin to the more precious ruby in all respects but color. In most stones, the sparkling blue color must be brought out by exposure to great heat. Once "cooked," the color change is permanent and does not otherwise affect the much-treasured durability of the gem.

Unlike their more common cousin, fire opals are full of vibrant hues: hot yellows, oranges, and reds so bright they almost cast their own light. Some believe that these gems derive their glow from a supernatural source, and not a few sages have claimed that each gem is a tiny portal to the Elemental Plane of Fire. However, scholars claim it is just the way the gem refracts the light around it.

Best known in its pale, orange-yellow form, topaz is an attractive gem that appears in well-formed, multifaceted crystals. These crystals can reach an incredible size, and specimens weighing several hundred pounds are not unknown. The largest stones are customarily reserved for gifts on state occasions, and only the greatest master gemcutters are allowed to work them.

Often called the "Poor Man's Ruby," the common garnet is nevertheless a distinct and attractive blood-red gem in its own right. The violet form, also called rhodolite, is the rarest, most prized, and most valuable form of the stone.

Prized for their vibrant green color, emeralds are fragile and need to be protected from the impacts and extreme temperature changes common to adventuring life. It is a highly prized gem by the wealthly and royality alike.

When cut and polished, aventurine is alluring as its name. It resembles misty quartz, but contains glistening flecks of green that give it a unique sheen. The witches of Rashemen are said to use aventurine for invocations, evocations, and spirit work.

A common but beautiful gem, feldspar comes in many colors - each of them nicely set off by the stones' glassy luster. Best known in its purple hues, which are commonly mistaken for amethyst, feldspar is the much softer of the two and will scratch, chip, and even burn easily.
