Unlike most leaves, which must be dried for long periods of time before being smoked, Ausirâ€™s Pleasure is best smoked a few hours after clipping. With some effort, though, it can be well preserved and smoked at a later time. It is also best harvested late at night, when the mists from the Forest of Mists coat and soften the stalks. Then the young leaves are simply peeled off the stalk, talking long threads of stalk material with them.

The taste is a sweet and seductive on the palate as a loverâ€™s kiss but this heady mix of earthy and mineral elements hides the more dubious nature of the plant. Ausirâ€™s Pleasure stimulates the mind and body more than any other known leaf. All the euphoria and effects of freshly discovered love and the delights of lovers can be found in the smoking of this leaf but be warned, love is a fickle and the agony or despair of love lost and the pain of rejection are also the possible price of this tempting preparation. It is this convergence of pleasure and pain which has led many Layonarans to think that this plant is a gift from Xeen herself to her followers. To this end it is rumored that a process to extract a purified essence of the leaf exists and this substances is used in the creation of a ritual wine in some Xeenite ceremonies.

If you want to sit and enjoy a relaxing pipe, you'll reach first for some Flatbottom Leaf.  It is well known to be a pacifier of the senses. 

Many hard days work are left behind in a cloud of Flatbottom smoke.  Some fine medicines and sedatives are said to be made from this leaf as well.

Connoisseurs can often be heard giving praises to this smoking leaf.  Other leaves may be sharper, more pungent, with more unusual combinations of tastes, but no other leaf, it's widely held, is as balanced and well rounded as The Great Draw.

This leaf has been used in ranger and druid gatherings for ages, particularly in the Great Forest region.  The leaves are smoked as a central ritual exchange, and in great quantities used as an incense during meditation ceremonies.  Most, however, simply smoke it from a pipe.  

The taste is so smooth, and the smoke is so easy, those who smoke it often do so exclusively and form a strong attachment to it.  That's why it is called The Great Draw, some joke, not only because it is such a great draw from the pipe, but because it is the reason people are drawn to the Great Forest.

This leaf isn't much to look at.  Its aroma and raw taste are quite unremarkable as well.  But when dried, hanging upside-down by dangling stems, and then touched by fire, magic seems to happen.  The smoke actually billows green and tastes like perfect combination of green apple, chestnuts and roasted meat.  This smoking leaf has been a favorite throughout Roldem for as long as anyone can remember.  It is also a favorite among dwarves, for its cave habitat and bold flavors.

As the name suggests, this leaf erupts with a splendid sweetness in one's palate.  The honey taste can actually be overwhelming for some, and because of this is often accompanied by bitter brews.

Learning how to clip the plant properly, and which part to smoke, is challenging and open to fierce debate.  Some believe the lower leaves make the best smoking.  Others argue it is the higher leaves and their stems.  Some think the flower petals themselves should be gently plucked and combined with both types of leaves.

The Halflings who live in the Great Plains region of Dregar will argue weeks on end that this is the finest smoking leaf in all of Layonara.  It grows in the lush valleys and rolling hillsides of the Great Plains, mostly cultivated by families of Halfings who have lived in those parts and cultivated these herbs for as long as their family histories can be traced.

The leaf, when chewed or burnt, has an exceptional spicy sweetness to it.  It's this playful character which gives the leaf its playful name.  The leaf also seems to elevate ones mood, making those not acclimated to it almost seem giddy.  These qualities make the Plain's Exceptional a favorite throughout Layonara for entertaining and for company on long lonely strolls.

It took a Wolfswood Ranger to first smoke this plant, for no other would dare sink his hand deep into its thorny tentacles to clip off the soft curling leaves.  Though the leaves are soft, the stems are quite stout, and require either a firm grip or special shears to harvest just right.

Often you'll find a Wolfswood Ranger puffing on the Cuts, as they are called, during a break or relaxing after a hard day's patrol.  This sight is seen so often that some say the properties of this leaf are what give the rangers their sharpened senses and alertness.

Layonara - Crime & Punishment

Law on the continent is primarily governed by a union of good between the Churches of Toran and Rofirein.

Organisation of the Law:

Official senior representatives of the church of Rofirein are responsible for overseeing the interpretation of the law and thus will act as a Judges when criminals are on trial. 
These judges in all cases are considered to have the best knowledge of Rofirein's will and are thus considered divine experts.  A priest of Rofirein is always the final deciding factor if the interpretation of the law is ever in doubt.

Powers Granted too Judges -

1.	Oversee any hearings as required. 
2.	Pass sentence upon the guilty as directed by their divine link to Rofirein. 
3.	Supersede the power of any local governing body in direct relation to interpretation of the law and punishment. 
4.	Revoke the powers of any law enforcer that has shown themselves to be unworthy of these burdens. 
5.	Consult with experts in specific fields as required for use as expert witnesses.  Specifically in the areas of Magic and Magical crime. 

Official senior representatives of the church of Toran (predominantly Paladins) are responsible for carrying out the will of the Judge and enforcing the law. Those chosen shall be known as "Justiciers".  These souls devote their lives too carrying out the duty of Toran and upholding the law.  Wherever possible a "Justicier" will be called upon to carry out all law enforcement in conjunction with local government.  Local law enforcement will relinquish in ALL cases their powers too that of the "Justicier".

Powers Granted too Justiciers - 

1.	Carry out the will of the divine court of Mistone with direct reference to punishment. 
2.	Apprehend any person believed to be guilty of a crime or as directed too by the divine court. 
3.	Where immediate action is required or a representative of Rofirein cannot be contacted carry out sentence and punishment for minor crimes. 
4.	Take control of and direct local authorities where serious crimes are involved or the stability of the continent is in jeopardy.

Local Authorities 

Local authorities are responsible for enforcing the law out with the presence of a Justicier and make up the majority of law enforcers.  These include but are not limited to Royal Guard, Local Guard etc

Individuals

Individuals have the right too -

1.	Petition the divine courts of Mistone for a hearing. 
2.	Petition a "Justicier" to apprehend a suspected criminal. 
3.	Petition the divine courts for a retrial where new evidence is discovered that is directly related to the case. 
4.	Stand as a representative during trial for an individual on trial. 
5.	Attend the court as a witness. 
6.	Receive fair and just judgement and punishment as directed by the divine Rofirein and Toran. 
7.	Appoint a representative to speak on their behalf at a trial. 
8.	Request trial by the divine courts of Mistone where fair trial and punishment is believed to have not been given by local authorities. 
9.	Be safe and secure within their home and owned lands. 
10.	Defend themselves and their property with use of appropriate force if threatened by those out with law enforcement. 
11.	Be innocent until proven guilty. 
12.	Be informed of any changes to the law made by the Churches of Rofirein and Toran.

Anything not covered by these rights will be left to the discretion of the representatives of Rofirein and Toran and assessed on an individual basis.

Crimes and their Punishment by Category

Crimes and their punishments are decided directly by the representative of the church of Rofirein who oversees the trial however the following is a guideline:

Major Crimes (Usually carry sentences of death or imprisonment decided directly by the Judge) 
Murder 

Intermediate Crimes (Do not carry sentences of death but usually prolonged periods of imprisonment or related things) 
Counterfeiting.
Impersonation of a Law enforcement official.
Rape
Theft of large items (repeat offences)
Man slaughter
Adultery

Minor Crimes (Will never carry death sentences and rarely long term prison sentences. More likely community service or rehabilitation at correctional institutes. Time in the stocks, fines, flogging etc)
Theft of minor items (first offence)
Assault
Resisting Arrest
Slander

Welcome to the Wild & Dead Magic Disturbance Tool for GMs.

This tool is used to add a temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone (which is a disturbance in the Al'Noth) to an Area. An Area can only have one Disturbance; the Disturbance affects the entire Area.

A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area which is already a permanent Wild or Dead Magic Zone. A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area marked as a no temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone Area.

Disturbances do not persist across Module resets.

Adding a Wild or Dead Magic Disturbance will create a Placeable Object for the players to interact with. This allows them to attempt to repair the disturbance in the Al'Noth. Success is dependant upon the player's highest Spellcaster level, their Spellcrafting ability, whether they are a Lucindite or Aragenite, the use of any special (World Leader Reward) Disturbance repairing items, and the difficulty of the Disturbance to be repaired. It should be noted that failure is likely to be fatal.

The Disturbance repair difficulty can be altered any time after the Disturbance has been added to the Area. There are five difficulty settings, ranging from Simple (100% multiplier to the chance of success) to Impossible (0% multiplier to the chance of success).

The Disturbance Object is created 1.5 meters in front of the tool activator, facing the activator.

The Disturbance Object can be created directly from the DM-Client "Creator" (under "Placeable Object/Custom/Visual Effects/Magic Effects"). However, it will need to be conversed with immediately afterwards by the GM to properly attach the Disturbance to the Area. Until then, it is non-functional.

.set / .get / .got functions
----------------------------------------

.get % - brings this set character to you.

There MUST be an NPC, summoned creature, familiar or "voice" within range for these functions to work.  Repeated text is ALWAYS ignored (ie in testing hi, hi, hi)

BASIC VOICE FUNCTIONS:
-----------------------------------------
**structure is /dmSPACE **
The SPACE is mandatory.  The basic structure is to use the DM channel to "hide" the throwing of your voice.  There is NO way to not spam the DM channel.

will speak your "native" language.  If you have more than one, use the language widgets to determine the language you will be speaking.

/dm ; your text here

Your familiar or companion will say your text.

/dm ,your text here

Your summoned creature will say your text.


*emotes*
--------------
Bracketing text between two * will attempt to perform an emote.  This does NOT need to use the DM channel.  This applies to simple spoken text by the PC.

This will work for DM possessed creatures or for players.  The action will be taken by the speaker.

Two uses:  

1) is for skill checks or ability checks - ie *uses strength to move rock*

2) is for emotes - ie *bows to the leader of the town*

Appropriate actions include:

All abilities and all skills (spell them just like the actual skill or ability - ie use magic device)

There are two ways to set up the voice wand.  One is to write a script to load up the conversions (yuck) and the other way is to record them live using the DM client.

Recorded phrases are set as campaign variable and therefore have persistence - travel to new modules etc.  IF you record them in game,  then they are ALSO set as Tokens so you will see the text show up in the conversation to help your memory of what was recorded where.

Both tokens AND the recorded phrases are persistent - Recording them in game is recommended for easiest set-up.

The precise origins of this amulet are unknown, and as such things go, deeply shrouded in legend, rumor and hearsay.  The most plausable of these rumors is that it was created and worn by a powerful mage who many called the Stormcaller.

He was rumored both to be many things, from a devotee of Mist to a rather eccentric and insane evoker with a fascination with storms.  It was said that any time there was a storm near his home on the eastern shores of Dregar, he could be seen standing in the open at the edge of a cliff in the open, his arms stretched out above him amongst the wind, rain and lightning and seemingly without fear.  Some say he called the storms, while others claimed he simply reveled in their power. Still others say he used his own power to amplify that of the storms. For what purpose he might do any of this, no one knows.

The fate of the Stormcaller is likewise wrapped in supposition and rumor.  It was said that one morning, after a particularly violent midnight storm, his smoking remains were found near the edge of his usual cliff.  All that remained intact was his ever-present amulet, its large central gem replaying scenes of the most violent of storms ever to strike the coasts of Dregar.

The central gem of this necklace radiates magic even to the untrained.  It appears flawed at first, but looking into its depths, one can see the ever-changing chaos and energy of a fierce thunderstorm.

The youngest of the dreamers with a mere sixteen years to her name Gali is also considered to be the most promising. The ethereal nature of the dream realms seems to flow from Gali, her form almost becoming ethereal when she engages her talents.  Her eyes tell tales of the mysteries beyond that dreamers are privy to, while her face seems to hold little guile to disguise or hide any such secrets.  Long chestnut hair completes the portrait, framing her flower like face in long waves of red brown highlights. 

  Gali has honest features and an open heart, one that due to her youth has not been subjected to the rigours that many other of the dreamers have faced.  Caring and emotional she tends to act as her feelings dictate, choices made by deep wells of care stored within.  Due to her youth however Gali also lacks the deeper understandings of the mystery, and due to this is often overlooked. Not terribly confident she is constantly seeking assurance from outside herself, looking to others for support.

   Currently served by Syn as holder, both needing to find confidence in themselves as individuals regardless of race or age.  A journey to take together.

A small active young elf just barely into her adulthood, Ulathia displays the intense curiosity so apparent to the new adult.  Slim and boyish she is rarely walking when she can be running, rarely on the ground when she can be climbing trees, rarely doing nothing if she can be doing anything else.  Sun browned arms and legs poke constantly from mismatched clothes as she tumbles her way through life, every day a new  experience that she seems to relish to the very limits of her being.

    Yet if one were to peer closely into the green glades that are her eyes, an intense fear can be found.  The past and abuse of her gifts left its mark, marks evident in the fear that can be seen to dominate her demeanor and everyday behavior. Her rush to live life to the fullest driven clearly by the fear of it ending before she has experienced all, the joy in each moment robbed by the terror of losing something yet to be known.

  Currently served by Hargranar Craggenhilt as holder, the dwarves sage wisdom showing he can guide this young dreamer to further understanding as she recklessly walks the path of life.

Slender as a lance and with a tongue to match Carolyn is clearly of a noble house.  Her sharp presence and quickness to judge unique among those who have been themselves so persecuted. Piercing blue eyes constantly seem to glare out of a sharp aristocratic face, her bearing would be remarked upon as regal if it was not also so arrogant and lacking of understanding. Long straight hair the colour of molten copper hair spears down her back, the only warmth in an otherwise cold demeanor. 

    Of course reasons for her attitude exist and these may be found in the sharp scars lacing her back and arms, scars that speak of the whip and a past that was likely not as promising as the present.

   Currently Carolyn is served by Justicar Remiel of Toran as holder, Remiels bravery and judgment showing him able to supply the great care needed to tend this difficult dreamer.

Of average height and build Theresa has short cropped black hair and dark brown haunted eyes. Young and once gentle of feature the recent torment inflicted upon her due to her gifts has left its mark, the smooth and guileless smile gone to be replaced by one with that always seems to contain lingering memories of regret and pain.

   Shy and reclusive Theresa says little, her emotions which are scattered and few being conveyed solely by her emotive hands, hands that move fluently whenever she truly feels about that which she speaks of.

  Currently Theresa is served by Bill as her holder, the small goblin showing great heart in accepting the bond of the dream.

     Before the Cataclysm, Molten Island was attached to the Troll Mountains on Dregar; however, it is now a huge and active volcanic island. Inhospitable, and without any trading ports of interest, the island is not of much value to anyone. However, in the port pubs of Waysend, sailors can be heard to tell tales of a red dragon flying out from the island.

Firesteep Mountains
     Fisterion is the ancient red dragon who resides in the deeper levels of the Firesteep Mountains. He is a cruel and malicious beast, nearly godlike in power, who surpasses any red dragon previously known. 

     The mountains play host to many types of beasts, especially those attuned to elemental fire, such as fire elementals, red slaads, fire giants, and balors. Planar beasts, such as rashkasas and devourers, are not uncommon. Undead are also said to haunt its upper levels.

IN AND OUT


Begin by rolling the appropriate die to determine the starting player. Lowest number rolls first.

Before play begins, the amount of the Start must be agreed upon.

-The Start is the opening bet and coin dropped for each Out; it is the same for all players.

Play begins with the first player rolling four six-sided dice one at a time. The dice may fall three ways: Out, In, or In and In.

-Out: No doublets rolled (example: 1, 6, 3, 5)

-In: One doublet rolled (example: 2, 2, 4, 6 or 3, 3, 3, 1)

-In and In: Two doublets rolled (example: 2, 2, 3, 3)

Players may stay in play so long as they can drop the Start each time they roll an Out. When a player is out of True to make the Start bet, they are Out and Out.

Players who roll In do not need to add the Start coin to the pile.

Players who roll In and In take the pot and play begins again.

HAZARD


Begin by rolling the appropriate die to determine the starting player. Lowest number rolls first. The person holding the dice is called the Caster.

The caster specifies a number between 5 and 9 inclusive; this is the Main.

The caster places his bet that he will roll the Main.

The caster rolls two six-sided dice one at a time. If the caster rolls:

-the Main, he wins his bet and an amount equal to it.

-a 2 or a 3, he loses his bet; dice pass to next player.

-an 11 or 12, the result depends on the Main:

-if the Main was a 5 or 9, caster loses bet;

-if the Main was a 6 or 8, caster loses on an 11 and wins on a 12;

-if the Main was a 7, caster wins with 11 and loses on a 12.


Quick Reference:


Main is 5: Win on a 5, lose on a 2, 3, 11, or 12

Main is 6: Win on 6 or 12, lose on 2, 3, 11

Main is 7: Win on 7 or 11, lose on 2, 3, 12

Main is 8: Win on 8 or 12, lose on 2, 3, 11

Main is 9: Win on 9, lose on 2, 3, 11, 12


If the caster neither wins or loses, the number thrown is called the Chance and the caster throws again:

-if the caster rolls the Chance they win;

-if the caster rolls the Main they lose;

If neither the Chance or Main are rolled, caster rolls until either the Chance or Main is rolled and in addition:

-a 2 always loses

-if 11 or 12 are rolled, consult rules above to determine win or lose

Tournament and Betting:

Bets are placed between the caster, audience and the House. Audience may bet that the caster will win or lose. The caster may only bet that theyâ€™ll win.

In the event the caster does not win or lose, additional bets can be placed by the audience that the caster will either win or lose. A bettor cannot bet both win and lose in the same betting round.

In tournaments, the House collects the True and backs bets one to one.

"Killer"


All participants throw one dart. The unmodified number (between one and twenty) is that player's number.

All players start with three lives.

Highest player number throws first.

Five darts are thrown per player's turn; if a player throws their number again, they become a "killer".

Once a player is a "killer", they may aim for other player's numbers. Each successful hit removes one life from the player whose number was hit.

Once a player is out of lives, they are out of the game. Last player standing wins!

Optional rule: If a killer's number is hit, they may opt to rescind their killer status instead of losing a life, and return to trying to regain "killer".



Around the Sundial


Players each throw one dart; the highest number starts.

Each player throws three darts. Scoring is done from 1-20 in order; the first player to hit each number once in order wins. Numbers do not have to be hit consecutively.

Example:

Player one throws 3, 1, 6 - they have hit "1" and will try to hit "2" on their next turn.

Player two throws 1, 2, 9 - they have hit "1" and "2" and will try to hit "3" on their next turn.

Player three throws 5, 17, 11 - they will try to hit "1" on their next turn.

A hand-written book of anecdotes and entertaining stories to pass the time...

-----

Sir Wilber was a lesser known knight of Rofirein, but he was an accomplished furniture maker. His latest creation was a magnificient armoire which he had covered with pure silver plate. When the piece was all polished up, it shone like nothing anyone had ever seen.

The young Rofirenite hero was not ready to settle down yet, but Gracie, his girl, wanted to get married right away. She had become tired of waiting and decided to go to Wilber and pop the question herself. When Wilber saw the woman coming, he jumped into the armoire to hide.

Gracie entered Wilber's quarters and looked around. She didn't see anybody and turned to leave. Suddenly Wilber sneezed. Gracie ran to the armoire and flung the door open. there stood Wilber: he was trapped!

The next day, the castle newsletter's headline proclaimed: "Lady Gracie Finds Her Knight In Shining Armoire!" 

-----

A knight and his men return to their castle after a long hard day of fighting.

How are we faring? asks the king.

Sire, replies the knight, I have been robbing and pillaging on your behalf all day, burning the towns of your enemies in the west.

What?! shrieks the king. I donâ€™t have any enemies to the west!

Oh! exclaimed the embarassed knight. Well, you do now...

------

There were three kingdoms on the shores of a lake. There was an island in the middle of the lake, which the kingdoms had been fighting over for years. Finally, the three kings decided that they would send their knights out to do battle, and the winner would take the island.

The night before the battle, the knights and their squires pitched camp and readied themselves for the fight. The first kingdom had twelve knights, and each knight had five squires, all of whom were busily polishing armor, brushing horses, and cooking food. The second kingdom had twenty knights, and each knight had ten squires. Everyone at that camp was also busy preparing for battle. At the camp of the third kingdom, there was only one knight, with his squire. This squire took a large pot and hung it from a looped rope in a tall tree. He busied himself preparing the meal, while the knight polished his own armor.

When the hour of the battle came, the three kingdoms sent their squires out to fight (this was too trivial a matter for the knights to join in). The battle raged, and when the dust cleared, the only person left was the lone squire from the third kingdom, having defeated the squires from the other two kingdoms.

I guess this just proves that the squire of the high pot and noose is equal to the sum of the squires of the other two sides.

Grannoch

Aliases: 
     Mother of Giants (used by all giant-kin), Lady of Lightning (used by storm giants), Shaper of Stone (used by stone giants), Tamer of Flame (used by fire giants), Mistress of Cold (used by frost giants)
Race: Giant
Worshippers: 
     Usually giants, half-giants or humans with some giant blood in their ancestry.
Domains: 
     Protection, Fire, Air, Earth, and Water. The cleric always has the Protection domain together with one elemental domain which is always based on the type of giant they are (Fire for fire giants, for instance)
Governs: Storms, earthquakes, volcanoes, ice

Dogma: 
     The first words of Grannoch when she created the giant races of Layonara were these:
     "My Children, I, Grannoch, Mother of Giants, am the One that is Four. The Four are One inside Me. Since I am the Four, none can be supreme."

     Mother of the giant races of Layonara, Grannoch is worshipped by all of them, be they storm, fire, frost or stone giants.
     Being the ruler of all four elements, and firmly believing that none is superior to the other, Grannoch has laid down the Dogma of Elements to her clerics: "My Children, I, Grannoch, Mother of Giants, am the One that is Four. The Four are One inside Me. Since I am the Four, none can be supreme."
     Since all giant kin are her children, she does not favor one giant people above the other.  As with all children, this does not mean that the different giant kin do not strive to be better than the other: all try to curry her favor.

     Grannoch balances the elements, since she embodies all elements. All elemental powers are granted by Grannoch, and thus, all are equally powerful. None should reign supreme and those striving to make one more powerful than the other should be stopped. Never slay a fellow follower of Grannoch. Protect your homes and families.

    Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
Grannoch's followers favor mauls, often enchanted with the elemental power of the domain of the cleric. 

     Clerics are usually dressed in the colors of their domain, so red for fire, dark blue for water, brown or green for earth, and light-blue to white for air. The elemental color is possibly combined with another color of their choice, but the other color is never the color of another element. 

     Clergy and Temples: Most giant communities have a couple of clerics, both male and female; usually the most powerful is the leader, but there is no specific title given to this cleric. There is also no large, community- spanning hierarchy, although every giant race has a male and a female cleric that are considered the most wise and powerful. These are generally referred to as the Son and the Daughter of the particular element: the Son of Air and the Daughter of Air, for example. It is rare to have such powerful clerics dwelling in the same community, however.

     Grannoch is generally prayed to at dawn and at dusk, for example by praying to a fire, a bowl of water, with hands touching the ground, or with arms extended upwards to the sky. She is also invoked when strength or aid is needed: when going into battle or when child labor is difficult, for instance. When praying to Grannoch, clerics try to use words related to elements in their prayers.

     For example, a prayer of a cleric with the Earth domain, before going into battle:
     "Oh Grannoch, Shaper of Stone, make me strong as the bedrock and my foes tremble before me as if you were quaking the earth itself!"  
     Or, a cleric with the Water domain, praying to give a mother strength during a particularly difficult childbirth:
"Mother of Giants, hear my plea, please assist your daughter in bringing another one of your children into the world. Make this birth as easy as the effortless flow of a mountain stream."

     The only special day of worship is the first day of spring, also called Birth of Giants, when all giants remember the birth of their races on Mount Tulbane, as well as the birth of all the giants born since the last Birth of Giants.

The LeShay are a powerful type of Fey that have the ability to create weapons of pure force using nothing but the energy of their own body.

A living vault is just that - a magically animated chamber constructed by the most powerful epic wizards to store and protect prized possessions. A living vault is primarily a defensive entity, designed to guard treasure of all sorts, though that does not prevent it from attacking if necessary.

Boltr is the highest ranking Deep Smith in Twar Shal. He refuses to wear anything else but his smith's outfit, even in presence of his King and is always seen with his flaming hammer, waving it around as if it weighs nothing.
Dagmar Oregatherer is head of Twar Shal's merchant council, Dagmar is a staunch supporter of the King and knows her business, be it legal, or less than legal.

The pale elf before you looks like one of the oldest elves you've ever seen. His body looks ver frail, but his eyes, however, do not show his age at all and do not seem to miss much of what goes on around him.

The Matriarch of House Zau'ana, Ilph'afay, has only recently taken over from her unfortunate predecessor. The Patriarch of House Zau'ana, Altondar, who also holds the position of First Patriarch of Olath Chath, is said to have killed the previous Matriarch as she was seeking to get too much power to herself. Ilph'Afay, or Emerald Eyes as she is also called, seems content with her new position, at least for the time being.
Matriarch of House Torlyl of the city of Olath Chath, Jysdrill is carefully watching the moves of the other Matriarchs, waiting for her chance to claim the Prime Matriarch position.

You see a man, past his fifties, who seems to radiate confidence and authority.
He is dressed as judges are, in the ceremonial armor of a Guardian of Justice, with the Blade of Justice around his waist.
The golden dragon symbol of Rofirein hangs around his neck.

Respected by many, Judge Kirus is considered a highly competent Judge, his sentences are often harsh, but always just. Having been the Judge for the Hlint area for nearly two decades now has also given him a wealth of experience in 'stranger' cases then most other Judges would face.

His built is lean and his hair is starting to gray, however, his piercing blue eyes do not seem to miss a thing and when his gaze meets you, you cannot help but look away, making you feel like you've just been Judged.

Rumored to once being a queen of a great powerful kingdom of demons, Maluxchialmina The Seductress was stripped of her powers. Now, going through life as Malu until her powers return, she is biding her time in Olath Chath, as new proprietress of the Inn of Endless Pleasure.

This duergar has a paler skin than most, and there is something about him but you cannot quite put your finger on it.... His robe has a single rune embroidered on it. Mirkik is one of the King's advisors.

About 200 years ago, the previous Archmage of Olath Chath was found dead in his summoning circle. After two years of plotting and scheming amongst themselves, the mages of Olath Chath's Faerl Tower chose, or were forced to choose, Nad'Irhac as their new Archmage. Now, he has renounced his ties to his House and tries to further his own schemes of power.

This Dark Elf is paler than most. He is Nimor, Patriarch of House Teken'erv. He is the third patriarch of Teken'erv to take the position in the last two decades. Zesafea, Teken'erv's Matriarch does not allow any male to consolidate his position, therefore, the last two Patriarchs all had an 'unfortunate' accident.

Grandmaster of the Adamantine Brotherhood, Rokru Ironbender's fists are legendary. Reputed to be able to smash a nugget of adamantium into pieces with a bare fist, he is respected by many and feared by all. He is one of King Rotak's advisors.

The Duergar that stands before you radiates authority, it is Rotak Stoneforger IV, King of Twar Shal. Firmly in control of his city for approximately 40 years now, Rotak Stoneforger IV has the respect of the other clan leaders as well as Sulterio's clergy. He has successfully grown the powerbase that his forefathers established.
He prefers to lead his own troops into battle, and is a skilled  tactician.

Warmistress of Olath Chath, Shurynne is believed to be behind an ambush that killed her predecessor. Of course, it could not be traced back to her, and now she is Olath Chath's most brilliant tactician and Warmistress of its forces.

These colourful beasts are covered with thousands of glittering scales, which are constantly changing colour. This makes the Prismasaurus very hard to hit, in spite of its otherwise large size. A Prismasaurus has very keen eyesight, and can deliver devastating bites and tail swipes.

A retriever specializes in recovering lost or desired objects, runaway slaves, and enemies and bringing them back to its master. A retriever has a body the size of an ox, with legs spanning more than 14 feet. It weighs about 6,500 pounds.
A serious looking Roldemian guard in his traditional armor.
Before you stands Geirr Gravesmiter, strongest of the Chosen of Sulterio in Twar Shal, he is therefore the head of this part of Sulterio's Church. He is also one of King Rotak's advisors.

This creature looks like an evil-faced old human with the lower body, legs, and wings of a reptilian monster. Its hair is tangled, filthy, and crusted with blood. It carries a Longbow and aims at you with uncanny precision.
A calm and soothing expression surrounds this man's face.

Xora, a mysterious woman who controls a powerful tower of magic near the northern forests of Dregar. Rumoured to be a great wizard whot trusts no one but herself.
A faint glimpse of sadness can seen crossing her face but its quickly replaced with a stern look and she approaches you with a resolute demeanor.
A ring of energy, waiting to take you far away.
Dark Elf Warrior of the Spider
Forest Giant Shaman of the Deep Grove Clan
A strange beast, this being seems otherworldly in some manner, it's garb is adorned in red symbols and images of death.
Blighted Weavedrinker of The Glittering Isles
Guard of Milara - Mountain Giant Warrior
Guard of Milara - High Ogre Mage
A relatively young looking man, dirty with forge grime.
Warrior's Destiny - Traditions in Arms and Armory for 353 years. Established by Hulgrid Arman Gues IV.
Warrior's Destiny - Traditions in Arms and Armory for 353 years. Established by Hulgrid Arman Gues IV

Aliases: Mother of All Magic, Lady of Spells  
Race: Human 
Alignment: NG 
Governs: Magic, Sorcery, Spellcraft, Health 
Domains: Good, Healing, Knowledge, Magic, Trickery 
Description: Lucinda is the Goddess of all things magical. She believes that magic will make the world prosper and her followers will only make the world stronger. While Lucinda has a heart of gold and is more than generous with her blessings, she is also quite mischievous at times, and her methods for achieving her goals, while never ever harming anyone, are sometimes not considered frank, direct or honourable even by her friends.

Grillondon's most priced possession, a belt that is sure to give him an edge against his rivals.

Tall and slender with soft green eyes and blond hair, Violet is a picture of elven beauty. Her gestures are graceful though unmeasured, her emotions visible in many a spontaneous outburst.  As she moves you can clearly see the subtle grace that is inherent to her form, every line a picture of fluidity in motion.  Flawless alabaster skin finishes her figure, heated only by the warmth of her nature.

    As her eyes meet with yours you can clearly see defiance and honestly linked with a depth of compassion and care that is rarely seen.  Within the depths of green dwells what many would see as the final mystery of the dream, the realms of hope and and an eternity, of wishes come true swimming among emerald currents.
  
    Originally thought to be the last of her kind, Violet now leads the Dreamers, in a hope that the future will be kinder to her and hers than the past.  

Currently served by Kobal Bluntaxe as her holder, the dwarf and Violet gaining much trust and respect for each other in recent endeavors.
Gum arabic extracted from the sap of trees and used for the casting of various spells.
Used in spells that cause increased movement, mainly those of haste and mass haste.
A handcrafted helmet made of bronze.
A handcrafted helmet made of Iron
A handcrafted helmet made of copper.

This rustly old helmet is badly dented, uncomfortable and difficult to see out of the eye slots. Several dents poking in feel as if they would poke into your head should you be hit while wearing it. Yet for all it's short commings it still seems to offer some protection.
More of a tool than a weapon, the skinning knife is a handy item to carry.
Used to cast the spells darkness in neutralize poison.  In the latter its consumed and the former it's tossed into the air.

This small package consists of some dried cheese, a bit of dry tack and a hard biscuit.

It's tasteless, bland, and salty... but hey, it'll last until you eat it. Or until you feed it to a starving dog.
This is flint and steel.  It is used for starting fires.  ...That's it.
This natural resource can be used in the crafting of some baked goods and possibly even a potion.
Bolt, Copper Tipped Hickory Falcon Tail
Arrow, Copper Tipped Hickory Falcon Tail
A Bottle of Water (Spell Component Use Only)

A component used in many spells that have a spherical shape to them, these include:

Globe of Invulnerability
Minor Globe of Invulnerability
Scintillating Sphere

Brandished during the casting of Cone of Cold, Feeblemind, Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning spells. This rod occasionally melts, a wise spell caster is prepared for that and is ready to hurl it aside. Melting glass tends to scar.
Used in spells such as hold person and hold monster, generally considered a binding regent.
Thrown during the casting of color spray.
Used in the casting of dismissal.
Thrown at the target during the casting of ball lightning.
These gloves must be worn during the casting of all of the Bigby's spells.
Used in the castings of both displacement and freedom of movement.
Used as the primary casting agent in the spell of Poison.
Eaten during the casting of Evard's Black Tentacles...calamari anyone?
An item used in the casting of Clairaudience and Clairvoyance.
The primary component used in Mestil's Acid Sheath.
A Glass Statue of a Man
Used in the casting of Melf's Acid Arrow.
Consumed during the casting of True Sight.
Used mainly in the casting of Greater Magic Weapon.
Sprinkled into the air during the casting of flesh to stone.
Used in the casting of Protection from Alignment spells, the caster spreads the powder around himself or the person the spell is being cast on, in a circle, as if a ward.
Burned while meditating, for the casting of Legend Lore.
Dead fleas used in the casting of various spells.
A spell often associated with necromantic spells/powers, spells such as animate dead, create undead, death armor, and circle of death all require this variety of gem.
Spread over the fingers before the casting of the spell inferno.
Rolled into a ball and hurled during the casting of fireball, this is, by many to be considered an envokers best friend.
Consumed during the casting of Ironguts, what doesn't kill you makes you stronger.
Used mainly in the casting of Horrid  Wilting spells. Simulates the drawing out of moisture.
This club has no makers mark of any kind. However its creator clearly had one goal in mind. Making it a better choice for putting the undead to rest.

A simple looking staff at first glance. However upon closer examination you notice a small opening at one end and a small button where you would typically hold the staff. I wonder what this button does?
This wavy blade is rusted and set with many spiked burs along the blade. It is poorly balanced and may break apart with a strong parry, but it sure looks like it would hurt like the blazes going in.
Plied from dead creatures or found scattered, these darts show the effects of weather and exposure.

These bandages require the use of the Heal skill.  The target will be healed 4d4 hitpoints plus 1.25 times your Heal skill.  In addition, if the healer succeeds a d20 + Heal vs DC15 the target is healed of all poison and disease. Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.
This potion will heal the target 4d4 hitpoints.
Apparently some discarded necklace. It is so badly tarnished most would not want to show it around their necks. Its small gem does seem to have a faint glow to it if looked at in the darkness.
Shafts used to make Arrows or Bolts in Wood working.
Small Shafts for use in Wood working.
This mineral is hard to identify with all the muck stuck to it.  A good bath should help.
A pinch of dust taken from the ruined land where the city of Zolinar once stood, before the city's reconstruction began.

The knowledge of the origin of shields of this make is either lost to time or a guarded secret. There are two recent theories, however both seem equally fanciful. The first places their creation at somewhere between 4500 and 5000 years prior to the cataclysm. In the wake of the Second Dragon Purge there were likely hundreds of Dragon corpses littering the battlefields. Enterprising (or foolhardy) humanoids may have scavenged the corpses for their hides. The second theory is that they were made within the last millennia from the hide of a slain dragon. Due to the sheer age of the shield assuming the first theory and the rarity of dragons in the recent age, both theories are questionable. Regardless of their true origin, many such items end up hidden or locked in storage vaults as to be seen wielding such an item by a dragon is to garner its wrath.
When used properly, a small shield can grant lightweight protection with very little encumbrance to the wielder.

As the tales tell, several centuries ago the town of List was beset by a horde of horrid trolls that poured forth from the nearby moors. Its decentralized settlements easily fell prey to the marauding trolls. In fact, word of the attacks did not even reach the town until almost all of its citizens that lived between central list and the moors had been overrun and summarily devoured.

List's salvation came from an unlikely location: the highwaymen that collected "road tolls" from merchant caravans on the road to haven. These outlaws, after calling several groups of their thieving brethren, became the largest group of men at arms near List. Led by an uncommonly noble (or scheming) commander, and armed with a score of these powerful blades of mysterious origin, the ruffians lost their status as outlaws by turning wave after wave of the troll invasion away from the town. They were hailed as "The Hero's of List" and few cared to remember what their occupation had been previously. They were granted an official pardon from the Lord of Haven. The commander and several of his officers were granted land and minor titles or political positions in the region.

The blades themselves were held in List, on display and ready to be the town's "Last Defense" if ever needed again. Over time life in the town and its surrounding settlements returned to normal, and the level of viligance slacked. Only three of the blades entitled the Last Defense now remain in the display case in List, and a few of the elderly of List if asked why only three remain may mention a cowardly theft in the night before getting lost in a tangle of ale and tangential stories.

All of these two-handed flamberge's appear identical with the most prominent feature being a gleaming many-faceted fire opal set in the pommel. Its waved blade glints red in the light of the sunset, the time of day when troll attacks begin, and sunrise, when the hordes finally retreat from the rising sun.
The greatsword is an impressive weapon by any measure, and is held with two hands by all but the largest of creatures.

Although the followers of Pyrtechon generally do not favor a specific weapon, many often use ranged weapons imbued with fire when facing their enemies. These arrows are tipped with heads shaped from a strange reddish brown metal set upon a shaft of darkened bone with black fletching.

It is rumored that this metal, said to be a gift of the Dragon God Pyrtechon himself, was first discovered washed down a small stream on Firesteep after an erruption that occured while a cleric of Pyrtechon performed his prayer ritual at sunset when The Eternal Flame was prominent in the orange sky.

The arrowheads magically return to their molten state as they speed through the air toward the archer's target burning their victims with The Destroyer's Breath.
Arrows can vary in form and function, but most are 20 to 40 inches long and have some form of fletching (usually feathers) to provide stabilization.

Although the followers of Pyrtechon generally do not favor a specific weapon, many often use ranged weapons imbued with fire when facing their enemies. These bullets, naturally formed from the molten metals of Firesteep are said to be a gift of the Dragon God Pyrtechon Himself.

It is rumored that this type of bullet was first discovered washed down a small stream on Firesteep after an erruption that occured while a cleric of Pyrtechon performed his prayer ritual at sunset when The Eternal Flame was prominent in the orange sky.

These bullets magically return to their molten state as they speed through the air toward the slinger's target burning their victims with The Destroyer's Breath.
Sling bullets are smooth balls of metal that can produce severe bruising and even broken bones when launched effectively.

Although the followers of Pyrtechon generally do not favor a specific weapon, many often use ranged weapons imbued with fire when facing their enemies. These bolts are tipped with heads shaped from a strange reddish brown metal set upon a shaft of darkened bone with black fletching.

It is rumored that this metal, said to be a gift of the Dragon God Pyrtechon himself, was first discovered washed down a small stream on Firesteep after an erruption that occured while a cleric of Pyrtechon performed his prayer ritual at sunset when The Eternal Flame was prominent in the orange sky.

The tips of the bolt magically return to their molten state as they speed through the air toward the archer's target burning their victims with The Destroyer's Breath.
Bolts or quarrels are the standard ammunition for all types of crossbows, varying in function depending on the shape of the head.

Within the chruch of Az'atta, the tale goes that these cloaks were given to the first generations of her clergy by Az'atta Herself.  In the days before Her name was known, the clergy often found it best to choose when to spread her word carefully, and that avoiding certain confrontations was often wise.  While it is unlikely that all of these cloaks, or even any of them, were gifts from Az'atta herself, they serve to teach a valuable lesson, both through the telling of their tale when they are gifted and through their use, to the newest members of the clergy.  This particular example also embodies Az'atta's hatred of poisons and its divine magic serves to strengthen the wearer against its evils.
Cloaks are simple cloth garments used to protect the wearer from bad weather and other hazards of the open road.

Within the chruch of Az'atta, the tale goes that these cloaks were given to the first generations of her clergy by Az'atta Herself.  In the days before Her name was known, the clergy often found it best to choose when to spread her word carefully, and that avoiding certain confrontations was often wise.  While it is very unlikely that all of these cloaks, or even any of them, were gifts from Az'atta herself, they serve to teach a valuable lesson, both through the telling of their tale when they are gifted and through their use, to the newest members of the clergy.
Basic Robes made by a Tailor, Then enchanted againsted Acid Attacks.
Basic Robes made by a Tailor, Then enchanted againsted Fire Attacks.
Basic Robes made by a Tailor, Then enchanted againsted Electrical Attacks.
A handcrafted helmet made of platinum.
This was one mans attempt at proving that things look better when you're drunk. Although many wonder what his motives truly were in making such an odd item.
Created originally by the mage Daevinn to compliment his robe Avoidance, these gold and blue bracers have elaborate bead work on the edges.

This shirt looks to be made of woven hemp, but upon closer inspection, one finds it to instead be a mesh of incredibly tiny rings. With a strange ability to stretch to more than twice it's original size, this shirt seems to have found its way out of the hands of the fey creatures who made it.
Reddish metal chainmail that looks like it was used for target practice by Rael's army.

Created locally in Spellgard then enchanted at the Academy, these fine wrist-length silk gloves are powder blue with white piping. To someone attuned to the Al'Noth, they glow brightly. There is a tag on the inside embroidered with a spool of thread spelling out "Tweed, since 1301".

Given out to acolytes of Xeen, these "robes" are usually made of leather and are tailored to fit closely to the body. Creative adaptation is encouraged so long as it facilitates the purpose of the garment; to get one's way.
Path of the Vine Acolyte Robes

Given out to acolytes of Xeen, these "robes" are usually made of leather and are tailored to fit closely to the body. Creative adaptation is encouraged so long as it facilitates the purpose of the garment; to obtain obedience upon demand.
Path of the Whip Acolyte Robes
Favored by rat catchers in cities all over the world, this cloak is reasonably easy to copy yet provides that extra edge to vermin-hunters.

Item description: Made and copied by countless students in Spellgard, this cloak has the outward appearance of a standard item of clothing. When worn, it makes a quiet crinkling noise; careful inspection reveals that the inside lining is a soft gauze that is see-through when pressed against the material next to it. The inner material of the cloak is tight-woven wool with a paper cover that can be removed from a zipper on the bottom. Pressing the gauze against the paper allows the wearer to see whatever is written there. Due to this item, cloaks must now be removed before a student takes his desk during a school day in Spellgard.
Modeled after one of the hoods worn by Sharina Shadowfang, it is woven with dye-able hair. The strands contain illusion magic that allows the wearer to more convincingly claim to be someone else.
Worn leather armor that still offers some protection.
Warthog Smithyz mak armur fur yu. Gud skin tak hard hit. Warthog hide mak strongr. Yu like!
Plate armor built for the personal guard of a prominent Creedo family; the armor is hinged and enchanted to allow bursts of swift movement.
This belt is for those who can dish it out but can't take it. A favored item of less than savory characters.
Looks like something A monk would Wear.
The powerful magic of the black Malar Panther enfuses this armor with extra physical protection. Both Mages and Sorcerers consider this to be a worthy addition to their wardrobes.
Crafted Wand of Melf's Acid Arrow
Bolt, Copper Tipped Oak Falcon Tail
Arrow, Copper Tipped Oak Falcon Tail
Arrow, Iron Tipped Oak Raven Tail
Bolt, Iron Tipped Oak Raven Tail
Arrow, Silver Tipped Oak Raven Tail
Bolt, Silver Tipped Oak Raven Tail

This small gem was created using a diamond and various divine spells. When used it will record your True Name, and if given to a cleric, they can use this stone to pull your soul back from the Plane of the Lost.

A small sacrifice is needed to encode the gem with your Name.

A cleric can not read the persons True Name, but does know whose gem it is by a ressonating warmth when near its owner.

The first pair of blades of this design were said to have been the prized possessions of Markell Fastfoot, a halfling thief who found some renown working the docks of Port Hampshire.  The legend goes, that after losing several of his fingers in unsuccessfull attempts at thievery, he commissioned a minor wizard to place this enchantment upon his blades.  By all accounts, he was a terrible thief, but somehow he always seemed to be able to outrun the guard.  Watching Markell's success, the wizard went on to make quite a fortune selling similarly enchanted blades untill he was jailed for indirect obstruction of justice.  He died in prison.  Markell himself was eventually killed for freelancing in a powerfull guild's territory.  The hilt of the blade is carved with in ornate M, whether for Markell, or for the name of the forgotten wizard, it is impossible to say.
One of the first types of sword to come into existence, the short sword is a double-edged weapon about two feet long. It is an economical weapon, and a favorite of archers and rogues.

It has been told that on nights of the new moon, points of light can be seen dropping from the constellation of the viper.  Peasants say to their children that on such nights the viper sheds his teeth, only to grow more, dripping with poison to replace the old.  Children must not go out on such nights, lest they be struck by one of these poisoned teeth falling from the sky.
These missile weapons are close in size to a small dagger, and are hurled in combat toward their target.
Any burgeoning privateer would be wise to learn well the lesson taught to the former owner of this blade.  Do not offend Mist.
The rapier is a light, thrusting sword popular among nobles and swashbucklers. Often associated with dueling and sport fighting, rapiers are nonetheless deadly in trained hands.

Many, many axes have been made by the orcish followers of Grand since his ascension. However, one orc smith named Bracht achieved a great deal of notoriety near the Grand Temple by producing axes of very high quality, and learning to smith the more difficult metals. Holding a grudge against elves and humans as well as dwarves, his axes were constructed to give advantages against all three races. Now working for Jukha exclusively, some of his earlier weapons have been looted by adventurers and come into the market.
This mighty hammer displays several dwarven symbols. It has seen its fair share of battle against giant kin.

These spears are often used by Giant kind to skewer a smaller creature. Either to be eaten off the spear right away or turned on a spit at a later time. Then the spear doubles as a toothpick digging bits of the meal from their teeth.

This deadly Katar was the favored weapon of a mercenary from the Katherian area. He could drive this Katar into his enemy with such force that it would even pierce plate armor. Though his favorite attack with it was to surprise his target from behind and place a well aimed punch to the base of the neck.

A sputtering, sparking nightmare with blades, bumps and pointed tips thrusting forth from various holes in the weapon's head seemingly at random. Wielding this club requires concentration and balance, which puts the wielder at a disadvantage in combat

The Shewper Shillelagh (shuh-ley-lee). It's not just a club it's a Shewper Shillelagh! This was the sales pitch of the clubs creator, John Shewper. He peddled his Shillelaghs across Mistone. Unfortunatly John had a horrid lisp and often drew several giggles when he'd cry out... You will alwayshh be shaffe wiff a Shooper Shilaylee at your shide!

The Shin Biter is powerful tool and status symbol of giant hunters around the globe. Braided from the nose hairs of fallen giants, these giantbane slings are imbued with gnomish alchemy to seek out the hides of those who grew them. The Shin Biter also grants one the giantkin knowledge of "catching" rocks, albeit smaller ones. 

Originally created by the gnomish Giant hunter, Gromak Kneesplitter, this sling was his answer to his opponents' throwing boulders. It is said that the mad little barbarian would scale the tallest mountain and rain death down upon them from above, shouting "Who's the tallest now? Who's the tallest NOW?!" with maniacal fury. Giants who look upon these weapons are equally filled with fear and rage, and they have long been forbidden to the faithful of Grannoch. While Voraxians and giants layers both hold this item with high regard, no one enjoys them quite as much as the Shadonites. It is made out of nose hair, after all.
This sling was made for a wagon master from Hlint. He frequently found his caravan under attack from goblins. He had this sling made to help keep them at bay when he traveled.

Given to the armies of Sinthar, this ammo is fine shot with razor edges embedded. It is slung in handfuls rather than singly. Once embedded the shot is very difficult to remove and the shrapnel does as much damage as the bullet. It is often found in areas that Blood's armies fought.

Originally designed by an unnamed, frustrated crossbow-wielding undead slayer. Designed with a rounded head and additional counterweight, these bolts work just fine against the walking dead and the living alike.
This simple looking sling was always at the side of a halfling known to hunt on Mistone. He was able to take down even the biggest of wild game with what many wrote off as a childs toy.

Used by the dwindling Broken Glade giant clans outside Prantz, these massive axes are not wieldable by anyone smaller than a half-orc. With thick oak branches for handles and iron axe heads that can weigh over forty pounds, this axe in the hands of one strong enough can kill with a single blow. With the giants almost always at war with rival tribes these axes can sometimes be found around the Forest of Fog
These small daggers are made of Onyx, or volcanic glass. They are so razor sharp that they often leave a wound that continues to bleed.

This crossbow appears to be constructed of two different types of material.  The stock is some type of lightweight hardwood. The bow itself is made mostly of metal. This seems to give the crossbow a bit more snap than its all wood relatives.
A longbow of mahogany that has seen long and hard use.

This special wind and fire wheel was made for a circus performer from Fort Wayfare. He would do special tumbling and twirling routines all while wielding one or two these wheels. Each blade tip of this wheel seems to have been enchanted with a different element.
One of several ranged weapons made by a woodsman from Alindor. His skills in crafting ranged weapons was highly sought after. Thus some of them can still be found today.

These bandages require the use of the heal skill.  You will first make a DC roll, d20 + Heal vs. DC15. If that is successful you will then heal the target of all poison and disease as well as heal them 4d4 plus 1.25 times your Heal skill.  Both the healer and the target must not be in combat.
This potion will heal the target 8d8 hitpoints.

This ring is the product of years of research from noted gemologist and wizard Kay Whitehall. Having found a deposit of diamonds in a long-abandoned site with what she claimed was a special affinity for enhancment, it was her idea to enchant the diamonds with the power to boost all aspects of a being's abilities. She was disappointed to find that the diamonds were not much stronger than their normal kin and shattered when too much magical energy was cast upon them, but not before she'd perfected a way to enhance two different attributes and add other boosts. Passing of old age in 1486, her secret went to her grave with her and shortly after, her entire collection magical ring experiments went missing with no explanation. 

A few of the rings have been spotted on the hands of the very rich over the last two decades and even fewer have popped up in odder places. The ring you hold bears her signature carving in the gold band - KHW.

Crafted by the mad Shadonite bard Rocco Sockopopper, this mandolin has been imbued with strange enchantments designed to make it pack a hefty punch. Known for his chaotic displays of violence against squashes, watermelons and various furniture on the stage, the demented gnome long lamented the rising costs and inconvenience of replacing instruments on the road. With alchemical gusto he studied long and hard formulas of hardening and strengthening. His works culminated into fine gems of mayhem such as this. These instruments are valued highly by both tricksters who enjoy fighting flashy, as well as skalds and battle bards who tend to be rough on their instruments

Worn by the militias of Morholt, this heavy sapphire and diamond amulet practically screams "bribe me". Vicious turf wars between slavers and thieving guilds over territory have brought a few of these to the market.

These are the favored instruments of the hedonist satyrs, played through merrymaking and drunken revelry. A free-spirited people, the winds of these pipe are as random as their wild whims. The sound of this instrument is enchanting, leading one into a sense of deep relaxation as their minds begin to wander to places distant. It is said that such woodwinds are only freely given to friends of the forest, though a good pint of dwarf sledge and a sizable slice of roasted mutton may also seem a fair trade to a satyr in his drunken state. The satyrs' sense of revelry courses through the veins of those who play these pipes, feeling the urge to stay awake just one moment more for another round, song or dance.
A rough unprocessed nugget.  This is a popular material used in the blacksmithing trade.
Mahogany wood is a favorite material of  bow crafters.
Mahogany wood is a favorite material of bow crafters.
This is a basic Stave used in the making of wood products.

These pipes were originally made by an unknown and forgotten Dwarven Clan. All that is known is that the fathers made and handed down a new pipe to each of their sons. Originals bear the clan symbol on the bowl of the pipe. The ones found now are cheap copies of the originals and bear no clan symbols.
Oak wood is a favorite material of  weapon and tool crafters.

Granting seemingly unrestrained movement to even the most experienced Swordsman, these bracers balance hands and arms in perfect positions.

Never catching the wearer off-guard, those lucky enough to find these gloves normally end in the unlucky chase of a greedy pirate.

These delicate leaves are rumoured to have been shed by the Great Oak itself at the passing of seasons.

Lingering throughout the lands, the fortunate druids and rangers who find these leaves, wrap them around their arms to feel closer to the heart of Nature.

Fortunately for them, the animals they meet also acknowledge the presence of their spiritual homes and grant them free passage throughout their territories

Polished with the finest of oils and layered with the shiniest of metals, these reflective bracers are anything but flattering. Every single surface in these gloves has been skillfully deformed to offer the onlooker a humorous version of themselves.

Used by Royal Jesters, skilled fighters are said to have crafted these jovial arm bands and used them for far more practical purposes.

Contrasting perfectly with any surface, the fine material these gloves are made of allow for inticrate examination.

Soft ends on each digit impede any sort of alteration to be made to that which is being investigated, making them very handy for underground scouts and your all around adventurer.

Comfortably molding to even the most delicate of fingers, these gloves are almost imperceptible to the user. 

Such graceful shaping enhances the skills of even the most talented performing, granting insight into harmonious patterns, never seen before.

The pure white gloves are made from the most refined of silks and bordered with delicate cottons. 

Allowing for free movement along any injury, a healer tending to wounds using these gloves can normally avoid infecting any wounds. Or at the least, see when they are dealing with blood or a more sinister substance.

Rigid leathers covered in plated steel lock these gloves in two positions, that of a firm grip and another with outstretched fingers.

Extremely uncomfortable and stubborn, those who wear these gloves after sometime gain a sense of self-control that defies logic. Or perhaps just stiff fingers.

Constructed of a fine cloth and an unusual weave that seems to reflect very little light, making its exact color rather difficult to determine. As it moves for whatever reason, the same quality makes it seem to flow like some dark fluid.

Armor given to the rangers following Athlonus, who fought Milara's monstrosities from the woods and forests around Alindor. Most of Athlonus's followers were elves, and the armor was designed to survive massive blows from the often huge creatures.
A favorite sport in cities where animals are often used for entertainment, bull running has given rise to specialized equipment. This has become as sought-after item by cattle herders as well.
Gloves supposedly blessed by The Lifegiver, Aeridin. The power within them helps bring undead souls to rest.

For the fearless and prepared who walk in the Deep, these boots have been made and copied to provide protection from a number of Deep dwellers. As a few have made their way up from the depths of Layonara they have become favored by spies, assassins, and politicians (for obvious reasons).

For an enterprising sneak, these gnome-designed boots have it all. Made from metal-reinforced leather, they have a self-oiling mechanism (replenished from a small intake tube above the heel) to keep steps quiet. The dark-stained foot ware also has tools hidden in the top fold and inside slits along the heel, to aid in gaining entrance unannounced.
It's mithril, yes but the maker either didn't know how to forge it or the metal cooled wrong.  This doesn't feel right in the hand and doesn't move fluidly in combat.

After the failed defense of Prantz, bodies littered the city and surrounding areas. Despite Rael's attempts to collect all the armor and weapons from the battle areas, a few of these suits of half-plate found their way off of the men and women who in life wore them, and into the black markets.

Worn by the mages that help defend Sadinia on Voltrex, these robes were scavenged from a battlefield in southern Dregar. Why they were there, and who they fought is unknown. The Sadinian ruling council has requested the return of all items belonging to their mages, but with information as to the purpose of the battle and the reason so many mages were found dead not forthcoming, the robes have begun to sneak out of custody and into the marketplace. 

The robes themselves are powdery blue with black trim, woven through with mithril thread much thicker than standard reinforced clothing. They also carry powerful enchantments that can be cast upon the wearer.
This suit was formed from several parts off of dead, broken and dismantled constructs. Woven with Al'Noth it has become a good suit to have should one be dealing with constructs.
This large shield is particularly good at deflecting missile attacks off its flared edges. Rumor has it the design dates back to the human-elf wars, as used by the humans.
Useful for day and night reconnaissance, these enchanted leathers are given to scouts of the Wolfswood Ranger Corps. Scouting being as dangerous as it is, not every owner of a suit returns.

This rather ingenious shortbow was clearly crafted by a follower of Shadon as the emblem of this deity is etched into the handle of the bow.

The ingenuity of this crafty little bow comes in two fashions.  First, at the top end of the bow a masterkey has been fashioned with a series of retractable lockpicks and other various size ranges of picks and gadgets for use in finding the softer spots of locks and traps.  But more impressive then this is the fact that the bow is actually trapped.  At the bottom the core of an electrical trap has been intricately designed with a bow string attached to the trap's core so that a surge of electricity will course through the string just as it's released and fly towards the target.  The trap itself is clearly enchanted in some fashion beyond mere tinkering and design, as it glows a shade of blue and purple and sparks now and then with powers surpassing a simple gnomish tinkerer.

It is clear this bow has a tendency to kill those unskilled however, as numerous bloodstains are found on the bow itself, most likely from both battle and error in the function of the trapping bow.

// GM NOTE: The arrows produced from this bow are for the sole use of the bow's owner and are not to be traded or sold under any circumstances.
A curious metal protrusion comes off the top end of this bow... it almost looks like a key.  At the bottom end of the bow the string is wound around what seems to be a trap of some sort.

Found at the bottom of a small, now-defunct enclave of Rofireinite priests, these one-handed staves seemed designed to repel undead that would find a desert environment hospitable. Since the re-discovery of the abandoned monastery, the staves have been reproduced and named for the city closest to their origin.

The runes of an intricate maze are etched into the side of this roughly crafted greataxe. The minotaurs make such weapons to assist in navigating the dungeons and mazes where they dwell. Always a fondness for traps and paths of complexity, the minotaurs betray their bestial nature with a fierce cunning. Those poor souls lost in their tunnels wander aimlessly for miles in fatigue through endless perils before the Maze Lords command their forces upon them. The bite of this axe may also send the mind into a maze, leaving an enemy lost on its feet.

This double scimitar was the lifes work of a man from Dregar. He was constantly seeking to balance good and evil. His attempt with this weapon was to find a balance by combining each. Positive, and Negative, Light and Darkness.

Created by a dwarven clan deep in the Spine Mountains of Tilmar during an extended war with dark elves from the deep, and later...other things, a few of these morningstar maces have made their way into the hands of traders and occasionally adventuring souls.
Created by a Dorand-worshipping craftswoman who moved to Gi from the Brech Mountains to join the community, these weapons stress fluidity and forethought as well as lethal efficiency.
Light as a feather, this finely crafted bow's strings are quite warm to the touch.

A brutal mercenary from Dregar wielded this scythe. Some who stood their ground were frozen in fear as they saw this weapon bear down on them. It got to the point that people simply ran when they saw this sinister weapon coming at them, for they knew if they stood their ground death would be greeting them soon.

The powerful dwarf Jorgan Graniteside once wielded this axe around 1402, the Dark Ages of Layonara. He was a quiet fellow, but his axe spoke volumes. He was rumored to have bested an entire group of powerful ogres single-handed that attacked attempting to steal the ore he mined earlier that day. With this mighty axe in hand Jorgan had an ability to call upon an inner rage making him far stronger than normal. However this strength came at a price and that was his eventual downfall. Several years later copies of his mighty axe began to show up across the lands.

Tales speak of a rogue whose delicate touch was his bread and butter searching for a way to avoid damage to his fingers in combat; after experimenting with a metal gauntlet on his off hand, he struck on the idea of a bracer worn on the off hand with a fixed blade jutting from the fist. With the flare of the bracer, people often mistake it for a buckler with a fixed blade. Whatever it is, it's very useful for deflecting attacks and does not require the skills required by larger, more bulky shields.

This goad was changed from a simple tool that herds cattle into a formidable weapon against snakes and other vermin. A man who often roamed the deserts of Mistone had this made after having to many run-ins with snakes.

A halfling thief from Vehl once called this hammer his own. He would leap out at his targets and SMACK! land this hammers head right on their foot. Typically sending the target to the ground and often slowed considerably because of how badly they would hobble on one foot when trying to chase him down.

This sword was commissioned by Tsaryn, a Blackguard of Corath from smiths in Gi. Their fine work was unbeknownst to them enchanted with dark magic, and then used to kill the smith and a few other villagers when Tsaryn returned test his new toy.
These Arrows are said to have been blessed by the Longstrider, Folian S'Pae. They are handed out to those that excel in carrying out his will.
This potion will heal the target 70 - 100 points of damage.

Created by the mage Miza four hundred years ago, these armored neckpieces provided extra protection for his personal guard. His eventual death and the bickering over his considerable estate resulted in a goodly number of his more interesting creations being crated away for centuries. Just before Sinthar's return, a few of these crates were opened by curious distant relatives, and the gorgets were quickly discovered and replicated. Now the occasional copy is popping up in markets all over Layonara.

This chunk of ore is imbued with the protective magics typical of olden dwarven clans.  Built by dwarves golems  made of ore such as this were enchanted prior to completion so that their protective mithril coating would be resistant to all elemental attacks, and thus resist both attacks and the depreciation to time.
A strangely bright chunk of ore.
Strands of silk gathered from the cocoon of a Bebilith.
Padding made from the silk of a Queen Spider.

Notes:  Legend of Iliarial

By Hadrian Quillsong


In my days of research, I have come across a legend most intriguing.  The validity of it I have sought to test, far and wide.  Of it's truth, I've found little backing.  It remains, however, one of the more interesting, though elusive, tales I've researched.

Tattered parchments that for all I may know may be the figment of a bard's imagination put on paper, tell of a line of kings who bore the name Iliarial.  These parchments were brought to me by a fellow scholar of ancient peoples, and though I am curious to what is written, I was not impressed by their condition.  What I did note was that the parchment used was a strange variant of paper from a yew tree, which is quite rare to begin with and generally not wasted on trifle tales.  The condition of the parchment was pitiful however, and knowing the lasting nature of paper made from yew, it would seem that these texts are quite ancient indeed.

The apparent writer was seeking out some ruins, his purpose for doing so quite obvious... to loot them.  From what I have made out from his text, written in a curious mixture of the Elvish and T'oleflor languages, these ruins were of a kingdom ruled by men, with the surname of Iliarial.  I have not been able to determine where he indicated these ruins were, though vague references seem to cancel out the possibility of Mistone or the greater Dregar continents.  The Ruins of Iliarial seem to have held some allure to this adventurer of old, passages I've translated such as the following indicate adequate optimism:

"Statues of rubies, shields of emeralds, cloths sewn from diamonds... hold for me Iliarials Tomb will."

Or:

"Found the key I have, or found the key has me.  The key the key, the key to loosening the ancient blades."

Various mentions of treasures pour out in the little readable text I have.  And for an apparent rogue such as our writer, the allure is clear.  The old names for mithril and titanium are used, and some mention of magical silver is made several times, though the translation is difficult on these topics.  Needless to say, our writer felt that this kingdom of men had quite a command over their crafts, in particular magical imbuing if I've read correctly.  The magical nature of this culture is made clear in several passages:

"Never seen metals of golems I have seen..."

Or:

"Statues live or dead neither have been, wandering the hallways where I have hidden..."

The latter passage is interesting to note, as it implies the rogue adventurer did indeed see these ruins, and perhaps walk their halls if any still stand.  In my research this has confused me the most, as the writer implied the only access to these ruins was a magical password.  In one section he suggests he has discovered the password, and much to my lamentations this section has been oddly burned from its page.  However, multiple mentions of passwords fill these pages, and they hold a notable theme.  See here phrases used repeatedly, and sometimes even with reference to a password:

"Virtue and Justice"
"Golden on thy Skin"
"Wisdom beget Knowledge"
"Hraykirlar of Lihariax"  Note: This latter word appears unfinished in the scripts.
"Reverence and Honor"
"Debasement of Evil"
"The Broken Blade"

There may in fact be several more passwords, though these phrases seem indicative.  My confusion on this subject arises on the validity of this writer even seeing the ruins.  As mentioned, he claims to have seen these treasures and magical apparatus.  He claims to have seen many things, which I will proceed onto shortly.  But the problem with these claims comes in the introductory passage:

"If to never again be seen may I be, then leave these pages for you I will.  And if to be doomed I am, then under the first treasured gem will again you see me.  I go now to the floatingman's tree, for my password I think will to he bring me...."

The remainder of this passage has withered over time, and I have been unable to finish the last sentence nor the obviously positioned password underneath this farewell.  Regardless, it becomes a contradiction with other passages describing the ruins in full, since this text begins as a departing tale.  The plausibility therefore of Iliarial's Ruins is fully in question based on this fact.

But still I seek it out.  The single most disturbing passages have been quite difficult to translate, but there seems to be a motif of what can be best described as light becoming darkness.  Whether this is literal or figurative, the wording is not descriptive enough to say for certain.  However, there is clear reference to demons several times in the text.  Once again these references appear to have been written in hindsight.
