There is no rhyme or reason to this reference, though light to darkness, and either fire to ice or ice to fire, is mentioned several times in conjunction with demonic parallels.  For this reason I believe there is a figurative expression herein.  Especially when coupled with the probable passwords which indicate what can best be described as Toranite, Voraxian, or perhaps even Rofireinite sentiments.  The possible age of this parchment begs questions as to what gods were even in power at the time, however that is not our focus.  These ruins, or the tale of them, appear to contain a fallen grace theme, which becomes quite colorful at times.  I shall continue to seek the truth on this matter out, but for now I have recorded this for the benefit of other researchers that might know something of the names or implied histories within these texts.

One last note regarding the possibility of a password or other such code to enter these ruins, again if they should in fact have an entrance.  On every page of the rogue adventurer's parchments there lay a strange symbol in the center of each page.  I do not understand the nature of this symbol as it is quite foreign to anything I've seen before.  However, should it be required to fashion something with this symbol to fit a keylock perhaps, or simply to recognize it as some key to a puzzle... I am tracing it on the following page to make sure anyone who does go out in search of these ruins has this symbol in front of them to decipher.  Should this symbol be integral to entrance, or escape for that matter, of these ruins, it is my recommendation that all who seek out the Ruins of Iliarial bring a copy of this symbol as I have taken great care to trace it in its full detail in this tome.

*The book contains several notes, and carved within the core pages there is a small stone with the engraving of an eye.  The eye has strange slits and glows blue, as sapphire dust seems to have been sprinkled and bonded in the carved slits.*

The journey to the caverns is one I've heard many a tale of.  But the true impetus of my travels came from the best known of them, which I include here for all adventurers to see:


"Here lies the tale of Harolgar, Frostblade of the White Fox Clan....

The first levels were all sculpted by dwarven hands, regular and smooth walls, gentle slopes and stones alive with arcane light at regular intervals. Our dwarven companion told us that these caverns were very old and even he was surprised that not even time managed to take away its beauty. Residents of these upper caverns were all sorts of small beasts and clans of humanoid creatures, nothing that our group of well worn campaigners couldn't handle.

As we descended we came upon the last dwarven tunnel, a hallway that led to a large natural cavern. The hall was roughly as though the cutters broke through into the cavern and left their duties of perfecting the path for another time, one that never came. Thus began a descent deeper and deeper, tunnels not dug by hands but burrowed or even eaten from the solid core of the mountain high above us lead from cavern to cavern. No more level rooms were to be found as we went down, further and further into Layonara. The simple clans and beasts from above grew scarce as deeper and fouler beasts, some that have never seen the sun, turned common and our group now trekked slowly and carefully.

Agheas, our cleric, felt himself sick after coming to a lit cavern with walls covered in a stinking gray mold. He said he felt death in the air, he felt life seeping away, stolen by the mold that surrounded us, he felt as though we were crossing a gateway from life into unlife, a feeling that none of us shared with him but we all felt as we pressed on deeper.

Beyond the gray mold room, the caverns and hallways were empty of life and even our dwarf sensed that the stone, always so true to him, started to lie. An uneasy silence muffled the noise of our armor, not even our bard's song could keep it away. Cavern upon cavern of silence passed as we lost track of time and became increasingly worried of what lay beyond the next curve of the now grotesque tunnels, irregular as the slime of a slug's path.

As our will to press on wore to thin, we reached a cavern deep within the world. Its floor was flat, solid and glossy black to our arcane light and torches, the surface of a great underground lake separated us from the other exits on the other side of the odorless black water. Our expedition halted and breathed in relief for we were now forced to turn back for none of us had a way of crossing this mere. We sat on the shore sharing a quiet meal, for we were now headed back, when a subtle movement in the deep caused a single ripple spread over the water - the silent roar stole the rest of our courage and our party of weathered adventurers that have braved dragons and armies of undead ran for our lives as frightened children.

We regrouped in a cavern far above the lake and started our trek upwards, unsure of what we had seen but sure that it wasn't a good omen of what lay beyond.

Perhaps the menace is a thing lurking in the black depths or perhaps it was nothing but our heads. "

My travels did not take me as far as these proport to have seen, and no knowledge do I have of this 'lurking' menace.  Only dwarven halls have I seen, and at their end, a strange carving of letters in stone which I dared not riddle out following the burns from misjudged notions, and the slithering cobras that rose from the pits at my guesses.  I've done much research since, and have found no true keys.  The tales of the caverns tell only of azure pools, the azure eye, azure riches, and the azure soul... I can not speculate as to what truly lies beyond the dwarven gates nor what this speech of things blue truly means.  There is not even a riddle to derive a thought from, it is only the gates, and the letters.  I'd tried to use the plates to speak 'open'... but as I said... it yielded only near death.  Someday I will find the missing peices of this puzzle.

The dwarven clan home itself is a mystery to me.  Through the annals of the Runic Anvil have I searched, and the only tale I find is of a clan of dwarves which settled in the Great Spikes to create their city called K'halziras.  Their thane had apparently sought the riches of the cold mountains and led his clan there some centuries ago.  I can tell you from the little I've seen that while riches they might have found, and a glorious clanhome their efforts yielded... they found also their deaths.  Or perhaps they abandoned it... though the dwarven bones seem to defy that notion.  Or... just maybe I would venture, they did not all die, and now live beyond that passage.  Ah... one day I will find my answer.

A very in-depth study of the various magical attacks utilized by golems and their constructors. It seems the scribes who copied this book did so in extreme detail, so all footnotes, side notes, cross outs, and doodles are also included. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
A Study and Details of Constructs and Their Elemental Abilities

A copy of a treatise on those who defend the forests, written by a druid who was later left his order and then joined the Wolfswood Rangers. His transcriptions of spellsongs and spellweaving done by the creatures is woven into the  pages and translated into common. Excerpt: "She moved as a faun, her hooves as delicate, her modesty unheeded except for natural fur around her hips; and I could not look away for despite the goat-shaped pupils, she was as beautiful as anything I'd ever seen. It was then she sang and the voice - oh, the voice! - My falling into slumber was worth the glimpse, for the satyrs are most protective of their females." As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
Beauties and Beasts: Dryads, Satyrs, and Other Forest Natives

Dark elves are the enemy. We have known this for millennia, and as they and Milara become bolder in their assertions of the surface, we can no longer hide our eyes and pretend they will stay out of the light. Read these pages and know them; their spells, their abilities, and their treachery. Be ready - for they have the patience of a spider and they have been waiting." As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.

A thin book that includes magical studies of shaman and the few magically gifted orcs, goblins, ogres, and (included in the author's estimation) giants. Spell gestures are carefully described on the pages in common with trigger words that will release the magic. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
Shaman and Magic: Of Orcs, Goblins and Other Inferior Races

The title on the binding and cover says it all. A wealthy man wanted to be able to summon beasts to aid him but he had no Divine connection to any deity. Nor did he have any knowledge of the Al'Noth. What he did have was stacks and stacks of True coin. Which it took most of before this book was perfected.

Page upon page of creatures from the briny deep and the spells they learn to cast under water; from slimy aboleths to the Saguahin to the monstrous kraken, each creature is given a diagram and in the cases where spells are cast, the magic is woven into the pages. As these are copies and not well made, the book becomes worse for wear with each spell released until it finally disintegrates.
The first knuckle of a troll carved with arcane symbols. Rumored to be made by a necromancer from around the River of Darkness, but not verified

The origin of these boots is unknown.  What tribe of men found a shaman to imbue them with their strange powers is a mystery, though it is clear by the shape of the boots that it was either half-orcs, humans, or something of that general size.

The actual leather of these boots has stone sewn and pressed in with no apparent pattern.  Extremely heavy for a pair of boots, the obvious detriment of wearing them is that they are harder to lift and move around, and generally clink together as one moves.

The enchantment appears to lie in the stone of the boots, as whatever devious shaman created these also allowed the wearer to evoke the protective magic of the stones around them for short durations.  Additionally, those wearing the boots have always felt hardier, healthier, and as strong as the stone itself.
Extremely heavy boots, they look to have chunks of strange rock sewn into them.

Jorel, a ranger from the far northern reaches of Krashin. A man of honor, he held a great hatred for all aspects of the dark arts. The reasons behind his deep hatred sprung from a fountain lost in history, but it is known that his mission throughout life would bring a reckless doom onto all magic users.

Throughout his life, Jorel made the mistake of entrusting a gnomish mage to smith and enchant weapons, armors, and other creations of antimagery. At first Jorel would be applauded for his efforts in destroying necromancers throughout the lands. But in his ignorance and arrogance, his goals shifted towards darkness themselves, as he began to slay all things magic, good and evil alike.

The gnomish mage, still in his youth, was named Klinkutter Hogsbreath. An honorable young gnome with a bright future in tinkering and magic alike, Klinkutter began aiding Jorel with the purest of intentions. As Jorel began his blind crusade however, Klinkutter reluctantly sought to somehow cease the madness by enchanting these creations. So one day he imbued them all with the ability for only a truly good being to wield them. He merely sought to teach his dear friend Jorel a lesson in what it was he was doing. Jorel, however, rushed foolishly into battle that evening, only to find the weapons burn in his hands, his cloak withering from his shoulders. He fell dead that night to the mages he had rushed upon, feebly charging with his fists alone.

Klinkutter fell to insanity after hearing the news, unable to distinguish his mistake in the hard lesson he had ultimately failed to teach. He withdrew to the swamplands of Belinara, never to be seen again.

This cloak is one of many of Klinkutter's creations for Jorel.  It's threads are powerfully imbued with a resiliance to all things magic, as well as regenerative qualities and magics of hardiness.  The nature of the strange threads of this cloak make it mostly transparent.
A heavy cloak with broad shoulders.  It is clearly made for the most stout of warriors.

This robe is fantiastically woven from enchanted silks from the webbing of driders.  Rubies from the Deep adorn the chest and waistbelt of this highly magical robe, while enchanted mithril ore is inset on the belt and wrist cufflinks.

The robe itself seems to be imbued with powerful, yet dark magics.  The make is familiar to most familiar with the lore of the Deep, clearly the workigns of powerful dark elves using the finest of materials available to them.

It is truly a beautiful robe to behold, though the make of it offers very little thought to the movement of the wearer.

Feryl Drakeblood was a monster of a man who, with four kills to his credit, thought he had perfected the art of dragon slaying. He aided his efforts by creating magical equipment from his previous victories, including several different boots he mockingly called his Dragon Slippers. Amazingly, Feryl was not defeated by his preferred enemy, but was surprised by a small band of goblins on his way to a hunt.

These boots are all that remains of Feryl's legacy, and retain the lingering enchantments of this man's life of dragon slaying.  Who or what imbued these magics on the Dragon Slippers is unknown, be it Feryl or a hired scholar of magic and enchantment.  What does seem clear, is that the magics imbued within carry with them a distinct air of Feryl's attributes and deeds, both good and bad.  It is said that the gods amongst olden dragons had long ago laid an ancient curse upon these boots, and that all who wear them will one day meet the dragon who knows them for what they are, and exposes that weakness in the bearer's slaughter.

This belt is commonly known as a Goranite creation.  The first of these were known to appear around 1376, and with that date known, they are likely the creation of Gringilian Hobnoblik the gnomish inventor of Dregar lore.  Like many of his other creations, the quality of the creation is a mixture of mechanical and magical invention.  Gringilian was known for his outspoken support for those mages and inventors of the lands to find means to combat the forces of Sinthar Bloodstone.  His particular focus seemed to be in allowing the common man to take up arms, even if untrained and unexceptional.  This shield is an excellent example of that effort.

Aside from having a beautifully carved and enchanted cobalt emblem for a buckle which is adorned spectacularly with extremely small diamonds in a jumbled mix that would seem reminiscent of the constellation of Goran's Tool, the ingenuity of the belt comes in a rolling blue ball that rests magnetically on a single iron spine that wraps around the belt.  The spine itself seems a contorted weave, and as the wearer of the belt moves, the ball seems to roll about erratically.  The ball and spine itself are clearly enchanted with some curious manner of magic, as the ball seems to roll in a direction to counterweight the body's movement in increments of impressive minutia.

The function and impressive magic behind this seems to allow the most common of men to adjust to the weight of a shield on their arm, and it is said to also aid even in the balancing of two weapons wielded.

Constructed from the silk gathered from killed rock devourers, this armor is as impressive as the beast from whom the silk derives.  Rock devourers are peculiar to the many regions of the Deep.  They burrow through stone and ore, and are known to be near impossible to kill.

It is said that the Ether Giants are the masters of storms and the lords amongst all giants.

With their superior intellect and culture, the Ethers are known to have blessed the lands with several notable creations and relics of old.  This helmet is one such relic.

What clan of Ethers was behind this particular crafted feat is unknown, though the quality is clear.  Made of cobalt melded ore, the helmet is infused with a magic that is quite apparent to the wearer.  Upon initial contact with the bearer of the helm, a tingling is felt all over the body, and a noise that can only be described as a distant and shimmering thunderclap is 'felt' within the bones of their head.

Ancient documents exist still of the first known war where elves, dwarves, and humans united.  In the effort to protect their own lands as well as that of the less established free races of gnomes and halflings alike, the nations once at war united to combat the hordes of monstrous beings in the years of the -1800's.

During this age of strife coupled with unprecedented racial unity, the existance of many heroes had been documented and still exist in journals today.  One group of heroes emerged in these annals that would be known as the Order of Hryndel, a group who seems by all accounts to have held faith to an order that most closely resembles what we know today as a Sacred Fist.   As for what religion they followed is lost to time.  What is known is that these guantlets bear their namesake for the small but ever vigilant temple of this order.  It is said that during the wars of this tumultuous age, Hryndel's order patrolled the borderlands of lesser, mostly defenseless towns, villages, and clans of all races alike.  They would cover massive distances at great speeds to ensure their watch, acting purely in a defensive manner which exhibited their distaste for the allegiances and goals of the wars.  The order protected the free races they knew to exist in relative peace, but they operated under no banner save for this common effort of this particular vigil.

Shunned by the armies of humans, dwarves, and elves during their age of war for their non-participation in any semblance of the alliance's organization... time has told Hryndel's tale far more fondly as history looks back at their efforts.  By all estimation this strange order was vastly more effective then the larger armies organized by rulers of varying origin, and in their purely defensive task they likely provided a means for more constant supply of surviving youth to join ranks in the wars.

The guantlets themselves are made by a strangely flexible weave of cobalt scales laid over an extremely thick leather of unknown origin.  What power has blessed these gloves is not known by many, but their vigil remains eternal in the hands of those that live up to their namesake's intent.
These gloves sparkle at the fingers' tips.

Known amongst the slaves of the Deep, the mere mention of this cloak brings hope to those who find no solace on their horizon.

Its weave is simple, its fabrics plain, no jewels adorn it, and no precious ores are lined in it's threads.  Nevertheless it is beautiful in it's simplicity, and the loving and dedicated care that has gone into each of it's type is evident as your hand grazes over the smooth cloth.

The emblems of three gods adorn this shield in three corners.  Vierdri'ira, Baraeon Da'Cuz, and Sulterio.

At it's center there lies a word, written in a script most likely of Deep Gnomish origin:  "Contumacy".

As the emblems are examined closer, it is obvious that they are defaced in an impressively intricate manner.  Images of bright green emeralds peirce the emblems, in an almost illusory or animated manner.  Fires are etched in tiny detail on the emblems, in an image as though each are about to explode.  The illustrations are strewn about showing dying spiders, mushrooms cleaved, broken whips, shattered ores, and a variety of other defiant gestures.

The origin of the shield is unknown, but the intent clear.  This shield is a defiant gesture of the enemies of the deep dwarves and elves, and likely all origins of oppression in the Deep.  The images of emeralds imply the faith of Beryl, and given the historical nature of the Deep Gnomes, this is likely a shield made in honor of the slave's defiance.  And a bold one at that.

The shield's make offers obvious enchantments, and a blue aura of magic eminates from it's edges.  The design is peculiar, and seems to have a protective upper section as though geared towards foes of a certain size.
The symbols of dark gods adorn this strange shield.

A flat square ruby lies along the tarsal line of the gloves, glowing a warm gentle red with the occasional spark emitting now and then. The glove fabric itself shimmers with strange glows, usually rotating and cycling between a black and white. It can only be speculated as to whom crafted these masterpieces.

A mask of leather and wolf fur made to look like a hound's face that aids a stealthy individual with alertness and perception. Said to have been first created by Branderbackian mages, a very limited number of copies have been made.

Several sources have been credited for these powerful cloaks; Aeridin's Church being one, Az'attan's being another. The cloaks themselves provide a boost against most venoms and also grant the wearer the ability to see magically cloaked individuals.

A set of robes for the battle cleric, made by the aged tailor mage Shelia Basting of Spellgard. When pressed about her personal worship, she refuses to give up her denomination (if any) -- her work, she says, "is for everyone".

Once a featured dancer in the taverns around Port Hempstead, Edna Reelhawk slowly succumbed to age, as we all do. She fought, however, and fought hard; first by dying her hair, then using every anti-aging medicine she could find. When finally she could not gloss over the cracks, she turned to magic. She began paying to have her favorite dancing clothes enchanted to add to her physique and beauty. When her dancing clothes failed to cover her advanced years, she turned to questionable magics, that failed...fatally. Her enchanter was given the outfit he spent so much time weaving magic into and he decided to make a few copies and cash in on the desire for the illusion of eternal youth.
Having seen several of the normal archers belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.
Having seen several of the normal brawlers belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.
Having seen several of the normal swordsmans belts. A tailor decided to see if he could improve upon them. This was the result of his many years of hard work.

Very few men and women believe that the world they live on is only one of many; most cling to the belief that their reality is the only one in existence. Fewer still have proof of another pit, and only a few handfuls have walked more than one.  These boots, exceedingly rare, are rumored to be a copy of a pair worn by a creature "not of Layonara"...and for the brave handfuls who travel far beyond their comfort zone, are very sought after

Worn by any officer of Molvaren's that lead troops numbering one-hundred or greater, these green broadcloth sashes have a mark similar to the tattoos that etched the skin of Molvaren's sentient tools enchanted indelibly upon the buckle. No attempt so far to remove the mark has worked, and that is why despite their power the sashes are rarely used.
Sash of a Green Dragon Officer

Tales from battle lines in Rael speak of a warrior infamous for "turtling" behind his shield. After his shield's poor balance was used against him one too many times, he had a shield of this design made using the Al'Noth and mundane counterbalancing to foil those attacks and leave him on his feet.

"These boots were made by the gnomish inventor Yolanda Shinstepp. She loved to go dancing and found that the larger people at the Tavern would knock her around while on the dance floor. She could not make people watch out for the little folks, so she got to working on an item that would improve her dancing and keep her from being knocked around.
 
After a few years of testing and failed prototypes she came up with her dancing boots. They were an instant hit with people who tried them on. They could dance the night away without fear of bumping into others, even when they got drunk. People actually got better the more they drank.
 
After a few years she started to get a desire to wear her Dancing boots even when not dancing. It got to the point where she never took them off, even to bathe.

Curious boots, these were produced by elvish rangers around the time of Folian's rise as a deity of the lands.  In reverence to their god, these boots were initially worn with only a minor enchantment allowing deft movement about the woodland regions.  But in time, as the rangers proved their faith to Folian in their practice as diligant rangers of the lands, Folian allowed a blessing to be achieved within the soles of these boots.

As history tells it, the actual bootmaker of these had hardened the leather near the sole, which was initially frowned upon by the other rangers of their vale as it would be noisy on the leaves of the forest.  But the bootmaker retorted, saying that the true ranger of Folian would be able to connect with the very breaths of the land, it's movements, and the movements of all things around him.  He said that the blessing and enchantment that he'd provided these simple boots would feel the very vibration of the lands and everything in them.  He claimed that the appearance of the land would change, that the true ranger would see all around him in a new light, in full connection with the lands.  He also claimed that this ability would render them quicker on their feet, more capable of reaction and perhaps even foresight to those actions around them.

For many years, his boots did no such thing other then make increased noise in the woodlands.  But the rangers held true to their faith, and it is of course part of the legend, that it was indeed Folian who eventually saw it fit to bless these boots.
A pair of old leather boots with a symbol of a wolf etched in to the sole.

The Lichbane Mace.  In it's simplicity it earns great respect amongst all living beings opposed to undeath and necromancy.  The make of these maces are said to have derived from The Shining Hand of Toran sometime around the 5th century following the cataclysm.  These weapons were distributed amongst the Order of Undead Hunters at that time, though in recent ages the making of such weapons seems a lost art.

The weapon is quite simple and quite plain despite it's powerful enchantments.  The metals and ores used are simple and unimpressive, though the rough edges glimmer with a magic and divine energy crackling within.  One lone mithril ring of ore circles the mace at it's midline, and a gold star made of a tiny topaz shines alone, centered on that ring.

This old blade shows curious craftsmanship.  A strange ore comprises the majority of the blade, it seems iron at first but is warm to the touch.

The tales surrounding this blade are many, and date as far back as the race wars following the great cataclysm.  Which race made it is uncertain, for it is the same type of tale each time, though in each it pits the other as the enemy.

What is consistent is the reasoning behind it's construction in each tale.  In each, a melancholy hero has his family slaughtered in an apparent act of random violence based on their race alone.  Throughout the stories, the violence is unwarranted, unexpected, and a matter of poor luck in the face of racial hatred.  It's theme circles around the terrible reality of random violence, and pain in the face of having that tragedy befall the hero unfairly.

For all races, they have clung onto these tales of their blades as a coming of reckoning, lashing out at the chaos of violence on tribes, families, clans, and towns undeserving.  The enchantments on the blade show no sign of truth in one tale or the next, and what tragedy truly resulted in the construction and enchantment of these beautiful masterpeices.. it is clear that the will behind it finds unity amongst all races... that undeserving violence will face it's day of reckoning.
This shaft of wood is used in the making of bronze weapons.

In K'halziras tradition, the greatest warriors of the clan were the Deep Hunters.  Defense from the tribes and wilds aboveland were left to the main defenders of the dwarven clan.  But to venture into the depths, to defend the clanhome from the Azure threat that lay in wait... this was a task for only the Deep Hunters.

The rangers of K'halziras were not rangers in the traditional sense.  They were bred assassins, hunters of a known enemy.  With limited supplies these honored warriors would set forth, always alone, to combat the creatures of the Deep below their clanhome.  Survival and stealth was paramount to these hunters.  They sought out the greatest enemy of the K'halziras.  That which comes from the Azure Pools to steal man and dwarf from their home.

These axes are holy, and in the days of K'halziras, they were given to only a handful of hunters in each generation of the clan.  They are imbued with magics for seeking out this particular prey... though as tales tell, very few of the Azure Hunters would ever return from the depths they set out to assault.
K'halziras Holy Axe of the Azure Hunter

This dagger is well known amongst assassins.  The exceptionally sharp edge of the simple iron weapon has strange barbs at it's sides which are weakly molded to the blade.  On close examination, these barbs have numerous 'burrowing' protrustions.  The intent is that upon thrusting the blade into the victim, the barbs will break free and burrow with the victim's movement thereafter.

An impressive little blade, the magics imbued in the hilt and the blade itself are such that they enhance the seeking instinct of the hunter.

These blades were designed by an assassin of unknown origin, though it is suspected he found great success in them as his identity has always been concealed.  It is said that a blade of this type is left in the body of each victim he has found... and such is the reason for so many being available in marketplaces of the underworld.

Very little is identifiable about this weapon save for the elven words that circle the spiralling blade to it's tip.

"The darkness shall one day know my fear as it's own, for my blade is many, and its light shall glimmer in such number that it shall suffocate the emptiness of the Deep"

One of only a few weapons created by the mad weapon smith Argaman Harnoshan, one of the few surviving dwarf-human hybrids that snuck through before such cross-breeding stopped altogether in the early 1400's. Although Argaman lived through his birth and grew to manhood, most say his brains were not strapped in right and he was known to alternate between lucid periods of productivity and rage-fueled killing sprees in the wilds.

This Scimitar was the only weapon of a man known as the Desert Fox. To the best of any ones knowledge he spent his entire life in the Anuroch Desert. He avoided people whenever possible. But on a rare occasion a traveler would stumble upon him as he fought the local Desert Giants. His scimitar gleaming in the hot desert sun would cut them down like they were nothing. His blade was found hung as a trophy within a settlement of Desert giants... so one can only assume he was killed.

The Fiendish String, a terrible device constructed with the woven hairs of shadow beasts from a negative reality unlike your own.

The bow itself is of a strange wood foreign to your lands.  It is as though it exists only as a shadow of your world, a dark shadow draining to all things around it.

The string bears the most magical presence and force of the bow.  It is draining to the touch, and incredibly difficult to pull upon.  The power of the string unleashed however, is a sight to behold.  For as it whips forward projectiles of immense force and strength scream forth towards it's target, wailing their distant death cry as they whistle through the air.
An evil aura surrounds this dark bow.

From the copy of Rainstorff's axe that exists, reproductions have been made by several different dwarven smiths. A very few of these have been enchanted in an attempt to create a working copy of the great Vorax Champion's weapon. How close to the original these heavily enchanted and powerful copies are is unknown but at a couple seem to fit some of what is known of the great dwarven champion's weapon.

This walking stick burns with the flames eternal. One would think it would be smoldering hot, but no, it is quite cold to the touch. This is because it is food for the Fire Genesai. Those extra-planar beings craft these walking sticks to fuel their flames and fill their bellies on their long jaunts beyond the planes and into the mortal realm. Perpetually burning, the wood of this staff seems to soak up the heat around it, and visa versa... replenishing anew, only to be burned and burned again.
 
Mages who specialize in the ways of fire feel especially hungry while wielding this staff. They feel the need to cast even more fire than before, and occasionally lick of it its sweet barky sustenance as they make their long journeys across the mortal realm. This is hunger of the flame ever-burning. The blood of fire mages yearns for release when they wield this staff. The desire to burn, the desire to feed. And so, like the Fire Genesai who held this staff before them, they become bastions of the primal elements, yearning to engulf the world in flames. Some people live to watch the world burn. You would be one of these people, should you choose take up this staff. Your blood as flame, and the world around you, kindling.
Walking Stick of the Fire Genesai
This potion will heal the target 20d20 hitpoints.

These amulets, produced in mass quantity by a gnomish tinkerer by the name of Hriligril, were probably created in an effort for either Stone or Bloody Gate during the dark ages of Layonara.  They were reported lost during a shipment across Dregar intended to be sailed to Katherian.
A glimmering amulet with the initials HGL hanging off the neck of the chain.

The magics in this ring are quite astounding, and it is doubtful that anyone other then the most powerful of enchanters created this relic of power.

The ring itself appears to be a strangely enchanted ring of fortitude.  Dwarvish runes encircle the beautiful ring, they appear to hold magics warding off death or other evil blights.
A wonderfully beautiful golden ring.  Holding it in your hand you are quite taken with it's intricate detail.

Klinkutter Hogsbreath, the gnomish mage of the swamplands who ultimately fell to his own madness.  This strange creation is curiously made in a fashion which takes safety into consideration, a trait quite rare in the relics of this mad mage.

It is told that the gnomish magician began creating these staves early in his life, which would explain the less chaotic nature of it's make.  At it's tip lies a massive chunk of sapphire gem.  Klinkuter seems to have carefully enchanced the magical qualities of this large deposit of untouched crystal in order to imbue the holder with some of it's inherent resistances.

The actual base of the staff is split between ore and wooden handles.  Two adamantium segments have been split by a well designed yew handle.  While the weight of this staff is often awkward for most spinners of the weave, the handle seems perfectly placed for balance, insofar as to allow a small being such as even a halfling to find balance in it's movement.  Two diamonds lie inset at the top and bottom of the yew handle, and it is apparent that they have been enchanted with particular spells to supply the holder with elements of fortitude and will.
A large sapphire clings to the tip of this staff.  It's base feels warm to the touch.

This peculiar staff is made of two parts.  The base of the staff appears to be mahogany, while the tip of the staff is some sort of fashioned ivory tusk.  From what creature it came, not even the wisest of druids can discern.  The ivory is smoothed and very obviously enchanted with the weave.

These staves are said to derive from the northern isles of Krashin, though remarkably similar staves of identical construction show signs of origin in the southern hemisphere of Layonara as well.  The supposed origin of the Krashin isles indicates the enchantment by barbaric seers and wisemen that practiced both arcane and divine magics as the witchdoctors of their people.  The runes displayed on the mahogany portion of the staff are a mixture of arcane and divine expressions of magic, though the divine expressions are entirely linked to the natural world in the fashion a druid would find power in.

These staves are old, though not overly uncommon amongst the well travelled of the lands.  Their magic is rumored to bring good tidings to the natural world, and any wielder of this staff will find flow with both the weave and the land as he travels.
A rune circled wooden staff with an ivory tusk on the end.
Forged from blessed silken strands for the Sisters of Rebirth, rare amulets such as these are still found where one of the sisterhood may have fallen where seeking out the corrupted.
A simple band of mithril, this ring radiates magic but has no maker's mark.
This tomb when used on an Item.  Helps the user to see the effects of certain spells.
This tomb when used on an Item.  Helps the user to keep Discipline.
This Enchanted Ear from a Troll will add Regeneration to any Item.
This will add Darkvision to the item your Choice.
This will add Keen to the Weapon of your Choice.

This key was the brainchild of a halfling from the Hempsted area. He had hoped to create a key that once inserted into a lock would change its shape to move all the pins and tumblers into the proper position. Thus opening the lock. The drawback the key would destroy itself after one use. He never overcame this flaw thus the keys are highly sought after items.
This tomb when used on an Item.  Helps the user to to Carry a greater load, great distances.
Armor Stand - Male (Posses to make custom clothes)
Armor Stand - Female (Possess to make custom clothing)

This is used to maintain a matching connection between player IPs and their ip addresses.  Don't mess with it.  There should be one per module.
This is used to store regex memory.
Mostly immobile at it's great age, this golem, once powerful, has become one with the forest around it, overgrown, almost lost to time as the world grows over it's now gnarled and rooted body.
Vicious and raging. This most dangerous fowl would make a succulent meal if you can manage to survive its fury!
This is the automated gnomish room renter, would you like a room?

NOTE:  If you remove yourself as the registered owner, you will no longer be able to retrieve gold from this tavern's sales.  The next person to use this device will have the option of making themselves the owner.  Do you really wish to remove yourself as the registered owner?

I want to make myself the owner of this tavern.
