Halflings
    Lightfoot halflings are a small race of people, but they make up for their short stature through many other useful characteristics. They are a a clever, enterprising, adaptable and extremely resourceful people, and what they lack in strength, they make up in agility. Halflings are about the same height as gnomes, standing at around 3 feet tall, but they have an even lighter frame, weighing, on average, 30 pounds. Their adaptable nature means they can assimilate themselves into any civil community on Layonara with minimal problems. Due to this carefree adaptability, you will find halflings in settlements across the world. While dwarves and gnomes value their facial hair, halflings rarely grow beards. Halflings are longer-lived than humans, but compared to other races they have a below-average life expectancy of about 270 years. Their adaptability also makes them good, solid adventurers, and their curious nature often drives them to the adventuring life.
Lightfoot halflings tend to form matriarchal nomadic clans that gravitate to places where work can be found or new unexplored lands. The mother of the clan, also known as the Story Teller, normally leads the clan in a collective direction. She also represents the clan in case of conflict and is in charge of passing the knowledge they have gained to next generations. Halfling families tend to be composed of a husband and a wife, but many clans have no qualms with a female having several husbands. 

    The varieties of halflings found in Layonara are Ghostwise Halflings and Strongheart Halfings.  I will now write a few lines about each.

Ghostwise Halflings
    Ghostwise halflings were once very much akin to their lightfoot cousins. But as they explored the lands, this small tribe of halflings came to see the atrocities commited by the bigger races. They asked all the tribes to unite to bring a balance to the chaos, but they were harshly turned down. Refusing to mimic those that they disliked the most, The Wise Tribes, as they were known at that time, decided to retire from civilized areas and isolate themselves in the forests. As time passed they chose to forget many of the lightfoot ways, opting for quiet meditation instead of non-stop adventuring. They Wise Tribes stopped worshiping Deliar and Prunilla, although they never stopped respecting the couple. They became a self-sufficient race and as such they respected their ancestors more than anything. Coming to worship their ancestors, or the "ghosts" of their past, and became to be known as the Ghostwise.

Personality: 
    Ghostwise halflings are very timid and shy. They come to trust very few, and are especially wary of tallfolk. Their lives are based around the survival of their tribe and its traditions; every ghostwise halfling is as important as the other, but the history of the tribe must survive before anything else. As such, very few of them leave their treetop villages and only do so under extreme circumstances or when facing "The Ritual of Change."

Physical Description: 
    Ghostwise halflings look very much like their lightfoot cousins in stature. Not as nimble as their cousins, some Ghostwise tend be slightly stockier in build. When leaving their treetop villages, they tend to spend most of their time outside in the sun, giving them slightly tanned skins and a light brown hair. Since they rely so much on physical communication, every Ghostwise has their name tattooed in tribal symbols on a visible place on their body, and many opt to tattoo many other tribal symbols representing people and events in their lives.

Relations with other races: 
    Ghostwise tend to trust very few outside races. They respect their cousins for carrying the same blood as their ancestors but never associate with them for extended periods of time. The only tall race they have come to freely associate with is the Wild Elves, as both races have many similar principles and traditions. It is not rare to see either Ghostwise halflings or Wild Elves visiting each other's tribes to share stories. Any other race they normally hold at an arm's distance and keep it that way.

Alignment: 
    Ghostwise seek balance, both inside themselves and around their homes, above all else. As such, most of them tend toward neutrality. A true Ghostwise is neutral to all and will not get involved in the bickering of the tall people unless their heritage is threatened.

Religion: 
    The Ghostwise stopped worshiping Deliar and Prunilla when the race split apart. They started depending on themselves and thusly hold inner strength above all. Ghostwise enjoy meditation to reach a balance within themselves, believing that inner balance is the first step to balancing one's environment. They hold Katia in great regard for giving them refuge in the forests, but never actively worship her. They respect their ancestors above all and worship the ghosts of the past. Ghostwise have many rituals of passage at different stages of their lives. The most noticeable is the Ritual of Naming and the Ritual of Change. The first one occurs when a Ghostwise reaches adulthood and is finally given her name tattoo. Before this event a child is known by many nicknames, and the one that sticks is the one tattooed onto her body. 

    The Ritual of Change occurs when a Ghostwise is not able to reach an inner balance and must seek it elsewhere. These halflings are given leave from their tribes to seek that which they need to reach a healthy state. Most Ghostwise seen roaming around the world are normally in the Ritual of Change.

Language: 
    This race of halflings, known by many as "The Silent," have developed a complex language of body expressions and hand movements. This language is so intricate that they do not need to speak in order to communicate with one another. Even when a ghostwise does speak, 90% of the time they use an old version of a halfling dialect originated during the racial split. Nevertheless, they are respectful of others, and will do their best at speaking the common language in the presence of those who will not understand them.

Names: 
    Ghostwise kept similar short first names as those of their lightfoot cousins as a sign of respect and everlasting brotherhood. However, they opted for different last names that portrayed their more naturalistic personality. Common last names are Slowillow, Stoutoak, Fallenleaf, and Wiseflower.

Adventurers: 
    Ghostwise adventurers are very rare. Normally every adventuring Ghostwise is undergoing the Ritual of Change. There are, however, Ghostwise exiles that venture the lands to either seek redemption for harm brought to the tribe or spread the seeds of the Ghosts across the world.

Strongheart Halflings
    Halflings, among the other small races, are normally known as The Children of the Earth. Many consider this a simple reference to the origin of dwarves, gnomes, and halflings, but these races know the words go far beyond that. 

    Strongheart halflings are far distant lightfoot cousins who opted to settle near mountainous regions. Brought together as a race by dwarven traders, Strongheart halflings are stout and healthy halflings that appreciate the way of the warrior and family life.

Personality: 
    Strongheart halflings are known to be the warmest of races. They treat most with a smile and a good story, and perhaps some ale or cider. They tend to their families with great responsibility and vigilantly maintain their clan and its surrounding areas. Many confuse Strongheart Halflings with young dwarves, for their love of battle is remarkable and many legends of Strongheart Giant Slayers have been assimilated into dwarven folklore. They tend not to wander the lands as much as their lightfoot cousins, thus many settled Strongheart clans are known around Layonara. The Fiercerock Clan is thought of as the strongest and most important clan, having settled a long time ago in the township of Stone.

Physical Description:
    Strongheart Halflings are not only thicker than lightfoots, but they are also taller, and consequently are often mistaken for small dwarves. Many Stronghearts are able to grow beards, and those who do are held in high regards within a clan. The women tend to be more settled than normal and grow wide hips that bear many children. "The larger the family, the stronger the clan" is a true Strongheart saying.

Relations with other races: 
    Stronghearts have a very stable trading tradition, especially with their dwarven brothers, as they like to call each other. They normally trade a lot with their lightfoot cousins, trusting them to spread Strongheart goods across the world. They get along and trade with humans, although they do not appreciate the rapid spread of their cities as much as dwarves do. They barely have contact with elves, and when they do, they have little in common to share. And as far as giants are concerned, to a Strongheart, the only good giant is a dead giant.

Alignment: 
    Strongheart Halflings respect the laws settled by the authorities of the lands they are in, and they keep utmost respect in their dealings with dwarves. As such, most of them tend to be Lawful Good.

Religion: 
    Stronghearts are very religious halflings, never missing an opportunity to celebrate and praise the couple that brought them here. They pray to Deliar every time they trade and truly worship him as The Protector. They love Prunilla for the gift of hearth and strong families and pray to her before every meal and during many family events. Many Strongheart clans have shrines to Vorax and Dorand to pay respect to their dwarven brothers.

Language: 
    Strongheart clans learn the language of those they trade with. As such they know the common language and they all strive to learn the dwarven trading language. They appreciate the halfling language and use it in their homes and among themselves.

Names: 
    Strongheart names are a strange combination of dwarven and hafling names. Common male names are Borki, Kasius, and Andrus. Female names are Jayla, Drasa, and Galgata. Their last names are always their clan name.

Adventurers: 
    Strongheart adventurers are normally those warriors sent to explore distant lands to meet other halfling and dwarven societies. Many also tend to go on adventures to train in battle before returning ready to defend their clans. But in many cases a Strongheart's life is simple and based entirely upon his homeland.
Small Bodies, Giant Spirits:  The Halflings of Layonara

Voltrex Locales

La'Mune Forest
    La'Mune forest, also called Moon Forest, is a forest in southern Voltrex, and like most forests on Voltrex, it is a place of rest and quiet.

Lake Sahale
    Lake Sahale is the largest lake on southern Voltrex and is fed by the small streams that come down from the Peaks of Voltrex as well as by the Emerald River.

Ulambree Forest
    A large forest in the center of the continent, Ulambree Forest is home to the largest tribe of Wood Elves on Layonara. Living in complete harmony with the forest, their villages are hard to find as they are high up in the trees. Nothing that goes on in Ulambree Forest remains undetected by these Elves.

Lilanthier Forest
    A large forest in the northwestern part of Voltrex which is home to many druids and rangers. It has almost overgrown the ruins of the old elven city of Ovdear

Relishian Forest 
    A small rainforest called the Relishian Forest lies at the northeastern tip of Voltrex. It is rumored that ages past, before the cataclysm and the Elven race wars, this is the jungle the Dark Elves lived in.

Emerald River
    The Emerald river winds its way through the foothills of the peaks towards Lake Sahale. Elven children are told stories about a unicorn that calls the banks of the Emerald River its home.

Peaks of Voltrex
    These mountains basically keep the island safe from attack on the western side. They are very rugged and form a natural barrier. They lead down to sharp corals in the ocean and those help to keep ships and boats away from land.

The Five Elven Towers 
    The Five Elven Towers have stood on Voltrex for ages and probably only the elves remember who commissioned their construction. Various rumors and folklore about these Towers abound outside of Voltrex, but one can distill the following information from these rumors.

    At the edge of the Evergreens, where the western winds that come in from the ocean and the eastern winds that are re-directed south-easterly by the Peaks of Voltrex meet, lies the Windy Outcrop. On top of the outcrop the Tower of Air rises into the sky. 
The winds are ever blowing around the Tower and change direction all the time. It is said that if the Winds ever stop, the precariously balanced tower will crash to the ground.  

    In the lush greenness of La'mune forest, the Tower of Nature placidly rises among the trees. All paths eventually lead here and one can always find lots of animals living peacefully together around the Tower's outskirts.

    The firm Tower of Earth stands rooted in the earth on top of a hill. Even miles away, one knows that the Tower is near due to the minor tremors that rock the area constantly.

    At the northern edge of the Peaks of Voltrex, in an area filled with crevices where the air is almost too hot to breathe and the occasional spurt of lava shoots into the sky, the Tower of Fire stands amidst a fiery blaze.
At Voltrex's northern edge, where the sea meets the land, is a cliff upon which the Tower of Water is built. It has been raining here since anyone can remember.

    Each Tower is home to a mage of a specific element, except the Tower of Nature, which houses a druid.

    Together, these five are the judging council for Elves when it comes to magic and power from the land and elements. The Council of Five are not the rulers of Voltrex, but their advice is always listened to.
Tales of Elven Landscapes:  The current state of knowledge about the continent of Voltrex

Az'atta

Aliases: The Heretic, The Wretched, The Redemptress  
Race: Dark Elf 
Worshippers: 
     Though she is a Dark Elf, any appropriately aligned intelligent being could worship Az'atta, as she is a goddess of penance, redemption, and love. Az'atta willingly accepts any that truly believe in these principles into her service.
Domains: Protection, Good 
Governs: Penance, redemption, love 

Dogma: 
     All creatures of Layonara are worthy of Az'atta's mercy, if they choose to accept it. You must offer all creatures, regardless of past acts, a chance to accept the mercy, redemption, and love offered by Az'atta. Go forth into the world and use your training and powers to serve and protect those in need in any way that you are able. Do not be passive, but be an active force for good in Layonara.
     Do not take up arms and armor, unless it is to protect yourself or others from harm.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Az'atta has no favored weapons for her clergy, as she prefers her clergy not to kill or harm anyone. She does place one restriction upon the weapon choices of her clerics:  They absolutely may not, under any circumstances, poison their weapons. Given the acts she performed while in the service of Baraeon, she does understand the need to take up arms on occasion, and does not restrict her clerics from doing so with good cause. It would also be appropriate for a cleric of Az'atta to take up arms to defeat any evils that are menacing the people or area they are currently assisting. 
     Az'atta wants all the peoples of Layonara to be able to immediately identify her clergy, so that they may be sought out for whatever help they can offer to those in need. As such, she requires that all of her clerics prominently display her symbol upon their person at all times when in public. This could be in the form of a device placed upon a shield or armor, a prominently displayed holy symbol, or a tabard with her symbol embroidered onto the front and back. Many of her clergy take this a step further, and proudly weave the colors of Az'atta's symbol into their clothing as well. 

     Az'atta knows what it is like to serve and to be utterly evil, for so she was for most of her life. Being Drow by race, and a devoted and greatly favored priestess of Baraeon Da'Cuz by choice, she committed many heinous and utterly evil atrocities in the name of her god. It was the worst of these horrific acts that changed her forevermore. After attacking and destroying the monastery housing the Llama, child-avatar of Aragen, the God of Enlightenment, Az'atta drank some of the Llama's blood while enacting a foul ritual in Baraeon's honor, and for a brief moment, she glimpsed the True Path of Enlightenment. Feeling great revulsion and sorrow for the slaughter of the Llama and his protectors, and all of the other evil acts she had committed over the years, Az'atta renounced her allegiance to Baraeon and the Drow people. 
     She and her most loyal followers fled the Underdark and moved to the surface lands. Pursued relentlessly by her people for her "betrayal" and not trusted by the surface races, she and her followers led difficult lives. Many of her followers chose to return to Baraeon's service, believing the Path of Enlightenment too difficult. They were ruthlessly slain by the followers of the Prince of Hate. In the end, only Az'atta and her two most loyal Handmaidens were able to remain living on the surface. Nevertheless, she and her followers sought out those in need of mercy, redemption, and love and aided them however they could, without thought or need of reward. The three of them did this to atone for the horrendous deeds they committed earlier in their lives. Az'atta always tried to aid monasteries and their inhabitants as much as possible as penance for her terrible sin against them. 
     After traveling widely, and providing many years of selfless service to those in need, Az'atta and her Handmaidens came to be accepted by the surface races, particularly humans. In the end, an assassin of Corath, acting on behalf of Baraeon, caught up with Az'atta and killed her. As a reward for all of the good that Az'atta had performed on the behalf of others at the end of her life, the gods Aragen and Goran elevated her to Goddesshood. Her two Handmaidens became the first High Priestesses of Az'atta's new church.

Clergy and Temples: 
     The hierarchy of Az'atta's clergy is fairly straightforward. All of her clerics are considered equals with one another, with the exception of her two most favored clerics, who receive the title of Handmaiden. These two clerics are the leaders of her faith, and informally share power. One of the two typically supervises the temples and their faithful, while the other watches over and assists the traveling clerics. Each temple's resident clergy select the most qualified priest or priestess to make the day-to-day decisions at that individual temple, and they look to this cleric for guidance and direction. 
Otherwise, while older and more experienced clergy are normally looked up to and well respected by younger priests and priestesses, there is no other formal rank structure. 
Az'atta's clergy build and maintain temples to her anywhere there are likely to be those in need of their help and protection. These temples provide hospice services and shelter for travelers, refugees, and any others in need. Her temples will also provide sanctuary and protection to anyone that Az'atta finds worthy. 

     A great number of her clerics can be found traveling both the civilized and wild areas of Layonara. These itinerant priests and priestesses actively seek out those in need of Az'atta's love, redemption, and protection. They can often be found in areas recently suffering from war, famine, plague, or natural disaster, doing what they can to ease the people's suffering and protect them from further harm. 

     There are two special Holy Days that those following Az'atta revere, and both are equally important and joyous occasions for the faith. The first of these celebrates Az'atta's enlightenment, and the beginning of her life of service to the people of Layonara, and is known as the Day of Redemption. Her other Holy Day celebrates Az'atta's elevation to Goddesshood by Goran and Aragen as a reward for the life of goodness and mercy she lived between her enlightenment and her death. This celebration is known simply as The Ascension.

     Prayers to Az'atta are depend primarily upon the need of her cleric at the time. If one is about to face battle, or a great trial while protecting others, his/her prayer might sound similar to this: "Az'atta, through the love that you feel for all, give me the strength to protect these good folk from harm."  A prayer for healing would likely go something like this:  "Az'atta, through your boundless mercy, grant me the power to heal this poor soul of his affliction."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Ilsare, Goran, Deliar, Lucinda, Aragen 

Friendly: Rofirein, Aeridin, Toran, Kithairien, Shindaleria, Beryl, Folian S'pae, Prunilla, Grand 

Neutral: Katia, Xeen 

Unfriendly: Vorax, Dorand, Shadon, Mist 

Enemy: Pyrtechon, Branderback, Corath, Baraeon Ca'Duz, Vierdri'ira, Sulterio

Voltrex
    Voltrex is the continent in the southeast part of Layonara. Little is known about Voltrex, for the continent is off limits to all but noble elves, a rule which is policed vigilantly. What is known about Voltrex is that many of the elves who once resided on the other continents migrated here as a final solution to the race wars. Due to its secretive nature, many genres of Voltex folklore have emerged throughout the other continents. One thing that is often repeated about Voltrex is that it is the home of the Five of Nature.

Well-known Cities:

Saida 
Location:  
     Saida is the capital city of Voltrex and lies at the southwestern tip of the continent. 
Population: 16,570 (100% elf) 
Government: Magocracy 
Defenses: 
    A large, heavily fortified castle looks over this city. The city is surrounded by reinforced masonry walls and is heavily warded by magic.
 
Miscellaneous Information:
    Who has visited this great elf capital and returned to tell tales?  There are few, if any. It is said that the mages who guard this city know you are coming before you do, and if you are found not worthy of admittance after their rigorous investigation, you are sent either across the ocean or to its bottom, in either case without ever having set foot in or laid eyes on the precious gem of Elven civilization. 

    It is also said that the extraordinarily exclusive group of individuals who are welcomed at the Saida docks are never seen or heard from again for other reasons. The city is rumored to be so sublime as to make men and Elves alike lose themselves within its shimmering structures and resplendent residents. It is likely the only major city in all of Layonara that preserves and perhaps even amplifies the natural splendor of the forest it is constructed in. They also say that much of the city can be found suspended in the canopy, built on the massive branches of the ancient trees of the southern Evergreen Forest. Even the weather in Saida, some tell, is always perfectly cool with a gentle breeze rustling the trees and stirring the pleasant forest scents. This is remarkable as Saida is the southernmost Layonaran city and thus should be subject to intense climatic forces.

    There is perhaps no place in all of Layonara of which more has been said. And there is perhaps no place in all of Layonara of which less is known.

Seldarine
Location: 
    Seldarine lies on the southern edge of the Ulambree forest and to the east of the Voltrex Mountains.
Population: 10,800 (100% elf)
Government:  Unknown
Defenses:  Unknown

Miscellaneous Information:
    There are rumors that a second great Elven city exists to the south of the magnificent Ulambree Forest. Of those who leave Voltrex and talk about it, many speak of this place. That is because Seldarine is ideally located to serve as a hub for travel and commerce on Voltrex, and so it does. Those who venture from Voltrex are likely to be trading or traveling minded, and thus are often attached to this place. Few live here, but many call it home. As such it is a city pulsing with life, desires and magnificent things found nowhere else in Layonara. 

Amluarial
Population: 650
Government:  Magogracy
Defenses:  
    Strange tales abound of Amluarial being protected by walls of wind and great magicians who can direct its flow with simple words and gestures.

Miscellaneous Information:
    The elven scholar Ramsiad studied the lore of this place extensively. Although he was never permitted passage to Amluarial, he did compile some interesting data on the place. According to Ramsiad, this medium-sized hamlet is situated in the coastal hills on the northeastern part of Voltrex. It lies above the Great Voltrex Range of mountains, and therefore has some intense weather patterns. The winds from the east whip up against the mountains and swirl right about Amluarial before being sucked up in the western coastal gusts. There is never a day without intense and shifting winds. Great hurricanes and tornados also plague this area. Why would any elf choose to live here then?  Quite simply, the elves of Amluarial have invented devices to harness the energy of the wind and transfer it into practical and magical applications. What sort of products these machines generate was never discerned. But Ramsiad did discover that many elves across Voltrex have heard of them and heard of them being used throughout Voltrex.

Darthoriadin
Location:  
    This Ulambree Wood Elf Village lies hidden in the Ulambree forest.
Population: 265
Government:  
    There are said to be numerous tribes in this village which vie for power, and in doing so balance and share control of this Wood Elf village.
Defenses:
    The defenses of Darthoriadin, according to some loremasters, are primarily based on elevation. The entire village is in the trees. Ladders can be easily raised and Wood Elf archers find easy targets below.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Those who claim knowledge of Voltrex say that the Ulambree Wood Elf Village is the rural counterpart to Saida. Rather than resplendent stone structures erupting gracefully from the forest canopy, Darthoriadin is barely visible even when you are standing on one of its platforms. The entire city is nestled in the branches of the old Ulambree trees. Their union establishes a sort of harmony between the essence of the forest and the Wood Elves. People talk of the Darthoriadinian Elves moving through the trees with the speed of eagles and having the gift of nature's touch. Many of them never set foot on the ground, and scorn those who do.

    A Temple of Folian S'pae, the Wood Elves patron God, can be found here.
Tales of the Elven Citadels:  The current state of knowledge about the cities of Voltrex by Ramsiad

Aasimar
    Proud, fair-skinned and tall, the aasimar are a race with a somewhat curious background. One of the two races that are known to be "Planetouched" (the others being the Tieflings), Aasimar are native to planes of law and order. They have holy blood somewhere in their ancestry. While some claim to have descended directly from the Gods, it is more likely that one of their ancestors was a Celestial, and not a God. However, most of them cannot trace their heritage back to a specific celestial being.

    There is no difference between Aasimar hailing from human, elven, or other lineage, it is the touch of the divine that makes them what they are, regardless of their other ancestry.
Most Aasimar have a human ancestry, a relative few have an elvish ancestry. 
Aasimar have no lands to call their own. They are welcome in most places, but can also be unwanted in others.

Personality: 
    Because of their ancestry, aasimar are always champions of good. Aasimar are very often paladins or clerics, devoutly following their deity. This devoutness can make them somewhat rigid in their opinions, however.
Since they have no place to call home, belonging completely neither in the Heavens nor Layonara, aasimar travel a lot. Even though they're well-liked in most places, they are always loners.
Aasimar do not tend to band together.

Physical Description:. 
    Aasimar are beautiful creatures. They are tall, with blond, almost white, or silvery hair and bright eyes that make others feel like they see right into the core of their being.

    They like to wear finely crafted metal armors, often decorated with sigils or coats of arms. In their fight against evil, they prefer to use greatswords or other weapons that allow them to use their height as an advantage. 

    Aasimar ancestry makes them very aware of their surroundings. They're also very perceptive of people's motives. Their ancestry also provides them some elemental protection. Some spells that are specifically used to control other humanoids will not work on Aasimar.

Relations with other races: 
    In general, aasimar get along with most good races, however, they can hate "evil" races with an almost fanatical fervor. This is especially true for the other Planetouched race, the Tiefling.
 
Alignment: 
    Because of their heritage, aasimar are always good, and usually Lawful or Neutral Good.

Religion: 
    Aasimar usually follow the deity their ancestors did. However, since they do not really have a place in the Heavens, some Aasimar refuse to follow or even acknowledge deities or their servants.

Language: 
    Common, Celestial

Names: 
    Depends on the other part of their ancestry (human, elf, et cetera).

Adventurers: 
    Having no home or lands to call their own, Aasimar travel the lands and are not likely to settle down in a particular location. They're usually traveling paladins or clerics, looking to fight evil where they can. Those who are not devout followers of a deity tend to become traveling bards.

Aragen

Aliases: The Wise God, The Lord of Knowledge  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: 
     There is no race in particular that follows Aragen, though elves are most likely to do so since they usually have the patience and lifespan to collect and use information for their god. Humans also follow Aragen, because learning and collecting information progresses society, and human society is very progress-oriented indeed. Half-orcs and half-giants (and tieflings, to a lesser degree) are least likely to follow Aragen, because they often care little for knowledge or the benefit of society, rarely have the patience for the required studies and observations, and would rather bash heads than talk. However, anyone willing to devote his or her life to the search for knowledge can worship Aragen. 
Domains: Knowledge, Protection and Travel. 

     Clerics of Aragen always pick Knowledge as one of their domains, so a cleric of Aragen could pick either Knowledge and Protection or Knowledge and Travel.

Governs: Knowledge, Research, Stories, Poetry

Dogma: 
     The search for and gathering of knowledge of any kind is paramount, both for the benefit of the faithful and for society as a whole. Even the smallest speck of information must be sought out and stored for everyone to see. Only through true enlightenment can balance be achieved. Use violent measures only when absolutely necessary; otherwise, stand out of harm's way, avoiding conflict and collecting as much information as possible. Make sure collected knowledge is archived for the use of others.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     The favored "weapon" of Aragen's clerics is the humble quarterstaff or a mage's staff. Only rarely is a staff used as a weapon, however, as it is usually used as a walking stick when the Aragenite travels to new places to gather information.
     Aragenites prefer simple clothing when travelling, as the burden of plate mail slows them down in their pursuit of knowledge, and they tend to avoid conflict when possible, so they usually have no use for the heavy armor anyway. Aragen's clerics have, however, been trained to wear heavy armor to better protect the knowledge they carry in their earthly bodies.
The clergy of Aragen always carry a notebook to write down the knowledge they gain. The most devout Aragenites will protect this book to the death, to ensure that knowledge is not lost.

Clergy and Temples: 
     The clergy of Aragen serve as the scholars and researchers of society, and if one happens to have a question of some kind they will almost always be ready to answer. There is no clear hierarchy in the temples of Aragen, but each temple has a head scholar who is the only person allowed to write in the Libra Prima, or First Book, of that temple.
     Temples devoted to Aragen usually resemble libraries or schools where knowledge is stored wherever possible: in books, on scrolls, and through even more secret and esoteric means. Books and other devices of knowledge are often littered everywhere, because genius thrives in chaos.
     Each temple has a Libra Prima, where every mote of knowledge collected by that temple's clerics is written down, but only the head scholar of the temple has the authority to write in this sacred tome. This is to ensure that no information is written twice and that all knowledge gained by that particular temple can be easily accessed. The tome is often enchanted with strong magic to allow for many more pages than it would otherwise appear to have, and also so only the current head scholar can write in the tome. If a temple is attacked or struck by natural disaster, then the First Book is artifact that the clergy will save, as it holds all information ever collected by acolytes of that temple.
     Knowledge gained by the Aragenites is spread to different temples by the Bearers of Knowledge, a Monastic Order.
     Clerics of Aragen do not pray at any particular time of day or in any particular location, though most often combine prayer with recording gained knowledge in their books and preparation of spells if a spell caster.
     Litanies of faith uttered by Clerics of Aragen can range from chant in an indecipherable language to a simple: "Lord Aragen, grant me wisdom, purpose, and strength of mind so that I can discover what is unfound, and enlighten the unenlightened."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Rofirein, Az'atta

Friendly: Dorand, Goran, Toran, Grannoch

Neutral: Aeridin, Katia, Kithairien, Shindaleria, Folian S'pae, Grand, Grannoch

Unfriendly: Ilsare, Shadon, Deliar, Lucinda, Baraeon Ca'Duz, Sulterio, Beryl, Prunilla, Vierdri'ira 

Enemy: Pyrtechon, Vorax, Branderback, Corath, Mist, Xeen
The Book of the Lord of Knowledge

Sulterio

Aliases: Adamantine One, The Brooding One  
Race: Grey Dwarf 
Worshippers: Mostly Duergar although a few other savage races occasionally also worship the Adamantine One. 
Domains: Death, Earth, Evil, Knowledge. Nearly all clerics have the Earth domain and one of the others.
Governs: Darkness, evil, mining, poisons 

Dogma:
     The riches of the Underdark should be mined in honor of the Adamantine One. Work and toil to gather these riches, for nothing worthwhile is easily acquired. Those who show weakness or lack of faith shall be punished. As adamantium is forged by fire into weapons and armor, so you shall be forged by your faith. Do not rely on the arcane arts, rely on strength. Be loyal to your clan and honor the ways of your people. Obey your superiors. Show no mercy to the other dwarven races.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     The favored weapon of all the clergy is the adamantium maul or hammer. They wear adamantium armors, heavily plated and always of a grayish/blackish color, so that they blend in with the rocks. They wear a mushroom-shaped talisman around their necks. When not wearing armor they wear dark, hueless garbs. 

Clergy and Temples:
     The clergy can roughly be divided into three sects: the Deep Smiths, the Adamantine Brotherhood, and The Chosen.

     The Deep Smiths were shown the ways of working the earth and all the ores within it, especially adamantium, the black and unyielding ore. This focus of knowledge has led to a well-established order of subterranean ore-crafters known as the Deep Smiths. They excel in the crafting of adamantium armors and weapons. Unlike their Dorandite counterparts, however, they create not out of love for the craft itself, but as a means to make better materials for war. Love of war replaces the pride of craftsmanship, and all of their works exude a martial, bloodthirsty aura. Nonetheless, items crafted by the Deep Smiths are highly prized and valued pieces of work. 

     The Adamantine Brotherhood seek to be more like the Adamantine One, and have taken to literally mimicking the title in the very fiber of their being. They have hardened body and mind in pursuit of the essence of their namesake metal. Some have compared them to the Voraxite Brothers of Battle, but the Brotherhood is much more numerous. They have fewer scruples and will not refrain from using poisons to help them in their dark endeavors. The Adamantine Brotherhood rarely surfaces, instead seeking to advance their physical and mental fortitude by delving even deeper into the earth and uncovering and claiming even more riches for the glory of the Brooding One. It is rumored that the greatest of the Brotherhood can actually reach into the core beneath the Underdark and extract molten adamantium from the very heart of Layonara.

     The third sect is The Chosen, battle clerics of Sulterio. They are a ruthless and vicious order, and can readily call upon the strength and viciousness of Sulterio in the throes of battle. Armies of the Underdark are often lead by these clerics; those that are not often regret not paying the hefty price needed to hire The Chosen when they fall prey to an army that did. 

     Other orders and specializations exist within the faith of Sulterio, including warriors, slavers, and even traders. But since the Duergar of different clans oftentimes mistrust each other (though never quite so much as they mistrust other races), the clerical hierarchy is usually based on a clan level. The sect's leader is chosen quite simply, through a trial of single combat. The cleric who defeats all challengers becomes the leader and guides his faction in faith and war. 

     Temples to Sulterio are rare on the surface world. The few that exist are generally deep within mountains to reflect the world of the Underdark. The temples are usually little more than fortresses of stone, though they are often adorned with adamantium ore. Altars are invariably also made of the most perfect deposits of adamantium. 

Prayers:
     With the exception of The Chosen of Sulterio, it is rare for any caste to pray regularly, except for guidance before extreme trial. To ask for help (even from one's own god) is considered a sign of weakness by Sulterio's faithful. Instead, followers of Sulterio worship him more in name and deeds than in words. The Chosen however, do pray each day upon rising so that Sulterio will better know the sound of their voice, lest their prayers go unanswered in the heat of battle because Sulterio did not hear them over the uproar.

Elves
    Elves are an ancient and aloof race. Compared to the human race, elves are quite small and frail. The tallest elves rarely reach five and a half feet, and some are as small as four and a half feet. They have a lithe build and usually weigh between 100 and 150 pounds. They are an agile and dexterous people, and they move with grace and beauty. The Elves prefer seclusion and tend to shun outsiders and the outside world as a whole. Of all the races of Layonara, Elves are the longest lived, with many elves reaching between 600 and 700 years of age. They have a natural affinity for magic, but also value martial skills with finesse weapons such as light swords and bows. While humans will venture into the unknown for many reasons, elves almost universally leave their cloistered groves to experience more of the world that their race holds at arm's length.

There are many varieties of elves.  I will include a brief description of some of them.

Gray Elves
    Gray Elves are one of the many kinds of surface elves on Layonara. They are among the tallest and most intelligent of their kin, and yet have a certain aura of arrogance about them. They are probably the most arrogant type of elf, seeking to put great distance between themselves and other races, including other elven races. The Gray Elves live deep in the mountains, past the point where even the dwarves turn around and go home. Gray Elves are a noble people, however, and seek to uphold good wherever they can. Gray Elves make excellent wizards, yet most remain secluded in their mountain homes. They conceal these homes with warding and illusory magics so that unknowing races leave them alone, and so that only the worthy will enter their domains. Be wary, though, because once stirred the Gray Elves will attack with highly disciplined knights mounted on war-trained griffons or hippogryphs, with the support of their uncanny wizards.

Personality: 
    Gray Elves are much more arrogant and aloof than other elven races. They regard every other race with disdain, even other elven races. They only have respect for other Gray Elves. Most Gray Elves are full of themselves, and usually only listen to themselves or other Gray Elves.

    Even so, they believe that they are one of the greatest protectors of good in the world and they work tirelessly to uphold this vigil. Though they feel this sense of noblesse oblige, it still takes the threat of a very great evil force to stir them from their isolated homes in deep in the mountains.

    When dealing with the few others that they do respect, Gray Elves are very noble and honorable, doing everything to make sure a promise is kept or a common enemy is defeated. To most common folk, though, Gray Elves mainly resemble arrogant knights.

Physical Description: 
    Gray Elves are unusually tall for elves, but are also more thinly built, lacking the strength and agility of their lesser cousins. Living in the mountains has accustomed them to harsh climates and the like, and as such they are more enduring than common elves. Gray Elves are among the smartest of elvenkind, and this is probably what contributes to their somewhat aloof behavior towards other races, including other elven races. Gray Elves tend to wear noble clothing and armor, with the mages wearing splendid robes colored white, silver, yellow, or gold that are often adorned with shining metals such as silver and mithril, or jewels. The Gray Elven warriors tend to don chain or platemail of shimmering metals; they also tend to wear metal helmets sporting distinctive wings. They prefer deep blue or purple cloaks.

    Gray Elves always have very pale skin, and tend to have gray or silver hair, along with amber eyes. Gray Elves with pale golden hair and violet eyes have been spotted, but these are very rare.

Relations with other races: 
    Gray Elves are doubtlessly the most haughty and aloof of the surface elves; they think almost nothing of other races, even other elven races. Gray Elves prefer to stay as isolated from other races as possible, and reside deep within the mountain ranges of Layonara. Due to living in the mountains, they have forged a friendship with the birds living there, and are bitter enemies with the giants also seeking claim to the peaks.

Alignment: 
    Gray Elves are usually of good alignment. They tend more towards being lawful than chaotic.

Religion: 
    Most devout Gray Elves tend to follow a deity of elven origin due to their disdain for "lesser" races.

Language: 
    All Gray Elves speak common and elven. Other languages commonly known by Gray Elves are Sylvan, Draconic, Auran, and the language of birds.

Names: 
    Issauria Windshear, Alin'dae Amberleaf, Sieylianna Silverdawn

Adventurers: 
    Though it might seem like Gray Elves aren't the types to go adventuring, lone Gray Elves leaving their mountainous homes seeking adventure is not unheard of. They see themselves as champions of good and as such some will go out into the world to defeat any kind of evil lurking in the shadows. Even so, this does not mean that the adventurous Gray Elves have let their arrogance and contempt for lesser races go.

Sun Elves 
    Sun Elves keep to themselves, perhaps even more than the other elven races. Nevertheless, they can be found throughout Layonara, although most of them live on Voltrex.
    They are ruled by noble Houses and greatly value tradition. Sun Elves do everything the 'elven' way, and consequently, their lore and art is still somewhat narrow, as they do not even bother to look at lore and art of other races.

Personality: 
    Sun Elves believe that they are the true defenders of Elven art, lore and magic. Because of this, they look down on all other races, and somewhat on their other Elven cousins as well. They strongly believe in tradition and are very conservative.

    Sun Elves are staunch isolationists. Even when they live in a larger city, they tend to group together in their own little enclave.

Physical description: 
    Taller and leaner than most of the other elven races, the Sun Elves are a beautiful race. Their skin has a copper or bronze hue, and their hair is blond, copper, gold, or black.

    They dress in simple garments of green and blue that seem inconspicuous at first, though a closer glance reveals the garments are made of exotic materials with exquiste cuts. These garments are subtly embroidered with patterns that seem simple, but are quite complex when one attempts to follow them. The same goes for their jewelry: simple, but exquisitely made.
Because of their focus on art and lore, they are not the strongest or hardiest of elves. They even tend to look down on combat, seeing it as a very crude way to settle conflicts.

Relations with other races: 
    Sun Elves tend not to concern themselves with the affairs of other races too much, as these are rather insignificant to them. Only relationships with other elves are important and meaningful (excepting, of course, their reviled cousins, the Dark Elves). However, Sun Elves have been known to act as diplomats, advocating the Elven side in conflicts.

Alignment: 
    Mostly lawful neutral

Religion: 
    Ilsare and Aeridin

Language: 
    Common, Elven

Names: 
    Sun Elves are named during a Naming Ceremony that takes places during the first dawn after the birth of a child. Their last name is the name of the House they are born to, such as Morningbreak and Sunbeam. Their first name is given by the cleric that performs the naming ceremony. Adventurers: 
    Sun Elf adventurers are few, as they tend not to care much about the other races of the world and their dealings. 

Wood Elves
     Wood Elves tend to be a bit shorter and stockier than the other elven races, but they are no less graceful. They make their home in the forests of Layonara, and, contrary to their Wild cousins, they're not nomadic. Instead, Wood Elves build villages in the treetops. Before the race wars, Wood Elves could be found throughout Layonara, but nowadays most have retreated to Voltrex and have settled in the Ulambree Forest.

    Great hunters and woodsmen, there is nothing that they do not know about the forests they inhabit.

Personality: 
    Proud like most elven races, the Wood Elves will go out of their way to protect and defend their forests and the creatures that inhabit them. Those who seek to harm the forest would do best to stay clear of the Wood Elves, as they will show no mercy to those who bear forests ill will.

Physical Description: 
    Like their cousins, the Wild Elves, the Wood Elves have dark hair and prefer to decorate themselves with tattoos. Their clothing is often made from leathers and leaves dyed in colors that make them blend into the forests. Having spent their entire lives in the forests, Wood Elves are often stronger and more agile than the other elven races. Wood Elves get their first bow at a young age, and are rarely seen without one. They're considered the best marksmen on Layonara, but are also fierce in close combat. For this they prefer short swords, as larger weapons are not practical in forests.

Relations with other races: 
    Wood Elves rarely have contact with other races, as they prefer not to leave their forests. They get along well with most other elven races, except for the Dark Elves.

    Relations with most other races are either neutral or strained at best, especially with races that do not respect the woods and cut down trees, like humans. They also hate orcs, who they're likely to shoot on sight. As long as others stay out of their forests, the Wood Elves could care less about them.

Alignment: 
    The majority of Wood Elves are neutral.

Religion: 
    Wood Elves follow Folian S'pae, their patron god. 

Language: 
    All the Wood Elves know common, Sylvan and elven. They see little reason to learn other languages as they do not actively seek contact with other races.

Names: 
    As with most elves, Wood Elf names tend to have symbolic meanings. They usually refer to plants, trees or creatures.

Adventurers: 
    Wood Elves are not very likely to leave their forests in search of adventure, unless there is something involved that threatens the forests or their tribe.

Wild Elves 
    Wild elves are barbaric and tribal elves living in the thick forests and open plains of Layonara. They are nomadic people and, unlike their cousins, they rarely stay in one spot for a long time. They live in small tribes of 10-60 people led by elders, but still have no real hierarchy. Wild elves are rarely seen by other races due to their nomadic nature, hiding skills, and taste for solitude. Wild elves are close to the nature and believe it gives them everything they need. They do not build or buy; they scavenge and hunt. Wild elves own very little and do not trade much, and thus have no real economy. Their almost feral nature makes them dangerous enemies in combat and most are also great hunters. Other races consider wild elves feral savages, but outsiders have trouble understanding the wild elf way of living and worldview. Wild elves travel the world completely free and use their own skills and wits to survive. 

Personality: 
    Wild elves are a proud race. Even though other races consider them savages, they contend that they are the true elves, for the others have lost their primal elven essence in their attempts to control nature. They are hardy elves who can survive under harsh conditions. They respect their traditions and ways, but are not bound by them. They live by the words: "Live as if you were to die tomorrow. Fight as if you were to live forever." Wild elves are generous to those they view as good and merciless to those they view as evil. 

Physical description: 
    Wild elves tend to have well-tanned skin and their hair ranges from black to light brown, lightening to silver white with age. They tend to be physically hardier than other elves but still maintain the elven elegance and grace. They're fond of decorative tattoos that also have practical purposes, such as depicting tales of their deeds. Wild elves dress in simple clothing of animal skins and basic plant weaves and wield simple weapons such as spears and bows. 

Relations with other races: 
    Wild elves prefer to live alone without much contact to other races and even avoid them whenever possible. They share their surface-dwelling cousins' attitude about everything non-elven and the Dark Elves, however. They actively try to avoid conflict, but if something threatens the things they hold dear, they will go to war. 

Alignment: 
    Most wild elves, due to their nomadic and barbaric nature, are chaotic neutral. 

Religion: 
    Kithairien is the patron god of the wild elves and they almost always worship him. They seek to become what he is as he was the first and the greatest. 

Language: 
    Common, Elven 

Names: 
    Wild elven names are very much like those of other elves. They are given to the children by the tribe's elders and the names always bear a symbolic meaning. 

Adventurers: 
    Wild elves are a nomadic race and thus it isn't uncommon for individuals or small groups to leave their tribe. Usually these are younger wild elves exploring the world out of curiosity or because the tribe's elders have sent them on a quest.

Millions of years ago Layonara came into existence through a slow process known as evolution. During those millions of years many things happened that have gone undocumented; at least, undocumented by any known race. We will begin at the earliest documented point, when the first Dragons arrived on the world.

    The first dragons to arrive on Layonara were the Metallic Dragons, massive reptilian creatures with scales made of gold, bronze, silver, and other minerals. In their five hundred years of dominance, they worked tirelessly to make the new world livable for other races, and there are rumors that they were responsible for the creation of some species. Word spread throughout the galaxy of a lush new Prime World that was just being settled. In response to this news, Dragons of color - red, blue, black and green,  along with a few others - began showing up on Layonara vying for power and their own control of the world. It is rumored that these dragons began to create races in order to reach their lofty goals and to defeat the established Metallic Dragons. It has never been verified that the Dragons ever created races, but the whispers cannot be discounted. After another thousand years the Dragon Gods began actively becoming involved in this world, in the hopes of saving the Dragons that followed them. It is a known fact that the Dragon Gods did create races to reach their goals and yet did not become "directly involved" in the everyday "life" of Layonara. 

    After two thousand years the Dragons fought a large war, which is now known as "The Dragon Wars". This war lasted for over one hundred years and involved nearly every race that existed on the World. The savage fighting of the Dragon Wars was fraught with consequences: some races were split up into different tribes or even different species, some races were rendered completely extinct, and all races were greatly diminished in population. It was during this war that the Elves and Dwarves split into separate evolutionary paths and the Humans became the dominant race. The fighting between races was just as savage - if not more so - than the battles of the Dragons. Every race believed in a Dragon's cause and fought bitterly to see their goal come about.

    From the acrid, blood-tinged smoke of battle came a young Human General known as Sinthar Bloodstone. Rather than aligning himself with a Dragon, he believed that Dragons were responsible for the death and destruction of the Dragon Wars. With that belief he formed his own army in the hopes of forcing both Dragon sides to surrender. His natural talents honed by bloody practice, Bloodstone ruthlessly wielded powerful magic and displayed exemplary tactics, and many believe that he never lost a battle. In time, the Dragons were forced to surrender to Sinthar and the World knew peace for a few hundred years.

    When the war ended the Dragons demanded, as part of their surrender, that Sinthar be banished from the world, never to return. At his sentencing Sinthar killed many of the jury and then disappeared after swearing vengeance on the world. Many believed that Sinthar's banishing was just a legend, until he did return two millennia later to seek his revenge, but that is another story.
The History of Layonara:  The First Generation

The second Generation began when the Humanoid Gods began to take interest in Layonara and the Dragon Gods were driven out. It is rumored that the Dragon Gods were driven out accidentally but who knows the ways of Gods? Many think that the Dragon Gods still have power on the world, but are remaining quiet and hidden as they build their strength.

    It is now known that Sinthar Bloodstone began his attempt to return to Layonara about ten years after being banished. Though the Second Generation is not centered around Sinthar's return, the coming of Bloodstone is seen as the event that ended the Second Generation and began the Third. During the Second Generation there were many race wars being fought, predominately between the Elves and Dwarves. The wars soured relations between the Elves and Dwarves for generations, preventing the two cultures from uniting in trade, invention, and power. For the most part these Race Wars are over, but every once in a while skirmishes will brew out of the hard feelings that will remain for Generations.

    The Elves are now split up into two distinctive groups, the Dark Elves and the Top Elves. The Dark Elves live below the ground while the Top Elves, and various sub-cultures thereof, live above ground. The Dark Elves used to follow the Dragons of Color while the Top Elves followed the Metallic Dragons. When the war ended their war began in earnest, their natural prejudices augmented by thousands of years of war.

    The Dwarves are also split into sub-cultures, but they are not openly hostile towards each other any longer. The Hill and Mountain Dwarves sometimes fight, but brawling is what Dwarves like to do.

    During this Generation the Dragons retreated and were rarely seen, but with the return of Sinthar the few that have left have retreated even farther, and can now only be found in the most difficult to reach or inhospitable places on Layonara.

    Sinthar was able to return after thousands of years through the use of portals that a rare few believe may be tied to Blood Wells. During his time on the World, Sinthar created the Wells to help in his battles against the Dragons. When he was banished he was able to communicate with one in control of a Well. Through this extraplanar communication, he corrupted the keepers of the Wells and they eventually fell under his limited control. With this limited control he influenced them to create more Wells and thus his power grew. He was able to convince a few to willingly help his cause with promises of knowledge, power and wealth. After hundreds of years he created enough power in three of the Wells that he was able to bring an army through from the Planes. Unfortunately for him, he miscalculated somewhere and over half of his army was destroyed - along with parts of the World being reshaped - due to unforeseen explosions and the Negative Plane. It is thought by many that if his army had not been destroyed that the World would have fallen within a few years. Even with only half of his army intact he was able to defeat a large continent, secure a stronghold, and build his army anew.
The History of Layonara:  The Second Generation

Dogma:
     Shadon teaches that life is fleeting, and therefore must be enjoyed. Every moment spent doing something boring is a moment wasted. As such, followers of Shadon relish constant festivals and adventuring. Clerics of Shadon will go to any extent to enjoy themselves, sometimes harming others along the way, but sometimes doing great good. Clergy Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of The Trickster prefer to use daggers, because they are easy to hide and it is extremely fun to take down a foe with such a small thing. They normally enchant their knives with electrical properties to allow witty comments on their shocking personalities. 
     Clerics of Shadon wear flashy clothes, normally tailored to make a loud fashion statement. When in combat, clerics of The Scamp wear shiny metals to distract or dazzle their opponents.

Clergy Temples:

Rofirein

Aliases: The All-Seeing, Lord Protector  
Race: Dragon 
Worshippers: Rofirein does not forsake any race, but he is predominantly worshipped by humans.
Domains: Strength, Protection, Knowledge, Magic
Governs: Protection, guidance 

Dogma: 
     You are a paragon of virtue and honor. Dedicate your life to justice, honor, and the pursuit of knowledge. Hold the law above all else at any cost, even if this means bringing loved ones or friends to justice. Without the order of law, chaos would reign and the world would descend into dark times where Pyrtechon would thrive. Extend honor to all, even your foes. Aid others whenever and wherever possible, as long as it is in accordance with the law and does not make way for acts of evil.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of Rofirein favor swords, especially bastard swords, over bludgeoning weapons, believing that a sharp blade metes the swiftest and most painless justice. They are often seen in full plate armor, favoring it along with a large shield bearing the symbol of Rofirein. Any armor that provides maximum protection to the wearer is preferred, as defense of self is required before one can defend others.

Clergy and Temples:
     The clergy of Rofirein have a distinct hierarchy, as would be expected by a church of law, and often work in close co-operation with the paladins of Toran.

     Temples of Rofirein are a mixture of grand and humble affairs, often doubling as local courts and houses of justice. All temples maintain a fair library that holds documents of law and other books of factual interest. The largest place of worship is the Cathedral of Rofirein in Pranzis, a magnificent edifice replete with the splendor and majesty of the Law. Each local temple is home to a High Priest, a number of local clerics, and serves as a temporary home for questing clerics. 

     The High Priest is often the oldest and wisest of clerics, rumored to be in frequent direct contact with the Great Wyrm himself. The local clerics are attached to one temple or church at a time and oversee the day-to-day tasks. They will never move far from their temples, except in times of crisis. This is in contrast to the questing clerics, as they are mobile, traveling the length and breadth of Layonara to provide protection to those that cannot protect themselves, bringing honor, justice, and chivalry wherever they go. They are often turned to when wisdom or a non-biased opinion is needed and can operate in a judiciary role if required. 
There is also a group of non-clergy; these lay followers of Rofirein are those who have not undergone the initiation into the clergy or paladinhood, and comprise all those employed for service by the temple itself. Stablehands, cooks, groundsmen, and the like all hope to serve Rofirein in a greater capacity someday. 

There are several ranks in the Rofireinite order:
     The first step of the path of Rofirein is that of the Initiate. All classes spend at least 4 years as an initiate, learning law and various others skills including basic combat, etiquette, diplomacy, honor, chivalry, and healing. On completion of this period of training, each soul is presented with a shield bearing the symbol of Rofirein by the high priest during an appropriate ceremony. 
     After the ceremony, it is believed that Rofirein communicates his guidance on to a soul during a session of solitary prayer so that it may know the next step upon its path:

Librarians/scribes/historians:
     These are predominantly mages and clerics who favor the pursuit and maintenance of documentation and official records, including the local census. These souls are also primarily responsible for all logistical matters of a temple.

     It is rumored that at one time Rofirein actually walked on Layonara. He has a deep love of the world and wants nothing more than to see it prosper. He hopes to aid Layona's prosperity by offering his protection and guidance to all that follow him.

     Guardians of Justice (Judges):
     These are clerics that specialize in the law as passed down from the Great Wyrm himself. Judges are predominantly made up of the clerics who spend several years' further study in all aspects of the law. These clerics are always attached to a local courthouse or place of law where guidance and wisdom is required.
     Guardians of the Wyrm (Temple Guards) - Most Temple Guards are drawn from the ranks of fighters, rangers, and paladins. These souls have dedicated their lives to protecting the temples and other sacred places of the Rofireinite faith. They spend many years perfecting their combat technique, with special emphasis on use of the tower shield and defensive tactics.
     Knights of the Wyrm (Questing Clerics) - Almost anyone can join the Knights of the Wurm, (though fighting classes comprise the majority) who have dedicated their lives to the defense of others through the use of sword and shield. Unlike the Guardians, they have no desire to be tied to one place, often establishing distant outposts and bringing the word of Rofirein to unknown lands. Besides further combat training, these clerics are also given additional training in healing and law and are taught to ride. These souls are the first to respond to a threat and are often called upon in times of need.
All clerics of Rofirein display a statue of a golden dragon as a focal point for worship and blessing. Many come to touch the statue of the great dragon to ask for guidance in difficult times. His clerics pray at least twice a day, both in the morning and in the evening. Their prayers are often straight and to the point when the path is already known. They often involve invoking particular aspects of a Great Wyrm like the strength of their claws or the protection of their scales.

The Roldem Navy

     The Navy of Roldem is currently the greatest sea power in Layonara; however, the Kingdom of Roldem did not have the influence of the sea until Port Hampshire fell when it was attacked by Dark Elves. During the battle, Port Hampshire's naval forces was completely destroyed, giving Roldem the chance to prosper on the waters of Layonara.
     Right after the fall of Port Hampshire navy, Greatwatcher Weu-Cheng enforced a grand plan that greatly improved the efficiency of the military ships and the docks. It called for a much more rigid training program and selection process for the crew. The plan marked the beginning of an era of naval dominance for Roldem.
Seven years later, Watcher Xiao-Way wrote a book titled Sea, the Throne of Power that discussed the importance of the naval power, which further influenced the growth of Roldem's Navy, doubling its size in less than three months.
     The men of the Roldem Navy are known for their efficiency and loyalty. All of the men took an oath before serving that binds them to protect the ship with their life. The high-ranking naval officers of Roldem enjoy a special prestige in the Kingdom, many even enjoying greater power than the nobles, securing the place of the Navy in the king's court.
     Greatwatcher is the highest-ranking officer in the Navy, and there are only three, each governing three of the nine fleets in the Roldem Navy. The fleets are divided into the Sun, Star, and Moon Fleets, and a Greatwatcher heads each one. Then there is a Watcher for each of the nine fleets. Each ship is then commanded by the Shipmaster, then the Shipvoicer, and finally the Deckmaster. Learner is the lowest ranking officer; they concern themselves with learning the basics of leadership onboard the ship.

Grandeur of the Sun-Class Ships:
     The Sun-Class is the most advanced ship in the entire Roldem Navy, and there is currently only one Sun-Class ship built and commissioned. Jewel of the Golden Sun, the flagship of the fleets, is 180 meters in length, has nine masts, and can carry over 1000 passengers if needed. (40 Officers, 220 Crewmen)

River of Roldem-Class Ships:
     The frigate class of the Roldem Navy, the River-Class ships are light and agile, and quick. However, they lack thick hulls and can sustain major damage easily. River-Class ships are mostly used for surveillance of enemy forces and patrol of the sea.  Examples of this class are Profit of the River, Evenness of the River, Connection of the River, and Peace of the River. (10 Officers, 70 Crewmen)

Eternally Dutiful-Class Ships:
     This class is heavily armored, affording them much more protection than the River-Class ships. The trade-off is in maneuverability: Eternal-Class ships are much slower and harder to navigate. They are more often engaged in combat missions. Examples of this class are Eternal Resoluteness, Eternal Mortality, and Eternally Humane. (25 Officers, 155 Crewmen)

Median of Mount Spine-Class Ships:
     Median-Class Ships sit between the River-Class and Eternal-Class ships. They balance armor and agility, creating a multi-purpose ship. They also have larger cargo holds and can serve as hospital ships, supply ships, or passenger-carrying vessels. Most of Roldem's ships are Median-Class. Some of the Median-Class ships are Beginning of the Median, Median Fundament, Establishment of the Median, Shining Light of the Median, and Strength of the Median. (15 Officers, 130 Crewmen)

Corath

Aliases: The Mad God, The Black Sun  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: Humans, half-orcs, orcs, demons
Domains: Death, Evil, Chaos, Trickery
Governs: Death, blood, lust, murder, lies, hatred, deception 

Dogma:
     Corath wants his clerics to spread evil across the lands. The more insanity, the more lies, the more havoc they wreak, the better they will stand in front of his eyes. Wherever a cleric of the Mad God walks, death shall follow their trail. The Mad God also encourages his followers to let their feelings of lust and hatred fuel their existence. Corath teaches that the virulent spread of evil is the goal of his followers' existences; consequently, many worshippers of The Black Sun seek to extend their lives by making pacts to attain undeath.

Clergy Weapon and Clothing:
     Corath's clerics prefer to use a short sword, since it delivers an average amount of damage, is easy to conceal, and is quick to coat with a poison. Normally every follower of the Black Sun also carries a frost-enchanted short sword to represent the coldness of death. 

     Clerics garb themselves in chain armor to stop most piercing and slashing attacks. Their armor is usually night black and blood red and adorned with the skulls and bones of fallen enemies.

Clergy and Temples:
     Being the god of death, some of Corath's temples can be found in well-established societies. In those, Acolytes of the Bones manage graveyard duties. Those temples in the unknown areas are the center of demonic acts of corruption, and the extent of their cruelty is legendary. Acolytes and Masters of the White Skull normally handle the gathering of bodies (recruits) and the high priests (liches), leading them to spread their evil seed. As a whole, though, organization and order is sketchy at best. 

     They celebrate All-Hallow's Eve, the day when all the dead raise from their graves to haunt the living. Corath's clerics pray at midnight to regain their spells.

Prayers Before battle:
     "The blood of my enemies will only sate my thirst when I use their bodies to serve your cause."

Kithairien

Aliases: The Runner  
Race: Wild Elf 
Worshippers: Usually wild elves.
Domains: Animal, Strength, Travel, Trickery
Governs: Time, strength, quickness of wit, hunting prowess 

Dogma: 
     Rely not on others for your survival. Live free. Embrace nature and its gifts, but do not take or keep anything you don't have to. Law and order other than those of nature restrict; thus, they are not to be followed in any way. Wait patiently for the opportunity, but when your chance comes, act swiftly, wasting no time or effort.

     The Runner was the first of his people. He spurned the lives of other elves, embracing nature. He spent his time travelling the world of Layonara, more at home on the open plains than among people. He established the first wild elf tribes, and eventually became their most revered figure. Strong and proud, he is the embodiment of what all wild elves strive to be. He is a master hunter, a trickster, and a fierce warrior.


Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Clerics of Kithairien favor the spear. The simple yet versatile weapon is suitable for many things other than combat. Armor isn't necessary, for a true warrior of Kithairien waits for the opportunity and strikes without getting hit himself. Clerics wear light, unencumbering armor such as cloth and leathers to aid their evasive prowess. Natural colors are usually preferred as they create an effective camouflage. Usually, clerics of Kithairien wear or in some other way display the colors blue and white, which represent the open sky and the freedom it symbolizes.

Clergy and Temples: 
     The church of Kithairien consists primarily of clerics living in solitude and small tribes of wild elves, and, as such, has little in the way of formal hierarchy. Actual temples to Kithairien do not really exist. There are places of worship, though, mostly magnificent and mystical places of nature. Clerics of Kithairien pray for their spells at no particular times; for a hunter, time does not truly matter. The church of Kithairien does not celebrate widely recognized holy days. Instead, the tribes of wild elves mark anniversaries of important events in the group's history and celebrate them in Kithairien's name.

     Prayers to Kithairien are usually for the hunt. Also, wild elves wishing to become like their hero-god ask for some of Kithairien's qualities. For example a wild elf cleric of Kithairien praying before hunting: "Oh great hunter, grant me your wisdom so that I may know the moment to act. Grant me the speed and agility of the great Runner, that I may act swiftly when the time comes, and bestow upon me your great strength, that my prey shall fall as easily as yours."

The Servants of the Weave

     The Servants of the Weave are a somewhat peculiar part of the Church of Lucinda, if it is an actual part of the Church at all. Wizards of Mistone

     That which people do not understand, they fear. Given all the magical mishaps and evils let loose by wizards in Layonara's history, is it any wonder that wizards are shunned?  The Wizards of Mistone are thought to be librarians of lore and teachers to those with potential, seeking to prevent the catastrophes that may turn their people against magic-users and magic in general. They keep close watch on foreign wizards, while keeping rogue wizards on Mistone in line with their beliefs.

Underdark
Also know as the Dark Realm, the Endless Night

     A vast, labyrinthine network of caves and passages, subterranean lakes and rives, home of creatures that do not bear well the light of day, the Underdark is one of the least understood - and most feared - areas of Layonara. No one, residents included, knows exactly how large the Underdark is, but many believe it to be immeasurably immense. Entrances, or rumors about entrances, are known on every continent of Layonara, so the Dark Realm likely spans the globe, and is probably larger than the surface lands due to its multilayered nature.
Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, cave-ins, mining, and burrowing by untold creatures have made a conclusive map of the Endless Night impossible. Not even by those who have dwelled there all their lives can claim anything more than a passing knowledge of the Underdark's geography. As with the corridors and caverns, entrances into this realm come and go. One might be stable for ages, then suddenly collapse, leaving no possibility of ever entering via that route again.
     As for those who dwell there, the most commonly known are the Dark Elves, as they tend to raid the surface lands. Magnificent cities have been constructed in vast caves (vaults) by the Dark Elves, radiating an evil beauty in the deep darkness. 
     A less-known race that roams the deeps is the Duergar, or Gray Dwarves. The Duergar live in great caverns, their homes carved out from the bedrock, their smithies close to volcanic areas to take advantage of the natural heat.
Perhaps the least understood of the Underdark's native cultures are the infamous Illithids, or mind-flayers. Capable of controlling other creatures' minds, they are feared by all races of the Underdark. Rumor has it they devour the brain of those unlucky enough to fall before them. Their deep hatred of sunlight hardly ever leads them to the surface. Illithid cities are rumored to exist, but those who have seen them are not likely to have returned, serving as slaves or snacks to the squidlike Illithids.
     Seen occasionally in ruins or caves closer to the surface are the Beholders. These large floating eyes can kill with a single gaze and thus feared by many. Little is know about their cities in the Underdark, if they even have any.
The last fairly well-known race that dwells Below are the Deep Gnomes, or Svirfneblin. Lovers of gems, they have managed to secure trade agreements with various surface communities. Their cities are hewn out of the bedrock near rich gem deposits, and despite their (mutual) hatred of the Dark Elves, they have relied on stealth and cleverness to survive. 

     The Underdark, a place of endless wonder and terror, is not a realm to be visited by the faint of heart. No one knows exactly what is lurking in the dark.
