Death

What does it mean to die?

When someone dies on Layonara, his or her soul will be sent to the Plane of the Lost, where all souls go after death. This plane is controlled by the Soul Mother and her second in command, The Harvester of Souls. It is thought that eons ago the Soul Mother made some sort of deal with the then upstart deities and was granted this plane of existence in return. 

The Two Types of Souls:
     Lost Souls are souls of those that die and do not follow a deity or have somehow angered their god. These souls make their way to the Soul Mother and are judged. Not all lost souls are necessarily damned, as at times a deity will speak up and accept one of them, but it would depend on their actions in life and their respect for the Soul Mother. It takes at least three days to judge a soul. If, for some reason, the soul is somehow lost forever (i.e. permanently dead), it is pushed to the front of the line and judged quickly. 
     Called Souls are souls of those that die in good standing with a god. They arrive on the Plane of the Lost and travel to a location called the Doors of the Gods. There they wait for three days (in game time) before entering their deity's plane of existence. No one is sure why it takes three days, but sages hypothesize that it is because of the deal struck long ago between the gods and the Soul Mother.

The Harvester of Souls
     Sages think that the Harvester is the one that travels to various planes and primes, seeking out living beings and marking them when they die. When a character is marked, it draws the attention of the Soul Mother. Sages disagree on why the Harvester does this, but the strongest argument is that it somehow taints the soul in a way so that if a soul ever arrives on the plane to be judged, the mark gives the Soul Mother a way to see into the mortal life of the soul.

The Soul Mother
     She is the patron "deity" of the Plane of the Lost. Sages speculate that she may have somehow betrayed the deities in their bargain, and in the gathering of souls over the eons she has grown in power. A few sages even go as far as to wonder if she is the cause of the current god wars.

Blood Wells
     It is thought that Blood Wells somehow touch the Plane of the Lost, and therefore, when you die near one, you will lose a part of your soul (in game terms, gain a death token).

Death on the Plane of the Lost
     If a creature dies on the Plane of the Lost they are instantly lost forever (in game terms, permanently dead) and are judged by their deity or the Soul Mother instantly. 

Bargaining with the Soul Mother
     It is said that if a character ever permanently dies, that brave adventurers could travel to the Plane of the Lost and deal with the Soul Mother in order to get a small part of their soul returned. This would surely be a deadly and highly dangerous quest, however, and it is rarely attempted. Even souls that have traveled to their deities' planes of existence must return through the Plane of the Lost, so one must still deal with the Soul Mother.
Thoughts on Death by Roferien's cleric Mercutio

Aeridin

Aliases: The Protector and Preserver of Life, The Lifegiver  
Race: Elf 
Worshippers: Predominantly Elves 
Domains: Air, Earth, Healing, Sun, Water, Good

Clerics of Aeridin often combine the Healing domains with one of the other domains.

Governs: Weather, dawn, rebirth, vitality, youth, sun, moons 

Dogma: 
     Preserve and protect life, but bear in mind that in the Great Cycle of life, death also has its place, so life should not be artificially prolonged. Seek out the undead and put them to rest, so they can rejoin the Great Cycle. Do not harm or kill others except in the most dire of circumstances. Do not refuse to aid those who need it.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     In general, clerics of Aeridin prefer to wear white robes. They'll only don armor when absolutely necessary, and even then with great hesitation. However, if they do, they'll wear full plate, either coated with a layer of silver or - more rarely - made from mithril. Their armor is usually embossed with golden leaves.

     In general, they wield quarterstaffs and shun the use of maiming weapons like axes or greatswords. A necklace with a golden leaf is often worn around the neck as a holy symbol.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples to Aeridin can be found everywhere, from the largest city to the smallest village. Most also act as a house of healing for the wounded and the sick and as a place where the poor or unfortunate can find help to get their lives back on track. Spread far across all continents of Layonara, the Church of Aeridin stands in good regard with most peoples.

     Despite the Church's throng of followers, there is not a strong central hierarchy that dictates how the Church operates. There is a hierarchy at the local level, which is mostly based on seniority, not on the actual power a cleric is capable of wielding. All temple communities remain very much in contact.

     Clerics of Aeridin pray for their spells either at noon or during a full moon.

     Religious days are many and tied in to the positions of the sun and the moons. Nights where one of the moons is full hold special importance; however, nights where both Orn and Ausir are full are of prime importance.

Katia

Aliases: 
     Mother Nature, She Who Shapes All  
Race: Human 
Worshippers Race: Mostly humans 
Domains: 
     Air, Animal, Earth, Plant, Water. Clerics of Katia combine the Animal or Plant domains with one of the other domains.
Governs: 
     Nature, forests, agriculture, plants, gardens 


Dogma: 
     Layonara is Nature. Without Nature there is no Layonara; therefore, aid, protect and defend Nature. Oppose those who seek to unbalance Nature. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics and Druids of Katia often wear leather armor dyed in green and brown hues, as worked metal makes them feel out of touch with Nature. 

     Followers of Katia usually use large wooden staves, which are actually strong, almost straight straight branches "given" by trees. They also often use longbows. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Katia's dogma is interpretable in many ways, making her faith somewhat individualistic. So, although the clerics and druids of Katia seek to protect and defend Nature, just exactly how this is to be done varies. Despite the differences in interpretation of the dogma, however, the clergy strives to be viewed as a friendly and good faith, since that is more beneficial. There are those who help nature takes its course by nurturing the forests and the plants, planting and nourishing new growth, and helping and nursing sick animals. These are the ones who are generally seen by the populace and have given the Katian faith an aura of good.  

    However, there is more beneath the surface than meets the eye. There are also those who believe that Nature cannot survive without their help. Civilization is spreading across Layonara and is proving a threat to its wilderness. Already, the forest that once covered Mistone completely has been severed into forests of a smaller size such as the Sielwood, the High Forest, and the Dire Wood. Roads have been laid across the wild plains and agricultural fields spread every year to feed the mouths of those who live in the ever-expanding cities.

     These more extreme followers of Katia will use drastic measures to prevent the felling of the forests, the cultivation of the plains, and the expansion of the cities. They will not shy from breeding fierce animals and setting them loose in order to make areas less safe and prevent villages from expanding. They will also not shy from covertly sponsoring bands of brigands to frequent certain areas, making roads less passable and allowing them to be grown over again.

     However, regardless of how a follower of Katia interprets the dogma, they realize that everything involving Nature takes time and planning. It might take years for their plans to bear fruit, just as it takes years for a sapling to become a tree.

     Because of Katia's dogma being subject to interpretation, there is not one Church of Katia. Followers are loosely organized and tend to live in small groups, with each group being headed by its most senior member. There is no strong, central hierarchy.

     Temples to Katia cannot be found in cities, but are groves secreted away deep in the forests, or large standing stones at the edges of forests.

     Clerics of Katia pray for their spells at sunrise. Prayers to Katia usually involve terminology referencing Nature, like plants, animals, or weather.

     Special holy days are the first days of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

Xeen

Aliases: Mistress of Pleasure and Pain  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: Mostly humans
Domains: Animal, Destruction, Plant, Water 
Governs: Pleasure, wine, love, insanity 

     Xeen is the daughter of Corath and Lucinda. She is the embodiment of excess, sometimes appearing as a beautiful woman in perfect health, and sometimes appearing drained from too much debauchery. Xeen is a very fickle and emotional goddess. She is fond of perverting the inventions of Aragen and Goran, much to their ire. Xeen is credited with making wine and opiates both pleasurable and harmful at the same time.

Dogma: 
     Life is to be lived to its fullest, in decadent sensual fulfilllment of the carnal desires of yourself and others. Pleasure is to be sought at every opportunity, even if it will eventually cause harm to you or others. Reason is for those who do not know how to savor life the way it was meant to be enjoyed. Infinite experiences await those who explore the world of pleasures, so try the new as well as savoring the old. Enjoy love when you can, for it shall not last long. Make wine and other gifts of Xeen and offer them to everyone, that they may enjoy the blissful taste and free themselves of their worldly cares. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Xeenites prefer the whip, a weapon that can in skilled hands be used for both great pain and great pleasure. Clerics of Xeen prefer either loose or tight-fitting clothing, depending on the situation. They prefer leather armor and clothing over metal. They always try to be dressed as seductively as possible to invoke feelings of pleasure in others. The color of what they wear doesn't matter, as long as it makes them look desirable. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The church of Xeen is casually organized, though they often work together to organize parties and celebrations for whatever cause. The clergy of Xeen often run festhalls in bigger cities that cater to all senses and include nearly every pleasure imaginable. Xeenites are also known for their skill in making great wine, and for this reason they can be often seen working for royalty and nobility. 

     The festhalls are often considered temples of Xeen, and often serve as such since they are favorite gathering places of her worshippers. Smaller temples to Xeen exist also, but they aren't very numerous due to the clergy preferring to spend their time in the festhalls rather than some boring temple. Both the temples and the festhalls are beautifully decorated and nearly all of them contain a fountain of wine where people can gather around and enjoy the taste of the goddess' gift. 

     Clerics of Xeen pray for spells in the morning after they wake up so that they may magically remove harmful effects from the previous night's revelry and immediately begin preparing for another, more spectacular day and night of celebration. The clergy of Xeen spend most of their time celebrating and enjoying life, and they tend to make up holy days of Xeen whenever they want to have fun. This has led to no one exactly knowing what holy days exist, but they are more numerous than anyone could imagine.
     The only day of celebration that has a set date is the "Night of Flesh and Magic," which is also known as Xeen's birthday. Xeenites celebrate this day together with Lucindites, for Lucinda is Xeen's mother. Followers of Corath, Xeen's father, aren't usually invited. The Night of Flesh and Magic is celebrated annually, but never on the same day. It's always the seventh day of a month, but every year it's one month later than it was the previous year. This is because Xeen wants to appear much younger than she really is, even though she doesn't age. 1368 the night was seventh of Oclar, 1369 seventh of Novlar, etc. The celebration begins at midnight between the sixth and the seventh day, and lasts for 24 hours. 

      Prayers to Xeen can often be heard anywhere there is a celebration. An example of a prayer to bless wine: "Xeen, Mistress of Pleasure, bless this wine, that the people gathered here can enjoy the taste of your gift and find eternal joy in fleeting love and pleasure."

Xantril
    It can be said that in the history of Xantril there are two moments that both devastated all foundations and became the cornerstones for the twisted continent that emerged. The first was the Cataclysm, which tore Xantril apart from Dregar and sent it drifting east for many dark ages of relative isolation. The second was the arrival of the Prince of Demons, Xandrial, and his merciless minions. There are many tales of Xandrial's arrival upon Layonara.     Some believe that Xandrial was the first demon that forced its way through the gate made by the foolish experiments of Oriax on the continent of Mistone.  Some believe that Xandrial was called by one of the most concentrated efforts of Drow faith and magic to torment the surface dwellers.     Some believe that Xandrial was summoned forth by Bloodstone or Milara to serve their vile purposes. Whatever the truth, the continent of Xantril belongs to the Prince of Demons. All who lived on this continent prior to his arrival either quickly bent to Xandrial's will, were tortured and died in dances of demonic desire, or now live an inescapable nightmare to further pleasure the demons. This is what we know of Xantril, and we know it because Xandrial wants all of Layonara to know it.

    When you first enter Arabel, you'll know you are in Xantril and that the terrible things you have heard are true. From all around, tortured screams will accost your ears and tear at your soul. Much of the city is in ruins. Disease, famine, and violence are all part of the everyday routine of Arabel. Somehow the city manages to operate the docks with relative efficiency. Likely this is because the demons want fresh souls to torment, even though most know by now to stay far away from Arabel.
Arabel was not always a tormented city under the sway of demons. Between the Cataclysm and the arrival of Xandrial, Arabel was one of the few towns on Xantril to establish some sort of prominence and connection with the other continents. Arabel's location on the southern tip of Xantril gave them an advantage in securing trade with both Dregar and the Kingdom of Roldem. Over the years, the merchant families of Arabel built themselves up into a commercial powerhouse, funneling most of the surplus goods from the middle and south of the island through their docks. The former stature of Arabel can still be seen in glimpses of its working ruin. Those who lived in the old Arabel are haunted by its memory. Those who contributed to its glory are now forced to work the sewers.
Major Temples to Corath and Shadon have been constructed in Arabel.

Westgate 
Location:
    Western shore of the continent of Xantril. 
    Population: 4,000 (40% human, 15% half-orc, 12% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% orc, 6% gnome, 4% dark elf, 2% demon, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tyrany 
Defenses:   
    A reinforced masonry wall surrounds this city. It is also enhanced with magic. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
    Westgate is a port city directly west of the Demon Mountains. When Xandrial sends his demonic minions to Dregar or beyond, they go through Westgate. The only creatures allowed to live in this city are those who directly serve this purpose and as such are evil to the core.
 
Reth 
Location:
    Western side of the Great Forest on the Island of Xantril. 
Population:   500 (55% human, 45% elf) 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses: 
     A wooden palisade surrounds this small town. 
Miscellaneous Information:
    Some say this small forest hamlet is the gathering point for rangers and druids who are dedicated to protecting the sanctity of the Great Forest of Xantril. Their secondary concern, rumors have it, is to keep the demons from descending upon the Ancient Oak. As the northernmost town in Xantril, and since it is shrouded by the Great Forest, it is one of the few places on Xantril where Xandrial's influence is not complete. This gives the dedicated few rangers and druids a chance to work undetected on the forest's behalf. As this is a dangerous occupation, these agents of the Great Forest are re-circulated, though none but the druids and rangers themselves are sure how.

Fort Militrix
Location:  
    Located at approximately the center of the continent, Fort Militrix overlooks the road north towards the Roughlands.
Population: 375
Defenses:  
    Fort Militrix is defended by alternating sections of stone and wood walls. Inside are platforms for ranged attacks, and historically speaking the fort has always been well garrisoned.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Militrix is of key military concern, as it is situated on the road which runs east and west between Prumar and Mithrain and divides the continent into its northern and southern sections. All traffic between the north and south falls under the watch of Fort Militrix. For this reason the Fort has always been heavily garrisoned with the most disciplined and skilled troops Pranzis could muster. The officers were also bolstered five or six times their numbers by recruits gathered on the march north from Arabel. This, of course, was all prior to Xandrial's arrival. But this fortitude made Militrix resilient to Xandrial's onslaught. Some believe that Militirx is holding fast, a bastion of hope amidst a sea of raging demons. 

Fort of Last Hope
Location:  
    At the edge of the Demon Mountains, in the wastes of the Tortured Lands, lies the Fort of Last Hope.
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    Hope Fort is well defended by stone walls and battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    The name of Hope Fort has become something of a Xantril joke. More often now it goes by Fort of Last Hope. It is said that a handful of soldiers still fight against the waves of evil minions that pour from Xandrial's keep. If they do, it is assumed that Xandrial allows them to do so for some other twisted purpose, for none could live free so close to Xandrial's seat of power.

Hilm Castle
Location:
    At the edge of the Fields of Death and the Orsraun Mountains stands Hilm Castle.
Population: 1600
Government:  Theocracy
Defenses:  
    Hilm is heavily defended with high stone walls and well designed battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Hilm is dreadfully close to the Demon Mountains. Still, Xandrial's gaze is somewhat obscured by the Orsraun Mountains which lie between the demon king and Hilm. Hilm also lies to the north of Xandrial's keep, away from the more heavily populated areas of Xantril. These two facts give Hilm some room to maneuver on this demon-dominated continent.
    For ages, Hilm ruled the north as the last major settlement on the road to the Archwood and the Great Forest. By looking at the arrangement, you would likely have thought Hilm ruled with an iron fist, putting the wild folk of the forest under the civilized boot. This is simply not the case. Hilm established its authority in the northern regions by repeatedly defending the interests of the Great Forest and its residents from the waves of settlers and treasure seekers who fled the central region of Xantril, tortured and convoluted in the seismic events of the Cataclysm. Hilm regulated all traffic north, allowed only some to continue into the forest and turned back many. This, of course, makes Hilm particularly unpopular with the residents of the lands to the south. The forest folk to the north, however, have a deep respect for Hilm that they are reminded of daily as they enjoy the wilds in which they reside.
    This conflict, like all other conflicts on Xantril, shows signs of flaring up. The southerners, possessed with demonic rage, grasp at targets to lash their hate upon. To them, Hilm is a perfect choice. Only minor forces have thrown themselves upon the Hilm walls thus far. Either they are wild groups of the demonically driven whipped into a spontaneous frenzy and thus unorganized, or they are simply testing the defenses. In either case, fear intensifies in Hilm, as all within its walls can feel the darkness sweeping across the Tortured Lands toward their gates.
Cities of the Demon East by Xantril scholar Dulugu Ganalan

Baraeon Ca'duz

Aliases: Prince of Hate, Lord of Spiders, Left Hand of Black  
Race: Dark Elf 
Worshippers: Dark Elf males only
Domains: Death, Evil, Trickery
Governs: Hatred, revenge, cruelty, spiders, darkness 
 
     Baraeon was the dark elven hero that led his people into the darkness after they were betrayed by the other elven clans. 
     Baraeon taught his people how to live in the darkness, and with the help of Pyrtechon the race of dark elves thrived. Baraeon also taught his people the arts of revenge and cruelty. 
His own personal revenge against the surface elves culminated when he poisoned the first born daughter of Ilsare. Taking the form of a spider, he managed to sneak into the Ilsare's chambers, where she slept with her young child. Baraeon poisoned the child, and then woke Ilsare so she could watch the child die in her arms. Pyrtechon rewarded Baraeon by elevating him to godhood. 

Dogma: 
     Vengeance is an art. It is sweet and should be savored, a pleasure not to be rushed. Nothing is more satisfying than watching your plans for revenge come to fruition and have the object of your retribution realize you were behind it...but realize too late. The Prince of Hate will look down favorably upon you if your subterfuge remains hidden to all but your target. The weak and the faithless should be destroyed. 

     Dark elves are the supreme race, and Dark Elf males are better than females. 

     The Dark Elves shall reign supreme in Underdark. Annihilate the surface elves and take their lands from them. Do not aid the enemies of the People. Strive to better yourselves, even at the expense of others; this way you will gain and keep the power that is rightfully yours. Do not harm any spider, ever. Harming a spider is an affront to Baraeon Ca'Duz, and should only be done if the spider's poison is used for the art of vengeance.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Priests of Baraeon Ca'Duz prefer to use a shortsword slathered with poisons. Their garb is predominantly black, and stained with dark shades of green. Around their neck they wear a medallion in the shape of a spider, the symbol of their god. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Priests of Baraeon Ca'Duz are the most powerful people in Dark Elf society, next to Priestesses of Vierdri'ira. Every Dark Elf city has one temple for the Prince of Hate. Temples are led by a High Priest, who only remains in that rank as long as no craftier or more powerful Priest removes him from that position.

     Temples to the Lord of Spiders are usually shaped like a spider. One enters a Temple through one of the legs, immediately noticing the greenish light that permeates the entire temple. Depending on the size of the temple, four legs are for training the male clerics. One leg is home to the acolytes' quarters, and one is home to the high clergy. 

     The central body of the spider is the Hall of Poisons. This Hall is filled with webs and spiders, and it is here that the general worship of Baraeon Ca'Duz takes place. The head of the spider is the Inner Sanctum, where the most profane rituals are performed and the temple's treasure and relics are housed. Only the eight highest clerics are authorized to or capable of entering the Sanctum.

     Females are not allowed to enter temples of the Left Hand of Black, on pain of death. This was not the case until about 1500 years ago, when Az'atta betrayed Baraeon Ca'Duz.  Until then, both males and females worshipped the Prince of Hate. However, after being betrayed by Az'atta, Baraeon had his male followers expel or kill all of his female clerics as an act of vengeance for Az'atta's betrayal.

     Males who do not worship Baraeon Ca'Duz but enter the Inner Sanctum are to be sought out and killed unless they are converted to worship Baraeon within 7 days. Proof of conversion is given by undergoing the Test - the same set of trials all Dark Elves have to go through to prove their loyalty to their deities and their People - to demonstrate their loyalty to Vierdri'ira and Baraeon; those who fail either die or are transformed into the fearsome Driders. 

     Clerics pray for their spells before they go into reverie. Prayers are often couched with references to spiders, webs, and poison: "Lord of Spiders, grant me your favor that my enemies do not notice the web of intrigue I have spun to ensure their demise."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Pyrtechon, Branderback, Corath, Vierdri'ira

Friendly:Shadon, Xeen 

Neutral: Goran, Mist, Aragen, Kithairien, Grand, Grannoch

Unfriendly: Katia 

Enemy: Rofirein, Vorax, Dorand, Aeridin, Ilsare, Deliar, Toran, Lucinda, Az'atta, Shindaleria, Sulterio, Beryl, Folian S'pae, Prunilla

Mistone
    Mistone is a continent in the western part of the hemisphere. It seems to be one of the few places which have not yet felt the crushing impact of Bloodstone's most recent wave of invasions, though most believe this dread will come in time. The reason for this relative isolation is that Mistone has for many years now been semi-autonomous. Although Mistone is of course still under the rule of Dregar and the capital of Pranzis, this remote influence is not often felt. More likely if you ask a Mistoner who rules, they will tell you Queen Allurial in Blackford Castle. Mistone has remained relatively stable in terms of economic infrastructure, a large factor in its relative self-sufficiency. Lately this illusory sovereignty is being seen with increasing frequency and intensity to be just that, an illusion. Some attribute this to unchecked growth. Others believe it is the effect of more sinister machinations.

Well-known Cities:

Hlint
Location 
    Hlint lies close to the center of the continent of Mistone. 
Population 
    1,830 (60% Human, 15% Halfling, 10% Dwarf, 5% Half-Orc, 5% Gnome, 5% Elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:
    There are wooden walls within and around parts of this city. They are mostly decorative, however, or used to partition space within the town itself. For protection, the denizens of Hlint primarily rely on Fort Llast, their neighbors to the west.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Hlint is a boom town. Of course, it is neither as grand as Leilon to the northwest nor as established as Fort Llast to the west. Nevertheless, it has grown in just about every aspect due to several clear reasons. Hlint fortuitously lies on unarguably the most secure and therefore most traveled east-west passage on the continent of Mistone. On the north side of this well-trodden road are the Greypeak Mountians, and the Sielwood Forest grows to the south. Both the mountains and the woods beckon to would-be adventurers and resource seekers, bringing them in droves from all over the continent. Because of this, Hlint has become the adopted home of most of those who call themselves adventurers on the continent of Mistone. Some of the great heroes of our age have made roots in this bustling town and The High Council of Layonara has made Hlint its headquarters. This also means that Hlint has been the stage for countless dramas, some universal, some inane, and some far reaching in their global sociopolitical ramifications. A temple of Ilsare can be found here as well.

Leilon
Location: 
    Leilon is situated in the northwest corner of the continent of Mistone. 
Population:
    3,575 (50% human, 30% half-orc, 12% halfling, 3% dwarf, 3% gnome, 2% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:  
    Leilon is well defended by thick stone walls which climb over twenty feet in most places. Along the top of the walls are ramps and embattlements.

Miscellaneous Information:
    The city of Leilon began as a small town some 300 years ago. The inhabitants were people who migrated away from the thriving cities the south looking for their own niche on the continent of Mistone. For approximately the first one hundred years of their existance, life was fairly serene and prosperous. The population of the town grew, and began to attract more artisans and scholarly types.

    Unfortunately it was around that time that the barbarian tribes of the north discovered Leilon. The tribe called the Long Axes raided the town, decimated the male population, and left many women raped and with child. The Long Axes filled their longboats with loot, leaving the town with little food for the winter. Many of the people fled to the south, and the town's population dwindled from over 10,000 to a mere 2,000. The harsh winter further whittled the population down to less than 1,000. That spring the people rebuilt their town and prosperity soon returned. Life appeared to have returned to normal, until the Long Axes returned in the fall. The Long Axes would have destroyed the village for good, but for a retired old mage named Arn of Corbone. He had come to the village in the summer, looking for a place to spend the last of his years. The news of the raid last fall almost made him leave again, but his old body was in need of rest after weeks of travel. Arn expected the Long Axes to return that winter. With great effort and skill, he managed to rally the town, organize the defenses, and quell the barbarian assault. The barbarians would not return for several years after their encounter with Arn.

    The Long Axes were fierce warriors, acustomed to fighting. When they returned that fall, they smashed their way through the defenses and proceeded to raid the town as they had before. Taking matters into his own hands, Arn called upon his considerable magic powers, and changed the history of both Leilon and the Long Axe tribe. Many of the Long Axe warriors fell to the firestorms that erupted from Arn's fingers. Arn was ruthless, mowing down Long Axe warriors as they fled back to their longboats. Fearing that his tribe would be destroyed, Ingmar Stormhammer, the Long Axe chief, sacrificed himself in what many still regard an epic battle. Ingmar leapt through a wall of flames, and drove his spear through the chest of an incredulous Arn of Corbone, who did not even try to get out of the way. The flames had left Ingmar mortally wounded as well. The few remaining Long Axe warriors limped home in their longboats. The catastrophe at Leilon ultimately forced the Long Axes to be absorbed by other tribes.

    The winter passed with little incident. That spring, an old friend of Arn's came to Leilon to visit. His name was Golvin Dawntella, a knight of the Griffin. The people greeted him warmly, and several townsfolk asked him to make the town his demesne. While Golvin was saddened by the loss of his friend, he was also intrigued by the opportunity of becoming the town's leader. Golvin sent for his retainers, and gave his old lands to his younger brother. Golvin then asked the mayor for his daughter's hand in marriage to further cement his claim on the town of Leilon.

    Golvin set about building his keep and organizing the town's militia. Over the next five years, the town prospered greatly. The keep was completed, and a wall was erected around the town. The militia was formed and trained. The town was well prepared when a coalition of barbarian tribes attacked that fall. The militia was outnumbered six to one, but were able to barely repel the raid.

    The battle inspired what would eventually be a war between Leilon and the barbarians to the north for the next 80 years. Over the years the Leilon Militia established themselves as one of the best on all of Mistone. The barbarians did have several victories, but as the years wore on, the militia established themselves as superior. Eventually, the barbarians gave up trying to sack what was now the city of Leilon.

    Since that time, relations with the barbarians have steadily improved, and now the two factions are very good trading partners. With no enemies to fight, the city of Leilon has since focused itself into becoming a major trading power. The discovery of whaling some forty years ago only contributes to what was already a booming economy.

    There are some on the continent of Mistone who would, if asked, point to the city of Leilon as an example of the brutal aftermath of a leader installed by military necessity. For in Leilon, justice is said to be as swift as the coin flows. Poverty and wealth seem to grow hand in hand. Yet none dare challenge the Blackwatchers, the Leilon city guard, who follow orders with ruthless efficiency.

    A temple of Mist can be found in Leilon.

Melnon
Location:
    Melnon lies in northwest portion of Mistone, near Lake Huron and at the base of the Greypeak Mountains.
Population:
800 (40% human, 20% halfling, 15% elf, 15% gnome, 5% half-orc, % dwarf) 
Government: 
    Melnon is organized as a feudal city-state subordinated to the nearby Blackford Castle.
Defenses:
    There are no walls around the town and defenses are scattered at best.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Melnon has traditionally been the starting point for most expeditions heading beyond the lower range of the Greypeak Mountains. The city has no walls and there are a few battlements situated in those portions of town where the Greypeak Giants have in the past attempted to barrel through town. The temple of Lucinda once drew mages from all over Mistone for worship and training. Since new roads have been carved between the lower and higher ranges, Melnon's prominence is becoming little more than a memory.

Center
Location:  As the name suggests, Center is located in the center of the continent of Mistone.
Population:
3400 (50% Human, 22% Halfling, 18% Dwarf, 10% Elf)
Government:  Center is ruled by a council of merchants.
Defenses: A small wall surrounds the town.

Miscellaneous Information:
    While the town has existed in one state or another for many centuries, it has only seen prosperity after the arrival of three somewhat prosperous halfling families that took advantage of its central position along the trade route between Port Hampshire and Haven Castle. They are now commonly found on most caravans traveling through the area, filling whatever roles they can. It's not uncommon to find many household goods that are produced in Center. 

Far Reach
Location:  Far Reach is on the western side of the continent of Mistone, west of the Sielwood and North of Far Reach Forest.
Alignment:  Neutral
Government:  Far Reach considers itself subject to the Mistone monarchy located in Blackford and has a local representative.
Defenses:
    Far Reach is defenseless.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Far Reach was once on the north-south road, just north of the Broken Forest. When new routes were established through the forest Far Reach fell into a kind of peaceful out-of-the-way slumber. Considering the torment they'd received from nymphs and Dark Elves and undead for years before, this new status is welcomed by nearly all Far Reachers.

Fort Hope
Location:  Fort Hope is centrally located on the island of Mistone, just south of the Broken Forest
Population: 760
Government:  
    Fort Hope has a two-tier system of government. There is a military commander to run the Fort's garrisons and military function as well as an appointed mayor who administers the social and economic affairs of the fort.

Defenses:  
    An old and resilient military outpost, Fort Hope is well defended.

Miscellaneous Information:
    The first thing you'll likely notice upon entering this centrally located Mistone outpost are the tents, caravans and newly built structures. These new developments arise in the wake of recent migration to the area. For years Fort Hope served as a watch station for the undead, which often overflowed from the Broken Forest. This fact made Fort Hope one of the least desirable posts on the continent. This is true particularly since clean-up crews frequently left the safety of the fort to remove the walking rot and shadows from the crucial road which runs north and south through the forest. These crews almost never returned. And for hundreds of years the road remained hopelessly overrun, controlled by some unknown sinister influence.
The optimistic name of this post has always seemed to play with this kind of historic irony. Although many believe the name of the fort derived from the hope to curtail the evil influence of the Broken Forest, more investigation will reveal that it was actually established and named during the race wars.
A small group of humans pushed past the front lines, situated on the then sublime forest, and supplanted an elven outpost in that same location. Once the fort was captured, their only hope for survival and victory was the drive of the great human general Draislar. He was to wedge through the elven armies of the Far Reach plains and the Broken Forest to regroup at the fort and use it as a base of operations. Draislar never arrived. The battle which ensued claimed the lives of Draislar and his army, but also, and quite mysteriously, the bulk of the elven armies of the region. This battle marked the beginning of the end of the elf and human wars on Mistone. And with countless souls strewn upon the desecrated forest floor, the human chapter of Far Reach began.
The most recent and most prosperous chapter of Fort Hope's history begins with the heroic deeds of the rangers Triba Guess and Enzo Reynolt, who mended the long broken nature of the forest. Once the dead no longer rose to torment the living, the road north and south became passable and the frequency of caravans looking for a respite at the Fort increased rapidly. Fort Hope is coming into its own as a key security and mercantile force, made more crucial by its central location and resilient traditions.

Forewarn Fort 
Location:  
    Fort Forewarn is on the eastern shores of the continent of Mistone. 
Population: 
4,000 (45% human, 20% halfling, 15% half-orc, 10% dwarf, 15% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    Masonry walls surround this city. The walls are reinforced for protection from attacks from the sea.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This is a primary shipping port between the continent of Mistone and Dregar. As such, Forewarn Fort is a major inlet of goods and information as well as a good place to leave Mistone in the aft horizon. With good shipping routes, however, come pirates. The Gulf of Bagira to the north of Forewarn is known to be a pirate hideout and launching point. With the Forsaken Islands off the coast, and stories of whole ships becoming marauding crews of undead, only pirates or fools would sail those waters. These facts draw the seedy elements of Mistone to Forewarn, making it a rough town as well as a sound choice for the headquarters of the Mistone Alliance.

Fort Llast
Location:  
    Fort Llast is in the northwestern part of Mistone. It can be found on the east-west road that runs through Hlint and meets up with the road that runs north and south between Blackford Castle and Krandor.
Population:  275
Government:  
    The government in Fort Llast is a strict military hierarchy under the command of Lieutenant Jursen who answers to Blackford Castle.
Defenses:  
    There is a short stone wall surrounding the city. It is also home to a Temple of Toran, so there are always a couple of paladins around.

Miscellaneous Information:
    A quick glance at a map of Mistone can tell the story of this town's significance. The fort lies at the crossroads of two of the most frequented roads on the continent. This allows the Llast guards to monitor most of the travel and trading in northern Mistone. It is also the job of the Fort to ensure the road which connects Leilon, Blackford Castle and Port Hampshire far to the south remains open and relatively safe. When Fort Llast is well staffed, and it almost always is, guards can be found patrolling the road as far south as the Broken Forest and north until it reaches the ocean at Leilon. 
Monitoring and ensuring smooth movement on Mistone, however, are secondary considerations. Fort Llast was founded in a warm summer of the early 3rd century, at the height of the Human and Elf wars. Blackford Castle was the seat of human power on the continent even then. In the 287th year after the Cataclysm, the castle nearly fell to the elves, an outcome which could have altered the fate of humans and elves on Mistone. 

    Despite being heavily garrisoned and defended, the castle was caught unprepared by the waves of elves who seemed to appear on the Grunwald Plains as swiftly as an ocean storm. Peasants, merchants and guards carrying crucial supplies scrambled to reach the castle before the portcullis fell. Many were left stranded outside and were slaughtered by a hailstorm of elven arrows and bolts. Startled and dismayed by the grisly scene just beyond the walls, the humans who did make it to the castle struggled to regain composure and perform their duties. The disciplined Blackford soldiers, however, snapped into action with drilled precision and managed to turn back wave after wave of elf invaders. 
The elves, however, came prepared to smother every human in that castle with fear and hunger. Their numbers were great, and swelled even greater with reinforcements after each skirmish. The blockade was complete. So with every human soldier pinned in the castle and the nearest garrison far to the south with no hope of contact, the castle lay under siege for months. It took that long before the humans, with the help of some dwarf miners caught in the outskirts, tunneled beneath the castle to a small valley in the Greypeak Mountains. There, two small groups of scouts emerged. One made the trek to Leilon, where they sailed south to the Rodilin Hills to alert the marauding human armies. The second traversed the treacherous peaks to call upon the aid of Haven Castle.

    The elves, pinched by a human army moving north along the Zainge River and another moving west along the northern border of Sielwood forest, were forced to retreat. Elves flowed into the Sielwood and vanished among the ancient trees. At that moment it was clear that the elves had used the cover of the forest to amass their armies and establish supply lines. Thus, Fort Llast was built, perfectly situated as a first line of defense against elven invasion from the deep shadows of the Sielwood forest.

Fort Velensk
Location: 
    Fort Velensk lies at the very southern tip of Mistone between the Battle Fens and the southern ranges of the Berhagen Mountians.
Population: 9385
Government:  
    Fort Velensk is ruled by an allegedly corrupt military dictator.
Defenses:  
    Thick stone walls and battlements surround the city to protect it from terrestrial attacks. However, the town's defenses are more oriented toward guarding the crucial docks.

Miscellaneous Information:
    At the southernmost part of the continent, Fort Velensk is the primary point of connection between Mistone and Rilara. Port Hampshire is the place for more official dockings, but anyone who knows anything about Rilara will know that is why Velensk prospers. In contrast to Port Hampshire, the relative isolation of Fort Velensk between the Berhagen Mountainsto the east and the Battle Fens to the west, as well as having no significant settlements nearby, makes it a preferred destination for more nefarious Rilaran traffic. The large and defensible docks contribute to this function as well. In Rilara, Milara's dominion is said to be total. And considering his grasping ambition, particularly his goal to bring all of Mistone under his sway, Fort Velensk is busy indeed.

    With this said, it is obvious that the fort is a wickedly volatile place. The economic and political elite barely attempt to maintain a thin veil of respectability, a veil which only ever fools the most vapid or gormless transients. Many residents live in squalor; they dwell in alleys and sewers, feeding off of the shipping rubbish and dockside rats. Pirates and outlaws and Rilaran agents of disruption flow through the city with seeming impunity. Of course, this is only true so long as such unseemly agents do not counter the direct interests of the ruling elite. With such desperate and corruptible characters in force on its streets, Fort Velensk also proves an ideal headquarters for mercenary recruiters. Equally logical is the presence of the temple of Rofirien, which beams light from its shimmering surfaces over the dark streets. It is one of the few places of mercy in Mistone's most notorious den of villainy. The men who vault their essence in the Fort Velensk temple and undertake Rofirien's mission of justice are compelled by unmatched faith, often deadly but always selfless. They are among Mistone's most valorous.

Haven
Location:  
    Haven can be found on the eastern rim of Mistone.
Population:  3,300 (50% humans, 30% dwarves, 10% halflings, 10% elves)
Government:  
    Monarchy with landed serfs in surrounding areas
Defenses:  
    The outskirts of Haven, where most reside, are not defended except for by foot patrols. If the town is raided, as many as possible are pulled into the heavily defended stone walls of the castle.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Haven is most noted for the trade route it was built upon. Forewarn Fort, which ships the majority of the continent's goods, is just to the south and Haven is directly between it and the capital of Blackford. Also, while the route is longer, it is still safer for the convoys from Port Hampshire to head through the city rather then the often treacherous forest.

    For many centuries the people of Mistone traveled this long stretch of road with nothing but their own blades to defend the goods they rode with. Eventually small towns began to sprout, offering travelers some refuge from bandits as well as the harsh seasonal weather. 

    These towns brought much relief and grew quickly as the valuable goods stopped in their markets before heading off to their ultimate destination. As the settlements grew, they became all the more ripe for any man brave enough to take advantage of their actual weaknesses. Milick was such a man. 

    Milick was an intelligent man who felt stifled and oppressed by the huge merchant conglomerates of the city. Angered by this, he decided to exact revenge. Milick organized a convoy that would follow the normal route north at the same time as many other convoys. That way, they would all stop near the same locations during the night. Of course, instead of goods, he was carrying a small army of mercenaries bought from the streets of the city. As the other convoys slept under cover of the small towns, Milick's men raided them, killing guards and merchants in their sleep and stealing the goods for themselves. 
Milick ran northwest with his men and booty, hoping to camp within the forest. There he would gather more men and fence his stolen goods to increase the numbers and quality of his army for hire. His desire for vengeance upon Haven could not be assuaged. 

    During the night a fight broke out between Milick and his own appointed mercenary captain. They quarreled over whether they should continue the plan or just settle with the money they had. Angered by the change of plans, Milick lunged at the captain and ripped him open with his blade before the mercenaries could subdue him. By the time they had finished, he had been beaten to death. The next day, they returned to the fort only to find the peasants of the Haven fields rallied and fervent about blocking the hired army's path. A fierce battle ensued, but the peasants eventually managed to overcome the mercenaries, who underestimated the determination of the farmers as well as the sharpness of their scythes. With the captured gold and goods, these unlikely heroes set about creating the fort so travelers and locals could find reliable shelter in dire times.

Krandor
Location:  
    In the central western part of Mistone.
Population: 1600 (60% human, 30% elf, 10% Halfling)
Government:  
    Krandor has a mayor, chosen by the property-owning families in the vicinity.
Defenses:  The only defense Krandor has is a few patrolling guards.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Where the western edge of the Sielwood forest dances endlessly with the expansive meadows just beyond lies the town of Krandor. The unobtrusive architecture and lack of clear border make Krandor seem in harmony with the natural landscape. Because of this, many outdoorsmen are drawn to this town. Some go to Krandor to use the town as a launching point for hunting expeditions into the Sielwood. Others fall in love with the forest and attempt to halt, or at least try to manage the impact such groups have upon the forest. 

Lar
Location: Near the Highstar lake in the Greypeak mountains.
Population: 1200
Government: Feudalism
Defenses: 
    Lar can only be reached by a narrow mountain trail, which can be easily defended by just a handful of guards. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    Lar is very small and remote. It's more of a trader's outpost than a town. Most of those who call Lar home serve the miners and trappers who live and wander in the Greypeak Mountains. Locals speak of the town being founded on the banks of a gorgeous mountain waterfall by Larnida. In recent years, a statue has been erected on that spot to commemorate the event. On founder's day, and other somewhat secretive ritual days, people bring offerings to the statue. 

    There are many dwarves in Lar. This is either a fortuitous circumstance for defense against the many giant attacks upon the city, or the dwarves have come to Lar for a piece of the action. As a trading outpost for trappers and miners, with a high dwarven population and unceasing attacks from giants, life in Lar is clearly a demanding and arduous endeavor. That's why those who call Lar home are some of the most gruff and resilient people to be found on all of Mistone. Lar is also the village where Ta'karsh Blacklung, High Hammer of Dorand, has chosen to build the Citadel of the Hammer in honor of Dorand, god of crafters.

List
Location:  
    List is southwest of the High Moor swamp on the continent of Mistone, near Haven Castle.
Population:
1,175 (45% human, 20% half-orc, 15% dwarf, 10% halfling, 5% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    List is without defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    List is affiliated, both economically and politically, with Haven Castle to the southeast. It is little more than a center for the widely dispersed farmers of the area to come for company, supplies, and transport to the Haven markets for their goods. As such, the residents of the town proper are far outnumbered by those living in the outlying agricultural areas.

Liken
Location:  
    Liken is found at the coast of the northeast corner of the continent of Mistone.
Population:  360
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
    Liken has no defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Nestled in the coastal hills of northeast Mistone and blessed with the perfect climate for growing pipeweed, Liken is a popular place for halflings. There is a single dock right in the middle of the town which launches and receives small ships for local distribution of Liken's and the northeast region's goods.

Kheldell
Location: 
    Kheldell is on the northern tip of Mistone in the High Forest.
Population:
350 (60% human, 20% elf, 5% halfling, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 5% half-orc) 
Government:  Theocracy
Defenses: 
    A wooden palisade surrounds this small hamlet. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    Kheldell is a somewhat self-sufficient town located where the High and Lost Forests together meet the ocean. The town is a part of the forest, obtaining every resource for nourishment, warmth, and shelter from the verdant woodland. As such, Kheldell's residents are raised to be resilient, surviving cycles of intense hardship. The woodsmen who take to this arduous lifestyle are proud of the town and its accomplishments. They therefore tend to discourage outsiders from doing anything more than passing through. They discourage all hopeful settlers except the occasional individual bearing the unmistakably weathered signs of a rugged past spent working the woods. The docks, used sparingly and typically to import regional goods from Liken, are closed to outsiders without prior authorization except, of course, in cases of emergency.

Krelin's Tents 
Location: 
    In the Blood Desert on the continent of Mistone 
Population:
120 (60% human, 25% half-orc, 10% halfling, 2% gnome, 2% dwarf, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tribal 
Defenses:  None

Port Hampshire
Location:  
    Port Hampshire is the major city and port on the southwest coast of the continent of Mistone. 
Population: 
49,000 (70% human, 15% halfling, 5% dwarf, 4% gnome, 4% elf, 2% half-orc) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses: 
    Superior masonry walls surround much of the city. In some key places the walls are also reinforced. In addition to this, some of the walls have also been magically reinforced. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This city is rich and prosperous. Large veins of gold and silver are shipped in from the Swordrust Mountains to the northeast. If an adventurer is looking for something special, she is likely to find it in this city.
Six hundred years ago, this great city was destroyed by a combined force of Drow and dragons. The city was left shattered and stripped as the forces plundered over five million gold from it. The city struggled to rebuild, as the Duke had lost his former power and its resources had been plundered. The only sources of capital in the wake of the destruction were the individual merchants. They pulled together and as quickly as they could began rebuilding the city and raising armies. Their interest in the port and their links to the invaluable resources in the surrounding areas were dear enough to risk everything to defend it. 
The Duke, still attempting to retain authority, could do little to stop the organized merchants.  On several occasions when he attempted to defy them, the merchants quickly placed him under house arrest and kept his castle guarded at all times by their own superior troops, effectively making him a puppet. For centuries this arrangement persisted, and the Dukes of each successive generation increasingly came to accept their fate as adjuncts of the city economy. Every attempt to act otherwise was swiftly curtailed. Now the Duke's tradition in Port Hampshire is to work for and within the systems of power established by the merchants. Through this arrangement, the merchant organizations and the Duke have merged interests and formed a coherent power structure.

    The bottom line in Port Hampshire is still an economic one. The peasants and landowners who live in the surrounding areas often complain about being under the boot of the Port. The laws of the land are implemented to protect the interests of the major merchant powers, who sometimes use this fact to expand their exploitative labor practices and resource capturing endeavors. Some say this is the cause of the unrest which has emerged in the southwest region. Others believe the uprising it is not a legitimate grass roots movement in the interests of those in the shadow of the port, but a machination implemented by Milara or demons or both to destabilize the region in preparation for future maneuvers. Some believe it is both.
Major Temples of Deliar and Shadon can be found in Port Hampshire.

Shoufal
Location:
    Southern part of the continent of Mistone, right in the middle of the Berhagen Mountains. 
Population: 
6,500 (85% Mountain Dwarf, 5% halfling, 5% human, 3% gnome, 1% elf, 1% half-orc) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses: 
    This Dwarven city is surrounded by superior masonry walls that are further reinforced with fiercely guarded Dwarven skills passed on through oral tradition.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Shoufal, also called Gem of Berhagen, is a very proud city steeped in tradition. They do not like outsiders and only after years of living among them will one be grudgingly accepted. This only ever happens when an individual works through the labor and crafting ranks, all the while supporting and defending the community. 
The majority of the populace are devout followers of Dorand and Vorax, and the arms and armors created by the Shoufal smithies are of great renown.
Where the Sun Sets:  A traveller's guide to the cities of Mistone by Lanzo Liftupover

     The "Warstars" is an elite force of warriors in Alurial's army. These forty fighters are the personal bodyguards of the royalty. The Warstars are led by Highstar Belinmeric. The Warriors of the Star are wholly supported by royal grants.
Warstars, by Altain, Priest of Corath

Vorax

Aliases: The Father of Battle, The Eternally Vigilant  
Race: Dwarf 
Worshippers: Primarily worshipped by dwarves. Although strong warriors of other races (especially human) will often times call upon the Father of Battle as well. 
Domains: Good, War, Protection 
Governs: Battle, war, valor, bravery, vigilance 

Dogma:
     Vorax honors all who believe in bravery, war and valor. His clerics despise weakness of character, believing one should have strong moral values. They hate pacifism, as any morals and ideals worth having should also be worth fighting for. They loathe an idle mind, as it becomes fertile ground for unrighteous seeds to plant themselves, and equally hate an idle body, as it becomes soft and unsuitable for the rigors of war. They have a great mistrust of arcane magics, and as a result generally do not mix well with wizards and other arcane spell-casters. Above all, the clerics of Vorax abhor dishonorable and deceitful tricksters. War should be fought for righteous causes, and won through honorable battle. 

     War is a sacred rite for the followers of Vorax, and as such is never entered into lightly. War should always be an option of last resort and should only be engaged in for the most just of causes. However, once engaged, a war should be fought strictly by the established rules and the righteous cause must be made victorious. There is no shame in losing a battle, but there is great dishonor in losing a war. To lose a war is to fail the just and the righteous, and therefore show weakness in the Father of Battle. Because war is so sacred to the church, the tools of war are considered sacred instruments. Thus, weapons of war are treated with great reverence. 

     To encompass all of this, a follower of Vorax must have a strong and just moral character. Followers of Vorax must be like The Ever Vigilant himself, keeping their bodies and minds prepared at all times to defend the just and righteous of the world. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     The favored weapon of the clergy of Vorax is the battleaxe, although many of the dwarven clergy prefer the dwarven variety. Silvered varieties of weapons are often favored as well, as they are exceptionally handy when fighting the undead minions of one of Vorax's biggest enemies, Corath. 

     The favored armor of the clergy and followers is strong, hardy full plate, often painted in silver and red to emulate the armor worn by Vorax himself. The temple clergy rarely wear such armor, but they do still possess it. Instead, temple clergy tend to wear robes of red or black with silver and gold highlights and threading. They tend to wear very formal robes, however, since such attire is less conducive to idleness of the body. Battle Priests of Vorax rarely go anywhere without their armor on. Instead, they have robes fitted to be worn over the outside of their armor. Although most followers actually spend less time in armor than without, the Battle Priests are the exception, usually only taking it off to sleep, bathe, or clean the armor itself. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The hierarchy of the church of Vorax is broken down into three divisions, each with its own way of doing things. 

     The first sect is the Scholar Clerics of Vorax. These are by far the most numerous as they are often educators and counselors of the lay as well as the devout. These clerics are the ones who rely on prayer as much as anything else as a daily guide in their lives. This sect is led by a council of elders, who in turn give authority to carry forth the word to other members of their order as they see fit. Only the most pious and devout followers of Vorax ever sit on the council. Once there, they sit for life; only when a member dies will another be chosen to fill his or her place. This new member is chosen by secret ballot by the council. The ballots are kept secret as to prevent clan rivalry from influencing votes. The longest-sitting member of the council is the leader, holding the title of High Elder of Vorax. 

     The second sect is the Battle Priests of Vorax. These priests spend less time in communal prayer with Vorax, and as such do not wield his power as fully as those of the scholarly sect. What they lack in divine strength, however, they make up for in strength of arms. Unlike their scholarly counterparts, Battle Priests spend more time honing their bodies and minds for war than they do in pious contemplation. Many of the strongest warriors of the time can be found among the Battle Priests, but raw strength alone does not suit them; Battle Priests must also be wise in the ways of war. Battle Priests often become generals of armies and leaders of men, for through long and intensive study and actual field practice, they have learned the intricacies of battle strategy and the true art of war. No Battle Priest begins in the sect; rather, they are called to it over time. Sometimes a scholar finds within their studies a calling to become more like Vorax, and so takes up arms and begins fighting more and praying less. Other times grizzled warriors begin to learn that there is more to war than brute force, and begin to study its art and learn more of Vorax, that they may find his favor come time for battle. The hierarchy of the Battle Priests is rigid. All Battle Priests have a standing within the hierarchy which they are made to memorize from top to bottom so that there is never a question of whose authority is greater. The very top of the hierarchy is the General Superior of Vorax. The General Superior is the longest standing member of the Council of Battle Generals. There are seven Generals, each of equal rank, and all others fall below them. Promotion through the ranks for those below them can only happen in two ways, either there is a death, and everyone moves up, or the Generals promote one of those they lead to a higher position. Only the General Superior can promote a Battle Priest to the elevated position of Battle General of Vorax. The Battle Generals of Vorax are the most capable warleaders to be found anywhere. 

     The third sect of the church is the Order of the Bloody Axe. These clergy are also militant, but are in the service of either of the previous sects. They have the divine strength granted to them through close communing with Vorax, but the strength of body of a warrior or Battle Priest. These are the Paladins of Vorax, and in some rare cases Champions of Vorax. The hierarchy here is very loose. Once a person is accepted as a Paladin of Vorax, it is expected that they need no hierarchy to give them guidance or structure. They are glowing beacons of good and righteous character with unimpeachable moral fiber. Among their kind, though, there is a certain amount of deference for those that have served longer as Paladins, for the longer they have served, the more experience eradicating evil they have had. There is but one elevated position among the given to its longest standing member: the Righteous Axe of Vorax.

     Although rarely ever assembled, the leaders of each of the three sects form the High Council of Vorax. It is these three that come together in times of crisis to provide direction for the church, and it is this council of three that has final say in the interpretation of church doctrine and mission. It is also this council that, on very rare occurrences, will select from among the followers a Champion of Vorax. This Champion nearly always comes from the Battle Priests or the Paladins, and serves as an honorary member of the High Council of Vorax until death. 

     Prayer times for each of the sects vary. Scholars pray quite frequently throughout the day, praying as they rise from their rest at dawn and again at the end of the day before retiring for the night, at a minimum. They also offer prayer after any intervention by Vorax is perceived, such as after a healing is performed or a battle won. Battle Priests pray far less often, since they rely as much on their own ability as the intervention of Vorax. They do acknowledge Vorax at the beginning of each day, and always before engaging in planned battle. The prayer practices of Paladins are much like those of Battle Priests, but they will pray for guidance and strength at any time they feel that their services will be needed to ensure that Vorax helps them in their righteous cause. 

     The only religious holiday observed by the church as a whole is the first day of the new year. It is held in reverence as a reminder of the rebirth and reaffirmation of good and life in the world. As to other days of celebration and revelry, they are usually clan-based and used to mark the day of some great battle in the history of the clan.

Merchants of Layonara
     Perhaps the most powerful guild on all of Layonara the Merchants guild is well known by all because of their ties with the commoners. They have a presence in nearly all major cities and large towns throughout the world.
Very Brief Notes on the Merchants of Layonara Organization

Deliar

Aliases: The Blessed One, The Protector and Provider  
Race: Halfling 
Worshippers: Halflings (normally male) and merchants or shopkeepers of every race.
Domains: Good, Protection, and Travel 
Governs: Trade, Money, Wealth, Luck, Fate, Harmony, Family 

Dogma: 
     Trade is the best road to enlightenment and enrichment. Use trade to bring prosperity to everyone in the world. Seek out and develop new markets and new opportunities. Hone your skills as a tradesman. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Deliar's worshippers favor a short sword, mainly because of its portability and variety of uses. They have also been known to embellish their swords with precious metals and pommel gems to show their wealth and, consequently, Deliar's favor. 

     Clerics of Deliar tend to wear chain mail, adorning it with pricey metals like gold, silver, or mithril. The higher the rank of the cleric, the rarer the metal and the more favored and wealthy they are. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Despite Deliar being a god worshiped by merchants and shopkeepers of all races, the real clergy mostly consists of halflings. Deliar's halfling followers tend to live in small clans, with the elder being the leader, though normally there is little need for any type of leadership because halflings seem to naturally work together.

     Temples are normally tents, for the lives of Deliar's servants are rarely sedentary. Protection for the temples is also easier this way, as they are not in set locations. However, most larger, more prosperous cities have huge, exquisitely decorated temples to Deliar.

     Clerics can be found praying multiple times of the day. They pray for luck before a trade, believing that it brings wealth and harmony to the family.
 
Prayers to Deliar often revolve around trade and travel:
     "Father Deliar, bless this journey with good fortune and protect us from harm."

Molten Island

     Before the Cataclysm, Molten Island was attached to the Troll Mountains on Dregar; however, it is now a huge and active volcanic island. Inhospitable, and without any trading ports of interest, the island is not of much value to anyone. However, in the port pubs of Waysend, sailors can be heard to tell tales of a red dragon flying out from the island.

Firesteep Mountains
     Fisteron is the ancient red dragon who resides in the deeper levels of the Firesteep Mountains. He is a cruel and malicious beast, nearly godlike in power, who surpasses any red dragon previously known. 

     The mountains play host to many types of beasts, especially those attuned to elemental fire, such as fire elementals, red slaads, fire giants, and balors. Planar beasts, such as rashkasas and devourers, are not uncommon. Undead are also said to haunt its upper levels.

Folian S'pae

Aliases: The Longstrider, Prince of Wolves  
Race: Wood Elf 
Alignment: NG 
Worshippers:  Wood Elves, though many rangers of various races also follow Folian. 
Domains:  Animal, Good, Plant, Sun.      Most Popular are Animal, Plant
Governs: Animals, forests 

Dogma: 
     Be one with the forests and live in harmony with nature's creatures. Take no more than you need and give as much as you can in return. 

Clergy Favored Weapons and Clothing: 
     Those who follow Folian are very skilled archers. Some even go so far as to make bows their sole weapon. Long swords, scimitars, and rapiers are the chosen blades of Folian's followers, but clubs and staves are common due to the wood from which the weapon was created. Most who use clubs, staves, or bows make their own or have it handed down to them. Folian approves of those resourceful enough to carve - often literally - their weapons out of what nature gives them.

     Leather armors are the primary garb of Folian's clerics, though lighter metal suits are used to some extent. Armors are dyed in greens and browns. Clerics of Folian will never don a full suit of armor, which, cumbersome and heavy, prevents them from feeling the connection to the lands they are sworn to protect. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Due to the highly individualistic nature of Folian himself, there is no structured Church of Folian. The majority of followers have been rangers at some point in their lives before turning to the more settled life of a cleric. Clerics usually maintain their link to the forests, not moving to cities or villages.
     Because of this, temples of Folian are always found in or near to wooded areas. Some of the oldest known places of worship are inside humongous trees, veritable living temples of nature.

     Clerics of Folian have no set time of day to pray for power and guidance, nor do they pray every single day. They pray when needed and as often as needed, no more, no less. They do, however, prefer to be close to nature when the need for prayer arises, often choosing to stop and pray in a grove of trees rather than inside the walls of town.
     Spring is significant to Folian's worshippers, for the woods and their inhabitants typically wake from their long winter's slumber to start life anew at this time of year.

Prayers: 
     "Longstrider, guide my steps. Help me to defend and serve the wood and those within."
A common goodbye: 
     "May The Prince of Wolves watch over you."

Ballad of the Unnamed Hero

Sing, spirits, sing and hear my story, 
Hear it on this mourning misty morn! 
Hear my tale of strife and glory, 
Of one now dead, and one never-born! 

A hero was he, with eyes of fire, 
Strong of arm, with lightning steel. 
He rose to fight at Toran's ire, 
A fight not his his fate did seal. 

Four days it's been forth he went, 
Four days of trials and travails fierce, 
Four days before my sad lament, 
Four days before his heart lay pierced! 

Forth he went, four days before, 
To mete the great god's wrath. 
Armor bright, and shield before: 
Faith and Iron to guard his path! 

He fell in val'rous battle with 
A foe that never drew breath, 
Fell and died on sword-thrust fifth 
Straining 'gainst the grim undeath! 

And when he fell five sword-strokes in, 
The lich-lord cackled on the moor, 
"Fear not, your new life shall begin, 
Soldier now mine, paladin poor!" 

The hero managed a bloody smile, 
And spoke through broken teeth, 
"If die I must, thou creature vile, 
Thou diest too, upon this heath.

"I stood steadfastly through five thrusts 
Before my quest was done. 
You forget, in your blood-lust, 
I stood long enough to see the sun." 

The lich, forewarned, turned to flee 
As a shy and startled fawn, 
But the fighter's fight doomed him to see 
The white-hot light of dawn! 

In the light the lich changed shape 
Flesh appeared and breath was drawn, 
Cap and clothes and even cape 
Appeared in the light of dawn. 

The change was done, a man now stood 
In the lich-lord's place. 
He cried and screamed and wished he could 
Turn back time's heady pace! 

But the hero spoke to the new-wrought man 
Words fit to end his strife: 
"I was sent here by Toran, 
To deal not death, but life." 

Spirits sing, and hear my story! 
A hero lies this morning mourned! 
In the earth, bereft of glory, 
His new-dug grave, unadorned! 

Heed me spirits, and heed me man, 
For as along as I draw breath, 
I shall sing his praises when I can: 
He who delivered me from death!

Lucinda

Aliases: Mother of All Magic, Lady of Spells 
Race: Human 
Worshippers: 
     Mostly humans, half-elves, and elves; fewer worshippers among other races. 
Domains: Good, Healing, Knowledge, Magic, Trickery 
Governs: Magic, sorcery, spellcraft, health 

Dogma: 
     Magic is the Gift of the Lady of Spells, and those who wield it are greatly privileged. Magic will make the world prosper if used wisely. Use magic to shape the world when you know it will eventually serve the greater good. Do not keep your knowledge to yourself; teach magic to all those with the will to learn and follow Lucinda's teachings, and tell all about the Weave.      Encourage creativity in magic in all ways and at all times. Always help others out of the goodness of your heart. Do everything you can for the Weave, for otherwise, magic may fade away. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Lucinda favors strongly enchanted weapons over normal ones. Clerics of Lucinda often carry staves and wands containing useful magic, and heavier quarterstaves for melee combat.      Lucinda's clerics often wear useful enchanted robes like arcane spellcasters. The colors on these robes are usually light and vivid, most often white and blue. 


Clergy and Temples: 
     The hierarchy of the Lucindite church is varied, separating into eight Orders that each concentrate on one school of magic: abjuration, conjuration, divination, enchantment, evocation, illusion, necromancy, or transmutation. Each Order consists of numerous groups that include both arcane and divine spellcasters. These orders have their own places of study and their own hierarchy. Each group with more than thirty members is led by a master of the spell school who is usually the most powerful and experienced caster in the group. All of the orders are led by a grandmaster; for instance, the Order of Evocation is led by the Grandmaster of Evocation. All the Orders are good aligned and led by the Council of Magic, which consists of the eight Grandmasters of the Orders. 
     There are also some academies of magic and many smaller temples where spells of all schools of magic are taught to any willing students. This is the part of the clergy that is most visible to the public. These academies and temples have members of each Order of magic working in them, and they also provide healing, supplies, and shelter for traveling Lucindites. The church also sponsors a small society of paladins, often called the Chosen of Lucinda or the Protectors of the Weave. They defend Lucinda's temples, protect the Weave from any possible harm, and keep magical artifacts out of evil's reach. Lucinda's temples (and related buildings, such as the academies) can be of any size and any style, but they all have one thing in common: all temples to Lucinda are great works of the Art, enwrapped in countless spells, containing numerous magical items, and surrounded by an aura born of the very strong Weave about the place. 
Lucindites pray for spells any time they need to, as Lucinda recognizes the need to be able to cast at any time. Lucindites don't have too many calendar-related holy days but they celebrate many things on a more individual level. Discovering new spells and ways to use magic or creating great magical items are often times for great celebrations among Lucindites. Temples and academies have annual events at which local mages to gather and share whatever they have accomplished during the past year. These events are generally called Spellmeets, but many temples call them by different names. Lucindites and Xeenites have a special night of celebration once a year called "The Night of Flesh and Magic," which celebrates the birth of Lucinda's daughter Xeen. Usually more Xeenites than Lucindites join this event, as it mostly concentrates on worldly pleasures rather than the somewhat ascetic discipline of magic. 

     Prayers to Lucinda can be heard almost anywhere involving magic and spellcasting. For example: "Oh great Lady of Spells, empower my Art, that it may better World and Weave."
