The Basics of Gem Crafting
-------------------------------------------

1)  The process of working with gems is a very detailed one that involves multiple steps and multiple crafting devices. These are as follows: 

Gem Deposits:  First you must gather gem minerals from the gem deposits. 

Gem Cutting Stone: Used to cut gems. 

Gem Crafters Table: Used to detail cut gems. 

Mineral Wash: Used to identify the mystery minerals that are found while mining. 

Jewelers Bench: Used to create rings, scarabs, necklaces and amulets. 

2) To begin, the player must locate a gem deposit and successfully dig an uncut gem mineral. The player must have a Gem Chisel equipped in order to mine gem minerals.

3) Once a gem mineral is extracted, it needs to be cut. This is done at the Gem Cutting Stone. The player will need to have a Set of Gem Crafterâ€™s Tools in their inventory. This process will yield either cut gems or flawed gems and gem dust as a bi-product. 

4) To detail a cut gem, the player will again need to have a Set of Gem Crafterâ€™s Tools in their inventory. This process is done at the Gem Crafters Table and will yield either fine gems or flawed gems. 

5) To create rings, necklaces, scarabs and amulets, the player must use the Jewelers Bench. These items require a mold, enchanted gems and enchanted ingots. 

6) Occasionally, players will find mystery minerals while mining. These minerals can be identified by washing them in the Mineral Bath.

The Basics of Scribing
----------------------------------

1) Scribing begins with the collection of sawdust produced by the carpenterâ€™s bench. 

2) Saw dust must be used to make raw parchment at the farmerâ€™s press.

3) The raw parchment is then baked into scrolls by the bakerâ€™s oven.

4) Inks are made at the scribing ink desk using misc plant resources. 

5) Finally, the scrolls and Inks can be combined along with a spell to produce a scroll.

The Basics of Tailoring
------------------------------------

1) Tailoring involves both the creation of leather and cloth, and the creation of leather and cloth based items, respectively. These items include various armor types, boots, belts, gloves and cloaks. 

2) To create cloth the player must harvest cotton. To create leather, the player must obtain animal skins. These can be acquired by hunting the desired animal and skinning it. To skin an animal, the player must equip a Skinning Knife on the animal corpse. 
3) Animal skins come in small, medium and large sizes. To create leather, the skins must first be cured. This process is done at the Curing Tub and uses various ingredients. 

4) Leather is created at the Tailors Table and requires a cured hide and tanning oil. Tailors must also possess a Sewing Kit in their inventory in order to use the Tailors Table. 

5) To craft leather armor and other pieces of clothing, the player must combine leather or cloth, a pattern and any other required ingredients.

6) To create a pattern, the player must include a Book of Patterns and a piece of cloth. These are also made using the Tailors Table.

The Basics of Tinkering
--------------------------------------

1) Tinkering requiresa set of tinkers tools in. Tinkers can make a variety of different items ranging from glass ingots to crafting tools to deadly traps. These items are created at the following crafting devices: 

Tinkers Device: This strange looking device is used to create arrowheads and misc tinkering items. 

Tinkers Toolkit: This device is used to create traps and crafting tools. 

Tinkers Furnace: This device is very similar to the forge, except that it makes molds, glass ingots, and various glass products. 

2) Tinkering uses two raw materials that can be mined. These are sand and clay. To mine these, the player must have a Shovel in their inventory. 

3) Sand deposits yield bags of sand and clay deposits yield lumps of clay. 
4) Shovels, like the minerâ€™s pickaxes, will wear out from time to time when used.

The Basics of Wood Crafting
---------------------------------------------

1) Wood crafting combines carpentry, bow crafting and fletching. 

2) Wood Crafting also involves harvesting wood. This is done by equipping a Woodcutterâ€™s Axe and using it to bash a Hickory Tree, a Mahogany Tree or an Oak Tree. 

3) Trees produce branches that can be turned into wood shafts, wood planks and wood staves.

4) To create wood crafting items, the Carpenters Bench must be used while possessing a Set of Carpenterâ€™s Tools.

Description: A set of darkly coloured clothes. Reinforced by leather pads and metallic plates in several places this set could be taken for an armour instead of simple clothing. A sinister aura permeates its appearance and when worn one often feels chilled even when sitting at a warm fireplace. Others, especially priests or people of faith, often display intense or even angry reactions towards whomever wears the armour in public.


The history of the armour of the Final Rest is as blurred as it is bloody. Having been in the possession of numerous assassins, assassin mages and other sinister personae in the past the Final Rest has seen much use and changed hands many times. 
The most notable owner of the armour through history was the assassin and Shadow Thief Dubron Tevorel. Rumoured to have been one of the founders of the famous Shadow Thieves, Dubron was a man both feared and revered. It was Dubron who lead three Claws of assassins to a meeting of the leaders of every thieves guild in the city, thereby dealing the death blow to organizations such as the Scarlet Glove and the Veiled Dagger. The bloodbath in 1321, which eliminated all other competition to the Shadow Thieves in Port Hampshire, is remembered to this day.
The only lesson that may be drawn from the records of the Final Rest is that it seems to be in the nature of the armour to cause the downfall of its bearer. 

Nothing is known about the origin or the creator of the Final Rest. The massive investment of negative energy and necromantic spells in the armour, however, speaks its own language. 
The powers of the armour are undeniable, as well as the toll paid by whoever wears the Final Rest. At times the strain upon one's vitality can be physically felt, almost like a hand around one's neck. One does well in taking off the armour before going to sleep, since the Final Rest is a deliverer of nightmares that prey upon the sanity of the bearer.

The places of Mistone

Broken Forest
    Little is known about this forest near the center of Mistone, but it is rumored that an ancient Elven Tomb lies somewhere in its trees. The Elves used to call the place "Faraway Forest" because it was so far away from the place they call home. It is rumored that the Elves no longer enter the forest for some reason, but that has yet to be proven. It is also rumored that there is a magical glade, abhorrent to evil, somewhere within the forest. Druids supposedly bring the severely ill to the glade to cure them of disease and lycanthropy. Some say the the remnants of the T'oleflor hide themselves in the Broken Forest, but aarakocra, centaurs, and sprites are the most obvious residents.

Far Reach Forest
    On the western side of Mistone Continent is the Far Reach Forest, a puzzling place with an air of mystic secrecy. Infamous Kellian's Tower stands in the southeastern glades of the forest, near the ends of the Silent Mountains, which hide griffon lairs. The woods have never been logged, even by the voracious humans, and the forest is shunned by locals. Even today its depths are largely unknown. Many locals claim the Far Reach Forest harbors fearsome creatures, and numerous reports of missing woodsmen and patrols seem to verify this claim.

High Forest
    Just north of the Greypeak Mountains, the High Forest sits as the northernmost territory of Mistone. Settlements in the forest are rare due to the isolationist nature of the rangers, druids, woodsmen and centaurs who call it home. For beautiful scenery, the forest is unmatched: placid Unicorn River winds its way lazily through the trees, Lake Sieron sparkles under the suddenly open sky, and a visit to the tranquil Harmony Grove with its shrine to Katia has been known to rejuvenate many soul-weary adventurers. The forest is not a visitor's paradise, however; orcs, ogres, orogs and a variety of other foul beings maraud through its trees and glades. Many say that the forest conceals entrances to the Underdark, but the civilized denizens of the forest are tight-lipped about the veracity of such a rumor.

Sielwood Forest
    The Sielwood Forest's verdant sprawl is located in central Mistone. The forest is fed by the lakes Ravine and Anon, which are the sources of the Ro and Asare rivers. The abundance of water makes this forest especially thick with foliage, and perhaps this is why the Rangers' Vale is hidden away deep in the Sielwood. Rumors abound that once a year, on a date determined by the phases of the moons, all the rangers in Mistone gather in Aeridin's grove in the Vale for a meeting. Opportunities for dungeon-delving abound; the savvy adventurer can find the Watcher's Tower, Lost Ruins, and Nameless Dungeon overgrown by and shrouded in the forest's greenery. Many evil creatures make their homes here, but small enclaves of good creatures like unicorns and pegasi have carved out their own niche in the Sielwood.

Greypeak Mountains
    The Greypeak Mountains have lured many adventurers south of the High Forest, their mist-shrouded, snow-capped peaks whispering the possibilities for adventure into the minds of all who look at them. Though there are occasional small settlements in the mountain passes, most of the territory is wild and untamed. At one time, the mountains were heavily settled, but all that remains of those unnamed towns is ruins and the occasional still-standing tower. Various goblinoids call the mountain caves home, and the locals complain of attacks from such creatures as orcs, bugbears, and goblins. Griffons make their nests high in the peaks, and do not like being disturbed. More powerful adventurers visit the mountains in an attempt to find a way into the sparkling cloud-castles that can occasionally be glimpsed through the mists; the cloud giants who call such places home are reputed to spend time in the mountain areas hunting and foraging.

Swordrust Mountains
    The Swordrust mountain range, near the center of Mistone, is littered with dungeons and caves. Adventurers and fortune seekers insist that some of these caves connect to the Underdark, but those who have entered searching for the passage to the subterranean kingdom have not returned to verify their guesses. There is an encampment that is fairly safe from the natural dangers of the Swordrust Mountains, unless you count gnolls as a natural danger, for it is their watch camp. Besides the gnolls, goblins and ogres roam the passes and caves, searching for their next hapless meal.

Berhagen Mountains
    These rugged mountains in southeast Mistone are dominated by hill, mountain, storm and cloud giants. They are also home to ogres, orcs, trolls, gnolls and various other nasties. The area is riddled with dungeons, caves, and mines, and the dwarves have set up a fortress to draw the resources from the Berhagen range.

Silent Watch Mountains
    These mountains are known to be rich in minerals, but only the brave (or stupid) actually mine here. Little is known about the mountains. The mountains are always silent, almost as if someone or something has taken a personal interest in the visitors. It is rumored that there are a few magical portals that move around in the mountains, but no one knows where they take the hapless explorers who enter them.

Dire Wood
    This strange, hilly land in south Mistone is named the Dire Woods because of a legendary massacre of humans that caused the soil to redden. Once a frenzied and ever-expanding area of chaotic, inexplicable magic, centuries of relative peace have stablized the unpredictable forces, though the weather here remains charged by the old magical field and bears no resemblance to that of the outside world. During its expansion, the Dire Wood's boundaries were marked by black, petrified trees. Creatures long extinct elsewhere are found here in abundance, though they die if forced out beyond the twisted trees that mark the beginning of the woods.

    Adventurers are strongly encouraged to enlist the services of a druid or ranger when entering the Wood; few have survived without their aid.

Blood Desert
    A vast expanse of snakes, scorpions, and sand that constitutes the eastern coast of Mistone. Adventurers will likely visit the oasis of Krellin's Tents, the only source of water for miles around. Few creatures can survive the blazing heat of the Blood Desert, and those that can are often fierce predators.

Ajari Swamp
    A bog on the southeastern shore of the continent of Mistone, the Ajari Swamp grows out of the western edge of the Gulf of Coreanys. There is a dungeon of some kind deep in the watery mess, but the lizardmen and trolls who call this fen home dissuade most from adventuring that deeply into the swamp.

Battle Fens
    Little is known about this deep dark swamp, except that it is in southwestern Mistone. Insane or glory-hungry adventurers make their way to the Battle Fens to fight lizardmen and troll tribes, raid the Locust Tower, and hunt the dragons that have been reported in the deepest parts of the swamp.

High Moor
    Long ago, an elven forest flourished in northeastern Mistone.Then, the elves were struck by one of the greatest calamities in their history, the Dark Disaster: a killing magic that took the form of a dark, burning cloud. When the cloud faded away months after it descended, neither the trees nor the elves survived. All that was left was an open, blasted moor: the High Moor. Dungeons and ancient ruins dot the moor, remnants of that long-dead elven civilization.

Broken Swamp
    Several rich castles and manor houses stand flooded in the Broken Swamp, a stinking hole west of the Greypeak Mountains, with only spires and battlements showing above the dark waters. Sunken riches and powerful magic await those mighty enough to wrest them from their evil guardians. The swamp has grown in recent memory, swallowing several farms and holdings along the mountains and lake, and it's now avoided by all but crazed adventurers equipped with water-breathing magic and looking for loot.

The Outlands
    A vast, dangerous land in the Southern area of Mistone. A Blood Well is rumoured to be in the area, guarded by an ancient dragon of immense power. The Outlands are also rumoured to be a focus of necromantic energy, demonstrated by the Tower of Darkness and a mysterious ritual altar, steeped in shadow. 

Blackford Castle
    Home to Allurial, Queen of Mistone, Blackford Castle is probably the strongest fortress on the continent. Built with the aid of dwarves, its walls can withstand nearly anything. Allurial has also construced a temple to Lucinda inside its walls.

Layonara's Most Notable Legends and Artifacts

The Bardic Block
     There is really nothing worse, except maybe finding slaad eggs in your food rations, but imagine, if you will: it's been a long day, most of which you've spent slaving in fields, slaughtering monsters, or studying the arcane arts. You settle down in a comfy chair and relax with an ale in the local inn. To your dismay, a bard strikes up, possibly the worst you've ever heard, certainly worse than me. As I'm sure we've all experienced, heckling never works, and simply killing them doesn't go down too well with local law enforcement. 
     A quick-thinking mage, however, found a solution to our little dilemma. After several nights of trouble with a local bard, Svern Cinderbrow decided to get his own back. He returned to his home and set about creating a coin with a secret bite to it. A simple gold coin that, once placed into a hand, silenced the recipient for anywhere from three to four hours. 
     The following evening, he approached the bard and placed the coin into the bard's hand, apologizing for his behavior of late. The bard would have thanked him, but the coin had already taken effect. This idea became so successful that Svern went into business with a local merchant, and became wealthy from sales of his miracle coin. 
     This venture came to a dramatic end when Svern and his partner were found beaten to death in an alley beside a local inn, broken lutes smeared with blood and brains lying nearby. Unfortunate as it was, they definitely "coined" the phrase: "Silence is golden."

Coup de Grace
     The Coup de Grace, or the Final Strike, as it is sometimes called, is a true legend. Heralded as the greatest fencing sword in Mistone, the Coup de Grace has only possibly surfaced twice in recorded history. Rumored to have been created by the dwarven smith Berhand Silverbeard, the existence of this item has never been truly confirmed.
     One such record is of orcish origin; therefore slightly less trustworthy. This depiction speaks of a shining metal needle, two and a half feet in length, which shimmered brightest blue as it was swung, as if it cut the air itself. Obviously I retell this depiction with a touch more flair than its original author; Orcish never translates delicately to Common (or any other language, for that matter). Nevertheless, the tale tells of a war band ambushing a passing shopkeep, a successful raid until a passing rider stopped to aid the stricken merchant. The orcs tell of a brilliant flash of blue when they charged the rider, who was either elven or human. Blinking, they looked back to see the head of their warleader tumble from his shoulders, his chain coif sliced through with a cleaner cut than could be believed. They then mention a "dr'gonba," or "tactical retreat," which in Orcish means "running away without screaming too loudly." Although a rough translation, this is said to be the first recorded sighting of this wondrous weapon. 
     The second account tells of another orc encounter, this time with a guard patrol. Records show an eight-man patrol was ambushed by fifteen or so orcs, well-armed and well-organized. Beaten down, the men were bound, gagged and prepared for their execution by beheading. The first was brought to the block, and his head removed with two swings of the chief's greataxe. However, as the second was brought to the block, a cloaked figure appeared in the light-dappled forest clearing. 
     Again the record tells of a fantastic blue flash as the blade was drawn, this time by a character of small stature, dwarven or tall halfling. The blade was said to scream as it moved, again as though the air itself felt the keenness of its edge. The guards' record tells of "armor cut through as though it were paper." The orcs rapidly fell to the well-armed opponent, only scoring one hit during the battle. Once battle was over, the cloaked figure unbound one of the men and vanished into the blackness of the forest. 
     Blood trails from the cloaked figure were picked up the next day by trackers, but the trail was lost just beyond the Zainge River. This is the last known record of this sword. 

The Forge Golem
     Deep beneath the Swordrust Mountains, it is rumored that there once existed a dwarven smith, living in seclusion and plying his trade undisturbed by the outside world. With only his golem as company, it is said that Berhand Silverbeard created some of the most impressive weapons ever seen on Layonara. His monstrous forge, which supposedly was fueled by lava from the continent's crust, was kept at such a heat that only his golem could approach it.
     Few of his weapons have ever been seen; even those that are said to be born of his hand could not be proven so. He was so proud of his weapons that he refused to taint them with a trademark. One rumored weapon is the Coup de Grace, a rapier so fine it can open plate armor with a single slash. This weapon, however has its own story. 
     The tale of his demise is handed down in dwarven lore and bardic songs, and while the details vary each time it is told, the basics remain the same. 
     Legend has us believe he was nearing completion of his finest work, a mighty broadsword called Legacy. Said to have power unlike any other on Mistone, his crowning work was to be his last before his return to the surface. With a blade of forged adamantium folded over two hundred times, the sword was a sparkling example of true craftsmanship. However, the light of day was never to grace his old eyes, misfortune and a temper as hot as his forge saw fit to that. 
     In the final stages of his work, Legacy was to be tempered once more before its completion. The golem approached the forge, as it had done many a time before, placing the blade into the flames. Unfortunately the blade slid from the golem's hand, disappearing into the flames. Berhand ran forward, screaming as his most prized creation disappeared into the flames. He smashed his smith hammer into the golem's head, cursing it for its foolishness and demanding that it retrieve the lost blade. 
     At its master's command, the golem strode into the flames, melting with each step it took. It is claimed that the golem retrieved the blade, only to bring the forge down around it. The resulting explosion killed Berhand as his workshop crumbled around him, burying the countless treasures of his life's work along with him. 
     Rumors say that his golem, however, instead of being destroyed, became one with the lava and molten metal, and still strides the destroyed halls, blade in hand, in desperate search for its lost master. 

Karrak's Weaponry
     Several centuries ago, when Xantril was still called the Roughlands, the Guild of Power was the place where fighters and weapon masters from all over Layonara came to practice and hone their skills to perfection.
     Once every decade, the Guild's founder, Karrak, and his successors would host the Guild Championships, one for every type of melee weapon. The Championships would go on for weeks, but in the end, there would be a winner for every type of melee weapon. These skilled fighters would then be anointed Master of the weapon in question.
     This was not just a ceremonial title, as the new Masters would also receive the Master's Weapon. These weapons were specially commissioned by Karrak when he founded his Guild, and a Master would bear the weapon for a decade. These weapons were not just ceremonial, but things of beauty and power. A Master's weapon could be recognized by the Guild of Power's emblem somewhere on the weapon's striking surface.
     Unfortunately, the Guild has been destroyed and Karrak's weaponry has been scattered across the continents, the owners probably not even aware of the history and the power of the weapons they possess. 

Rainstorff
     Rainstorff was a special kind of dwarf, and the greatest dwarven fighter ever to walk on Layonara. During his life he did a great many deeds: he built, or helped to build, a great dwarven fortress in the Berhagen Mountains, but found that he could not yet settle down there and took up adventuring again, at which point another dwarf, Ullgrid, took over the construction and rule of the fortress. Rainstorff set out again to continue his adventures in the Roughlands, building quite a reputation there, aiding all those who needed aid. While traveling the Roughlands, Rainstorff and his party came upon a mysterious poem about Fields of Bone, which drew them to Rilara right around the time that Milara appeared there. 
     When on Rilara, Rainstorff was called to aid the dwarves of Bloody Gate in their fight against the invader. He then disappeared for almost a year, and rumor has it he was captured by Milara. However, when questioned, he refused to discuss his absence.
     He returned to the Roughlands, and when he thought he was ready to settle down after his many years of adventuring, he was elected King of the Roughlands. 
     He was a strong ruler, defending his lands together with his Guards, the Red Axe Warriors, who had named themselves after Rainstorff's Red Axe. When they charged into battle they cried "Battle is Honor," and to honor them in return, Rainstorff had these words engraved on the blade of his Red Axe.
     He was loved and worshipped by his subjects, and he established good diplomatic relationships with nearly all races.
     However, not all agreed with his rule. He was sought out by Fisterion the Red, a mighty dragon who was raiding the Roughlands at the time. Dwarf and dragon battled for nearly a day, and the ground trembled as they fought. As both neared exhaustion with neither having a clear advantage over the other one in battle, they came to respect each other's strength, and so Fisterion and Rainstorff came to an arrangement. 
     Fisterion had to quit raiding the countryside and was never to return to the Roughlands, but he could keep his lair. In return the dragon would not be killed today, nor hunted down for a three month period. If Fisterion refused to cease his raids, Rainstorff and his Red Axe Warriors would hunt him down and kill him. Fisterion moved his lair to Firesteep, but since that day harbors a hatred of all dwarves, especially Rainstorff.
     Rainstorff then performed the largest and most important deed in his life. His god, Vorax, was imprisoned in the Plane of Hate and Loss, but Rainstorff, with the aid of his companions, managed to save his god. And now, according to popular dwarven tavern songs, Rainstorff never died, but was made immortal by Vorax.

Through the Looking Glass
     I wonder what Alice might have said if she had picked up this looking glass? I may ask the very same about any of you, for looking into its depths for too long, you are sure to see something you would not expect. 
     It is said that this mythical item was created by a demon bound to Layonara, cursed to remain there as a slave to his master. Through the ages, however, master and slave grew closer, eventually becoming as close to friends as a demon and elf can become. Legends would have us believe the master created a mirror, imbued with the power to see through the planes, allowing his slave to view his home whenever he chose to. 
     Upon the death of the master, the slave was returned to his home plane, taking the mirror with him. Curiously, rumors say that the mirror's effect was reversed in this moment, allowing the holder to view Layonara at any time they chose. 
     If true, this artifact could prove incredibly dangerous in the wrong hands.

The Blood Wells
     Of the many great evils Sinthar Bloodstone brought to Layonara, Blood Wells are one of the more mysterious. These gaping energy portals create an aura of negative energy around them, causing irreparable harm to those close by. It is said a soul lost near a Blood Well is lost forever.
     Although the actual function of the Blood Wells are a mystery, it is a popular theory that they may have been used to increase Bloodstone's power either on Layonara or on the plane he was banished to. How they were created is yet another mystery. The exact number of Blood Wells across Layonara is unknown, and it is unlikely that all of them remain active. 
     Blood Wells should not be confused with the portals Sinthar used to re-enter Layonara, which, although damaging, hold nowhere near the destructive force of the failed portals around the Forsaken Isles. It is claimed any mortal to pass near the Forsaken Isles will be instantly twisted in to an undead monster. It is thought that a hole was torn in the negative plane when Blood's portals failed and collapsed. A disaster indeed, but possibly fortunate as well, for had they not failed, Sinthar would most likely rule Layonara by now. 
     "In every dark action, there is good. Look hard enough, and it is always there."

Stones of Traveling
     According to legend, there are four powerful Stones of Traveling in the world. Each stone has three buttons and the number of that stone on it. If a button is pushed and then one walks through the stone, they will end up at the stone of the same number as the button that was pushed.

The Loaded Deck
     Cards: a game for gentlemen and rogues, where each endsup cheating as often as the other. Loaded decks are not an uncommon thing, tricks like marking cards, weighting cards to disrupt a shuffle, and so on are relatively commonplace. There is one deck, however, which is said to be loaded with more than "luck." 
     The story goes that a fallen noble, giving up his business and title, fell into a lifestyle of gambling. After several fights concerning cheating in a local tavern, the noble decided to protect himself against these brawls. 
      He approached a local gnomish weapon smith, known for his bouts of insanity when it came to the creation of weapons. The gnome was so impressed with the noble's idea that although the noble offered all his winnings from previous nights, the gnome took on the project for free. His only request was that his name should be stamped on his creation.
     A few short weeks passed, and the noble returned to the gnome with his luck on the up. There on the table lay a stunning deck of cards. Made of silver, the cards were wafer thin, beautifully crafted to resemble a normal deck to the unexpecting eye. The final trick, however, came when the cards were contorted a certain way, the corners folding out to form a shuriken stamped with the name of the gnome. 
     Happy with his new deck, the young man returned to the tavern for another evening of poker. With all weapons left at the door, the poker game began. The evening progressed and it became apparent that one member of the group's luck seemed to be far greater than  the others'. The noble suggested a change of deck, trying to avoid the imminent brawl. Things rapidly went from bad to worse as the lucky man rose from his chair, and a good five feet of the floor, for that matter. 
     His glowing hands struck at two of the men as they fled in fear, burning great frozen marks into their backs. A third stood and swung his chair at the mage, only to be frozen in mid swing. The noble panicked, quickly flicking out one of his new cards. With a lucky shot, the first luck he had seen all night as it was, he planted the shuriken between the eyes of the mage. Gathering his winnings, he fled the town. 
     Upon daybreak the four were found slain, three by cold burns, one with a silver star in his forehead. The only clue found was a name, stamped on the rear of the star. The gnome was quickly found and executed. 
     The cards, however, seem to show up across Mistone from time to time, identifiable only by the name Jan Tong embossed on the back.

Pealing Doom
     This item has been claimed to originate on another plane of existence, for it is said no mortal could ever create such a terrible item. The item in question is a brass bell, simple in its appearance, yet terrifying in use. Forged in two parts, the bell handle creates a circle of silence that surrounds those who hold the bell. The bell base, however, creates the most terrible noise when used; prolonged exposure to this noise is said to paralyze and kill, yielding an effect similar to a banshee's wail.
     The only known appearance of this item on Layonara was in what is now Haven, almost two hundred years ago. It is said that the bell was found by a bard down on his luck, having sold his lute to feed himself. 
     Considering his luck for only a second, he ran towards the bustling marketplace, aiming to put on a show for the busy shoppers and merchants. He arrived in the market, found himself a good vantage point, and began to toll his bell. Confused by the lack of sound, he shook the bell more and more violently. Despondent, he stopped shaking the bell, only to look up to see the devastation he had caused. Not a single soul in the market was left alive; almost a hundred people, from rich merchants to the lowest peasant, lay dead, bleeding from their ears. 
     It is said the bard dropped the bell in shock, sounding its terrible noise once more... 
     This is the last known record of the bell, resigned to paper by an unknown source and left at the scene of the disaster. It is unknown whether the bell was taken by the authorities who discovered the scene, or by the "person" who wrote the record.

The Stop Clock
     Buried in myth and legend, it is doubtful that this artifact ever existed at all. If it had, the bearer would almost inevitably be in control of the world by now. 
     It is said the Stop Clock resembles no more than a simple bronze sundial, albeit mounted on the tooth of a chromatic dragon. The owner of the Stop Clock is said to possess the power to control time itself. 
     Fairytale has it that when the humanoid gods took their interest in Layonara, they created the item in order to establish their station on the world without the interference of the dragons. Once the tooth is stabbed into the soil, time stops, awaiting the commands of its new master. Using a simple light, the dial may be turned back, along with time. 
     More myth than legend, the Stop Clock is confined mostly to children's stories rather than campfires. Few adventurers take the story seriously.
     In the same end, a wiser man than I told me fairy tales do not tell children dragons exist, for children already know dragons exist. Fairy tales tell them dragons can be killed. 
Stop Clock or no, your time is yours to control. Make the best of it while you can. 

Lich Skin
     The process of becoming a lich is never a particularly pleasant one, certainly not something you would care to be reminded of, I imagine. One lich, however, a female by the name of Farile Whipwind, decided to keep a memorabilia.
     Farile, ever the vain mage (aren't they all?), refused to live out eternity in the skeletal form she was forced to take. Instead she took the skin from her body as she was transformed into a lich and had it formed into a robe. The robe would fit over her whole body, disguising -  albeit badly - her bony form. 
     The robe had hair sewn into it, even eye lashes and brows. In dark light or through poor vision, one could almost consider her human. 
     As the years progressed, Farile spent most of her time enchanting the robe to improve her looks. Upon completion, whoever was to don the robe would be perceived as the true visage of feminine beauty.
     An untimely end was to greet the lich after an adventuring party raided her tower. Most unfortunate it was that the majority of the party turned out to be female. 
     Little has been heard of the artifact since, although one appearance was noted in the shape of a siren, said to haunt the Broken Forest. This is the last known sighting of the Lich Skin.
Layonara's Most Notable Legends and Artifacts, by Gilles Deleuze

The Mistone Alliance

     The Mistone Alliance came into existence around the time Katia, the Goddess of Nature, was rumored to be imprisoned, around the year of 1357.

     The Mistone Alliance was founded by Queen Allurial of Mistone to serve as her executive body. The organization's purpose was to ensure the welfare of the people of Mistone. The Alliance is headed by the Triumvirates, which consist of three members that each share an equal vote on major issues. The Alliance is composed of five ministries: Ministry of War, Ministry of Intelligence, Ministry of Commonwealth, Ministry of Magic, and Ministry of Justice. The ministries work together to achieve their goals. 

     Although the Alliance receives direct funding from the Queen, there are shortage of resources in the Alliance due to the war with Blood; therefore, the Alliance often seeks the aid of adventuers of Mistone to ensure that the continent is protected from any threats, domestic or foreign.

Monastic Orders
     Monastic Orders come in many varieties. Some focus on peace, others on battle. Some focus on knowledge, others on discipline. Many Orders exist, and some of the more well-known can be found below.

The Sisters of Rebirth
     Monks from this Order follow Aeridin. The majority of monks are elves, but members of other races are not uncommon. This Sisterhood was founded in ancient times and devotes itself to the preservation and nurturing of life. They follow Aeridin's dogma to the core; everything has its place in the great cycle that is the universe: from the Sun and the Moons in the sky to the tiniest insect in the ground, all are important. They accept that death is part of life, but firmly believe that since Aeridin is everywhere, everything will always be reborn. Since Aeridin is everywhere, they do not see the need to pray, as Aeridin is also present in themselves. Instead of prayer, they meditate, train, and live in the forest to draw Aeridin's strength from within their own beings.
      Most Sisters are elves from Voltrex, but the Sisterhood is represented on all continents. They will never turn down requests for aid and will always come to life's defense wielding their wooden staves. 

The Adamantine Brotherhood
     The Adamantine Brotherhood seek to be more like their god Sulterio, the Adamantine One, and have taken to literally mimicking his title in the very fiber of their being. They have hardened body and mind in pursuit of the essence of their namesake metal. Some have compared them to the Voraxite Brothers of Battle, but the Brotherhood is much more numerous. They have fewer scruples and will not refrain from using poisons to help them in their dark endeavors. The Adamantine Brotherhood rarely surfaces, instead seeking to advance their physical and mental fortitude by delving even deeper into the earth and uncovering and claiming even more riches for the glory of the Brooding One. It is rumored that the greatest of the Brotherhood can actually reach into the core beneath the Underdark and extract molten adamantium from the very heart of Layonara.

The Brothers of Battle
     Followers of Vorax, the Brothers of Battle is, not surprisingly, one of the most militant orders on Layonara. It was founded by Thergrim Stonefist approximately 1500 years ago, when he fell down a crevice when traveling through the Berhagen Mountains. Bereft of his axe, which he lost in the fall, Thergrim found himself stuck in the rocks with no way to free himself.
     Fighting the cold with every breath, refusing to let it weaken him, Thergim suddenly received a vision of fists smashing the rocks that trapped him. Using his own fists, he relentlessly punched and clawed at the rocks until he was free.
     Now convinced that he needed nothing but his fists to serve the Father of Battle, he founded the Brothers of Battle, taking Stonefist as his new surname. In memory of  Thergrim's miraculous deed, the head of the Brothers of Battle is still called "The Stonefist." Members of the Brotherhood can be found throughout Layonara, but they gravitate to areas of conflict. 

The Bearers of Knowledge
     The Bearers of Knowledge are a well-known Order. Followers of Aragen, they dedicate their lives to Knowledge. Prohibited from using violence except in the defense of knowledge, self, or others, they wander the world in search of wisdom, be it forgotten or new. They serve an important role in the Aragenite Church as they are mostly responsible for the sharing of knowledge between the temples. 
     Bearers of Knowledge are among the most intelligent and perceptive monks around. They often give lectureson subjects ranging from history to engineering to philosophy to literature. They usually travel in pairs, as two see, hear, and remember more than one.
     The head of the Order is called the Loremaster and resides at the Keep of the Tome, deep within one of Layonara's mountain ranges.
Notes on the Monastic Orders of Layonara, by Annete Blaugrund

T'oleflor
    The T'oleflor are an ancient sprite type race that are extremely close to nature; in fact, some say they ARE nature. The T'oleflor train the best elves, centaurs, and sometimes humans to become elite rangers and druids, the ultimate protectors of nature. They are lead by their Queen and their sole purpose is to support and create nature. They are very rarely seen and only live in one section of the world; it is rumored that they are very nearly extinct. 

Personality: 
    They are a beautiful race and as "uppity" as High Elves. They know that nobody in the world has their capabilities towards nature or intelligence. Violence and anger are frowned upon, and T'oleflor are taught to always be in control of their emotions and actions. From the time they are born until the time they die, they dedicate their lives to nature and T'oleflor's Nature Dance, a martial art system employed by their rangers. T'oleflor live in perfect harmony with nature, and never intentionally harm a living creature except in self-defense. 
T'oleflor are strict vegetarians, as they consider the eating of meat a disgusting habit (although not actually evil). 

Physical Description: 
    T'oleflor are sleek and slender. They never weigh more than 60 pounds and are usually around 45 pounds. They stand about 24" on average. Although slender and small, they are still quite strong and agile.

    T'oleflor skin tone is usually light to dark green. Their hair is often black, sometimes silver or white, and always well kept. They usually have silver, green, or blue eyes. They move with a fluid grace that is distinctly beautiful, like slow dancing. T'oleflor feel awkward in heavy clothing and armor, and thus only wear such things in extreme circumstances. They prefer the lightest garments, and never wear armor or clothing made from the hides of animals. 

Relations: 
    They very distrustful of nearly all races on Layonara. They despise the races that are constantly bringing war and destruction to the world. They hold grudges for centuries at a time when a certain race defaces a part of nature. 

Alignment: 
    T'oleflor are always Neutral in alignment but strongly nature-minded. Some may lean towards good alignment but very rarely is one evil. 

T'oleflor Lands: 
    Little is known where this race now lives, if they even survive to this date. They were last known to exist in the Vale of the Wilds on the continent of Mistone but that was at least one hundred years ago. 

Religion:  
    The T'oleflor worship Katia in everything they do. Other races whisper that they may be direct descendants of Katia, but that cannot be verified. 

Language: 
    T'oleflor speak the language of Florane. This language is gentle and soft-spoken, but extremely lyrical and pronounced with a complex cadence. When spoken in the rich, melodic tones of the T'oleflor, it is among the most beautiful music that can be heard on Layonara. 

Names: 
    T'oleflor feel very strong family ties, and those who encounter a long-lost member of her family will welcome the stranger as a dear friend.

Male Names:

A few candidates:

Allurial
     Allurial is the Queen of Mistone and one of the Seven Sisters, well-liked by the majority of her subjects. She is known to be fair and even-handed. She's rumored to be the Chosen of Lucinda herself.

Drezneb
     Drezneb used to be one of the strongest forces of good on Layonara; however, he fell victim to the influence of one of the first Bloodwells ever found. Tunred into an undead, he is now one of the most evil and foul creatures to ever walk on Layonara and also a general of Blood.

Eon
     One-time ruler of of the northern part of Xantril, which was then still called the Roughlands, Eon is thought to also have fallen to the influence of one of the first Bloodwells ever discovered. Like Drezneb, he has turned into an undead and became a general of Blood.

Highstar Belinmeric
     Leader of the Warriors of the Star, Highstar Belinmeric is one of Allurial's most trusted servants.

Karem of Waylend
     Karem of Waylend is the King of Pranzis. Technically, this also means he is Emperor of Layonara, but he does not use that title, as the last one who did was brutally murdered.
     His rule on the continent of Dregar is absolute, but his grip on the other continents and islands of Layonara is tenuous at best. He commands one of the largest armies on Layonara, counting over 100,000 men. However, because of the large losses he had when Blood returned, most of these are, at the moment, just trainees.

Milara
     Nobody is sure just exactly what Milara's agenda is. According to legend, he served the King of Pranzis several centuries ago, and then left to walk the planes. It is also said that he was pulled into another world and did not return to Layonara for a century. Upon his return, he had turned to evil and is now a general of Blood, although many think he has plans of his own. 

Misty
     One of Seven Sisters, Misty is the odd one in the family. She does not adventure much and prefers to stay at home. She is undyingingly loyal to her sisters, though, and will come at their call.

Moraken
     Probably the most powerful mage on Layonara, Moraken is rumored to once have traveled the planes in order to battle Xandrial. Of course, he is still alive, but so is Xandrial, so no one is sure about the truth of this rumor. Moraken, in any case, refuses to talk about this subject. Little else is known about him, except that he is one of Allurial's greatest allies and that he is continuously seeking ways to defeat Blood and Xandrial.

Selian
     Selian is rumored to be the oldest of Seven Sisters, but she is also known to be the most chaotic of them. She is feared by many, loathed by many more, and loved by few. She will go to any length to make sure things are "right" in her eyes. Her stance shows that she has great power and deserves great respect.

The Sielwood Witch
     The Sielwood Witch can see people's lives in the waters, both what is past and what will be. She can only see the future as different forks in the waters are uncovered. She is known to have warned scholars and rulers of impending danger when the pebbles tossed became rocks that caused the waters to sweep over the banks. She is one of Seven Sisters, at least one of whom is believed to be the Chosen of Lucinda.

Sinthar Bloodstone
     Ages ago, Sinthar Bloodstone was a brilliant human general that led his armies to victory against the dragons. He was banished from Layonara for war crimes, but vowed to return and have his vengeance on the dragons as well as on the people of Layonara. It took him centuries to return, but when he did, he brought vast armies with him. Blood, as he is also known, is well underway to bringing all of Layonara under his rule. However, rumor also has it that some of his generals have their own agenda, which may create problems for him in the future.

The Shifter
     The Shifter is a creature that inhabits the Tower of Darkness near Krandor. He is rumored to have recently been shifted through time and space without the strength of his Tower to protect him, which has left him a shade of his former self. Who he is, or where he comes from, is subject to a lot of speculation.

The Striker of Fear
     Not many know her real name and she has never been known to share it willingly. There is something about her, perhaps her overwhelming confidence in her abilities, that warns that she should not be crossed. Rumor has it that she is one of Seven Sisters.

Xandrial
     It is not known how Xandrial arrived on Layonara, whether he was summoned by Drow, arrived together with Blood, or found his own way here. However, as the inhabitants of Xantril can attest to, he is here. Rumor has it that he came to collect souls and that even facing him forfeits yours. Xandrial is one of Blood's generals.

*This appears to be Abiorn's journal.  While perusing it would be likely quite rude, you do note a great deal of chapters pertaining to several central points of dicussion.  One, his dead wife Aesa.  His writings seem to come back to her in almost every ethical discussion, as though she embodies his conscience.  Two, his family.  You are able to note the names of his siblings, Ardelis, Akithn, and Atrsil.  His parents were apparently Jovn and Kestian.  His writings on his family seem to have diminished in intensity as of later entries... and his somewhat crazed and melancholy sentiments seem to have vanished.  Third, he seems to speak of his education in later life, under the strangely short lived guidance of a monk near the Monastery of Dreams.  He does not detail the exact words exchanged, nor the duration of his invitation to speak with this monk... though it seems a great peace overcame him following these interactions.  Abiorn's writings seem to almost diefy the wisdom of this stranger by the lake, and it is quite clear an epiphany of self-awareness followed.  The journal as a whole takes a wondrous turn from crazed to clarity at this apparent turning point in his life.  He writes of his studies to maintain control over himself, through things as simply as his self-titled 'lazy tongue' of an accent, to things as complex as understanding the nature of the tragedy that befell his mind following Aesa's death.  A sense of duty pervades the writings following these chapters, as though much reason was given for a purpose in existance.  The discussion of those magics that ultimately destroyed his peaceful existance with Aesa take a turn towards tumultuous internal debate as the journal works forward.  The discussion of necromancy as a tool of oppression that must be sought out and destroyed seems obvious, distinct, and absolute in early writings.  Then the topic of the dark-skinned gnome Casrushier enters into his writings.  There seems to be a turning point in his emotions and absolute judgement on these matters as this gnome enters his life.  The complexity of his arguments seem strained under the pressure of some manner of internal debate, though it would take much reading of this journal to fully begin to understand these emotions.  The last topic that seems to fill the most recent chapters of his journal revolve around the Black Mages, their offer, and his subsequent battles with them.  The journal seems to be open from this point forward, with much speculation and paranoia apparent in his tone as he speaks of his overwhelming enemy.

An iron statue of a rider on horseback stands upon a stone pedestal. Emblazoned on the rider's shield is a crimson eagle, wings spread. Upon the pedestal, there is a plaque which reads as follows:

"Long ago the great city of gold, Port Hempstead, was under siege by the dark elves. In the center of the great city an eruption of cobbles occurred, and from it burst forth a horde of the Deep. Deep dwarves swarmed forth followed by the dark elves; the guards ran to the city's aid but were overcome. In the skies, death on black wings soared overhead. Chromatic dragons laid waste to the city's defenders as the sacking of Hempstead began. But not all was yet lost, for as the dark elves turned the city into a base of operations, a call throughout Mistone was heard.

So it came to pass that the forces of good gathered, and after weeks of planning, the retaliation against the denizens of the Deep and those that came to their service began. From the south, the Ulgrids sent forth an army of dwarves to challenge the hordes of ogres beginning to fortify the city. From the north came the druids of the Silkwood, who challenged the goblin clans massed at the call of war. Finally, from the lands of man and the King of Mistone, came the Crimson Eagles, the greatest knights of their time despite numbering only forty five.

Upon the crest of dawn the forces of Mistone attacked the invaders, determined to reclaim what was theirs, and within the burning city of Hempstead all would be decided. The gates burst open and a horn did sound; the dark elves rallied in the square, determined to end the threat to their conquest quickly. Yet they did not expect knights such as the Crimson Eagles who swarmed through the gaps in the walls instead of the crushed gates. Lances lowered, they charged into the throng of dark elves. The Captain of the Eagles spied the leader of the dark elves, a mage of considerable power, turning to unleash a demon from the depths of the Pits.

Armor torn by poisoned arrows, he charged onwards. Horse and rider crashed through the throng of foes seeking but one target, allies at either side. The dark mage spoke the last word of the incantation and from the depths of the Pits roared a general of fires, a balor. With great sweeping blows of its sword it cut down man, dark elf, and horse on all sides. Laughing at the failed attempt upon his life, the mage ordered the demon to destroy those coming in the gate, leaving his back turned to the wounded captain of the Crimson Eagles. Drawing his sword from scabbard he thrust it through the mage's back, impaling his black heart. With blood flowing forth from his mouth, the mage wailed in death and defeat. The demon grabbed his body, dragging it back down unto the Strife as it was banished.

To the northern wall of the city a battle was being fought as well, the dragon ally a great blue with a host of goblinoid minions waged war with the druids and rangers of Silkwood. Lightning and nature's fury swarmed forth. Hosts of small vermin from the wargs slew their riders, and then the foul mockeries of the wolves themselves. At last, it was merely the high druid of Silkwood and the dragon. As all others fell back, the dragon circled, seeking advantage as the druid merely watched the skies, waiting. And so it began to rain, water trickling down the faces of the quietly smiling druids as the goblinoids shrieked and melted in the vengeance of druids long angered at the abominations burning their woods. The dragon shrieked in pain as it too felt the sting of the spell, lightning crackling across its scales. Whirling, it sought to flee the pain, however its wings had been damaged from the battle, and the spell sent it plummeting into a merciless sea, where it was pulled under by the denizens of the deep.

Alas, the deep dwarves saw their dwarven kin, and in determination that they not share the same fate as the fool dark elves and weak goblins entered the fray, and blood spilled that day like none before. Thus two races locked in eternal hate waged war so furious that all fell aside to watch in horror, as axe against axe and adamantium upon dwarven steel clashed. The general superior of the dwarves beseeched Vorax for aid against the deep dwarves and was shown the Battlefather's axe; he charged unto the fray. So the deep dwarves, disgraced, turned back and fled with the remaining dark elves into the depths of the Deep from which they had emerged. A great rumbling occurred then, as passageways began to collapse underneath the ruined city, leaving those that fled in an eternal tomb.

So of those called to defend Mistone, the Crimson Eagles remained the most prominent, quelling several rebellions against the King. They themselves helped rebuild the city once more into its glory. Thus, it is here we honor those that died fighting the forces of evil, and those that survived to bring this city once more into its proper glory."

Notice of Entry to Port Hempstead

The laws of Port Hempstead forbid entry into the city of any evil humanoid races. This includes, but is not limited to:

- Dark Elves
- Goblinoids
- Orcs & Half-Orcs
- Giants & Half-Giants
- Lizardmen
- Kobolds

Any of the above who are caught in the city will be escorted out by the guard upon first offense. 

Second offense will result in instant punishment of death. 

The exception to this is Dark Elves for whom there is no first offense and are subject to instant extermination.

By Order of the Council of Port Hempstead

This is a statue of the halfling deity Deliar, also known as The Lucky Wanderer, The Merchant of Fate, The Wind of Destiny whose dogma is: 

Deliar teaches that in order to lead a fulfilling life, one must constantly strive to discover new ways to trade with the world. His objectives and priorities deal with a harmonious existence in which everything is spread throughout all the communities that touch any goods or services that can be bartered with. The Lucky Wanderer promotes wealth, yes, but such wealth should not be enjoyed at the expense of others, and particularly not at the expense of the community as a whole; thus he welcomes success in monetary gains as long as other needs have been satisfied.

All followers of The Merchant are encouraged to spread and explore the world, carrying their families with them if necessary, because the only way to truly appreciate existence as a whole is by exploring all its possibilities and letting others know of the treasures from distant lands. These treasures aren't just in gold, but in all the uniqueness that a culture can offer, particularly in the things that they create to identify themselves--that way, there is a little bit of everyone all over Layonara.

To hone your skills as a tradesman is to worship Deliar at what he does best - which is to understand the true value of an item and make everyone gain from it, even though perhaps the person they are exchanging with may not at first see the bigger picture. In the end, as long as no one is harmed by the trade, their role has been fulfilled. The best kind of exchange is the kind where each side walks away feeling like they came out on top.

Finally, all those who follow the path of the Lucky Wanderer understand that little in life is predictable, that the roads in life have only the certainty of uncertainty within them, and that every turn may throw at them a good or bad experience. The concept of Luck and Fate, whether 'good' or 'bad' is embraced by all Deliarites fully, as they know that the fruits of today may not be as bountiful as those of tomorrow and life does particularly well in bringing surprise to everyone. Because of this, many worshipers of Deliar are extremely superstitious and have many quirky rituals and talismans that must be performed or carried before embarking on a particular journey or going on about their daily routines.

Talan discovered some blueprints of various places before stumbling upon one of the Demon Fortress, which seemed rather odd, so nothing jumped out at us initially until Lalaith looked at it with True Sight.  What was revealed was a hidden passage marked in the back of the fortress.  We thought about the discovery a bit and came to the conclusion that it might be best to go investigate it but taking even an army there might not be the best course.

So after speaking with Jennara and Connor too, it was soon decided that Lalaith and I would go in stealth, myself on the ethereal plane and while Lalaith knew she could hide in the shadows for some of the way, she also recalled the Lumbral had to help them pass beyond the true sight of the enemies the time we sought to return Xandrial.  we decided it would be necessary that I would have to craft some Greater Sanctuary scrolls for Lalaith to use at various points and so it was done and thus we travelled to Xantril.

We made our way to the Fort of Last Hope, then beyond into the Demon Mountains before coming upon the bridge to the Demon Tower, Lalaith was spotted and she soon joined me on the ethereal plane for us to travel the rest of the way to the Fortress.  The fortress was lined with demons from cliff face to mountain.  It was like wading through a wheat field of fiery fury, even being on the other plane, the nerves were high and our hearts were thumping.  It would have taken an army of great repute to have fought our way through.

We discovered a passage in the back and with a little ingenuity and strength we were able to open a rusted grate into a tunnel which led us inside the Demon Fortress.  Even the knowledge of being on another plane didn't ease  some of the fears as we slipped inside and around massive demons and followed the blueprints around, searching the floor.  And then we saw it...

There hovering in a shaft of unlight being absorbed by the ruby at the top was the staff we saw in the book.  It radiated a torrential evil and was guarded by warding traps all around and a Balor High Prince standing near.  We stood there unsure of a course of action, do we return and let everyone know? Would it have even been possible to bring everyone here?  Do we even attempt to disarm the traps? What of the Balor? 

We wavered on a decision while the precious time of our spells dwindled, at one point Lalaith disappeared on me, back to the prime, only to return momentarily with the ash of a hellball covering her, a little wide eyed but relieved. Lalaith was pretty confident she could disarm the traps and we finally decided to at least give that an attempt while I preoccupied the demon with some flight and taunting.

I cancelled my sanctuary and fluttered about the demon, calling down a storm of Her powerful nature and keeping his sight from the glowing staff while Lalaith began to work the traps.  Her hands moved rapidly but diligently and then it happened...

A flash of light...Then a sound, much like air blowing through a pipe or hose started coming from the staff.  The light around the staff began to freeze and was no longer entering the ruby.  The sound grew louder and the light trembled. Then it began to shoot out in a dazzling blaze...and then the staff, as though it was set free from some unseen grasp, simply clattered to the ground.. 

By this time the Balor was just as intrigued as us, he ran to guard it and hovered over it.  I yelled for Lalaith to grab it as the demon stood over it for what seemed an eternity.  I swung again wildly at the demon and without even thinking twice, Lalaith scooped up the staff.  We returned to the Ethereal plane.. and we ran.

That was when Lalaith started realizing the demons were actually following us despite being on the other plane.  Through the fortress and outside they were drawn to our location by something, something surely from the staff.  We weighed our options quickly and decided it best to fly off to the Fort of Last Hope.  I gathered all my strength and called for the aid of my best falcon guides and we took to the air...

*She seems to be intently studying a plant which lies limp across both her hands.  She looks up for a moment and acknowledges your presence with slightly dipping shoulders.  Then she returns her focus to the plant and whispers to it as she turns away from you.*

*As you observe Legodia from a distance, she seems engaged in tidying up her camp from the aftermath of what you would guess was an elaborate ritual or procedure.  After placing a herb bundle off to the side she turns gracefully and steps toward you.*  Greetings.  The forest felt your path carrying you here.  What can I do for you?

*she gives a slight yet pleasant smile*  I'm a druid of this forest, it's caretaker.  The High Druid of this forest, Mistone's High Druid as well, is likely abroad serving Nature in his proactive way.  You'd surely learn more from his personal experience and close connection with the Great Oak than from me.

He is called Rhizome.  And he can be found near Katia's Grove in this forest from time to time, or in Aeridin's Grove in the Silkwood.  He also spends some time on the sacred island at Corax Lake.  *she tilts her head*  But he is a wandering sort.  So, you might find him just about anywhere.  *somewhat absentmindedly, she redirects her attention to her herbs and ritual objects.  Then for a moment she remembers your company*  Nature's blessings on your journey.
*Legodia dips her head as she walks from her tent and approaches slowly*  Did you find Rhizome and learn about the wisdom of the Great Oak?
*she nods and puts her hands together in what appears to be a symbolic gesture*  Then let the wisdom of the Great Oak shape your path and strengthen your will to ensure Nature's balance.
*she looks at you with a welcoming smile*  Oh, you've returned.  May the wisdom of the Oak continue to guide your way.

*Legodia bends in a graceful courtesy with a warm smile.  As she rises her hands come together in front of her in a symbolic gesture*  Welcome back Rhizome. *she looks up into the canopy a moment and smiles wider*  Welcome back indeed.
I am hoping to learn more about the Great Oak.  I figured you would know something about it, seeing as how you are the druid of this forest.
*you shake your head and mutter something to yourself about tree-huggers and wander off after a polite departing gesture*

I will follow my path and do what I can.

*Rhizome bows and as he rises returns the symbolic hand gesture*  Always forward Legodia.  *He kneels down slowly, like a weary traveler, and brings up a bit of the forest floor between his thumb and forefinger.  As he rubs it around under his nose he gives a joyful smile*  Connectivity and solidarity in the roots of the world comrade.
