Not my problem, but good luck with that.
Anything I can do to help?
Welcome to my Tower.  If you need spells, please speak with my assistant.  If it's work you're looking for...*examines you closely*...come back when you're not so much of a whelp.

Have you ever heard of Storan? No? That's too bad. Storan is rumored to have had a magical ring on him when he died, a ring that is much more than its semblance. Would you care to retrieve Storan's ring for a nice reward?

Storan is in his crypt, of course. Did you not know he is an undead now? Anyway, his crypt can be found in the mausoleum on the outskirts of Hlint. Bring me the ring that he is rumored to have worn and I will reward you handsomely.
Well? Have you recovered Storan's ring from his animated body?
Splendid! Now I can do some more research.  The ring is rumored to be tied to Blood himself...perhaps now, I can fathom the link. As for your reward, here. You've more than earned it.
Thank you for bringing the ring to me. My experiments are proceeding.
Dead adventurers and old relics don't really interest me.  Goodbye.
Where is Storan at?  What is this ring?
The undead give me the creeps, and undead wearing powerful magical rings sounds like more than I want to get involved in.
Now you tell me...all right, I'll find this ring of yours.
I was trying to put my grandfather's ashes in the Crypt...*sob*...and out of nowhere this skeleton started chasing me.
It was glowing green!  I dropped the ashes and ran for my life...I'm too scared to go back!
I was deep in the crypt when I dropped them.
*she wipes the tears from her face hopefully as you approach* Have you found grandfather's urn yet?
Oh, thank you! May I have it, please?
Thank you so much. Please take this as a token of my thanks.
Thank you for returning grandfather's ashes to me.
Really? What did it look like?
Where exactly did you leave the ashes?
Would you like me to go look for them?
Of course. I'll recover your grandfather's ashes...wait here.
I'm still looking for it, sorry.
Actually, I think I'll keep it.
Hello, stranger. You look like a well-to-do <class>, mayhaps you can retrieve an item for me?

I was traveling from Krandor the other day and it started to rain. I took shelter in a cave in the Silkwood Forest and couldn't see a thing in the dark, so I slept. I awoke to something slimy eating away at my feet. I ran away, leaving my great grandmother's necklace in the cave. It would mean a great deal to me if you could retrieve that necklace.
I just saw this big, shimmering thing in the cave. Find that creature and you will find my necklace.
Have you found my necklace yet?
Ahh, great grandmother's necklace! Here, take this as a token of my gratitude.
Thank you so much for retrieving my necklace.
That I am.  What might I do for you, bard?
Any idea where it might be?
I just remembered I'm afraid of the dark...maybe some other day.

<Boy/Girl>, I am in need of your help.  A denizen of these woods has taken the life of a companion of mine. I have taken it upon myself to destroy these vile creatures. There is one such creature that I wish to see removed from this land. He goes by the name of Zamin.
I have some work but you do not look experienced enough in life at this time. Come back later.
Most excellent.  Bring back the vile little thing's head and I shall reward you.
Have you killed that blasted creature yet?
Thank you. I can now safely travel and sell my goods in Fort Llast. Please take this cloak as a reward.
You have avenged my companion, thank you.
Yes, and here is the proof.
My <Lord/Lady>, I have a proposal for you.
Uhh ... let me just make this very simple. Go find the Red Goblin Cave. Bring me back the head of the leader and I will give you gold. Yes?
Er... right. Just remember tol bring me back the head as proof and I'll give you some gold. Understand? SHINY..!
Er... alright, well bring me back what I need and I'll give you some gold. Understand? SHINY..!
Thank you. The trading route will be safer for a while. Oh, here is your reward. See? Shinies, just like I promised!
Oh, you again. Thank you for bringing me the head. It is good to know that the trade route is safer now, and travelers can continue to make a living on it.

On the roads north of the Silkwood, between Fort Llast and the township of Hlint, there is a trading road that leads into the Goblin Wastelands. These goblins often send scouting parties into the area, and they have plagued the trade wagons along those roads for years.

As you can see from my wagon, I am something of a traveler. I have recently come into a little windfall of True from a deal that Deliar himself must have blessed, and I would like to do something about the trade road. But I know Lieutenant Astork has had bounties on those scouts for years. You have to cut the head off the beast, I say, not the ear!

You look like the competent sort. I'd like to hire you to bring me back the head of the leader of the goblin clan. That should strike a blow and free up the trade route for a while! In return for your services, I will pay you in gold. How does that sound?
Most excellent.  Bring back the creature's head and I will give you a handsome reward.
Ah, you are back. Have you the head of the leader for me?

Ahhh, wonderful. It pleases me, to know the trade route is free again, at least for a little while. Perhaps I'll make a trip up there soon myself ... Oh, but here is the gold I promised you. Thank you for your help.
Oh, you again. My thanks once more for your help. It is good to know that the trade route is safer now, and travelers can continue to make a living on it.

On the roads north of the Silkwood, between Fort Llast and the township of Hlint, there is a trading road that leads into the Goblin Wastelands. These goblins often send scouting parties into the area, and they have plagued the trade wagons along those roads for years ...
Whatever it is, I'm not interested.
No! Hey! What pro-po-sal?! Stoopid big word.
Me no know wut ju talk 'bout.
Yu velcum. Me take shinies now.
I changed my mind. I have to go now.
I have no idea what you're talking about.
Sounds like a waste of my time. Goodbye.
Sounds disgusting and barbaric. No thank you!
Well met, traveler. Name's Rowan. Be warned, this is dangerous territory. You may want to head back to the safety of the fort.
In that case, would you be willing to check it out for me? If you can bring me back proof one way or another, I'll reward you for your troubles.

The Dark Peaks of the Watcher is a fearsome place indeed. Rumor has it that it is full of strange magic and stranger creatures, and not a light anywhere to save you from blundering into them. The less said about it the better. Trust me.

Apart from the wild animals, the greatest danger in the Forest of Moans is the satyrs who live within its boundaries and protect the woods. They came to the forest to heal it after a great hurt was done to the region, but they are very territorial and do not like trespassers. You would do well to leave them alone.
Fort Wayfare lies through the mountain pass to the east just yonder. You would be safer within its walls.
Have you found proof of whether the stories of creatures in the caves are true yet?
Well let me know when you do.
Oh? What was it you were wondering about?
Just doing my part, to warn travelers of the dangers. A lot of people pass through this way, and not all of them know the land too well.
Ahh, so this is what they look like. Thank you for your help. I'll be sure to warn other travelers.
If that's so, perhaps you would care to help me with a little problem?
Well met again, traveler. Enjoy the fire, if you wish. Where are you headed today?
As you wish. Safe travels then.
Well, be sure to enjoy a good ale for me at the inn then. Safe journey.
Well, I'd warn you that there are dangerous creatures down there, but you know all too well, don't you? Be safe then, friend.

Sometimes travelers come through here looking for a pass south through the mountains. There is actually a cave that is said to connect all the way to Windjammers Bay, but few are willing to risk the journey and I usually have to send them back to the fort.
As you wish. Safe travels then, friend.
Well, behind me lies the Forest of Moans and the Dark Peaks of the Watcher. And in these foothills there is a cave that descends deep below the surface. Which danger were you curious about?
The cave is part of a deep system. It is supposed to connect all the way to the coast by Windjammer Bay, but few are willing to risk the journey to find out.
Strange creatures are said to live in the caves, and the way is not safe for most travelers. Those who have made it out have spoken of noises deep within the caves, and horrible beasts with scales.
I would, but I have to stay here at my post to warn other travelers.
I can pay you for your troubles, if that's what you're worried about.
Thanks for the advice, but I can take care of myself.
Why don't you go check it out yourself then?
And make other people do your work for you. I don't think so.
In that case, I'll see what I can do for you. Farewell for now.
Probably a bunch of stories. I don't believe it.
Sounds like someone needs to take care of it.
I will see what I can do for you. Farewell for now.
The Dark Peaks of the Watcher
I'll keep that in mind. Thanks for the advice.
Actually, I had a question for you.
Why you are out here all by yourself
Oh, I see. Okay, farewell then.
Doesn't sound like my kind of problem. Find someone else.
None of them. I changed my mind.
Greetings, adventurer. Welcome to Silkwood Forest.
Hello, <FullName>, it is good to finally meet you. The animals spoke of your coming.  When you feel you are powerful enough I have a very difficult task for you...do you believe in your strength?

Good. I am in need of the eyestalk of a Beholder. The one I am interested in only falls from a Mage Beholder, though, so you must be very powerful to even consider confronting it in its lair. Bring me the eyestalk, however, and I will give you a great reward.
Do you have the Mage Beholder's eyestalk?
I see you were right to believe in your strength. Here is the reward I promised, and good fortune to you, adventurer!

Thank you for your help.  I am using the eyestalk in a spell that will help scry upon whatever dangers may threaten our lands in this time of trouble in the aftermath of Blood's defeat.  Believe in your strength, <FullName>.
Sounds dangerous. I may come back at a later date.
I believe in my strength. Tell me what you need.
I will find this item for you.
Greetings. If you need temple services, please speak to the healer.
Greetings, friends. Welcome to the temple of the Lifegiver. How can I help you?
Blood's general? I am not too familiar with the story...but I believe Athus mentioned it on the letter he wrote to me a few month before.
Yes, Athus Dephillie, a fellow healer of Aeridin.  He is out traveling at the moment, perhaps you can find him on the road.  He has rich brown hair, and a sunshine smile you can't miss.
Greetings again, have you spoken with Athus?
Ah, good.  I hope that information would help you on your journey. Farewell with the touch of the Lifegiver.
Well met, friend. May Aeridin be your guide in the Great Cycle.
Hello Athus! Many people have been asking me about Drezneb.  Hope you've taught them a thing or two.
Perhaps you know something about the Drezneb's powerful ring?
I'll try to seek him out.
Yes, it was a very informational meeting.
Have you come to aid Katia?
Very good. Some poachers have set up shop in the Outskirts. Please find them and bring them the justice of nature: hunt them as they have hunted the animals.
Katia is the goddess that watches over the forest, known to many as Mother Nature.  You have not heard about her?
Have you hunted the hunters? Are the poachers dead?
Katia, her animals, the forest, and I all thank you.
Thank you for helping Katia's animals and removing the threat of the poachers from the forest.
No, I have not, and I'm not interested.  Goodbye.
No, I have not found them yet.
Yes. Here is the leader's head.
Greetings, I am Jasmin of the High Moors Swamp.  I am looking for a few Skeleton Knuckles for a potion of mine.  Are you interested in earning some coin?
Then bring them to me when you find them.
Welcome Back <FirstName>.  Have you found any Skeleton Knuckles?
Well done.  Here is your payment.
Thank you <FirstName> for retrieving the skeleton knuckles for me.
Greetings, I am Jasmin of the High Moors Swamp.  I am looking for a few Skeleton Knuckles for a potion of mine.  Are you interested in Earning Some coin?
Thank you <FirstName>.  For retrieving the skeleton knuckles for me.
No thanks, I do not like the undead.
Yes I have fought many and I have some for you.
No thaks, Me no lic e Dead dings.
Greetings, I am Quartermaster Talon.  I am looking to offset the Hlint Guard positions by recruiting young adventurers like you.  Are you interested?

Well <FirstName>, Goblin Scouts have been searching the area to find weaknesses in our defenses.  We need to kill them so that they cannot report back to the leader.  Bring me back there ears for a reward.
Welcome Back <FirstName>.  Have you found any Goblin Scouts?
Thank you <FirstName>.  On account of you, the city is safe from the Goblin threat.
Greetings friend.  May I help you?
No thanks, I do not want to be a guard.
Sure I have always wanted to help out.  You can sign <FirstName> as a volunteer guard.  What can I do?
Ok Quartermaster, I will look for them.
Yes I have fought many and I have brought back the ears for you.
Well kind of, I have a <CUSTOM56007>.
Greetings! My name is Johan the Fur Trader. I need some help gathering supplies, if you've got the time.
Great! Only four more to go. Bring me a deer pelt this time.
Have you found the deer pelt yet?
Excellent. A cougar's pelt is the first of the final three.
Have you found the cougar pelt yet?
Almost done, adventurer! Now I need the pelt of a brown bear. Be careful, they're vicious.
Have you found the brown bear pelt yet?
The last pelt I need is another brown bear pelt. If you brought one back, a second can't be that hard, right?
Have you found the second brown bear pelt yet?
Terrific! Thank you so much, from me and my wife. Here is a cloak I made with the first bear pelt. I hope it keeps you safe.
Thank you for gathering all of the pelts for me.
My wife is sick and I cannot leave her bedside for very long. I need you to gather some pelts for me, if you would.
First, I need a simple rat pelt.
Have you found the rat pelt yet?
Great! Only seven more to go. Now find me a bat pelt.
Have you found the bat pelt yet?
Six more to go. I now need a badger pelt.
Have you found the badger pelt yet?
Excellent. Five more pelts!  Now, bring me the pelt of a boar.
Have you found the boar pelt yet?
No, I'm already pressed for time.
Three more to go...I'll be back.
Sure. What can I do for you?
Okay, I will find one for you.
Then I will take it. Bring me a Copper Battleaxe next.
Have you found the Copper Battleaxe yet?
Only four more items to go. Next, bring me a Copper Mace.
Have you found the Copper Mace yet?
Splendid. The locker only needs three more weapons, starting with a Copper Scythe.
Have you found the Copper Scythe yet?
You're doing a great job, and you're almost finished. Just two more items, the first of which is a Copper Spear.
Have you found the Copper Spear yet?
We're nearly done. Just bring me an Oak Shortbow, and you can have your reward.
Have you found the Oak Shortbow yet?
Are you the warrior I have heard so much about?
Finally, I feel that we are properly equipped to battle the Gnolls if we are attacked again. Thank you for your help.
Welcome back to Haven, and thanks again for equipping my troops.
My Friend I think you should go adventuring more before we talk again.
A friend of mine, Lieutenant Jursen, said that he gave that helm to a person who helped him restock his equipment locker. The description seems to match you.
I am also trying to gather some weapons. Could you help me?
Great. The first weapon I need is a Light Copper Hammer.
Have you found the Light Copper Hammer yet?
Then I will take it. Thank you. I only need seven more items, starting with a Copper Handaxe.
Have you found the Copper Handaxe yet?
Thank you. I only need six more items now. For now, bring me a Copper Morningstar.
Have you found the Copper Morningstar yet?
You are welcome. I'll be back.
A scythe? Are you training farmers? Fine, I'll be back.
No thanks, I don't have time.
I will find one for you.
You are welcome. I'll be back with the handaxe.
Greetings, my name is Lieutenant Jursen.  I have recently been transferred to Fort Llast from Hlint after enlisting a hero to eliminate the feared Throatripper.
Thank you. A Copper Longsword is next on the list.
Do you have the Copper Longsword I requested?
A fine blade indeed. The shortbow you fetched me doesn't seem to have enough pull; could you acquire a Hickory Long Bow?
Do you have the Hickory Long Bow I requested?
Thanks much, recruit. Just a couple more, starting with a Hickory Heavy Crossbow.
Do you have the Hickory Heavy Crossbow I requested?
Great! Now they need to train with a blunt weapon...can you find a Copper Warhammer to round out the closet?
Do you have the Copper Warhammer I requested?
You've been a great help, and our weapons locker is full. Drop by the training area sometime...it's actually kinda fun to watch the recruits hurt themselves.
Thanks  for helping me fill the closet, <FirstName>
Thank you...though even Lieutenants need help on occasion. Do you have time to run some errands for me?
I need to restock the training closet with eight different weapons. The first item I need is a dagger.
Do you have the Copper Dagger I requested?
Thank you. Now I need a Hickory Light Crossbow.
Do you have the Hickory Light Crossbow I requested?
You'd be amazed how many of my soldiers don't know the proper way to handle a crossbow. Thanks. Could you get me a Copper Shortsword next?
Do you have the Copper Shortsword I requested?
Splendid! Only five more weapons to pick up. I keep telling them, the pointy end goes into the bad guy. Could you get me a Hickory Short Bow next?
Do you have the Hickory Short Bow I requested?
Perhaps. Good day to you, Lieutenant.
No thanks; there's nothing heroic in fetching weapons.
I'll find one and be back soon.
Seven more to go...I'll be back.

Greetings. I am Apprentice Natasha Sommerhof of the Mages of Light. My master is looking for eight spell components.  I, however, am not equipped to go out into Layonara to find them. Perhaps we could make a deal?
Have you found the Fairy Dust?
You are doing well, my friend. Next, I need a sample of herbs...Belladonna should do nicely.
Splendid! Two more to find, starting with a Polished Bone.
Do you have the Polished Bone?
The final component my master needs is the hair from an Owlbear. Do be quick about it.
Do you have the Hair from an Owlbear?
My master will be quite pleased with me. As for you, adventurer, you have my thanks.
My master's spell is coming along nicely, thanks to you.
Bring all eight to me and you will be rewarded. The first item I need is a Skeleton's Knuckle.
Have you found the Skeleton's Knuckle?
Excellent. Only seven more to go. Now...a Fire Beetle's Belly.
Have you found the Fire Beetle's Belly?
This shall do. Next, the silk gland from an Ettercap...
Have you found the Ettercap's Silk Gland?
Five more to go, adventurer, beginning with a Gargoyle Skull.
Have you found the Gargoyle Skull?
This next assignment is a bit...lighter. Bring me some Fairy Dust.
And only three more after that...back soon.
Off to pick some flowers, I guess.
I'll go as fast as I can.
Well done. Here's the gold. Next, I need a vial of poison made from a giant spider.
Do you have the giant spider poison I requested?
I'm impressed. But now I need the poison from an aranea spider. Think you can manage that?
Welcome back. Do you have the aranea poison I need?
Good. A customer has been waiting for this. Now, let's try something with a bit different. Bring me a vial of poison from a phase spider.
I was hoping I would see you soon. I hate replacing suppliers. Do you have that phase spider poison?
Very good. Here is your payment. Now, let's try something with a bit more bite to it. Bring me a vial of poison from a dire spider, and don't dally.
Guess the dire spiders didn't get you. Or do you even have the poison?

I'll take that then. You are proving to be more useful than I thought. I wasn't sure you'd last this long. I only need two more poisons to restock my inventory, but you may find them more of a challenge. Think you can handle getting poison from a queen spider?
Do you have that queen spider poison yet?
That might be arranged. Unfortunately, though, I am a little low on my stock right now. I don't suppose you know a good supplier?
Excellent. Here is your gold. Now just one more ... I have a special order for the poison of a bastard sword spider. And make it quick.
Well? Do you have the last poison for me?
Well don't wait too long. You're expendable, you know.
And you didn't get bitten to death? Did you even make these yourself, or are you just playing middleman with the real supplier? No, no, don't tell me. A deal is a deal. Here is your last payment.
Looking for more work? Sorry, but I need to move this inventory before I take any more deliveries.

Oh, you again. Sorry, friend, but I don't need any wares just now if you're selling. And if you were looking to buy, I do not have anything in that you haven't proven you can get yourself. But thanks for your help sorting out my inventory problem.
Whatever you are looking for, I suggest going elsewhere. I don't have time to waste on the likes of you just now. Come back when you're worth my time.

Well, I am a little low on my stock of wares right now. One of my suppliers got eaten by the spider he was trying to harvest glands from. You could replace him on a temporary basis ... if that kind of thing appeals to you and you can get the goods.

I need to restock my inventory with a selection of different poisons. I'll compensate you well for every vial you deliver. Let us start with something simple: bring me a vial of poison made from a small spider.
Not too bright, are you? I thought you knew what we were talking about. Well, nevermind then.
Something tells me we serve different gods and masters. And mine will judge me just fine, thanks.
This is Arnax, friend. Go ahead.
Do you have the small spider poison I requested?
Good. Here is your payment. Next, I need a vial of poison made from an ettercap.
Excellent, you're back. Do you have the ettercap poison I requested?
The gods will judge you for your actions!
I should report you to the authorities!
It's a deal. I'll acquire one and be back soon.
An ettercap? Alright. I'll deliver it back here once I have it.
Apologies. I thought you were someone else.
A bastard sword spider? Sounds nasty. See you soon.
Yes. I want to buy an ... exotic "potion" ... if you get my drift. Something nice and deadly.
Thank you. Any other supplies you need?
Ah, I see. Well goodbye then.
That's why I came here! Nevermind. I'll find someone else.
I could help you out with that.
Perhaps. I might be looking for some work.
This sounds shady, and definitely not what I had in mind for work. Find someone else! I'm leaving.
What would you want me to do?
On second thought, I think I will look elsewhere for what I need. Good luck with that, though.
Wait, wait ... you want me to supply you with poisons?! That's despicable!

This set of robes looks like a normal set of greater mage armor. 
Yet, it also seems different. It seems soaked with the tremendous amounts of negative energy it has been exposed to, energies that have twisted it into something else.
This looks like your old set of robes.
Well hello there. Something I can do for you?
Certainly. I see patients and sell healing supplies, which I make mostly from local herbs here at home. Just like the herbs you gathered for me. Which reminds me, how did the potion work out for you?
Well feel free to come back and buy some more whenever you run out. Is there anything else I can do for you?
I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to see my other potions?
Certainly. I see patients and sell healing supplies, which I make mostly from local herbs here at home. Did you know that nature can supply a remedy for almost any ailment you can suffer?
Certainly! But you'll have to buy them this time. Still interested?

Of course. Let's see here ... hmm ... well, the bad news is that there is nothing I can do for you, friend. But the good news is that it is only because I can find nothing at all the matter with you! I detect neither physical wounds nor any afflictions.
As you wish <sir/madam>, but this will cost you <CUSTOM141> gp. Are you sure?
Well is there anything else I can do for you?
That is everything I could do for you. Is there anything else you wish?
Certainly. Oh ... hmm, you indeed seem to be in need of some healing, dear. This is what I can do for you ...
Why yes I do! Welcome to <CUSTOM51500>. I sell healing and natural supplies. Would you like to see my wares?
It's true! Why don't I prove it to you? Help me gather some herbs, and I will give you one of my favorite healing potions as thanks and proof.
Well I don't really need an apprentice right now ... but if you really wanted to help you could gather some herbs for me. In return, I'll give you one of my favorite potions to study.
Let me know if you change your mind. Anything else I can do for you?
Why yes I do!  Welcome to <CUSTOM51500>. I sell healing and natural supplies. Would you like to see my wares?
Wonderful! The first herb I need is a clove of garlic. Please bring it back when you have it.
Thank you. Is there anything else you need before you leave?

My name is Elora. I'm a healer, and this is my house. Oh, but don't worry, you're welcome here! It's also my shop and my infirmary. I sell healing and natural supplies, and take the occasional patient. Now, was there something I can do for you?
Oh good, you're back. I was hoping you would be. Do you have that clove of garlic for me yet?
Well please get it soon. I need these herbs for my potions. Is there anything I can do for you in the meantime?
Thank you! This is exactly what I needed for my healing potion. Next, I need a fresh aloe leaf. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
There's a familiar face. I was hoping you'd stop by soon. Do you have that aloe leaf for me yet?
Thank you! Aloe juice is sticky, but it is so good for soothing burns. Next, I need a strip of birch bark. Please bring it back to me when you have it.

Certainly. I see patients and sell healing supplies, which I make mostly from local herbs here at home. Just like the herbs you are gathering for me. Speaking of which, please bring me the rest of the herbs soon ... unless there was something else you needed from me first?
Welcome back! Do you have that piece of birch bark for me yet?
Thank you! This is exactly what I needed for the tea I'm making. Nothing relieves a headache like birch bark tea. Next, I need a piece of lichen. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
Nice to see you again. Do you have that piece of lichen for me yet?
Thank you! Did you know you can pack wounds with lichen in a pinch? Next, I need the root of a comfrey plant. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
Well, well, you're back! Do you have that comfrey root for me yet?
Thank you! Nothing beats a comfrey root for a soothing brew. Next, I need a purple mushroom. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
There's a familiar face. I was hoping you'd stop by soon. Do you have that purple mushroom for me yet?
Oh, so there is something you needed after all?
Thank you! This will be a big help in my work. Next, I need a red mushroom. They can be a little hard to find, but do your best. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
Nice to see you again. Do you have that red mushroom for me yet?
Thank you! This is exactly what I needed for my healing potion. The last herb I need is the root of a ginseng plant. Please bring it back to me when you have it.
Welcome back! Do you have that ginseng root for me yet?
Thank you! This is exactly what I needed for my healing potion. You have been such a big help gathering these herbs. Here is my favorite healing elixer, as a reward for your troubles.
Please be sure to come back if you ever need more potions or some healing.
Well hello there. Thank you for gathering those herbs for me. Something I can do for you today?
Well, goodbye then. Please bring me those herbs soon.
No thanks. I'll be on my way now.
Actually, I changed my mind. I don't need anything.
I don't know. I haven't used them yet.
Wonderful, thank you. Can I have some more?
I suppose so. Do you sell anything else?
Yes. Can you check my health for me?
I can feel something is not right. I insist on a complete health check and treatment.
Yes. Can you tell me more about what you do here?
Yes. Do you have anything for sale?
I agree. In fact, I would be interested in learning more about your work.
Yes, I need something else before I go.

Forged by Fort Vehl blacksmiths, these militia helmets are used in the defense of the city against the nearby giant threat. 

Somewhat dwarven in design, Captain Rord also uses it occassionally to reward those who run errands for him in representation of the militant fort.
This necklace was given to you by Jasmin of the Swamp. The skeleton knuckles look creepy on this necklace but it seems to offer some sort of protection against the undead.
Oh, it's you again. Thank you for helping me fetch that spider silk for spinning.
I've been looking for an adventurer to help me with something.
Mother sends me out to gather silk for our weaving. Mother dyes the silk and grandmother weaves it, so I have to collect it all. The only problem is ... I am scared of spiders!

Beryl

Aliases: Deep Mother, Her Perfection, Flawless Diamond  
Race: Deep Gnome 
Worshippers: Deep Gnomes and others who mine or work with gems. 
Domains: 
     Earth, Good, Healing, and Trickery. Most clerics prefer to choose the Earth to be close to the Deep Mother and then one of the other three.
Governs: Gemsmithing, stealth, healing, safety 

Dogma: 
     Always seek to find and cut the perfect gem. Make it your life's pursuit to create jewelry and bring beauty and perfection to the world. Do not take unneeded risks, and rely on stealth and wit to keep you safe.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing
     Most clerics of Beryl prefer the mace or the heavy mace, usually together with an enchantment that does not involve Water (although such enchantments are not necessarily forbidden).

     When choosing armor, most clerics prefer the fine craftwork of one of their Dwarven allies. They prefer heavy metal armor such as plate or half plate, since this metal came from the Deep Mother's domain. Most clerics enhance their armors with a resistance to cold.

     When not traveling the Underdark in search of gems, clerics of Beryl dress outrageously, with a myriad of colors and many piercings showing off different gems from their travels. If they do travel, they tend to cover all jewelry, as moving through the Underdark unseen is of prime importance if you want to survive.

     They use jewelry consisting of the gems of their rank as focus for their spells.

Clergy and Temples:
     Those new to the faith are called "Greenstones," then as they progress in knowledge and power, they progress in ranks arranged by the rarity of gems (Greenstone, Malachite, Aventurine, Phenelope, Fire Agate, Feldspar, Garnet, Topaz, Alexandrite, Sapphire, Fire Opal, Ruby, Emerald, and Diamond), with diamond being the highest in rank. There is only one cleric at a time who is the Diamond of Beryl, and it is this cleric that heads the faith.

     Nearly all of Beryl's temples are hidden in the Svirfneblin cities in the Underdark; however, at least one is known to be on the surface, in the city of Stone on Rilara. Clerics like to pray during the day or next to a light source to enhance the beauty of their precious stones. During prayer, the cleric will often use their focus jewelry to scatter light and color across the wall or temple.

     Prayers to Beryl often revolve around gems and jewelry. For example, a jeweler about to start cutting a gem can say: "Allow me to cut the perfect stone for you," or a cleric trying to mine some raw gems from the earth might say "Fiddlesticks, Beryl, just give me one perfect stone."

Rilara
    Rilara is the southernmost continent of Layonara. It has always been a battleground for conflicts over territory, political power and wealth. It is even more so now that Milara has carved his wicked throne into the Iriand Mountains. Milara's machinations have added the strongest of all ingredients into the chaotic stew that is Rilara. As such, Rilarans are pragmatically suspicious and necessarily scheming. Those who are not have simply been subsumed into Milara's plans, whether they know it or not. Any city you visit in Rilara now will have a kind of subterranean tension, which seems ready to lash out into the everyday without notice. Many communities have stockpiled supplies, weapons, and hired henchmen to protect their precious homes only to find themselves in the service of the wicked master of Rilara the next day. The continent, it is safe to say, is not far from being entirely in the sway of Milara.

Well-known cities:

Casterly Castle
Location:  
    Casterly Castle can be found on the southwesternmost corner of the continent of Rilara
Population:  1600
Government:  Military Dictatorship
Defenses:  
    The castle is heavily defended with reinforced walls and battlements. It also houses a temple of Aragen inside its walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    In the many years of conflict on the continent of Rilara, the Casterly clan has managed to establish dominance in the southwestern region. They did this not by force of arms, but as many savvy rulers throughout history have, through the morally binding obligations of gift giving. For hundreds of years the wealthy Casterly family showered the towns of the southwestern region with gifts, gifts that couldn't possibly be repaid. The towns, therefore, repaid the castle with their allegiance. 
     Now, most of the surplus agricultural and trade goods of the region are shipped to the castle for redistribution. Some of it is traded with the elite of Point Harbor. Most, however, is packed south to the Casterly's port annex of White Harbor. The White Harbor cargo ships' manifests state that the primary destination is the Kingdom of Rodlem, a fact which has not slipped the attention of their rival city Karthy. Still, as the shipping routes on the south side of the continent rarely receive surveillance, and it is therefore hard to know for sure where these goods are shipped.
    There are many rumors about the involvement of the Casterly clan in Rilaran affairs. Rumors abound that an army is being amassed behind the walls, and that weapons and supplies are being stockpiled. Some think the Casterlys are preparing to fight Milara's forces, which they believe are gathering in Fort Himlad, a key central outpost. Others believe the Casterlys have received a gift from Milara, one which they can only repay with their allegiance. Whatever the murky truth is, Casterly is a key player in the unfolding struggle over Rilara.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Bitterbridge is the sister city to Bloody Gate, though far less stable. It lies on the northern portion of the Delwin River, at the point where the waterway falls from great heights from Lake Ire in the Ledros Mountains. The sight is one that many throughout Rilara once traveled to see. But it is more than a tourist attraction; the river is also the reason Bitterbrige exists. Originally many humble souls found the falls too gorgeous to part with and settled at their base. They built a bridge, where Bitterbridge now stands, for ease of passing through the rapid waters. It didn't take long for them to realize that the bridge would have to be defended from giants wandering between Wolfswood and the Mountains. The giants, not needing a structure to cross the raging Delwin, would simply smash the bridge for fun. 
    After a small fort had been established there and anti-giant measures taken, many travelers began to stay at Sweetbridge, as it was once called, to venture out at dawn for the rainbow mists of the Delwin Falls. Similar to the history of Bloody Gate, however, when Milara set his palace upon the Iriand Mountains, everything changed. Even the idea of Milara being so close sent the town into chaos. They knew Milara would march out for Karthy and would use the bridge, the product of their honest toil, to accomplish his task. Some thought to destroy it, some to defend it; others simply evacuated. Now the few who remain in the renamed Bitterbridge are said to have gone mad from the sheer stress of the situation.

Bloody Gate is situated on that pass, between two dramatic craggy peaks. It has been the site of countless epic struggles, epic victories and epic defeats. All of these have contributed to Bloody Gate's well-deserved name.

Others retort that they are dwarves and would die before becoming servants to such a wicked ruler. Those might say that it has been these dwarves who have kept Milara from controlling Karthy.     13,500 (60% human, 18% dwarf, 10% half-orc, 5% gnome, 5% halfling, 3% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:  
    Heavily fortified city with a reinforced masonry wall surrounding it.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Karthy is a rough and tumble city with very strict laws. The laws may be strict, but are subject to sudden change, hardly followed and yet executed with a kind of twisted pleasure by the Karthy guards. It is said that Milara has controlled this city for many years, and that its economic and political interests are his own. Supplies come to him through this port and his spies and troops depart from here. Therefore, all activity in this port is carefully monitored and recorded. A pervasive sense of paranoia grips the whole city, and travelers in particular as they are bombarded with askew glances and eyes peering through half-opened shutters. 
    The Kingdom of Roldem on the island of Calishan is trying to defeat the city but it seems that Milara is always one step ahead of them. This conflict dates back to the Cataclysm. Before Layonara was torn asunder in the great energies of the Cataclysm, Calishan and Rilara were pressed together in one huge central landmass. As they were cleaved apart, so were the people who lived in considerable turmoil on those lands. For many years two great families had battled for dominance on Calara, what people in retrospect call the unified territories. When they split, however, the two families were not split evenly. Many of the Roldem family was left on Rilara. But since they were cleaved in two by the Cataclysm and the ocean span too great to call for aid, the Roldem family was hunted down and quickly eradicated from Rilara. On Calishan, however, they established their dominance and came to rule the island. They still remember their kinsmen and have always had a mind to recapture Karthy and avenge their family's misfortune. With Milara taking control of much of Rilara, and Karthy as his primary port, this desire has intensified considerably. To say Roldem and Milara are at war would surely be an understatement.
    A major temple to Xeen can be found in Karty.

King's Landing
Location:  
    King's Landing can be found on the southern coast of Rilara.
Population:  2700
Government:  
    Monarchy, though in recent years it is suggested that King's Landing has fallen into a chaotic state.
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended castle, with bastions and reinforced walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    King's Landing, as the name suggests, is where the King first landed on Rilara after sending some of his finest men to pacify as much of Rilara as they could. Giants, bugbears, wild men, and feral elves alike fell to this solution to the Rilara settlement problem. The lands of the northeast were still too wild, and the southeast is primarily mountains, so the King's advisors directed him to this spot for his ceremonial claiming of the continent. Even now in King's Landing there stands a statue of the ancient king erecting a victorious flag on the banks where the Delwin River meets the ocean.
    Milara must have a sense of historical irony, for it is said that this is also where he first set foot on the island of Rilara. Where he came from, no one knows. But his berth at this port gives the name King's Landing a clever double meaning. As the well-buttressed city on the mouth of the southeast's most important waterway, Milara's presence here also has practical purpose.
    Whether or not it is true that Milara landed and took control of King's Landing, all reports document that this city is falling further and further into a state of lawless frenzy. The streets, it is said, are littered with corpses and looted possessions. The city elite have abandoned the town and the guards do more work keeping the wild commoners within the city than keeping any invading army without. The nearby cities of Wyk and Lann have done all that they can to keep the waves of King's Landers at bay. From the state of these towns it is easy to see that they are not very successful. 

Lannisport
Location:
    Lannisport is small village on the northern shore of Rilara.
Population: 685
Government:  Tribal council
Defenses:  
    Lannisport has a stone wall surrounding the town, though not the forces to man it in case of attack.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Traditionally, Lannisport was a fishing village. The north and central waters off the coast of Rilara boast some of the best fishing in all of Layonara. Lannisport fish can be found throughout Rilara and have been served for fine banquets in prestigious places as far as Port Hampshire, Leilon and Pranzis. The locals have always attributed their fishing prosperity to Shindaleria. Many years ago, on a cliff overlooking the natural harbor, the people of Lannisport established an impressive temple to their patron deity in a gesture of gratitude for years of prosperity but mostly to influence the future to proceed in their favor.
In the days of Milara, however, Lannisport has taken on a more nefarious pastime. Though small, or perhaps because of their diminutive stature, the docks at Lannisport have served as an ideal launching point for Milara's agents to sneak into the southern reaches of Mistone. For the most part, ships from Lannisport have been thought innocuous fishermen come to sell and spend. As such, they are mostly unquestioningly welcomed into the ports at Fort Valensk and Port Hampshire, and sometimes as far north as Forewarn Fort. Milara, it is said, uses this traditional oversight to his advantage and is said to have established himself well in certain areas of Mistone through such unsuspected vessels. 
    The situation has become more visible to Mistone authorities. The Mistone Alliance knows that at least some of the Lannisport fishing and cargo vessels are not what they appear to be. Notices have begun appearing at docks throughout Mistone, but as the gregarious fishermen swing from the rails of their vessels and dart for the bars and brothels as they always have, the notices are commonly shrugged off.

Point Harbor 
Location: 
    Northwestern tip of the continent of Rilara, at the edge of Dinen Forest.
Population:
    36,000 (45% human, 20% halfling, 12% elf, 10% dwarf, 8% half-orc, 5% gnome) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses:
    Point Harbor is a heavily fortified masonry fortress. Parts of the walls extend out into the bay. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
     Point Harbor is the most prosperous harbor of Rilara, and most of the continent's trade passes through here. Since the Forsaken Islands are so deadly that even passing by them is rumored to turn a whole crew into ghasts, goods headed east from Mistone usually come through Point Harbor. Either they re-supply and travel the dangerous north coast of Rilara or they travel overland to Karthy. Neither trek is desirable and it is not uncommon for Point Harbor to be the settled upon destination of many supposedly Dregar-bound captains.
    To protect its wealth, it is heavily fortified, both from the land as well as from the sea, making it a difficult city to capture. Its main trading partner is the city of Port Hampshire on Mistone, but passage to many of the great ports of Layonara can be booked on ships docking in Point Harbor. Boats from Point Harbor are likely the only ones you'll see on the books at any port outside of Rilara, excepting Xantril. The reason for this is simple. Being on the northwest corner of the vast continent of Rilara, Point Harbor is as far from Milara's seat as possible. This doesn't mean Milara overlooks it or cannot reach it, rather that his grasp there is less firm. Because of this, Point Harbor is one of the few ports on the island of Rilara that conducts business not entirely in the interests of Milara. 

Stone
Location:
    Stone is located in the central north of Rilara, in the foothills of Mount Taras 
Population:  
    670 (90% deep gnome, 5% human, 5% dwarf)
Government:  Miner's oligarchy
Defenses:  None that can be seen.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Stone is a town of deep gnomes. That fact alone should draw your attention to the fact that Stone is just the tip of the Mount Taras iceberg. The town itself is the relay station for mining supplies headed deep under the mountains and the point of commercial contact between the deep gnomes and the outside world. This is why the gnomes have recruited a small number of humans to manage their surface affairs, trading a very small portion of the minerals they uncover for other necessary supplies. A Temple to the deep gnomes' patron goddess, Beryl, has been established in Stone.

Fort Himlad
Location:  
    Fort Himlad lies at the southern edge of Wolfswood Forest on the banks of the Falas River. 
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Himlad lies at a strategic crossroad, with a road north leading into the Wolfswood, another heading east towards King's Landing and the Iriand Mountains, and yet another which leads west towards the numerous villages and hamlets that populate southwestern Rilara. Despite its crucial function of guarding the intersection of these key thoroughfares, it's not a big fort; its walls are wooden palisades.
    Rilarans of the southwest often send agents of seemingly meaningless commerce to Fort Himlad. Most believe they are spies. It is no secret that most of the southwest lives with a kind of rational paranoia of what Milara will do next and see Himlad as the crucial staging point or thoroughfare for any plans he might have with their homeland. Because of this, people of Himlad suspect the people of the southwest of planning an offensive against them. Minor skirmishes on the road west have already taken place. It seems only a mater of time before things escalate. Milara, it is rumored, shows up from time to time on nearby bluffs and watches the situation deteriorate with beaming expressions of gratification.

Dregar Locales

Iriand Mountains
    A vast mountain range on the southeastern edge of Rilara. In these mountains, Milara has his throne, launching attacks upon the continent from Bloody Gate. These mountains are known for the great mountain giants that inhabit them.

Wolfswood Forest

Tau'ren Hills

Belgaer Hills
    These lush green hills east of Dinen Forest comprise a large part of western Rilara. It tends to rain a lot in these hills, and not many settlements have been set up here.

Dinen Forest
    Although this forest is relatively small compared to the Wolfswood, it can still hardly be avoided if traveling east from Point Harbor.

Bear Island
    South of Point Harbor, off the Rilaran coast, lays Bear Island. This small island has been home to a clan of bugbears for as long as many can remember.

Swamp of Lost Souls
    This swamp in northeast Rilara was once home to a coven of necromancers. Twelve of the dark mages convened one fateful night to form a dark pact, but an adventuring party disrupted the ritual before the spell could be completed. Due to the result of the the adventurers' interference, the swamp has since been called the Swamp of Lost Souls.

Would you like to play Roulette?

A 100 gold Straight-Up Number bet on the number 5 would be '100 Number 5'.  A 10 gold Split bet on the numbers 00 and 3 would be '10 Split 00 3'.  A 500 gold Street bet covering the row of numbers 7, 8 and 9 would be '500 Street 7-9'.  A 100 gold Corner bet covering the numbers 23, 24, 26, and 27 would be '100 Corner 23-27'.  A 50 gold Fives bet covering 0, 00, 1, 2, and 3 would be '50 Five'.  A 500 gold Line bet covering the numbers 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, and 24 would be '500 Line 19-24'.  A 10 gold bet on the third column, covering every multiple of 3 would be '10 Column 3'.  A 50 gold bet on the second dozen covering the numbers 13 to 24 would be ' 50 Dozen 2'.  A 100 gold bet on all odd numbers would be '100 Odd'.
Place as many bets as you'd like during the time between the spins of the wheel.  Every 2 minutes, I'll spin the wheel and give out the winnings.

There are several types of bets, with different odds of hitting.  The first type of bet is a Red/Black, Odd/Even, or Low/High bet.  The payoff of these bets is 1:1, and they cover half of the numbers on the table, not including 0 and 00.  The second type of bet is a Column bet or a Dozen bet.  The payoff of these bets is 2:1, and they cover 12 numbers on the table, either one of the groups of 12 numbers numerically, or the 12 numbers included on one column of the table..

The third type of bet is called a Line bet, and it covers 6 numbers included in two adjacent rows of the table.  Its payoff is 5:1.  The fourth type of bet is the Five-Number bet, and it covers the numbers 0, 00, 1, 2, and 3.  Its payoff is 6:1.  The fifth type of bet is a Corner bet, which covers four numbers that make a square on the table.  Its payoff is 8:1.  The sixth type of bet is a Street bet, covering a single row of three numbers on the table and paying off at 11:1.

The seventh type of bet is a Split bet, which covers two adjacent numbers on the table, including 0 and 00.  This bet pays off at  17:1.  Finally, there is the most risky, and most profitable, Straight Up number bet.  This is a bet on a single number slot, and pays off at 35:1.  Do you need to know how to make bets?

Making bets is simple, just tell me what you'd like to bet on, and I'll put it on the table for you.  The format for telling me bets is to say "amount | bet type | numbers" (using the conversation bar, where it says 'Say:').   Valid betting amounts are 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 5000, and 10000 gold.  Any bet is possible, as multiple amounts on the same bet stack.  Valid betting types are Number, Split, Street, Corner, Five, Line, Dozen, Column, Odd, Even, Red, Black, High and Low.  For example, a 100 gold bet on the number 2 would be "100 Number 2" and 50 gold bet on Odds would be "50 Odd".

The 'numbers' field isn't necessary for Odd, Even, Red, Black, High, Low, and Five bets.  For a Number bet, just put the number you'd like to bet on after 'Number'.  Valid numbers include 1 through 36,  0 and 00.  For a Split bet, just put the two numbers that you'd like to bet on with the lowest number first.  (They have to be adjacent to eachother on the table.)  For a Column or Dozen bet, valid numbers are 1, 2 and 3.  For Columns, the numbers correspond to the top number in the column.  For Dozens, the numbers correspond to 1-12, 13-24, and 25-36.

For a corner bet, you'll need to put the highest and lowest number in the corner with a dash inbetween, such as 1-5 or 2-6.  Note that this bet doesn't cover all numbers in the range, just the ones that make a square.  (1-5 doesn't include 3, and 2-6 doesn't include 4, etc.).  The same applies to Line and Street bets, though all the numbers in the range are included.

Dregar
    The largest continent of Layonara, Dregar is also home to the capital of Pranzis, from which the emperors ruled. The King of Dregar is still rebuilding after losing over 200,000 troops (not just in Pranzis) defending his populace from Blood and the forces that came through the rifts. The continent is in turmoil because of the rebuilding process and the lack of protection from qualified soldiers. Some upstarts are attempting to claim their own territories and bandits have their rein on the countryside. On top of all of this, Blood still has a very sizeable army and attacks outlying areas quite frequently.

Defenses: 
    Superior masonry walls surround much of the city. In many places the walls are also reinforced. In addition to this much of the walls have also been magically reinforced. The defenses are solidly constructed and security is tight, as one would expect in the world's capital.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This is the city to visit when you are looking for that special item or are in need of military training. It directly supplies military forces to Fort Thunder, North Fort and South Fort. 

    As largest city in the world, many religions have built temples here. Most noteworthy is the majestic cathedral of Rofirein, but temples to Toran and Branderback can also be found here.

Hurm 
Location:
    Hurm is on the west coast of the continent of Dregar, on the Bay of Carocsa, not far from the Forsaken Islands. 
Population 
    3,000 (75% human, 5% Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% halfling, 5% half-elf, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    There is a wooden palisade around this coastal town. The town is often in a state of disrepair, so its defenses are unreliable at best. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Just thirty years ago Hurm was a prosperous city with a bright future. Since Blood's return, however, it has deteriorated rapidly. The town is no longer the shipping potentate it once was, largely due to the proximity of the Forsaken Islands. 

Lorindar 
Location:  
    Lorindar is at the southernmost tip of the continent of Dregar.
Population: 
    15,000 (45% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:
    A large, well fortified masonry wall surrounds this city. The ruler is proud of the protection the wall offers the city. Some parts of the wall are also protected by spells. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    The twin horsemen of Lorindar are either the first or last landmark most people see on the continent of Dregar. In the early days of the rule of Pranzis a company of horsemen were sent into the wilds of the southern plains to make the lands livable by common folk. A massive Drow invasion in the prior century had drawn all of the capital's attention and left the south, despite being so close, to fall into shadow. The towns of the southern plains were quickly overrun and the people either fled further south or went missing. Once the capital was settled, the horsemen left the gates to reclaim the towns and clear the roads. In the end, only two made it to the southern tip of the continent. There they found an impressive and resilient throng of Dregarians living in scattered coastal communities under the constant threat of assault.

  The two horsemen, a twin brother and sister of the Galeright family, rallied these scattered tribes under the flag of the capital and brought them to the ruined outpost at Lorindar. There they rebuilt the town by hand and with primitive equipment. Still, they rebuilt it with enough motivation and skill to withstand the swarms of bugbears and giants that crashed against their walls like waves against their stone docks. Of course the Galeright twins were in front of the walls, meeting each wave with astounding skill and passion.
Rather than return to the capital, the Galeright twins settled in Lorindar and brought the king and queen themselves to witness the mighty will of the southerners. It was a glorious day in the history of Dregar, one that lives in the proud tales of Lornidarians. Shortly thereafter, the capital redirected immense funds and manpower to Lornidar, sensing its strategic, economic, and political significance as well as the sentimental unifying force it had for southern Dregarians. 

    Now Lorindar is the busiest and most strategically situated port, always bustling with commerce and strange faces. The people of Lorindar are proud of their city and their close connection with Pranzis and work hard to maintain their dominance in the shipping business of Dregar. Most of the merchants and associated industries find honor in honest and fair business dealings, and the city has become known throughout the realm as such. Nevertheless, Lorindarians are often suspicious of outsiders, particularly those from competing ports, notably their rival city, Waysend.

Redstone 
Location:
    Redstone lies west of the Serpent Mountains and north of Pranzis on the continent of Dregar. 
Population:
    950 (85% Hill Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% human, 2% halfling, 2% half elf, 1% elf) 
Government:  Clan 
Defenses:
    Redstone has masonry walls that surround the town. These walls were built by dwarves, so they are very sturdy and can withstand a large scale attack. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Redstone has one of the largest populations of Hill Dwarves on the continent of Dregar. Many dwarves end up settling in Pranzis and plying their trades and skills there. The populace of Redstone is known as hardy folks that have had a hard life. 
 
Vale 
Location: 
    Vale is in the southern part of the continent of Dregar in the Forests of Mists. 
Population: 
    600 (50% elf, 20% human, 15% half-elf, 5% halfling, 5% gnome, 5% dwarf, 5% half-orc. 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses:   
    Nestled in the great trees, this town is protected by remoteness and lore of hallowed ground. Rangers and druids have dedicated their lives to protecting Vale, and do so with passion. A short stone wall surrounds the village core. The chest-high wall is perfect for rangers to shoot over and druids to cast behind with some protection.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Vale is more of a spiritual center and forest outpost than a town. Of those who call Vale home, most live remotely among the old trees, yet they retain a practical and spiritual attachment to this place amidst nature.
On the continent of Dregar, Vale is never far from the hearts of rangers and druids. Deep in the heart of the Forest of Mists, its serene power is unsurpassed. Dregar's nature folk make regular pilgrimages to the legendary tree shrine of Vale to fulfilll their vows or renew their spirit. It is known that every decade, each druid throughout Layonara is required by oath to make a pilgrimage to this central forest and central shrine of Katia within. It is rumored that most come more frequently, as the experience is reinvigorating as well as a key to the spiritual and pragmatic unity of Layonara's druids. Through this hub of the druidic network, information is shared, new members are indoctrinated, roles are shuffled and objectives established.

Dalanthar
Location:  
    Dalanthar can be found in northern Dregar, between the Thunder Peaks and the Darkland Mountains.
Population: 1900
Government:  
    Two families struggle with each other for rule of Dalanthar
Defenses: None

Miscellaneous Information:
    Ages ago, the city of Dalanthar was the site of an awesome conflict between dragons. In the clash, the town was reduced to fire and rubble. The few survivors reconstructed the town upon the ruins. Today it is a shadow of its former glory. This is partly caused by the ever-present darkness that emanates from the Great Rift found northwest of town in the Darkland Mountains. It is also only a shell of its former self because for a powerful few, the dragon conflict still rages, animating intra-village aggression. One prominent family still sides with one dragon, blaming all the town's woes on the other. A second prominent family points its finger at the first. This conflict is manifest in the geography of town, as a huge craggy ridge separates the town into two halves. Each half is primarily under the influence of one of these two families..

Highpass
Location: In the Storm Horn Mountains
Population: 95
Government: Waysend representative

Miscellaneous Information:
    Highpass is a tiny village that sprung around Highpass Fort, and is located on one of the few usable passes through the Storm Horn Mountains. The pass is of major importance to the city of Waysend to the southeast, as this is one of the main roads for transporting goods to and from the port city. It is also home to a temple of Goran.

North Fort:
Location: 
    Bordered by Deadman's Pass and the Drift Lands on Dregar.
Population:  700
Government:  Military rule

Miscellaneous Information:
    North Fort is little more than a high desert camp. The frequency of suspicious events in the desert has kept North Fort well attached to the capital, despite the distance. The numbers of inhabitants are never high, however, as skirmishes between the king's and Bloodstone's armies are all too common. As such, the fort is continually re-supplied and at a constant state of alert.

North Point:
Location:
  North Point is the northernmost town on Dregar, west of the Singing Forest
Population:  800
Government:  
    There are several tribes which struggle for control in North Point at any given time.
Defenses:  
    North Point has no defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    For years fishermen traveled to this spot to exploit the huge schools of fish brought to the coast by the strong ocean currents off the north edge of the continent. Makeshift encampments eventually became this well-developed fishing village. Those who won this land from the hands of the previous occupants were rugged indeed, and the city still retains this surly character. This, by the way, makes North Point attractive for pirates who raid the cargo ships trying to sail swiftly by in the current and offshore winds. This doesn't seem to bother the fishermen much as pirates rarely hunt for fish and they do bring a steady supply of gold and goods into the town. A temple to Aeridin can be found here.

Orc's Watch
Location:  
    North of Vale at the north rim of the Forests of Mists
Population:  150
Government:  Tribal
Defenses:  
    A wooden wall and gates protect the meager interior of this outpost.

Miscellaneous Information:
    As its name suggests, this series of buildings on a tall hill serves as a lookout for Bloodstone's activity in the Forest of Mists. Sources say that it was overrun in a sweeping march along the north rim of the Forest of Mists by Bloodstone's army and now remains almost entirely abandoned.

Saudiria
Location:  
    On the east coast of Dregar, at the edge of the Anuroch Desert and the Drift Lands lies the city of Saudiria.
Population: 8500
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
    There is a wooden and adobe wall surrounding this city for protection. Mostly it is protected by the desert and the ocean.

Miscellaneous Information:
    How you come to Saudiria will determine your perception of it. From the desert, Saudiria will greet you with the enticing natural rhythms of an oasis. From the ocean, Saudiria wil greet you with a windblown lullaby and an inviting bed of grass made just for your weary head. Saudiria is both. It is desert oasis and costal vale. That fact, combined with the way the sun sets where desert wisps swirl in coastal gusts, make Saudiria known throughout the known islands for its magical beauty.

    The surrounding desert will testify that Saudiria hasn't always been blessed thus. Something or someone carved this coastal glade and farmland out of the sand and dust of the desert. The terrain of Saudiria is considered one of the great works of Dregar. Many come to Saudiria to enjoy its sights. Others come to answer the riddle of this amazing transformation: was it wealth, labor, magic, or some other power that created this land?  Residents never tell. Wanderers mostly choose to reside. Only fables tell the truth. Some wonder if it is the temple of Az'atta that can be found here.

Thorns Keep
Location:  
    In the Thunder Peaks in the northern part of Dregar
Population:  200
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended keep, well protected by both the walls of the keep itself and the sheer rock walls of the Thunder Peaks.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Like the name suggests, Thorn's Keep is not at all inviting. It lies in a particularly barren and inhospitable region of the Thunder Peaks. There are, however, two key reasons for the massive keep to exist there. First, there is a small but crucial body of water there which drains in the spring and summer to irrigate the fields of the Great Central Plains of Dregar below. Second, it is situated on a mountain crest which allows surveillance of that same key region. Those that reside in Thorn's Keep are therefore vigilant yet gruff, meshing perfectly with its overall persona. Contact with the keep has been cut off by Blood for sometime, however. Some believe that the Keep has fallen into the hands of the enemy.

Castle Raxswell
Location:  
    North of Lorindar, Castle Raxswell stands.
Population: 800
Government: Military rule
Defenses: 
    The castle is heavily defended by high and wide stone walls with ramparts and reinforcements.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Traveling north from Lorindar you'll come to Castle Raxwell. Both the castle itself and the temple of Prunilla located therein are notable for their spartan aesthetic. The castle is situated as a point of defense for the major port city of Lorindar. Many battles against the armies of Bloodstone have been waged on this barren and blood-soaked soil. Pranzis continually sends troops to this castle, knowing well its importance in the struggle for control of Dregar.


Willows Weep
Location:
    North of the Darkland Mountains, west of the Singing Forest and south of North Point you'll find Willows Weep.
Population:  660
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  none

Miscellaneous Information:
    This rare Elven town on Dregar exudes a mystical sullenness which seems to dance hauntingly along with the drooping willow branches. It is a small town, but built with elegant extravagance. The stylized and prominent crypts in the area have suggested to travelers that this city is somehow rooted in those crypts or servants of the dead.

Xora's Tower
Location:
    Xora's Tower can be found in the northeasternmost part of Dregar
Population:  140
Government:  Military dictatorship
Defenses:  very little

Miscellaneous Information:
    On the northeasternmost point of the continent of Dregar, perched on a rounded bluff, lies the haunting tower of Xora. For ages this tower served as a watchpoint for invaders from the sea or demons from Xantril. Rumor now spreads that this tower has been captured by demons or Bloodstone and has been turned to other purposes. Within sight of the tower lies an ancient shrine where magical force beckons. Knowledge of its origin and its use are either carefully guarded or lost over generations.

Waysend 
Location: 
    On the east cost of the continent of Dregar is the city of Waysend.
Population 
    6,000 (55% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government: Republic 
Defenses:
    There is a masonry wall that is about 80% completed that surrounds the city. The ruler is spending lots of money to ensure the city is well protected from bandits and ships alike. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Waysend has recently come into its own, since Blood's arrival. With Hurm disintegrating and with Pranzis rebuilding its troops, Waysend has been left on its own and is building a good shipping business. Waysend is one of the cities that is trying to break away from Pranzis' rule.

Aasimar
    Proud, fair-skinned and tall, the aasimar are a race with a somewhat curious background. One of the two races that are known to be "Planetouched" (the others being the Tieflings), Aasimar are native to planes of law and order. They have holy blood somewhere in their ancestry. While some claim to have descended directly from the Gods, it is more likely that one of their ancestors was a Celestial, and not a God. However, most of them cannot trace their heritage back to a specific celestial being.

    There is no difference between Aasimar hailing from human, elven, or other lineage, it is the touch of the divine that makes them what they are, regardless of their other ancestry.
Most Aasimar have a human ancestry, a relative few have an elvish ancestry. 
Aasimar have no lands to call their own. They are welcome in most places, but can also be unwanted in others.

Personality: 
    Because of their ancestry, aasimar are always champions of good. Aasimar are very often paladins or clerics, devoutly following their deity. This devoutness can make them somewhat rigid in their opinions, however.
Since they have no place to call home, belonging completely neither in the Heavens nor Layonara, aasimar travel a lot. Even though they're well-liked in most places, they are always loners.
Aasimar do not tend to band together.

Physical Description:. 
    Aasimar are beautiful creatures. They are tall, with blond, almost white, or silvery hair and bright eyes that make others feel like they see right into the core of their being.

    They like to wear finely crafted metal armors, often decorated with sigils or coats of arms. In their fight against good, they prefer to use greatswords or other weapons that allow them to use their height as an advantage. 

    Aasimar ancestry makes them very aware of their surroundings. They're also very perceptive of people's motives. Their ancestry also provides them some elemental protection. Some spells that are specifically used to control other humanoids will not work on Aasimar.

Relations with other races: 
    In general, aasimar get along with most good races, however, they can hate "evil" races with an almost fanatical fervor. This is especially true for the other Planetouched race, the Tiefling.
 
Alignment: 
    Because of their heritage, aasimar are always good, and usually Lawful or Neutral Good.

Religion: 
    Aasimar usually follow the deity their ancestors did. However, since they do not really have a place in the Heavens, some Aasimar refuse to follow or even acknowledge deities or their servants.

Language: 
    Common, Celestial

Names: 
    Depends on the other part of their ancestry (human, elf, et cetera).

Adventurers: 
    Having no home or lands to call their own, Aasimar travel the lands and are not likely to settle down in a particular location. They're usually traveling paladins or clerics, looking to fight evil where they can. Those who are not devout followers of a deity tend to become traveling bards.

Krashin
     The northwesternmost island on Layonara, according to its cartographers. Many refer to Krashin as Barbarian Island. It is a cold and mountainous island, almost continuously covered in snow. The biting cold makes it difficult to explore the mountains for a long period of time, unless one comes well prepared to brave the breezing wastes.

Well-known cities:

Raven's Watch
Location:
     On the southern coast of Krashin lies the walled hamlet Raven's Watch. 
Population: 385
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
     A meager wooden palisade surrounds the city.
Miscellaneous Information:
     Not a rich community by any means, Raven's Watch primarily makes its living in the almost ever-present snow by trapping and selling hides. Those who live here are called barbarians by most Mistoners, particularly by the residents of Leilon, for it is from this city where the boats of the Long Axes set out to raid the north regions of Mistone. Before its walls were erected and fortified, their favorite target was Leilon. After several failed attempts to raid the fortified Leilon, the Long Axes retreated to Krashin and have been slowly regrouping ever since. Toran

Aliases: The All Watching, The Great Leader  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: Humans, but often worshipped by half elves as well. Also has the occasional highly righteous, justice-seeking worshipper from other races such as dwarves and elves.
Domains: Good, Protection, War
Governs: Honor, truth, loyalty, duty, vigilance

Dogma: 
     Protect the realms and rout injustice wherever you find it. Raise up the weak and empower them, so that they might see the strength of Toran. Seek out the servants of evil, most notably those who follow Corath and Pyrtechon, and bring them to justice.
Be a shining example of goodness and righteousness by bringing order and safety to the lands. Your word is your bond.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     The favored attire of the followers of Toran is shining full plate and the longsword. When not attired in their armor, they wear simple robes that are more functional than decorative. The holy symbol of the people of Toran is the ankh, which is generally worn around the neck and displayed openly at all times. The colors of the church are silver, blue, and gold.

Clergy and Temples:
     Followers of Toran can roughly be divided into three categories: the general clergy, the Justicers, and the Paladins.

     The Justicers are followers of Toran well versed in the law (often taught to them by the most devoted of Rofirein's followers). These Justicers are appointed by the Divine Court as executioners of punishments handed down by the Judges of the court. The Justicers are beyond reproach, the best of the best that the church of Toran has to offer. Justicers are often chosen from among the veteran ranks of the Paladins, although they have been known to come from other bodies as well. Justicers have responsibilities for districts, traveling from town to town to dispense the justice of the court. The righteous standing of a Justicer is such that they are entrusted to hear trivial matters of law during their travels so that they might keep such matters from bogging down the Divine Court. They are also empowered, in times of crisis, to take charge of local authority and militia to see that law and order are maintained or restored. As the Justicers are to Judges, so too are Paladins to Justicers. 

     The Paladins belong to the arm of the church that carries out the rulings of the Justicers. It is their job to bring bloody retribution to evildoers. Should they find someone committing a crime, it is their duty to hold them for trial by a Justicer. Should a Justicer be unavailable to hear a case, and the crime not so severe that the Divine Court should become involved, then it is up to the Paladin to make his own moral decision and to ascertain that evil does not go unpunished. This punishment however, may not be death, for such a sentence is reserved for the domain of the High Court or a Justicer appointed by the Court. Despite the authority of a Paladin to detain evildoers, and in some cases mete judgement on them, Paladins do not hold power to assume authority over a region. Unlike Justicers, Paladins are not tied to any region. Instead, they are free to roam as their morals and faith dictates. It is the place of the Paladin to seek out and decimate evil and wrong-doing, rather than wait for it to be brought before them.
 
     A small sub-sect of the Church of Toran is the Order of the Undead Hunters. Although officially part of the Judiciary branch of the church, they are an authority unto themselves. The Order of Undead Hunters is made up mostly of Paladins, as they have the martial prowess needed to deal with the undead that many other clergy lack. Only the most devoted of priests ever joins the Order, as the prayers and skills necessary to become the bane of undead are potent indeed, and come at a high cost. The Order of the Undead Hunters is lead by a Paladin of Toran granted the title of "The Shining Hand." The Shining Hand of Toran is personally chosen by his or her predecessor. The choice is absolute and undisputable, even by the chosen. In the unlikely event that the Shining Hand has not appointed a successor, the most senior member of the Order assumes the position. Upon ascending to the position of Shining Hand of Toran, the Paladin is presented to the Divine Court as such, so that he or she may be entered into the rolls. At this time, the Shining Hand is granted all the authority and powers of a Justicer, the only Justicer NOT appointed by the Divine Court. Further, the Shining Hand does not have a territory, nor does he serve the Divine Court. Instead, the Shining Hand is an authority unto himself, answering only to the High Priest of Toran and to Toran himself. In the event of a crisis that brings a Justicer and the Shining Hand together, the Shining Hand is the reigning authority. 

     The temples of Toran are known the lands over as houses of safety and refuge. None in need shall ever be turned away. They are strongholds in their communities, ready to harbor any and all comers from encroaching evils. All Temples have at least one Paladin assigned to them. Some temples are also homes to Justicers. However, since there are so few Justicers, they are forced to travel throughout regions to hear cases and to make decisions. This means that every temple has a room prepared should a Justicer arrive unannounced, so that they may always have a place to lay for rest and to contemplate trying issues in solitude.
