This appears to be Abiorn's journal. While perusing it would be likely quite rude, you do note a great deal of chapters pertaining to several central points of dicussion.

One, his dead wife Aesa. His writings seem to come back to her in almost every ethical discussion, as though she embodies his conscience. 

Two, his family. You are able to note the names of his siblings, Ardelis, Akithn, and Atrsil. His parents were apparently Jovn and Kestian. His writings on his family seem to have diminished in intensity as of later entries... and his somewhat crazed and melancholy sentiments seem to have vanished. 

Third, he seems to speak of his education in later life, under the strangely short lived guidance of a monk near the Monastery of Dreams. He does not detail the exact words exchanged, nor the duration of his invitation to speak with this monk... though it seems a great peace overcame him following these interactions. 

Abiorn's writings seem to almost deify the wisdom of this stranger by the lake, and it is quite clear an epiphany of self-awareness followed. The journal as a whole takes a wondrous turn from crazed to clarity at this apparent turning point in his life. 

He writes of his studies to maintain control over himself, through things as simple as his self-titled 'lazy tongue' of an accent, to things as complex as understanding the nature of the tragedy that befell his mind following Aesa's death. A sense of duty pervades the writings following these chapters, as though much reason was given for a purpose in existance. 

The discussion of those magics that ultimately destroyed his peaceful existance with Aesa take a turn towards tumultuous internal debate as the journal works forward. The discussion of necromancy as a tool of oppression that must be sought out and destroyed seems obvious, distinct, and absolute in early writings.

Then the topic of the dark-skinned gnome Casrushier enters into his writings. There seems to be a turning point in his emotions and absolute judgement on these matters as this gnome enters his life. The complexity of his arguments seem strained under the pressure of some manner of internal debate, though it would take much reading of this journal to fully begin to understand these emotions.

Later chapters of his journal frequently revolve around the Black Mages, their offer, and his subsequent battles with them. There is a great deal of speculation and paranoia apparent in his words when he speaks of his overwhelming enemy.

In other sections his concern for a loved one is glimpsed here and there in comparisons to the trauma he experienced after his wife's death, and the crazed turn his mind took after his wife's death. In this time he had the opportunity to bring someone, marked through occasional affectionate terms in gnomish, from a dark place and reintroduce them into the world, as he once regained self-awareness long ago.

Near the end, he lingers often on a move to unburden himself of the artifacts and treasures he'd discovered in the world and the desire to make a lasting influence on it for good. References to astronomical maps and ship designs are infrequently mentioned, as well as concern for a companion's shrinking time in the world.

To even skim the contents of this journal reveals a rare life with many turns. One that went from unhinged ramblings into one others looked to, one who found himself leading others into dark places and out again, from highest peaks to lands that had never seen the sun.
The aura of anguish around this spirit in particular is quite frightening to behold.

Seven tenants of faith:
* Do not fail, for failure is weakness and not tolerated by the Dark One.
* Fear nothing, fear is a weakness and a weapon of your enemy.
* You are the instrument of Corath, seek always his will and to spread his influence.
* Obey with utmost diligence.
* Let hatred and malice feed your fury.
* Master oneself that you may master others.
* Mercy is weakness; exact your punishment with the cold malice of death.

In my days of research, I have come across a legend most intriguing.  The validity of it I have sought to test, far and wide.  Of it's truth, I've found little backing.  It remains, however, one of the more interesting, though elusive, tales I've researched.

Tattered parchments that for all I may know may be the figment of a bard's imagination put on paper, tell of a line of kings who bore the name Iliarial.  These parchments were brought to me by a fellow scholar of ancient peoples, and though I am curious to what is written, I was not impressed by their condition.  What I did note was that the parchment used was a strange variant of paper from a yew tree, which is quite rare to begin with and generally not wasted on trifle tales.  The condition of the parchment was pitiful however, and knowing the lasting nature of paper made from yew, it would seem that these texts are quite ancient indeed.

The apparent writer was seeking out some ruins, his purpose for doing so quite obvious... to loot them.  From what I have made out from his text, written in a curious mixture of the Elvish and T'oleflor languages, these ruins were of a kingdom ruled by men, with the surname of Iliarial.  I have not been able to determine where he indicated these ruins were, though vague references seem to cancel out the possibility of Mistone or the greater Dregar continents.  The Ruins of Iliarial seem to have held some allure to this adventurer of old, passages I've translated such as the following indicate adequate optimism:

"Statues of rubies, shields of emeralds, cloths sewn from diamonds... hold for me Iliarials Tomb will."

Or:

"Found the key I have, or found the key has me.  The key the key, the key to loosening the ancient blades."

Various mentions of treasures pour out in the little readable text I have.  And for an apparent rogue such as our writer, the allure is clear.  The old names for mithril and titanium are used, and some mention of magical silver is made several times, though the translation is difficult on these topics.  Needless to say, our writer felt that this kingdom of men had quite a command over their crafts, in particular magical imbuing if I've read correctly.  The magical nature of this culture is made clear in several passages:

"Never seen metals of golems I have seen..."

Or:

"Statues live or dead neither have been, wandering the hallways where I have hidden..."

The latter passage is interesting to note, as it implies the rogue adventurer did indeed see these ruins, and perhaps walk their halls if any still stand.  In my research this has confused me the most, as the writer implied the only access to these ruins was a magical password.  In one section he suggests he has discovered the password, and much to my lamentations this section has been oddly burned from its page.  However, multiple mentions of passwords fill these pages, and they hold a notable theme.  See here phrases used repeatedly, and sometimes even with reference to a password:

"Virtue and Justice"
"Golden on thy Skin"
"Wisdom beget Knowledge"
"Hraykirlar of Lihariax"  Note: This latter word appears unfinished in the scripts.
"Reverence and Honor"
"Debasement of Evil"
"The Broken Blade"

There may in fact be several more passwords, though these phrases seem indicative.  My confusion on this subject arises on the validity of this writer even seeing the ruins.  As mentioned, he claims to have seen these treasures and magical apparatus.  He claims to have seen many things, which I will proceed onto shortly.  But the problem with these claims comes in the introductory passage:

"If to never again be seen may I be, then leave these pages for you I will.  And if to be doomed I am, then under the first treasured gem will again you see me.  I go now to the floatingman's tree, for my password I think will to he bring me...."

The remainder of this passage has withered over time, and I have been unable to finish the last sentence nor the obviously positioned password underneath this farewell.  Regardless, it becomes a contradiction with other passages describing the ruins in full, since this text begins as a departing tale.  The plausibility therefore of Iliarial's Ruins is fully in question based on this fact.

But still I seek it out.  The single most disturbing passages have been quite difficult to translate, but there seems to be a motif of what can be best described as light becoming darkness.  Whether this is literal or figurative, the wording is not descriptive enough to say for certain.  However, there is clear reference to demons several times in the text.  Once again these references appear to have been written in hindsight.  There is no rhyme or reason to this reference, though light to darkness, and either fire to ice or ice to fire, is mentioned several times in conjunction with demonic parallels.  For this reason I believe there is a figurative expression herein.  Especially when coupled with the probable passwords which indicate what can best be described as Toranite, Voraxian, or perhaps even Rofireinite sentiments.  The possible age of this parchment begs questions as to what gods were even in power at the time, however that is not our focus.  These ruins, or the tale of them, appear to contain a fallen grace theme, which becomes quite colorful at times.  I shall continue to seek the truth on this matter out, but for now I have recorded this for the benefit of other researchers that might know something of the names or implied histories within these texts.

One last note regarding the possibility of a password or other such code to enter these ruins, again if they should in fact have an entrance.  On every page of the rogue adventurer's parchments there lay a strange symbol in the center of each page.  I do not understand the nature of this symbol as it is quite foreign to anything I've seen before.  However, should it be required to fashion something with this symbol to fit a keylock perhaps, or simply to recognize it as some key to a puzzle... I am tracing it on the following page to make sure anyone who does go out in search of these ruins has this symbol in front of them to decipher.  Should this symbol be integral to entrance, or escape for that matter, of these ruins, it is my recommendation that all who seek out the Ruins of Iliarial bring a copy of this symbol as I have taken great care to trace it in its full detail in this tome.

The magics in this ring are quite astounding, and it is doubtful that anyone other then the most powerful of enchanters created this relic of power.

The ring itself appears to be a strangely enchanted ring of fortitude.  Dwarvish runes encircle the beautiful ring, they appear to hold magics warding off death or other evil blights.

The Lichbane Mace.  In it's simplicity it earns great respect amongst all living beings opposed to undeath and necromancy.  The make of these maces are said to have derived from The Shining Hand of Toran sometime around the 5th century following the cataclysm.  These weapons were distributed amongst the Order of Undead Hunters at that time, though in recent ages the making of such weapons seems a lost art.

The weapon is quite simple and quite plain despite it's powerful enchantments.  The metals and ores used are simple and unimpressive, though the rough edges glimmer with a magic and divine energy crackling within.  One lone mithril ring of ore circles the mace at it's midline, and a gold star made of a tiny topaz shines alone, centered on that ring.

Cursed is he who does not honor our customs and justice shall be as swift as our lord's blade allows.

Honor our people as you would honor your own, know our customs and we shall learn to know yours.  Forget not the laws of our righteous lord, do not betray that which you must respect.

Cursed is he who would not walk the path of honor.  For it is under their raised honor that he shall find himself an ally.

Cursed is he who knows only greed.  For he who dares covet their glory shall know their sacrifice.

Cursed is he who does not honor knights fallen.  For he who dares step beyond the stones of honor shall see their wrath.

Fall shall he who honors not our King.  Show deference, and approach closely do not.  Show respect and honor, and walk always as allies.  For our lord above shall be always watching.

Known shall he be for he shall retreat from darkness, known from the beginning shall those weak of heart become.  And by the strength of our lord shall you fall.

It is said that the Ether Giants are the masters of storms and the lords amongst all giants.

With their superior intellect and culture, the Ethers are known to have blessed the lands with several notable creations and relics of old.  This helmet is one such relic.

What clan of Ethers was behind this particular crafted feat is unknown, though the quality is clear.  Made of cobalt melded ore, the helmet is infused with a magic that is quite apparent to the wearer.  Upon initial contact with the bearer of the helm, a tingling is felt all over the body, and a noise that can only be described as a distant and shimmering thunderclap is 'felt' within the bones of their head.

This tainted blade is a smithed shard of Vreliaxia's Silver Sword, a fabled blade of it's time, this blade was once wielded by one of the greatest knights defending the honor of the Kingdom of Iliarial.

The blade itself is mithril in making, though a strange and flowing silver seems to glimmer on it's edges, holding magics that will forever be unknown to most.

It was once said that only the true of heart might wield the blade that Vreliaxia the paladin of Iliarial once held.  Now though... fragments of her old blade have been forged with the curse she and her kingdom have been forced to bear for the mistakes of the forsaken defilers.

A very small and extremely beautiful pair of gloves.  Their weave shimmers with a brilliance rarely seen.

Delicate strands of ancient woven ores of mithril, and what seems to be some type of strange silver lace the outer weaves of this smooth silken cloth.  At the wrist of these gloves exquisite rubies of the smallest size dangle in what at first appears to be a tenuos connection to the weave of the glove, though upon inspection, they are quite impossible to pull off as fine mithril strands have been somehow interlaced with the cut of the gem itself.

Upon placing these gloves on one's hands, the fingers immediately vibrate with the energy of the woven enchantments.  It is said by most who have managed, rather been allowed, to place their hands in these tiny gloves that a brief surge of confidence, conviction, and what many describe as a powerful emotion washes over them.

These wondrous guantlets came into the possession of the Krakaria Family by unknown means, but are clearly a prized peice of what this noble family has come to own in its great store of heirlooms and treasures.

The namesake of these gloves is in no way true to it's origin, which is speculated to be as old as the race wars of -1812.  The name they now carry was borne unto a young boy of the Krakaria family who died at the age of 9.  Likisir Haliar Krakaria was murdered at the hands of what he thought an injured gypsy to whom he'd blindly run to aid.  The story recorded in the Krakarian Lineage Annals tells that Likisir was a particularly benevolent young boy, who at a very young age began to study the preachings of Aeridin, and had begun his studies entirely towards ends of aiding those sick or weak.  The Krakarian family fully supported this effort, as in his youth, he was the only of their family to ever find the ability to place his hands in these wondrous gloves they had kept for ages, unused.
They knew the gloves to be enchanted with a power of healing, and encouraged his benevolence and capability in curing those ailing.  In this event however, the boy had apparently been alone on the roads outside North Point, and had run to aid a man injured and bleeding on the ground.  The man slew Likisir and robbed him, though found himself unable to pry the beautiful gloves from the young boy's hands.

What is known of these silken gloves is that they are imbued with an incredible healing power, and that the magics that vibrate within will shimmer and vibrate in the presence of any being that is tainted with a malevolent presence.

The magic of these gloves are such that they may never be altered by conventional crafting means.

This is a statue of the elven deity Aeridin, also known as The Healing Light, The Keeper of Life, The Lifegiver, The Caring Light whose dogma is:

Preserve and protect life, the gift to exist is not one to be taken lightly and thus one must lead an exemplary life devoted to benevolence and care. Tend to those who ail, offer your gift of healing to make their stay in the mortal realm a wholesome experience, yet once death has taken its toll, respect the passing and enjoy the fond memories of their life. Do not dwell or mourn for those who pass for too long, death is sadness, but without understanding sorrow one cannot understand happiness.

Promote health and the well-being of the mind and body before anything else. Any extension, transformation, alteration or corruption to the natural forms and shapes of beings is an affront against the sanctity and purity of life and should be confronted at first with gentle lessons and benevolent teaching, and if such ways do not work, with a stern and firm stance instead. Violence is the last option; use it only on those who defy these teachings.

Undeath is the most blatant aberration to the sanctity and purity of life, put them to rest by any means necessary so that their souls may reach their homes. Use the Gift of the Caring Light to bring brightness to the darkest of places, never succumb to its temptations for they only bring a taint upon the spirit.

A dangerously lusty red wine with intoxicating effects, this wine is an essential part of Xeenite celebrations and rituals everywhere. 

The key to making this wine is to use only grapes who's vines scale the walls of temples of Xeen. It is said that the grapes that grow on Xeen's temples already have an intoxicating affect even before being made into wine. 

The recipe for this wine is said to be guarded very closely by Xeen's priestesses themselves, and is rumored to have been stolen by one of the proprietors of the Leilon Arms Inn and Tavern after a very prominent Xeenite festival in Katherian. However, not too many people know how much truth is in this tale. If there is any truth to it, those who know, don't talk about it. Truth or not, everybody benefits from the knowledge of this recipe, as it is the finest wine ever made.

The Basics of Armor Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Armor types - There are 7 basic armor types that a crafter can make. These range from a chain shirt to full plate armor.
 
2. Armor Materials - Armor can be crafted from Bronze, Iron, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt and Mithril. Armor may also be adorned with gold. Adorned armor has a higher AC than regular armor. 

3. Armor Components - Armor requires ingots and a pattern.  

4. Crafting Armor - To craft a set of armor, one must equip a smiths hammer, posess the required raw materials and use an armor crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Armor may be smelted. Smelted armor generally yields two less ingots than were originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tailoring, and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Mining
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

In addition to ore, miners may also mine clay and sand. 

2. Mining Equipment - To mine ore, one must use a pickaxe. Pickaxes require the martial weapon feat, so certain non combat classes will have difficulty mining. A shovel is required to mine clay and sand.

Pickaxes and Shovels are subject to damage while mining and will eventually break. it is advised to acquire a backup pickaxe and shovel prior to attempting mining.

3. Misc. Infomation - Ocassionally, one might get lucky and chip off a second nugget of ore or find a rare gem or other  item. 

4. Related Skills - Smelting, Weapon Crafting, Armor Crafting and Tinkering all use ore, sand and clay byproducts. Please read their respective books for more information about them.
The book of patterns contains a large collection of pattern designs used by tailors and armor crafters to make various pieces of clothing and armor.

The Basics of Smelting
----------------------------------

1. Ore types - There are 10 common ore types found in Layonara. These are Copper, Tin, Iron, Gold, Platinum, Adamantium, Cobalt, Silver, Titanium and Mithril. All may be smelted. Bronze is made by combining Copper and Tin.

2. Smelting Equipment - To smelt ore, one must use a smelting tongs. Ore nuggets are inserted into a smelting forge and melted into ingots. 

3. Related Skills - Weapon Crafting and Armor Crafting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

The Basics of Weapon Crafting
--------------------------------------------------

1. Weapon types - There are 21 basic weapon types that a crafter can make. These range from a simple Dagger to a Greatsword.
 
2. Weapon Materials - Weapons can be crafted from Copper, Bronze and Iron. Weapons may also be coated with Silver and Titanium. Silver coated weapons are more effective against undead foes, while Titanium coated weapons do more damage.

3. Weapon Components - Weapons generally require ingots and a casting mold. Casting molds come in small, medium or large sizes. Some weapons also require wood shafts. 

4. Crafting Weapons - To craft a weapon, one must equip a smiths hammer, posses the required raw materials and use a weapon crafting anvil. 

5. Misc. Information - Weapons that require 2 or more ingots to craft may be smelted. Smelted weapons generally yield one less ingot than what was originally required. 

6. Related Skills - Smelting, Tinkering, Wood Crafting and Enchanting. Please read their respective books for more information about them.

Unlike most leaves, which must be dried for long periods of time before being smoked, Ausir’s Pleasure is best smoked a few hours after clipping. With some effort, though, it can be well preserved and smoked at a later time. It is also best harvested late at night, when the mists from the Forest of Fog coat and soften the stalks. Then the young leaves are simply peeled off the stalk, talking long threads of stalk material with them.

The taste is a sweet and seductive on the palate as a lover’s kiss but this heady mix of earthy and mineral elements hides the more dubious nature of the plant. Ausir’s Pleasure stimulates the mind and body more than any other known leaf. All the euphoria and effects of freshly discovered love and the delights of lovers can be found in the smoking of this leaf but be warned, love is a fickle and the agony or despair of love lost and the pain of rejection are also the possible price of this tempting preparation. It is this convergence of pleasure and pain which has led many Layonarans to think that this plant is a gift from Xeen herself to her followers. To this end it is rumored that a process to extract a purified essence of the leaf exists and this substances is used in the creation of a ritual wine in some Xeenite ceremonies.

Connoisseurs can often be heard giving praises to this smoking leaf.  Other leaves may be sharper, more pungent, with more unusual combinations of tastes, but no other leaf, it's widely held, is as balanced and well rounded as The Great Draw.

This leaf has been used in ranger and druid gatherings for ages, particularly in the Great Forest region.  The leaves are smoked as a central ritual exchange, and in great quantities used as an incense during meditation ceremonies.  Most, however, simply smoke it from a pipe.  

The taste is so smooth, and the smoke is so easy, those who smoke it often do so exclusively and form a strong attachment to it.  That's why it is called The Great Draw, some joke, not only because it is such a great draw from the pipe, but because it is the reason people are drawn to the Great Forest.

As the name suggests, this leaf erupts with a splendid sweetness in one's palate.  The honey taste can actually be overwhelming for some, and because of this is often accompanied by bitter brews.

Learning how to clip the plant properly, and which part to smoke, is challenging and open to fierce debate.  Some believe the lower leaves make the best smoking.  Others argue it is the higher leaves and their stems.  Some think the flower petals themselves should be gently plucked and combined with both types of leaves.

It took a Wolfswood Ranger to first smoke this plant, for no other would dare sink his hand deep into its thorny tentacles to clip off the soft curling leaves.  Though the leaves are soft, the stems are quite stout, and require either a firm grip or special shears to harvest just right.

Often you'll find a Wolfswood Ranger puffing on the Cuts, as they are called, during a break or relaxing after a hard day's patrol.  This sight is seen so often that some say the properties of this leaf are what give the rangers their sharpened senses and alertness.

Unlike most leaves, which must be dried for long periods of time before being smoked, Misty Morning is best smoked a few hours after clipping.  With some effort, though, it can be well preserved and smoked at a later time.  It is also best harvested late at night, when the mists from the Forest of Fog coat and soften the stalks.  Then the young leaves are simply peeled off the stalk, talking long threads of stalk material with them.

The taste is a bit harsh for those who aren't used to it, with considerable earthy and mineral characteristics.  But Misty Morning stimulates the mind and body more than any other known leaf.  This, combined with its nature, makes the Forest of Fog leaf perfect for a morning pipe.  It is this perfect convergence of nature and utility which has led many Layonarans to think that this plant is a gift from Katia herself to her followers of the Forest of Fog and beyond.

Layonara - Crime & Punishment

Law on the continent is primarily governed by a union of good between the Churches of Toran and Rofirein.

Organisation of the Law:

Official senior representatives of the church of Rofirein are responsible for overseeing the interpretation of the law and thus will act as a Judges when criminals are on trial. 
These judges in all cases are considered to have the best knowledge of Rofirein's will and are thus considered divine experts.  A priest of Rofirein is always the final deciding factor if the interpretation of the law is ever in doubt.

Powers Granted too Judges -

1.	Oversee any hearings as required. 
2.	Pass sentence upon the guilty as directed by their divine link to Rofirein. 
3.	Supersede the power of any local governing body in direct relation to interpretation of the law and punishment. 
4.	Revoke the powers of any law enforcer that has shown themselves to be unworthy of these burdens. 
5.	Consult with experts in specific fields as required for use as expert witnesses.  Specifically in the areas of Magic and Magical crime. 

Official senior representatives of the church of Toran (predominantly Paladins) are responsible for carrying out the will of the Judge and enforcing the law. Those chosen shall be known as "Justiciers".  These souls devote their lives too carrying out the duty of Toran and upholding the law.  Wherever possible a "Justicier" will be called upon to carry out all law enforcement in conjunction with local government.  Local law enforcement will relinquish in ALL cases their powers too that of the "Justicier".

Powers Granted too Justiciers - 

1.	Carry out the will of the divine court of Mistone with direct reference to punishment. 
2.	Apprehend any person believed to be guilty of a crime or as directed too by the divine court. 
3.	Where immediate action is required or a representative of Rofirein cannot be contacted carry out sentence and punishment for minor crimes. 
4.	Take control of and direct local authorities where serious crimes are involved or the stability of the continent is in jeopardy.

Local Authorities 

Local authorities are responsible for enforcing the law out with the presence of a Justicier and make up the majority of law enforcers.  These include but are not limited to Royal Guard, Local Guard etc

Individuals

Individuals have the right too -

1.	Petition the divine courts of Mistone for a hearing. 
2.	Petition a "Justicier" to apprehend a suspected criminal. 
3.	Petition the divine courts for a retrial where new evidence is discovered that is directly related to the case. 
4.	Stand as a representative during trial for an individual on trial. 
5.	Attend the court as a witness. 
6.	Receive fair and just judgement and punishment as directed by the divine Rofirein and Toran. 
7.	Appoint a representative to speak on their behalf at a trial. 
8.	Request trial by the divine courts of Mistone where fair trial and punishment is believed to have not been given by local authorities. 
9.	Be safe and secure within their home and owned lands. 
10.	Defend themselves and their property with use of appropriate force if threatened by those out with law enforcement. 
11.	Be innocent until proven guilty. 
12.	Be informed of any changes to the law made by the Churches of Rofirein and Toran.

Anything not covered by these rights will be left to the discretion of the representatives of Rofirein and Toran and assessed on an individual basis.

Crimes and their Punishment by Category

Crimes and their punishments are decided directly by the representative of the church of Rofirein who oversees the trial however the following is a guideline:

Major Crimes (Usually carry sentences of death or imprisonment decided directly by the Judge) 
Murder 

Intermediate Crimes (Do not carry sentences of death but usually prolonged periods of imprisonment or related things) 
Counterfeiting.
Impersonation of a Law enforcement official.
Rape
Theft of large items (repeat offences)
Man slaughter
Adultery

Minor Crimes (Will never carry death sentences and rarely long term prison sentences. More likely community service or rehabilitation at correctional institutes. Time in the stocks, fines, flogging etc)
Theft of minor items (first offence)
Assault
Resisting Arrest
Slander
Worship of unrecognised deities determined to be evil or directly threatening to the continent.

Aliases: The Blessed One, The Protector and Provider

Worshippers: Halflings (normally male) and merchants or shopkeepers of every race.
Domains: Good, Protection, and Travel 
Governs: Trade, Money, Wealth, Luck, Fate, Harmony, Family 

Dogma: 
     Trade is the best road to enlightenment and enrichment. Use trade to bring prosperity to everyone in the world. Seek out and develop new markets and new opportunities. Hone your skills as a tradesman. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Deliar's worshippers favor a short sword, mainly because of its portability and variety of uses. They have also been known to embellish their swords with precious metals and pommel gems to show their wealth and, consequently, Deliar's favor. 

     Clerics of Deliar tend to wear chain mail, adorning it with pricey metals like gold, silver, or mithril. The higher the rank of the cleric, the rarer the metal and the more favored and wealthy they are. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Despite Deliar being a god worshiped by merchants and shopkeepers of all races, the real clergy mostly consists of halflings. Deliar's halfling followers tend to live in small clans, with the elder being the leader, though normally there is little need for any type of leadership because halflings seem to naturally work together.

     Temples are normally tents, for the lives of Deliar's servants are rarely sedentary. Protection for the temples is also easier this way, as they are not in set locations. However, most larger, more prosperous cities have huge, exquisitely decorated temples to Deliar.

     Clerics can be found praying multiple times of the day. They pray for luck before a trade, believing that it brings wealth and harmony to the family.

Welcome to the Wild & Dead Magic Disturbance Tool for GMs.

This tool is used to add a temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone (which is a disturbance in the Al'Noth) to an Area. An Area can only have one Disturbance; the Disturbance affects the entire Area.

A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area which is already a permanent Wild or Dead Magic Zone. A Disturbance cannot be added to an Area marked as a no temporary Wild or Dead Magic Zone Area.

Disturbances do not persist across Module resets.

Adding a Wild or Dead Magic Disturbance will create a Placeable Object for the players to interact with. This allows them to attempt to repair the disturbance in the Al'Noth. Success is dependant upon the player's highest Spellcaster level, their Spellcrafting ability, whether they are a Lucindite or Aragenite, the use of any special (World Leader Reward) Disturbance repairing items, and the difficulty of the Disturbance to be repaired. It should be noted that failure is likely to be fatal.

The Disturbance repair difficulty can be altered any time after the Disturbance has been added to the Area. There are five difficulty settings, ranging from Simple (100% multiplier to the chance of success) to Impossible (0% multiplier to the chance of success).

The Disturbance Object is created 1.5 meters in front of the tool activator, facing the activator.

The Disturbance Object can be created directly from the DM-Client "Creator" (under "Placeable Object/Custom/Visual Effects/Magic Effects"). However, it will need to be conversed with immediately afterwards by the GM to properly attach the Disturbance to the Area. Until then, it is non-functional.

.set / .get / .got functions
----------------------------------------

These allow you to set an NPC to a key like "!", "@", or "#".  Once set you can use them just like using ":" which is the default setting.

EX:   .set % will set the last voice target to %.

You can then use "/dm :text here" for your default NPC or "/dm %" for this character.

.get % - brings this set character to you.
.got % - takes your avatar to that character.

A reference manual for voice commands for players and DMs

There MUST be an NPC, summoned creature, familiar or "voice" within range for these functions to work.  Repeated text is ALWAYS ignored (ie in testing hi, hi, hi)

BASIC VOICE FUNCTIONS:
-----------------------------------------
**structure is /dmSPACE **
The SPACE is mandatory.  The basic structure is to use the DM channel to "hide" the throwing of your voice.  There is NO way to not spam the DM channel.

/dm [your typing here]

will speak your "native" language.  If you have more than one, use the language widgets to determine the language you will be speaking.

/dm ; your text here

Your familiar or companion will say your text.

/dm ,your text here

Your summoned creature will say your text.


*emotes*
--------------
Bracketing text between two * will attempt to perform an emote.  This does NOT need to use the DM channel.  This applies to simple spoken text by the PC.

This will work for DM possessed creatures or for players.  The action will be taken by the speaker.

Two uses:  

1) is for skill checks or ability checks - ie *uses strength to move rock*

2) is for emotes - ie *bows to the leader of the town*

All abilities and all skills (spell them just like the actual skill or ability - ie use magic device)

The precise origins of this amulet are unknown, and as such things go, deeply shrouded in legend, rumor and hearsay.  The most plausable of these rumors is that it was created and worn by a powerful mage who many called the Stormcaller.

He was rumored both to be many things, from a devotee of Mist to a rather eccentric and insane evoker with a fascination with storms.  It was said that any time there was a storm near his home on the eastern shores of Dregar, he could be seen standing in the open at the edge of a cliff in the open, his arms stretched out above him amongst the wind, rain and lightning and seemingly without fear.  Some say he called the storms, while others claimed he simply reveled in their power. Still others say he used his own power to amplify that of the storms. For what purpose he might do any of this, no one knows.

The fate of the Stormcaller is likewise wrapped in supposition and rumor.  It was said that one morning, after a particularly violent midnight storm, his smoking remains were found near the edge of his usual cliff.  All that remained intact was his ever-present amulet, its large central gem replaying scenes of the most violent of storms ever to strike the coasts of Dregar.
In the path of the Storm...

This appears to be a shrine to the goddess Mist. Carved into what was originally an ocean rounded boulder are images of storms and mighty waves smashing against shore and ship. The images seem to depict weak sailors, unworthy of the goddess floundering in the grey depths of the oceans while strong courageous sailors are challenging the sea and storm, bravely navigating their vessels through the challenges Mist lays before them.

A plaque on the bottom of the shrine reads, "May all that kneel here to pay homage to the Lady of the Sea be blessed by the fury of her storm and have her tempest fuel their soul. Dedicated to Muireann for her service to the druids."

The youngest of the dreamers with a mere sixteen years to her name Gali is also considered to be the most promising. The ethereal nature of the dream realms seems to flow from Gali, her form almost becoming ethereal when she engages her talents.  Her eyes tell tales of the mysteries beyond that dreamers are privy to, while her face seems to hold little guile to disguise or hide any such secrets.  Long chestnut hair completes the portrait, framing her flower like face in long waves of red brown highlights. 

  Gali has honest features and an open heart, one that due to her youth has not been subjected to the rigours that many other of the dreamers have faced.  Caring and emotional she tends to act as her feelings dictate, choices made by deep wells of care stored within.  Due to her youth however Gali also lacks the deeper understandings of the mystery, and due to this is often overlooked. Not terribly confident she is constantly seeking assurance from outside herself, looking to others for support.

   Currently served by Syn as holder, both needing to find confidence in themselves as individuals regardless of race or age.  A journey to take together.

A small active young elf just barely into her adulthood, Ulathia displays the intense curiosity so apparent to the new adult.  Slim and boyish she is rarely walking when she can be running, rarely on the ground when she can be climbing trees, rarely doing nothing if she can be doing anything else.  Sun browned arms and legs poke constantly from mismatched clothes as she tumbles her way through life, every day a new  experience that she seems to relish to the very limits of her being.

    Yet if one were to peer closely into the green glades that are her eyes, an intense fear can be found.  The past and abuse of her gifts left its mark, marks evident in the fear that can be seen to dominate her demeanor and everyday behavior. Her rush to live life to the fullest driven clearly by the fear of it ending before she has experienced all, the joy in each moment robbed by the terror of losing something yet to be known.

  Currently served by Hargranar Craggenhilt as holder, the dwarves sage wisdom showing he can guide this young dreamer to further understanding as she recklessly walks the path of life.

Folian S'pae

Aliases: The Longstrider, Prince of Wolves  
Race: Wood Elf 
Alignment: NG 
Worshippers:  Wood Elves, though many rangers of various races also follow Folian. 
Domains:  Animal, Good, Plant, Sun.      Most Popular are Animal, Plant
Governs: Animals, forests 

Dogma: 
     Be one with the forests and live in harmony with nature's creatures. Take no more than you need and give as much as you can in return. 

Clergy Favored Weapons and Clothing: 
     Those who follow Folian are very skilled archers. Some even go so far as to make bows their sole weapon. Long swords, scimitars, and rapiers are the chosen blades of Folian's followers, but clubs and staves are common due to the wood from which the weapon was created. Most who use clubs, staves, or bows make their own or have it handed down to them. Folian approves of those resourceful enough to carve - often literally - their weapons out of what nature gives them.

     Leather armors are the primary garb of Folian's clerics, though lighter metal suits are used to some extent. Armors are dyed in greens and browns. Clerics of Folian will never don a full suit of armor, which, cumbersome and heavy, prevents them from feeling the connection to the lands they are sworn to protect. 

Clergy and Temples:
     Due to the highly individualistic nature of Folian himself, there is no structured Church of Folian. The majority of followers have been rangers at some point in their lives before turning to the more settled life of a cleric. Clerics usually maintain their link to the forests, not moving to cities or villages.
     Because of this, temples of Folian are always found in or near to wooded areas. Some of the oldest known places of worship are inside humongous trees, veritable living temples of nature.

     Clerics of Folian have no set time of day to pray for power and guidance, nor do they pray every single day. They pray when needed and as often as needed, no more, no less. They do, however, prefer to be close to nature when the need for prayer arises, often choosing to stop and pray in a grove of trees rather than inside the walls of town.
     Spring is significant to Folian's worshippers, for the woods and their inhabitants typically wake from their long winter's slumber to start life anew at this time of year.

Prayers: 
     "Longstrider, guide my steps. Help me to defend and serve the wood and those within."
A common goodbye: 
     "May The Prince of Wolves watch over you."

A hand-written book of anecdotes and entertaining stories to pass the time...

-----

Sir Wilber was a lesser known knight of Rofirein, but he was an accomplished furniture maker. His latest creation was a magnificient armoire which he had covered with pure silver plate. When the piece was all polished up, it shone like nothing anyone had ever seen.

The young Rofirenite hero was not ready to settle down yet, but Gracie, his girl, wanted to get married right away. She had become tired of waiting and decided to go to Wilber and pop the question herself. When Wilber saw the woman coming, he jumped into the armoire to hide.

Gracie entered Wilber's quarters and looked around. She didn't see anybody and turned to leave. Suddenly Wilber sneezed. Gracie ran to the armoire and flung the door open. there stood Wilber: he was trapped!

The next day, the castle newsletter's headline proclaimed: "Lady Gracie Finds Her Knight In Shining Armoire!" 

-----

A knight and his men return to their castle after a long hard day of fighting.

How are we faring? asks the king.

Sire, replies the knight, I have been robbing and pillaging on your behalf all day, burning the towns of your enemies in the west.

What?! shrieks the king. I don’t have any enemies to the west!

Oh! exclaimed the embarassed knight. Well, you do now...

------

There were three kingdoms on the shores of a lake. There was an island in the middle of the lake, which the kingdoms had been fighting over for years. Finally, the three kings decided that they would send their knights out to do battle, and the winner would take the island.

The night before the battle, the knights and their squires pitched camp and readied themselves for the fight. The first kingdom had twelve knights, and each knight had five squires, all of whom were busily polishing armor, brushing horses, and cooking food. The second kingdom had twenty knights, and each knight had ten squires. Everyone at that camp was also busy preparing for battle. At the camp of the third kingdom, there was only one knight, with his squire. This squire took a large pot and hung it from a looped rope in a tall tree. He busied himself preparing the meal, while the knight polished his own armor.

When the hour of the battle came, the three kingdoms sent their squires out to fight (this was too trivial a matter for the knights to join in). The battle raged, and when the dust cleared, the only person left was the lone squire from the third kingdom, having defeated the squires from the other two kingdoms.

I guess this just proves that the squire of the high pot and noose is equal to the sum of the squires of the other two sides.

Begin by rolling the appropriate die to determine the starting player. Lowest number rolls first. The person holding the dice is called the Caster.

The caster specifies a number between 5 and 9 inclusive; this is the Main.

The caster places his bet that he will roll the Main.

The caster rolls two six-sided dice one at a time. If the caster rolls:

-the Main, he wins his bet and an amount equal to it.

-a 2 or a 3, he loses his bet; dice pass to next player.

-an 11 or 12, the result depends on the Main:

-if the Main was a 5 or 9, caster loses bet;

-if the Main was a 6 or 8, caster loses on an 11 and wins on a 12;

-if the Main was a 7, caster wins with 11 and loses on a 12.


Quick Reference:


Main is 5: Win on a 5, lose on a 2, 3, 11, or 12

Main is 6: Win on 6 or 12, lose on 2, 3, 11

Main is 7: Win on 7 or 11, lose on 2, 3, 12

Main is 8: Win on 8 or 12, lose on 2, 3, 11

Main is 9: Win on 9, lose on 2, 3, 11, 12


If the caster neither wins or loses, the number thrown is called the Chance and the caster throws again:

-if the caster rolls the Chance they win;

-if the caster rolls the Main they lose;

If neither the Chance or Main are rolled, caster rolls until either the Chance or Main is rolled and in addition:

-a 2 always loses

-if 11 or 12 are rolled, consult rules above to determine win or lose

Tournament and Betting:

Bets are placed between the caster, audience and the House. Audience may bet that the caster will win or lose. The caster may only bet that they’ll win.

In the event the caster does not win or lose, additional bets can be placed by the audience that the caster will either win or lose. A bettor cannot bet both win and lose in the same betting round.

In tournaments, the House collects the True and backs bets one to one.

Tall and slender with soft green eyes and blond hair, Violet is a picture of elven beauty. Her gestures are graceful though unmeasured, her emotions visible in many a spontaneous outburst.  As she moves you can clearly see the subtle grace that is inherent to her form, every line a picture of fluidity in motion.  Flawless alabaster skin finishes her figure, heated only by the warmth of her nature.

    As her eyes meet with yours you can clearly see defiance and honestly linked with a depth of compassion and care that is rarely seen.  Within the depths of green dwells what many would see as the final mystery of the dream, the realms of hope and and an eternity, of wishes come true swimming among emerald currents.
  
    Originally thought to be the last of her kind, Violet now leads the Dreamers, in a hope that the future will be kinder to her and hers than the past.

"These boots were made by the gnomish inventor Yolanda Shinstepp. She loved to go dancing and found that the larger people at the Tavern would knock her around while on the dance floor. She could not make people watch out for the little folks, so she got to working on an item that would improve her dancing and keep her from being knocked around.
