Gnomes
    Gnomes are extremely intelligent and also very sought after as inventors and engineers of the highest order. They prefer to remain with their own kin, although they are also at home with dwarves (whom they are distantly related to). They are renowned for both their technical expertise and their prankish nature, though their pranks and jokes can make them hard to get along with. Gnomes are even smaller than dwarves, with the average gnome standing at about 3 feet in height. However, they have a light frame and small muscles, giving them an average weight of 45 pounds. Like many other races, gnomes have a great longevity with an average life expectancy of 340 years, though some live much longer. They share the Dwarven pride in facial hair, though gnomes prefer to have a trimmed beard compared to the long bushy ones of the dwarves. The gnomes relate well with the Dwarven and halfling races and the three get on well together. The gnomes' varied skills make them capable adventurers and their curiosity usually leads them on adventures to learn more about the world.

Deep Gnomes (Sverfneblin)
    Deep Gnomes, also called svirfneblin in their own language, are not much like their cousins on the surface. They're a gruff lot and very suspicious of other races; for good reason, as they've been betrayed or waged war upon numerous times by the other races that dwell in the Underdark, They are very good miners and gemcrafters and their jewelry are prized possessions, both in the Underdark and on the surface.

Personality: 
    Deep Gnomes are distrustful, and treat every stranger as possible enemy. However, once they've given their trust, they're loyal allies. They are not a passionate people unless it comes to gems and jewelry. They love metalwork, even more if it is made to bear gems, especially crowns, necklaces or rings. They're expert crafters and don't do half-jobs, since their culture is infused with a perfectionism and respect for the work.

Physical Description: 
    Deep Gnomes are no taller than 3 or 4 feet and have grayish skin, camouflaging them against the subterranean rocks. Their eyes are black or dark gray. Males are nearly always completely bald, but if they do have hair it's more like white patches. Females usually do have hair, which also tends to be pure white.
During the ages they've lived below ground they've grown very ugly in the eyes of other races.

Relations with other races: 
    Deep Gnomes do not trust other races, and they rarely ally themselves with anyone, preferring to remain neutral and outside of every conflict. However, the drow hunt them with a passion, so conflict cannot always be avoided. With the guidance of their goddess however, they manage to stay hidden very well. This guidance, together with the strange magics of the Underdark have given the Svirfneblin some unique powers of hiding and resiting magic.

Alignment: 
    Usually neutral good

Religion: 
    Deep Gnomes worship the goddess Beryl, who shares their passion for gems.

Language: 
    Common, Undercommon, Gnomish

Names: 
    Names often have to do with gems. Common surnames are Gemcutter or Opalcarver. First names are a lot shorter than the names of their surface cousins.

Adventurers: 
    Deep Gnome adventurers are not very common as they do not like to deal with other races. The occasional Svirfneblin that does leave his home settlement is usually a bold merchant.


Forest Gnomes
    This subrace of gnomes is not so common as the others, but its members fill an important niche in their environment. Forest gnomes are shy and reclusive, and often the mere arrival of human settlers within their wooded domain is enough to send them migrating to a new, unspoiled home. Nevertheless, they have been known to aid adventurers from other races and fight monsters invading the forests they inhabit. 

Personality: 
    Forest gnomes prefer a life in which no one knows who they are or where they live. They dwell in large swaths of woodland, and - unlike the other gnomish subraces - prefer to dwell in houses that are at least partially above ground. They are creatures of nature far more than any of their cousins, and to those rare folks who meet them they can prove to be steadfast allies and delightful companions. 

    However, forest gnomes have not totally abandoned the love of gemstones that is so inherent to all gnomes. The emerald is the favored gem of the forest gnomes, no doubt because it most accurately reflects the healthy green of their verdant homelands. While these gnomes can make excellent gemsmiths and jewelers, their work tends to be reverent images of the flora and fauna that are such a key part of their environment. 

Physical description: 
    The tiny forest gnomes are the smallest of the gnomish subraces. They share the stocky physique of the rock gnomes and the bulbous nose which is so characteristic of the race in general. They are the only gnomes inclined to wear long beards and hair. 

    The skin of a Forest Gnome tends toward a greenish cast of tan, rather like bark. Their eyes are generally brown or blue, but green eyes are not unheard of. Their hair color is usually brown, often becoming gray or white in old age. 

Relations with other races: 
    Forest gnomes prefer to live alone without contact to other races. They are friends with the elves who cohabit the forests. They hate orcs, goblins, and lizardmen and tend to attack these races which often invade the forest gnomes' homes. 

Alignment: 
    Usually true neutral 

Religion:
    Forest gnomes often worship nature gods such as Katia and Aeridin. 

Language: 
    Common, Gnome 

Names: 
    Forest gnome names are similiar to other gnomes with the exception that their surnames often including something nature-related. For example: Male: Burgell, Dorag. Female: Lyiss, Jaree. Surnames: Redtree, Greatleaf. 

Adventurers: 
    Forest Gnome adventurers are extremely rare, even more so than the race. The reason for one to adventure outside the forests they live in would have to be a very special one.

Blackfeather Mountains
    The Blackfeather Mountains sit just north of the Forest of Fog. Years ago the Broken Glade Giants drove out the hordes of crows that settled in the eastern parts of the forest. No one is sure why the crows were there or why the Giants drove them out, but after they flapped wildly around the forest for a week or so they came to rest on the mountains just to the north. If you walk through one of the long abandoned dwarf trails through these peaks you'll find layers of crow's feathers at your feet. Despite the slippery footing, it is still worth the treacherous walk. The views of the forest, desert and ocean from even the lower ranges are breathtaking.

Black Hills
    When you are in the Black Hills you'll know it. The soil here is jet black and seems to radiate an unnatural darkness. Even on a cloudless summer's noon, the hills seem dimmed. These dark, foreboding mounds can be seen from a distance. Most people are thankful for this, as they become easier to avoid. Despite the many roads which wind their way through these hills, travelers are seldom seen.
    If you do venture to the Black Hills, and climb as high as you can go, you'll find an area known as Hangman's Bluff. Not too long ago Zoroon's Castle faced a major uprising from the peasants in the countryside. Zoroon was a reasonable and respected leader. But his son and even more so his grandson were powermongers, bent on economic exploitation for personal gain. When the peasants could no longer tolerate the squalor and servitude which had ground them to near death, they took up arms and attacked the taskmasters and tribute collectors of Zoroon III. They were quickly suppressed and many were captured. A line of their emaciated forms stretched up the slopes of the tallest Black Hill bluff. On the top, they were hung, one after the other, for three days straight. Many watched. Most cried and the word went out about the intolerable injustice being done in this central Dregar province. It didn't take long for people from the city of Dresden and the Forest of Fog to rally to their cause. Zoroon III was overthrown soon after. The castle now stands nearly abandoned, certainly not the political figure it had once been.
Some residents of the central Dregar area trace the dark dirt and dimness of the Black Hills to this event. They argue that the hundreds of souls tortured and ripped from their body spread a pungent lament across the landscape. A few priests of Prantz were recently sent to investigate this phenomenon. They didn't get far with the research, however, as they were run off by a camp of bugbears from the Eternal Flame clan. These elite agents of Bloodstone's evil machinations find the twisted and miserable conditions of the Black Hills quite welcoming. Since few people ever visit this woeful area, the bugbears were left to assemble numbers enough to best the Prantz guards sent to deal with the situation.

Cave of the Snake
     The Cave of the Snake lies somewhere in the southern Viper's Teeth. Those few who have spelunked in this cave report that there are indeed large snakes in the depths. However, the upper layers are filled with Blood's Eternal Flame bugbears. There are reports of snake paintings on the walls of the upper levels and that the Eternal Flames, in any region, have shed snake skins wrapped around the handles of their weapons. This leads some bugbear experts to the conclusion that the Eternal Flame bugbears are a snake worshipping cult, and that this cave has central significance for their organization.

Corax Lake
    Every year, on the spring equinox, the people of Southern Dregar and the Prantz area gather at Corax Lake for a festival. Joyous music and wild dancing ripple the surface of this unusually calm lake. People come in large groups to avoid the danger on the roads, quickly swelling the crowds at the lake to huge proportions. 
    The main event at the festival is the Corax Dive. When the Dive is about to begin, the crowd gathers around the lake and watches a small boat paddle out to the center. From the boat several long strands of woven rope with a large bright yellow rock tied to the end are lowered into the water. Along the rope are small detachable pouches of leather which are sealed off to float and suspend the rope. These pouches are painted particular colors at different lengths of the rope. The music changes from the festival tunes and resonates with the dangerous acts about to be performed. The divers then swim to the middle of the lake and when the whistle is blown their feet fly into the air and then disappear into the depths. The winner is the diver who can bring the deepest leather pouch to the surface.
    The excitement of the contest is heightened by the sheer depth of the lake. In some places, it is said, there is no bottom. Every few years one of the ropes goes missing, supposedly pulled by the yellow rock down into an eternal depth. The lake used to be called Deep Lake until Corax came along and stunned everyone with his diving ability. The half-orc barbarian dove swiftly to the bottom of one of the ropes and after an amazingly long time holding his breath emerged near the shore with the yellow rock rather than one of the leather pouches. The crowd was whipped into jubilation. After that day, people began to call the lake Corax Lake. In recent years the surveyors in Prantz have made this name more official, giving the lake dual nomenclature.
    Corax's dive was hundreds of years ago. Since then no-one has come closer than 10 pouches away from the yellow stone. This fact has made people grow increasingly suspicious about Corax's feat and the nature of the lake.

Dalos Lake
    Dalos Lake is named for a mid-kingdom prince who used to daydream here. He spent such an inordinate amount of time at the banks of its calm and soothing waters that his father sent spies to monitor his activities there. That same trip, a giant snatched up the prince into his huge arms and lumbered away faster than they could follow. When the king learned of this he sent a brigade of his finest after his son's kidnapper. Many giants died in the pursuit and a few horsemen fell as well. When they reached the cave where his son was, they attacked the giant before surveying the situation. Nearly all involved died:  most of the brigade, over 50 giants, the son, and the kidnapping giant. With his cracked skull held in the firm arms of a Prantz guard, the prince whispered that the giant was a friend, not a kidnapper, and he cursed his father for his meddling. 
    In commemoration of the wicked event, the king and the giant's ruler agreed to designate Dalos Lake as neutral ground. No skirmishes should be fought there between the giants and the Prantz guards, but often are anyway. Beyond the lake the two great powers clash with fervent hatred and a skewed battle cry, both of which are rooted in that fateful series of events.

Sinister Forest
    The Sinister Forest is naturally dark. Black oaks create much of the dense canopy and the soil is a rich brown color. As if drawn by the name of this forest, a few hundred years ago something turned the essence of this forest figuratively dark as well. Many adventurers have sought the cause of this darkness, but they have only ever found its effects. These effects include dark spiders and dark treants, locally twisted and powerful varieties of spiders and treants. Rumors abound of a particularly deadly spider deep in the swamps at the northern rim of the forest. The forest has also become overrun by black snakes and shadow trolls, who have established some sort of complex organization and cave system just south of the forest.
    Those who have studied the forest believe that the whole area was cursed by an evil cleric long ago. Some believe that it happened while the drow concealed themselves in these forests to launch attacks upon Prantz. They used the dense tree cover and unnatural darkness to conceal their dark deeds and shade their red eyes. Others think the timing is off, and that the forest was tainted a few decades before the drow arrived. They suggest that there is some unholy force which continues to flow into the River of Darkness and is then absorbed into the dark soil. The likely source of this unholy contamination is the crypts which are concealed by the dense forest growth. None, however, have delved more than a few hundred yards into the overwhelmingly evil Mosscrypt, so named for its mossy opening and entryway.

Darkland Mountains
    The Darkland Mountains to the north of the Great Rift seem to siphon some of its negative energy into the area, absorbing it into the unsettled earth. Things seem to change quickly and radically in the Darkland Mountains, as if some great force rearranges the whole range every day. This, of course, makes it impossible to have predictable routes through the range and makes it easy to get lost and cornered. The changes may be due to the forces from the Great Rift themselves, or they may be wrought at the hands of the Great Rift Giants who have migrated to this area. These massive and powerful creatures have been seen carrying boulders the size of houses. They may indeed have the collective strength to move the whole mountain, as it is suggested they do. Still, what purpose they have in doing so remains another of Dregar's great mysteries.

Deadman's Pass
    Deadman's Pass is the only road through the central ranges of Dregar if you are not on foot and well prepared. The pass separates the Spine and Viper's Teeth. At one point Prantz protected the pass with intense vigilance. Deadman's Pass is the place that the "True Line," that started with Raklin Loenar as first Emperor in Prantz, ended. The fifth ruler in that family line was slain by a guard that protected him in this pass, and to this day you can still see his grave.
    Now, however, since the Sinister Forest just west of the pass has grown even darker and fewer people use the pass for legitimate travel, Prantz has let its vigilance slip. Every once in a while you can hear someone in the capital crying out from the steps or a crate about what should be done about this crucial road. They have a point, as scouts have reported that the powerful forces of Blood have set up camp there and perform aggressive fundraising for their evil cause. "Didn't we learn anything from the Drow attacks?  A whole army can come through that pass and down through the Sinister Forest!" The paranoid crier's warning spreads throughout the city, but the King's attention seems drawn elsewhere.

Wandering Dunes-Great Desert
    The rain shadow of the Backbone Mountains creates this expansive desert. It is so expansive that those desert druids and oasis dwellers have distinguished between three desert zones. There is the high mesa region, which is home to the Oasis giants. There is the deep valley desert in the northern areas, where scorpions and vipers are said to roam. There are also the dunes and sandstorm deserts, which are whipped into their wild forms by the eastern coastal gusts. There you can find armies of ants and formians, creatures whose sturdy exoskeletons protect them from the blasting sandstorms. These creatures have dwelled in the desert as long as anyone can remember. Their presence is simply natural for those who live in the Wandering Dunes.
    This desert is nicknamed the Wandering Dunes for one reason: huge sections of the desert seem to drift around. When they drift, they pull open great chasms and cause deep sinkholes. The shifting and churning desert has swallowed whole villages. The tips of their ruined abodes reach out from the sand as if in a last gasp for recognition. There are a few stable areas, though predictably, they tend to be home for the desert dwellers mentioned above and thus are the most dangerous.

Wandering Dunes Caves
    Beneath the Great Desert are the Wandering Dunes Caves. These caves stretch in all directions underneath the great desert. Some believe the caves even open up in the Backbone Mountains and Forest of Fog, but those routes are unlikely to be found and impossible to remain, because the same churning which pulls the desert around in maddening directions is also what gives form to these caverns. New caverns open and old ones fold in on themselves every day. This makes the Wandering Dunes Caves a risky but exciting venture for many dwarves and gnomes who seek the mineral treasures uncovered by the churning caverns.
Some treasure hunters also seek the great lost city of Great Desert. This city, the jewel of Dregar in the years before the great Cataclysm, is said to have fallen deep into the earth when the Cataclysm tore the desert into the huge chunks which slide around today. Treasure hunters boast that the vaults of this ancient city would hold riches beyond belief, and whoever finds them will surely be wealthy - and famous - all the days of her or his life.
    Only the mad or ridiculously brave will even set one foot into these caves to attempt to find the treasure or chip a few minerals. Oasis Giants block almost every stable passage in these caverns. And if those who delve deep enough, like few fateful parties have done, encounter one of Layonara's most feared beasts. The locals call her the Long Storm, a dragon whose very sight sends most people into a heart wrenching panic. The Long Storm emerges from the desert cave to torment Audira and other hamlets near the desert from time to time. Mostly she bursts in a huge cloud of sand from the smooth desert floor right at the beginning of a great sand storm and desert quake. It is unknown whether she causes them or knows they are about to happen and leaves the earth temporarily for the safe yet exposed sky. Either demonstrates her awesome power.

Forest Giant Cave
    Within the Forest of Fog there is a cave which seems to serve as the central settlement of the Broken Glade Giants. Their chief lives with his elite guard and many other giants among the amazing natural vaults and stalagmites and stalactites that form great pillars. When Prantz comes on their frequent giant raids, the Broken Gladers pull back into the caves and defend the entrance. With great might and amazing numbers, the Broken Gladers fight back the attack and then begin to plan, in the messy giant way, for their counter-raid on Prantz and surrounding environs.

Forest of Fog
    One of the largest and oldest forests of Layonara, the Forest of Fog is also one of the most mysterious. It is said that more rangers and druids live in this forest than any other in Layonara. Despite this, Bloodstone's bugbears find footholds in the wooded valleys and barren bluffs, from which they strike out with their brutal raiding parties. The bugbears simply appear in the forest, despite the patrols established to track their movements and keep them out. 
    The Broken Glade giants live in these woods as well and they are no less a mystery than the suspicious movements of the bugbears. The giants lived in, and some argue tended, the forest for many years before Bloodstone's return. In recent years, however, the Broken Glade giants are being designated by officials in Prantz as enemies and allies of Blood. These officials assert this forcefully and seem unwilling to entertain other reasoning about the giants, despite the attempts by a group of rangers to portray the situation differently. Conflict has increased and aggressive maneuvers by both the Broken Gladers and the Prantz guard have been witnessed. The Rangers of the Glade, as they have come to be known, assert that the aggression on the part of the giants is a response to the actions of Prantz. Prantz, and most Dregarians, view the increased hostility as an effect of Blood's influence over these weak-minded behemoths.
    As for the forest itself, what makes it mysterious and spectacular are the unexplainable mists which sweep across the forest unpredictably and without warning. Many travelers have found themselves far off course when the thick layer of mist blanketed the forest floor. Every year some go missing, even those traveling together in the same caravan. Mothers, husbands, guards, or companions either wander wildly to their peril or are abducted somehow by the mist itself. Those who live in the forest have far less trouble as they know to wait the mist out or use the trees, which jut gracefully from the mist, as markers and guides. Occasionally, however, a ranger disappears as well.
    Many adventurers have sought the source of this mist. Some say it is a lake. Many argue it pours from the mouth of a cave. Others believe the mist is the breath of the trees or Katia herself.

Great Plains of Dregar
    Dregar's Great Plains stretch from the east to the west coast beneath the northern mountain ranges. Silt carried down from the mountain run-off makes the plains extraordinarily fertile. Those who live there, particularly in the rolling hills region, boast that the Great Plains of Dregar has the best soil and produce in all of Layonara. The plains are also subject to frequent flooding. Scholars have spent countless hours trying to apply a schedule to the flooding, but to no avail. To some this is a sign of malevolent machination; to others, it is a sign of nature's mystery.

Great Rift
    It seems like the land in this area was grabbed in both hands by a god and ripped apart, leaving a huge gouge and jagged landscape. Every step through the surface area of the rift is laborious and treacherous. The Great Rift Giants, which dwell on the plateaus on the surface and in surrounding areas, attack on sight. These giants are tall even among giants, and have displayed exceptional visual acuity in hunting the large grey-backed armadillos that superbly blend into the craggy grey rocks. Their height and sharp vision means they can see intruders coming a long way off. These giants, it is argued by scholars in Prantz, are stone giants who have been transformed by the energy wafting out of the cracks in the violent landscape here. The Bloody Stump giants, as they are called for their unusual constitution, are able to withstand (and sometimes even regenerate limbs lost from) dismembering blows, and are regarded as a more intense version of their surface cousins.
    Besides all the chasms and cracks, there is also a cave opening somewhere in the Great Rift. No one knows for sure what creatures dwell in the unending depths of the Rift itself, but tales concoct the vilest creatures imaginable. Wafting from this cave mouth is an intense negative energy. It sweeps across and transforms the whole area. Few have stood at its opening and lived to tell about it. Those few who have, always returned somehow transformed, turned wicked. A royal survey crew, accompanied by the King's best knights, was lost at this cave opening. One of the knights was seen a few months later wearing jet black armor and singlehandedly sacking the whole town of North Fort. Since then, the Rift has been officially designated as off limits by the crown.     Those wishing to venture there are asked to speak to the King's advisors to establish a formal team.

Ore Hills
    The high iron content in the soil here gives the hills a brilliant red color. Children's stories of the region, however, attribute the red soil to the countless who have spilled blood in ogre raids. Needless to say, ogres are feared in the area. Since the local farmers stay far from the ogre cave in the Ore Hills, the ogres have, for the most part, let the farmers be.

O'Taogor
    Some of the mightiest trolls known in Layonara live in this cave system. It seems that they were drawn here by the expansive caverns and the underground lake. These Trolls are so fierce that those who have faced them insist that their power must have been gifted from Bloodstone or one of the evil gods. Their community seems nearly entirely underground and they seldom venture from the cave mouth. Despite this, many believe that the day will come when Blood or some other wicked force will whisk their masses into action. As such, the entrance along the River of Darkness is always under hidden surveillance and a system of messengers can relay an alarm quickly to Prantz and nearby towns if the need arises.

River of Darkness
    This river either picks up its negative energy as it passes through the Sinister Forest or is itself the source of that negative energy as its water is absorbed by the dark flora. In either case, the river draws dark creatures to it, whether in the forest or as it emerges from the forest and spills into the northernmost regions of the Southern Plains. Malar panthers, vampires, and black snakes all find the banks of this river a welcoming abode. There is also a temple of Baraeon Ca'Duz somewhere near one of the stagnant back-current pools. Those who know about this temple are up in arms about it. There have been many petitions to the king to do something about it and many Dregarians have tried to take matters into their own hands, with little success. Those who live near the Sinister Forest blame the temple for the proliferation of the spiders which sneak into their village and steal away loved ones at night. The priests of the temple insist that they are just there to study and pay respects to the great spiders of the Black Forest region.

Rolling Hills
    The Rolling Hills are in the central region of the Great Dregar Plains. Even though they don't reach very high, they can be seen for miles around on the flat farmlands. The sudden rise of these gentle bluffs spawned all sorts of mythologies and gives the hills a spiritual presence in the lives of the nearby farmers. 
    Many halflings have settled in these comfortable hills. Recently, the human farmers down in the nearby farm plains have begun to call the halflings' land rights into question. The hills, according to the human agriculturalists, were left undeveloped for a specific reason. They were used as funerary mounds for many generations of their ancestors. As the halflings dig their homes into the hills, they claim, they are desecrating not simply graves and memories, but the connection each human farmer has with her and his ancestors. The halfing newcomers refuse to leave, claiming traditional halfling land-use customs. Dregar has sent mediators to the area to try to work something out. The talks are heated, but no violence has erupted between the two groups yet.

Viper's Teeth
    These mountains are named more for the treacherous, serpentine paths and poisonous plants than any overwhelming presence of snakes or serpent-like creatures. Reports from mountain scouts suggest that there are also bugbears holed up in many of the remote valleys. Despite these trials and dangers, the Viper's Teeth are simply sublime and draw nature lovers and adventurers throughout Layonara to behold the expansive vistas, gently tumbling waterfalls and myriad species of trees.

Singing Woods
    The amazing thing about the Singing Woods is that it actually does sing. Those residents of northern Dregar who can afford to often make treks to this forest for purposes of spiritual rejuvenation or respite from their arduous daily existence. It has long been a debate whether the gentle song of this sublime forest is magical or if it emerges out of the unplanned and un-conducted confluence of the various forest sounds. Scholars of Katia who argue the latter also believe that the forest here, because of this emergent symphonic organization, has taken on a kind of aggregate identity. In other words, many who have studied the forest say that it is alive and self-aware in a way unlike any other forest in Layonara. If you visit, expect to be asked to leave after a very short stay if you aren't willing to merge with the forest and surrender your autonomy to its supra-individual agency.
Within this forest there are ancient ruins. Some of them seem to crumble more rapidly under the sway of the forest's singing, while others seem almost animated by it. There is one ruin that somehow seems to manage both. Every once in a while a creature enters the forest and finds the singing to be hideous and piercing. They scramble about, searching frantically for a way to make the sound stop. When this happens, northerners say, they almost always find themselves at the entrance to one of the ancient ruins. And as they step through the threshold they are transformed and lost from sight. Because of this, northerners call them the Ruins of Madness and have long spread the word to avoid it at all costs.

Southern Plains
    These plains run between the west coast of Dregar and the Forest of Fog. Depending on who you ask, the whole southern tip of Dregar may be considered a part of these broad, windswept grasslands. For many years, these plains were wild and left uncivilized by the power of Prantz, which was distracted by other dark deeds at the time. Since the horsemen rode though and established control at Lor, the plains have become uniquely peaceful and settled. Blood's armies seem to gather elsewhere and direct their attention to other targets. As this information spreads more and more people seem to be traveling south. Many new settlements have sprung up across the Southern Plains and the established cities in the plains are finding themselves faced with a population issue.

Backbone Mountains
    The Backbone Mountains are like the backbone of Dregar, jutting out from its earthy flesh as they run long-ways down the continent. Dregar mythology portrays these mountains as the spine of one of the original dragons who lay down in the ocean near the beginning of time to create the central region of Layonara. The tremors which send avalanches of snow and rock down upon the lower regions occasionally remind people of their indebtedness to this dragon. Those who actively assert this idea, rather than just live with it as a dead tradition, explain all of Dregar's natural and magical activity in terms of this dragon. They also believe that one day the dragon will shake the soil from its scales and rise into the heavens again. Then it will shrug off the arrogant non-believers to drown in the ocean while gathering the faithful to its bosom as it flies toward the stars.

Mountains of Storms
    As the name suggests, the Mountains of Storms are thrashed nearly every day of the year with violent storms. Only the most resilient barbarians lived here for centuries. These barbarians, also known as scryers, eventually acclimated and adapted to their environment. One peculiar feature of these barbarians is their massive lungs and amplifying voice box. They are said to be able to hurl a battle cry through a thundering storm with far better range and force than any other barbarian standing on a sunny field.
    The Storm Horn barbarians, however, have not been seen in the Mountains of Storms for ages. It seems that they were forced from their homeland by an invasion of Bleeding Rock Giants supposedly delivered to the Strong Horn's door by none other than Sinthar Bloodstone. This, according to historians, is one of the first things Blood did when he returned, indicating either some crucial significance to the area or a grudge against these barbarians. Every Storm Horn, however, vows at the age of manhood to strive every day toward reclaiming their precious homeland. 

Triera Mountains and the Thunder Peaks
    There is much exposed granite in these areas. Stone giants who moved here ages ago build simple structures out of it. For many years these giants smashed and shaped the granite by hand. Either by some process of natural changes - or as a gift from Grannoch as the giants themselves claim - they have developed extraordinarily large hands with sharp knuckles that can strike a rock like the most powerful pick ever made by man or dwarf. A passing half Deep Grove giant observed these giants smashing whole granite shelves into crude blocks and was awestruck. Triera worked his way into the giant's community and began to show them how to be more precise with their stone smashing. Triera spent many years in the late 12th century selling these blocks to castles and cities throughout Dregar. He named these giants the Granite Fists and he was said to have badly exploited them. When his life drew towards its end, Triera felt remorse for this exploitation, the people of northern Dregar assert. Because of this he bought the whole range of mountains, which was really only a few parcels he didn't already own, and gifted it to the giants. 
    A recent fire in the Prantz hall of records, however, has conveniently destroyed any documentation that the Granite Fists are the rightful owner of their granite ranges. No one really recognizes giants as true owners of land in Dregar anyway. Adventurous stonemasons now gingerly tread into the Triera mountains in search of good granite slabs to export to growing cities. Conflicts, as you might expect, have begun to flare, making this a particularly hot and contested region of Dregar. Many of the Granite Fists have now migrated to the neighboring Thunder Peaks.

Saddleback Mountain
    At one point in Dregar's history there were trolls throughout the northeastern region. Giants and encroaching human development pushed them far into the mountains, toward the coast. For ages they have lived there in nearly complete isolation. Because of this, they have become their own sub-species of troll. The mountain which most of them call home grants these trolls its nomenclature: they are called the Saddleback Mountain Trolls.
The ocean views from Saddleback Mountain are breathtaking. Word of Saddleback Mountain's snowy beauty has tumbled down the slope to nearby human settlements and explorers have begun to carve trails through the ranges to this rare coastal peak. As more and more explorers and winter wonderland seekers make their way to Saddleback Mountain, organizations bent on the eradication of the Saddleback Mountain Trolls become more populous and outspoken.

Dark Elves 

    The Dark Elves, The Drow, Those Below, Those Who Have Turned to Evil, The Accursed. These are the names given by surfacers to the obsidian-skinned elves who dwell in Underdark cities. Mysterious, elegant, dark and deadly, they are feared and hated by all the races of Layonara. They are masters of magic and treachery, trusted by none, not even each other.

    When Dark Elves come to the surface to raid, they come at night, and every child of Layonara has heard the whispered tales of the Dark Ones even before they have been officially warned of Those Below.

    Ages past, Dark Elves were already known to be a proud and warlike race, attacking their neighbors for power and wealth, or other, more insidious gains. However, after The Betrayal by the other Elven Clans around the year -2311, they were led below ground by a Dark Elven hero, Baraeon Ca'duz. With the help of Pyrtechon, Baraeon taught his people to thrive in their new subterranean home, the Underdark.
Their warlike nature had not changed after The Descent, and it did not take them long to start to establish their own territories in the vast reaches of the Underdark, often capturing settlements of other species and enslaving them in the process. However, they also fought among themselves for control of their new found realm, and as no Dark Elf trusts another, this led to the numerous independent city-states where most Dark Elves dwell today. 

Personality: 
    The Dark Elf deities, Vierdri'ira and Baraeon Ca'duz continuously strive to prove themselves better than the other. This is reflected in the personality of the Dark Elves as well. Females think they are better than males, and vice versa.
Dark Elves enjoy magic, especially releasing its power. They also love sculptures or other crafted items (especially well-made lethal weapons). They also admire physical beauty; Dark Elves are proud of their physique and do not hesitate to show it. This has also led to the custom of slaying all newborns with physical deficiencies.
Dark Elves are always in search of more personal power. Therefore, they do not trust other Dark Elves. Instead, they strive to weaken or eliminate their rivals to gain a greater advantage. This is not just the case between cities, but also in the politics of the various noble Houses inside a certain city, or even within a House itself. It is this internal strife between the Dark Elves themselves which keeps the surface races safer than they would be if the Dark Elves were united. On the occasions some Dark Elf cities did unite, they wreaked great destruction, as the capture of the human city of Westgate in the year -103 and the destruction of Port Hempstead in 834 can attest to. If all the Houses of a single city were to unite for one purpose, they could bring cities like Hlint and Haven to their knees.
Dark Elves also do not trust other races. They accept none as superior to theirs, although they may admit some races, such as Illithid or Duergar, are almost equals. Treaties with these races are usually born through hard bargaining and mutual-gain agreements. Dark Elves will negotiate with other (lesser) species, but will break such agreements at the moment they are no longer beneficial. To the Drow, bargains with lesser races are not considered to be binding. Most races have learned by now that they should be prepared for treachery when, not if, it comes.

Physical Description: 
    Dark Elves are a lot like surface elves, they tend to be lithe, slim, and graceful in their build, movements and appearance. The most striking thing that sets them apart from the surface elves is their obsidian skin. Also, females tend to be bigger and stronger than males. Because of this females tend to be the better fighter, but males tend to be the better mage. 
The second thing that sets them apart from surface elves is their eyes. Dark Elf eyes are usually red, but green, brown, or black eyes are not uncommon. When angered or upset, all Dark Elf eyes tend to turn redder. 
Thirdly, most Dark Elves have white hair, tending a bit towards yellow for females and towards gray for males as they get older. Occasionally, a Dark Elf can have silver or copper-hued hair.
Dark Elves can generally live as long as surface Elves can, and they do not show their age until about their 600th year. 

Relations with Dark Elves: 
     Dark Elf cities are ruled by a council of noble Houses, the Talthara. Every city has its First Patriarch and its First Matriarch, who preside over the Talthara (but not necessarily comply with its wishes). The Patriarch is always a cleric of Baraeon Ca'duz, and the Matriarch is always a cleric of Vierdri'ira. They need not be from the same House, although every House strives to occupy both positions for ultimate supremacy.

    Each House also has its Matriarch and Patriarch, who together rule a House. However, because of the gender struggles inherent in Drow society, it is unlikely that a House occupies both First positions on the Talthara, since a strong House Matriarch does not often condone a strong Patriarch in her own House. 
Two other powerful positions in a Dark Elf city are those of Archmage and Warmistress.

    Since males are more adept at magic, the Archmage is always a male. The Warmistress is always female, since females tend to be of bigger build. The Archmage and Warmisstress are the most important advisors to the First Matriarch and First Patriarch. In general, the House who provides a First Matriarch or First Patriarch will also try to control one of these positions. Of course, the other Houses are not likely to just allow this to happen.

    The Houses continually vie for supremacy in the Talthara, as well as for wealth and power. This struggle for power is also apparent between Dark Elf cities. Plans to increase Dark Elf power and influence are usually made by Houses who are already in excellent position, and who have nothing to lose in the plan.

    The surface world is hardly aware of the nature of Dark Elven society. 
The exact number and location of Dark Elven cities is subject to speculation. Even the Dark Elves themselves likely do not know exactly how many cities there are, due to the vastness of the Underdark and its ever changing caves and corridors.

Relations with other races: 
    Most dealings between Dark Elf cities and surfacers involve the slave trade. Dark Elves usually have goblinoid slaves, such as goblins, orcs and hobgoblins. Kobolds are considered too small, agile and independent to make good slaves. Human slaves are valued, but considered dangerous if they are trained fighters or magic-users. Slaves who are adept at crafting are valued highly, but most do not last long in the Underdark.

    With regard to other races, dwarves, humans, and of course the darthir (a word meaning both Surface Elf as well as Traitor in Dark Elf language) are traditional Dark Elf enemies on the surface. As far as other Underdark races go, Illithid and Duergar are traded with but never trusted or befriended, and there is no race a Dark Elf enjoys killing so much as a Deep Gnome.
 
Alignment: 
    The vast majority of Dark Elves are evil. However, there are a few neutral or good Drow, but these do not survive long in the twisted, cruel society of Dark Elven cities.

    Dark Elven Lands: Dark Elf cities can be found throughout the Underdark. A few locations are known, but there are probably more. Rumor has it that there is a city made of good Dark Elves, refugees from their vicious society, but that may be a myth. 

Religion: 
    Vierdri'ira and Baraeon Ca'duz (those who fail The Test are killed or turned into Driders, see also the entries for both deities). Before the treachery of Az'atta, the Dark Elven deities did not yet make a distinction on being a purely male or female faith. However, after being betrayed by Az'atta, Baraeon had his male followers expel or kill all of his female clerics as act of vengeance for Az'atta's betrayal.

    This then led to Vierdri'ira expelling all her male followers, who then turned to Baraeon Ca'duz, further polarizing Dark Elf society.

Language: 
    Dark Elves have their own language, also known as "Deep" or "Low Drow," which does not resemble the language spoken by the Surface Elves except in eloquence and musical inflection. All Dark Elves also learn "The Silent Language," a kind of "hand code" as detailed as spoken language. The Silent Language is used to communicate when silence is needed. This language, which requires a lot of tutoring, is a requirement before any Dark Elf is allowed to accompany a raiding party.

    Then there is the third, almost archaic language of "High Drow." This language is known and used only by the high clergy.

    Languages: Deep Drow, The Silent Language, Common, Elven, Undercommon. 
Other Languages: Duergar, High Drow (cleric only, for rituals)

Names: 
    Dark Elves are named at birth by their mothers. Like their Elven cousins, Dark Elves prefer names that flow off the tongue; however, their names tend to have a harsher sound to them. Names reflect and represent the race's attitudes and philosophies and usually consist of a prefix and one or more suffixes.

Female Names: 
    Zaraun (Zar meaning shadow, aun meaning dancer/player)
    Jyslin (Jys meaning hard/steel/unyielding, lin meaning arm/armor/commander).

Male names: 
    Quillyn (Quil meaning mighty, lyn meaning assassin/killer)

Adventurers: 
    Dark Elves do not often leave their cities by themselves to adventure. However, sometimes they are cast out (if they are not just killed) and make their way through the Underdark, and sometimes even to the surface.

Xantril
    It can be said that in the history of Xantril there are two moments that both devastated all foundations and became the cornerstones for the twisted continent that emerged. The first was the Cataclysm, which tore Xantril apart from Dregar and sent it drifting east for many dark ages of relative isolation. The second was the arrival of the Prince of Demons, Xandrial, and his merciless minions. There are many tales of Xandrial's arrival upon Layonara.     Some believe that Xandrial was the first demon that forced its way through the gate made by the foolish experiments of Oriax on the continent of Mistone.  Some believe that Xandrial was called by one of the most concentrated efforts of Drow faith and magic to torment the surface dwellers.     Some believe that Xandrial was summoned forth by Bloodstone or Milara to serve their vile purposes. Whatever the truth, the continent of Xantril belongs to the Prince of Demons. All who lived on this continent prior to his arrival either quickly bent to Xandrial's will, were tortured and died in dances of demonic desire, or now live an inescapable nightmare to further pleasure the demons. This is what we know of Xantril, and we know it because Xandrial wants all of Layonara to know it. 

Well-known cities:

Arabel 
Location: 
    Southern tip of the continent of Xantril 
Population: 
    24,000 (37% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 15% dwarf, 10% orc, 5% gnome, 1% dark elf, 1% demon, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tyrany 
Defenses:   
    A heavily fortified masonry wall surrounds this city. 
Miscellaneous Information:
    When you first enter Arabel, you'll know you are in Xantril and that the terrible things you have heard are true. From all around, tortured screams will accost your ears and tear at your soul. Much of the city is in ruins. Disease, famine, and violence are all part of the everyday routine of Arabel. Somehow the city manages to operate the docks with relative efficiency. Likely this is because the demons want fresh souls to torment, even though most know by now to stay far away from Arabel.
Arabel was not always a tormented city under the sway of demons. Between the Cataclysm and the arrival of Xandrial, Arabel was one of the few towns on Xantril to establish some sort of prominence and connection with the other continents. Arabel's location on the southern tip of Xantril gave them an advantage in securing trade with both Dregar and the Kingdom of Rohden. Over the years, the merchant families of Arabel built themselves up into a commercial powerhouse, funneling most of the surplus goods from the middle and south of the island through their docks. The former stature of Arabel can still be seen in glimpses of its working ruin. Those who lived in the old Arabel are haunted by its memory. Those who contributed to its glory are now forced to work the sewers.
Major Temples to Corath and Shadon have been constructed in Arabel.

Westgate 
Location:
    Western shore of the continent of Xantril. 
    Population: 4,000 (40% human, 15% half-orc, 12% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% orc, 6% gnome, 4% dark elf, 2% demon, 1% elf) 
Government:  Tyrany 
Defenses:   
    A reinforced masonry wall surrounds this city. It is also enhanced with magic. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
    Westgate is a port city directly west of the Demon Mountains. When Xandrial sends his demonic minions to Dregar or beyond, they go through Westgate. The only creatures allowed to live in this city are those who directly serve this purpose and as such are evil to the core.
 
Reth 
Location:
    Western side of the Great Forest on the Island of Xantril. 
Population:   500 (55% human, 45% elf) 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses: 
     A wooden palisade surrounds this small town. 
Miscellaneous Information:
    Some say this small forest hamlet is the gathering point for rangers and druids who are dedicated to protecting the sanctity of the Great Forest of Xantril. Their secondary concern, rumors have it, is to keep the demons from descending upon the Ancient Oak. As the northernmost town in Xantril, and since it is shrouded by the Great Forest, it is one of the few places on Xantril where Xandrial's influence is not complete. This gives the dedicated few rangers and druids a chance to work undetected on the forest's behalf. As this is a dangerous occupation, these agents of the Great Forest are re-circulated, though none but the druids and rangers themselves are sure how.

Fort Militrix
Location:  
    Located at approximately the center of the continent, Fort Militrix overlooks the road north towards the Roughlands.
Population: 375
Defenses:  
    Fort Militrix is defended by alternating sections of stone and wood walls. Inside are platforms for ranged attacks, and historically speaking the fort has always been well garrisoned.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Militrix is of key military concern, as it is situated on the road which runs east and west between Prumar and Mithrain and divides the continent into its northern and southern sections. All traffic between the north and south falls under the watch of Fort Militrix. For this reason the Fort has always been heavily garrisoned with the most disciplined and skilled troops Prantz could muster. The officers were also bolstered five or six times their numbers by recruits gathered on the march north from Arabel. This, of course, was all prior to Xandrial's arrival. But this fortitude made Militrix resilient to Xandrial's onslaught. Some believe that Militirx is holding fast, a bastion of hope amidst a sea of raging demons. 

Fort of Last Hope
Location:  
    At the edge of the Demon Mountains, in the wastes of the Tortured Lands, lies the Fort of Last Hope.
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    Hope Fort is well defended by stone walls and battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    The name of Hope Fort has become something of a Xantril joke. More often now it goes by Fort of Last Hope. It is said that a handful of soldiers still fight against the waves of evil minions that pour from Xandrial's keep. If they do, it is assumed that Xandrial allows them to do so for some other twisted purpose, for none could live free so close to Xandrial's seat of power.

Hilm Castle
Location:
    At the edge of the Fields of Death and the Orsraun Mountains stands Hilm Castle.
Population: 1600
Government:  Theocracy
Defenses:  
    Hilm is heavily defended with high stone walls and well designed battlements.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Hilm is dreadfully close to the Demon Mountains. Still, Xandrial's gaze is somewhat obscured by the Orsraun Mountains which lie between the demon king and Hilm. Hilm also lies to the north of Xandrial's keep, away from the more heavily populated areas of Xantril. These two facts give Hilm some room to maneuver on this demon-dominated continent.
    For ages, Hilm ruled the north as the last major settlement on the road to the Archwood and the Great Forest. By looking at the arrangement, you would likely have thought Hilm ruled with an iron fist, putting the wild folk of the forest under the civilized boot. This is simply not the case. Hilm established its authority in the northern regions by repeatedly defending the interests of the Great Forest and its residents from the waves of settlers and treasure seekers who fled the central region of Xantril, tortured and convoluted in the seismic events of the Cataclysm. Hilm regulated all traffic north, allowed only some to continue into the forest and turned back many. This, of course, makes Hilm particularly unpopular with the residents of the lands to the south. The forest folk to the north, however, have a deep respect for Hilm that they are reminded of daily as they enjoy the wilds in which they reside.
    This conflict, like all other conflicts on Xantril, shows signs of flaring up. The southerners, possessed with demonic rage, grasp at targets to lash their hate upon. To them, Hilm is a perfect choice. Only minor forces have thrown themselves upon the Hilm walls thus far. Either they are wild groups of the demonically driven whipped into a spontaneous frenzy and thus unorganized, or they are simply testing the defenses. In either case, fear intensifies in Hilm, as all within its walls can feel the darkness sweeping across the Tortured Lands toward their gates.

Molten Island

     Before the Cataclysm, Molten Island was attached to the Saddleback Mountains on Dregar; however, it is now a huge and active volcanic island. Inhospitable, and without any trading ports of interest, the island is not of much value to anyone. However, in the port pubs of Waysend, sailors can be heard to tell tales of a red dragon flying out from the island.

Firesteep Mountains
     Fisteron is the ancient red dragon who resides in the deeper levels of the Firesteep Mountains. He is a cruel and malicious beast, nearly godlike in power, who surpasses any red dragon previously known. 

     The mountains play host to many types of beasts, especially those attuned to elemental fire, such as fire elementals, red slaads, fire giants, and balors. Planar beasts, such as rashkasas and devourers, are not uncommon. Undead are also said to haunt its upper levels.

Lucinda

Aliases: Mother of All Magic, Lady of Spells 
Race: Human 
Worshippers: 
     Mostly humans, half-elves, and elves; fewer worshippers among other races. 
Domains: Good, Healing, Knowledge, Magic, Trickery 
Governs: Magic, sorcery, spellcraft, health 

Dogma: 
     Magic is the Gift of the Lady of Spells, and those who wield it are greatly privileged. Magic will make the world prosper if used wisely. Use magic to shape the world when you know it will eventually serve the greater good. Do not keep your knowledge to yourself; teach magic to all those with the will to learn and follow Lucinda's teachings, and tell all about the Weave.      Encourage creativity in magic in all ways and at all times. Always help others out of the goodness of your heart. Do everything you can for the Weave, for otherwise, magic may fade away. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Lucinda favors strongly enchanted weapons over normal ones. Clerics of Lucinda often carry staves and wands containing useful magic, and heavier quarterstaves for melee combat.      Lucinda's clerics often wear useful enchanted robes like arcane spellcasters. The colors on these robes are usually light and vivid, most often white and blue. 


Clergy and Temples: 
     The hierarchy of the Lucindite church is varied, separating into eight Orders that each concentrate on one school of magic: abjuration, conjuration, divination, enchantment, evocation, illusion, necromancy, or transmutation. Each Order consists of numerous groups that include both arcane and divine spellcasters. These orders have their own places of study and their own hierarchy. Each group with more than thirty members is led by a master of the spell school who is usually the most powerful and experienced caster in the group. All of the orders are led by a grandmaster; for instance, the Order of Evocation is led by the Grandmaster of Evocation. All the Orders are good aligned and led by the Council of Magic, which consists of the eight Grandmasters of the Orders. 
     There are also some academies of magic and many smaller temples where spells of all schools of magic are taught to any willing students. This is the part of the clergy that is most visible to the public. These academies and temples have members of each Order of magic working in them, and they also provide healing, supplies, and shelter for traveling Lucindites. The church also sponsors a small society of paladins, often called the Chosen of Lucinda or the Protectors of the Weave. They defend Lucinda's temples, protect the Weave from any possible harm, and keep magical artifacts out of evil's reach. Lucinda's temples (and related buildings, such as the academies) can be of any size and any style, but they all have one thing in common: all temples to Lucinda are great works of the Art, enwrapped in countless spells, containing numerous magical items, and surrounded by an aura born of the very strong Weave about the place. 
Lucindites pray for spells any time they need to, as Lucinda recognizes the need to be able to cast at any time. Lucindites don't have too many calendar-related holy days but they celebrate many things on a more individual level. Discovering new spells and ways to use magic or creating great magical items are often times for great celebrations among Lucindites. Temples and academies have annual events at which local mages to gather and share whatever they have accomplished during the past year. These events are generally called Spellmeets, but many temples call them by different names. Lucindites and Xeenites have a special night of celebration once a year called "The Night of Flesh and Magic," which celebrates the birth of Lucinda's daughter Xeen. Usually more Xeenites than Lucindites join this event, as it mostly concentrates on worldly pleasures rather than the somewhat ascetic discipline of magic. 

     Prayers to Lucinda can be heard almost anywhere involving magic and spellcasting. For example: "Oh great Lady of Spells, empower my Art, that it may better World and Weave."

Dorand

Aliases: Master of Crafts, The Priceless Gem  
Race: Dwarf 
Worshippers: 
     Nearly all worshippers of Dorand are either dwarvish or human. Given that there are members of all races that craft, there are pockets of worshippers of nearly any race. He accepts all those that desire to Make.
Domains: Earth, Fire, Protection, and Strength
     Dorand's clerics can choose any two of the above domains; it is well known, however, that nearly all clerics of Dorand embrace the Strength domain, which represents the strength and endurance needed for long hours at the forge. While this is not universal, it comes naturally with the process of becoming a Hammer of Dorand. Mostly, those who practice the crafts not involving mining and smithing are the clerics that do not practice the Strength domain.
Governs: Mining, Smithing, Craftsmanship, Stonework 

Dogma:
     Follow the Way of the Hammer. Create the new for the greater glory of Dorand. If you do not craft, you are not serving His purpose. Serve as tool and instrument of Dorand and strive to perfect your craft. Never fall into inaction. Support those that seek new knowledge or create new inventions.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Nearly all clerics of Dorand wield some version of a hammer or axe, since these are the tools used in both their craft and their worship and thus are the most important things that a Hammer of Dorand possess. They tend towards browns and greys, the colors of earth and stone.

Clergy and Temples:
     Nearly all clerics of Dorand are known as Hammers, the reason being that his clerics consider themselves his tools, and the greatest instrument of creation for Dorand is the Hammer. Within the church hierarchy there are different ranks, from Acolyte of the Hammer (lowest) to the High Hammer, the most exalted cleric of Dorand on Layonara.

     Creation is Dorand's primary concern. It is true, however, that many people confuse clerics of Dorand with clerics of Deliar since many of his priests fund themselves though the selling of their creations. Dorand's clerics, as they rise through the ranks and study the Way of the Hammer ever more, sell their wares less often, crafting instead to perfect their art. Often these items are given to Dorand as offerings.

     Most temples of Dorand are natural things, usually dug into a mountain or hill, though there are exceptions where a master builder wanted to plan, design, and build a temple of unusual size, beauty, or décor.

     Clerics of Dorand pray for spells when they can. They can often be found catching a quick nap in the forge while waiting for the coal to heat up, for it is during the art of creation that they are most directly worshipping Dorand. Many use time at the forge (or other craft) as a time of quiet meditation, relaxing their mind and communicating with Dorand on a spiritual level, while allowing him to guide their bodies to create.

Vierdri'ra

Aliases: Mother of Darkness, Quarvalsharess (Goddess in Dark Elven) 
Race: Dark Elf
Worshippers: Dark Elf females only
Domains: Destruction, Evil, Trickery, War 
Governs: Stealth, night, darkness, poison

     During the times before The Descent, the Dark Elves already worshipped Vierdri'ira. Believed to be the first obsidian-skinned Elf to walk the lands, she is the Prime Matriarch, the Mother of Darkness, the epitome of Dark Elf feminine supremacy.
     Vierdri'ira is the pinnacle of cruelty and cunning, malicious in her dealings and vicious in a fight.
     She and her counterpart Baraeon Da'Cuz have vowed that the Dark Elves will reign supreme in the Underdark. Once that is accomplished, their second goal is utter annihilation of the surface Elves and submission of their lands. However, to achieve this goal, the People must strive among themselves to strengthen the race and prevent a fall into decadence.
     Vierdri'ira and Baraeon both consider themselves to be the supreme Dark Elf deity: Vierdri'ira because she was the First, Baraeon because he was elevated to godhood for his actions and his cunning and therefore has proven himself the better one. The strife between them is reflected in the divisive, cutthroat Drow society.

Dogma: 
     Worship the Mother of Darkness or die. Destroy the weak and the faithless. Strive to better yourselves, even at the expense of others; in this way you will gain and keep the favor of the Mother of Darkness. Dark elves are the supreme race, and females are better than males. The Dark Elves shall reign supreme in Underdark. Annihilate the surface elves and take their lands from them. Do not aid the enemies of the People.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Priestesses of Vierdri'ira prefer to use a whip. They're always dressed in black, whether they're in armor or clothing. They prefer armor made from blackened mithril or adamantium. Usually they wear an obsidian necklace with two red eye-shaped rubies hanging from it. The only other colors they occasionally add to their black garments is purple or red.

Clergy and Temples:
     Priestesses of Vierdri'ira are the most powerful people in Dark Elf society, next to Priests of Baraeon Ca'Duz. Every Dark Elf city has one temple for the Mother of Darkness. Temples are led by a High Priestess, who only remains in that rank as long as no other, more powerful Priestess removes her from that position.

     Two red eyes always glow menacingly above the entrance of Her temples and only females are allowed to enter; males entering the temple will be killed. 

     Inside these temples, it is very dark, with only the slightest purple or red glow to light the way. The main room of a temple is the Hall of Submission, where the Dark Elves worship their goddess. Further inside the temple is the Inner Sanctum, where the most secret and powerful rituals are performed. It is only during these rituals inside the Inner Sanctum that the name "Vierdri'ira" is used, and the Inner Sanctum is also the only place that the sacred High Drow language is still used. During all other rites, the language used is Deep Drow and she is referred to as "Quarvalsharess" or "Mother of Darkness." Since the Inner Sanctum also holds the temple's most powerful artifacts, only the six most powerful priestesses are allowed to enter. 

     Females who do not worship her but enter the Inner Sanctum of a temple are to be sought out and killed unless they are converted to worship the Quarvalsharess within seven days. Proof of conversion is given by undergoing a Test to demonstrate their loyalty to Vierdri'ira and Baraeon; those who fail either die or are transformed into the fearsome Driders. This is the same test that all Dark Elves have to go through to prove their loyalty to their deities and their People.

     Clerics pray for their spells before they go into reverie. The Mother of Darkness requires that her followers bring her many offerings, be they riches or offerings of slaves, captives, or traitors.

Sinthar has been on the World for just over thirty-two years now and he has destroyed nearly all of the Dragons that were still alive. His forces now control all but two continents and two islands. He grows stronger by the day. Rumors spread of his generals begining to run their own agendas; however, it is thought that he still has heavy control over all of them. It is time for Layonara to unite, but what heroes will answer the call?

    This is our history, yet to be written.  What will we scribe in the book of time?

Vanavar Island
     In ages past, the only people to inhabit Vanavar were Gray Elves, who made the Broken Mountains their home. They dubbed the island Vanavar, or "strong-willed." However, as the humans expanded across the face of Layonara, they came to recognize Vanavar's strategic position and started settling the island. When Xandrial arrived, he too recognized the strategic value of Vanavar and was quick to send his forces in.
     Vanavar's forces were hardly prepared to face the hordes of the Demon Prince, and the Duke of North Hampton, as last resort, sent a messenger bird to Rohden, requesting aid and offering his allegiance to the King of Rohden if he came to Vanavar's aid. However, the Duke was too late, as Xandrial's forces arrived first and laid waste to all the settlements of the island. Now, only a few survivors are left and struggling to survive.
     With the Duke's patrols gone, Vanavar is now also an ideal base for pirates. Xandrial allows them to use the island's secluded coves as long as they don't interfere with his own ships.
Nobody knows what happened to the Gray Elves that inhabited the Broken Mountains, as they have not been heard from since the rise of the human settlements on Vanavar. It is unlikely that they still inhabit the mountains without lifting a finger against Xandrial, so it is likely that they were killed or left for Voltrex. However, no one truly knows the fate of the Vanavarian Grays.

Well-known Cities:

North Hampton

Population: 150 
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None

     Located at the northern tip of Vanavar, North Hampton was the major city of the island and one of Layonara's larger trading ports, acting mostly as a trade hub for ships from Westgate and Waysend as well as Huangjin and Lor on the south. Now, after Xandrial nearly torched it to the ground, it is but a shell of its former self, its inhabitants either killed or enslaved.

Murdoch

Nothing much is left of it today except for a few families of fishermen, trying to survive and unable or unwilling to leave. Murdoch was the last town on Vanavar to be destroyed by Xandrial. This scheme never came to fruition, however; together with North Hampton, Celine was one of the first Vanavarian towns to be destroyed.

Locales:

Broken Mountains
     The mountain range at the center of Vanavar breaks the island basically in two, so when the first human settlers arrived, the name Broken Mountains quickly took hold.
     Though inhabited by Gray Elves before the human incursion and Xandrial's attacks, no one is certain of the proud elder race's fate.

Krelin Forest
     An old but small forest of tall trees, the village of Celine had big plans to use the Krelin Forest's excellent wood to enter the shipyard business.

Ilsare

Aliases: 
     Archer of Love, The Heart of Gold, Lady of Dreams  
Race: Elf 
Worshippers: 
   Mostly elves, humans, half-elves and halflings; fewer worshippers among other races.
Domains: 
     Air, Good, Protection
Governs: Beauty, love, passion, dance, music, art, sculpting 

Dogma: 
     Life is worth living because of the beauty found in the world and the love that draws hearts together. True beauty is more than skin deep. Believe in romance, as true love will win over all. Always follow your heart, for it leads you to your true destination. Perform loving acts, and seek to awaken love in others. Acquire beautiful items of all sorts, and encourage, sponsor, and protect those who create them. Find love wherever it takes root, and bring it to its fullest bloom so that all may share the joy and beauty it creates.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Ilsare's clerics favor bows as their weapons. After all, Ilsare is the Archer of Love, and love indeed is like an arrow fired by a bow: it strikes swiftly and with great power. Ilsare's clerics favor beautiful clothing and any kind of armor works if it is needed, as long as it is beautiful. Red is the color of love and fiery passion and thus clerics of Ilsare often prefer red clothes.

Clergy and Temples: 
     Ilsare's clerics are somewhat flighty and the hierarchy of the church is loosely organized. Ilsare's temples are always beautifully designed buildings with numerous interesting pieces of art decorating them. Clerics of Ilsare pray in the morning, after a refreshing bath and clothing themselves in whatever wonderful raiments they will wear that day. Their greatest celebrations are held every month beneath the full moons. These celebrations involve dancing, poetry and beautiful music. Romantically involved participants are said to experience the full bloom of their affections on such nights, allowing them to evaluate the strengths of their feelings. It is not uncommon for artists to unveil their latest work at such holy days as well.

     Prayers to Ilsare are usually for situations involving love or art, and are often almost works of art themselves, as some can be quite long and poetic hymns. Clerics of Ilsare pray so that love may bloom. They pray when they watch an artist work so that Ilsare may bless their creation. For example, a cleric praying before creating a beautiful piece of clothing that can possibly help someone fall in love with the person who wears it: "Oh Ilsare, Heart of Gold, bless this dress I am about to craft with great beauty, and bless the one who is to wear it with your gift of love."

Pyrtechon

Aliases: The Destroyer, The Raging One  
Race: Dragon 
Worshippers:  Worshippers of Pyrtechon are primarily human, with a few elves or dwarves. Pyrtechon also has a significant following among the monstrous races.
Domains: Strength, War, Destruction, and Evil.
Governs: Destruction, chaos 

Dogma:
     Consign Layonara and all of its attendant races to oblivion. Do not preserve; preservation is not the way of Pyrtechon. Only in the purity of absolute destruction can the world be cleansed.
     The fires of The Destroyer will purge this place, life plays no part beyond its brief dance in the flames. Glory in destruction, and do not cease until all life is extinguished.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of Pyrtechon show no particular favor toward one weapon type, seeing all as tools to achieve the ends of their Dark God. Weapons are made to kill and are all considered to be worthy of use. Indeed, many Clerics of Pyrtechon are skilled in the use of a range of weapons, far beyond the followers of other deities. Weapons are often enchanted with fire, to emulate Pyrtechon's breath.
     Clerics are normally heavily armored for better protection in combat, which they often see. Flame-red platemail and splintmail are highly favored, as both are considered representative of the scaled hide of Pyrtechon.
     Clerics often wear a necklace of basalt (always chipped from the statue of Pyrtechon held in the central worship hall) carved into the representation of a talon wreathed in flames of gem dust. The more powerful the cleric the more valuable the gem dust of the wreath, with ruby considered to be at the pinnacle. Beyond ornamental purposes, these charms are used by Pyrtechonites to evaluate each other's abilities, with challenges not uncommon for those considered to be exaggerating their powers.

Clergy and Temples:
     Clerics of Pyrtechon are an individualistic array, and thus find it difficult to establish a truly coherent structure. This individualism, added to the clergy's inclination toward destruction of both life and social order, makes a complex formal hierarchy almost impossible to achieve. Followers of Pyrtechon tend to be solitary individuals who keep their worship out of the public eye.

     It is rumored that Pyrtechon once walked on Layonara but was somehow forced to retreat by the humans that plague the world. As such he wants to blast the world into oblivion and hopes to accomplish this through destruction and chaos. The clerics of Pyrtechon prefer to associate with those that deal with anarchy, death, lies,                      traps and trickery. They have quite a lot of influence with nobility questionable reputations.

     With this attitude toward life (and, indeed, each other), one would expect that these clerics would be disorganized. This is far from the truth. Though formal temples are few and far between, small groups are often highly effective at working together to create as much havoc as possible. These groups are typified by a cleric who rules by virtue of strength alone and rules only as long as he is able to hold that position.

     In theory, all Pyrtechonites are answerable to the High Priest. Much like the leaders of smaller cabals, he maintains authority through strength and achievement. If the High Priest was ever to falter, he would be consumed by someone within his own ranks. The temple has a highly effective network of communication, thus allowing them to keep in contact with the many small groups operating throughout Layonara at any one time.
The central temple itself is a remarkable edifice of red stone, dominating and impressive. A strange miasma of violence fills the halls, making all feel watched by the baleful gaze of the Dragon God. Naked flame lights the temple, illuminating the richly appointed suites and corridors, casting a garish glow throughout. The Hall of Worship is accessible to all, with a huge basalt statue of Pyrtechon at the central point of adoration. The statue is exquisitely carved, the ruby eyes glaring down upon the assembled faithful, no damage apparent from the horde of amulets chipped from its stony skin.
Beyond this hall, however, is where the true rites of the faith, dark and gruesome, are performed. This sanctuary is only available to the High Priest and those few he selects to aid him in the rituals to Pyrtechon's greater glory. These rites are sadistic and violent, and it is not only flames that bathe the room red. The remainder of the temple is devoted to housing the clerics who reside at the temple, the Chambers of Learning, and the Hall of Petitions.

     Clerics of Pyrtechon pray for their spells at dusk or dawn. Both are seen as a time of death, with one state - day or night - being banished to oblivion in favor of another. Most, however, choose the death of the sun as the holiest time, due to its symbology of life and all that its fall represents.
