Dwarves
    Dwarves are a stout and stocky race of people. When it comes to battle you would be hard pressed to find a more skillful or dedicated warrior than a dwarf. Many Dwarven settlements are underground, and they consequently have an affinity with all things that pertain to the earth, including mining and the fighting of underground creatures. They are quite short, with most dwarves being around 4 feet in height, yet due to their stockiness they can still range from 130 to 200 pounds. They take great pride in their facial hair and it is not uncommon to see dwarves with great, bushy beards that hang to their knees. Due to their stockiness, dwarves are able to take an extreme amount of physical and magical punishment, making them good front-line fighters. There aren't many Dwarven adventurers as they are loath to leave their settlements, but a few feel the call to adventure, and they generally become quite capable fighters.

    I don't know enough to comment about the Duergar, one of the most feared races in Layonara.  However, I did spend time with some Gold Dwarves one summer.  This is what I learned.

Gold Dwarves 
    Unlike the other dwarven subraces, gold dwarves prefer to live on the surface rather than in isolation deep within the mountains. They were forced to leave their ancestral homes long ago and now live in cities on the surface. They are great craftsmen and traders but less focused on war. They are the most liked and social of the dwarven subraces. Unlike other dwarves, they no longer have clans, but they still follow the dwarven ways and traditions. 

Personality: 
    Gold dwarves are the least warlike of the dwarven subraces. They live on the surface, craft and trade. They still possess the combat skills and great drinking ability common to all the dwarven races however. 

Physical description: 
    These sturdy dwarves tend towards blonde hair and dark skin tones. They value their beards even more than the other dwarves and prefer to keep them tidy and groomed. 

Relations with other races: 
    Gold dwarves get along with other surface races well enough and often trade with them. They hate orcs, goblinoids, and giants, like all dwarves. They do not hate the Duergar as much as the shield dwarves do but still dislike them greatly. 

Alignment: 
    Gold dwarves are often of lawful neutral alignment.
 
Religion: 
    Most gold dwarves worship Dorand. Vorax isn't as popular among gold dwarves as he is with shield dwarves. 

Language: 
    Common, Dwarven 

Names: 
    Like other dwarven names. Even though they don't have clans, they have kept the name of the clan of their ancestors as their surname. 

Adventurers: 
    Gold dwarven adventurers aren't uncommon. A gold dwarven adventurer is most commonly in search of riches. Some of them are in search of the lost clans of their ancestors.

Long, long ago, in a past shrouded by the mists of millennia, the T'oleflor - a race of feylike beings who created the elves - called the Golden Dragons to this World. The Dragons ruled here, and the existing races prospered side by side with the broods of the Dragons. But as long as there is good, there is evil who seeks its undoing.... 
    The Chromatic Dragons, beasts as cunning and evil as the Golden Dragons were wise and benevolent, fell from the stars to wage war upon their adversaries and the T'oleflor. Fully half of Dragonkind was slaughtered in the ensuing conflict, until an uneasy peace was made, a treaty born out of exhaustion and attrition. To prevent the spilling of further dragon blood, both sides began to create other races - today's humanoids - as pawns for another battle, a decisive one to end the feud and drive the losers from the face of the World. When the peace expired, the Chromatic Dragons renewed their assault against the Metallics, reinforced by the slave races they had created. The fury of this battle eclipsed even the initial clash, claiming three quarters of the Dragons and Dragonkin on both sides and annihilating entire species. Other casualties of the second campaign included the cultures of the humanoid races; split by allegiances to different dragons, the humanoids began to war against each other as well, shattering into factions that carry hatred towards each other to this day.
    The Chromatic Dragons changed their tactics in what would become the Dragon War, the third major conflict. Instead of striking directly against the Metallics, they shifted their attention towards the creations of their enemies. The humans were the main target of the Chromatic assault, their race shattered, driven back, and nearly eradicated. In the bleak face of extinction, a young man named Sinthar Bloodstone stepped out of the carnage and into legend. He was a mage of budding power, strong enough to challenge a young dragon. He led his hosts of human warriors against the Dragons: not just the evil Chromatics, but the Metallics as well. Sinthar believed that the Chromatic Dragons had been drawn to Layonara because the Metallics were there, and the Metallics were there because of the T'oleflor's meddling. He considered himself a crusader, a valiant warrior fighting against the alien creatures who sought to control his homeland. A merciless and brilliant strategist, Bloodstone never lost a battle in seventeen years of war, overcoming seemingly insurmountable odds time and time again. As he grew in power, he fashoned several wells of power that would later be come known as Bloodwells. The Bloodwells touched the plane of lost souls, allowing him to siphon the energy of millions of the dead. With the aid of this massive influx of power, Sinthar augmented his magical powers to near godhood and summoned forth hosts of demonic creatures. Finally, beaten back by the relentless assault and straining under the duress of Sinthar's forces, the Dragons allied themselves against their common threat. The Chromatics wished to wipe out the threat to themselves, and the Metallics saw Bloodstone as a power-hungry despot bent on enslaving the world.
    The alliance of the Dragons ended the strife, but not conclusively. The Dragons were more powerful, but were fighting carefully, each side expecting the other to strike against them as soon as the tide turned against Sinthar. Sinthar's armies were a united and motivated whole under the command of a master tactician, but could not overcome the power of the united Dragons. Finally, a treaty was struck. The Dragons promised to relinquish their control over the young world's affairs, and many of the remaining Dragons left. The Tol'elfor would settle into a caretaker role, guiding and advising the elves and their forests. Sinthar Bloodstone, however, was to be tried for his crimes against life, nature, and the races. A Council of Seven was convened - one or two representatives from each race - and they unanimously found Sinthar guilty of all charges. At the urging of the Chromatic Dragons, the Council sentenced Bloodstone to high banishment.
    And so it came to pass that Bloodstone lashed out at the Council of Seven, slaying half of them before he was forced into the portal to his exile, screaming all the way, spitting oaths that he would one day return to Layonara to finish the Dragons and avenge himself against the races that betrayed him.

Prunilla

Aliases: Lady Comfort, Lady of the Harvest  
Race: Halfling 
Domains: Earth, Healing, Plant, Sun, Good
Worshippers: Halfling (primarily female) 
Domains: Earth, Healing, Plant, Sun
Governs: Food, agriculture, hearth and home, marriage, family 

Dogma: 
     Planting and harvesting are an eternal cycle. As you nurture the land, plant crops and tend them to the best of your abilities. As you nurture the land, so the land will nurture your family. Family is the foundation of society.


Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Prunilla's favored weapon is a modified farmer's sickle with electrical enchantments. Her clerics, when anticipating battle, favor studded leather in brown and green. When no combat is expected, clerics of Prunialla are seen in more casual attire that often shares the earthy colors of their armor.

     Prunilla is the wife of Deliar. While the two are very devoted to each other, they have at times been at odds at how to accomplish their goals. While Deliar emphasizes the importance of trade and mercantilism, Prunilla stresses agriculture as a means of family support. When Deliar gets particularly stubborn, Prunilla can often change his mind by baking him a scrumptious bumbleberry pie.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples are found underground or in the side of hills. They appear to be very small on the outside yet are very spacious, warm, and inviting on the inside. Clerics routinely offer small amounts of the harvest to Prunilla.

     Prayers for blessings are normally at the beginning and the end of the day, and often express gratitude for successful crops and healthy families. Clerics who devote their lives to the honor of Prunilla will only call upon her for guidance when necessary. Clerics of Prunilla often function as farming experts, teaching the peasantry about things like crop rotation and irrigation. Most also double as a village healer or midwife.

     Special tribute is given to Prunilla on Planting (the 15th day of Mar) and Harvest Day (the 15th day of Seplar). 

Prayers to Prunilla often center around healing and harvest:
     "Mother Prunilla, bless this field, that Earth and Sun may work together to make the harvest fruitful. "
     "Lady Comfort, please deliver your graces to this burdened soul. Heal him with your touch, so he may shine in your grace once more."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Ilsare, Goran, Lucinda, Deliar

Friendly: Aeridin, Katia, Kithairien, Shindaleria, Beryl, Folian S'pae, Grannoch 

Neutral: Az'atta 

Unfriendly: Rofirein, Vorax, Dorand, Toran, Mist, Aragen, Xeen 

Enemy: Pyrtechon, Shadon, Branderback, Corath, Baraeon Ca'Duz, Sulterio, Vierdri'ira, Grand
Sailors' Stories of Corsain, compiled by Finneaus Finefeather

Corsain
   One of three key islands to the southeast of Dregar, Corsain is part of the kingdom of Rohden

Well-known cities:

Western Gate
Location:
     Southwestern part of the Island of Corsain 
Population: 
     18,500 (85% human, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 3% elf, 2% halfling) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses: 
     A heavily fortified masonry walls surrounds this city; parts of the wall are reinforced. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
     Tiburn is the launching point of the Kingdom of Rohden's forces. Over the ages, Tiburn has fought many battles with Katherian and the people of northeast Rilara. Before the Cataclysm, these two regions were once united geographically but torn asunder by political allegiance and civil warfare. When the two factions were unevenly split by the Cataclysmic forces that tore the lands asunder, the warfare intensified on Rilara and the Rohdens who were trapped there died torturous deaths. On Corsain, the Rohdens prospered, and even today burn with the need to avenge their kinsmen. With the rise of Milara on that vile continent, the people of Rohden's thoughts turn more and more to these bloody desires. War between the two great regions seems on the horizon, and Milara, interestingly enough, seems to have neglected his influence in the Kingdom of Rohden. In Rohden, Milara is simply known as the tyrant of Rilara, a convenient symbol upon which to heap their festering animosity towards the continent.
     A large temple to Aragen can be found here.

Loriel
Location:
     At the eastern edge of the Blackwood on the Island of Corsain lies the city of Loriel
Population: 1685
Government: Monarchy
Defenses:
     None that are immediately noticeable.
Miscellaneous Information:
     Loriel is one of the many towns that occupy the densely packed Island of Corsain. Loriel's most notable pastime is an open invitation rogue tournament that happens once a year and is announced throughout Layonara. Throngs of people gather to try their ability to spot the spies of Rohden as they watch and infiltrate the crowd. By now, Rohden intelligence is able to identify on sight most of the skilled, yet unwise, rogues of Mistone, Rilara, and Dregar. They use this information, it is said, for purposes of recruitment and for defense.

Corsain Locales:

Tiburn Plains
     The lush plains of Tiburn are home to many prairie-like creatures. It is also the most fertile farmland of Rohden. During times of war, the plains are also used as staging areas for massive combat drills, but the plains are sacred land for the regionals, who are very careful never to spill blood there.

The Black Woods
     Rumors exist that the forests are littered with many hidden temples and monasteries. Many seek them to learn the ways of the spirits, while others seek them out to obtain the hidden knowledge they may have.
     The Rohden Forests, otherwise known as "The Black Woods," are said to come to life at night, and anyone who wanders there at night is under the danger of being stepped on by an angry oak or a powerful birch tree. The nearby monasteries use these woods as training grounds, and the monks believe that one who has been able to survive the wrath of the dark spirit of the forest is able to attain a special balance within oneself.

Lake of Dreams
     The Lake of Dreams is home to the Monastery of Dreams, where the most sublimely skilled of Layonara's monks are rumored to walk upon the walls. A great statue of a golden dragon rises over the temple walls, a guardian of the lake as well as a symbol of the rigid discipline of the monastery. Very few gain the privilege of training at these hallowed grounds, but it is said that those that can decipher the cryptic passage on the temple doors will gain the favor of the grandmaster.

Grey Watch Tower
     The Grey Watch is that time in the morning just before the dew settles and the mists of the oceans spread; it is also a time when many naval battles occur as fleet commanders jockey for surprise in the fog. In this marvelous tower, thrice have the great sailors of Rohden stopped the enemy forces from invading their precious island. All these occured during the Grey Watches, earning the tower its name. 
     During peaceful times, ferries can be taken from the Tower to Alibor, although only the stalwart or foolish try to brave the island's dangers.
Sailors' Stories of Tilmar, compiled by Finneaus Finefeather

Tilmar 
     Tilmar is one of three key islands to the southeast of Dregar and part of the Kingdom of Rohden. Because of its central location, the island is known for its trading ports, usually used as halfway stops or meeting grounds for trading partners. As such, the Island of Tilmar has grown extraordinarily wealthy over the ages. In fact, the island, lead by the elite of Huangjin, threatens to break away from the rule of the King of Rohden. Much attention, therefore, is focused on this small island, and with good reason.

Well-known cities:

Serenity Port
Location:
     The port town of Serenity Port is located at the southern point of the Island of Tilmar.
Population: 935
Government:  Communal Collective
Defenses:  None
Miscellaneous Information:
     Serenity Port once competed with Huangjin to be the central trading port of Layonara. They grew side by side, attracting cargo vessels in a kind of maritime merchant tug-of-war. Both cities were successful and grew rapidly. Serenity Port, however, stopped short along this trajectory, whereas Huangjin became more and more committed to its dockside entrepreneurship. In a reflective moment in history, the people of Serenity Port realized, or so the town lore goes, that in dedicating themselves to business, they were increasingly subordinating their entire lives to the pursuit of wealth. At that time a magnificently charismatic figure emerged in Serenity Port. Stories differ whether he was born in Serenity Port or came on one of the merchant vessels. But the all agree that he spoke with enchanting eloquence, and he used that oratory skill to speak to the unsettled sentiment of the villagers, transforming the village literally overnight. Now Serenity Port is one of the few villages in Layonara which works as a collective. All land and resources are collectively owned by the community. They no longer trade for profit, striving instead for a semi-autonomous subsistence based economy. Any trade Serenity Porters do is only to attain products not available in their region. Most of the time they refuse to trade in gold, demanding direct barter instead. 
     This political and economic arrangement in Serenity Port is reflected in the town's architecture. The symbol of the town, one which has become somewhat famous throughout Layonara, is the community longhouse. It is located in the middle of the town, and every Serenity Port family lives in it, except for those foraging expeditions.
A temple of Shindaleria can be found in Serenity Port as well.  

Huangjin
Location:
     On the Northern coast of Tilmar lays the wealthy city of Huangjin. 
Population: 7985
Government: Monarchy
Defenses: 
     High white walls surround the city
Miscellaneous Information:
     The sheer opulence of this city dazzles many visitors. Nearly every building looks sparkling new and not a single cobblestone seems out of place on the streets. All visitors enter Huangjin through the glorious docks, and one would have to travel far into town to observe even a cracked surface...let alone a glimpse of the meager domiciles of Huangjin's servant underclass.
     The reason for the extravagance is simple: Huangjin is the central trading port for all of Layonara. Huangjin has adorned itself in signs of success and beacons that light up the night clouds in an attempt to lure passing cargo vessels to their markets. For ages, these tactics have worked. Ships have often stopped their journey between Dregar and Rilara short, dumping their cargo at a competitive price to be resold to a vessel traveling the opposite direction for the same goods. Captains can't resist cutting their voyage in half, even if it means paying a little extra gold for their cargo.
     Every trade good throughout Layonara makes its way at least occasionally through Huangjin, a fact of which Huangjin' innumerable and hard working dock-hands are proud. Ships from Voltrex have been seen at this port in recent years as well. Since the docks at Saida are closed to outsiders, Huangjin has become the trading outpost for fine elven wares, boosting their economic prospects ever further.
The King of Rohden looks at Huangjin with suspicion however, as the city seems to be growing too influential for his comfort. Rumors support the suspicions of the King, as it is said that Huangjin thinks of itself as the ruling seat of its own kingdom on Tilmar Island. Unconfirmed reports suggest that Huangjin has stopped paying its tributes to Rohden as well. The ruling elite of Huangjin seem to be taking advantage of the contemporary turmoil and are exacerbating it at the same time. With position, politics, and money all playing huge factors in the port's existence, Huangjin is a crucial variable in the current campaign for Layonara. 

Tilmar Locales:

Swamp of Reawakening
     The Swamps of Reawakening have been the stuff of many legends and rumors in the area. Strange sights are reported by those that walk near the dangerous crypts that surround these swamps. Many have entered their gloomy depths never to return, and as the legends grow, so does the number of dead or missing adventurers. One would expect trolls to live in these swamps, but the absence of the beasts makes the Swamp of Reawakening more surreal and frightening than normal. 

Swamps of Storms
     The torrential weather in this area has allowed very few adventuring groups to know much of its makeup; little is known about these swamps except rumors of moaning caves and eternal whirlwinds.
     The Beach of Thunder, Lightning Strand, The Watery Peninsula, The Swamp of Storms. Many names are given to this area of Tilmar. Every attempt to clean the peninsula and make it a flourishing port city have been met with massive failure. To this day, people are trying to find out why the weather is so torrential in this area. Some even say the storms might not come from the sky at all.

The Dead Forest
     The perils of the nearby swamps spill over into this barren forest. Dead spirits are seen wandering at night, and the brash or inattentive are routinely made permanent visitors.
     The reason this once lush forest is now barren is unknown to many, but some say that a great betrayal ocurred many centuries ago and withered the forest beyond recognition. Now, during the silent hours, the spirits of those who were betrayed can be heard moaning for redemption...or revenge.. 

Backbone Mountains
     The Backbone Mountains are riddled with internal cave systems that many wondrous and dangerous creatures call home. Rumor has it that rare gems can also be found here, as well as passages that go into the unexplored depths of the earth.
The Backbone Mountains cover the central section of Tilmar Island. Some say they are simply a curious geographical feature; others think that the mountain range is the body of an ancient dragon that now holds the island together. Whatever it may be, the Backbone Mountains are rumored to hide dwarven strongholds and certainly hide several tribes of giants. Very few have taken the effort to explore these mountains fully, and those who have will not speak of their experiences among the peaks and passes.

Seas and Oceans
     The seas of Layonara are both beautiful and deadly. They can bring great riches to budding adventurers and crafty merchants alike, but if underestimated, the currents can bring swift ruin and death. The seas surround all of the major continents of Layonara, and travel by ship is often the most efficient - if not the only - way to reach a destination. The oceans of Layonara beckon to adventurers, however: many islands await the daring, as does sunken treasure and even underwater dungeons that drunken sailors speak of in hushed tones. But only woe will befall those who tread lightly in domains of Mist and Shindelaria.
     In many ports, one can book passage on ships to travel to other ports on a continent, or even to other continents.

Bay of Carocsa
     The Bay of Carocsa is a mid-sized bay with gorgeous beaches that stretch all the way around its U-shaped shoreline. The sun sets gently on an often angry ocean, giving the bay a sublime attraction in the contrast of the peaceful sun with the violent water. Still, you won't find many people on the beach, and far fewer in the sun-warmed, bathlike water. The bay is notorious for a deadly undertow which has claimed many lives. Locals say the undertow is no natural phenomenon, but Mist taking fools for sacrifice.
If the undertow doesn't get you, the ever-present sharks will. There are a wide variety of sharks in the Bay of Carocsa, regardless of the season. There is a strange explanation for this unique aquamarine phenomenon: Carocsa, a sea-elf druid, lived on the beach here for many years. She established a place of worship to Shindaleria on the beach, so that at high tide the water would slap gently against the huge stone boulders of the shrine. She also created an underwater observatory for the study of marine animals, particularly the sharks that prowled the bay (not nearly as often as they do today).
     Once day the Shark-Lord and his entourage came to the bay; some say to explore the link Carocsa opened between the surface and the depths. The crowd of sharks in the bay caused chaos and one of the sharks was flung into Carocsa's observation area, throwing her bleeding body into a swarm of frenzied sharks. They circled their prey as the Shark-Lord watched. Before his astonished gaze, Carocsa polymorphed into a shark and fought off the first line of would-be feeders. At that point the Shark-Lord swept in, stopped the swarm and demanded Carocsa follow him to his territorial waters.
     What happened after that is even wilder speculation. Some believe they fell in love and Carocsa abandoned her legs and lungs to remain at the Shark-Lord's fins. Others, who claim to witness humanoid figures emerge from the bay occasionally and mysteriously reenter, guess that Carocsa taught the Shark-Lord how to obtain a humanoid form, and they spend their time plotting control both above and below. Others are certain the Shark-Lord devoured the druid. Whatever happened, it is clear that in the aftermath sharks are drawn to this spot. The influence of Shindaleria is still strong at Carocsa's shrine to her.

Windjammers' Bay
     Locations such as the Windjammers' Bay await those seeking treasure, places where many ships, their hulls laden with gleaming gold and powerful magic, have sunk. These treasure hunters succeed only if Mist permits it, because she is said to have a special interest in causing chaos in this particular bay, to the great annoyance of the inhabitants of the nearby Port Hempstead.
 
Gulf of Coreanys
     The seas of Layonara are not without their mortal dangers, either. The Gulf of Coreanys might seem a welcoming place to weather a storm, but the placid appearance of the waters deceives, as pirates and their ilk crowd the Gulf. Unwary merchant ships travelling in or near the Gulf often fall victim to pirate raids. Wary of the Gulf's reputation, most merchants either sail a long way around, or make sure to hire an able crew - sometimes including adventurers - to defend themselves. Pirate activity in this area however, also makes it an attractive site for adventuring, since pirates often have plundered treasure.

Broken Corals
     The Broken Corals are among the most perilous and feared waterways on Layonara. For those seeking to take the quickest route around the southern part of Mistone, this strait would seem the fastest, but successfully navigating the Broken Corals is a fool's hope, for even the smallest of vessels will have great difficulty in passing the perilous reefs intact, and any larger vessel entering this area is almost certainly doomed to a watery grave. Only pirates make frequent use of the corals to deter pursuing larger ships, but even for them it is perilous. Many once-mighty vessels sleep silently on the seafloor, but only the truly foolhardy will attempt to recover their lost riches.

The Great Coral Bay
     Other large masses of corals exist, such as The Great Coral Bay on the west coast of the elven island of Voltrex. Only the graceful ships of the elves are said to able to navigate these corals with success, and as such the bay deters all but the most successful of merchants from enterprising on the island. Shindelaria pays special attention to these waters, to make sure that Mist does not try to spread her chaos towards the elves. Treasure awaits those who dare explore the bay, but malevolent creatures are said to lurk in the depths.

Coral of Faces
     On the southeastern side of the continent of Rilara, one will find the Coral of Faces, which appear to be an extension of the Mountains of Madness Mountains. Though they pose navigational hazards, it is said that one's true face can be found on those beautiful corals.

Forsaken Islands

     When Blood returned to the world through his rifts, he caused a few problems. It seems that a few of his magical portals touched the negative plane and have not closed. The problem is spreading, but mages and clerics cannot make sense of the situation because anyone who approaches the islands is turned undead. Sometimes the transformation is instantaneous, other times it takes up to a week...but the horrid metamorphosis always happens.

Shindaleria

 Aliases: Mother Ocean  
Race: Sea Elf 
Description: Shindaleria is the patron goddess of sea elves. Little is known about her other than that she is the oldest of the elven gods. She is bitter enemies with Mist, as both deities struggle to exert their influence on the seas. 
Worshippers: Sea elves, sailors 
Domains: Animal, Healing, Magic, Water, Good
Governs: Sea life, oceans, healing, wisdom 

Dogma: 
     The Mother Ocean has always been and always will be; seek the embrace of her safety whenever you need it. Respect the sea and its harmony and it will not harm you in any way. Swim both the great currents and the shallow seas. Promote knowledge and use of the sea by reasonable folk, and fight those that would taint or deplete its beauty and bounty. Think long and wisely before acting; the seas do not alter quickly, but when the waters move, great change is sure to follow. Seek out fellow swimmers who honor the ways of Mother Ocean, and ally with them against those who follow Mist and who feel not the serene waters but only the chaotic waves. 

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Clerics of Shindaleria, most of them sea elves living underwater, prefer weapons and armor they can wear underseas. The trident is a useful weapon for underwater combat and hunting. Clerics of Shindaleria often spend most of their time in the sea, so they need to be able to swim; thus, they prefer clothing over heavy armor that makes them sink and rusts. Followers of Shindaleria prefer blue as their color, be it the light blue of the shallow seas or the deep dark blue of the deep ocean. 

Clergy and Temples: 
     The clergy of Shindaleria doesn't have much of a hierarchy. The sea is quite wide and her clerics travel a lot, not meeting each other very often. The oldest and wisest of her clerics are considered closest to Mother Ocean. 

     Shindaleria has no actual temples, but numerous underwater shrines exist. They are simple grottoes, walls full of holy text, deep under the surface and rarely visited. Shindaleria's shrines are used to record events in the seas and Mother Ocean's clerics travel there once in a while to record past events in the cave walls. The locations of the most ancient shrines containing the most ancient history of Layonara are guarded secrets, known only to a few of the oldest sea elves. 

     Clerics of Shindaleria pray for spells at the high tide closest to midday. Mother Ocean doesn't really have widely recognized holy days, but individual sea elf communities celebrate certain days in her name. The only widely recognized holy day of Shindaleria is The Returning. The first week of Junar, clerics of Shindaleria walk the land, gathering beautiful objects and pieces of art and then taking them to the sea as gifts to Mother Ocean. Everything started in her waters, and eventually, everything returns to them. 

     Prayers to Shindaleria, due to most of her clerics being sea elves and spending most of their time in the water, aren't often heard. Some sailors pray to Shindaleria before crossing the sea, for example: "Mother Ocean, grant us passage through your gentle waters, as we pose no threat to you or the life of the seas."

Allies and Enemies:

Allied: Aeridin, Ilsare, Katia, Beryl, Folian S'pae 

Friendly: Deliar, Toran, Lucinda, Az'atta, Prunilla, Grannoch

Neutral: Rofirein, Vorax, Dorand, Goran, Aragen, Kithairien, Xeen 

Unfriendly: Shadon, Corath, Sulterio, Grand

Enemy: Pyrtechon, Branderback, Mist, Baraeon Ca'Duz, Viedri'ira

Aragen

Aliases: The Wise God, The Lord of Knowledge  
Race: Human 
Worshippers: 
     There is no race in particular that follows Aragen, though elves are most likely to do so since they usually have the patience and lifespan to collect and use information for their god. Humans also follow Aragen, because learning and collecting information progresses society, and human society is very progress-oriented indeed. Half-orcs and half-giants (and tieflings, to a lesser degree) are least likely to follow Aragen, because they often care little for knowledge or the benefit of society, rarely have the patience for the required studies and observations, and would rather bash heads than talk. However, anyone willing to devote his or her life to the search for knowledge can worship Aragen. 
Domains: Knowledge, Protection and Travel. 

     Clerics of Aragen always pick Knowledge as one of their domains, so a cleric of Aragen could pick either Knowledge and Protection or Knowledge and Travel.

Governs: Knowledge, Research, Stories, Poetry

Dogma: 
     The search for and gathering of knowledge of any kind is paramount, both for the benefit of the faithful and for society as a whole. Even the smallest speck of information must be sought out and stored for everyone to see. Only through true enlightenment can balance be achieved. Use violent measures only when absolutely necessary; otherwise, stand out of harm's way, avoiding conflict and collecting as much information as possible. Make sure collected knowledge is archived for the use of others.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     The favored "weapon" of Aragen's clerics is the humble quarterstaff or a mage's staff. Only rarely is a staff used as a weapon, however, as it is usually used as a walking stick when the Aragenite travels to new places to gather information.
     Aragenites prefer simple clothing when travelling, as the burden of plate mail slows them down in their pursuit of knowledge, and they tend to avoid conflict when possible, so they usually have no use for the heavy armor anyway. Aragen's clerics have, however, been trained to wear heavy armor to better protect the knowledge they carry in their earthly bodies.
The clergy of Aragen always carry a notebook to write down the knowledge they gain. The most devout Aragenites will protect this book to the death, to ensure that knowledge is not lost.

Clergy and Temples: 
     The clergy of Aragen serve as the scholars and researchers of society, and if one happens to have a question of some kind they will almost always be ready to answer. There is no clear hierarchy in the temples of Aragen, but each temple has a head scholar who is the only person allowed to write in the Libra Prima, or First Book, of that temple.
     Temples devoted to Aragen usually resemble libraries or schools where knowledge is stored wherever possible: in books, on scrolls, and through even more secret and esoteric means. Books and other devices of knowledge are often littered everywhere, because genius thrives in chaos.
     Each temple has a Libra Prima, where every mote of knowledge collected by that temple's clerics is written down, but only the head scholar of the temple has the authority to write in this sacred tome. This is to ensure that no information is written twice and that all knowledge gained by that particular temple can be easily accessed. The tome is often enchanted with strong magic to allow for many more pages than it would otherwise appear to have, and also so only the current head scholar can write in the tome. If a temple is attacked or struck by natural disaster, then the First Book is artifact that the clergy will save, as it holds all information ever collected by acolytes of that temple.
     Knowledge gained by the Aragenites is spread to different temples by the Bearers of Knowledge, a Monastic Order.
     Clerics of Aragen do not pray at any particular time of day or in any particular location, though most often combine prayer with recording gained knowledge in their books and preparation of spells if a spell caster.
     Litanies of faith uttered by Clerics of Aragen can range from chant in an indecipherable language to a simple: "Lord Aragen, grant me wisdom, purpose, and strength of mind so that I can discover what is unfound, and enlighten the unenlightened."

Sulterio

Aliases: Adamantine One, The Brooding One  
Race: Grey Dwarf 
Worshippers: Mostly Duergar although a few other savage races occasionally also worship the Adamantine One. 
Domains: Death, Earth, Evil, Knowledge. Nearly all clerics have the Earth domain and one of the others.
Governs: Darkness, evil, mining, poisons 

Dogma:
     The riches of the Underdark should be mined in honor of the Adamantine One. Work and toil to gather these riches, for nothing worthwhile is easily acquired. Those who show weakness or lack of faith shall be punished. As adamantium is forged by fire into weapons and armor, so you shall be forged by your faith. Do not rely on the arcane arts, rely on strength. Be loyal to your clan and honor the ways of your people. Obey your superiors. Show no mercy to the other dwarven races.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     The favored weapon of all the clergy is the adamantium maul or hammer. They wear adamantium armors, heavily plated and always of a grayish/blackish color, so that they blend in with the rocks. They wear a mushroom-shaped talisman around their necks. When not wearing armor they wear dark, hueless garbs. 

Clergy and Temples:
     The clergy can roughly be divided into three sects: the Deep Smiths, the Adamantine Brotherhood, and The Chosen.

     The Deep Smiths were shown the ways of working the earth and all the ores within it, especially adamantium, the black and unyielding ore. This focus of knowledge has led to a well-established order of subterranean ore-crafters known as the Deep Smiths. They excel in the crafting of adamantium armors and weapons. Unlike their Dorandite counterparts, however, they create not out of love for the craft itself, but as a means to make better materials for war. Love of war replaces the pride of craftsmanship, and all of their works exude a martial, bloodthirsty aura. Nonetheless, items crafted by the Deep Smiths are highly prized and valued pieces of work. 

     The Adamantine Brotherhood seek to be more like the Adamantine One, and have taken to literally mimicking the title in the very fiber of their being. They have hardened body and mind in pursuit of the essence of their namesake metal. Some have compared them to the Voraxite Brothers of Battle, but the Brotherhood is much more numerous. They have fewer scruples and will not refrain from using poisons to help them in their dark endeavors. The Adamantine Brotherhood rarely surfaces, instead seeking to advance their physical and mental fortitude by delving even deeper into the earth and uncovering and claiming even more riches for the glory of the Brooding One. It is rumored that the greatest of the Brotherhood can actually reach into the core beneath the Underdark and extract molten adamantium from the very heart of Layonara.

     The third sect is The Chosen, battle clerics of Sulterio. They are a ruthless and vicious order, and can readily call upon the strength and viciousness of Sulterio in the throes of battle. Armies of the Underdark are often lead by these clerics; those that are not often regret not paying the hefty price needed to hire The Chosen when they fall prey to an army that did. 

     Other orders and specializations exist within the faith of Sulterio, including warriors, slavers, and even traders. But since the Duergar of different clans oftentimes mistrust each other (though never quite so much as they mistrust other races), the clerical hierarchy is usually based on a clan level. The sect's leader is chosen quite simply, through a trial of single combat. The cleric who defeats all challengers becomes the leader and guides his faction in faith and war. 

     Temples to Sulterio are rare on the surface world. The few that exist are generally deep within mountains to reflect the world of the Underdark. The temples are usually little more than fortresses of stone, though they are often adorned with adamantium ore. Altars are invariably also made of the most perfect deposits of adamantium. 

Prayers:
     With the exception of The Chosen of Sulterio, it is rare for any caste to pray regularly, except for guidance before extreme trial. To ask for help (even from one's own god) is considered a sign of weakness by Sulterio's faithful. Instead, followers of Sulterio worship him more in name and deeds than in words. The Chosen however, do pray each day upon rising so that Sulterio will better know the sound of their voice, lest their prayers go unanswered in the heat of battle because Sulterio did not hear them over the uproar.

Elves
    Elves are an ancient and aloof race. Compared to the human race, elves are quite small and frail. The tallest elves rarely reach five and a half feet, and some are as small as four and a half feet. They have a lithe build and usually weigh between 100 and 150 pounds. They are an agile and dexterous people, and they move with grace and beauty. The Elves prefer seclusion and tend to shun outsiders and the outside world as a whole. Of all the races of Layonara, Elves are the longest lived, with many elves reaching between 600 and 700 years of age. They have a natural affinity for magic, but also value martial skills with finesse weapons such as light swords and bows. While humans will venture into the unknown for many reasons, elves almost universally leave their cloistered groves to experience more of the world that their race holds at arm's length.

There are many varieties of elves.  I will include a brief description of some of them.

Gray Elves
    Gray Elves are one of the many kinds of surface elves on Layonara. They are among the tallest and most intelligent of their kin, and yet have a certain aura of arrogance about them. They are probably the most arrogant type of elf, seeking to put great distance between themselves and other races, including other elven races. The Gray Elves live deep in the mountains, past the point where even the dwarves turn around and go home. Gray Elves are a noble people, however, and seek to uphold good wherever they can. Gray Elves make excellent wizards, yet most remain secluded in their mountain homes. They conceal these homes with warding and illusory magics so that unknowing races leave them alone, and so that only the worthy will enter their domains. Be wary, though, because once stirred the Gray Elves will attack with highly disciplined knights mounted on war-trained griffons or hippogryphs, with the support of their uncanny wizards.

Personality: 
    Gray Elves are much more arrogant and aloof than other elven races. They regard every other race with disdain, even other elven races. They only have respect for other Gray Elves. Most Gray Elves are full of themselves, and usually only listen to themselves or other Gray Elves.

    Even so, they believe that they are one of the greatest protectors of good in the world and they work tirelessly to uphold this vigil. Though they feel this sense of noblesse oblige, it still takes the threat of a very great evil force to stir them from their isolated homes in deep in the mountains.

    When dealing with the few others that they do respect, Gray Elves are very noble and honorable, doing everything to make sure a promise is kept or a common enemy is defeated. To most common folk, though, Gray Elves mainly resemble arrogant knights.

Physical Description: 
    Gray Elves are unusually tall for elves, but are also more thinly built, lacking the strength and agility of their lesser cousins. Living in the mountains has accustomed them to harsh climates and the like, and as such they are more enduring than common elves. Gray Elves are among the smartest of elvenkind, and this is probably what contributes to their somewhat aloof behavior towards other races, including other elven races. Gray Elves tend to wear noble clothing and armor, with the mages wearing splendid robes colored white, silver, yellow, or gold that are often adorned with shining metals such as silver and mithril, or jewels. The Gray Elven warriors tend to don chain or platemail of shimmering metals; they also tend to wear metal helmets sporting distinctive wings. They prefer deep blue or purple cloaks.

    Gray Elves always have very pale skin, and tend to have gray or silver hair, along with amber eyes. Gray Elves with pale golden hair and violet eyes have been spotted, but these are very rare.

Relations with other races: 
    Gray Elves are doubtlessly the most haughty and aloof of the surface elves; they think almost nothing of other races, even other elven races. Gray Elves prefer to stay as isolated from other races as possible, and reside deep within the mountain ranges of Layonara. Due to living in the mountains, they have forged a friendship with the birds living there, and are bitter enemies with the giants also seeking claim to the peaks.

Alignment: 
    Gray Elves are usually of good alignment. They tend more towards being lawful than chaotic.

Religion: 
    Most devout Gray Elves tend to follow a deity of elven origin due to their disdain for "lesser" races.

Language: 
    All Gray Elves speak common and elven. Other languages commonly known by Gray Elves are Sylvan, Draconic, Auran, and the language of birds.

Names: 
    Issauria Windshear, Alin'dae Amberleaf, Sieylianna Silverdawn

Adventurers: 
    Though it might seem like Gray Elves aren't the types to go adventuring, lone Gray Elves leaving their mountainous homes seeking adventure is not unheard of. They see themselves as champions of good and as such some will go out into the world to defeat any kind of evil lurking in the shadows. Even so, this does not mean that the adventurous Gray Elves have let their arrogance and contempt for lesser races go.

Sun Elves 
    Sun Elves keep to themselves, perhaps even more than the other elven races. Nevertheless, they can be found throughout Layonara, although most of them live on Voltrex.
    They are ruled by noble Houses and greatly value tradition. Sun Elves do everything the 'elven' way, and consequently, their lore and art is still somewhat narrow, as they do not even bother to look at lore and art of other races.

Personality: 
    Sun Elves believe that they are the true defenders of Elven art, lore and magic. Because of this, they look down on all other races, and somewhat on their other Elven cousins as well. They strongly believe in tradition and are very conservative.

    Sun Elves are staunch isolationists. Even when they live in a larger city, they tend to group together in their own little enclave.

Physical description: 
    Taller and leaner than most of the other elven races, the Sun Elves are a beautiful race. Their skin has a copper or bronze hue, and their hair is blond, copper, gold, or black.

    They dress in simple garments of green and blue that seem inconspicuous at first, though a closer glance reveals the garments are made of exotic materials with exquiste cuts. These garments are subtly embroidered with patterns that seem simple, but are quite complex when one attempts to follow them. The same goes for their jewelry: simple, but exquisitely made.
Because of their focus on art and lore, they are not the strongest or hardiest of elves. They even tend to look down on combat, seeing it as a very crude way to settle conflicts.

Relations with other races: 
    Sun Elves tend not to concern themselves with the affairs of other races too much, as these are rather insignificant to them. Only relationships with other elves are important and meaningful (excepting, of course, their reviled cousins, the Dark Elves). However, Sun Elves have been known to act as diplomats, advocating the Elven side in conflicts.

Alignment: 
    Mostly lawful neutral

Religion: 
    Ilsare and Aeridin

Language: 
    Common, Elven

Names: 
    Sun Elves are named during a Naming Ceremony that takes places during the first dawn after the birth of a child. Their last name is the name of the House they are born to, such as Morningbreak and Sunbeam. Their first name is given by the cleric that performs the naming ceremony. Female names: Elenya, Luthién, Nessa, Celebriänn Male names: Cìrdan, Celahir, Haldamir, Findaráto

Adventurers: 
    Sun Elf adventurers are few, as they tend not to care much about the other races of the world and their dealings. 

Wood Elves
     Wood Elves tend to be a bit shorter and stockier than the other elven races, but they are no less graceful. They make their home in the forests of Layonara, and, contrary to their Wild cousins, they're not nomadic. Instead, Wood Elves build villages in the treetops. Before the race wars, Wood Elves could be found throughout Layonara, but nowadays most have retreated to Voltrex and have settled in the Ulambree Forest.

    Great hunters and woodsmen, there is nothing that they do not know about the forests they inhabit.

Personality: 
    Proud like most elven races, the Wood Elves will go out of their way to protect and defend their forests and the creatures that inhabit them. Those who seek to harm the forest would do best to stay clear of the Wood Elves, as they will show no mercy to those who bear forests ill will.

Physical Description: 
    Like their cousins, the Wild Elves, the Wood Elves have dark hair and prefer to decorate themselves with tattoos. Their clothing is often made from leathers and leaves dyed in colors that make them blend into the forests. Having spent their entire lives in the forests, Wood Elves are often stronger and more agile than the other elven races. Wood Elves get their first bow at a young age, and are rarely seen without one. They're considered the best marksmen on Layonara, but are also fierce in close combat. For this they prefer short swords, as larger weapons are not practical in forests.

Relations with other races: 
    Wood Elves rarely have contact with other races, as they prefer not to leave their forests. They get along well with most other elven races, except for the Dark Elves.

    Relations with most other races are either neutral or strained at best, especially with races that do not respect the woods and cut down trees, like humans. They also hate orcs, who they're likely to shoot on sight. As long as others stay out of their forests, the Wood Elves could care less about them.

Alignment: 
    The majority of Wood Elves are neutral.

Religion: 
    Wood Elves follow Folian S'pae, their patron god. 

Language: 
    All the Wood Elves know common, Sylvan and elven. They see little reason to learn other languages as they do not actively seek contact with other races.

Names: 
    As with most elves, Wood Elf names tend to have symbolic meanings. They usually refer to plants, trees or creatures.

Adventurers: 
    Wood Elves are not very likely to leave their forests in search of adventure, unless there is something involved that threatens the forests or their tribe.

Wild Elves 
    Wild elves are barbaric and tribal elves living in the thick forests and open plains of Layonara. They are nomadic people and, unlike their cousins, they rarely stay in one spot for a long time. They live in small tribes of 10-60 people led by elders, but still have no real hierarchy. Wild elves are rarely seen by other races due to their nomadic nature, hiding skills, and taste for solitude. Wild elves are close to the nature and believe it gives them everything they need. They do not build or buy; they scavenge and hunt. Wild elves own very little and do not trade much, and thus have no real economy. Their almost feral nature makes them dangerous enemies in combat and most are also great hunters. Other races consider wild elves feral savages, but outsiders have trouble understanding the wild elf way of living and worldview. Wild elves travel the world completely free and use their own skills and wits to survive. 

Personality: 
    Wild elves are a proud race. Even though other races consider them savages, they contend that they are the true elves, for the others have lost their primal elven essence in their attempts to control nature. They are hardy elves who can survive under harsh conditions. They respect their traditions and ways, but are not bound by them. They live by the words: "Live as if you were to die tomorrow. Fight as if you were to live forever." Wild elves are generous to those they view as good and merciless to those they view as evil. 

Physical description: 
    Wild elves tend to have well-tanned skin and their hair ranges from black to light brown, lightening to silver white with age. They tend to be physically hardier than other elves but still maintain the elven elegance and grace. They're fond of decorative tattoos that also have practical purposes, such as depicting tales of their deeds. Wild elves dress in simple clothing of animal skins and basic plant weaves and wield simple weapons such as spears and bows. 

Relations with other races: 
    Wild elves prefer to live alone without much contact to other races and even avoid them whenever possible. They share their surface-dwelling cousins' attitude about everything non-elven and the Dark Elves, however. They actively try to avoid conflict, but if something threatens the things they hold dear, they will go to war. 

Alignment: 
    Most wild elves, due to their nomadic and barbaric nature, are chaotic neutral. 

Religion: 
    Kithairien is the patron god of the wild elves and they almost always worship him. They seek to become what he is as he was the first and the greatest. 

Language: 
    Common, Elven 

Names: 
    Wild elven names are very much like those of other elves. They are given to the children by the tribe's elders and the names always bear a symbolic meaning. 

Adventurers: 
    Wild elves are a nomadic race and thus it isn't uncommon for individuals or small groups to leave their tribe. Usually these are younger wild elves exploring the world out of curiosity or because the tribe's elders have sent them on a quest.

Millions of years ago Layonara came into existence through a slow process known as evolution. During those millions of years many things happened that have gone undocumented; at least, undocumented by any known race. We will begin at the earliest documented point, when the first Dragons arrived on the world.

    The first dragons to arrive on Layonara were the Metallic Dragons, massive reptilian creatures with scales made of gold, bronze, silver, and other minerals. In their five hundred years of dominance, they worked tirelessly to make the new world livable for other races, and there are rumors that they were responsible for the creation of some species. Word spread throughout the galaxy of a lush new Prime World that was just being settled. In response to this news, Dragons of color - red, blue, black and green,  along with a few others - began showing up on Layonara vying for power and their own control of the world. It is rumored that these dragons began to create races in order to reach their lofty goals and to defeat the established Metallic Dragons. It has never been verified that the Dragons ever created races, but the whispers cannot be discounted. After another thousand years the Dragon Gods began actively becoming involved in this world, in the hopes of saving the Dragons that followed them. It is a known fact that the Dragon Gods did create races to reach their goals and yet did not become "directly involved" in the everyday "life" of Layonara. 

    After two thousand years the Dragons fought a large war, which is now known as "The Dragon Wars". This war lasted for over one hundred years and involved nearly every race that existed on the World. The savage fighting of the Dragon Wars was fraught with consequences: some races were split up into different tribes or even different species, some races were rendered completely extinct, and all races were greatly diminished in population. It was during this war that the Elves and Dwarves split into separate evolutionary paths and the Humans became the dominant race. The fighting between races was just as savage - if not more so - than the battles of the Dragons. Every race believed in a Dragon's cause and fought bitterly to see their goal come about.

    From the acrid, blood-tinged smoke of battle came a young Human General known as Sinthar Bloodstone. Rather than aligning himself with a Dragon, he believed that Dragons were responsible for the death and destruction of the Dragon Wars. With that belief he formed his own army in the hopes of forcing both Dragon sides to surrender. His natural talents honed by bloody practice, Bloodstone ruthlessly wielded powerful magic and displayed exemplary tactics, and many believe that he never lost a battle. In time, the Dragons were forced to surrender to Sinthar and the World knew peace for a few hundred years.

    When the war ended the Dragons demanded, as part of their surrender, that Sinthar be banished from the world, never to return. At his sentencing Sinthar killed many of the jury and then disappeared after swearing vengeance on the world. Many believed that Sinthar's banishing was just a legend, until he did return two millennia later to seek his revenge, but that is another story.

The second Generation began when the Humanoid Gods began to take interest in Layonara and the Dragon Gods were driven out. It is rumored that the Dragon Gods were driven out accidentally but who knows the ways of Gods? Many think that the Dragon Gods still have power on the world, but are remaining quiet and hidden as they build their strength.

    It is now known that Sinthar Bloodstone began his attempt to return to Layonara about ten years after being banished. Though the Second Generation is not centered around Sinthar's return, the coming of Bloodstone is seen as the event that ended the Second Generation and began the Third. During the Second Generation there were many race wars being fought, predominately between the Elves and Dwarves. The wars soured relations between the Elves and Dwarves for generations, preventing the two cultures from uniting in trade, invention, and power. For the most part these Race Wars are over, but every once in a while skirmishes will brew out of the hard feelings that will remain for Generations.

    The Elves are now split up into two distinctive groups, the Dark Elves and the Top Elves. The Dark Elves live below the ground while the Top Elves, and various sub-cultures thereof, live above ground. The Dark Elves used to follow the Dragons of Color while the Top Elves followed the Metallic Dragons. When the war ended their war began in earnest, their natural prejudices augmented by thousands of years of war.

    The Dwarves are also split into sub-cultures, but they are not openly hostile towards each other any longer. The Hill and Mountain Dwarves sometimes fight, but brawling is what Dwarves like to do.

    During this Generation the Dragons retreated and were rarely seen, but with the return of Sinthar the few that have left have retreated even farther, and can now only be found in the most difficult to reach or inhospitable places on Layonara.

    Sinthar was able to return after thousands of years through the use of portals that a rare few believe may be tied to Blood Wells. During his time on the World, Sinthar created the Wells to help in his battles against the Dragons. When he was banished he was able to communicate with one in control of a Well. Through this extraplanar communication, he corrupted the keepers of the Wells and they eventually fell under his limited control. With this limited control he influenced them to create more Wells and thus his power grew. He was able to convince a few to willingly help his cause with promises of knowledge, power and wealth. After hundreds of years he created enough power in three of the Wells that he was able to bring an army through from the Planes. Unfortunately for him, he miscalculated somewhere and over half of his army was destroyed - along with parts of the World being reshaped - due to unforeseen explosions and the Negative Plane. It is thought by many that if his army had not been destroyed that the World would have fallen within a few years. Even with only half of his army intact he was able to defeat a large continent, secure a stronghold, and build his army anew.

Shadon

Aliases: The Trickster, The Irrepressible Scamp 
Race: Gnome 
Worshippers: Gnomes, halflings, and some goblinoid races. 
Domains: Chaos, Luck, Trickery.
Governs: Illusions, traps, humor, trickery 

Dogma:
     Shadon teaches that life is fleeting, and therefore must be enjoyed. Every moment spent doing something boring is a moment wasted. As such, followers of Shadon relish constant festivals and adventuring. Clerics of Shadon will go to any extent to enjoy themselves, sometimes harming others along the way, but sometimes doing great good. Whether your actions were good or evil does not matter, as long as they were fun to do. Always have a prank or two ready and Shadon will be happy with you.

Clergy Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of The Trickster prefer to use daggers, because they are easy to hide and it is extremely fun to take down a foe with such a small thing. They normally enchant their knives with electrical properties to allow witty comments on their shocking personalities. 
     Clerics of Shadon wear flashy clothes, normally tailored to make a loud fashion statement. When in combat, clerics of The Scamp wear shiny metals to distract or dazzle their opponents.

Clergy Temples: 
     Whenever a group that follows Shadon actually manages to organize themselves (which rarely happens), they normally take charge over the local bars and festivities. Organization is rarely more than a long word, and Shadon's followers encourage everyone around them to forget propriety, morality, or inhibitions and enjoy themselves. Clerics pray whenever they feel like praying, often right after getting daily supplies for the next adventure.

Prayers:
Before combat: "ShadonmakesurethatwhenIwhackthisguyontheheadhescreamsinafunnywaysothatIcancompletemycollectionofbobscreams."
At any time: 
"Shadongivemetheabilitytoshowthe....whatsthat?Letsgocheckitout!!!"

Allied: Branderback, Baraeon Ca'Duz 

Friendly: Pyrtechon, Xeen, Vierdri'ira 

Neutral: Goran, Mist, Aragen, Grannoch, Grand 

Unfriendly: Rofirein, Dorand, Aeridin, Deliar, Lucinda, Katia, Corath, Shindaleria, Sulterio, Beryl

Rofirein

Aliases: The All-Seeing, Lord Protector  
Race: Dragon 
Worshippers: Rofirein does not forsake any race, but he is predominantly worshipped by humans.
Domains: Strength, Protection, Knowledge, Magic
Governs: Protection, guidance 

Dogma: 
     You are a paragon of virtue and honor. Dedicate your life to justice, honor, and the pursuit of knowledge. Hold the law above all else at any cost, even if this means bringing loved ones or friends to justice. Without the order of law, chaos would reign and the world would descend into dark times where Pyrtechon would thrive. Extend honor to all, even your foes. Aid others whenever and wherever possible, as long as it is in accordance with the law and does not make way for acts of evil.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     Clerics of Rofirein favor swords, especially bastard swords, over bludgeoning weapons, believing that a sharp blade metes the swiftest and most painless justice. They are often seen in full plate armor, favoring it along with a large shield bearing the symbol of Rofirein. Any armor that provides maximum protection to the wearer is preferred, as defense of self is required before one can defend others.

Clergy and Temples:
     The clergy of Rofirein have a distinct hierarchy, as would be expected by a church of law, and often work in close co-operation with the paladins of Toran.

     Temples of Rofirein are a mixture of grand and humble affairs, often doubling as local courts and houses of justice. All temples maintain a fair library that holds documents of law and other books of factual interest. The largest place of worship is the Cathedral of Rofirein in Prantz, a magnificent edifice replete with the splendor and majesty of the Law. Each local temple is home to a High Priest, a number of local clerics, and serves as a temporary home for questing clerics. 

     The High Priest is often the oldest and wisest of clerics, rumored to be in frequent direct contact with the Great Wyrm himself. The local clerics are attached to one temple or church at a time and oversee the day-to-day tasks. They will never move far from their temples, except in times of crisis. This is in contrast to the questing clerics, as they are mobile, traveling the length and breadth of Layonara to provide protection to those that cannot protect themselves, bringing honor, justice, and chivalry wherever they go. They are often turned to when wisdom or a non-biased opinion is needed and can operate in a judiciary role if required. 
There is also a group of non-clergy; these lay followers of Rofirein are those who have not undergone the initiation into the clergy or paladinhood, and comprise all those employed for service by the temple itself. Stablehands, cooks, groundsmen, and the like all hope to serve Rofirein in a greater capacity someday. 

There are several ranks in the Rofireinite order:
     The first step of the path of Rofirein is that of the Initiate. All classes spend at least 4 years as an initiate, learning law and various others skills including basic combat, etiquette, diplomacy, honor, chivalry, and healing. On completion of this period of training, each soul is presented with a shield bearing the symbol of Rofirein by the high priest during an appropriate ceremony. 
     After the ceremony, it is believed that Rofirein communicates his guidance on to a soul during a session of solitary prayer so that it may know the next step upon its path:

Librarians/scribes/historians:
     These are predominantly mages and clerics who favor the pursuit and maintenance of documentation and official records, including the local census. These souls are also primarily responsible for all logistical matters of a temple.

     It is rumored that at one time Rofirein actually walked on Layonara. He has a deep love of the world and wants nothing more than to see it prosper. He hopes to aid Layona's prosperity by offering his protection and guidance to all that follow him.

     Guardians of Justice (Judges):
     These are clerics that specialize in the law as passed down from the Great Wyrm himself. Judges are predominantly made up of the clerics who spend several years' further study in all aspects of the law. These clerics are always attached to a local courthouse or place of law where guidance and wisdom is required.
     Guardians of the Wyrm (Temple Guards) - Most Temple Guards are drawn from the ranks of fighters, rangers, and paladins. These souls have dedicated their lives to protecting the temples and other sacred places of the Rofireinite faith. They spend many years perfecting their combat technique, with special emphasis on use of the tower shield and defensive tactics.
     Knights of the Wyrm (Questing Clerics) - Almost anyone can join the Knights of the Wurm, (though fighting classes comprise the majority) who have dedicated their lives to the defense of others through the use of sword and shield. Unlike the Guardians, they have no desire to be tied to one place, often establishing distant outposts and bringing the word of Rofirein to unknown lands. Besides further combat training, these clerics are also given additional training in healing and law and are taught to ride. These souls are the first to respond to a threat and are often called upon in times of need.
All clerics of Rofirein display a statue of a golden dragon as a focal point for worship and blessing. Many come to touch the statue of the great dragon to ask for guidance in difficult times. His clerics pray at least twice a day, both in the morning and in the evening. Their prayers are often straight and to the point when the path is already known. They often involve invoking particular aspects of a Great Wyrm like the strength of their claws or the protection of their scales.

The Rohden Navy

     The Navy of Rohden is currently the greatest sea power in Layonara; however, the Kingdom of Rohden did not have the influence of the sea until Port Hempstead fell when it was attacked by Dark Elves. During the battle, Port Hempstead's naval forces was completely destroyed, giving Rohden the chance to prosper on the waters of Layonara.
     Right after the fall of Port Hempstead navy, Greatwatcher Weu-Cheng enforced a grand plan that greatly improved the efficiency of the military ships and the docks. It called for a much more rigid training program and selection process for the crew. The plan marked the beginning of an era of naval dominance for Rohden.
Seven years later, Watcher Xiao-Way wrote a book titled Sea, the Throne of Power that discussed the importance of the naval power, which further influenced the growth of Rohden's Navy, doubling its size in less than three months.
     The men of the Rohden Navy are known for their efficiency and loyalty. All of the men took an oath before serving that binds them to protect the ship with their life. The high-ranking naval officers of Rohden enjoy a special prestige in the Kingdom, many even enjoying greater power than the nobles, securing the place of the Navy in the king's court.
     Greatwatcher is the highest-ranking officer in the Navy, and there are only three, each governing three of the nine fleets in the Rohden Navy. The fleets are divided into the Sun, Star, and Moon Fleets, and a Greatwatcher heads each one. Then there is a Watcher for each of the nine fleets. Each ship is then commanded by the Shipmaster, then the Shipvoicer, and finally the Deckmaster. Learner is the lowest ranking officer; they concern themselves with learning the basics of leadership onboard the ship.

Grandeur of the Sun-Class Ships:
     The Sun-Class is the most advanced ship in the entire Rohden Navy, and there is currently only one Sun-Class ship built and commissioned. Jewel of the Golden Sun, the flagship of the fleets, is 180 meters in length, has nine masts, and can carry over 1000 passengers if needed. (40 Officers, 220 Crewmen)

River of Rohden-Class Ships:
     The frigate class of the Rohden Navy, the River-Class ships are light and agile, and quick. However, they lack thick hulls and can sustain major damage easily. River-Class ships are mostly used for surveillance of enemy forces and patrol of the sea.  Examples of this class are Profit of the River, Evenness of the River, Connection of the River, and Peace of the River. (10 Officers, 70 Crewmen)

Eternally Dutiful-Class Ships:
     This class is heavily armored, affording them much more protection than the River-Class ships. The trade-off is in maneuverability: Eternal-Class ships are much slower and harder to navigate. They are more often engaged in combat missions. Examples of this class are Eternal Resoluteness, Eternal Mortality, and Eternally Humane. (25 Officers, 155 Crewmen)

Median of Mount Spine-Class Ships:
     Median-Class Ships sit between the River-Class and Eternal-Class ships. They balance armor and agility, creating a multi-purpose ship. They also have larger cargo holds and can serve as hospital ships, supply ships, or passenger-carrying vessels. Most of Rohden's ships are Median-Class. Some of the Median-Class ships are Beginning of the Median, Median Fundament, Establishment of the Median, Shining Light of the Median, and Strength of the Median. (15 Officers, 130 Crewmen)

Kithairien

Aliases: The Runner  
Race: Wild Elf 
Worshippers: Usually wild elves.
Domains: Animal, Strength, Travel, Trickery
Governs: Time, strength, quickness of wit, hunting prowess 

Dogma: 
     Rely not on others for your survival. Live free. Embrace nature and its gifts, but do not take or keep anything you don't have to. Law and order other than those of nature restrict; thus, they are not to be followed in any way. Wait patiently for the opportunity, but when your chance comes, act swiftly, wasting no time or effort.

     The Runner was the first of his people. He spurned the lives of other elves, embracing nature. He spent his time travelling the world of Layonara, more at home on the open plains than among people. He established the first wild elf tribes, and eventually became their most revered figure. Strong and proud, he is the embodiment of what all wild elves strive to be. He is a master hunter, a trickster, and a fierce warrior.


Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing: 
     Clerics of Kithairien favor the spear. The simple yet versatile weapon is suitable for many things other than combat. Armor isn't necessary, for a true warrior of Kithairien waits for the opportunity and strikes without getting hit himself. Clerics wear light, unencumbering armor such as cloth and leathers to aid their evasive prowess. Natural colors are usually preferred as they create an effective camouflage. Usually, clerics of Kithairien wear or in some other way display the colors blue and white, which represent the open sky and the freedom it symbolizes.

Clergy and Temples: 
     The church of Kithairien consists primarily of clerics living in solitude and small tribes of wild elves, and, as such, has little in the way of formal hierarchy. Actual temples to Kithairien do not really exist. There are places of worship, though, mostly magnificent and mystical places of nature. Clerics of Kithairien pray for their spells at no particular times; for a hunter, time does not truly matter. The church of Kithairien does not celebrate widely recognized holy days. Instead, the tribes of wild elves mark anniversaries of important events in the group's history and celebrate them in Kithairien's name.

     Prayers to Kithairien are usually for the hunt. Also, wild elves wishing to become like their hero-god ask for some of Kithairien's qualities. For example a wild elf cleric of Kithairien praying before hunting: "Oh great hunter, grant me your wisdom so that I may know the moment to act. Grant me the speed and agility of the great Runner, that I may act swiftly when the time comes, and bestow upon me your great strength, that my prey shall fall as easily as yours."

The Servants of the Weave

     The Servants of the Weave are a somewhat peculiar part of the Church of Lucinda, if it is an actual part of the Church at all. Their main focus is on the last part of Lucinda's dogma: "Do everything you can for the Weave, for otherwise, magic may fade away." Members are few and scattered across Layonara, but consist of all types of magic users, be they cleric, sorcerer, wizard, or bard.

     The Servants will go out of their way to protect, preserve, and maintain the Weave and actively seek out those who try to corrupt or destroy the Weave. This does not mean that evil magic users are sought out and destroyed, but rather that unnatural use of magic is sought out and stopped, like magical experiments gone awry, wild magic areas, unbound fiends, or liches.
The World Beneath:  What Interrogations of Drow has Revealed about the Underdark, by Prantz Guard Maloney McHugh

Aeridin

Aliases: The Protector and Preserver of Life, The Lifegiver  
Race: Elf 
Worshippers: Predominantly Elves 
Domains: Air, Earth, Healing, Sun, Water, Good

Clerics of Aeridin often combine the Healing domains with one of the other domains.

Governs: Weather, dawn, rebirth, vitality, youth, sun, moons 

Dogma: 
     Preserve and protect life, but bear in mind that in the Great Cycle of life, death also has its place, so life should not be artificially prolonged. Seek out the undead and put them to rest, so they can rejoin the Great Cycle. Do not harm or kill others except in the most dire of circumstances. Do not refuse to aid those who need it.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing:
     In general, clerics of Aeridin prefer to wear white robes. They'll only don armor when absolutely necessary, and even then with great hesitation. However, if they do, they'll wear full plate, either coated with a layer of silver or - more rarely - made from mithril. Their armor is usually embossed with golden leaves.

     In general, they wield quarterstaffs and shun the use of maiming weapons like axes or greatswords. A necklace with a golden leaf is often worn around the neck as a holy symbol.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples to Aeridin can be found everywhere, from the largest city to the smallest village. Most also act as a house of healing for the wounded and the sick and as a place where the poor or unfortunate can find help to get their lives back on track. Spread far across all continents of Layonara, the Church of Aeridin stands in good regard with most peoples.

     Despite the Church's throng of followers, there is not a strong central hierarchy that dictates how the Church operates. There is a hierarchy at the local level, which is mostly based on seniority, not on the actual power a cleric is capable of wielding. All temple communities remain very much in contact.

     Clerics of Aeridin pray for their spells either at noon or during a full moon.

     Religious days are many and tied in to the positions of the sun and the moons. Nights where one of the moons is full hold special importance; however, nights where both Orn and Ausir are full are of prime importance.
