This is the golden Harp of Ilsare. Only one of these harps is known to exist and is rumored to have been crafted by Ilsare herself to be possessed solely by the Harper. 

Those who have possessed the harp have been rumored to  have been skilled diplomats, and stories of coaxing mortal enemies to put down their arms surround this item.

Vanavar Island
     In ages past, the only people to inhabit Vanavar were Gray Elves, who made the Broken Mountains their home. They dubbed the island Vanavar, or "strong-willed." However, as the humans expanded across the face of Layonara, they came to recognize Vanavar's strategic position and started settling the island. When Xandrial arrived, he too recognized the strategic value of Vanavar and was quick to send his forces in.
     Vanavar's forces were hardly prepared to face the hordes of the Demon Prince, and the Duke of North Hampton, as last resort, sent a messenger bird to Roldem, requesting aid and offering his allegiance to the King of Roldem if he came to Vanavar's aid. However, the Duke was too late, as Xandrial's forces arrived first and laid waste to all the settlements of the island. Now, only a few survivors are left and struggling to survive.
     With the Duke's patrols gone, Vanavar is now also an ideal base for pirates. Xandrial allows them to use the island's secluded coves as long as they don't interfere with his own ships.
Nobody knows what happened to the Gray Elves that inhabited the Broken Mountains, as they have not been heard from since the rise of the human settlements on Vanavar. It is unlikely that they still inhabit the mountains without lifting a finger against Xandrial, so it is likely that they were killed or left for Voltrex. However, no one truly knows the fate of the Vanavarian Grays.

Well-known Cities:

North Hampton
Location: Northern tip of Vanavar
Population: 150 
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Located at the northern tip of Vanavar, North Hampton was the major city of the island and one of Layonara's larger trading ports, acting mostly as a trade hub for ships from Westgate and Waysend as well as Rodez and Lorindar on the south. Now, after Xandrial nearly torched it to the ground, it is but a shell of its former self, its inhabitants either killed or enslaved.

Murdoch
Location: Southwestern tip of Vanavar
Population: 100
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Murdoch was just coming into its own, starting to becoming a prosperous village by taking Lorindar and Rodez trade from the larger city of North Hampton. Nothing much is left of it today except for a few families of fishermen, trying to survive and unable or unwilling to leave. Murdoch was the last town on Vanavar to be destroyed by Xandrial. Those that managed to flee the island did so from here.

Celine
Location: Southeastern tip of Vanavar
Population: 50
GP limit: 15
Alignment: Neutral Evil
Government: Nonexistent
Defenses: None
Miscellaneous information:
     Celine, located at the edge of Vanavar's scant forest, was a farmer's village, responsible for most of the food supply to the other towns on Vanavar. The mayor of Celine had plans to partner with the town of Murdoch to develop a shipyard building ships from the prime wood of Krelin's Forest. This scheme never came to fruition, however; together with North Hampton, Celine was one of the first Vanavarian towns to be destroyed.

Locales:

Broken Mountains
     The mountain range at the center of Vanavar breaks the island basically in two, so when the first human settlers arrived, the name Broken Mountains quickly took hold.
     Though inhabited by Gray Elves before the human incursion and Xandrial's attacks, no one is certain of the proud elder race's fate.

Krelin Forest
     An old but small forest of tall trees, the village of Celine had big plans to use the Krelin Forest's excellent wood to enter the shipyard business.

Description: The gauntlet resembles a gigantic forearm, inscribed with runes and symbols that trace the entire length of the gauntlet. In truth the gauntlet was tailored from the forearm of a giant. Hollowed out and dried the gauntlet is a ghastly piece and exhausts very unpleasant odours when subjected to water or other liquids.


Worn by Kei'rull "Bonebreaker" during his reign as chief of the giant tribes in the Thunder Peaks, this mighty gauntlet became his symbol of power and dominion over the tribes. By means of cunning negotiations and martial prowess the half giant Kei'rull boldly united 3 tribes and lead them into a succession of raids against the neighbouring human settlements or whomever passed too close to their territories. It is said that whenever a barrier was erected or a gate closed to block the path of Kei'rull's force the chieftain himself stepped forward and battered the barrier away with a mighty punch by his gauntleted right fist.
No one seemed able to oppose the might and rage of the giant army and so Kei'rull lead them ever onward, as far south as Fort Thunder. There the army was ambushed and savagely cut down by a mixed militia of dwarves from Clan Stonesmasher and humans from the surrounding settlements and towns.

Kei'rull, however, escaped the annihilation of his army and was believed to have travelled south. It is believed that Kei'rull became the leader of a band of brigands and cutthroats roaming the outskirts of the Forest of Fog. No further records exist regarding Kei'rull's fate, nor are there records that mention the reappearance of the gauntlet that marked him as chief and champion of the tribes.

Description: A plain platinum chain. The only thing that catches the eye is the singly tooth dangling from it. A tiny hole has been drilled into what much be the tooth of a large wolf allowing the chain to pass through it. 


The records describe Sharl Etris Abryn as an elven ranger and devout follower of the Prince of Wolves.
Sharl was bound to a path of vengeance by a crime long forgotten. He was relentless in his hunt for the cruel and hated orcs that roamed the vast Forest of Fog. Sharl was always seeking confrontation and battle with his avowed enemies, where he was wont to come out as the victor, but was never content with his victory.
Sharl was gifted the necklace by a priest of Folian S'pae to aid him in what was perceived as being devotion to his Lord and protection of the Forest in his name. In many ways Sharl lived up to those virtues, but more and more often his path was left littered with corpses. As years went by, Sharl began to enjoy the killing of his prey. What before had been the hunter's clean kill turned into a game of torture and senseless slaughter.

In the end it was his own blinding lust for dealing death that saw him killed. A group of adventurers passed through his territory, among them a female half orc. As Sharl spotted her he was overcome by rage, his mind clouded by lust for her blood. Sharl was no match for the swords and unveiled magic of the group. He was slain and laid to rest in a clearing, at the roots of a young oak tree.

Made by the loving hands of the halflings Kobal rescued from the clutches of Yegar and the Bloody Axe, this dooner is a patchwork of love and devotion, small halfling hands spending hours in handcrafting each individual path and sewing them together into a dwarf sized whole that radiates the gentle spirit of these people.
 
    Crafted delicately, this multicoloured display depicts different symbols of home and hearth that are intricately linked to Prunilla and her ideals of family and comfort.  Small woven images of Clovers and cornucopias, framed in wreaths of leaves all play across its warm and cosy surface. Colourful and benign they play, offering a small portable smattering of the joy and healing that is held within the hearts of individuals so caring.

    Lastly the dooner is reinforced by the blessings of many Lucky Clovers and given over to Prunilla's divine touch to supply a healing of both body and spirit whenever it is used to cover or warm the body. Its heat promoting mending and restoration of many ills that may afflict the wearer with its simple embrace of textured patchwork.

It is said this shield was formed when the four spirits of the dwarven clans once more gave the essence of the people back to the Mount, the very soul of those who were lost imbueing the lifeless dwarven home once more with the spirit of grace that was taken from The Crecent Moon and Shield.

    Rumour runs that after destruction of the bloodpool at the ancestral home, the four spirits, summoned and embodied forces of dwarven power appeared to Kobal and there were to diffuse the essence of what they were back to those who had gifted them life in the beginning.  So it was that the spirits dissipated, finally unbound and choosing to give back to the dwarves lost and scattered to time and atrocity.

    It is said that when these four spirits, Magic, Metal, Heat and Heart dissolved, a great work of magic formed in the dead and decaying heart of the clan homes, one that was bright with promise of new life and a gathering of force for the lost.

    Rumour would hold that the light in the centre of the homes persisted for many months, bright with magic and heat, drawing metals from the ground itself and infusing it with the very heart of the clan home itself.  Dwarves have come to say that the spirits as a last gift to Kobal left a portion of themselves, held in what was, when the light faded, revealed to be an extraordinary sheild.

   Beyond early manafacture this shield seems to contain four distinct metals, each cross section forged together seamlessly into a whole of cunning craftsmanship.  Each portion inscribed with a rune of incredible detail, the making of each lost to time, yet the meaning standing clear.

   The first section of pure mithril, bright and unbending it stands as the ultimate gift of metal, a defence from sharp swords or the crushing blows of the mace. The metal unmarred seems to have not been ever touched by hammer or blow, given as the deepest of dwarven delving and forged in the fires of dwarven spirit. Sitting proud in the centre of the quarter stands the dwarven mark for metal, seeming bound and part of the very mithril itself.

    The second quarter seems to be forged of purest adamantium, far purer than can by acquired by usual means of mining and smelting. Red in colour it seems to radiate waves of warmth, its surface a constant shimmer of heat haze. Blazoned proudly upon it sits the dwarven rune for Heat, once more bound to the adamantium itself.

   The third quarter forged of silver is marked with spell forces outlined with the fierce glow of starfire, one of the finest fuels of magic.  Emanating menace the singular rune seems to jump and play, pushing at the phantasms that distract the mind, pure threads of the weave marking out the indomitable dwarven will for all to see.  Within the centre of the starfire marked portion sits the dwarven rune for magic.

    The last quarter of the shield proves to be the strangest, formed from simple but effective iron it stands stalwart and of the earth. Unlike the rest of the shield the last portion is not immaculate, indeed it seems to have taken many blows and even sits tarnished in places, dents and scratches covering its plates.  However far from being the plainest of the four, this portion seems to truly show character, each mark scribing experience and personality to the shield with battles faced and overcome.  Sitting in the middle of the final quarter, traced in diamond dust sits the dwarven rune for spirit.


   Named Wall of the Four Thanes in respect for the four guardians now considered to be integral to the clans survival it is considered to be a mark of the Thane of the Crescent Moon and Shield, a replacement for the ring lost to the bloodpool of the old Thanes.  This significant artifact marks the start of a new era for the clans of Mount Norand.

These arrows are truly a rare sight outside the elven continent of Voltrex and even there they are far from common. Hand crafted from rare stones most often fond amidst the Peaks of Voltrex by a group of elven rangers guarding the mountain range, these arrows are rarely gifted to anyone outside the ranks of the ranger unit.

The Naatyam á Meneluin, known to humans as "The Sky Guard" or more literally "Keepers of the Blue Sky" take sometimes years to slowly hone the stones they call "Laecelam Nel" so that they will be sharp enough to serve as the point of an arrow. During the process they use secret oils and incantations to prevent the natural magical power of the stone from vanishing. Once finished the tip can serve the ranger trough multiple centuries, never losing its power as long as the ranger keeps regulating the magic trough a set of command words. Without such care however, the tip will soon lose any power it might have once held and for anyone not privy to the knowledge of the rangers it is often hard if not impossible to tap into its power.

The shaft and tail of the arrow may vary but the tip is always made of silver coloured, surprisingly light stone. On the stone, on both sides of the tip, two runes are carved. One of the runes is always the elven rune signifying both Light trough darkness and Ausir. The other rune is something personal to each ranger, something that allows them to separate their arrows from ones made by their brothers and sisters.

Somewhere around the year 1130 a human entrepreneur claimed that he had somehow succeeded in securing a large number of these arrows from a contact in Voltrex and managed to sell hundreds of them before the officials of the crown felt they had to step in and declared that the reason why people were not able to invoke any magical effects while using the arrows was not because they were inapt archers but rather because the arrows were fake.

Lost in the annals of time are the histories of those powerful mages and sorcerers who created the Academy of High Magery.  Their work is renowned as marvels of magic and those called by the Dragon can attest to the effects of their bindstones. 

An expedition to investigate baffling ruins uncovered by a local landslide on the eastern shores of Dregar lead to the discovery of 3 bags of small stone, among other artifacts.  Before the stones could be catalogued and sent on for further study they disappeared.  Oddly enough the Halfling in the archeological group disappeared the same night.  Within a year small stones began to appear on the black markets of most of the port towns.  Those versed in the arcane arts could recognize them as a repository of magic but one very old and complex.  There has been much scholarly debate about these stones but it is generally agreed upon they are the work of the Academy of High Magery.  Archmage Emile F'strame of the famed Ubem Academy of Pranzis and accepted authority on draconic artifacts recently posted a paper on the stones; stating them to be the work of Adepts with in the academy.  The fact that he magic contained within these stones seems to be draconic in origin is a bit unsettling. It is a good thing they have lost much of their potency over the tides of time.

This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind. Examined closely the pages seem to radiate the aroma of oak leaves. This collection of essays is clearly devoted to those involved the arts of tracking and observation.  The runic letter W appears on the back cover as a maker's mark. Upon use, the pages scatter like leaves in the wind.
This elaborately bound book appears to be a spell book of some kind.

In a time not too long ago, The Hall of Norand was restored after a long age of destruction and chaos brought on by the forces of Sinthar Bloodstone, who laid rein to this place of Dwarven skill and beauty.  With the aid of companions and many of the Dragon called of Layonara, a leader emerged to destroy the evil that brewed in the depths and bring back some of what once was.  It is said that after a battle that lasted for many days and a victory was reached that a Blessed Mithril Spirit spoke clearly these words "To the clans... I return metal, the land will flourish and deposits once dead awaken at dwarven touch.  May axes find only richness in the stones of the mountains."  Then her form glowed brightly a moment and like many fireflies, bursts to show the rock at her feet.  

These sets of armor were the first armors crafted in the Hall of Norand by the reforged Crescent Moon and Shield.  The armor's properties are inspired by the leadership shown as events transpired that day.  For as the Dwarven Hero and his companions ascended from the depths of the Halls, worn and beaten, dirtied and bruised with the wounds of war, despite the sadness in his features, the spark of perhaps pride in the dwarf's eye shone through.  The beauty of this armor reflects that spark for as the clan began to return slowly, the first order of business was a commemoration of the epic moment.  Picks were bought and rock was smashed from the very sides of the Halls and the armors were painstakingly worked to reflect all the emotion in the features of the Dwarven Leader.

The plainly bound book appears to be one of chicken recipes.  One versed in the short hand of street thieves might recognize it for what it is.  Attributed primarily to Branderback mages, this book surfaces from time to time, but generally they are kept well hidden.

As many know, the town of Katherian is often full of crimes.  In order to be better protected from those who would wish to lighten loot chests, many go so far as to put traps on their doors when they sleep at night, instead of just your normal locks.  Rumor has it that the creation of these belts were inspired by what a cleric of Shadon saw one dismal night in the very docks of Katherian.

It was from the shadows that eve, this priest of Shadon peered, content with himself after a successful night of his own trickery and mischief.  He caught a glimpse of a young raven-haired elf whom he began to watch curiously as she stepped from hiding to pick the lock of the front door of the house.  Obviously from out of town, or perhaps just so excited that she picked the lock, the elf failed to realize the door was trapped.  Once unlocked, she tried to open the door, only to set off an intense electrical trap.  Although she tried to escape, she just wasn't quick enough to retreat from the lightning's bolts and ended up falling to a shocking death.  The Cleric laughed at her mishap, but was inspired to create an item that might help with the retreat of such situations.  In thanks of the idea, and in his amusement, the cleric raised the elf and sent her on her way simply saying, "Don't do that".  This is one of such belts, inspired from that dark Katherian night.

After the dust cleared from Operation Bloodfall on Roldem, The Wolfswood Rangers were shocked and saddened to hear of the fatality of their Commander in charge.  The Commander's passing was mourned greatly amongst the troop.  Yet with the tragedy came a glimpse of hope as a hero amongst many and a stalwart ranger rose to the promotion.  It was under the new guidance of this Commander, the Rangers began massive efforts to restructure, rearm, and outfit the Corps.  

These bows were fashioned during that time by only the best woodcrafters, and given an extra blessing from the Longstrider, Folian S'pae.  When armed with the bowstring tucked amongst your fingers, the feel of the bow heightens your very senses, awakening your eyes and ears to your surroundings to let your arrows strike hard and true.

Ancient tomes speak of this skull having once been that of a great wizard who sought to overcome the bonds of death.  While his spirit has long since been vanquished a part of him remains within this skull.  When placed upon the head of the worthy, this skull reveals its true nature.

Slightly north of the forest of the Mist on the continent of Dregar spans a mountain range known as Blackfeather Mountains.  It is said that years ago the Broken Glade Giants drove away flocks of crows that had made home in the eastern parts of the forest, forcing them towards the North.  The crows flapped wildly around for days of unrest after being forced from their home, until finally coming to rest on the nearby mountain range.  Some say if you walk through one of the abandoned dwarf trails at the foot of the mountain, you will find a layer of crow's feathers at your feet.

The origin of this necklace is thought to be that very place.  Rumor has it that along with the crows, a powerful shaman also inhabits the mountains.  Strangely however, those who go looking for him either never seem to find him, or never come back.  It's said that on some nights when Ausir and Orn sit just right in the sky, the Shaman of Blackfeather Mountains comes out.  His slender elven figure can be seen in the moonlight as he makes his way through the dwarf trails picking up and blessing the crow feathers with powerful magics.  Once strung together feathers give gifts of the night.  Though a powerful aid, it's important to be weary of artifacts such as this since nobody knows what exactly the Shaman had in mind when creating them.

Growing on the skirts of the Ire Mountains, right at the edge where they meet the blazing sun of the Spirit Dunes, this strange small flower grows only during the first and few days of rain in the region.

Once collected it is normally regrown in milder weathers, but those few that manage to survive the unkind desert weather gain a unique quality.

When held high, The Desert Firstbloom Wildflower bathes the area in a brilliant blue light. This light seem to recall travellers of the stars gleaming in the desert skies, thus why some locals call it the Starlit Bud.

A few enterprising individuals who experimented with the flower discovered that if the petals are torn a stream of positive energy spews forth from its stem. Destroying the flower, yet healing wounds at a miraculous rate.

In the days when Elf fought man and dwarf alike, there existed a company of fine archers that were the bane of many an enemy troop.  Their bows were the things of legend and even after some semblance of peace arose between the nations, they were still coveted by many an archer.  Bows were handed down through families and cherished as heirlooms such that even the training versions of the more elite bows become treasures.  You see before you the bow of an elf that had obtained a more direct link with his weapon.  As such his dedication and training made the arrows fly true and strike with greater force upon the opponent.  It is no wonder the sight of these bowmen on a wall put fear in to the hearts of their opponents. The fine craftsmanship of this weapon attests for the link between elf and his bow, as such only ones of elven descent may use it.
This rope seems to have been greased at one time. Perhaps it was to allow the one that was going to hang a chance to escape if their neck was not broken.

In the third age of Layonara, when the Soul Mother's power began to thrive and her lust for more brought her to reach out for the dominion of life, a cleric of Aeridin rose up to stop her.  In this effort, with the support of companions and friends, he was able to weaken her hold on the souls of the world.  In their success, a new sensation was felt throughout the world as his actions caused a ripple to be felt and soul strands were returned.  Those once lost to her began to return, a hero of Layonara truly had evolved. 

To thank this hero the temple of Aeridin at North Point created several pairs of gloves made from the gentlest of material and blessed for healing.  In the true essence of Athus, the gloves were used to heal the sick and wounded, nursing them back to health so that they might continue down their path to the greater destiny that awaits them.

A heavy plate mail armor constructed of a platinum alloy metal.  Due to the bulkiness of the armor the wearer is somewhat restricted in his movement, or is there something else at work.

Long ago a series of these plate mail armors were fashioned for a group of warriors that Bloodstone sought to employ as mercenaries.  Knowing the nature of mercenaries, Bloodstone enchanted the armors to better control his soldiers.  To this end he imprisoned the soul of lesser demon.  The demon feeds off the lifeforce of those who attack the wearer, but such is not without cost.

For as the Dwarven Hero and his companions ascended from the depths of the Halls, worn and beaten, dirtied and bruised with the wounds of war, it was clear that their courage and will was tried and tested.  This shield is an inspiration for those who use it, for as the clan began to return slowly, the first order of business was a commemoration of the epic moment.  Picks were bought and rock was smashed from the very sides of the Halls and the shields were painstakingly worked to reflect the all will and discipline displayed by the heroes.

It has a small maker's inscription in back corner that resembles the runic letters AA. Upon use the parchments glow and then fade to nothingness.
It is said that a Cleric of Dorand blessed these ornate rings to aid his adepts in the more exacting detailing of his weapons. Just how they made it out into the general population is unknown.

It is said that a cleric of Dorand blessed these simple and utilitarian rings to aid his apprentices in the completion of the detailing of his weapons. Just how they made it out into the general population is unknown.

A magnificent weapon Latyemean'Ceviran boasts the finest of Elven craftmanship. It glows softly with an inner light, rune edged blade melting seamlessly into ornate crossguard and finely wrapped hilt. Perfectly balanced the blade is an extension of the hand for those chosen.

  Yet beyond the workmanship it is the intricate elven runes traced upon the surface that catch the eye. For those runes tell the tale of the blade, from forging onwards.   Over the years the tale has lengthened, the story adding itself in elven scripture to the blade itself, writing its history as it is once more wielded by a new owner. As the tale of the owner lengthens the blade becomes more potent, molding itself to the needs, and the fears of the one who uses it.

For those who can read the runes the tale reads:


    "Forged in fire to fight the dark, thus where all birthed. To four families did we go, receptacles to traits that they hold. Secret not given, need to be found, make the mark on the metal he ground.

  Two families found the grace of blades, one died and was lost, and I, the other never made. 

  Generation passed. Onto the next I moved, a son who had no desire for the blade. His talents called elsewhere, to the arcane he gave.

  A Knight he was made, to fight the dark until grave, yet none could see the impression the first had gave.

  Turn he did, fled under dark moon. Heirloom was all he took from his room. His family wept for the son they lost, the blade was forgotten as a loss of trust.

  Under the earth light grew dim, rust coated the surface, runes grew thin, the bearer, this shard of a soul committed evil after evil and we all grew old. 

  Death came at last as to all it does. Placed in a tomb, a relic of the past. There the blade sat until one picked it up.

  The shard reunited with its brothers a portion he left. Enough for the blade to pick up its true gift.

  Hands of righteous blade did find, hands that swung in place divine. Justice was met on swift knife edge, dispensation with holy Toranite pledge.

  Evil vanquished in tides and flood, dimmed runes brightend in paths of blood. Traces of heart in majesty found, yet runes and sigils to dull upon ground.

  For in a compassionate heart weakness found root, a place of love, shoulder of despair, deception was found in a heart once so fair.

  Holy Toranite vows forgotten, misplaced, the paladin fell from Torans shining grace. Standing head bowed, golden crown stricken, titles and roles now duly forbidden.

  Yet for paths feet found, lost in human embrace, the story continues to travel apace. In Torans grace will it ascend once more, or will it be caught in passionate encore?

Altáriël Nénharma, an elf of middling years with a shock of red hair and bright blue eyes.  She has a playful demeanor and is very rarely seen without at least a politically correct smile on her face or laughter gracing her elfin features.  Energetic and good natured some say she was elected by the Council due to her great love for The Weave and all things that it governs. Yet those who know her well find this to be a false on an epic scale, for behind the smiling eyes and easy nature sits a mind that is sharp, observant and willing to see that her Goddess is preserved at all costs.
This is a receipt for a temple donation.

An unusual tome... written by a powerful mage and scriber... for his less than intelligent friend.

It came to the mage Arian, whilst traveling with his rather burly friend in the Forest of Fogs.

They were beset upon by a group of giants, and instantly the two dived into battle to defend themselves.

The mage called forth all forms of the Al'noth to dispose of his enemies, slaying a group of six in a matter of moments.

When done, he turned to observe his muscular warrior friend, desperatly fighting for his life against a single, lone giant.

The suddeness off the battle allowed no time for the mage to cast wards upon his friend.

And so it came to him.
A book of basic spells, scribed with special enchantments and magical runes.
His friend would merely have to touch the runes inscribed upon the parchment, and speak the words printed... and the spell would be cast.

Tempests' arrows... not to be confused with the Mistite High Priest or Priestess.

Sallaron Tempest, a rather dubious individual, famed in Hurm for his Ant-Slaving works, combined his master fletching skills with the rather explosive skills of the Al'noth his wife possessed.

The result was these... finely crafted, hollow tipped arrows.. each with a small enchantment placed by his sorceress wife which.. on impact, covers the target in a small flaming spell.

Rumour tells that, upon the first batch being created, his wife made him the official "guinea pig" for their testing.

A very rare and powerful item when used for the purpose of its creation.
The bracers themselves are a dark, sandy colour, and the leather seems to have a worn depiction of a figure in a long, dark coat.

Rumour has it they were created by a Conjurer in Spellgard, their design inspired by a man of some small reknown in battling and dealing with those from other planes.

All rumour of course, but whether summoning or holding back the beings that dwell in the Pits and numerous Planes, these bracers provide a sturdy defense against what we would rather not have creep into our world.

Rumour has it Rhizome the Wanderer himself, took down a weak branch from an ancient oak tree, and blew on, joining it with the air and sky.

Whether this is true or not is uncertain, though if one were to ever come across the elusive man it may be wise to ask.

Held in the palm, a simple and gentle blow breathed upon them activates a powerful blessing, as the wind rises all around to push and hasten the bearer and his allies for a short time.

Aliases: The Lady of the Sea, Lady Doom  
Race: Human 
Alignment: CN 

Worshippers: Mist draws worshippers from all races, with none being particularly dominant. Followers of Mist are, however, predominantly drawn from those who rely upon the sea or hold a particular reverence for it.

Cleric Alignments: CG, TN, CE, CN

Domains: Air, Destruction, Strength, and Water.

Governs: Oceans, winds, currents, storms, rebellion 

Clergy and Temples:
Temples of Mist tend to be situated near the ocean, open to the sea breeze where possible. Buildings appear light and delicate, but always contain hidden strength sufficient to withstand any unexpected storm. The whole interior is usually bathed in a subtle blue light, and visitors can always feel moisture and the tang of the sudden storm biting against their skin. Pools of water are common and are often found placed at seemingly random intervals throughout the complex, though many speculate that there is reason in such seemingly odd placements.



Constellation:
Mist’s constellation, ‘Ladies of the Seas’, as it is called is oddly both erratic and stationary all the time. Puzzling many astrologists and clerics Mist’s eight star constellation has one of all of it’s eight stars pointing in a different direction, North, South, East, West, North East, South East, North West, and South West, and is known to most as the Heavenly Compass. 
It has no real divine power other than in the words of the clerics of Mist, being “a blessing given to those of the sea by Lady Doom.” It is perhaps the greatest tool that a sailor can have. However, Mist would not be called Lady Doom if it was always useful. Supposedly, those who have fallen from Her graces can get misdirected and sail to their dooms when sailing with the aid of the Heavenly Compass.


Many sailors have also told stories of Mist’s ‘Ladies of the Seas’ actually overlapping Shindaleria’s ‘Great Tide’ in what some say is a show of power in a great rivalry.

Death vines are a much more recherché cousin to the assassin vine. Stronger, faster and more deadly these rare vines are said, despite thier name, to hold healing properties within their leaves.

Branderback
Aliases: The Wary Shadow, The Black Hound  
Race: Halfling 
Worshippers: Halflings, humans, half-elves.
Domains: Evil, Trickery, Destruction
Governs: Stealth, night, darkness, greed, self-preservation 

Dogma: 
     Branderback teaches his followers to live their lives to their fullest extent. There should be no limit to what one may desire, and if you can obtain it, then there is no reason why you should not have it. Branderback also teaches that although temporary allegiances with like-minded groups are necessary, you should always depend on yourself. Never be caught unaware, and have a backup plan to the backup plan. If all else fails, always blame someone else; why should you take the blame for something that was meant to happen?

Clergy's Weapons and Clothing. 
     Branderback's clerics prefer ranged weapons, especially those that can be enchanted to disable your opponents. Acid and poison are also acceptable, since they can be used to enhance arrows or darts and weaken foes. Clerics of The Wary Shadow garb themselves in black leathers to be concealed, and prefer to hide their skins to avoid having weak spots.

Clergy and Temples:
     Temples of Branderback are rare and normally hidden from the eye. Most of them are facets of the underworld and can often be found in alliance with a local thieves guild. Rankings are very rare since most clerics of Branderback are loners, but it is rumored that every major region is under the watch of a High Silent Shadow, a very powerful and gifted cleric. Clerics of the Black Hound pray at dusk to welcome the coming of the night, and they celebrate Winter's Solstice since it is the longest night of the year.

Prayers:
While getting spells:
     "Let my acts be hidden in the shadows of the night, so that I may gain that which is rightfully mine."

When doing something fishy:
     "I pray that wealth belong to the greedy and careless, so that I may take from them what is rightfully mine."

This sturdy blacksmith's anvil bears the dented sheen of long use. Something in you wonders what great weapons and armor have been shaped upon its well-worn surface. 

This is a Bindstone to Dorand. The energy emitting from this powerful Bindstone touches your very soul.

Description: A thick woollen cloak. It has a sturdy look to it and it has not seen much wear. On the inner side of the cloak, near the neck, the two letters S. and A. are traced with silver thread in elvish style writing. 


Looted from an elven grave in the Forest of Fog, the previous history of this cloak remains a mystery. Since the appearance of the cloak it has been traded or forcibly changed hands several times. The unique craftsmanship in combination with the magical investments make "Balance" an item wanted by many. The cloak's past is a stained by bloodshed and betrayal, yet the cloak itself remains untarnished.

The Basics of Alchemy
-----------------------------------

1) The art of alchemy consists of brewing potions.  Potions consist of two or more main ingredients. 

2) Essences are made by combining several ingredients and pouring the mixture into a glass vial. 

3) Potions are made by combining an essence and various ingredients along with an empty flask. This is also done at the Alchemists Table.

4) Unsuccessful, attempts at alchemy will destroy recipe ingredients, but glass vial and flasks will remian.

The Basics of Baking
----------------------------------

1) Baking allows the creation of many  things, such as, bread and pies. 

2) Gathered grains can be converted to flours or meals using the Farmer’s mill.
 
3) Oils can be crafted out of many grains and nuts using the Farmer’s Press.

4) Juices can be crafted out of fruits also by using the Farmer’s Press. 

5) Eggs can be gathered from chickens by feeding them either corn grains or corn meal, although they will produce eggs three times faster eating corn meal. 

6) Milk can be gathered from cows by feeding them a variety of different grains. Cows prefer some grains above others and will oblige you for your donations by producing milk faster. 

7) Flour, eggs, milk, salt, sugar and fruits are typical ingredients used in the bread and pie recipes. These can be crafted by the Baker’s Oven.

The Basics of Brewing
-----------------------------------

1) Brewing beer, wine and liquor begins with the gathering of wheat grains. Corn, barley, wheat, rice, rye and oat grains. 

2) Grains must be roasted to bring out their flavor using the Brewer's Oven. 

3) The Farmer’s Mill is then used to crack the roasted grains to produce malted gain.

4) Malted grain can then be combined with other natural resources and cooked to make wort using the Brewer’s Kettle.

5) Finally, the wort and sugar are combined with water and bottles in the Brewer’s Keg.

Basics of Enchanting
---------------------------------

1) Enchanters can make a variety of items as well as enchant weapons, armor and shields. Enchanters require items made by Tinkering, Gem Crafting, Weapon Crafting, Armor crafting, Baking, Alchemy and Smelting. 

2) Enchanters use the following crafting devices: 

Enchanting Alter: Used to create elemental bags, enchanted gems and enchanted ingots. 

Enchanting Statue: Used to enchant shields. 

Enchanting Pool: Used to enchant weapons.

Cloth: 2 cotton

Padding: 1 cloth and 2 cotton

Patterns: 1 Book of Patterns and 1 cloth

Hides: 1 animal skin, 1 curing salt,  and 1 tanning acid 

Leathers: 1 cured animal hide and 1 tanning oil

Light Bow String: 2 spider silk and 2 almond oil

Sling: 1 bat leather and 1 pattern

Belt: 1 badger leather and 1 belt pattern

Gloves: 2 rat leather and 1 glove pattern

Boots: 2 deer leather and 1 boot pattern

Cloak: 2 cloth and 1 cloak pattern

The Basics of Gem Crafting
-------------------------------------------

1)  The process of working with gems is a very detailed one that involves multiple steps and multiple crafting devices. These are as follows: 

Gem Deposits:  First you must gather gem minerals from the gem deposits. 

Gem Cutting Stone: Used to cut gems. 

Gem Crafters Table: Used to detail cut gems. 

Mineral Wash: Used to identify the mystery minerals that are found while mining. 

Jewelers Bench: Used to create rings, scarabs, necklaces and amulets. 

2) To begin, the player must locate a gem deposit and successfully dig an uncut gem mineral. The player must have a Gem Chisel equipped in order to mine gem minerals.

3) Once a gem mineral is extracted, it needs to be cut. This is done at the Gem Cutting Stone. The player will need to have a Set of Gem Crafter’s Tools in their inventory. This process will yield either cut gems or flawed gems and gem dust as a bi-product. 

4) To detail a cut gem, the player will again need to have a Set of Gem Crafter’s Tools in their inventory. This process is done at the Gem Crafters Table and will yield either fine gems or flawed gems. 

5) To create rings, necklaces, scarabs and amulets, the player must use the Jewelers Bench. These items require a mold, enchanted gems and enchanted ingots. 

6) Occasionally, players will find mystery minerals while mining. These minerals can be identified by washing them in the Mineral Bath.

The Basics of Scribing
----------------------------------

1) Scribing begins with the collection of sawdust produced by the carpenter’s bench. 

2) Saw dust must be used to make raw parchment at the farmer’s press.

3) The raw parchment is then baked into scrolls by the baker’s oven.

4) Inks are made at the scribing ink desk using misc plant resources. 

5) Finally, the scrolls and Inks can be combined along with a spell to produce a scroll.

The Basics of Tinkering
--------------------------------------

1) Tinkering requiresa set of tinkers tools in. Tinkers can make a variety of different items ranging from glass ingots to crafting tools to deadly traps. These items are created at the following crafting devices: 

Tinkers Device: This strange looking device is used to create arrowheads and misc tinkering items. 

Tinkers Toolkit: This device is used to create traps and crafting tools. 

Tinkers Furnace: This device is very similar to the forge, except that it makes molds, glass ingots, and various glass products. 

2) Tinkering uses two raw materials that can be mined. These are sand and clay. To mine these, the player must have a Shovel in their inventory. 

3) Sand deposits yield bags of sand and clay deposits yield lumps of clay. 
4) Shovels, like the miner’s pickaxes, will wear out from time to time when used.

The Basics of Wood Crafting
---------------------------------------------

1) Wood crafting combines carpentry, bow crafting and fletching. 

2) Wood Crafting also involves harvesting wood. This is done by equipping a Woodcutter’s Axe and using it to bash a Hickory Tree, a Mahogany Tree or an Oak Tree. 

3) Trees produce branches that can be turned into wood shafts, wood planks and wood staves.

4) To create wood crafting items, the Carpenters Bench must be used while possessing a Set of Carpenter’s Tools.

Layonara's Most Notable Legends and Artifacts

The Bardic Block
     There is really nothing worse, except maybe finding slaad eggs in your food rations, but imagine, if you will: it's been a long day, most of which you've spent slaving in fields, slaughtering monsters, or studying the arcane arts. You settle down in a comfy chair and relax with an ale in the local inn. To your dismay, a bard strikes up, possibly the worst you've ever heard, certainly worse than me. As I'm sure we've all experienced, heckling never works, and simply killing them doesn't go down too well with local law enforcement. 
     A quick-thinking mage, however, found a solution to our little dilemma. After several nights of trouble with a local bard, Svern Cinderbrow decided to get his own back. He returned to his home and set about creating a coin with a secret bite to it. A simple gold coin that, once placed into a hand, silenced the recipient for anywhere from three to four hours. 
     The following evening, he approached the bard and placed the coin into the bard's hand, apologizing for his behavior of late. The bard would have thanked him, but the coin had already taken effect. This idea became so successful that Svern went into business with a local merchant, and became wealthy from sales of his miracle coin. 
     This venture came to a dramatic end when Svern and his partner were found beaten to death in an alley beside a local inn, broken lutes smeared with blood and brains lying nearby. Unfortunate as it was, they definitely "coined" the phrase: "Silence is golden." 

Gates to Heaven, Gates to Hell,
Gates to Planes one knows so well.
Gates to commerce, Gates to war,
Gates to oblivion, Gates to lore.
Alas!  Mordinar's Shimmering Gates are no more.
          -old Dregarian tavern song

Coup de Grace
     The Coup de Grace, or the Final Strike, as it is sometimes called, is a true legend. Heralded as the greatest fencing sword in Mistone, the Coup de Grace has only possibly surfaced twice in recorded history. Rumored to have been created by the dwarven smith Berhand Silverbeard, the existence of this item has never been truly confirmed.
     One such record is of orcish origin; therefore slightly less trustworthy. This depiction speaks of a shining metal needle, two and a half feet in length, which shimmered brightest blue as it was swung, as if it cut the air itself. Obviously I retell this depiction with a touch more flair than its original author; Orcish never translates delicately to Common (or any other language, for that matter). Nevertheless, the tale tells of a war band ambushing a passing shopkeep, a successful raid until a passing rider stopped to aid the stricken merchant. The orcs tell of a brilliant flash of blue when they charged the rider, who was either elven or human. Blinking, they looked back to see the head of their warleader tumble from his shoulders, his chain coif sliced through with a cleaner cut than could be believed. They then mention a "dr'gonba," or "tactical retreat," which in Orcish means "running away without screaming too loudly." Although a rough translation, this is said to be the first recorded sighting of this wondrous weapon. 
     The second account tells of another orc encounter, this time with a guard patrol. Records show an eight-man patrol was ambushed by fifteen or so orcs, well-armed and well-organized. Beaten down, the men were bound, gagged and prepared for their execution by beheading. The first was brought to the block, and his head removed with two swings of the chief's greataxe. However, as the second was brought to the block, a cloaked figure appeared in the light-dappled forest clearing. 
     Again the record tells of a fantastic blue flash as the blade was drawn, this time by a character of small stature, dwarven or tall halfling. The blade was said to scream as it moved, again as though the air itself felt the keenness of its edge. The guards' record tells of "armor cut through as though it were paper." The orcs rapidly fell to the well-armed opponent, only scoring one hit during the battle. Once battle was over, the cloaked figure unbound one of the men and vanished into the blackness of the forest. 
     Blood trails from the cloaked figure were picked up the next day by trackers, but the trail was lost just beyond the Zainge River. This is the last known record of this sword. 

The Forge Golem
     Deep beneath the Swordrust Mountains, it is rumored that there once existed a dwarven smith, living in seclusion and plying his trade undisturbed by the outside world. With only his golem as company, it is said that Berhand Silverbeard created some of the most impressive weapons ever seen on Layonara. His monstrous forge, which supposedly was fueled by lava from the continent's crust, was kept at such a heat that only his golem could approach it.
     Few of his weapons have ever been seen; even those that are said to be born of his hand could not be proven so. He was so proud of his weapons that he refused to taint them with a trademark. One rumored weapon is the Coup de Grace, a rapier so fine it can open plate armor with a single slash. This weapon, however has its own story. 
     The tale of his demise is handed down in dwarven lore and bardic songs, and while the details vary each time it is told, the basics remain the same. 
     Legend has us believe he was nearing completion of his finest work, a mighty broadsword called Legacy. Said to have power unlike any other on Mistone, his crowning work was to be his last before his return to the surface. With a blade of forged adamantium folded over two hundred times, the sword was a sparkling example of true craftsmanship. However, the light of day was never to grace his old eyes, misfortune and a temper as hot as his forge saw fit to that. 
     In the final stages of his work, Legacy was to be tempered once more before its completion. The golem approached the forge, as it had done many a time before, placing the blade into the flames. Unfortunately the blade slid from the golem's hand, disappearing into the flames. Berhand ran forward, screaming as his most prized creation disappeared into the flames. He smashed his smith hammer into the golem's head, cursing it for its foolishness and demanding that it retrieve the lost blade. 
     At its master's command, the golem strode into the flames, melting with each step it took. It is claimed that the golem retrieved the blade, only to bring the forge down around it. The resulting explosion killed Berhand as his workshop crumbled around him, burying the countless treasures of his life's work along with him. 
     Rumors say that his golem, however, instead of being destroyed, became one with the lava and molten metal, and still strides the destroyed halls, blade in hand, in desperate search for its lost master. 

Karrak's Weaponry
     Several centuries ago, when Xantril was still called the Roughlands, the Guild of Power was the place where fighters and weapon masters from all over Layonara came to practice and hone their skills to perfection.
     Once every decade, the Guild's founder, Karrak, and his successors would host the Guild Championships, one for every type of melee weapon. The Championships would go on for weeks, but in the end, there would be a winner for every type of melee weapon. These skilled fighters would then be anointed Master of the weapon in question.
     This was not just a ceremonial title, as the new Masters would also receive the Master's Weapon. These weapons were specially commissioned by Karrak when he founded his Guild, and a Master would bear the weapon for a decade. These weapons were not just ceremonial, but things of beauty and power. A Master's weapon could be recognized by the Guild of Power's emblem somewhere on the weapon's striking surface.
     Unfortunately, the Guild has been destroyed and Karrak's weaponry has been scattered across the continents, the owners probably not even aware of the history and the power of the weapons they possess. 

Rainstorff
     Rainstorff was a special kind of dwarf, and the greatest dwarven fighter ever to walk on Layonara. During his life he did a great many deeds: he built, or helped to build, a great dwarven fortress in the Berhagen Mountains, but found that he could not yet settle down there and took up adventuring again, at which point another dwarf, Ullgrid, took over the construction and rule of the fortress. Rainstorff set out again to continue his adventures in the Roughlands, building quite a reputation there, aiding all those who needed aid. While traveling the Roughlands, Rainstorff and his party came upon a mysterious poem about Fields of Bone, which drew them to Rilara right around the time that Milara appeared there. 
     When on Rilara, Rainstorff was called to aid the dwarves of Bloody Gate in their fight against the invader. He then disappeared for almost a year, and rumor has it he was captured by Milara. However, when questioned, he refused to discuss his absence.
     He returned to the Roughlands, and when he thought he was ready to settle down after his many years of adventuring, he was elected King of the Roughlands. 
     He was a strong ruler, defending his lands together with his Guards, the Red Axe Warriors, who had named themselves after Rainstorff's Red Axe. When they charged into battle they cried "Battle is Honor," and to honor them in return, Rainstorff had these words engraved on the blade of his Red Axe.
     He was loved and worshipped by his subjects, and he established good diplomatic relationships with nearly all races.
     However, not all agreed with his rule. He was sought out by Fisterion the Red, a mighty dragon who was raiding the Roughlands at the time. Dwarf and dragon battled for nearly a day, and the ground trembled as they fought. As both neared exhaustion with neither having a clear advantage over the other one in battle, they came to respect each other's strength, and so Fisterion and Rainstorff came to an arrangement. 
     Fisterion had to quit raiding the countryside and was never to return to the Roughlands, but he could keep his lair. In return the dragon would not be killed today, nor hunted down for a three month period. If Fisterion refused to cease his raids, Rainstorff and his Red Axe Warriors would hunt him down and kill him. Fisterion moved his lair to Firesteep, but since that day harbors a hatred of all dwarves, especially Rainstorff.
     Rainstorff then performed the largest and most important deed in his life. His god, Vorax, was imprisoned in the Plane of Hate and Loss, but Rainstorff, with the aid of his companions, managed to save his god. And now, according to popular dwarven tavern songs, Rainstorff never died, but was made immortal by Vorax.

Through the Looking Glass
     I wonder what Alice might have said if she had picked up this looking glass? I may ask the very same about any of you, for looking into its depths for too long, you are sure to see something you would not expect. 
     It is said that this mythical item was created by a demon bound to Layonara, cursed to remain there as a slave to his master. Through the ages, however, master and slave grew closer, eventually becoming as close to friends as a demon and elf can become. Legends would have us believe the master created a mirror, imbued with the power to see through the planes, allowing his slave to view his home whenever he chose to. 
     Upon the death of the master, the slave was returned to his home plane, taking the mirror with him. Curiously, rumors say that the mirror's effect was reversed in this moment, allowing the holder to view Layonara at any time they chose. 
     If true, this artifact could prove incredibly dangerous in the wrong hands.

The Blood Wells
     Of the many great evils Sinthar Bloodstone brought to Layonara, Blood Wells are one of the more mysterious. These gaping energy portals create an aura of negative energy around them, causing irreparable harm to those close by. It is said a soul lost near a Blood Well is lost forever.
     Although the actual function of the Blood Wells are a mystery, it is a popular theory that they may have been used to increase Bloodstone's power either on Layonara or on the plane he was banished to. How they were created is yet another mystery. The exact number of Blood Wells across Layonara is unknown, and it is unlikely that all of them remain active. 
     Blood Wells should not be confused with the portals Sinthar used to re-enter Layonara, which, although damaging, hold nowhere near the destructive force of the failed portals around the Forsaken Isles. It is claimed any mortal to pass near the Forsaken Isles will be instantly twisted in to an undead monster. It is thought that a hole was torn in the negative plane when Blood's portals failed and collapsed. A disaster indeed, but possibly fortunate as well, for had they not failed, Sinthar would most likely rule Layonara by now. 
     "In every dark action, there is good. Look hard enough, and it is always there."

Stones of Traveling
     According to legend, there are four powerful Stones of Traveling in the world. Each stone has three buttons and the number of that stone on it. If a button is pushed and then one walks through the stone, they will end up at the stone of the same number as the button that was pushed.

The Loaded Deck
     Cards: a game for gentlemen and rogues, where each endsup cheating as often as the other. Loaded decks are not an uncommon thing, tricks like marking cards, weighting cards to disrupt a shuffle, and so on are relatively commonplace. There is one deck, however, which is said to be loaded with more than "luck." 
     The story goes that a fallen noble, giving up his business and title, fell into a lifestyle of gambling. After several fights concerning cheating in a local tavern, the noble decided to protect himself against these brawls. 
      He approached a local gnomish weapon smith, known for his bouts of insanity when it came to the creation of weapons. The gnome was so impressed with the noble's idea that although the noble offered all his winnings from previous nights, the gnome took on the project for free. His only request was that his name should be stamped on his creation.
     A few short weeks passed, and the noble returned to the gnome with his luck on the up. There on the table lay a stunning deck of cards. Made of silver, the cards were wafer thin, beautifully crafted to resemble a normal deck to the unexpecting eye. The final trick, however, came when the cards were contorted a certain way, the corners folding out to form a shuriken stamped with the name of the gnome. 
     Happy with his new deck, the young man returned to the tavern for another evening of poker. With all weapons left at the door, the poker game began. The evening progressed and it became apparent that one member of the group's luck seemed to be far greater than  the others'. The noble suggested a change of deck, trying to avoid the imminent brawl. Things rapidly went from bad to worse as the lucky man rose from his chair, and a good five feet of the floor, for that matter. 
     His glowing hands struck at two of the men as they fled in fear, burning great frozen marks into their backs. A third stood and swung his chair at the mage, only to be frozen in mid swing. The noble panicked, quickly flicking out one of his new cards. With a lucky shot, the first luck he had seen all night as it was, he planted the shuriken between the eyes of the mage. Gathering his winnings, he fled the town. 
     Upon daybreak the four were found slain, three by cold burns, one with a silver star in his forehead. The only clue found was a name, stamped on the rear of the star. The gnome was quickly found and executed. 
     The cards, however, seem to show up across Mistone from time to time, identifiable only by the name Jan Tong embossed on the back.

Pealing Doom
     This item has been claimed to originate on another plane of existence, for it is said no mortal could ever create such a terrible item. The item in question is a brass bell, simple in its appearance, yet terrifying in use. Forged in two parts, the bell handle creates a circle of silence that surrounds those who hold the bell. The bell base, however, creates the most terrible noise when used; prolonged exposure to this noise is said to paralyze and kill, yielding an effect similar to a banshee's wail.
     The only known appearance of this item on Layonara was in what is now Haven, almost two hundred years ago. It is said that the bell was found by a bard down on his luck, having sold his lute to feed himself. 
     Considering his luck for only a second, he ran towards the bustling marketplace, aiming to put on a show for the busy shoppers and merchants. He arrived in the market, found himself a good vantage point, and began to toll his bell. Confused by the lack of sound, he shook the bell more and more violently. Despondent, he stopped shaking the bell, only to look up to see the devastation he had caused. Not a single soul in the market was left alive; almost a hundred people, from rich merchants to the lowest peasant, lay dead, bleeding from their ears. 
     It is said the bard dropped the bell in shock, sounding its terrible noise once more... 
     This is the last known record of the bell, resigned to paper by an unknown source and left at the scene of the disaster. It is unknown whether the bell was taken by the authorities who discovered the scene, or by the "person" who wrote the record.

The Stop Clock
     Buried in myth and legend, it is doubtful that this artifact ever existed at all. If it had, the bearer would almost inevitably be in control of the world by now. 
     It is said the Stop Clock resembles no more than a simple bronze sundial, albeit mounted on the tooth of a chromatic dragon. The owner of the Stop Clock is said to possess the power to control time itself. 
     Fairytale has it that when the humanoid gods took their interest in Layonara, they created the item in order to establish their station on the world without the interference of the dragons. Once the tooth is stabbed into the soil, time stops, awaiting the commands of its new master. Using a simple light, the dial may be turned back, along with time. 
     More myth than legend, the Stop Clock is confined mostly to children's stories rather than campfires. Few adventurers take the story seriously.
     In the same end, a wiser man than I told me fairy tales do not tell children dragons exist, for children already know dragons exist. Fairy tales tell them dragons can be killed. 
Stop Clock or no, your time is yours to control. Make the best of it while you can. 

Lich Skin
     The process of becoming a lich is never a particularly pleasant one, certainly not something you would care to be reminded of, I imagine. One lich, however, a female by the name of Farile Whipwind, decided to keep a memorabilia.
     Farile, ever the vain mage (aren't they all?), refused to live out eternity in the skeletal form she was forced to take. Instead she took the skin from her body as she was transformed into a lich and had it formed into a robe. The robe would fit over her whole body, disguising -  albeit badly - her bony form. 
     The robe had hair sewn into it, even eye lashes and brows. In dark light or through poor vision, one could almost consider her human. 
     As the years progressed, Farile spent most of her time enchanting the robe to improve her looks. Upon completion, whoever was to don the robe would be perceived as the true visage of feminine beauty.
     An untimely end was to greet the lich after an adventuring party raided her tower. Most unfortunate it was that the majority of the party turned out to be female. 
     Little has been heard of the artifact since, although one appearance was noted in the shape of a siren, said to haunt the Broken Forest. This is the last known sighting of the Lich Skin.
The steps spiral upward for what seems like some time.
There is a heavy scraping sound as it is opened.
The enormous door looks to have weathered many years.
