The Final Days of Tha'Azail Neverborn --

The shield clanged loudly as it hit the rough cavern floor. "Man those giants hit hard," Iradril grunted, leaning against the rock wall. Blood was pouring down his arm where the giant's maul had smashed and splintered his shoulder.

Tha' nodded grimly. Calling upon the healing power of Aeridin, he watched as Iradril's splintered bones grew back together, and the flesh knitted itself until it had a normal healthy black sheen.

A short time later, Tha' was thinking the same thing. These giants did hit hard. A group had come into the mines behind them, and then rushed forward saying something about coming for vengeance.

Tha', Iradril, and Owen had followed behind them, trying to ascertain if they needed help. Very quickly it became apparent that they did as the group was overrun by a band of giants. One of the group got slammed against the wall, and then came running back toward Tha' and his friends. Iradril and Owen charged forward to aid the other group. Without thought Tha' placed himself between the giant and the one who was fleeing back.

Tha' intended to hold the giant off long enough for Iradril or Owen to provide relief, so that he could heal those who needed it. He was surprised as one giant became two. Tha's mighty shield held the first blow back; his 'hammer smashing the giants kneecap in return. Tha' felt the air as the second giant swung and attempted to duck behind his shield. His shield was a little low, and Tha' heard his helmet crunch and then everything went black.

Tha' awoke and gently began to feel his head, expecting to feel a mangled helmet. His eyes sprung open when his hands came in contact not with his helmet, but with his hair. As he looked around, Tha saw a barren, rocky landscape. He was in a wide valley, all around the ground rose into blunt hills, and behind the hills at the horizon loomed sharp mountains. Tha' felt groggy as if he were moving underwater, everything seemed surreal. That is when he felt the presence behind him.

Looking behind him he saw a stocky woman garbed in black. She seemed to be swiftly winding a golden string or cord as she fluidly tucked it deep within one of her wide sleeves. She had her hood pulled up, disguising her features. The woman straightened herself imperially and then raised one arm. Slowly she extended a finger encased in a black lace glove, pointing towards the east.

Tha' looked in the direction she indicated and noticed a bright golden glow at the base of one of the hills. Oddly enough the glow reminded him of his own Golden Leaf. As if in response to the thought, his holy symbol began to glow. Tha' noticed then that he was missing not just his helmet, but all of his armor. He was clad in a simple robe, much like the one he had worn for many years in his home temple. At his side hung his 'hammer. On his finger was the ring he made from the gem that had marked him as a Lightbringer. Tha' was beginning to feel strangely at peace and turned to ask the stranger who she was and where he was. She was nowhere to be seen. The landscape suddenly seemed bleaker and more forbidding. When he turned eastward however, Tha' felt calmness return, and he felt drawn toward the glow. With a half grin, he began walking toward the glow and what awaited him there.

Tha' walked and walked. On the second day it occurred to him that he had not eaten or drunk, nor did he feel hungry or thirsty. At the beginning of the third day Tha' could see his goal. At the base of the hill was an enormous oak tree, even larger than the Great Oak. Within the trunk of the tree was a large door, shaped like Aeridin's Golden Leaf. The door was ajar, and the golden light was spilling outward from within.

Tha' reached the door at what he thought of as noon, although there was no real light or sun in this land to confirm his feeling. The only light that seemed real was coming from within the tree. As he reached the tree the door slowly opened all the way, releasing the soft golden glow. The glow made it impossible to see what lay within, but the feeling of comfort and serenity was not to be ignored. Tha' stepped toward the doorway, and then paused and looked back into the desolate wasteland. Could he take this final step? Was his work back there really done?

In response to his unasked question the feeling of welcome and peace intensified from within the doorway. Inside his head, Tha heard seemed to hear an ancient and wise voice. "The cycle is in constant motion. You have new lessons to learn. You have done well, review what you have accomplished if you will, and then move forward into what awaits with confidence that it is the continuation of what has gone before." At once images began to flood into Tha's consciousness.

Once again he was a young priest unsure as he stepped out into the world. He was standing before a great Golden Dragon and given a mission. Tha' recalled arriving in Hlint with a sense of purpose and those he met there destined to be his friends and companions.

A flash of light and once again he was on the road with Iradril when he was blessed by a messenger of Lucinda and together with Owen they made the trip to Blackford Castle so that Iradril could give thanks and proclaim his devotion.

Another flash and he could feel the deep oppressive gloom of Arindor's crypt. The shadows all around as Arindor taunted all that had come there to thwart his hold over Bidwick. Tha' was once again filled with Aeridin's Light and strength and was able to overcome the oppressive fear imposed by Arindor.

The blazing light from Tha's Golden Leaf flared and once again he was with Owen, Iradril, Talan, Gulnyr and others as he met Rhizome. Even then Rhizome was the high druid of Mistone. He remembered the honor and pleasure he gained from the friendship he and "Aeridin's Strongest" shared.

The scene shifted slightly and Tha' stood in the company of Talan, Lalaith, Rhizome, Plenarius, Brisbane, Owen and Iradril. The group had been granted an audience with Ozlo where they were given clues and instructions to help return the metallic dragons to Layonara. Ozlo's gaze was intense, knocking Owen and Iradril to the ground. Within the gaze Tha' thought he recognized a familiar glint. Tha's hunch was proven many years later, when Ozlo appeared in draconic form in defense of the Great Oak.

Once again Tha' could smell the dust, dirt and mold that was present in almost every crypt he had ventured into. He could recognize this crypt by its scent, however. He was at the bottom of the crypt in Krandor, and once again he was calling forth Aeridin's holy light upon the gem he had been given. In a flash of light and pain Tha'Azail had become a Light Bringer of Aeridin.

The next images that flashed through his mind included the Lost Souls, those poor children that had dedicated themselves to Shadison. Tha' recalled the small part he had played, chasing the books left behind and diminishing Shadison's presence as well as redeeming Dougal, the fallen paladin.

In his mind Tha' was once again in Hlint being approached by Aeridin's messenger. He was being given his 'Hammer and congratulated on his work in Aeridin's name. Tha' caressed the now worn handle of his 'hammer and smiled in mixed pride and a sense of humility that he had been so honored.

The 'hammer reminded him of the day that he, Owen, and Iradril had stumbled upon Eon outside of Storan's crypt and the search of the crypt that lead to the very short confrontation with Eon. He also remembered the many trips to the crypt to return its residents to the Great Cycle.

That train of thought led him to think of his good friend Aralin, and the fateful day Aralin began forming the Vakhar. Tha' thought of the many good things the Vakhar had done. He thought of the safe path they had created to Folian's temple, and the way the Vakhar had helped the Wolfswood Rangers. Tha' thought of all the work they had done in the present darkness caused by the great clouds of dust and debris. The Vakhar were working to preserve the trees and other plants and thus help sustain the cycle disrupted by the unnatural conditions.

Thoughts of the Vakhar led full circle back to Rhizome and one of the most beautiful days of Tha's life. Tha' remembered how he had the great honor of seeing Rhizome ascend to the position of Hierophant, and witnessed him planting the Silver Vein. The ceremony strengthened the Great Oak and helped ensure the defeat of Blood. Tha' had been honored and humbled when Plenarius had called upon him to add the blessings of Aeridin to the blessings of Katia over the momentous occasion.

That feeling of happiness echoed within him when he was traveling with his two best friends, Iradril and Owen. It was hard to think of Iradril without remembering the day he was once again blessed by Lucinda and in thanks for retrieving a blade of importance for her he was granted the knowledge to meld sword and shield with the weave to become a spell sword. It was even harder to think of Owen without thinking of his great quest to meet and speak with the dragons, to record at least one of their stories and create a grand epic for the edification of all of Layonara.

Thinking of friendships also caused him to think of AnnaLee. He thought of the night on the docks when they had spoken of their pasts and their hopes for the future. He thought about the contentment he had felt that night, a contentment he usually only felt in the presence of Aeridin.

The presence of Aeridin.... Tha' smiled and walked forward into the light, the door closing softly behind him. For a brief moment the last rays of the sitting sun lit the doorway in amber fire, then after a final flare the wasteland was dark and desolate once more. 

-- Anonymous
By My Death Or My Honor

Rurik left his forest home to seek adventure, and what he got was much more.

His first years on his road to adventure were far less then that, spending most of his time looking for work and tracking game across Mistone to further his crafting so that he could afford the luxuries that one needs to adventure. Soon he became a well respected tailor and bowmaker and was sought out by a dwarf name Gloin and a human fighter Alex, who spoke to Rurik about forming a crafters guild to make a better quality and quantity of products to the masses. He agreed to this as Gloin explain that this guild would take him on grand adventures to far away places and fight monsters that Rurik wouldn't believe. Soon the three friends started out traveling and working the raw products the gathered from around  Layonara into sellable items. The grandest adventures they had and the fun they had doing it.

"These are the days" thought Rurik and he never wanted them to end, but nothing that good ever last. Soon Alex and Gloin grew distant and their only connection that held the group together was Rurik and it hurt knowing that the best of friends couldn't be like they once were. One year later Alex left saying he was going to try to find himself. After that day Rurik as well left the Orcbashers promising himself that he would never craft again to make items for the gain of money but for only to meet his needs on his travels.

During his travels he made many friends, Ahndar cleric of Lucinda, Vin Onyxshade, Plenarius Bird lord and cleric of Katia, Xiao Lin, Tathnolu, Seteece, Pathfinder, Sago Spellfinder, Celgar cleric of Lucinda (and golem fanatic), Triba, Rhizome high Druid of Dregar, Synal'dur paladin of Toran and many others took up the call to fight the forces of Bloodstone and to end his reign of terror and fear on Layonara. Together they fought and soon had put up a great resistance to Blood. In time they learned where two Blood pools were which gave Bloodstone his power and they sought them out and destroyed them weakning Blood. After which they raised the Lost Library and brought it back to rest on the elven Island of Voltrex. Then they sought out to gain an Alliance from the remaining dragons of Layonara which was a very difficult challenge to undergo, but soon they were able to bring them together and have a new ally in the upcoming battle.

Soon Rurik grew weak from the war. The Soul Mother had come and taken too much of his soul and last night during his quest to bring the inhabitants of the Dragon Isles together to fight off Bloods army that had taken control of the land, he fell for the final time trying to help the wemics remove an outpost of Blood's forces. But, he died knowing that they had succeded the battle and knowing that his friends lived. So as the Soul Mother came, Rurik died with a smile on his face.

Has Rurik Kessel left his mark on the world? Let the gods decide that. Has he left his mark on his friends? In the end isn't that the most important question?

Fa sa wailanir em sa irelem. By my death or my honor.

Ylanec aniraalw eo Fceew. Until the end of Blood.

Gotak was the second born son of Gragar and Tilar Gungur. He always looked up to his older brother Grogil, who had a reputation as one of the best bodyguards in Mistone. Through misfortune an bad luck Grogil was dishonored and was forced to exile from Mistone. He left no message behind and left for an unknown destination for a honorable death.

Gotak soon became aware of his brothers leave, and took up the heavy burden from his brother to carry on in his place. Gotak was always the biggest of the two brothers and therefore had some trouble adjusting into the the new surroundings in Hlint always being the mockery of elven jokes.

The last day of Gotak Gungur:

Gotak looked beyond the trees to see a smoke rise from the outskirts of haven. He looked around to his fellow adventures, and they all decided to go to investegate this incident. Not a days journey from Haven, they were attacked by great numbers of Slaads. Gotak was the first to run into the slaads with his axe above his head. Two slaads quickly went down, and a 3rd was injured beyond recognition before his friends could react. The fight was quickly over. They made their way to the outskirts, near the forsaken resting place of Arindor. Here they encountered many more slaads, which Gotak seem to enjoy as his axe sliced through the soft flesh of these frog like creatures. When they came close enough to the entrance to Arindor, The great Necromancer Nathan could see that it ws not smoke that rose from the doorway of Arindor. It was solid matter, the type that occured when a planar rift have occured. The party rested to regain some strenght and decided to make their way down into the depts to close this planar rift if possible. As usual Gotak went first and complety surprised the waiting slaads. They were prepared for an small army, but a dwarven warrior with a determination was to much for the packs of slaads that eagerly awaited any who would enter this place. When all the others came down through the narrow staircase a single slaad was all there was left. As they went further down into the dungeon, it became clear that the winds of arindor would make it difficult for clerics to rest properly and prepare enough protections for all. Gotak decided to give up his protection in favor of a younger adventurer, and went on to engage the slaads who were spilling out from the depts of the dungeon. Suddenly a yellow bright light encircled Gotak he blinked for a moment and then his soul was torn away from his body. His friends quickly dispatched the remaining slaads in the area, and came to see to him. Plenarius the cleric said that his soul was gone for good, and that it never would return. As the adventures stood over Gotak's body a slim looking demoness appeared and took the soul of Gotak with her. Gotak had died the way he lived. Fast and furious. This was his time. May his spirit live on forever.

Born: 15 Junar 1387 - Died: 11 Mai 1412

Born in the city of Prantz to Allaim Jin'Daern her father and Gloria Jin'Daern (maiden name Zimmer) on the 15th day of Junar in the year 1387, Melanna grew up an only child. Neglected by her parents all her life in matters of love and attention Melanna learned to manipulate her parents for her own selfish wants. Eventually she talked them into hiring an instructor to teach her the arts of martial training, specifically in the use of the great sword. Eventually Melanna came to depend upon the council of this instructor, a city guard of Prantz by name of Ruvan, who turned her from being a completely spoiled brat into a young lady with a sense of duty and honor. Ruvan's teachings would form the core of moral beliefs, though she would remain quite willful much to the disapproval of her parents.

After the fall of Prantz to Rael's forces, and the resulting death of her friend and teacher Ruvan, Melanna later left the city and her neglectful parents behind in the year 1405, arriving in the town of Hlint on the day of her eighteenth birthday. With respect for her friend, councilor, and confidant Ruvan, who had fallen defending Prantz from Rael's forces, Melanna set herself to continue her training in mastery of the great sword on her own. In time, she would learn to embrace his teachings even more personally as she realized how they applied to herself and she eventually found herself a 'servant of the people' using her skill with the great sword to remove by force those things which might threaten their well-being as she saw it.

She also began practicing the forging of her own weapons and armors and her skill at crafting these things quickly grew. As a result of her practicing she donated almost all of her completed practice equipment to local militias, or other charitable causes such as the Rohden Relief Effort and the Princess Kayana Memorial Foundation.

In Apreal of the year 1406 Melanna encountered an Ogre by name of Glurgle who spoke the Common tongue and expressed his wishes for peace between himself and the people of the Haven community. At first their relationship began as an agreement to trade food for iron ore, which Melanna needed to continue her crafting efforts. Eventually Glurgle expressed that there were a growing number of Ogres among his tribe who were of like mind and wished for the violence between his people and the peoples of the surface to end. Melanna took the initiative and began to realize even more deeply the teachings of her mentor Ruvan and saw the chance for peace between the Ogres of the Haven Mines and the community of Haven as a goal that would be beneficial to both peoples.

In Jenra of 1407 Melanna received the opportunity to begin realizing her goals to bring peace to Haven and the Ogres of the mines there. Lord Rodor of Haven Keep bid her to prove the Ogre's innocence in the disappearance of a shipment of weapons and other supplies inbound from Port Hempstead via the route through Spellgard. She, with the aid of several companions, whom Lord Rodor had also bid bear witness to the peacefulness of the Ogres and the provision of proof of their innocence, uncovered a new clan of Gnolls moving into the Haven and Silkwood area. It was proven quickly that these new Gnolls were responsible for the disruption of trade into Haven, and that they held a large and well organized encampment deep within the Silkwood and appeared to be marshaling for invasion under the guidance of an unknown, but evil source. Meanwhile, by Seplar of 1407, Glurgle and those Ogres he had gathered under himself began a civil war with the rest of their tribe within the Haven Mines in order to unite the tribe and allow for its peaceful relocation elsewhere.

The new Gnolls continued to harass the Haven community, stealing livestock and other animals in sporadic raids both within and without the area's borders. These new Gnolls had the ability to appear and disappear almost as with the wind, making fighting them nearly impossible for Kit and the local militia who were already sorely taxed with keeping order in general.

Finally, things took some major turns by the 24th day of Oclar of the year 1410. Glurgle and those supporting him at last won out against the former leader of the Haven Mine Tribe and what was left of the tribe stood united under Glurgle's benevolent leadership. Melanna was given the clearance by Lord Rodor to move the tribe out to the Silkwood where they would help to confront the Gnoll threat and establish their new home. However, taking advantage of the Ogre's absence from the mines, the Gnolls moved simultaneously to take the mines for themselves and establish control over the entire Haven community, isolating it from outside help. Melanna and those with her returned to find Haven occupied by the Gnolls and themselves roughly powerless to free it. As fate would have it, however, all was not lost and the group chanced to capture an artifact from the Gnolls. It was eventually determined this artifact held the key to the Gnolls defeat, and that power which had been guiding them. Once again Melanna called upon her friend Glurgle and his Ogres to help protect the group of her comrades while the ceremony to destroy the artifact and free the Gnolls from possession of an evil shadow being from Dark-elven lore was performed. Muireann, a priestess of Mist, Galen Tweed (of the Spellgard Tweeds) and Melanna's own close friend Elohanna Min A'Litae performed the ceremony while Melanna, the Ogres, Pyyran Rath, Lex'or Gravedigger, Amilia Tannnes, Aiek Lo'Sashaien, Valaria La'Elis, and Sonya Darsus protected them. For a few moments a bright light shown over Haven visible from as far away as both Hlint and Spellgard, and after which the Gnolls regained control of them selves and began fleeing. Unfortunately, a great number of the once possessed Gnolls held their refuge within the Haven Mines, taking the place of the Ogres who had recently moved out, and leaving the Haven community to struggle in being rebuilt without the resources of the mines to draw upon.

Also during her years spent serving the common folk, Melanna assisted in a matter regarding unusually powerful goblins and their use of necromantic magic.

Ayla Bineau was born in Kheldell as the oldest of four children, a compassionate and caring woman that held the word of Aeridin in the highest respect. Ayla did many a great thing throughout her too short life, and made a great impact on many a person who had the luck to meet her. Many recall meeting her in Hlint when they first arrived and how she helped them get started on the life of adventuring. Perhaps many would have found it dull to only help and protect, but Ayla was not so. To her this was the meaning of life, why she was here. 

She cared as much for one as for another, with no regard to heritage or affiliation, for all life to her was worth saving. As such a more dedicated follower of Aeridin has seldom been seen, even her foes she would care for like she did for Corash the orc. Once she was part of a band of heroes who sought to end the threat from orcs in the Whitehorn Forest of Mistone. She and others were turned into orcs to get into the camp in the forest and find a way to defeat the leader called Corash or Red Raven, who could not be slain because of the blade Grand had given to him. 

Throughout this Ayla never gave up on compassion and she made all who were part of this understand the tragedy that had befallen Corash. So great was her love for life and her caring that she did even seek to redeem those who would kill her. She composed a song of Corash the orc which she sung to him before his blade was broken. A hunter proud stood on a hill, both happy and content. His skill fed all his growing tribe. His elders honor sent. The maidens looked at him with awe, and one was special, too. A life of hunting, love and babes stretched out before his view. But on a hunt he was struck down, not by his prey at all. And not in battle hon'rable was he content to fall. A band of war-bent mercenaries slew him as he stood And chopped at his poor corpse as though 'twere made of only wood. No chance had he to even fight, against the Vorax-crazed. No time to grasp a weapon tight and strike a blow that dazed. No growing child would look to him for pattern for its life Nor would the Orcs call Corash' shade to keep them safe from strife. And yet, and yet, One saw the rout and thought to use it well. He snatched the dead unto himself in very depths of hell. 

An orc, great orc, enormous grown, in hate and power strong, 'Twas Grand himself, betrayed himself, who sought to use this wrong. Red Raven then, Grand named the dead, and brought it back to life, To life, but only for revenge, tied to a dreadful knife. The blade glowed red, Red Raven blade, imbued with all Grand's hate Red Ravens both, they drank Grand's blood, accepting then their fate. Still Corash did not know that fate, the deaths that lay in store. He went, he thought, to get revenge from one of Vorax's spore. A dwarf he found in distant Hlint, and challenged him to fight, Skullcracker proved his name that day, though others helped his might. In agony Corash arose, no peace for him in death. Again he strove, again he lost, again he had no breath. In agony Corash arose, death could not ease his pain. But now he seemed to understand he'd die and die again. 
"Vorax!" he screamed. "Vorax betrays! In this fight you serve Grand!" With skill that rose as fighters closed, he fought with blade in hand. His god's red drink empowered him. He fought with verve and dash, And yet again, a Vorax win, he died of Skull's fell bash. Again he drank the evil blood; again he rose from clay, But now Corash more thoughtful seemed, "You've helped me on this day." "Stand back. I'll go, for now," he said. "Stand back or I will kill." With measured tread he left the town; he'd made it know his will. Bound tight to Grand with ties of blood, Red Raven rules his kin. He pushes them to Grand's designs upon the world of men. 

And yet, and yet, does Corash live within that stern domain? Does Corash mourn the hunt, the love, the maiden without claim? Could Corash still put down the blade and take his spear anew? Or is he now Red Raven, just Grand's weapon thru and thru? Does Corash mourn the hunt, the love, the maiden left behind? Or is he just Red Raven, and a blade that kills, that's blind? And THEN, oh then the shaman STRUCK and broke the dreadful blade With spell so strong it smote them both and took a hand in trade. We healed them both, but only one arose from that black hell-- Poor Corash slept, his self sleeps still in Aeridin's fair dell. Will hunter ever proudly stand upon a hill content? Will mate and child live by his skill, and honor fill his tent? As gods have spoiled, so gods may save, and folk may help his plight. We wait the will of Aeridin to aid us in the fight. Her gentle voice made even Corash shed a tear, a final tear before it was all over. Had she not moved him so, with her love of all that lives, perhaps today Lar and the Citadel of Dorand there would not stand. 

But alas she was taken from this world far too soon. In Haven mines a great host of ogres had taken up residence and as she went down then mines with others a fierce battle ensued. Many fell and alas so did Ayla at the deadly touch of a magic-wielding ogre as she tried to heal those who were badly wounded. The last piece of her soul was taken from her as she fell on the cold stone floor. That night even the sky wept as rain poured down over those who brought her body to Hlint and its final journey. After her death Ayla was bestowed the title of Honorary Half-dwarf of Mistone by her dwarven friends, for as they said, no human was ever more worthy of such title. Still though she is gone, she is still with us in spirit. In the hearts of those she touched with her gentle being she will live on, giving them light in their darkest hours.

The Last Days of Varka Cleaveson, as told by Kobal Bluntaxe, Regent of the Runic Anvil:

The tale starts out when Varka set out to remove the upstart tyrant Gunderforn and reinstated the true King Rory Rockfist. Hereby he, alongside trusted friends, ensured peace and prosperity for the Bloody Gate for any years to come.
Never truly satisfied with his work and ever striving to live up to the legends of his ancestors, Varka strived to strengthen the Gate, so that it would ever be a safe haven to the people he loved. Therefore he worked hard to organize the defences and train new warriors to replace those who had perished in battle against Gunderforn and the troops of Milara sent to bolster his ranks within the city.

As this was accomplished, King Rockfist offered a last task to Varka - to seek and secure the 'Triqueta of Gates'. A relic of myths, the Triqueta was the symbol of the strength of the three gates into the city. Said to be made from the fusing together of the three keys originally made for deh three first gates into the Bloody Gate, the myth says that it was suspended over the King's throne as a warning that one of the King's sacred responsibilities was to tend to the gates of the city. This was because the three gates were the prime defence against any enemy that would seek to enter the Bloody Gate. A common saying in the Boody Gate goes: "The only way into the Gate is through the King".

An aspiring priest blessed with a vision from Vorax had recognized the truth of the myth and knew it's worth to the Bloody Gate. So he spoke to King Rockfist of his vision, who then sent for his most trusted and loyal warrior, Varka Cleaveson. Together with friends he set out to the depths below the mountains, seeking passages not used by dwarfkin for generations.

Following words of an ancient scroll that described how the King's nephew foolishly had stolen the Triqueta in a fit of rage and jealousy and fled into the lower dungeons, the party set out to reclaim what had been lost so many years ago.

Far below ground, within a hive of ghastly enemies the treacherous young dwarf was discovered along with the Triqueta. Cursed by Vorax for his deed, the dwarf had been turned to stone and the Triqueta wrapped in a magical field that protected it from the hands of the unworthy.
The cursed soul, however, had left something behind for those seeking to reclaim his prize. A scroll case held information that showed that he had regretted his deed and defended it until his end. It had been his final act to invoke a prayer to Vorax and ask him to protect what he had foolishly risked. So he was cursed and his soul tied to the Triqueta. It was discovered that to reclaim the Triqueta for the King and the Bloody Gate, another would have to take his burden. The price of past pride would need to be paid anew.

It was then that the warlord stepped forward and made his intentions known. He made his goodbyes to his friends that had fought at his side for so many years and had aided him in his quests for the Bloody Gate. Then, without blinking, Varka Cleaveson stepped forward and clasped the crystal that encased the Triqueta. He uttered a prayer to Vorax:

"The boundaries of time are come undone, I stand in the gateway between two worlds, Hear me through the veil that hides you from my sight, Help me through this day, Watch me. Shelter me. I am your child!"


These words were his last, for as they were uttered, the curse was released and Varka turned to stone. The Triqueta was freed and returned to hower in suspension above the King's throne, while the statue of Varka Cleaveson was carried back up to the Bloody Gate where it now adorns the throne room as a constant reminder of Varka's sacrifice to the people he loved.

This is his tale.

Monastic Orders
     Monastic Orders come in many varieties. Some focus on peace, others on battle. Some focus on knowledge, others on discipline. Many Orders exist, and some of the more well-known can be found below.

The Sisters of Rebirth
     Monks from this Order follow Aeridin. The majority of monks are elves, but members of other races are not uncommon. This Sisterhood was founded in ancient times and devotes itself to the preservation and nurturing of life. They follow Aeridin's dogma to the core; everything has its place in the great cycle that is the universe: from the Sun and the Moons in the sky to the tiniest insect in the ground, all are important. They accept that death is part of life, but firmly believe that since Aeridin is everywhere, everything will always be reborn. Since Aeridin is everywhere, they do not see the need to pray, as Aeridin is also present in themselves. Instead of prayer, they meditate, train, and live in the forest to draw Aeridin's strength from within their own beings.
      Most Sisters are elves from Voltrex, but the Sisterhood is represented on all continents. They will never turn down requests for aid and will always come to life's defense wielding their wooden staves. 

The Adamantine Brotherhood
     The Adamantine Brotherhood seek to be more like their god Sulterio, the Adamantine One, and have taken to literally mimicking his title in the very fiber of their being. They have hardened body and mind in pursuit of the essence of their namesake metal. Some have compared them to the Voraxite Brothers of Battle, but the Brotherhood is much more numerous. They have fewer scruples and will not refrain from using poisons to help them in their dark endeavors. The Adamantine Brotherhood rarely surfaces, instead seeking to advance their physical and mental fortitude by delving even deeper into the earth and uncovering and claiming even more riches for the glory of the Brooding One. It is rumored that the greatest of the Brotherhood can actually reach into the core beneath the Underdark and extract molten adamantium from the very heart of Layonara.

The Brothers of Battle
     Followers of Vorax, the Brothers of Battle is, not surprisingly, one of the most militant orders on Layonara. It was founded by Thergrim Stonefist approximately 1500 years ago, when he fell down a crevice when traveling through the Berhagen Mountains. Bereft of his axe, which he lost in the fall, Thergrim found himself stuck in the rocks with no way to free himself.
     Fighting the cold with every breath, refusing to let it weaken him, Thergim suddenly received a vision of fists smashing the rocks that trapped him. Using his own fists, he relentlessly punched and clawed at the rocks until he was free.
     Now convinced that he needed nothing but his fists to serve the Father of Battle, he founded the Brothers of Battle, taking Stonefist as his new surname. In memory of  Thergrim's miraculous deed, the head of the Brothers of Battle is still called "The Stonefist." Members of the Brotherhood can be found throughout Layonara, but they gravitate to areas of conflict. 

The Bearers of Knowledge
     The Bearers of Knowledge are a well-known Order. Followers of Aragen, they dedicate their lives to Knowledge. Prohibited from using violence except in the defense of knowledge, self, or others, they wander the world in search of wisdom, be it forgotten or new. They serve an important role in the Aragenite Church as they are mostly responsible for the sharing of knowledge between the temples. 
     Bearers of Knowledge are among the most intelligent and perceptive monks around. They often give lectureson subjects ranging from history to engineering to philosophy to literature. They usually travel in pairs, as two see, hear, and remember more than one.
     The head of the Order is called the Loremaster and resides at the Keep of the Tome, deep within one of Layonara's mountain ranges.

T'oleflor
    The T'oleflor are an ancient sprite type race that are extremely close to nature; in fact, some say they ARE nature. The T'oleflor train the best elves, centaurs, and sometimes humans to become elite rangers and druids, the ultimate protectors of nature. They are lead by their Queen and their sole purpose is to support and create nature. They are very rarely seen and only live in one section of the world; it is rumored that they are very nearly extinct. 

Personality: 
    They are a beautiful race and as "uppity" as High Elves. They know that nobody in the world has their capabilities towards nature or intelligence. Violence and anger are frowned upon, and T'oleflor are taught to always be in control of their emotions and actions. From the time they are born until the time they die, they dedicate their lives to nature and T'oleflor's Nature Dance, a martial art system employed by their rangers. T'oleflor live in perfect harmony with nature, and never intentionally harm a living creature except in self-defense. 
T'oleflor are strict vegetarians, as they consider the eating of meat a disgusting habit (although not actually evil). 

Physical Description: 
    T'oleflor are sleek and slender. They never weigh more than 60 pounds and are usually around 45 pounds. They stand about 24" on average. Although slender and small, they are still quite strong and agile.

    T'oleflor skin tone is usually light to dark green. Their hair is often black, sometimes silver or white, and always well kept. They usually have silver, green, or blue eyes. They move with a fluid grace that is distinctly beautiful, like slow dancing. T'oleflor feel awkward in heavy clothing and armor, and thus only wear such things in extreme circumstances. They prefer the lightest garments, and never wear armor or clothing made from the hides of animals. 

Relations: 
    They very distrustful of nearly all races on Layonara. They despise the races that are constantly bringing war and destruction to the world. They hold grudges for centuries at a time when a certain race defaces a part of nature. 

Alignment: 
    T'oleflor are always Neutral in alignment but strongly nature-minded. Some may lean towards good alignment but very rarely is one evil. 

T'oleflor Lands: 
    Little is known where this race now lives, if they even survive to this date. They were last known to exist in the Vale of the Wilds on the continent of Mistone but that was at least one hundred years ago. 

Religion:  
    The T'oleflor worship Katia in everything they do. Other races whisper that they may be direct descendants of Katia, but that cannot be verified. 

Language: 
    T'oleflor speak the language of Florane. This language is gentle and soft-spoken, but extremely lyrical and pronounced with a complex cadence. When spoken in the rich, melodic tones of the T'oleflor, it is among the most beautiful music that can be heard on Layonara. 

Names: 
    T'oleflor feel very strong family ties, and those who encounter a long-lost member of her family will welcome the stranger as a dear friend.

Male Names: 
    Aka-(family name), Benesis, Duerkau, Forcasion, Hurion, Jurian, Kaselfar, Shadan, Shuri, Verxagha, Yesri.

Female Names: 
    Heriko, Kreala, Luthlien, Maeni, Melei, Murmika, Salandra, Worriea. 
Family Names: Adishau, Duidin, Erisei, Igrani, Modialli, Nuuni, Omidai, Rathmaet, Temloth, Vordesac. 

Adventurers: 
    Those T'oleflor who chose a life of exploration (extremely rare occurrence) often seek legends and artifacts tied to their ancestry.

This is a statue of the halfling deity Deliar, also known as The Lucky Wanderer, The Merchant of Fate, The Wind of Destiny whose dogma is: 

Deliar teaches that in order to lead a fulfilling life, one must constantly strive to discover new ways to trade with the world. His objectives and priorities deal with a harmonious existence in which everything is spread throughout all the communities that touch any goods or services that can be bartered with. The Lucky Wanderer promotes wealth, yes, but such wealth should not be enjoyed at the expense of others, and particularly not at the expense of the community as a whole; thus he welcomes success in monetary gains as long as other needs have been satisfied.

All followers of The Merchant are encouraged to spread and explore the world, carrying their families with them if necessary, because the only way to truly appreciate existence as a whole is by exploring all its possibilities and letting others know of the treasures from distant lands. These treasures aren't just in gold, but in all the uniqueness that a culture can offer, particularly in the things that they create to identify themselves--that way, there is a little bit of everyone all over Layonara.

To hone your skills as a tradesman is to worship Deliar at what he does best - which is to understand the true value of an item and make everyone gain from it, even though perhaps the person they are exchanging with may not at first see the bigger picture. In the end, as long as no one is harmed by the trade, their role has been fulfilled. The best kind of exchange is the kind where each side walks away feeling like they came out on top.

Finally, all those who follow the path of the Lucky Wanderer understand that little in life is predictable, that the roads in life have only the certainty of uncertainty within them, and that every turn may throw at them a good or bad experience. The concept of Luck and Fate, whether 'good' or 'bad' is embraced by all Deliarites fully, as they know that the fruits of today may not be as bountiful as those of tomorrow and life does particularly well in bringing surprise to everyone. Because of this, many worshipers of Deliar are extremely superstitious and have many quirky rituals and talismans that must be performed or carried before embarking on a particular journey or going on about their daily routines.

Beryl

Aliases: Deep Mother, Her Perfection, Flawless Diamond  
Race: Deep Gnome 
Worshippers: Deep Gnomes and others who mine or work with gems. 
Domains: 
     Earth, Good, Healing, and Trickery. Most clerics prefer to choose the Earth to be close to the Deep Mother and then one of the other three.
Governs: Gemsmithing, stealth, healing, safety 

Dogma: 
     Always seek to find and cut the perfect gem. Make it your life's pursuit to create jewelry and bring beauty and perfection to the world. Do not take unneeded risks, and rely on stealth and wit to keep you safe.

Clergy Favored Weapon and Clothing
     Most clerics of Beryl prefer the mace or the heavy mace, usually together with an enchantment that does not involve Water (although such enchantments are not necessarily forbidden).

     When choosing armor, most clerics prefer the fine craftwork of one of their Dwarven allies. They prefer heavy metal armor such as plate or half plate, since this metal came from the Deep Mother's domain. Most clerics enhance their armors with a resistance to cold.

     When not traveling the Underdark in search of gems, clerics of Beryl dress outrageously, with a myriad of colors and many piercings showing off different gems from their travels. If they do travel, they tend to cover all jewelry, as moving through the Underdark unseen is of prime importance if you want to survive.

     They use jewelry consisting of the gems of their rank as focus for their spells.

Clergy and Temples:
     Those new to the faith are called "Greenstones," then as they progress in knowledge and power, they progress in ranks arranged by the rarity of gems (Greenstone, Malachite, Aventurine, Phenelope, Fire Agate, Feldspar, Garnet, Topaz, Alexandrite, Sapphire, Fire Opal, Ruby, Emerald, and Diamond), with diamond being the highest in rank. There is only one cleric at a time who is the Diamond of Beryl, and it is this cleric that heads the faith.

     Nearly all of Beryl's temples are hidden in the Svirfneblin cities in the Underdark; however, at least one is known to be on the surface, in the city of Stone on Rilara. Clerics like to pray during the day or next to a light source to enhance the beauty of their precious stones. During prayer, the cleric will often use their focus jewelry to scatter light and color across the wall or temple.

     Prayers to Beryl often revolve around gems and jewelry. For example, a jeweler about to start cutting a gem can say: "Allow me to cut the perfect stone for you," or a cleric trying to mine some raw gems from the earth might say "Fiddlesticks, Beryl, just give me one perfect stone."

Rilara
    Rilara is the southernmost continent of Layonara. It has always been a battleground for conflicts over territory, political power and wealth. It is even more so now that Milara has carved his wicked throne into the Iriand Mountains. Milara's machinations have added the strongest of all ingredients into the chaotic stew that is Rilara. As such, Rilarans are pragmatically suspicious and necessarily scheming. Those who are not have simply been subsumed into Milara's plans, whether they know it or not. Any city you visit in Rilara now will have a kind of subterranean tension, which seems ready to lash out into the everyday without notice. Many communities have stockpiled supplies, weapons, and hired henchmen to protect their precious homes only to find themselves in the service of the wicked master of Rilara the next day. The continent, it is safe to say, is not far from being entirely in the sway of Milara.

Well-known cities:

Casterly Castle
Location:  
    Casterly Castle can be found on the southwesternmost corner of the continent of Rilara
Population:  1600
Government:  Military Dictatorship
Defenses:  
    The castle is heavily defended with reinforced walls and battlements. It also houses a temple of Aragen inside its walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    In the many years of conflict on the continent of Rilara, the Casterly clan has managed to establish dominance in the southwestern region. They did this not by force of arms, but as many savvy rulers throughout history have, through the morally binding obligations of gift giving. For hundreds of years the wealthy Casterly family showered the towns of the southwestern region with gifts, gifts that couldn't possibly be repaid. The towns, therefore, repaid the castle with their allegiance. 
     Now, most of the surplus agricultural and trade goods of the region are shipped to the castle for redistribution. Some of it is traded with the elite of Point Harbor. Most, however, is packed south to the Casterly's port annex of White Harbor. The White Harbor cargo ships' manifests state that the primary destination is the Kingdom of Rodlem, a fact which has not slipped the attention of their rival city Karthy. Still, as the shipping routes on the south side of the continent rarely receive surveillance, and it is therefore hard to know for sure where these goods are shipped.
    There are many rumors about the involvement of the Casterly clan in Rilaran affairs. Rumors abound that an army is being amassed behind the walls, and that weapons and supplies are being stockpiled. Some think the Casterlys are preparing to fight Milara's forces, which they believe are gathering in Fort Himlad, a key central outpost. Others believe the Casterlys have received a gift from Milara, one which they can only repay with their allegiance. Whatever the murky truth is, Casterly is a key player in the unfolding struggle over Rilara. 

Ereb

Government: Monarchy

    Ereb is one of the towns that has benefited from the trade generated by Point Harbor, as it finds itself at one of the most important traderoutes of Rilara.The town's small wooden palisade does not provide much fortification, but the relative closeness of Fort Aglon gives adequate protection to this small town at the edge of the Belgaer Hills.

Bitterbridge
Location:  
    Just to the west of the Ledros Mountains lies Bitterbridge
Population:  40
Government:  Anarchy
Defenses:  None
Miscellaneous Information:
    Bitterbridge is the sister city to Bloody Gate, though far less stable. It lies on the northern portion of the Delwin River, at the point where the waterway falls from great heights from Lake Ire in the Ledros Mountains. The sight is one that many throughout Rilara once traveled to see. But it is more than a tourist attraction; the river is also the reason Bitterbrige exists. Originally many humble souls found the falls too gorgeous to part with and settled at their base. They built a bridge, where Bitterbridge now stands, for ease of passing through the rapid waters. It didn't take long for them to realize that the bridge would have to be defended from giants wandering between Wolfswood and the Mountains. The giants, not needing a structure to cross the raging Delwin, would simply smash the bridge for fun. 
    After a small fort had been established there and anti-giant measures taken, many travelers began to stay at Sweetbridge, as it was once called, to venture out at dawn for the rainbow mists of the Delwin Falls. Similar to the history of Bloody Gate, however, when Milara set his palace upon the Iriand Mountains, everything changed. Even the idea of Milara being so close sent the town into chaos. They knew Milara would march out for Karthy and would use the bridge, the product of their honest toil, to accomplish his task. Some thought to destroy it, some to defend it; others simply evacuated. Now the few who remain in the renamed Bitterbridge are said to have gone mad from the sheer stress of the situation. 

Bloody Gate 
Location: 
    South of Region Forest and on the northwestern tip of the Iriand Mountains on the continent of Rilara.
Population:

Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:

Miscellaneous Information:  
    There is one main route through the Iriand Mountins. This means that there is one main route between Milara's throne and the rest of Rilara. Bloody Gate is situated on that pass, between two dramatic craggy peaks. It has been the site of countless epic struggles, epic victories and epic defeats. All of these have contributed to Bloody Gate's well-deserved name.
    There is a question which haunts the thoughts of nearly every Rilaran and any Mistoner who has any sense of world events. That question revolves around the allegiance of Bloody Gate. Since Milara's army must pass through this town, how could the fierce dwarves not be under his sway?      Others retort that they are dwarves and would die before becoming servants to such a wicked ruler. Those might say that it has been these dwarves who have kept Milara from controlling Karthy. The response may come quick that Karthy and Bloody Gate fell to Milara's whims long ago. The truth is that no one knows for sure, perhaps not even Milara and the residents of Bloody Gate themselves.

Karthy 
Location: 
    Northeastern tip of the continent of Rilara.
Population:
    13,500 (60% human, 18% dwarf, 10% half-orc, 5% gnome, 5% halfling, 3% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:  
    Heavily fortified city with a reinforced masonry wall surrounding it.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Karthy is a rough and tumble city with very strict laws. The laws may be strict, but are subject to sudden change, hardly followed and yet executed with a kind of twisted pleasure by the Karthy guards. It is said that Milara has controlled this city for many years, and that its economic and political interests are his own. Supplies come to him through this port and his spies and troops depart from here. Therefore, all activity in this port is carefully monitored and recorded. A pervasive sense of paranoia grips the whole city, and travelers in particular as they are bombarded with askew glances and eyes peering through half-opened shutters. 
    The Kingdom of Roldem on the island of Calishan is trying to defeat the city but it seems that Milara is always one step ahead of them. This conflict dates back to the Cataclysm. Before Layonara was torn asunder in the great energies of the Cataclysm, Calishan and Rilara were pressed together in one huge central landmass. As they were cleaved apart, so were the people who lived in considerable turmoil on those lands. For many years two great families had battled for dominance on Calara, what people in retrospect call the unified territories. When they split, however, the two families were not split evenly. Many of the Roldem family was left on Rilara. But since they were cleaved in two by the Cataclysm and the ocean span too great to call for aid, the Roldem family was hunted down and quickly eradicated from Rilara. On Calishan, however, they established their dominance and came to rule the island. They still remember their kinsmen and have always had a mind to recapture Karthy and avenge their family's misfortune. With Milara taking control of much of Rilara, and Karthy as his primary port, this desire has intensified considerably. To say Roldem and Milara are at war would surely be an understatement.
    A major temple to Xeen can be found in Karty.

King's Landing
Location:  
    King's Landing can be found on the southern coast of Rilara.
Population:  2700
Government:  
    Monarchy, though in recent years it is suggested that King's Landing has fallen into a chaotic state.
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended castle, with bastions and reinforced walls.
Miscellaneous Information:
    King's Landing, as the name suggests, is where the King first landed on Rilara after sending some of his finest men to pacify as much of Rilara as they could. Giants, bugbears, wild men, and feral elves alike fell to this solution to the Rilara settlement problem. The lands of the northeast were still too wild, and the southeast is primarily mountains, so the King's advisors directed him to this spot for his ceremonial claiming of the continent. Even now in King's Landing there stands a statue of the ancient king erecting a victorious flag on the banks where the Delwin River meets the ocean.
    Milara must have a sense of historical irony, for it is said that this is also where he first set foot on the island of Rilara. Where he came from, no one knows. But his berth at this port gives the name King's Landing a clever double meaning. As the well-buttressed city on the mouth of the southeast's most important waterway, Milara's presence here also has practical purpose.
    Whether or not it is true that Milara landed and took control of King's Landing, all reports document that this city is falling further and further into a state of lawless frenzy. The streets, it is said, are littered with corpses and looted possessions. The city elite have abandoned the town and the guards do more work keeping the wild commoners within the city than keeping any invading army without. The nearby cities of Wyk and Lann have done all that they can to keep the waves of King's Landers at bay. From the state of these towns it is easy to see that they are not very successful. 

Lannisport
Location:
    Lannisport is small village on the northern shore of Rilara.
Population: 685
Government:  Tribal council
Defenses:  
    Lannisport has a stone wall surrounding the town, though not the forces to man it in case of attack.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Traditionally, Lannisport was a fishing village. The north and central waters off the coast of Rilara boast some of the best fishing in all of Layonara. Lannisport fish can be found throughout Rilara and have been served for fine banquets in prestigious places as far as Port Hampshire, Leilon and Pranzis. The locals have always attributed their fishing prosperity to Shindaleria. Many years ago, on a cliff overlooking the natural harbor, the people of Lannisport established an impressive temple to their patron deity in a gesture of gratitude for years of prosperity but mostly to influence the future to proceed in their favor.
In the days of Milara, however, Lannisport has taken on a more nefarious pastime. Though small, or perhaps because of their diminutive stature, the docks at Lannisport have served as an ideal launching point for Milara's agents to sneak into the southern reaches of Mistone. For the most part, ships from Lannisport have been thought innocuous fishermen come to sell and spend. As such, they are mostly unquestioningly welcomed into the ports at Fort Valensk and Port Hampshire, and sometimes as far north as Forewarn Fort. Milara, it is said, uses this traditional oversight to his advantage and is said to have established himself well in certain areas of Mistone through such unsuspected vessels. 
    The situation has become more visible to Mistone authorities. The Mistone Alliance knows that at least some of the Lannisport fishing and cargo vessels are not what they appear to be. Notices have begun appearing at docks throughout Mistone, but as the gregarious fishermen swing from the rails of their vessels and dart for the bars and brothels as they always have, the notices are commonly shrugged off.

Point Harbor 
Location: 
    Northwestern tip of the continent of Rilara, at the edge of Dinen Forest.
Population:
    36,000 (45% human, 20% halfling, 12% elf, 10% dwarf, 8% half-orc, 5% gnome) 
Government: Monarchy 
Defenses:
    Point Harbor is a heavily fortified masonry fortress. Parts of the walls extend out into the bay. 
Miscellaneous Information: 
     Point Harbor is the most prosperous harbor of Rilara, and most of the continent's trade passes through here. Since the Forsaken Islands are so deadly that even passing by them is rumored to turn a whole crew into ghasts, goods headed east from Mistone usually come through Point Harbor. Either they re-supply and travel the dangerous north coast of Rilara or they travel overland to Karthy. Neither trek is desirable and it is not uncommon for Point Harbor to be the settled upon destination of many supposedly Dregar-bound captains.
    To protect its wealth, it is heavily fortified, both from the land as well as from the sea, making it a difficult city to capture. Its main trading partner is the city of Port Hampshire on Mistone, but passage to many of the great ports of Layonara can be booked on ships docking in Point Harbor. Boats from Point Harbor are likely the only ones you'll see on the books at any port outside of Rilara, excepting Xantril. The reason for this is simple. Being on the northwest corner of the vast continent of Rilara, Point Harbor is as far from Milara's seat as possible. This doesn't mean Milara overlooks it or cannot reach it, rather that his grasp there is less firm. Because of this, Point Harbor is one of the few ports on the island of Rilara that conducts business not entirely in the interests of Milara. 

Stone
Location:
    Stone is located in the central north of Rilara, in the foothills of Mount Taras 
Population:  
    670 (90% deep gnome, 5% human, 5% dwarf)
Government:  Miner's oligarchy
Defenses:  None that can be seen.
Miscellaneous Information:
    Stone is a town of deep gnomes. That fact alone should draw your attention to the fact that Stone is just the tip of the Mount Taras iceberg. The town itself is the relay station for mining supplies headed deep under the mountains and the point of commercial contact between the deep gnomes and the outside world. This is why the gnomes have recruited a small number of humans to manage their surface affairs, trading a very small portion of the minerals they uncover for other necessary supplies. A Temple to the deep gnomes' patron goddess, Beryl, has been established in Stone.

Fort Himlad
Location:  
    Fort Himlad lies at the southern edge of Wolfswood Forest on the banks of the Falas River. 
Population: 60
Government:  Military rule
Miscellaneous Information:
    Fort Himlad lies at a strategic crossroad, with a road north leading into the Wolfswood, another heading east towards King's Landing and the Iriand Mountains, and yet another which leads west towards the numerous villages and hamlets that populate southwestern Rilara. Despite its crucial function of guarding the intersection of these key thoroughfares, it's not a big fort; its walls are wooden palisades.
    Rilarans of the southwest often send agents of seemingly meaningless commerce to Fort Himlad. Most believe they are spies. It is no secret that most of the southwest lives with a kind of rational paranoia of what Milara will do next and see Himlad as the crucial staging point or thoroughfare for any plans he might have with their homeland. Because of this, people of Himlad suspect the people of the southwest of planning an offensive against them. Minor skirmishes on the road west have already taken place. It seems only a mater of time before things escalate. Milara, it is rumored, shows up from time to time on nearby bluffs and watches the situation deteriorate with beaming expressions of gratification.

Dregar Locales

    A vast mountain range on the southeastern edge of Rilara. In these mountains, Milara has his throne, launching attacks upon the continent from Bloody Gate. These mountains are known for the great mountain giants that inhabit them.

    South Rilara, east of Greywatch Tower,

Due to the result of the the adventurers' interference, the swamp has since been called the Swamp of Lost Souls.

The 'numbers' field isn't necessary for Odd, Even, Red, Black, High, Low, and Five bets.  For a Number bet, just put the number you'd like to bet on after 'Number'.  Valid numbers include 1 through 36,  0 and 00.  For a Split bet, just put the two numbers that you'd like to bet on with the lowest number first.  (They have to be adjacent to eachother on the table.)  For a Column or Dozen bet, valid numbers are 1, 2 and 3.  For Columns, the numbers correspond to the top number in the column.  For Dozens, the numbers correspond to 1-12, 13-24, and 25-36.

For a corner bet, you'll need to put the highest and lowest number in the corner with a dash inbetween, such as 1-5 or 2-6.  Note that this bet doesn't cover all numbers in the range, just the ones that make a square.  (1-5 doesn't include 3, and 2-6 doesn't include 4, etc.).  The same applies to Line and Street bets, though all the numbers in the range are included.

Given only to those most favored guards and devotees to Shindaleria, this spear is as much a symbol as a formidable weapon.  It seems to be made of water given shape, with flows and waves visible within its form. The design of the spear's tip allows it to move effortlessly through water. Its ends give off a strong chill, like the cold waters of the deep sea, though its wielder is somewhat isolated from such effects.
This weapon used by those that seek to eradicate the undead of the world was lost when a group of over ambitious hunters came to clean the heart of Sigil.

Dregar
    The largest continent of Layonara, Dregar is also home to the capital of Pranzis, from which the emperors ruled. The King of Dregar is still rebuilding after losing over 200,000 troops (not just in Pranzis) defending his populace from Blood and the forces that came through the rifts. The continent is in turmoil because of the rebuilding process and the lack of protection from qualified soldiers. Some upstarts are attempting to claim their own territories and bandits have their rein on the countryside. On top of all of this, Blood still has a very sizeable army and attacks outlying areas quite frequently.

Well-known cities:

Pranzis
Location: 
    Pranzis is the Capital City of the World and lies on the southern half of Dregar, west of the Forest of Fog. 
Population: 
    Approximately 42,000 (48% human, 18% dwarf, 12% halfling, 8% gnome, 7% elf, 5% half-elf, 2% half-orc) 
Government:  
    Monarchy - The King and Queen of Dregar live in the city. 
Defenses: 
    Superior masonry walls surround much of the city. In many places the walls are also reinforced. In addition to this much of the walls have also been magically reinforced. The defenses are solidly constructed and security is tight, as one would expect in the world's capital.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    This is the city to visit when you are looking for that special item or are in need of military training. It directly supplies military forces to Fort Thunder, North Fort and South Fort. 

    As largest city in the world, many religions have built temples here. Most noteworthy is the majestic cathedral of Rofirein, but temples to Toran and Branderback can also be found here.

Hurm 
Location:
    Hurm is on the west coast of the continent of Dregar, on the Bay of Carocsa, not far from the Forsaken Islands. 
Population 
    3,000 (75% human, 5% Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% halfling, 5% half-elf, 5% elf) 
Government:  Feudalism 
Defenses:
    There is a wooden palisade around this coastal town. The town is often in a state of disrepair, so its defenses are unreliable at best. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Just thirty years ago Hurm was a prosperous city with a bright future. Since Blood's return, however, it has deteriorated rapidly. The town is no longer the shipping potentate it once was, largely due to the proximity of the Forsaken Islands. 

Lorindar 
Location:  
    Lorindar is at the southernmost tip of the continent of Dregar.
Population: 
    15,000 (45% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 10% dwarf, 10% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government:  Monarchy 
Defenses:
    A large, well fortified masonry wall surrounds this city. The ruler is proud of the protection the wall offers the city. Some parts of the wall are also protected by spells. 

Miscellaneous Information:
    The twin horsemen of Lorindar are either the first or last landmark most people see on the continent of Dregar. In the early days of the rule of Pranzis a company of horsemen were sent into the wilds of the southern plains to make the lands livable by common folk. A massive Drow invasion in the prior century had drawn all of the capital's attention and left the south, despite being so close, to fall into shadow. The towns of the southern plains were quickly overrun and the people either fled further south or went missing. Once the capital was settled, the horsemen left the gates to reclaim the towns and clear the roads. In the end, only two made it to the southern tip of the continent. There they found an impressive and resilient throng of Dregarians living in scattered coastal communities under the constant threat of assault.

  The two horsemen, a twin brother and sister of the Galeright family, rallied these scattered tribes under the flag of the capital and brought them to the ruined outpost at Lorindar. There they rebuilt the town by hand and with primitive equipment. Still, they rebuilt it with enough motivation and skill to withstand the swarms of bugbears and giants that crashed against their walls like waves against their stone docks. Of course the Galeright twins were in front of the walls, meeting each wave with astounding skill and passion.
Rather than return to the capital, the Galeright twins settled in Lorindar and brought the king and queen themselves to witness the mighty will of the southerners. It was a glorious day in the history of Dregar, one that lives in the proud tales of Lornidarians. Shortly thereafter, the capital redirected immense funds and manpower to Lornidar, sensing its strategic, economic, and political significance as well as the sentimental unifying force it had for southern Dregarians. 

    Now Lorindar is the busiest and most strategically situated port, always bustling with commerce and strange faces. The people of Lorindar are proud of their city and their close connection with Pranzis and work hard to maintain their dominance in the shipping business of Dregar. Most of the merchants and associated industries find honor in honest and fair business dealings, and the city has become known throughout the realm as such. Nevertheless, Lorindarians are often suspicious of outsiders, particularly those from competing ports, notably their rival city, Waysend.

Redstone 
Location:
    Redstone lies west of the Serpent Mountains and north of Pranzis on the continent of Dregar. 
Population:
    950 (85% Hill Dwarf, 5% Gnome, 5% human, 2% halfling, 2% half elf, 1% elf) 
Government:  Clan 
Defenses:
    Redstone has masonry walls that surround the town. These walls were built by dwarves, so they are very sturdy and can withstand a large scale attack. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Redstone has one of the largest populations of Hill Dwarves on the continent of Dregar. Many dwarves end up settling in Pranzis and plying their trades and skills there. The populace of Redstone is known as hardy folks that have had a hard life. 
 
Vale 
Location: 
    Vale is in the southern part of the continent of Dregar in the Forests of Mists. 
Population: 
    600 (50% elf, 20% human, 15% half-elf, 5% halfling, 5% gnome, 5% dwarf, 5% half-orc. 
Government:  Theocracy 
Defenses:   
    Nestled in the great trees, this town is protected by remoteness and lore of hallowed ground. Rangers and druids have dedicated their lives to protecting Vale, and do so with passion. A short stone wall surrounds the village core. The chest-high wall is perfect for rangers to shoot over and druids to cast behind with some protection.

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Vale is more of a spiritual center and forest outpost than a town. Of those who call Vale home, most live remotely among the old trees, yet they retain a practical and spiritual attachment to this place amidst nature.
On the continent of Dregar, Vale is never far from the hearts of rangers and druids. Deep in the heart of the Forest of Fog, its serene power is unsurpassed. Dregar's nature folk make regular pilgrimages to the legendary tree shrine of Vale to fulfilll their vows or renew their spirit. It is known that every decade, each druid throughout Layonara is required by oath to make a pilgrimage to this central forest and central shrine of Katia within. It is rumored that most come more frequently, as the experience is reinvigorating as well as a key to the spiritual and pragmatic unity of Layonara's druids. Through this hub of the druidic network, information is shared, new members are indoctrinated, roles are shuffled and objectives established.

Dalanthar
Location:  
    Dalanthar can be found in northern Dregar, between the Thunder Peaks and the Darkland Mountains.
Population: 1900
Government:  
    Two families struggle with each other for rule of Dalanthar
Defenses: None

Miscellaneous Information:
    Ages ago, the city of Dalanthar was the site of an awesome conflict between dragons. In the clash, the town was reduced to fire and rubble. The few survivors reconstructed the town upon the ruins. Today it is a shadow of its former glory. This is partly caused by the ever-present darkness that emanates from the Great Rift found northwest of town in the Darkland Mountains. It is also only a shell of its former self because for a powerful few, the dragon conflict still rages, animating intra-village aggression. One prominent family still sides with one dragon, blaming all the town's woes on the other. A second prominent family points its finger at the first. This conflict is manifest in the geography of town, as a huge craggy ridge separates the town into two halves. Each half is primarily under the influence of one of these two families..

Highpass
Location: In the Storm Horn Mountains
Population: 95
Government: Waysend representative

Miscellaneous Information:
    Highpass is a tiny village that sprung around Highpass Fort, and is located on one of the few usable passes through the Storm Horn Mountains. The pass is of major importance to the city of Waysend to the southeast, as this is one of the main roads for transporting goods to and from the port city. It is also home to a temple of Goran.

North Fort:
Location: 
    Bordered by Deadman's Pass and the Drift Lands on Dregar.
Population:  700
Government:  Military rule

Miscellaneous Information:
    North Fort is little more than a high desert camp. The frequency of suspicious events in the desert has kept North Fort well attached to the capital, despite the distance. The numbers of inhabitants are never high, however, as skirmishes between the king's and Bloodstone's armies are all too common. As such, the fort is continually re-supplied and at a constant state of alert.

North Point:
Location:
  North Point is the northernmost town on Dregar, west of the Singing Forest
Population:  800
Government:  
    There are several tribes which struggle for control in North Point at any given time.
Defenses:  
    North Point has no defenses.

Miscellaneous Information:
    For years fishermen traveled to this spot to exploit the huge schools of fish brought to the coast by the strong ocean currents off the north edge of the continent. Makeshift encampments eventually became this well-developed fishing village. Those who won this land from the hands of the previous occupants were rugged indeed, and the city still retains this surly character. This, by the way, makes North Point attractive for pirates who raid the cargo ships trying to sail swiftly by in the current and offshore winds. This doesn't seem to bother the fishermen much as pirates rarely hunt for fish and they do bring a steady supply of gold and goods into the town. A temple to Aeridin can be found here.

Orc's Watch
Location:  
    North of Vale at the north rim of the Forests of Mists
Population:  150
Government:  Tribal
Defenses:  
    A wooden wall and gates protect the meager interior of this outpost.

Miscellaneous Information:
    As its name suggests, this series of buildings on a tall hill serves as a lookout for Bloodstone's activity in the Forest of Fog. Sources say that it was overrun in a sweeping march along the north rim of the Forest of Fog by Bloodstone's army and now remains almost entirely abandoned.

Saudiria
Location:  
    On the east coast of Dregar, at the edge of the Anuroch Desert and the Drift Lands lies the city of Saudiria.
Population: 8500
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  
    There is a wooden and adobe wall surrounding this city for protection. Mostly it is protected by the desert and the ocean.

Miscellaneous Information:
    How you come to Saudiria will determine your perception of it. From the desert, Saudiria will greet you with the enticing natural rhythms of an oasis. From the ocean, Saudiria wil greet you with a windblown lullaby and an inviting bed of grass made just for your weary head. Saudiria is both. It is desert oasis and costal vale. That fact, combined with the way the sun sets where desert wisps swirl in coastal gusts, make Saudiria known throughout the known islands for its magical beauty.

    The surrounding desert will testify that Saudiria hasn't always been blessed thus. Something or someone carved this coastal glade and farmland out of the sand and dust of the desert. The terrain of Saudiria is considered one of the great works of Dregar. Many come to Saudiria to enjoy its sights. Others come to answer the riddle of this amazing transformation: was it wealth, labor, magic, or some other power that created this land?  Residents never tell. Wanderers mostly choose to reside. Only fables tell the truth. Some wonder if it is the temple of Az'atta that can be found here.

Thorns Keep
Location:  
    In the Thunder Peaks in the northern part of Dregar
Population:  200
Government:  Military rule
Defenses:  
    This is a heavily defended keep, well protected by both the walls of the keep itself and the sheer rock walls of the Thunder Peaks.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Like the name suggests, Thorn's Keep is not at all inviting. It lies in a particularly barren and inhospitable region of the Thunder Peaks. There are, however, two key reasons for the massive keep to exist there. First, there is a small but crucial body of water there which drains in the spring and summer to irrigate the fields of the Great Central Plains of Dregar below. Second, it is situated on a mountain crest which allows surveillance of that same key region. Those that reside in Thorn's Keep are therefore vigilant yet gruff, meshing perfectly with its overall persona. Contact with the keep has been cut off by Blood for sometime, however. Some believe that the Keep has fallen into the hands of the enemy.

Castle Raxswell
Location:  
    North of Lorindar, Castle Raxswell stands.
Population: 800
Government: Military rule
Defenses: 
    The castle is heavily defended by high and wide stone walls with ramparts and reinforcements.

Miscellaneous Information:
    Traveling north from Lorindar you'll come to Castle Raxwell. Both the castle itself and the temple of Prunilla located therein are notable for their spartan aesthetic. The castle is situated as a point of defense for the major port city of Lorindar. Many battles against the armies of Bloodstone have been waged on this barren and blood-soaked soil. Pranzis continually sends troops to this castle, knowing well its importance in the struggle for control of Dregar.


Willows Weep
Location:
    North of the Darkland Mountains, west of the Singing Forest and south of North Point you'll find Willows Weep.
Population:  660
Government:  Chiefdom
Defenses:  none

Miscellaneous Information:
    This rare Elven town on Dregar exudes a mystical sullenness which seems to dance hauntingly along with the drooping willow branches. It is a small town, but built with elegant extravagance. The stylized and prominent crypts in the area have suggested to travelers that this city is somehow rooted in those crypts or servants of the dead.

Xora's Tower
Location:
    Xora's Tower can be found in the northeasternmost part of Dregar
Population:  140
Government:  Military dictatorship
Defenses:  very little

Miscellaneous Information:
    On the northeasternmost point of the continent of Dregar, perched on a rounded bluff, lies the haunting tower of Xora. For ages this tower served as a watchpoint for invaders from the sea or demons from Xantril. Rumor now spreads that this tower has been captured by demons or Bloodstone and has been turned to other purposes. Within sight of the tower lies an ancient shrine where magical force beckons. Knowledge of its origin and its use are either carefully guarded or lost over generations.

Waysend 
Location: 
    On the east cost of the continent of Dregar is the city of Waysend.
Population 
    6,000 (55% human, 15% half-orc, 15% halfling, 5% dwarf, 5% gnome, 5% elf) 
Government: Republic 
Defenses:
    There is a masonry wall that is about 80% completed that surrounds the city. The ruler is spending lots of money to ensure the city is well protected from bandits and ships alike. 

Miscellaneous Information: 
    Waysend has recently come into its own, since Blood's arrival. With Hurm disintegrating and with Pranzis rebuilding its troops, Waysend has been left on its own and is building a good shipping business. Waysend is one of the cities that is trying to break away from Pranzis' rule.

In a time when the Wolfswood of Alindor was teeming with a new birth of deadly spiders, a Ranger stepped from the Wolfswood Corps to take control of the situation and end the blight.

How exactly he was able to do this is uncertain, but it was deemed no simple feat to accomplish... and he was quickly promoted to Captain Rodlin of the WolfsWood Ranger Corps.
